          One Stat to Sum Up 2026-27 So Far for Every Premier League Team
        
      
                          
                      Oct 6, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Is it possible to summarise the 2026-27 Premier League season so far through just one statistic for each of the 20 teams? We’ve given it a go.

Five matchdays into the 2026-27 season, the Premier League table is looking rather better for some teams (Manchester City, Brighton, Brentford, Hull) than it is for others (Spurs, Fulham, Bournemouth).
But while the actual table is all that really matters, a look into the numbers shows there is more to the Premier League than meets the eye.

With that in mind, we’ve found one statistic that summarises each team’s campaign. From mitigating factors and reasons to be positive to concerning issues and damning truths, in order of current league position, this is the season so far in one stat for each team.
Just five games into the Enzo Maresca era, Manchester City sit top of the pile with the only remaining 100% record in the top four tiers of English football.

They have done it not by leaning on a solid defence but instead through an extremely talented and ruthlessly efficient attack. They are averaging higher-quality chances than any other team in the Premier League this season, with the average expected goals value of their non-penalty shots the best of the lot (0.15). That has helped them maintain the best non-penalty conversion rate, too (19.1%).

This is the 15th instance of a team winning their first five games of a Premier League season but, perhaps surprisingly, only four of the previous 14 have gone on to win the title. City’s lethal attack gives them as good a chance as any of joining the title-winning group.
Arsenal have the talent to beat anyone – yes, the Brighton defeat was an off day – but they also know how important it is to better your opponents when it comes to physical effort.
Across their first five games, Mikel Arteta’s men have run 22.7 kilometres more than their opponents, the biggest positive difference of any team so far.

The fact that they have more of the ball – often significantly so, averaging 59.5% possession – makes this statistic even more stark: Arsenal’s players work incredibly hard both in and out of possession. Sometimes, hard work trumps talent.
Speaking of physical effort, no other team has embodied the importance of hard work, specifically when out of possession, more than Brighton, whose high press has functioned brilliantly so far.

Fabian Hürzeler’s impressive side have enforced a suffocating high press to devastating effect, with the lowest PPDA (opposition passes per defensive action) rate (7.4) of every team in the Premier League, which shows how little time they give their opponents without putting pressure on them.
That has resulted in Brighton forcing more high turnovers (56) than any other team in the Premier League this season.
It helps when you’re trying not to lose matches if you never go behind, and Brentford have very nearly done just that so far this season.

Over their five Premier League matches, they have been trailing for just three minutes and 10 seconds, all of which came when they briefly went 2-1 down away to Bournemouth before equalising shortly afterwards.

That accounts for just 0.6% of their entire season so far which is, unsurprisingly, the lowest of all top-flight teams. They therefore remain one of just five undefeated sides and, flying high in fourth, will clearly take some beating.
Leeds have become a very good multi-faceted team under Daniel Farke, and while they are by no means reliant on set-pieces, they do use them more than most.

They are top of the Premier League this season for the proportion of their shots (46.7%) and xG (41.0%) which have been generated at non-penalty set-pieces. They have scored three of their seven goals from dead-ball situations, too.

Set-pieces aren’t the reason that Leeds are fifth in the table and one of the five remaining unbeaten sides, but they are clearly a significant part of the reason. Leeds are using dead balls better than most, and that’s nothing to be ashamed of.

With draws rescued late on against both Newcastle and Nottingham Forest, more dropped points at home to struggling Fulham, and two wins that weren’t exactly the most convincing against Ipswich and Bournemouth, it hasn’t been the strongest start to life at Anfield for Andoni Iraola.

          UEFA Women’s Champions League: Opta Supercomputer Matchday 2 Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Sep 30, 2026
          
                      Emily Clogg / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our UEFA Women’s Champions League match predictions across Matchday 2 in 2026-27.

It was goals galore for Lyon and Barcelona on Matchday 1 against Servette and Paris FC, respectively, whilst over in London, both Arsenal and Chelsea squeezed past their opponents with narrow 1-0 victories.
Meanwhile, reigning WSL champions Manchester City, came from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 against Bayern Munich City becoming the first English side to avoid defeat at Bayern Munich in the UWCL.
The next round of fixtures promises even more entertainment.

The blockbuster match of the week sees Chelsea travel to eight-time winners Lyon; Sonia Bompastor is set to make a return to her old stomping ground hoping to take all three points back to the English capital.
Matches elsewhere include Benfica hosting Bayern Munich, Arsenal travelling to Paris FC, and Roma facing the tough test of welcoming a formidable Barcelona to Stadio Tre Fontane.
Opta Analyst presents data-driven predictions for each game from MD2, powered by the Opta supercomputer’s pre-match simulations.
There are three 5:45pm kick-offs to start the matchday on Wednesday as BK Häcken, Paris FC and Roma host the first set of matches.
For inaugural 2025-26 UEFA Women’s Europa Cup winners Häcken, the supercomputer backs them to get the Italian job done this week after a tight 1-0 defeat at the hands of Inter Milan last time out.

This week’s opponents are six-time Serie A champions Juventus. The Bianconere won their opening league match of the season 2-0 against Napoli at the weekend, but tasted defeat in the UWCL at the hands of Portuguese outfit Benfica.
Häcken have lost each of their last three UWCL matches, equalling their longest-ever losing streak in the competition, previously set between 17 November 2021 and 15 December 2021.

The supercomputer predicts a similar fate for Juve this time around; Häcken came out victorious in 64.5% of pre-match simulations. In fact, the simulations saw more draws (19.0%) than wins for Juventus (16.5%).

Elsewhere, two-time UWCL winners Arsenal travel to the French capital to play Paris FC as they look to improve on their 1-0 win against HB Køge. The Gunners netted a stoppage-time penalty to sugarcoat what was otherwise a limp performance against the Danish side.
The big headscratcher for Renée Slegers is quite simply how to get the ball in the back of the net.

A disappointing 1-0 defeat against rivals Chelsea at the weekend leaves Arsenal seventh in the WSL table, having failed to score in two of their four games. In fact, only newly-promoted Charlton Athletic (3) have failed to score more often in league this season.

It will be the first meeting between Paris FC and Arsenal in the UWCL, with the French side having lost each of their previous three matches against English opponents in the competition, all against Chelsea (1-4, 0-4 and 0-4 between 2023 and 2025).

The Gunners came out victorious 1-0 in a pre-season friendly against their opponents this summer, and the supercomputer backs Slegers' side to start the UWCL campaign with back-to-back wins for the first time since 2022-23, coming out on top in 63.5% of the computer's 10,000 pre-match simulations.
The third and final early kick-off Wednesday has to offer comes in the form of Roma against competition giants, and favourites Barcelona.

Barça, perhaps unsurprisingly, are flying high once again this season boasting a perfect record in Liga F after five games, having scored 21 times and conceded just twice. Their quest for a fifth UWCL crown got off to a great start too as Barça dominated Servette in an 8-0 win last week.
Before the start of this year’s edition, the Opta supercomputer heavily favoured Barcelona ending the tournament as winners once again; the Blaugrana won the trophy in 41.2% of simulations.

          Vertical, Relentless, Effective: The Tottenham Transformation Under Martin Ho
        
      
                          
                      Sep 23, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Martin Ho has overseen a remarkable turnaround at Tottenham. From an 11th-place finish two seasons ago to one of the WSL's most exciting and progressive teams, and just one of four unbeaten sides this season after three games. How close are Spurs to closing the gap on the division's elite?

Tottenham Hotspur's 7-0 victory over Crystal Palace may have been the performance that turned heads in the Women's Super League this weekend, but the foundations for such a display have been building for some time.

Just over a year ago, Spurs were coming off an 11th-place finish and searching for a new direction. While there had been flashes of progress in earlier seasons, including fifth- and sixth place finishes in 2021-22 and 2023-24 respectively, their slide towards the bottom end of the table in 2024-25 underlined the gap that still existed to the league's leading clubs.
Since Martin Ho's arrival in July 2025, however, that trajectory has changed dramatically.

Tottenham collected a club-record 36 WSL points in Ho's first season in charge, winning 11 matches and returning to fifth place. Indeed, that points tally was the most ever by an English manager in their debut season in the competition.
Since taking the reins, Ho has overseen 13 WSL victories in just 25 matches, with only Manchester City (21), Chelsea (17) and Arsenal (16) winning more games in that period.
And their start to the 2026-27 campaign suggests that progress has continued.
Spurs are one of only four unbeaten teams remaining in the division, and sit second in the table after three matches, just behind Man City.

Tottenham are currently enjoying a six-match unbeaten run in the competition, equalling the longest in the club's WSL history, and the first since such a six-game streak between October-November 2023. The challenge now is sustaining that momentum.
They face the third-toughest fixture run in the division over their next five WSL games according to the Opta Power Rankings, coming up against London City Lionesses, Chelsea and Arsenal.
That makes their start even more intriguing.

Spurs won four of their opening five WSL games last season, before winning just seven of their remaining 17. This time around, Ho will be hoping his side can bridge that gap to the league’s elite, and, crucially, sustain their strong start across the entirety of the campaign.
The meetings with the ‘big four' will provide a significant test, but there is growing evidence that Spurs are closer to that level than they have been before.
Ho's emphasis on brave, front-foot football combined with defensive discipline is already evident in Tottenham's early-season performances, none more so than their 7-0 victory over Crystal Palace.

While the visitors were helped by Palace being reduced to 10 players after just seven minutes, scoring seven goals at WSL level is no simple task. After all, this was a Palace side that had drawn 0-0 against Arsenal at Emirates Stadium just a week earlier despite facing 30 shots.
The manner of Tottenham's dominance was particularly striking. Spurs registered 42 shots, the third-highest total in WSL history, and the most ever recorded by an away side in the competition.

They also amassed 82 touches in the opposition box, the most by Tottenham in a WSL match and the joint fourth-highest total ever recorded in the league. No team had reached that figure since Chelsea managed 82 against Leicester City in December 2024.
On top of that, the game was goalless at the break, with all seven goals coming in a ruthless second half.

There were standout individual performances.Olivia Holdt became just the second Tottenham player to score a WSL hat-trick, after Martha Thomas against Aston Villa in October 2023, while Amanda Nildén‘s late goal perfectly captured the collective nature of Spurs' attacking play.
Nildén's 86th-minute strike came at the end of a 37-second move involving nine different Tottenham players, the most players involved in a single WSL goal this season.

          UEFA Women's Champions League Predictions 2026-27: The Opta Supercomputer Projections
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      Yash Thakur / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Who will win the UEFA Women's Champions League in 2026-27? Will Barcelona retain their crown? Here, we detail how the Opta supercomputer sees this season playing out.
The UEFA Women’s Champions League is back with its 18-team league-phase format for the 2026-27 season, and Matchday 1 kicks off on Tuesday.

Each team will play six games in the league phase, with the top four teams at the end securing direct qualification to the quarter-finals, while the teams ranked 5th to 12th will compete in a knockout play-off to book their place in the last eight.

Barcelona were crowned champions for the fourth time in their history after thrashing OL Lyonnes 4-0 in the final last season. Ewa Pajor and Salma Paralluelo both scored twice in the second half to secure the title.

In a summer of major moves, two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas departed Barcelona for the WSL, while Salma Paralluelo made the switch to Lyon. Arsenal and Lyon have both strengthened their already potent attacks, Real Madrid continue to build around an exciting young core, and Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Manchester City will all be firmly in the hunt for silverware this season.
So, which side has got the Opta supercomputer's backing for European glory?

Barcelona come into another season as the favourites to win the competition and equal their men’s team’s tally of five European titles. The Spanish champions have featured in all the UWCL finals this decade, being crowned champions four times.

Despite losing some long serving members of the squad this summer, Pere Romeu’s side came out winners in 41.2% of the supercomputer's simulations. The Blaugranas are the side to beat in Europe and have lost just three out of 38 games in the UWCL since the start of 2023, with all three losses coming against English sides (1-0 vs Arsenal on 24 May 2025, 2-0 vs Man City on 10 October 2024 and 1-0 vs Chelsea on 20 April 2024).

After losing out to eventual champions Barcelona in the semi-finals of the last edition, Bayern Munich are the second most likely side to win the competition this season with Opta’s supercomputer. José Barcala’s winning machine reached the final in 34.8% of the simulations and were crowned champions in 17.3% of them.

In fact, Bayern’s only two losses in all competitions last season came at the hands of Barcelona (7-1 in October and 4-2 in May). Although Georgia Stanway switched the Bavarians for Arsenal this summer, Barcala should feel confident in their attack of Klara Bühl, Pernille Harder, Edna Imade and others.
Bayern and Barça are set to face each other again in the final match of the league phase this season. Bayern will hope to do better this time.
According to the supercomputer, all English teams and OL Lyonnes are expected to secure a place in the quarter-finals of the UWCL this year, alongside the title contenders of course.

Sonia Bompastor’s Chelsea (94.0%) have been given the second highest chance of reaching the last eight of the competition, behind Barcelona. This is largely down to their favourable draw as the Blues have the lowest average fixture difficulty rating of all teams in the league phase this year.

Surprisingly, the Opta supercomputer is not too bullish on the prospects of eight-time champions and last year’s runners-up OL Lyonnes, or the 2024-25 champions Arsenal. Those two teams came out on top in only 8.7% and 7.0% of the simulations, respectively.Jonatan Giráldez's side reached the final in 20.6% of simulations, behind Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Chelsea and Man City. Despite adding more attacking firepower to the side with the signings of Caroline Weir and Paralluelo, Lyon lack balance in the midfield following Lindsey Heaps’ departure this summer to Denver Summit FC.
The side struggled to maintain the intensity and compactness throughout the 90 minutes in last season’s final against Barcelona and could yet fall short in that regard this season.

Renee Slegers’ Arsenal have had their own issues in front of goal, unable to maximise their goalscoring opportunities, a glimpse of what has continuously haunted the Gunners when it comes to the fine margins.

Their recent goalless draw against Crystal Palace was another in a long list of games where they failed to convert their chances. According to the Opta supercomputer, Arsenal reached the final on just 17.8% of the simulations.

English champions Manchester City reached the semi-final stage in 50.1% of the simulations on their return to the competition. Andree Jeglertz’s side haven’t featured in the final four since the 2017-18 season, when they were beaten by the eventual champions Lyon thanks to a goal by Lucy Bronze.

Spearheaded by Khadija Shaw, City will hope to add a European star to their domestic triumphs, building on their momentum. The side has talented players across all positions but potentially lacks the depth needed to compete three times a week.

Outside the top six, Real Madrid have the highest probability of making the quarter-finals of the UWCL this season (49.6%). Las Blancas have lost their leading goalscorer and assist provider in the club’s history, Caroline Weir, but have brought in the prodigious talent of Felicia Schroder to lead the attack alongside Linda Caicedo.

108w6stzxj8zc1ujzo1taheqe5.title: Spain have 'no intention of stopping winning', says De la Fuente
108w6stzxj8zc1ujzo1taheqe5.subtitle: Spain's stellar unbeaten streak looked like it was under pressure at Wembley, but they came from behind to beat England in the second half.
paragraphs: Luis de la Fuente insists Spain have "no intention of stopping winning" after securing a 3-2 comeback win over England to start their Nations League campaign.
Lamine Yamal put the world champions ahead after just 105 seconds, capitalising on a Marc Guehi mistake, but they found themselves behind at the break after goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane.
A slow start to the second half saw Rodri give away a penalty, but Spain were given a reprieve when Kane sent his spot-kick crashing against the bar.
Two substitutes then flipped the script, with Alex Baena equalising before setting up Mikel Oyarzabal for the winner.
Spain are now unbeaten in their last 39 matches (across 90 minutes), extending the record run among all European nations in all competitions (W30 D9).
La Roja, who dominated for long periods, have won each of their last eight competitive matches, and De la Fuente was particularly impressed with the resilience his side showed.
"We are very happy with the result, with the performance, and for having shown the world that we have a lot of ambition and a strong desire to win," he told Teledeporte.
"It is true that there were moments when we had to suffer. But this is England.
"We talked at half-time. We had the game under control; we had three clear chances. We continue to show that this team never gives up, that we have no intention of stopping winning.
"I'm lucky to have these players. Anyone can step onto the pitch and be ready. It's about trying to make changes. They have exceptional talent."

Spain could have been out of sight in the first 30 minutes against England, with Ferran Torres having a goal disallowed for offside before he saw two golden one-on-one chances against James Trafford go begging.

Dani Olmo and Yamal also wasted opportunities before the Three Lions scored, and they went into half-time knowing they had conceded more goals in those 45 minutes (two) than they did in their World Cup-winning campaign (one).
"We conceded both of England's goals; it was a moment of disconnection," De la Fuente said in his press conference.
"They could hurt us, and we weren't able to fight them back. Generally speaking, the game was under control against a superpower.
"We all played our part, and I think we had the game under control against such a powerful opponent."
And when asked about the current unbeaten streak, he added: "What this generation of footballers is doing is truly remarkable.
"They never stop striving to improve. The statistics speak for themselves. It's incredibly difficult to replicate what Spain is achieving.
"We'll approach the match against Croatia as if it were our last. These players are always eager to keep developing."

10afbmzk5gc7e129jab1kjypud.title: Italy 3-1 Turkiye: Mancini's men grind it out
10afbmzk5gc7e129jab1kjypud.subtitle: Italy moved into second place in Nations League Group A1, with Riccardo Calafiori and Francesco Pio Esposito sealing a win over Turkiye.
paragraphs: Italy continued their strong start under Roberto Mancini with a hard-fought 3-1 win over Turkiye in the Nations League.
Mancini's second spell as Italy coach started with a loss to Belgium, but the Azzurri have now taken seven points from their next three outings to sit second in Group A1.
They had to do it the hard way at Stadio Renato Dall'Ara, where Turkiye – under the tutelage of Italian coach Vincenzo Montella – kept them in a tussle until the end.

A first half of few clear chances was punctuated by a real moment of quality from Gianluca Scamacca, who instinctively fired in a snapshot off the underside of the crossbar to break the deadlock in the 26th minute.
Yet a decent response from Italy early in the second half told when Aral Simsir turned into an empty net after the ball broke kindly for him at the back post.
Parity, however, lasted just three minutes, as substitute Riccardo Calafiori leapt highest to meet Nicolo Barella's delivery and thumped in a header to restore Italy's advantage.
The contest was settled in the 87th minute, as another of Mancini's substitutes, Francesco Pio Esposito, flicked in from Alessandro Romano's centre.
Esposito into the history books
It was a grind, but Italy got over the line in Bologna, and Mancini can reflect on a decent points haul from his first four matches back at the helm.
This was an even game, as evidenced by the match stats.
Italy had 15 shots to Turkiye's 14, while the Azzurri had six attempts on target to their visitors' five.
The hosts also had 28 touches in the opponent's box, whereas Turkiye had 27 going the other way, while Italy generated chances worth 1.9 expected goals to Turkiye's 1.31 xG.
Ultimately, Esposito settled matters with a smart finish.

He has become only the second player in the history of the Italian national team to score his seventh international goal before turning 22, after Giuseppe Meazza (20 years and 155 days on January 25, 1931).
Esposito will hope to be at the spearhead of Mancini's second spell, as the coach looks to repeat his success from the first time around.

10do9su6yhosq1ifgenic1r6mb.title: Bastoni 'in debt to the Italian people' following World Cup qualification failures
10do9su6yhosq1ifgenic1r6mb.subtitle: After Italy won for the first time since Roberto Mancini's return, Alessandro Bastoni admitted he must work to get their fans back on-side.
paragraphs: Alessandro Bastoni admits he is 'in debt to the Italian people' following the Azzurri's World Cup shortcomings, though he has urged patience as Roberto Mancini's team look to get things right.
Italy failed to qualify for a third straight edition of the World Cup this year, losing on penalties to Bosnia-Herzegovina following a 1-1 draw in a play-off in March.
Their task was made more difficult in that match by Bastoni being sent off late in the first half, having hacked Amar Memic down when he was racing clear on goal.

Italy are the first former champions to ever miss three straight World Cups, with their latest humiliating failure leading to the dismissal of Gennaro Gattuso and the return of Euro 2020-winning coach Mancini, following a lengthy and frustrating recruitment process.

Mancini's men started their Nations League campaign with a 2-0 defeat to France last week, but they bounced back with a 4-1 rout of Turkiye on Monday, with Bastoni scoring the opening goal as they roared into a 3-0 lead within 27 minutes.
After that victory, Bastoni reflected on the Bosnia-Herzegovina defeat and admitted he has plenty of work to do to atone for his red card.
"It was inevitable that my mind would go back to Zenica," Bastoni told RAI Sport. "I will be in debt to the Italian people for the next four years.
"When faced with difficult situations, I have always chosen to emerge with my head held high and take my responsibility.
"We hit rock bottom in recent years, but we want to get back on our feet.
"All we ask for is some balance and patience in judging this side, as there are many young players who want to learn."
Italy's win over Turkiye was their first by three or more goals away from home since November 2019, when they beat Bosnia-Herzogovina 3-0.

It was also their first win under Mancini in 1,198 days, having overcome the Netherlands 3-2 under him in the Nations League third-place play-off in June 2023, before he called time on his first stint in charge to join Saudi Arabia.
"We are still a young team overall, we have quality and we want to prove what we can do," Bastoni added, with a trip to France up next on Friday.
"We mustn't get too over-excited now, we had some peaks last year too, and then saw what happened. It is at least good to feel happy every now and then."

10nyiozd0a42n1mxlmxnedd14s.title: Mancini sets his sights on France after dominant victory over Turkiye
10nyiozd0a42n1mxlmxnedd14s.subtitle: Roberto Mancini claimed his first win since returning to manage Italy against Turkiye, but he is already thinking of the next match.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini immediately switched his focus to Italy's trip to France after he claimed his first win in his second stint with the Azzurri against Turkiye in the Nations League.
Mancini watched on as his Italy team emerged 4-1 victors in Bursaspor, with three goals inside the opening 27 minutes doing the damage against Vincenzo Montella's side.
Alessandro Bastoni handed the visitors a ninth-minute lead before Davide Frattesi rounded off an excellent passing move to double Italy's advantage in the 22nd minute.

Michael Kayode, on his international debut, put the Azzurri out of sight, as Italy scored three goals inside the first 30 minutes of play for the first time since a World Cup qualifier against Lithuania in September 2021.
Baris Alper Yilmaz threatened a comeback early in the second half, but Francesco Pio Esposito restored Italy's three-goal advantage in the 50th minute to seal an impressive win.
The result saw Italy win an away match by a 3+ goal margin for the first time since November 2019, when they beat Bosnia-Herzegovina 3-0.
More importantly, the Azzurri claimed their first win under Mancini, 1,198 days since his last win in charge of Italy, which came in a 3-2 triumph over the Netherlands in June 2023.

However, Mancini was already thinking about Italy's next game, which takes them to the Stade de France to face Zinedine Zidane's side, who sit top of Group A1 following their late win against Belgium on Monday.
"Now we have to focus on the next match, try to recover our strength, we've got fresh legs at home and will try to have our say in Paris," Mancini told RAI Sport.
The victory marked a huge improvement to the one Mancini oversaw on his second debut, with Italy outclassed during their 2-0 defeat against Belgium at the Stadio Olimpico.
Italy only registered an expected goals (xG) total of 1.7 from their 21 shots against Belgium, but they improved that to 2.4 from 14 attempts in a clinical display against Turkiye.

Mancini did, however, confirm that Giacomo Raspadori's substitution at half-time was because of an injury, and he was unable to add whether he would be available to face France and then Turkiye at home.
"We were on a pitch where it had been raining for a whole day, and it was only natural to expect a response from Turkiye," Mancini added.
"Everyone played a great game. Raspadori went off with a problem.
"We were worried that we might have to take him off after five minutes in the second half, so we substituted him at the break.
"The team pushed up, kept the ball, moved it around well. Raspadori did what we asked; he had a good game."

10tvummvu04th1i6on49egp0eh.title: Wicky excited to see Sporting KC's confidence build
10tvummvu04th1i6on49egp0eh.subtitle: Sporting Kansas City and the Seattle Sounders both head into Thursday's clash on the back of morale-boosting wins in MLS.
paragraphs: Raphael Wicky is hopeful that Sporting Kansas City's recent wins will continue to help build their confidence ahead of a visit to the Seattle Sounders in MLS.
Sporting have won two of their last three league games (L1), including a 2-0 victory over high-flying Houston Dynamo last time out.

That was their first clean sheet of the 2026 season, though they remain bottom of the Western Conference with 21 points, 14 behind the ninth-place Sounders, who occupy the final playoff spot with eight games left to play.
While Wicky had hoped for more goals against the Dynamo, he was thrilled to see another battling display, which he wants to carry forward.
"We had a chance to make it 3-0, and I think then it would be even harder for Houston to stay in the game," Wicky said after that result.
"We didn't, and 2-0 is always a tough result. I'm very pleased with what I saw, and I hope this gives the team confidence.
"I think over the last weeks, or even since the World Cup break, besides maybe two games, we've shown that we're competitive with most teams, so I'm happy with that."
Seattle were on a torrid run just a few weeks ago, having gone 13 games without a victory in MLS, but they have now won their last two games.

After beating Real Salt Lake, they followed it up with a 3-1 win over Minnesota United to move into the playoff places for the first time in months, but Brian Schmetzer believes the Sounders still have work to do to keep their revival going.
"Our structure, where we have a little bit of rotation between positions, is okay," he said, as quoted by Sounder at Heart.
"But the player who rotates into a different position has to understand the rules and responsibilities of where he's playing.
"You need to still be exciting, entertain the fans, do all that sort of stuff. I'm not trying to stifle any sort of creative moments.
"But we have to win games and make sure that we make a 2-0 lead, a 3-0 lead, and then we can kind of spitball and do what they want and have a little more joy."
Seattle Sounders – Albert Rusnak
Albert Rusnak assisted two of Seattle's three goals against Minnesota United, taking him to 12 assists on the season.
He has 38 assists over the last three seasons, the third-most in MLS in that time behind only Lionel Messi (49) and Evander (46).
Sporting Kansas City – Andre Luiz
Andre Luiz was directly involved in both goals in Sporting KC's win at Houston, scoring once and assisting once.
He is the first player to record a goal and an assist in a regular-season away match for Sporting since current Sounders player Dejan Joveljic against the LA Galaxy on March 14.
MATCH PREDICTION: SEATTLE SOUNDERS WIN
Seattle are unbeaten in four straight matches against Sporting KC (W3 D1), including a 1-1 draw in Kansas City on May 2.
The Sounders managed to avoid defeat only three times in their previous 10 against Sporting (W3 L7) dating back to 2019.

After a 13-match regular-season winless run, Seattle have recorded back-to-back victories with wins over Real Salt Lake and Minnesota. The Sounders, who drew the final five matches of that winless run, are now unbeaten in seven straight matches, the fourth-longest active streak in MLS.
As for Sporting KC, they won their third away match of the season on Saturday, a 2-0 victory at Houston.
Sporting last won two straight away from home in league play over five years ago, a three-match winning streak in July and August 2021 that included a victory in Seattle.
Seattle Sounders – 62.7%
Sporting Kansas City – 17.5%

Sporting last won two straight away from home in league play over five years ago, a three-match winning streak in July and August 2021 that included a victory in Seattle.

10u20asbr2uef17lke3udn2gyv.title: Netherlands and Dumfries target first clean sheet of the year
10u20asbr2uef17lke3udn2gyv.subtitle: The Netherlands are yet to keep a clean sheet in 2026, but they are hoping to change that when they host Serbia in the Nations League.
paragraphs: Denzel Dumfries insists the Netherlands are working to improve their defensive performances as they target their first clean sheet of the year.
The Netherlands face Serbia in the Nations League on Sunday, having conceded in each of their 11 matches in 2026.
They most recently conceded twice in a draw with Greece, though they did come from two goals down to salvage a point.
The Netherlands are unbeaten in their three games under Xavi (W1 D2), leaving them second in their Nations League group.
Despite their solid start, Dumfries acknowledged the Oranje still need to improve at the back.
"That is a nice challenge for the team. We want to change things and concede fewer goals," said Dumfries.
"It is not a problem, but it is, of course, an issue. When you look at the defenders we have, you shouldn't be conceding so many goals.
"That is a point of attention we are working on to improve."
It could be a special occasion at Philips Stadion for Netherlands captain Virgil van Dijk, who is in line to win his 100th cap for his country.

Van Dijk, who has scored 18 goals for the Netherlands, helped his country reach the semi-finals at Euro 2024, the quarter-finals at the 2022 World Cup and the final of the inaugural Nations League in 2019.
"It could be an emotional day for Virgil," Xavi said. "I am very happy to work with him and he is a true leader."
"He fits in well. One hundred caps is incredible. Whether he plays? We'll see on Sunday."

1108t1oiygwmm12mk678wpl61h.title: Pocognoli not concerned about Scotland's goal drought
1108t1oiygwmm12mk678wpl61h.subtitle: Scotland have not scored in any of their last three matches, but Sebastien Pocognoli believes their fortunes could change very quickly.
paragraphs: Sebastien Pocognoli insisted he is not concerned about Scotland's lack of goals ahead of their Nations League clash with Switzerland on Tuesday.
Scotland drew 0-0 with Slovenia in their first game under Pocognoli, despite accumulating 2.2 expected goals (xG) from 17 shots, four of which were Opta-defined 'big' chances.
Oliver McBurnie has failed to score in all 17 of his appearances for Scotland in all competitions, with the goalless draw at Slovenia his first game for the national side in 2,005 days.
Scotland have failed to score in their last three internationals after also blanking twice at the World Cup. They last failed to score in four consecutive matches between February and May 1971.
Nevertheless, ahead of his first home game in charge, Pocognoli is confident his Scotland side can change their fortunes in front of goal.
"It was one game. Some games you score. Some games you are unlucky," said the Belgian.
"I don't think there's any concerns from my side to score goals because we have good strikers. It's not only the strikers, but we are creating chances from many positions.
"Let's say we score [against Switzerland], I hope, and we can open another topic. I really hope we can start strong in the game.

"It will be a special moment, first time at home. I'm really looking forward for that moment since I've been appointed. As a new gaffer, that was really the date that was in my schedule that I want to experience."
Scotland have won just one of their last six meetings with Switzerland in all competitions (D3 L2), with this their first meeting since a 1-1 draw at Euro 2024.
Switzerland have won just one of their eight away games against Scotland in all competitions (D2 L5), though it was on their last visit in a March 2006 friendly (3-1).

113zwiiotwzbp1qrrhyk053ne3.title: De Bruyne: I did not try to leave Napoli
113zwiiotwzbp1qrrhyk053ne3.subtitle: Kevin De Bruyne previously seemed to suggest he could leave Napoli, but the Belgian has insisted he did not try to do so this summer.
paragraphs: Kevin De Bruyne has claimed he did not attempt to push through an exit from Napoli in the summer transfer window.
De Bruyne previously suggested he was unhappy at Napoli, and there was speculation linking him with a move away from the Serie A club.
The Manchester City great did not see eye to eye with coach Antonio Conte, who has since been replaced by Massimiliano Allegri.
De Bruyne, however, has now insisted he was not interested in leaving Napoli.
He told reporters: "No, I haven't really spoken to anyone about it.
"I just enjoyed my holidays and went straight back to Naples."
Napoli have made their worst start to a Serie A season in a decade, having taken seven points from their opening five matches.
De Bruyne, though, is not overly concerned.
He said: "We've had a rough start to the season, we've played a lot of strong teams already.
"We even had the chance to win it in the final minute against Inter, but we still lost. Those details are the difference between our seven points and the 10 or 11 we might've deserved.
"We're not doing so well in terms of points, but I think we're doing fine."
Injury restricted De Bruyne to 21 games last term. He scored five goals, assisted four more and created 40 chances.
De Bruyne has made six appearances this season, scoring once and providing one assist.

115tkn4u990fd1t4ot5v1ugy6b.title: Tuchel does not have 'anymore words' for Kane ahead of landmark England appearance
115tkn4u990fd1t4ot5v1ugy6b.subtitle: Harry Kane could become England's joint all-time leading appearance maker against Czechia, with Thomas Tuchel hailing his influence.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel says he has run out of words to describe Harry Kane, with the England captain in line to earn his 125th cap against Czechia on Tuesday.
Should he play at Wembley, Kane would equal Peter Shilton as the all-time record appearance maker for the England men's national team in this match.
Kane has 21 goals in his last 22 appearances for the Three Lions and has scored three goals in four games against Czechia.

Following a disappointing 3-2 loss to Spain in their opening Nations League match, England have since beaten Czechia and Croatia – who they thumped 7-0 – with Tuchel ready to rotate his squad ahead of the final match of the break.
While Tuchel did not give away too many hints about his squad selection, he was full of praise for the 33-year-old.
"I'm not sure I have anymore words," Tuchel said about Kane.
"He's on the shortlist for the Ballon d'Or. We've spoken so often about him, and I try to find new words which then make no sense!
"Everything he does, he does it on the highest level; he does it consecutively, and I am very sure he will be the one leading the team out onto the training pitch.
"He will lead the team in the warm-up and not do one step less or one step slower. That is the level he has.
"Since he took this major role for Bayern Munich, he found a new level. It's the highest level, on and off the pitch.
"All these number nines in world football, no matter in which league, they are built a bit different.
"They don't only do it so their team wins; they also do it for themselves and for the records: 'How many can I score? How many can I assist? Where is the next record?'
"That's what drives them, and it's good that drives them. You will not find a striker of this calibre who does not have these individual goals."
One of the players Tuchel will definitely be without is Alex Scott, who withdrew from the squad with a thigh injury on Monday.
Reports suggest Bournemouth are unhappy with how England have managed the 23-year-old's issue, given he could be out for up to eight weeks during a busy period for the club.
But Tuchel insists England took no risks with Scott's fitness when they chose to start him against Croatia.
"On a human level, I feel bad that he does not get his next cap [against Czechia]," says Tuchel. "In my mind, he started [the game].

"I would not have taken any risk, even if it was a big opportunity for him. We wanted him to start, but if we had the slightest idea it was a risk [to play him], we would not have taken it. We never do this.
"We – the medical and physical departments – are always in communication with all the players who are with us.
"We share information; this is a totally open process. I can understand that Bournemouth are not happy because they lose a key player.
"But I can just say that from the moment we took the decision, there was absolutely not risk apparent to me or our physical staff. It's a one-off."
England are unbeaten in all eight of their games against Czechia at Wembley Stadium (W6 D2), the most recent of which saw the Three Lions finish their Euro 2020 group stage campaign with a 1-0 win.
However, they were beaten by Spain at the national stadium earlier in this international window.
England last lost back-to-back competitive home matches between November 1999 (v Scotland) and October 2000 (v Germany) under Kevin Keegan.

1187i99ks00ua1ofbwlkojq45y.title: Van Bommel '100% happy and satisfied' after winning start to Belgium reign
1187i99ks00ua1ofbwlkojq45y.subtitle: Mark van Bommel began his tenure as Belgium boss with an impressive 2-0 victory over Italy at Stadio Olimpico in the Nations League.
paragraphs: Mark van Bommel said he was "100% happy and satisfied" after marking his first match as Belgium boss with a 2-0 victory over Italy.
Mika Godts opened the scoring at Stadio Olimpico after 20 minutes, while Dodi Lukebakio secured all three points in their Nations League opener with a stunning curler after the hour mark.
It marked Italy's second defeat on home soil while conceding at least two goals and scoring none in the last 40 years, following their 2-0 loss to Croatia in August 2006.
Belgium particularly dominated in the first half, where they accumulated 2.39 expected goals (xG) from 14 attempts while restricting Italy to 0.32 from five shots.

Gianluigi Donnarumma pulled off impressive saves to deny Godts, Charles De Ketelaere and Nicolas Raskin from adding a second before the break, though his efforts proved in vain after Lukebakio's strike.
Subsequently, Belgium defeated Italy for the first time in a competitive match since May 1972.
"I am 100% happy and satisfied, although of course one can always improve too," said Van Bommel in his press conference.
"We started work on Monday with the right hunger and intensity that we also saw on the field.
"We worked on this 4-3-3 system for three days, it wasn't a top performance, but we controlled the first half very well.

"Italy pressed us better after the break and Senne Lammens made an incredible save. With the changes, we regained control of the match and Lukebakio’s wonderful goal sealed it, just like he did at San Siro against Milan.
"We don’t just have 11 starters, everyone can make the difference. Some players didn’t have 90 minutes in their legs.
"Godts had an extraordinary performance, I told him to always try to run at players and make something happen.
"It is difficult to keep up this tempo for 90 minutes, especially at international level, but we hope to keep it going for as long as possible."

11noa022ig8rh1cetrnma34w5y.title: Wales boss Bellamy 'hurting' after Nations League defeat to Denmark
11noa022ig8rh1cetrnma34w5y.subtitle: Wales' poor run of form continued after they were beaten by Denmark in the Nations League, a result that left Craig Bellamy disappointed.
paragraphs: Craig Bellamy admitted he was "hurting" after Wales' defeat to Denmark in the Nations League, conceding his team were second-best at Parken on Sunday.
Wales slumped to back-to-back defeats to begin their Group A4 campaign, with Ben Davies' own goal and Gustav Isaksen's second-half finish sealing a 2-0 win for Denmark.
Rasmus Hojlund had seen a goal ruled out for offside before Denmark took the lead in the 53rd minute when Mikkel Damsgaard's free-kick was turned into the net by Davies.
And it was another Damsgaard free-kick that led to Denmark's second, with Isaksen's deflected volley looping over Danny Ward, and it could have got even worse for Wales.

Hojlund saw another goal chalked off after straying into an offside position, though Neco Williams was denied a late consolation for the visitors after the referee blew his whistle early for a foul by Ethan Ampadu in the build-up.

Wales have now failed to win any of their last six matches across all competitions (D3 L3), losing each of their last three. This is their longest run without a victory since a run of nine between June 2022 and March 2023.
Despite the loss, Bellamy remains confident his side will improve by playing against Europe's elite on a consistent basis, with Norway their next match this Thursday.
"I'm really hurting. When you see an athletic team run over you a little bit, but then, will we improve? I think we will," said Bellamy.
"This team will get better, these players will keep improving. There are young ones coming in well after I'm gone.
"For me now it's just focus, two more games to go. How can I help you improve for the next two games, but also how can I improve?
"I'm probably more loving when I'm losing, I'm probably more of a pain in the backside when I'm winning."

Denmark's dominance was backed up by the metrics. They fired off 20 shots, only managing more in the Nations League on two occasions, coming against the Republic of Ireland in November 2019 (26) and Portugal in March last year (23).
Brian Riemer's side are also now unbeaten in their last eight home matches across all competitions, winning six of those contests (D2).
Wales were only able to muster an expected goals (xG) total of 0.65 from their 10 attempts, but Sorba Thomas acknowledged there was still plenty of room for improvement.
"We are down as a team. We felt we were in the game. They had the proper chances, and they took them," Thomas said.
"We need to be more clinical, we need to start punishing teams when we're on top, that's what they did.
"I would have loved for my shot to go in, maybe the game could have been different. But we had more chances after that and didn't score. We've got to learn from that.
"Thankfully, we've got two games at home still to come. We'll have home advantage, so we need to show a reaction.
"We are just going to get better. We are a small nation, but we've got big hearts and beliefs and, for us, it's about showing that more on the pitch."
Bellamy's main frustration was the way in which his side conceded both goals, with Damsgaard's set-pieces causing the Wales defence all kinds of problems.
"I said to the players before the game, 'this is going to be tougher than Portugal'," Bellamy added.
"It was a different challenge but a very difficult one. The best team won overall.
"As disappointed as I am with that, the result I probably think was fair."

11obk5recdrfk1qntnmb3qyrvm.title: Mancini unfazed by Italy's lack of fluidity in win over Turkiye
11obk5recdrfk1qntnmb3qyrvm.subtitle: Italy were not at their free-flowing best against Turkiye in the Nations League, but Roberto Mancini's side managed to grind out a victory.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini admitted Italy's lack of fluidity against Turkiye in the Nations League was to be expected, given the number of changes he made.
Italy rounded off the international break with a 3-1 win over Turkiye, meaning they have now taken seven points across the first four games of Mancini's second stint in charge.
Aral Simsir cancelled out Gianluca Scamacca's first-half goal on the hour, but two substitutes secured the victory for Italy.
Riccardo Calafiori soon restored the hosts' lead, and Francesco Pio Esposito scored the clinching goal with three minutes of the 90 remaining.
Esposito became only the second player in the history of Italy's national team to score his seventh goal before turning 22, after Giuseppe Meazza (20 years and 155 days on January 25, 1931).

And though Italy did not look their best during the victory, Mancini, who made nine changes to his starting line-up from the draw with France last time out, was not too concerned about the performance.
"Despite the changes, naturally there was also fatigue," Mancini told RAI Sport.
"We suffered at the start, but the lads did well to get it back on track, score again after the 1-1, so it was a good game as the fourth in such a short spell of time.

"The only certainty was that we would lose some of that fluidity; it was fully expected and predicted. We also had two players on yellow cards and the referee seemed inclined to book them again, so I took them off."
Italy sit three points behind leaders France in Group A1, having improved following a 2-0 defeat to Belgium that began their Nations League campaign.
Their final two matches of the group in November will see them host France before travelling to Belgium, with the hopes of reaching the quarter-finals.
"We've got to continue like this; we'll probably have to play for our spot in Belgium," Mancini added.

"We suffered at the start, but the lads did well to get it back on track, score again after the 1-1, so it was a good game as the fourth in such a short spell of time.

"The only certainty was that we would lose some of that fluidity; it was fully expected and predicted. We also had two players on yellow cards and the referee seemed inclined to book them again, so I took them off."

Italy sit three points behind leaders France in Group A1, having improved following a 2-0 defeat to Belgium that began their Nations League campaign.

Their final two matches of the group in November will see them host France before travelling to Belgium, with the hopes of reaching the quarter-finals.

"We've got to continue like this; we'll probably have to play for our spot in Belgium," Mancini added.

11saz8tdl2qod1a8ck4tw8mtj9.title: Koge relishing Women's Champions League adventure after Arsenal edge out minnows
11saz8tdl2qod1a8ck4tw8mtj9.subtitle: Arsenal had 19 shots but hit the target just twice as they edged out minnows Koge in their opening Women's Champions League games.
paragraphs: Nadia Nadim says minnows Koge are simply relishing their Women's Champions League adventure following a narrow defeat to Arsenal.
The Gunners, European champions in 2025, clinched a 1-0 win over the Danish team, who are featuring in just their second Champions League campaign.
Mariona Caldentey's last-gasp penalty claimed the points for Arsenal, who were wasteful in front of goal.
Arsenal had 19 shots, but got just two of them on target, while they also hit the woodwork.
While Koge suffered late heartbreak, Nadim, who led the visitors' line, was thrilled with her team-mates.
"So proud of the team and the way we conducted ourselves, especially in the first half," she told ESPN on Disney+.

"We have a young team, a lot of them have no experience playing at this level, good for them to experience what it's like at this level. Good learning, disappointed they got the goal and penalty in the last minute. That's a part of the game, could've done better, but it's our first Champions League game and there's a lot of games left.
"We wanted to be compact and keep the ball, we had people who were comfortable with the ball. We changed in the last 30 minutes, and it didn't do us well because we couldn't get out of the pressure.
"Credit to Arsenal, great team, they find each other well. It's okay, happy for the young players to experience this.
"I enjoy the game. Physically, it's tough because you're so low, it becomes hard to be dangerous, takes a toll to try and get in the box the whole time.
"I love football, I love this game. It's nice to be back here. I always love the Champions League. Now we're a new team, let's see where this adventure will take us."
English sides are now unbeaten in their last 11 Champions League games against clubs from Denmark (W8 D3), since Arsenal’s 1-5 defeat to Fortuna Hjorring in the 2002-03 semi-final.
This win did see Arsenal snap a run of losing their opening Champions League fixtures in each of the past two seasons.
"We left it late," said Arsenal defender Steph Catley.
"It's tough at the moment and in the Champions League there are no easy games. They defended great, we didn't score early and it didn't come until the end.

"In the Champions League, you never think it's an easy day. I was expecting a tough game and it became really difficult but credit to the girls, they did everything and Mariona was very calm in that moment.

"It's hard to put your finger on it [what is going wrong], it is a bit of a slog and the goals are not coming as freely as they have in the past. It's not a lack of trying, we're doing everything we can to put the ball into the back of the net.

"We have great history in this competition and it's important we are in it every year and challenging to win. We have a real belief that we can go on and win it. It's a long season and we're working really hard so to get the wins early on is very important."
Elsewhere on Tuesday, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain drew 1-1.
Felicia Schroder opened the scoring for Madrid after just two minutes, but Sakina Karchaoui equalised from the penalty spot in the second half.

12fytptholf7i1erdgqmlacsmi.title: Australia friendlies the beginning of 'new generation' for Brazil, says Ancelotti
12fytptholf7i1erdgqmlacsmi.subtitle: Brazil face Australia in their first matches since exiting the World Cup, with Carlo Ancelotti making a string of changes to his squad.
paragraphs: Carlo Ancelotti says Brazil's friendlies during this international break should serve as the beginning for a "new generation", following their disappointing World Cup campaign.
Brazil were dumped out of the last 16 at this summer's World Cup by Norway, which was the earliest they had been eliminated from FIFA's flagship tournament since 1990.
Ancelotti has responded by making a raft of changes to his 26-man squad to face Australia (twice) and India, with Casemiro and Fabinho among the big names to miss out.
In fact, only Gabriel Magalhaes, Marquinhos, Bruno Guimaraes, Danilo Santos, Vinicius Junior, Raphinha, Endrick and Rayan remain from Brazil's World Cup contingent.
Ancelotti's selection is partly built around players who are also eligible for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, hoping he can use them as the spine of his squad for the 2030 World Cup.
The Brazil boss is expecting a tough test in Brazil's two friendlies against Australia, and he hopes they mark the start of the new era for the Selecao.
"It's difficult to say it's a friendly. For Brazil, it will never be a friendly game," Ancelotti said. "It will be an important game.
"A new season, we have a goal to find new players, to find a new generation of players for the World Cup and the Copa America. And we start the game tomorrow.
"I know that soccer in Australia is not the biggest sport. But they did really well [at the World Cup], and Tony [Popovic, Australia's coach] did a fantastic job.
"He organised a fantastic team, really compact, strong defensively, with a fantastic counter-attack. They won a fantastic game against Turkiye, then lost on penalties against Egypt.
"I think that in modern football, there are no easy games. You have to prepare well for the game; you have to respect the rival and do your best."
Australia come into the game fresh from reaching the World Cup knockout stages for the third time in their history, having lost on penalties to Egypt in the round of 32.
Tony Popovic is preparing Australia for the Asian Cup next January, at which point his contract is set to conclude.
It will be the first time that Ancelotti has managed a match in Australia, and he is looking forward to reuniting with Popovic, with whom he has a friendship with off the pitch.
"We are good friends," Ancelotti said of his relationship with Popovic. "Sometimes we have the possibility to meet to talk about football.
"We spent time together when I was in Milan; we spent time together in Brisbane. It's a pleasure to talk about football with him. He's doing a fantastic job here.
"A really passionate manager. I hope the best for him. I think the World Cup he had was a really good World Cup. The team showed strong quality, a compact team.
"We've had a fantastic reception, not only from the Brazilian community, but from all the people.
"The national team of Brazil is really respected everywhere in the world. [It's] my first time in Australia, so I'm trying my best to enjoy this beautiful country."

12n7mluytdhay182b4hp43ce2x.title: 'Fear doesn't exist' – Zidane relishing home debut as France boss
12n7mluytdhay182b4hp43ce2x.subtitle: Zinedine Zidane's first home match as France head coach comes against Italy in the Nations League, in a repeat of the 2006 World Cup final.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane is relishing what he believes will be a "very emotional" return to the Stade de France as he prepares for his first home match as France boss.
Les Bleus take on Italy in the Nations League on Friday, aiming to continue their perfect start in the competition.
After Kylian Mbappe helped secure a 1-0 win over Turkiye in their opener, Michael Olise's late stunner against Belgium clinched another 1-0 victory in the competition.
France completed 92.8% of their passes in the opponent's half against Belgium, their highest pass completion rate during a match over the last 20 years.
Zidane insists there is no fear ahead of his home debut, which he hopes to mark with an important win.
"It is very emotional being back here, and will be even more so when the stands are packed with fans," said Zidane in his press conference.
"Fear doesn't exist, otherwise I wouldn't be here. I've never thought about failure in my career. On the contrary, I see only opportunities.
"I have an incredible team, I'm ready to make the dream come true, and I'm going to give it my all."
France and Italy also met in the 2024-25 Nations League group stage, with the away side winning 3-1 on both occasions.
Zidane has a history with Italy; he infamously headbutted Marco Materazzi in the chest during the 2006 World Cup final, which the Azzurri won after Zidane was sent off.
"The images are being replayed everywhere on a loop, I've seen them," added Zidane.
"I haven't spoken to Materazzi since that day. I'm not proud of what I did. I've always said that, but at the same time, I have no regrets. It is part of my career.
"Fortunately, that is not all that I did in my career. There are positive and enjoyable moments, and I prefer to remember those. You can't just have a career of all great moments."

12vnvv8cqbur219mipd8ekmxq9.title: De la Fuente guarantees 'no complacency' from world champions Spain
12vnvv8cqbur219mipd8ekmxq9.subtitle: Spain face England in their first match since becoming world champions, and Luis De la Fuente remains as motivated as ever.
paragraphs: Luis De la Fuente has guaranteed "there will be no complacency" from his Spain side after becoming world champions.
Spain won their second World Cup after defeating Argentina in this summer's showpiece, with Ferran Torres scoring the only goal in a 1-0 victory.

La Roja are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest ever streak by a European nation, ahead of their Nations League opener against England at Wembley Stadium.
De la Fuente, who signed a new contract in recent weeks, insists his side can still improve as they chase more glory on the international stage.
"I guarantee there will be no complacency," said the Spain boss.
"I know these players; they want to keep winning and making history. It's the only way to achieve our goals.
"The drive to improve must be constant, and this team has it. This match will demand our absolute best.
"What we've done so far isn't enough, but this team has enormous room for improvement."
Spain have won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the final of the 2024 European Championship.
Their last away game vs the Three Lions also ended 2-1, at Wembley in the Nations League in September 2018.
When asked why England seem to falter in big matches, unlike Spain, De la Fuente chose to speak about the threat posed by Thomas Tuchel's side instead.
"I can only speak about what's happening to us; I don't know the inner workings of England," added De la Fuente.
"They're a great team, finalists in the last two European Championships and the World Cup. They're third in the FIFA rankings. A footballing superpower.
"Spain always tries to rise to the occasion in important matches. The game at Wembley will be against a very difficult opponent.
"We're currently in a moment of confidence and security, but any team can beat you, especially one like England."

12wp6fcugs0qg1dmw9ecnwclom.title: Chelsea's Estevao to 'seize every opportunity' after falling behind Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro
12wp6fcugs0qg1dmw9ecnwclom.subtitle: Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have shone as a front three for Chelsea this season, with Estevao playing a backup role.
paragraphs: Estevao is determined to "seize every opportunity" he gets at Chelsea, having found himself behind Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro in Xabi Alonso's pecking order.
The Brazilian arrived at Stamford Bridge from Palmeiras in 2025 and appeared 36 times across all competitions for the Blues in his debut season at Stamford Bridge.

Across those outings, 20 of which were starts, he scored eight goals and laid on three assists, while ranking second for dribbles attempted (133) and third for dribbles completed (58) among all players in Chelsea's squad, despite his relative lack of gametime.

The 19-year-old would have been hoping to kick on at the start of 2026-27, following Xabi Alonso's appointment as head coach, but he is yet to provide a goal involvement in six outings and has only started twice.
While Pedro Neto has found a new role at wing-back in Alonso's 3-4-3 system, the attacking trio of Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro have been highly impressive.
Of the Blues' 10 Premier League goals this season, only one – Romeo Lavia's opening goal in a 4-3 win over Brighton – has not involved at least one of that trio as the scorer or the assister.
Estevao understands the form of Chelsea's other attackers has limited his opportunities, but he hopes to make a big impression when he gets a chance.
"I think every coach has their own way of playing. Of course, we work every day, I give my best every day, and that's what I do," Estevao said at a press conference while on international duty.
"We have quality players at Chelsea, so what I do is focus on what I can control. I try to give my best in training. When I get an opportunity, I try to give my best, day after day.
"I try to seize every opportunity I have, control everything I can, and I leave it in God's hands, and I trust myself a lot, too."
Estevao has only played 148 minutes in all competitions for Chelsea this term, compared to 578 for Palmer and 552 for Rogers, with those figures making them the Blues' two most-used players.
Joao Pedro has played 377 minutes, having missed last Friday's 3-0 defeat to Brentford due to a knee issue.
That injury caused the striker to withdraw from Brazil's squad, but Estevao will hope to rack up some minutes when the Selecao face Australia (twice) and India in friendlies.

1353A34F9263AA99BB5F6F85641E5DE8.title: Jurgen Klopp’s new-look Germany yet to find their feet
1353A34F9263AA99BB5F6F85641E5DE8.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesJurgen Klopp’s new-look Germany yet to find their feetShareGermany are still reeling from their painful exit to Paraguay at the World Cup, and a third successive failure to reach the last 16.

In the immediate aftermath, it was clear change was imminent. Julian Nagelsmann resigned on July 3 and it wasn’t long before the German Football Association (DFB) intended to hold talks with former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund manager Jürgen Klopp regarding the vacant role.

Why would Klopp, who held a cushy position as Head of Global Soccer for Red Bull, wish to swap that life by returning to the stress of management? Was it a chance to restore national pride that made him take the job? Or was the itch to get back into the dugout simply proving too strong to resist?

Whatever the reason, the charismatic 59-year-old is back. His first target will be to lead Germany to Nations League glory next summer in what is a perfect warm up for the 2028 European Championships.
It hasn’t quite gone to plan thus far, though.
Euro 2028 may well be less than two years away, but there was plenty of optimism surrounding Klopp’s appointment that the Germans could pose a threat at the tournament – if he got things right.

Several nations changed managers following the World Cup, including Portugal, France, Netherlands, and Belgium. There are always likely to be a period of experimentation whenever a new man is at the helm, especially with a national side, but Klopp has gone one step further.
Indeed, the German opted to select 44 players for the four Nations League games, splitting them into two squads, each due to participate in two of their four Nations League fixtures.
“I want to get to know as many players as possible,” said Klopp during a press conference ahead of the matches.
“There is no A or B team. The squads are put together in a way that makes sense on the pitch and in terms of character and experience.”

The first set of players, which included the likes Nico Schlotterbeck, Jonathan Tah, Joshua Kimmich, Lennart Karl and Kai Havertz, were chosen to feature in the first two matches, while Florian Wirtz, Nick Woltemade and Aleksandar Pavlović were among those selected for the final two games.
Denis Undav and Leroy Sané – who both featured at the World Cup – missed out, with Klopp mixing experience with youth as 16 uncapped players were called up.

It looked as though Klopp was going to get off to a winning start against neighbours Netherlands in match one of the Nations League. A first half goal by Felix Nmecha had Germany well on their way to three points, before Cody Gakpo netted a late equaliser.
Still, a point away from home against arguably their biggest rivals for top spot was certainly encouraging.

Klopp’s first home tie in charge of Die Mannschaft came three days later – against Greece – and while his side dominated proceedings, recording 16 shots to Greece’s eight and finishing the game with 76% possession, the Greeks came away from the WWK Arena with a stunning 1-0 triumph.
Wirtz and Karim Adeyemi were drafted in early to the first squad due to injuries to Havertz and Jamal Musiala, yet neither could make the difference in the end.
Germany now occupy third place in Group 2, with matches against Serbia (home) and Greece (away) coming up over the next few days.
The key question now is, can Klopp’s B squad deliver a maiden victory?
Much will depend on the results against Serbia and Greece, but anything less than six points will surely be seen as a failure – both by Klopp himself, and those higher up in the DFB.
Germany were by far the more dominate team against the Greeks last time out, but failing to take chances is going to prove costly, no matter who it is against.

13q51g1bke3d3111iiywrd7opz.title: 'Ronaldo will never be forgotten' – Hojlund dedicates goal to 'idol' Cristiano
13q51g1bke3d3111iiywrd7opz.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal future is unclear, but Denmark's Rasmus Hojlund paid tribute to international football's record goalscorer.
paragraphs: Rasmus Hojlund paid tribute to his "idol" Cristiano Ronaldo in the best way he knew how.
Hojlund netted for Denmark against Portugal in the Nations League on Thursday.
Portugal went on to win 4-2, doing so in the absence of their iconic forward Ronaldo.
The 41-year-old sensationally left Portugal's squad earlier this week, reportedly due to a disagreement with coach Jorge Jesus over his game time.
Ronaldo's Portugal future is unclear, but former Manchester United striker Hojlund dedicated his goal to the five-time Ballon d'Or winner.
Hojlund mimicked Ronaldo's iconic 'siuuu' celebration, and explained he wanted to pay homage to his favourite player.
"I just wanted to dedicate my goal to my idol," Hojlund said.
"For everything Cristiano is going through at this point in his career, he will never be forgotten."
Ronaldo is the highest-scoring player in the history of international football, with 146 goals to his name.
He has netted 979 career goals in total.

Portugal went on to win 4-2, doing so in the absence of their iconic forward Ronaldo.

The 41-year-old sensationally left Portugal's squad earlier this week, reportedly due to a disagreement with coach Jorge Jesus over his game time.

Ronaldo's Portugal future is unclear, but former Manchester United striker Hojlund dedicated his goal to the five-time Ballon d'Or winner.

Hojlund mimicked Ronaldo's iconic 'siuuu' celebration, and explained he wanted to pay homage to his favourite player.

"I just wanted to dedicate my goal to my idol," Hojlund said.

"For everything Cristiano is going through at this point in his career, he will never be forgotten."

Ronaldo is the highest-scoring player in the history of international football, with 146 goals to his name.

He has netted 979 career goals in total.

13rfsg9b6p3sq19vkq2rgtc78d.title: Heavy workload led to Haaland substitution, says Solbakken
13rfsg9b6p3sq19vkq2rgtc78d.subtitle: Erling Haaland asked to be taken off against Portugal on Sunday, with Stale Solbakken revealing that fatigue played a big part in it.
paragraphs: Norway head coach Stale Solbakken revealed Erling Haaland's heavy workload led to him asking to be substituted against Portugal in the Nations League.
Haaland signalled to Norway's bench that he needed to be replaced in the 2-1 loss to the Group A4 leaders and was taken off in the 67th minute.
The striker started all four of the team's Nations League matches during the extended break, scoring three goals, though they all came in the first two games.
Haaland has also started all seven of Manchester City's games so far in all competitions, coming off the back of a summer in which he helped take Norway to the World Cup quarter-finals.
He was not moving freely before his substitution against Portugal, though Solbakken tried to allay injury worries ahead of Haaland's return to Manchester.
"He was tired against Wales," Solbakken said when asked about Haaland.
"That's why we had a heart-to-heart conversation [on Saturday]. We went through the possible options.
"He might have played the last 45 minutes against Portugal. That was a discussion. But he has very bad vibes and feelings about it. I am very pleased that he managed to pull out 60 good minutes.
"He's in the group that carries the heaviest workload — precisely because his team [City] plays in every tournament and he's the main man.
"It's tough. But we can't do anything about it. We just have to play the games we are called up for. It's tough.

"For those who play in the Champions League and have had little vacation, it's more brutal than for the others. Especially for the players who didn't get a vacation this summer because of the World Cup and that they came far. We did that."
Norway currently sit at the bottom of their Nations League group with only two games left to go: a home game against Wales before a trip to Denmark in November.
"The points haul is too poor," Solbakken added. "But there is no nut to crack.
"It's just a matter of continuing as we have done for a while, and which we have had great success with. We will get even more of that in the future if we have our best players with us."

13x92vs7xzx8b1hp7iojyveic9.title: Messi delivers emotional farewell ahead of final Argentina appearance
13x92vs7xzx8b1hp7iojyveic9.subtitle: Lionel Messi will make his final appearance for Argentina against Benin, and he has taken the time to thank the Albiceleste's supporters.
paragraphs: Lionel Messi penned an emotional tribute to the people of Argentina as he prepares to represent the national team for one final time in Buenos Aires.
Messi confirmed in August that he would draw the curtain on his stellar international career, following Argentina's 1-0 defeat to Spain in this summer's World Cup final.
The 39-year-old will make his 208th cap in a friendly against Benin. No player in Argentina's history has represented their country more times than Messi.
During his international career, which started in 2005, Messi has gone on to score 125 goals for Argentina, at least 69 more than second-placed Gabriel Batistuta.
He led Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022, while he has also won two Copa Americas and the Finalissima in that time.

Messi was included in a 28-man squad list published by the Argentine Football Association (AFA) for home friendlies against Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Benin during this international break, with it later confirmed Messi would only be present for the clash with Benin at Estadio Monumental.
And ahead of his goodbye, Messi paid tribute to the Argentina supporters.
"The moment has arrived. I leave in peace. I gave it my all. This shirt was my dream, my pride, and my life for years," Messi said.
"Thank you for loving me so much, thank you for your support. I will always carry you with me."

No player has directly contributed to more goals at the World Cup on record (since 1966) than Messi (33 – 21 goals and 12 assists), who has also featured in the most games at the finals (34) and most editions (six, level with Cristiano Ronaldo).

Messi's 12 assists in the competition are also the most of any player, while only Kylian Mbappe (22) has netted more often, though the Inter Miami star was the first to surpass Miroslav Klose's previous record of 16 this summer.
But the post-Messi era has begun strongly, with Argentina beating Bolivia 4-0 and Burkina Faso 7-0 across their two friendlies so far.

1429plvnrr9a91g86ly7cguppv.title: Saka: Seven-goal demolition of Croatia 'everything England were looking for'
1429plvnrr9a91g86ly7cguppv.subtitle: England crushed Croatia 7-0 in their third Nations League fixture on Saturday, with a performance Bukayo Saka felt was close to perfection.
paragraphs: Bukayo Saka said England's performance against Croatia was "everything we were looking for", after they made history with a staggering 7-0 win in Rijeka.
Saka joined Kane in scoring twice, while Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers were also on target on a memorable night for Thomas Tuchel's side.
England's win was their biggest over a team in the top 50 of the FIFA World Rankings since they were first published in 1992, while it was also the heaviest defeat in Croatia's history.

Croatia's previous worst result was a 6-0 Nations League defeat in Spain in 2018, while they had never previously lost a home game by more than a three-goal margin or conceded more than four goals in a match on their own turf, losing 4-1 to England in September 2008.

Kane, Gordon, Bellingham and Saka all scored in the first half, marking the first instance of four different England players netting before half-time in a single game since March 2013, when Frank Lampard, Jermain Defoe, Ashley Young and Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain did so in an 8-0 win over San Marino.
England now have six points on the board after three Nations League games, and a victory over Czechia on Tuesday would put them on the brink of qualifying for March's quarter-finals.
Speaking to ITV Sport after full-time, Saka praised the Three Lions for their relentless approach and their refusal to take their foot off the gas after half-time.
"It was an amazing night. We came out from the start and we were on top," he said. "We played with high energy, high spirit and we punished them.
"We enjoyed that performance. It was special and it was really fun to play in. We played with energy and we were really clinical today, which made the difference.
"Scoring two goals for England is always a nice feeling, so I'm really happy with that.
"I think we showed the hunger, passion and quality that we have. It was a mixture of everything. It's everything we were looking for, so we're really proud and we want to finish strongly on Tuesday.
"There's still three games left, but that will definitely give us a massive boost in confidence and momentum."
While Saka scored two right-footed goals in a game for the very first time in his senior career, on his 378th outing for club and country, it was Bellingham who truly stole the show.
He had three assists to go with his goal, becoming the first England midfielder to record four goal involvements in a game since David Platt scored four against San Marino in February 1993.
Bellingham, who was crowned England's Player of the Year for 2026 last month, created eight chances for team-mates.
No player has ever created more in a single top-tier game in the Nations League.
"He was amazing tonight, to be fair. He deserved to be our Player of the Year and he probably deserves Man of the Match tonight as well," Saka said of Bellingham.
"He was special. I'm so happy to play with him and to have him in the England team."

And Saka also heaped praise upon Gordon, who has been directly involved in a goal on each of his last five England appearances (four goals, two assists in total) – in the last 10 years, Kane is the only other player to achieve that feat for the Three Lions.
"He's another player who's also on fire in an England shirt," Saka said. "It's nice to have players like that around you, putting in performances like tonight."
