14f9ez1hoyyz21cti11qjbid9m.title: United States 3-0 Mexico: Sullivan overhauls Albert record in big win for Pochettino's men
14f9ez1hoyyz21cti11qjbid9m.subtitle: Mathis Albert was not the United States' youngest-ever goalscorer for long, as Cavan Sullivan overhauled him in a 3-0 win over Mexico.
paragraphs: Cavan Sullivan surpassed Mathis Albert as the United States' youngest-ever goalscorer – only four days after that record was set – in an eye-catching 3-0 win over 10-man Mexico.
Albert scored in Tuesday's 4-2 win over Chile at the age of 17 years and 131 days, but Philadelphia Union sensation Sullivan netted at 17 years and five days old on Saturday.
He was not the only young player to impress for Mauricio Pochettino's hosts in Glendale, either, with 18-year-old forward Julian Hall netting their 28th-minute opener.

After Santiago Gimenez passed up a huge early chance for Mexico, Hall was on hand to finish following some suspect goalkeeping from Raul Rangel, who found Malik Tillman's right-wing cross too hot to handle, following a lovely, disguised pass from Sebastian Berhalter.

Gimenez somehow steered wide with the goal gaping at the end of the first half, while his team-mate Roberto Alvarado was only denied by a reflex Diego Kochen stop early in the second, having thumped a volley goalwards on the swivel.

But the USA doubled their lead just beyond the hour mark, with a more glaring mistake from Rangel gifting Sullivan his first international goal. Under little pressure, he passed straight to the teenage midfielder, who immediately lobbed the goalkeeper from 35 yards out.
Things went from bad to worse for the visitors when Mateo Chavez was sent off for slapping Berhalter across the face, amid a melee prompted by his own late challenge on Yunus Musah.
And there was more self-inflicted pain for Mexico in the 84th minute as Tillman intercepted Alvaro Fidalgo's pass and lashed into the top-left corner.
Young Stars and Stripes shine again
Coming off the back of a traumatic World Cup elimination at the hands of Belgium in Seattle, this international break has proven very therapeutic for the USA.
Several new players have made the most of the opportunities handed to them by Pochettino, with Sullivan the latest – and the youngest – to do so.

The USA's youngest goalscorer record stood for just over 10 years between Christian Pulisic netting against Bolivia at 17 years and 253 days old in May 2016, and Albert overhauling him earlier this week.

But Albert's name was only in the record books for four days, with Sullivan capping a lively performance with a moment to remember. No USA player completed more dribbles than his three (from four attempted), while he won eight of his 11 duels in total.
The USA had lost each of their previous two games against Mexico, including the 2025 Gold Cup final, but they have now won six of the teams' last 10 meetings overall (D2 L2).

14qi2wh9aop4w1iaia6yqd00d6.title: Portugal 1-0 Wales: Joao Felix goal enough to give Jesus winning start
14qi2wh9aop4w1iaia6yqd00d6.subtitle: Portugal's first match under Jorge Jesus saw them beat Wales in the Nations League, but they were made to work for Thursday's victory.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus got his Portugal tenure up and running with a win as the defending Nations League champions began their 2026-27 campaign with a 1-0 victory against Wales.
Joao Felix struck the decisive blow in the first half at Estadio Jose Alvalade, though Wales had more than enough chances to at least claim a point away from home.
Portugal started brightly as Cristiano Ronaldo's first sight of goal saw him drag a shot wide, before Vitinha and Joao Felix had their efforts blocked by Wales' retreating defence.

The hosts had to wait until the 22nd minute for their first shot on target, and it resulted in a goal. Nuno Mendes skipped beyond Ethan Ampadu before laying the ball off to Joao Felix, who took a touch before seeing his attempt nestle into the bottom-left corner from the edge of the penalty area.
Ronaldo, in his quest to reach 1,000 career goals, then volleyed just wide before his tame effort after being found by Joao Felix was comfortably held by Danny Ward.

Portugal should have doubled their lead four minutes into the second half, but Ronaldo somehow turned Ruben Neves' cross over the bar, and he thought he had got his goal when he raced onto Bruno Fernandes' defence-splitting pass, only for it to be ruled out following a VAR check for offside.

But Wales spurned a glorious chance to draw level when Brennan Johnson ghosted in behind the Portugal backline and lofted an effort onto the crossbar, with Lewis Koumas' attempt on the rebound blocked off the line by Ruben Dias.

Daniel James and Mendes then fired wide at either end before substitute Goncalo Ramos stung the palms of Ward, with Portugal able to weather the Wales storm in the minutes that remained, getting themselves up and running in the Nations League.
Portugal fail to build on Joao Felix strike

With Wales missing several key players including Harry Wilson and Joe Rodon, many expected a comfortable outing for Portugal, and it looked as though it would be following Joao Felix's goal, which was his fifth in his last 10 starts for the Selecao.

He was teed up by the marauding Mendes, who registered his seventh assist for Portugal since the start of 2024. Overall, he's third for goal involvements in that time for his nation, behind Ronaldo (20) and Fernandes (17).

Portugal's 13 shots in the first half were also their most in the opening 45 minutes of a game since November 2025 against Armenia (17), but after the break, Wales looked the more likely to alter the scoreline.

Wales do, however, remain winless in their last five matches (D3 L2), their worst run under manager Craig Bellamy, but there will plenty of positives he can take from their performance ahead of facing Denmark in three days' time.

Jesus' side finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.36 from their 23 shots, only five of which were on target, compared to Wales' tally of 0.84 from their five attempts, with Portugal's next test seeing them take on Erling Haaland and Norway.

159b8hezyf6ze11g85cyffy3vo.title: 'I'm making the most of every moment' – Giroud admits retirement is close
159b8hezyf6ze11g85cyffy3vo.subtitle: Ahead of his 40th birthday, Olivier Giroud conceded his retirement is closer than ever, with the 2026-27 campaign likely to be his last.
paragraphs: Olivier Giroud has said this season will "very probably" be his last.
Giroud, now playing for Lille, will turn 40 on Wednesday and is seemingly set to call time on his career that began in 2005.
He has played for the likes of Arsenal, Chelsea, AC Milan and Los Angeles FC.
Giroud was also France's record goalscorer with 57 goals, earning the record at the 2022 World Cup, though it was beaten by Kylian Mbappe earlier this year.
"As a player, I think it is very probably my last season," he told L'Equipe. "That's why I'm making the most of every moment.
"I am at peace with myself and everything I have accomplished in my career. I feel more relaxed than ever.
"The goal is to enjoy every moment, to continue to find pleasure in what I do, what I love every day.
"Returning to France, making this choice after this long career as an expatriate abroad, has been one of the best decisions I've ever made."
Giroud won the 2018 World Cup with France and was also part of the squad that finished as runners-up at the 2022 edition, as well as the 2016 European Championships.
He made 137 appearances in total for Les Bleus with his last cap coming back in 2024.
At club level, the Frenchman has made 806 appearances across his career, scoring 303 goals, with 105 of those coming at Arsenal (253 games) – the most he has scored at any single club.
He also won league titles with Montpellier and AC Milan, as well as the Champions League and Europa League with Chelsea.

162qve87tj1fe1ffb7r6xmge7t.title: 'Full package' Kane deserves Ballon d'Or recognition, says Tuchel
162qve87tj1fe1ffb7r6xmge7t.subtitle: Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane is among the Ballon d'Or favourites, and he has the backing of his international manager.
paragraphs: England boss Thomas Tuchel firmly believes Harry Kane should win the Ballon d'Or this year, describing the striker as "the full package".
Kane is one of three players being tipped to contend for football's most prestigious individual award next month, alongside Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal.

That is off the back of a 2025-26 season in which he plundered 65 goals across all competitions for Bayern Munich, before hitting six more to help England finish third at the World Cup, the final tournament to fall in the 2026 Ballon d'Or eligibility period.
No other player from Europe's top five leagues scored more than 50 goals in all competitions last term, with Mbappe netting a half-century for Real Madrid.
But speaking in the build-up to England's 2026-27 Nations League opener against Spain on Saturday, Tuchel said Kane's game is about much more than his goals, highlighting his out-of-possession work.
Asked if Kane was his pick to be crowned the world's best player, Tuchel told ITV Sport: "Yeah. After this season, yeah.
"Seventy-plus goals [for club and country], three titles with Bayern Munich, the semi-finals at the World Cup and in the Champions League...
"He's getting better and better. I think he added a level of physicality to his match. He's just so committed to the high press and being involved in every part of the match.
"Be it in deep build-up, be it in finishing, be it in build-up play in the middle block, be it in defending. He's just the full package."

Last season, Kane recovered possession 124 times for Bayern, with 34 of those regains being in the final third. Those figures put him below Yamal (176 recoveries, 42 in final third) but ahead of Mbappe (65 recoveries, 30 in final third).
Kane also won 222 duels, less than Yamal's 381 but more than Mbappe's 162, and won 20 of his 28 tackles.
Yamal won 32 of 58 for Barcelona, while Mbappe – somewhat remarkably – only won two of six attempted tackles for Madrid, in 44 games.

After England fell short in the World Cup semi-finals, losing 2-1 to Argentina having gone ahead through Anthony Gordon's goal, many questioned whether Kane had played his final game at FIFA's showpiece tournament.
He will turn 37 shortly after the conclusion of the 2030 edition, which will be co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, but Tuchel feels he has every chance of featuring.
"Yeah, there's no problem," Tuchel said when asked about Kane's longevity. "Age is age. It doesn't matter. It's only about quality, and he has a long way to go."

After hosting Spain on Saturday, England continue their Nations League campaign away to Czechia next Tuesday, before visiting Croatia and welcoming Czechia back to Wembley Stadium for a swift return fixture.
England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine of those matches (D2).
However, one of those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0), with the other being away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).

          Croatia vs England Prediction: UEFA Nations League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 3, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Saturday's UEFA Nations League matchup with our Croatia vs England prediction and preview, as Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions look to make it back-to-back wins.
It's fair to say Croatia are familiar foes for England at this point.

A blistering second-half performance saw Thomas Tuchel's side overcome Croatia 4-2 in their opening game at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and they also beat the same opponents in their first match at Euro 2020 under Gareth Southgate.
Of course, the biggest meeting between the teams in recent years – in the semi-finals of the 2018 World Cup – went the way of Luka Modric and co.
With both teams on three points after two games in Group A3 of the UEFA Nations League, Saturday's clash at Stadion HNK Rijeka could be pivotal in the fight to make the last eight.
England needed a response after finishing on the wrong side of a five-goal thriller against Spain, and they got one against Czechia on Tuesday, helped by Pavel Sulc's first-half red card.

Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane were on target in a 2-0 win for the Three Lions, which was their sixth in their last eight Nations League matches (L2) across the top two tiers, scoring 20 goals in that span. That is more victories and goals than they managed in their first 18 games in the competition overall (W5 D6 L7, 18 goals).
It was also England's eighth straight away win in all competitions, giving them an opportunity to match a team record this weekend.
Only once have they ever won nine away games in a row, doing so under World Cup-winning manager Sir Alf Ramsey between December 1965 and October 1967.
And Kane – who smacked a penalty off the crossbar against Spain after losing his footing – has also enjoyed playing on the road lately, netting in each of his last five away games for England.

He could become just the fourth player to score in six consecutive away games for the Three Lions, after James Windridge (six from March to June 1908), Tom Finney (seven from September 1946 to May 1948) and Stan Mortensen (six from May 1947 to October 1948).

While Kane is almost a guaranteed starter, Tuchel has plenty of decisions to make elsewhere. Against Czechia, he handed Trent Alexander-Arnold his first England start since October 2024 (versus Finland), having made the more conservative choice to deploy Jarell Quansah at right-back against Spain.
Alexander-Arnold teed up Gordon's opener with a trademark delivery to the far post, which was also his first assist for his country since that Finland game under Lee Carsley.

Myles Lewis-Skelly has deputised capably for his Arsenal club-mate Declan Rice in midfield, but with Alex Scott winning his first senior cap off the bench in midweek and Morgan Gibbs-White also looking lively, Tuchel has plenty of options.
Slaven Bilic made a winning return to the Croatia dugout against Czechia last weekend, but a crushing 4-1 defeat to Spain brought them back to earth on Tuesday.

Croatia have now lost five of their 10 matches overall in 2026 (W5), just the third time they have suffered that many defeats in a single calendar year (also 2018 and 2020), though they have never previously lost six in one year.

Despite briefly getting back on level terms in the first half through Dion Beljo‘s first international goal, Croatia were well beaten by the world champions. They only attempted five shots to Spain's 16 and put up 0.47 expected goals (xG) to their opponents' 1.81.
They have only registered a lower xG figure in three previous Nations League fixtures – versus France in March 2025 (0.18), Sweden in November 2020 (0.3) and England in October 2018 (0.42).

Modric could return to the starting lineup after getting 10 minutes off the bench in Seville, while England's old nemesis Ivan Perisic has started both games in this international window. Perisic – who registered a goal and an assist against the Three Lions in that 2018 semi-final – has 15 goal involvements in his last 18 starts for Croatia (six goals, nine assists).

Eight years ago, Kieran Trippier‘s memorable fifth-minute free-kick in Moscow was cancelled out by Perisic's instinctive finish, before Mario Mandzukic sent Croatia through to the World Cup final with an extra-time winner, though they lost the final 4-2 to France.

16d97oet5l83c16w5c1p484jjt.title: Tuchel: Kane a one-off for England
16d97oet5l83c16w5c1p484jjt.subtitle: Harry Kane is just two appearances away from becoming England's joint-most-capped player, but Thomas Tuchel says the striker is a one-off.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel feels England are unlikely to see another striker of Harry Kane's level.
Kane is two games away from equalling Peter Shilton as England's all-time record appearance maker, on 125 caps.
The Bayern Munich forward is already England's record scorer, with 87 goals in 123 appearances for the Three Lions.
Kane has scored twice in England's last two games, although he did miss a penalty in last Saturday's 3-2 loss to world champions Spain.
The 33-year-old plundered 73 goals for club and country last season and Tuchel does not think there will be another forward of his ilk that comes along anytime soon.
"The highest level of goalscorer, of finishing," Tuchel said of Kane.
"He is the first one to push everyone and that is his mindset and he became a very, very hardworking forward on top of his finishing skills. He is a complete package."
Asked who could replace Kane once he retires, Tuchel said: "You will not get another Harry Kane, first of all.
"We look for different options and solutions. We finished the game with Jude [Bellingham] up front as a number nine.
"There will be someone else, but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry. We will find a solution when it comes to it but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years."
One possibility could be Jude Bellingham, who netted eight goals for England at the World Cup.
"I like him as a nine," Tuchel said of Bellingham. "Then he can contribute to both sides and overload the sides and doesn't affect so much of the balance.

"We found a bit of a new role for him in the last match, as a central 10, so he can go to both sides and it is more of a 4-2-3-1 than a 4-3-3 to have Harry and Jude closer together and to give them a chance to overload both sides. We are working on that.
"Jude in general should always be able to go through the last line and should always be able to end up in the box.
"He is a natural goalscorer and he has the hunger to be on the scoreboard. He wants to be there and have the decisive action, so it makes not a huge difference if he plays as a nine or a 10."

16ddte0k3n8vg1eorxrmyrc39r.title: Maresca can create 'siege mentality' at Man City, claims Mills
16ddte0k3n8vg1eorxrmyrc39r.subtitle: Danny Mills believes Enzo Maresca can use Manchester City's guilty verdict to his advantage by creating a "siege mentality" in the squad.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca can create a "siege mentality" off the back of Manchester City's guilty verdict, so says Danny Mills.
Earlier this week, the Premier League confirmed City had been found guilty of breaching the competition's financial rules across a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.
City still insist they are innocent and have pledged to fight the ruling and have until Friday to appeal it, while a sanctions hearing will take place separately.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said City had "systematically broken Premier League Rules for nearly a decade" and described the decision as the "most significant" in the competition's history.
Former City defender Mills, however, feels Maresca can use the situation to his advantage.

Mills told Stats Perform: "For Maresca, I think you can create that siege mentality and just go, 'Look, all we can do is do what we do now and get as many points as possible and just play football. You're all getting paid, lads. You're still getting paid. It's not a problem.'
"This is not going into administration and the club's going to go bust, and next week you might not have a contract, or you might not have a job.

"This is not like League Two when it was happening with Bury and things like that. Completely different scenario. So, ultimately, if the Manchester City owners weren't allowed to remain in charge, somebody would take them over.

"Wouldn't be a big problem for them. We've seen what's happened at Chelsea and everywhere else. So, yeah, I think you just have to say, look, 'Let's dig in, lads. It's the world against us. Let's just keep winning football matches and whatever stick we get, we're going to get and it's not our fault. It's not of our doing, but we're going to have to take it'."
Pep Guardiola has come out in support of City, while Rodri said last week that the players would not look back on their success at the club in a different light following this verdict.
In the years they have been found to have breached the rules, City won three Premier League titles, while they then went on to enjoy a period of dominance after 2018.
Mills, though, does not think any of the players who won titles at the club will be rushing to give away their medals.

He added: "[The Manchester City players] would not have been aware that there was effectively cheating going on or sports doping, whatever you want to call it. I'm not sure many of the managers did either.

"When you talk about Roberto Mancini going, 'Well, it wasn't my fault. Nothing to do with me.' Pep Guardiola has come out and been slightly, well, a lot more backing of the club, and he's got behind the club at this point.

"Obviously, there's an appeal process we expect that will happen in the near future. But it's hard as a player. I've seen some pundits say, 'They'll all be wanting to give their medals back.' No they won't. If they give their medals back, are they going to give back their bonuses, their contracts, their investments? No, it's not going to happen.

"The problem that you've now got is it's so far on from when it happened. It's going to be so difficult to punish those that were there at the time. Retrospective punishment is very, very difficult. You can only really punish now and going forward. And of course, that's a lot of the players who are at the football club who had nothing to do with this at all."
City sit top of the Premier League with a perfect record so far in 2026-27. They travel to Liverpool in their first game back after the international break.

176994dtvglxv169fdvjsxnrku.title: Croatia 1-2 Spain: Super-sub Merino inspires second-half comeback
176994dtvglxv169fdvjsxnrku.subtitle: Spain reached the quarter-finals of the Nations League after substitute Mikel Merino scored twice in their victory over Croatia.
paragraphs: Mikel Merino was Spain's hero from the bench as his double clinched a 2-1 win over 10-man Croatia in the Nations League.
Luis de la Fuente's side looked on course to see their long unbeaten run come to an end after Ivan Perisic's early goal, but Merino helped turn things around after the break.
Merino's two goals came either side of Perisic's red card, with his winning strike in the 88th minute ensuring Spain remained perfect from their four Group A3 matches.
Spain needed Unai Simon to come to their rescue in the 13th minute with a point-blank save to deny Josip Stanisic's towering header.
Croatia's pressure told in the 17th minute when Igor Matanovic's stinging shot was parried by Simon, with Perisic the quickest to react as he nodded in the rebound.

The hosts should have doubled their tally six minutes later when Simon's loose pass was picked off by Nikola Vlasic. He laid it off for Matanovic, but Spain's goalkeeper atoned for his error with a fine stop.

Spain's first attempt on target did not come until the stroke of half-time, but Mikel Oyarzabal's header was comfortably held by Dominik Livakovic, with Lamine Yamal then firing into the side-netting after he was picked out by Pedri's sensational pass.
De la Fuente brought on Merino at the break, and the Arsenal midfielder hauled Spain level just after the hour with a calm finish into the bottom-left corner.

From there, La Roja dominated proceedings as Yamal's deflected effort narrowly evaded the far post, but they were almost caught out at the other end when Martin Zubimendi's poor pass teed up Perisic, but his shot was straight at Simon.
But Croatia were forced to see out the final stages with 10 men when Perisic received his second yellow card after tripping Marc Cucurella, with the decision upheld by VAR.

And Spain made their advantage count when Merino brilliantly took down Zubimendi's ball into the area before hammering a left-footed strike into the top-left corner, sealing La Roja's progression to the quarter-finals.
Super-sub Merino proves his worth

With Spain struggling to create many chances in the final third during the first half, highlighted by their expected goals (xG) total of 0.57 from their five attempts, De la Fuente made the decision to replace Alex Baena for Merino, who turned the game on its head.

Merino has made a name for being a key player off the bench for Spain, and he has now scored six goals in 16 matches for La Roja as a substitute since the start of 2025. No player has netted more as a substitute for a European national team in that time.

The result also sees Spain's unbeaten run extend to 42 matches in all competitions (W32 D10), though there were some concerns for De la Fuente. The world champions have now conceded at least one goal in each of their last four official matches (five goals in total), their worst run of conceding since June 2025 (six matches).

It was also a mixed match for Perisic, who has been involved in five goals (two goals, three assists) in five matches against Spain, the most of any player against the nation over the last 20 years (level with Kylian Mbappe), before he was sent for an early bath for a needless coming together.
And though it was an improved performance from Slaven Bilic's side after their 7-0 thrashing by England, they came away empty-handed.
Croatia edged the xG battle with a total of 1.17 from their 10 shots, compared to Spain's tally of 1.08 from the same number of attempts.

The result also sees Spain's unbeaten run extend to 42 matches in all competitions (W32 D10), though there were some concerns for De la Fuente. The world champions have now conceded at least one goal in each of their last four official matches (five goals in total), their worst run of conceding since June 2025 (six matches).

It was also a mixed match for Perisic, who has been involved in five goals (two goals, three assists) in five matches against Spain, the most of any player against the nation over the last 20 years (level with Kylian Mbappe), before he was sent for an early bath for a needless coming together.

And though it was an improved performance from Slaven Bilic's side after their 7-0 thrashing by England, they came away empty-handed.

Croatia edged the xG battle with a total of 1.17 from their 10 shots, compared to Spain's tally of 1.08 from the same number of attempts.

176mwh9ppzb461d508p2ihc5h0.title: Shaw disappointed by Man City's slow start in draw with Madrid
176mwh9ppzb461d508p2ihc5h0.subtitle: Manchester City are still winless after two Champions League games, and Khadija Shaw felt a slow start cost them versus Real Madrid.
paragraphs: Khadija Shaw said Manchester City were disappointed with the way they started against Real Madrid and felt they should have won the game, even if the Spanish giants were denied a late winner by referee Silvia Gasperotti.
Having drawn 2-2 with Bayern Munich in their 2026-27 Champions League opener last week, City were again forced to settle for a point on Thursday, drawing 1-1 on home soil.

Linda Caicedo fired into the far corner to put Madrid in front in the 29th minute, and City could have few complaints at being behind at half-time, having only attempted five shots to their visitors' 11.
However, City came out stronger following the interval, drawing level when Shaw finished on the turn, having been fed by Yui Hasegawa in the 51st minute.

City ended the game with 1.69 expected goals (xG) to Madrid's 0.89, with both teams having 16 shots apiece, although visiting head coach Pau Quesada was furious to see Silvia Cristobal's late strike disallowed, with Gasperotti having already blown the whistle after the official inadvertently blocked Beth Mead on the edge of the City area.
And Shaw felt City would have won the match if they had produced their second-half level throughout the full 90 minutes.
"I think when you look at the game, we tried in the second half much better than we started the first, and I think that's one thing we're going to look at as a team," Shaw told Disney+.
"We're disappointed that we didn't win the game, but we definitely fought until the end and that's good.
"I think with our pressing, we gave them a lot more time in the first half. In the second half, we stuck in and pressed them higher up the pitch and that caused a lot of errors from them.
"I think if we had done that in the first half, it would've been a different game."
Reflecting on her goal, Shaw added: "When I'm in the box, I try to stay calm, with the players I have around me, that's something we try to build in training.
"Sometimes it doesn't come, but more often than not, they look for me. I try to stay calm, stay level-headed and focus on where the goal is.
"With the centre-backs I'm up against, it depends on what they give me. If they give me time and space, I know I can turn and get a shot off."
Thursday's draw ended City's seven-match winning run on home soil in the Champions League, which was the longest ever recorded by an English team in the competition.
Madrid have still won just one of their 10 Champions League games against English sides in the competition, though (D3 L6), beating Arsenal 2-0 in the 2024-25 quarter-finals.
Their win rate against WSL teams stands at 10%, making it their worst against teams from a specific country in the competition (minimum three games played).

17a93nv5v0pw1hjocx7gd3tbn.title: Klopp says Germany can do better after ill-tempered Netherlands draw
17a93nv5v0pw1hjocx7gd3tbn.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp's first match in charge of Germany, a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands, was marred by injuries to Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp was satisfied with a point on his debut as Germany's head coach, although he knows his side have plenty more gears to go through after their 1-1 draw with the Netherlands.
Felix Nmecha's 32nd-minute strike put Germany on course for victory against their old rivals on Thursday, on Klopp's eagerly anticipated international debut in the Nations League.

However, two minutes into second-half stoppage time, Cody Gakpo – who played 79 games under Klopp for Liverpool, scoring 23 goals in that time – met Ruben van Bommel's outside-of-the-foot cross with a sumptuous volley to snatch a point for the Netherlands.
The Oranje, who were playing their first game under Barcelona great Xavi, utterly dominated the second half, racking up 2.61 expected goals to Germany's 0.24 xG after half-time.
Overall, the Netherlands posted an xG figure of 3.12 from 22 shots, compared to Germany's 1.5 from 10 attempts, while they also had four Opta-defined 'big chances', with Klopp's men having two.

It was the first time the Oranje had created 3.0 xG or greater in a match against a team inside the top 30 of FIFA's world rankings since June 2019, when they had 3.1 in a Nations League semi-final win over England.
Speaking to RTL after full-time, Klopp acknowledged there was plenty for his team to work on ahead of Sunday's matchup with Greece, but his initial assessment was still positive.
"There were lots of things that worked. I'm very satisfied with many individual performances, with the passion as well," he said.
"But we can play better football, for sure. I would have loved to win, but I can live with the point."
Asked if he was nervous ahead of the game, Klopp replied: "I stood there over 1,000 times, so it was quite natural."

A high-octane and at times bad-tempered affair saw the Netherlands have two goals disallowed, with the first – a Virgil van Dijk header that was chalked off for Brian Brobbey backing into Marc-Andre ter Stegen – proving contentious.

And Germany's goal also came with a hint of controversy as Klopp's side played on while Brobbey was down injured, with the Netherlands' players reacting furiously after Nmecha swept into the top-left corner.

Brobbey had to be substituted when the game restarted, and his exit came after Germany striker Kai Havertz also hobbled off, having been on the receiving end of a high tackle from Quinten Timber – the twin brother of his Arsenal team-mate Jurrien.
Germany also lost Jamal Musiala to a thigh issue during the warm-ups, and Klopp is now waiting for updates on both players.
"Unfortunately, this happened to Jamal before the game, then Kai also said he felt it. They are both having an MRI at the moment. I hope we get the diagnosis tonight," he said.
"Of course, it's not great now. I hope it's just nothing bad. The boys are probably out of our next game, but hopefully they'll be ready to play again quite quickly."

17krq7bj4h1kr121kdkw5s68ve.title: Seattle Sounders 2-0 Real Salt Lake: Musovski and Rusnak end long winless streak
17krq7bj4h1kr121kdkw5s68ve.subtitle: Seattle Sounders had not tasted victory since mid-May, but they got three points on the board against a struggling Real Salt Lake side.
paragraphs: Seattle Sounders ended their long wait for a win in MLS as they beat Real Salt Lake 2-0 at Lumen Field.
The Sounders had not won a league game since May, but Paul Arriola got two assists to set up Danny Musovski and Albert Rusnak to secure all three points.
Arriola flashed an early shot just wide of the near post and into the side netting after the Sounders cut through RSL's defense.
Cristian Roldan also failed to hit the target, while RSL's only effort of the first half saw Sergi Solans bend a long-range shot well wide of the far post on the stroke of half-time.

But Seattle made a strong start after the break, taking just over two minutes to break the deadlock. Arriola laid it off to Musovski, whose low fizzer trickled past Rafael Cabral into the back of the net.

Solans forced a fine stop out of Andrew Thomas moments later from a tight angle, but Seattle continued to push, with Jordan Morris' effort – which could have been a cross – from the right of the box pushed away by Cabral.
A loose touch from Philip Quinton almost gifted Arriola a goal; the striker rushed onto the ball in the box, but Cabral rushed back to get his foot behind it.
Rusnak made sure of the points with 17 minutes remaining, though, as he was allowed to run through RSL's half before slotting it past Cabral.
Seattle taste victory again
After a strong start to the season, Seattle have slowly been sliding down the Western Conference table after failing to taste victory since a 3-2 win over the San Jose Earthquakes on May 13.

But on Wednesday, they ended a winless run of 13 straight MLS matches (D5 L8). They had lost eight straight before drawing each of their last five – including coming from 3-1 down to earn a point against the Colorado Rapids last time out.

The clear-cut chances were few and far between in the match, with the Sounders accumulating 0.91 expected goals (xG) from their 11 attempts, though four were on target. While RSL had 12 shots (0.43 xG), only two tested Thomas.
Arriola was the driving force, having a joint-game-high three shots and the only 'big' chance of the match, while he also got an assist from both of the chances he created.
While Seattle moved up to 10th in the West, level on points with the Portland Timbers, RSL sit 13th after extending their own winless run to 13 games, having lost each of the last four.

17m3llo12rkmq1obwgma87yxeo.title: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami: Messi free-kick not enough to halt winless run
17m3llo12rkmq1obwgma87yxeo.subtitle: Inter Miami are now winless in five MLS games after falling to a late 2-1 defeat against the Columbus Crew on Sunday.
paragraphs: Jamal Thiare scored a 98th-minute winner for the Columbus Crew in a 2-1 victory over Inter Miami at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.
Lionel Messi cancelled out Josef Martinez's penalty with a brilliant free-kick in the first half, but Thiare snatched a last-gasp winner shortly after Santiago Morales saw red for Miami.
Columbus started on the front foot as Anass Zaroury saw a strike from the edge of the box cannon off the woodwork 10 minutes in, though the Crew would take the lead just before the half-hour mark.
Yannick Bright wrestled with Martinez during a corner, with the latter winning the penalty and dispatching it for his first MLS goal for Columbus.
However, Miami were level just five minutes later as Messi scored a stunning free-kick from the right wing, curling the ball over Patrick Schulte and into the far corner.
The Herons struggled to create chances in the second half, while Zaroury struck the frame of the goal twice more as Columbus pushed for all three points.

And the hosts eventually struck in stoppage time; two minutes after Morales received a second yellow card for time-wasting, Thiare reacted fastest to a rebound after Rocco Rios Novo spilled the initial effort from Brais Mendez.
Miami given reality check by improving Columbus
Miami have won more points on the road than any other side in the Eastern Conference this season (27), but other than a moment of magic from Messi, they looked lost against Columbus.
While restricting the Herons to just 0.27 expected goals (xG) from five shots, the Crew registered 1.87 of their own, while also hitting the woodwork three times through Zaroury.

Messi, perhaps unsurprisingly, led Miami in shots (three) and chances created (two), but his team-mates failed to add any threat of their own, with Morales's two yellow cards soon after coming off bench summing up a poor performance.
Miami are now winless in five MLS games (D4 L1) and at risk of tumbling down the East, while back-to-back wins have moved Columbus closer to the play-off spots.

17sz9pe33kr6z1gvr1wj1fbhrh.title: Australia 2-4 Brazil: Raphinha and Vinicius score penalties in absorbing Brisbane friendly
17sz9pe33kr6z1gvr1wj1fbhrh.subtitle: Following a 1-1 draw between the teams last Friday, Brazil got the better of Australia in a six-goal thriller to cap their tour Down Under.
paragraphs: Raphinha and Vinicius Junior were both on target from the penalty spot as Brazil beat Australia 4-2 in a thrilling friendly encounter in Brisbane.

Carlo Ancelotti made seven changes to the Selecao lineup that drew 1-1 with the same opponents in Townsville four days prior, but three of those who kept their places – Raphinha, Vinicius and Bruno Guimaraes – got on the scoresheet in an entertaining win.

Brazil had to wait until the 95th minute for Rayan's equaliser on Friday, but they made the breakthrough far quicker this time around as Vanderson's touch sat up perfectly for the full-back to thump a volley across Patrick Beach and in with three minutes gone, after Gabriel Bontempo laid the ball back into his path.
Beach then repelled two efforts from Raphinha as Brazil's furious start threatened to overwhelm Australia, but the hosts grew into the encounter and equalised in the 28th minute.

Connor Metcalfe's inswinging corner somehow travelled all the way through to Alessandro Circati, who hooked his right foot behind him and sent an instinctive flick looping into the far corner. Referee Yusuke Araki initially awarded a foul on Brazil goalkeeper Otavio, but a VAR review led to that decision being overturned.
And the Socceroos were ahead only five minutes later, as a flowing move resulted in Metcalfe exchanging passes with Circati and sending a glorious, 20-yard strike dipping into the top-right corner.
However, Brazil got back on level terms just before half-time, with Raphinha planting his spot-kick into the bottom-right corner after Danilo Santos was tripped by Harry Soutter.

And, after Gabriel Magalhaes' header was kept out by Beach, Guimaraes put Brazil back in front in the 69th minute, sweeping into a gaping net after Vinicius linked up with his Real Madrid team-mate Endrick in the left-hand channel.

Another driving run from Vinicius led to him being felled by Nestory Irankunda, and with Raphinha having been substituted at half-time, the Madrid superstar became the second Brazilian to convert from the spot 10 minutes from time, finally putting the game out of Australia's reach.
Vinicius leads the way, but defensive issues remain for Brazil
Ancelotti's side were far from their free-flowing best at this summer's World Cup, as they were beaten by Norway in the round of 16.
And after Australia came within seconds of upsetting them in the first of two friendly matches between the sides, the Italian came in for more criticism from the Brazilian media.
However, his side looked much brighter in attack on Tuesday, putting up 3.62 expected goals from 18 shots, compared to Australia's 1.65 xG from eight attempts.

Vinicius was at the heart of everything positive about Brazil's play, tallying game-high figures for dribbles attempted (four), touches in the opposition area (seven) and chances created (two, joint with Bontempo).

Brazil still have defensive issues to solve ahead of Saturday's meeting with India, though. This was the first instance of Australia both scoring and conceding multiple goals before half-time in any game since a 2-2 draw with Saudi Arabia in June 2017.
The Socceroos also become just the second team from the AFC confederation to score twice against Brazil in a game in the last 21 years, after Japan beat the Selecao 3-2 last October.

17wh48u3h3xx2z5rkewiybzp9.title: Yildiz compared to Kvaratskhelia by Juventus boss Spalletti
17wh48u3h3xx2z5rkewiybzp9.subtitle: Luciano Spalletti has compared Juventus youngster Kenan Yildiz to another big-name attacker he coached while at Napoli.
paragraphs: Kenan Yildiz has the unpredictability and "madness of invention" that makes him comparable to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, says Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti.
Juventus went into the international break seventh in a congested Serie A table, having beaten Atalanta 2-0 to bounce back from a 3-2 defeat to Sassuolo.
Yildiz has only made one appearance, totalling 69 minutes, across all competitions this season, after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured metatarsal in August.
The Turkiye international, who is unlikely to return until next month, scored 14 goals and supplied 10 assists last season, leading all Bianconeri players in both categories.
He also created the most chances (100) and both attempted (220) and completed (105) the most dribbles for the Turin giants, leading Spalletti to compare him to another tricky attacker he has managed.

Spalletti worked with Kvaratskhelia – now a two-time Champions League winner with Paris Saint-Germain – in 2022-23 after the Georgian first joined Napoli, and he provided 14 goals and 14 assists that season as the Partenopei won the Scudetto.
"Yildiz makes football shine," Spalletti told Tuttosport. "His every move is ingenious and breaks the system.
"When he starts, even he doesn't necessarily have a plan of what he'll do next. Sometimes, in training, I see the defenders predict his movement, and they still can't stop him.
"He has the madness of invention. For me, he is comparable to Kvaratskhelia.
"He needs to play a bit more, but I see similarities in the unpredictability, the way he stays outside of the rules and timing you expect in football.
"He's a lovely guy, the boy next door type, but also a leader – one that doesn't need to talk much."
Juventus return to action following the extended international break next Sunday, as they visit a Cagliari side that currently sit one point above them in the table.

He also created the most chances (100) and both attempted (220) and completed (105) the most dribbles for the Turin giants, leading Spalletti to compare him to another tricky attacker he has managed.

Spalletti worked with Kvaratskhelia – now a two-time Champions League winner with Paris Saint-Germain – in 2022-23 after the Georgian first joined Napoli, and he provided 14 goals and 14 assists that season as the Partenopei won the Scudetto.

"Yildiz makes football shine," Spalletti told Tuttosport. "His every move is ingenious and breaks the system.

"When he starts, even he doesn't necessarily have a plan of what he'll do next. Sometimes, in training, I see the defenders predict his movement, and they still can't stop him. 

"He has the madness of invention. For me, he is comparable to Kvaratskhelia. 

"He needs to play a bit more, but I see similarities in the unpredictability, the way he stays outside of the rules and timing you expect in football. 

"He's a lovely guy, the boy next door type, but also a leader – one that doesn't need to talk much."

Juventus return to action following the extended international break next Sunday, as they visit a Cagliari side that currently sit one point above them in the table.

17y7t7f444xak1dh65qfruca6b.title: LAFC sack Dos Santos amid MLS struggles
17y7t7f444xak1dh65qfruca6b.subtitle: After just one win across their last 10 MLS games, Los Angeles FC have sacked head coach Marc Dos Santos ahead of an important run.
paragraphs: Los Angeles FC have sacked head coach Marc Dos Santos after a poor run of form in MLS.

Dos Santos was appointed to the role in December 2025 after serving as an assistant under previous boss Steve Cherundolo, but has been relieved of his duties after just 38 games in charge across all competitions.
The 49-year-old won 17 of his 38 games at the helm (D11 L10), with his 44.7% win rate the lowest of any LAFC head coach since their first match in 2018 (Cherundolo – 53.9%, Bob Bradley – 47.2%).
LAFC made a strong start to the 2026 season, but have fallen to sixth in the Western Conference after just one win across their last 10 games in the league (D5 L4).

The Black and Gold are now closer to eighth-place rivals LA Galaxy (five points) than they are to conference leader Vancouver Whitecaps (nine points), and they are very much at risk of missing out on home-field advantage for the play-offs.
With just six games to go before the postseason, LAFC have decided to part ways with Dos Santos.

“Marc has given a great deal to this club over the years, and we are grateful for his commitment, care and contributions to LAFC. We wish Marc and his family all the best moving forward," said John Thorrington, LAFC's president of soccer operations.
After the international break, LAFC host Vancouver and Austin FC before a trip to New York City FC.
The club are yet to name an interim boss, despite the play-offs now looming on the horizon.

18217lohamyel1k5rtcqbrvn2x.title: Hallgrimsson says rotation has kept Ireland fresh for Israel rematch
18217lohamyel1k5rtcqbrvn2x.subtitle: Ireland end their extended international break with a rematch against Israel, and Heimir Hallgrimsson believes his players are ready to go.
paragraphs: Heimir Hallgrimsson hopes his policy of shuffling Ireland's pack will ensure his players are raring to go when they face Israel in their final game of the international break on Sunday.

Ireland sit third in Nations League Group B3 with four points from their opening three games, having lost 1-0 to Kosovo, beaten Israel 3-0, then squandered a 2-0 lead to draw 2-2 with Austria on Thursday.
Troy Parrott scored twice for the Boys in Green last time out, with the first of his goals being an exceptional solo effort.

Parrott's four braces for Ireland are the most by any player aged under 25 for the country, surpassing Robbie Keane's three, and the Real Betis forward has nine goals in his last six competitive internationals overall.

He was one of several big names to be withdrawn by Hallgrimsson in the latter stages of Thursday's game, allowing Austria to play their way into the contest, but the 59-year-old insists those changes were necessary in order to keep everyone fresh for their next match.
"We need to think about this as a four-game window. Like we said in the beginning, we will rotate and we have been using our squad really well in these games," he said.
"We were always thinking about more than just that [Austria] game, but not on purpose – we didn't want to lose two goals in the end.
"But obviously, we had to think about the fact we are playing another game, both for players to avoid injuries and to be fit and fresh."

Ireland's draw with Austria was interrupted by protests relating to the staging of this Sunday's fixture – which will take place on neutral ground in Backa Topola, Serbia – and Hallgrimsson admits the extra scrutiny his team have faced during recent days has taken its toll.
But he hopes the experience of coming through a tough period will benefit Ireland in the long run.
"Surviving this camp, coming out of it together as one would be a massive win for me. That is coming from my heart," he said.
"After everything this team has gone through, the criticism, surviving as a group after this game would be a big win for me.
"As a coach, obviously having another three points would probably be more than I could have asked for before the camp, knowing what was to come.
"The most pleasing thing has been the togetherness and what they have done for each other. This bond of brothers will be stronger than others. All the obstacles we face in the future will be less."

18kaq92nmwrzf1g1gvjiraypwh.title: Ter Stegen says Klopp call-up was extra special following injury woes
18kaq92nmwrzf1g1gvjiraypwh.subtitle: Marc-Andre ter Stegen has already been named as Jurgen Klopp's Germany number one, after more than a year in the international wilderness.
paragraphs: Marc-Andre ter Stegen says being named as Jurgen Klopp's first-choice goalkeeper for Germany was extra special, following his well-documented injury issues.

Germany will face the Netherlands in their first match under Klopp on Thursday, in the Nations League, with further games against Greece (home and away) and Serbia to come during this international break.
And, with Manuel Neuer retiring from international football in the aftermath of Germany's shock round-of-32 World Cup defeat to Paraguay, the former Liverpool boss had to name a new number one.
Despite calling up Besiktas' Alexander Nubel, Bayern Munich's Jonas Urbig, Eintracht Frankfurt's Noah Atubolu and Augsburg's Finn Dahmen, he has gone with the experience of Ter Stegen.
The most recent of Ter Stegen's 44 caps came against France in the previous edition of the Nations League in June 2025, with injuries restricting his gametime in recent years.
He only made 10 appearances across all competitions combined in 2024-25 and 2025-26, for parent club Barcelona and Girona, who he joined on loan for the second half of last season.
But, after starting eight straight games for his latest loan club, Ajax, Ter Stegen is excited to be back on the international stage.

"It's always something special for me, to be here again now," he told Sky Sport DE. "Especially if you had a time when things didn't go the way you imagined, when your body wasn't by your side, then of course, you appreciate it all the more.

"I believe that I have worked a lot to make this happen again. I'm also looking forward to meeting many new faces, some old friends who are here, and just to start again and give our best for the team.
"There's a smile on my face. I'm just happy to be 100% back, to be able to be with the national team and hopefully play successful football. That is the wish of all of us."

Klopp takes charge of his country after overseeing 674 games in the Bundesliga and the Premier League, across wildly successful spells with Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool. That is more games in Europe's top five leagues than any previous Germany head coach had tallied before taking the job.
Ter Stegen said of Klopp: "He's one of one, as you know, with the joy he conveys and his interest in football, the enthusiasm he has for his own football.
"I don't think you need to say anything. I think everyone knows him and everyone knows how much he lives and feels football."

Klopp is one of only three bosses – alongside Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti – to have won the Bundesliga and Premier League titles, and he became famed for his "heavy metal" style of play with both Dortmund and Liverpool.

But Ter Stegen knows adopting that way of playing will be a learning curve for Germany, adding: "There are issues he would like to tackle, because he has his way of seeing football and understanding football. We have to try to internalise that as quickly as possible.

"For the time being, there are smaller levers that can and must be pulled, to then get into his philosophy. We want to play great football from the start, to defend not through individual actions, but really through the collective.
"We have very few training sessions to talk a lot about gameplan and so on, so we will keep it relatively simple now. We have to be attentive and implement that as quickly as possible."

18kqj4ll7crqczd8mfxkvej68.title: Branthwaite hopes injury issues are behind him following England recall
18kqj4ll7crqczd8mfxkvej68.subtitle: Injuries have restricted Jarrad Branthwaite to just one senior cap for England, but he will hope to add to that tally in the next two weeks.
paragraphs: Jarrad Branthwaite hopes he is back in the England setup for good after missing Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup, having earned a recall to the Three Lions' squad.
Branthwaite has been named in Thomas Tuchel's group for Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia (who they face both home and away) and Croatia.

He has been an ever-present for Everton so far this season, helping the Toffees keep three clean sheets in five games and concede the joint-fewest goals in the Premier League (three, alongside Leeds United).

Branthwaite won his only senior England cap to date in June 2024, when he was named in Gareth Southgate's preliminary Euro 2024 squad and appeared in a friendly against Bosnia-Herzegovina, only to miss out on the final party.
The 24-year-old also missed this summer's World Cup after an injury-hit 2025-26 season, in which he was restricted to just 10 Premier League appearances and seven starts.

But, having visited a specialist in Germany in a bid to combat his persistent hamstring issues during the off-season, Branthwaite hopes he can now challenge Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa for an England starting spot.
"Being out for such a long time with injury didn't help, missing three or four of the camps and missing a lot of football," Branthwaite said of his England struggles.
"My aim is to stay injury-free and play as many games as I can and keep giving myself the best possible chance to be in the squad.
"I've not spoken to him [Tuchel] recently. When we get there, we'll have a chat. I can't wait to join up with the squad and enjoy the couple of weeks.

"It is a proud moment. In the last season or so, it has been a target of mine when I've been out to get back playing and give myself the best possible chance of being in and around the England squad after missing a length of time.
"The season has started well individually and as a team and that has definitely helped. I believe I am good enough to be in the England squad, so hopefully I can show that."

Branthwaite, Guehi, Konsa, Jarell Quansah and Trevoh Chalobah are the centre-backs in England's group for this international break, with their Nations League opener against world champions Spain taking place at Wembley on Saturday.
England have won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of their last five without conceding.
Only once before have the Three Lions won six competitive home fixtures to nil, doing so between March 2015 and March 2017.
However, Spain are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest ever streak by a European nation.

18t5sflp7wkw1042382wl9t50.title: Klopp not anticipating more titles following Man City verdict
18t5sflp7wkw1042382wl9t50.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool were one of the teams that ran Manchester City close in several Premier League title races.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp is not readying himself to receive more titles retrospectively in the wake of Manchester City's guilty verdict.
It was confirmed on Tuesday that an independent commission had found Man City guilty on the vast majority of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League.
The charges, which were made in 2023, relate to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules across a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.
It has been found that City's breach amounted to around £900m.
During the period in question, City won three Premier League titles. However, it also paved the way for what was to come under Pep Guardiola.
In 2018-19, City won their fourth Premier League crown, and their second under Guardiola, by finishing one point ahead of Klopp's Liverpool.
That sparked a thrilling rivalry between City and the Reds, with Liverpool winning the title in 2020 and pushing Guardiola's juggernaut close again in 2022.

With a plethora of punishments open to the commission at an upcoming sanctions hearing, there has been a suggestion City could have titles stripped, but Klopp is not expecting to receive a retrospective winners' medal.
"I haven't given it much thought, even though I've seen it of course," said the Germany boss.

"Should any sanctions be imposed, I naturally have nothing to do with it anyway, and that's why I'm waiting to see how things pan out. But when you're talking about legal proceedings that have been going on for so long now, I assume there will be an appeal or something like that? That will take ages again of course.
"So I'm a long way from preparing myself for it in any way and I don't have any feelings about it."
City insist they are innocent and are expected to appeal the verdict.
Their next Premier League outing is against Liverpool at Anfield on October 11.

18wa22x9ciuea1k1fgkud5wunp.title: Muller extends Vancouver stay through 2027 MLS Sprint Season
18wa22x9ciuea1k1fgkud5wunp.subtitle: After helping the Vancouver Whitecaps reach their first MLS Cup final last season, Thomas Muller has extended his stay in Canada.
paragraphs: Thomas Muller has extended his contract with the Vancouver Whitecaps through to the end of the 2027 MLS Sprint Season.
The 37-year-old's previous deal was set to expire this December, but he will now remain with the 2026 MLS Cup runners-up until June 2027.
Muller has scored 19 goals and provided 12 assists in 45 appearances for the Whitecaps since joining as a free agent in the summer of 2025.
Since his arrival, Muller leads Vancouver players in direct goal contributions (27 – 16 goals, 11 assists) in MLS.
During his first campaign, Vancouver reached the MLS Cup showpiece for the first time, though they lost to Lionel Messi's Inter Miami, while they won the Canadian Championship.
The Whitecaps are leading the Western Conference this season, with Muller named an MLS All-Star earlier in the year.
"I've really enjoyed my time here from the beginning," Muller told the club website.
"Vancouver has been very open and welcoming to me, and I've felt that same spirit throughout the club.

"We have an offensive, possession-based style that is fun to play and fun to watch, and you can really feel the excitement around the team and the city right now. The fans are enjoying it, and I think everyone wants to be part of what we are building.
"For me, it's still so much fun to be out on the pitch every week, and I feel good physically.
"I'm very happy to continue this journey with the 'Caps, and I'm looking forward to what we can achieve together this year and next year in the Sprint Season."

194kvzunupcho1w6yo91gg0suu.title: Bompastor will not risk James in Champions League as Arsenal clash looms
194kvzunupcho1w6yo91gg0suu.subtitle: Chelsea open their Women's Champions League campaign against Austria Wien, but with Arsenal next up in the WSL, squad rotation is likely.
paragraphs: Chelsea will not take any risks with Lauren James against Austria Wien in the Women's Champions League, as Sonia Bompastor looks to get her ready to face Arsenal on Sunday.

The Blues are overwhelming favourites to open their European league-phase campaign with three points on Wednesday, with the Opta supercomputer assigning them a 93.3% chance of victory over the tournament debutants.
Chelsea's only previous meeting with an Austrian side in the Champions League came last season, as they thumped St. Polten 6-0 in the league phase.
Having gone out at the quarter-final stage last term following three straight semi-final defeats, the Blues are hoping to go further in Europe this term, but rotation is likely this week.
With a huge London derby against Arsenal on the horizon in the Women's Super League, Bompastor has already confirmed James – who picked up a minor injury in training – will be rested.
"She should be available for the game on the weekend, but we don't want to take any risks for the game tomorrow," Bompastor said of James. "She's a bit short."
Bompastor also confirmed Erin Cuthbert, Manaka Matsukubo and Aggie Beever-Jones are all back in training, with the latter being the only one of that trio to appear in a WSL match this season.
"They are training again with the team, so a lot of players and it's good news. Manaka is back in training, not fully fit yet, but it's good to have her back," Bompastor said.
"It's really good to see Erin back. I'm always happy when I have most of my players on the pitch. It brings positivity around the team and the quality on the pitch progresses.
"It's always good to have that competition in the squad, with everyone happy to be on the pitch together."
Chelsea lost just one of their eight games in the Champions League last season (W5 D2), conceding the fewest goals of any side in the competition (six).

Austria Wien will become the fourth different side from Austria to participate in the Champions League, but those teams are winless in 21 games in the competition (D3 L18) since St. Polten beat Slavia Prague 1-0 in November 2022.
English sides have won all five of their meetings with Austrian opponents in the competition by an aggregate score of 17-2.

Bompastor also confirmed Erin Cuthbert, Manaka Matsukubo and Aggie Beever-Jones are all back in training, with the latter being the only one of that trio to appear in a WSL match this season. 

"They are training again with the team, so a lot of players and it's good news. Manaka is back in training, not fully fit yet, but it's good to have her back," Bompastor said. 

"It's really good to see Erin back. I'm always happy when I have most of my players on the pitch. It brings positivity around the team and the quality on the pitch progresses.

"It's always good to have that competition in the squad, with everyone happy to be on the pitch together."

Chelsea lost just one of their eight games in the Champions League last season (W5 D2), conceding the fewest goals of any side in the competition (six).

Austria Wien will become the fourth different side from Austria to participate in the Champions League, but those teams are winless in 21 games in the competition (D3 L18) since St. Polten beat Slavia Prague 1-0 in November 2022. 

English sides have won all five of their meetings with Austrian opponents in the competition by an aggregate score of 17-2.

          Mass Overhaul or Squad Continuity: What is the Recipe for Premier League Success?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 2, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author, Ithiel Piñero / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
In an age when fans wants limitless spending on shiny new signings, we ask whether less change can sometimes be more beneficial.
If a cautionary tale was needed for a football club assuming the grass is always greener on the other side, Tottenham Hotspur’s experience so far in 2026-27 may well do the job.

After a dismal 2025-26, in which Spurs escaped relegation by the skin of their teeth, the club dived head first into their hopes for a shiny new era on the back of Roberto De Zerbi’s insistence the squad needed immediate, severe and costly surgery. After De Zerbi saved the club from the drop, he was handed the keys to a weighty war chest, and he spent big.

Upwards of £300 million was dished out and more or less an entire new team was brought in. Spurs signed 10 new players who have all gone into the first team; just five league games into the new season and all nine of the outfield signings have made at least one appearance in the Premier League, while many of them are already key players.
You don’t need a deep data dive to see it hasn’t worked yet. Spurs are bottom of the table without a win five games into 2026-27. It’s their worst start to a Premier League season.

It might all work out in the end. Spurs might become world beaters with this squad. Or even if it doesn’t go quite that well, they could feasibly become a half-decent team very soon indeed. This season obviously isn’t a complete write-off already.

But even if they do turn things around, by making such a poor start, they have given everyone else a head start. Spurs are playing catch-up with every other team, and now face a 33-game run in which they have to make up a deficit if they are to retain their Premier League status. They need to improve drastically to make the season anything like a success.

In fairness to De Zerbi, the evidence of the last two seasons was pretty strong. Spurs had finished 17th twice consecutively, last season playing some utterly miserable football while suffering a string of serious and debilitating injuries, and the squad clearly needed new additions. But has too much been changed too suddenly?

Spurs have become only the 12th team in Premier League history (excluding promoted teams) to hand more than 25 starts in the space of the first five games of a season to players who didn’t play for the club the previous year.

The concern for Spurs is, historically, doing that doesn’t go well. Six of the previous 11 have ended up finishing 17th or lower in the first season after the summer overhaul. Only one has finished higher than ninth.
Many of those teams were arguably always destined to be in a relegation battle and had attempted to avoid as much by making a lot of summer signings, such as QPR in 2012-13 or Portsmouth in 2005-06.

Spurs finished fifth as recently as 2023-24 and would have been hoping to get back into the elite quickly, but they are, whether they like it or not, a relegation-battling side. And the early evidence of this season along with the history of other clubs who have made this much change doesn’t bode well for them.
So, are these numbers and Spurs’ troubles the sign of a wider problem with significant player turnover? Were they wrong to approach the summer with this aggressive approach to the transfer market?

First up, it’s worth noting that there are examples of teams signing lots of players and things working out, if not always immediately, then in the long term. Nottingham Forest broke the record for the most players signed by a Premier League club after winning promotion in the summer of 2022 and have since established themselves as top-flight regulars (although they were later deducted four points for breaching the Premier League’s Profitability and Sustainability Rules). Chelsea transformed their squad and fortunes after Roman Abramovich arrived at the club. Sunderland qualified for Europe last season after a summer of overhaul following their promotion.

But there are many more examples of teams struggling after making a lot of signings, as is the case with many of the sides in the above table who gave lots of starts to new signings early on in the new season.
And this term, too, the teams who have started well are generally those who have not overhauled their squad.

Of the eight teams to give 10 or fewer starts to players who didn’t play for them last season, five are better off than the position in which the Opta supercomputer predicted they would finish before the start of the campaign. In other words, when comparing season-to-season changes in the starting XI with performance relative to (the supercomputer’s) expectations, teams who didn’t make many alterations are doing well.

And it’s the opposite at the other end of the spectrum. Of the eight teams who have given at least 13 starts this season to new players, all but one are currently in a lower position than they were in the Opta supercomputer’s pre-season predictions.

Whether by complete coincidence or not, there appears to be a correlation between the two. A greater number of new players this season has led to underperformance compared to what the supercomputer foresaw for that team.

There are a few obvious outliers. Bournemouth have given fewer starts to new players (five) than any other team in the Premier League this season (though they do have a new manager), but they are currently seven places lower than their predicted position from pre-season.

197rqdcsi8fzl10wb5mtwhz3tt.title: Romania 0-1 Sweden: Gyokeres continues hot streak
197rqdcsi8fzl10wb5mtwhz3tt.subtitle: Viktor Gyokeres scored his fourth goal in as many games for Sweden as Graham Potter's team edged out Romania in the Nations League.
paragraphs: Sweden are in prime position to earn promotion back to the top table in the Nations League after they beat Romania 1-0 on Monday.
Graham Potter's team rounded off the first international break of the season with a slender victory at Arena Nationala, with Viktor Gyokeres' goal proving decisive.
Sweden remain unbeaten in Group B4, which they top on 10 points, two ahead of Bosnia-Herzegovina.
Gyokeres' goal came just 12 minutes in, with the Arsenal forward pouncing on the rebound from Sebastian Nanasi's shot, which had struck the woodwork.
He should have doubled up later in the first half, but failed to direct a header goalwards after meeting Eric Smith's cross.
Viktor Johansson was called into action in Sweden's goal in the second half, as he denied Nicolae Stanciu and Florin Tanase, but that was all Romania could really manage in response.
Sweden close in on promotion as Gyokeres delivers
Three wins and one draw from their opening four fixtures is a fantastic start for Sweden, who are now on the brink of sealing a return to the top section of the Nations League.
That is where Sweden will feel they belong, given some of the quality they have at their disposal, albeit Gyokeres was their only real star name in action this time out.
He has now scored 25 goals for Sweden, and he led the way for Potter's team with four attempts here.
Gyokeres only managed to hit the target once, but he was in the right place, at the right time, to get the goal that mattered in the end.
His goal came from a chance worth a whopping 0.95 expected goals, so it would have been difficult for him to miss.
But in Alexander Isak's absence, Gyokeres is the main man, and he duly delivered for Sweden.

19p7xhsygyxob1j9e3g5vytwk4.title: Charlton Athletic 0-1 Manchester City: Greenwood free-kick keeps champions perfect
19p7xhsygyxob1j9e3g5vytwk4.subtitle: Manchester City made it four wins from four to begin their Women's Super League campaign, but they were made to work by Charlton Athletic.
paragraphs: Manchester City's perfect start to their Women's Super League title defence continued as Alex Greenwood's first-half free-kick sealed a 1-0 win over Charlton Athletic.
Greenwood curled in the only goal in the 36th minute at The Valley, moving Andree Jeglertz's side, at least now, five points clear at the top of the standings.
Jeglertz elected to make six changes to the side that came from behind to beat Liverpool last time out, with Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw starting on the City bench.
Charlton started brightly, but it was the visitors who registered the first shot on target, though Sophie Whitehouse had no problem collecting Mary Fowler's 19th-minute attempt.
Jodie Hutton's cross into the area almost caught out Eartha Cumings soon after, with Beth Mead then forcing a save out of Whitehouse at the other end moments later.
However, City took the lead nine minutes before half-time through captain Greenwood, who curled an effort over the Charlton wall that nestled into the bottom-right corner from 25 yards.
City should have pulled further clear shortly after the restart, but Whitehouse produced two instinctive saves to keep out Gracie Prior and Grace Clinton in quick succession.
Cassandra Korhonen should have done better when she was picked out by Hutton's cross, with Jeglertz introducing Shaw into the action in the 60th minute.

And she should have made it more comfortable for City, but she could only head wide of the left post from Carlotta Wamser's delivery. It mattered little, though, as they held on for a fourth league win.
Can anyone stop champions City?

City arrived into the contest having scored 3+ goals in each of their opening three games of a WSL campaign, becoming the first side to do so since Arsenal in 2021-22, and though they were unable to continue that stretch, they showed they can win in different ways.

The Citizens have now won each of their opening four games this season, equalling their longest 100% winning start across their eight most recent top-flight campaigns, having also won four in a row back in 2019-20.

In addition, they have also emerged victorious in 29 of their 30 WSL games against newly promoted teams, winning eight straight since a 2-1 loss at Liverpool in 2022-23, though it was a moment of magic from Greenwood that got them over the line.

Greenwood netted for the first time in the WSL since April 2024 against Bristol City, though Mead also impressed for the Citizens. She finished with game-high totals for chances created (four), touches (98) and passes in the final third (47).

City were deserving of their win too, finishing with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.98 from their 19 shots to Charlton's 0.63 from their five attempts, with Jeglertz now turning his attention to the Women's Champions League, with a tie against Real Madrid up next.

19w7m2lz4gt141q5b1vzbn3eje.title: Tuchel: England harnessed the pain of World Cup exit in Croatia rout
19w7m2lz4gt141q5b1vzbn3eje.subtitle: After England produced one of their all-time greatest displays to rout Croatia 7-0, Thomas Tuchel said his players were playing with pain.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel felt England's players harnessed the pain of their World Cup failure in a positive way against Croatia, after they trounced their old rivals 7-0 in the Nations League.

Less than four months on from the Three Lions' semi-final collapse against Argentina, when Tuchel was fiercely criticised for reining in his attacking players, his team showed a completely different side in Rijeka.

Harry Kane, Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham and Bukayo Saka all scored in the first half to put the result beyond all reasonable doubt, with Kane and Saka both clinching their braces and Morgan Rogers adding the final goal off the bench in the second period.
It was the heaviest defeat in Croatia's history and England's biggest-ever Nations League win, as well as their biggest victory over any top 50 team in the FIFA World Rankings.

The Three Lions had four different players score in the first half of a game for the first time since March 2013 against San Marino (Frank Lampard, Jermain Defoe, Ashley Young, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain), while their nine-match winning streak away from home is their joint-longest ever, having managed an identical run between December 1965 and October 1967 either side of their World Cup triumph.
And while Tuchel admits the pain of July's defeat to Argentina still weighs heavily on everyone connected to the England team, he was pleased to see them take out their anger on a top-tier opponent.
"This is the only way to move forward, even if you still feel pain," Tuchel said.
"You have to play with the pain if you still feel the disappointment, you have to play with it. That is the nature of sport.

"It was not an easy camp in the beginning, after this long tournament, for multiple reasons. But straight away, from the first training session... we had an excellent performance against Spain but not the result, then the reaction to that result in Czechia, and now the build-up here.
"The focus in the meetings, the translation of the meetings onto the pitch and to bring it in these circumstances in Croatia, to win with this dominant performance, that is the way to move on."
Although all of England's attackers impressed, Bellingham was the real star of the show, as he capped a 27-pass move for his goal and also added three assists.

The Real Madrid superstar – who recently won England's Player of the Year award for 2026 after scoring seven goals at the World Cup – teed up Kane and Saka in the first half, then supplied the defence-splitting pass for Rogers to add the seventh goal.
When asked if Bellingham had gone up a level in 2026, Tuchel said: "At the moment it seems like it, and you always need to. You can never stand still.
"It's like on these electric escalators, if you stand still, if you walk against the escalator, you have to walk to even maintain your level.
"You have to develop and you have to push for the next level, otherwise other teams will catch up."

England have six points on the board after three Nations League games, putting them three behind Group A3 leaders Spain and three above third-placed Croatia, ahead of Tuesday's clash with Czechia at Wembley.

19z4npnxn4rpj1oc4bi6y47yuc.title: Real Madrid's Asencio to have surgery on leg fracture
19z4npnxn4rpj1oc4bi6y47yuc.subtitle: Raul Asencio has failed to play a single minute for Real Madrid this season, and is now having surgery on the injury that has kept him out.
paragraphs: Real Madrid defender Raul Asencio is set to have surgery on a stress fracture in his right tibia.
Asencio has been struggling with the injury since the start of the season and was not included in any of Madrid's first five matchday squads this term.
Even following his return, he has not played a single minute for Madrid so far and seemingly aggravated the issue in training on Wednesday.
As such, he will undergo surgery on Thursday, with Spanish media reports suggesting he is set for two to four months on the sidelines.
Asencio made 34 appearances for Madrid in all competitions last term but lost his starting place in the latter stages of the season.
Jose Mourinho has been using Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen as his regular centre-back pairing since his arrival.
However, the Portuguese head coach could soon be able to call on Eder Militao, who has returned to training following hamstring surgery that has kept him out since April.
Madrid return to action at home to Villarreal on October 10 after the international break.
