1auf8cupqwdpn1rj3rx3mblv1a.title: Hallgrimsson says physical and mental fatigue saw Ireland 'run out of gas' against Austria
1auf8cupqwdpn1rj3rx3mblv1a.subtitle: The Republic of Ireland squandered a 2-0 lead to draw 2-2 with Austria, which Heimir Hallgrimsson blamed on physical and mental tiredness.
paragraphs: Heimir Hallgrimsson always expected the Republic of Ireland to "run out of gas" against Austria, as he put their 2-2 Nations League draw down to physical and mental fatigue.
Ireland stormed into a 2-0 lead in their third match in Nations League Group B3, as they attempted to build on last Sunday's 3-0 victory over Israel.
Troy Parrott scored both of Ireland's goals in Dublin, with his first being an incredible solo effort in which he skipped past two defenders before slotting past Florian Wiegele.
Parrot's second was a penalty late in the first half, which came after the game had twice been halted due to protests related to Ireland's upcoming reverse fixture against Israel.
And Hallgrimsson felt the mental toll of the debate surrounding that game – which will take place on Sunday on neutral ground in Belgrade – played a part in Ireland's second-half collapse.

Liam Kitching's error allowed Alexander Prass to pull a goal back for Austria in the 71st minute, and shortly afterwards, fellow substitute Michael Gregoritsch curled a free-kick past Caoimhin Kelleher to equalise, with Austria remaining top of the group on seven points from three games.
"Obviously we were happy to be 2-0 up at half-time," Hallgrimsson told RTE Sport afterwards.
"We knew, and I told you before the game, that this team is high energy; and we knew that we needed to do some rotation and make changes.
"I felt like we just lost organisation, probably due to tiredness, and then you start to make mistakes.
"That was something that we were obviously not happy with, but the first half was good, the organisation was good, we know we can do this.
"I expected us to run out of gas at some point, but maybe not so quickly. This week has not only been physically difficult, but it's been mentally difficult and that takes a lot of energy as well."

Parrott's brace took him to nine goals in his last six competitive outings for Ireland, while his four braces for his country are the most any player has ever scored for them while aged under 25, surpassing Robbie Keane's three.

Prass scored Austria's first goal just 208 seconds after coming off the bench, opening his international account on his 23rd senior cap, while Gregoritsch has now netted 25 times for Thursday's visitors, becoming the 11th Austrian to hit that figure.
Ireland have four points on the board ahead of their return fixture against Israel, who are bottom after earning their first point in a goalless draw with Kosovo on Thursday.

Heimir Hallgrimsson always expected the Republic of Ireland to "run out of gas" against Austria, as he put their 2-2 Nations League draw down to physical and mental fatigue.

Ireland stormed into a 2-0 lead in their third match in Nations League Group B3, as they attempted to build on last Sunday's 3-0 victory over Israel. 

Troy Parrott scored both of Ireland's goals in Dublin, with his first being an incredible solo effort in which he skipped past two defenders before slotting past Florian Wiegele.

Parrot's second was a penalty late in the first half, which came after the game had twice been halted due to protests related to Ireland's upcoming reverse fixture against Israel.

And Hallgrimsson felt the mental toll of the debate surrounding that game – which will take place on Sunday on neutral ground in Belgrade – played a part in Ireland's second-half collapse.

Liam Kitching's error allowed Alexander Prass to pull a goal back for Austria in the 71st minute, and shortly afterwards, fellow substitute Michael Gregoritsch curled a free-kick past Caoimhin Kelleher to equalise, with Austria remaining top of the group on seven points from three games.

"Obviously we were happy to be 2-0 up at half-time," Hallgrimsson told RTE Sport afterwards. 

"We knew, and I told you before the game, that this team is high energy; and we knew that we needed to do some rotation and make changes. 

"I felt like we just lost organisation, probably due to tiredness, and then you start to make mistakes.

"That was something that we were obviously not happy with, but the first half was good, the organisation was good, we know we can do this.

"I expected us to run out of gas at some point, but maybe not so quickly. This week has not only been physically difficult, but it's been mentally difficult and that takes a lot of energy as well."

Parrott's brace took him to nine goals in his last six competitive outings for Ireland, while his four braces for his country are the most any player has ever scored for them while aged under 25, surpassing Robbie Keane's three.

Prass scored Austria's first goal just 208 seconds after coming off the bench, opening his international account on his 23rd senior cap, while Gregoritsch has now netted 25 times for Thursday's visitors, becoming the 11th Austrian to hit that figure. 

Ireland have four points on the board ahead of their return fixture against Israel, who are bottom after earning their first point in a goalless draw with Kosovo on Thursday.

1ay7lniq06mzw1m1807f3fdoe9.title: 'It gave me goosebumps' – Pochettino impressed by USA's youngsters
1ay7lniq06mzw1m1807f3fdoe9.subtitle: Mauricio Pochettino fielded a new-look United States team against Peru, and he is thrilled by what he saw from the younger players.
paragraphs: Mauricio Pochettino says the United States' 4-1 victory over Peru "gave me goosebumps" after he fielded a lot of new faces at Inter.co Stadium.
The Argentine head coach, who signed a new four-year deal following the World Cup, handed out 11 senior team debuts on Saturday, with many of his new stars shining.
Justin Ellis and Julian Hall were both on the scoresheet during their first international cap, with Malik Tillman and Sebastian Berhalter also hitting the back of the net.
Mathis Albert also impressed off the bench, with one of his first involvements seeing him win the penalty from which Tillman scored.
Of the 11 debutants, eight of them were teenagers, and Pochettino was full of praise for how quickly they settled into the team.
"I am so proud of the performance," Pochettino said.
"To see these young players come in, embrace the moment, and play with this kind of freedom and courage – it gave me goosebumps at times.
"It is about opportunity: giving the opportunity, and then they have to take it. What we saw is that the future is here, but soccer is about now. They showed they can compete right now."
All eyes were on 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan – who turns 17 on Monday – as he became the youngest player to earn a senior cap for the USA since Freddy Adu in 2006.
He was one of three debutants in the starting line-up, and Pochettino made it clear that he is determined to open the door to as many players as he can during the new World Cup cycle.
"Nobody can think their place belongs to them because of what they did in the past," he added.
"It's a fresh start, a new cycle. Everyone has the door open, but you must earn it every single day."

1b1jzurh3d3i4144cnru6aexc4.title: Real Madrid 'living in another galaxy' over referee claims, says LaLiga chief Tebas
1b1jzurh3d3i4144cnru6aexc4.subtitle: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has slammed Real Madrid for their treatment of referee Ortiz Arias following Sunday's loss to Atletico Madrid.
paragraphs: Real Madrid are "living in another galaxy" if they believe LaLiga's officials are biased against them, the competition's president Javier Tebas said amid a fierce debate over refereeing standards.
Madrid were beaten 2-1 by Atletico Madrid in Sunday's derby at the Estadio Metropolitano, but the controversial nature of their loss sparked a furious reaction from Los Blancos.

Jose Mourinho's team had Dean Huijsen sent off for a last-man foul early in the second half, but Madrid felt Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have seen red for Atleti, the former for a high challenge on Federico Valverde and the latter for treading on Jude Bellingham.
Mourinho brought printed images of both incidents to his post-match press conference, saying they were the "story of the game" and describing referee Ortiz Arias as weak and inexperienced.
Atleti hit back on their social media channels on Monday, posting an image taken during Mourinho's press conference alongside the caption: "Stop referee harassment now."
Madrid used the title "a terrible refereeing performance decides the derby" for their official club-produced match report, accompanied by images of the Lee and Romero challenges.
And Tebas – who has criticised Madrid's treatment of referees and desire to set up a breakaway European Super League in the past – has now slammed the club's behaviour.

"Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime's television, building the same old narrative: the permanent conspiracy," Tebas wrote on X, responding to a Spanish media article that alleged referees routinely favour Madrid's opponents.
"Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy.
"That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.
"It's more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what's happening on the pitch.
"GET THE BLINDERS OFF! It's September, and they're already claiming the League is tainted. Nobody with common sense believes that old excuse anymore."

Madrid previously sent a formal letter of complaint about LaLiga's referees to the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) in 2025, prompting Tebas to accuse Madrid of harming the competition and "building a story of victimhood."

1b69u0q1qpg61114oxvae5thsv.title: Bastoni confident Italy can take on anyone after France draw
1b69u0q1qpg61114oxvae5thsv.subtitle: Italy fought from a goal down to draw 1-1 with France in the Nations League, giving Roberto Mancini's side a huge confidence boost.
paragraphs: Alessandro Bastoni believes Italy "can do it against anyone" after holding France to a draw in the Nations League.
Italy drew 1-1 with Zinedine Zidane's side at the Stade de France on Friday, with Bastoni cancelling out Michael Olise's stunning opener.

After also netting against Turkiye, Bastoni is only the third centre-back to score in two consecutive appearances for Italy in the last 10 years, after Gianluca Mancini (October-November 2025) and Alessio Romagnoli (October-November 2019).
Gianluigi Donnarumma also played a huge role in the draw, making seven saves, including an impressive double save to keep out Desire Doue and Ousmane Dembele in quick succession.
Only twice has Donnarumma made more saves in a single game for the Azzurri: 10 against Bosnia-Herzegovina in March 2026 and eight against Spain in June 2024.
"It was a tough game, we knew it would be, it's hardly news, but I am so happy with the team performance," Bastoni told RAI Sport.

"We fought hard, we suffered, we even ruined some of France's objectives for tonight, as they were prepared for a big celebration. We knew we weren't coming here for a walk in the park, and that's how it was.

"It's certainly pleasing to score again, but the moment it was done, I thought we had to make sure we didn't concede another, otherwise it was all points. This is a good result that boosts our confidence going forward.
"It's a strong signal, because if we can put in a performance like this against France in Paris, then we can do it against anyone."
Italy won the expected goals (xG) 1.46 to 1.21, with both Moise Kean and Davide Frattesi squandering good opportunities in the first half.

Nevertheless, head coach Roberto Mancini agreed with Bastoni's sentiment, as he told RAI Sport: "We knew it would be a very difficult match, especially at the start, but we did well to allow them very little in terms of chances, even if they had more possession.
"We played as a team, attacking and defending together, and so it is certainly a very positive evening for us.
"I wanted this to be another step forward in our journey. I liked that we tried to play football, despite being against an extraordinary France side full of champions."

1bw4b4j8qe5t618na967le382d.title: Alaba joins Udinese as free agent following Real Madrid exit
1bw4b4j8qe5t618na967le382d.subtitle: Following five successful years with Real Madrid, David Alaba will now ply his trade in Serie A after joining Udinese on Thursday.
paragraphs: David Alaba has laid out his ambitions to "win again" after the former Real Madrid defender completed his move to Serie A side Udinese on Thursday.
Alaba has joined Udinese as a free agent on a contract that will run until the end of the 2026-27 season, following five successful years in the Spanish capital.
The 34-year-old brings with him a wealth of European experience, having also spent 13 years with Bayern Munich before making the move to Madrid in 2021.

He won 25 trophies with the Bundesliga giants, before going on to win two LaLiga crowns and two Champions League titles, in addition to a Copa del Rey, a Supercopa de Espana, a UEFA Super Cup, a Club World Cup and an Intercontinental Cup with Los Blancos.
Alaba was a regular in his first few seasons with Madrid and started their 2022 Champions League final win against Liverpool, but injuries have hampered him in recent seasons.
The Austria international missed 13 months of action after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in December 2023, and failed to rediscover his impressive form.
He was restricted to 17 appearances in 2023-24, across all competitions, then made 14 in 2024-25 and 16 in 2025-26.

He only played 600 minutes in 2024-25 and was limited to 575 last season, with both of those campaigns ending without silverware, something he intends to change having now sealed his switch to Udinese.
"I've had a lot of different experiences, and I've won a lot during my career, but one thing hasn't changed. I want to compete and win again," Alaba said.
"I still want to achieve something special and that is the mentality I will bring to Udinese."
Alaba joins an Udinese side that sit 13th in Serie A this season, having taken four points from their opening five league games of 2026-27.
Only Venzia (13), Fiorentina and Monza (both 12) have conceded more league goals than Udinese (11) this term, something Alaba will be aiming to improve.
"The signing of David Alaba is a source of enormous pride for the whole club," said Udinese general manager Franco Collavino.
"We're welcoming an established champion, a leader and an exemplary professional. His arrival demonstrates Udinese's desire to grow and compete at the highest levels."
Udinese return to action after the extended international break on October 12, with a trip to Torino up next.

1c0qv932xf7y61j04brselmuro.title: Yamal 'on his way to being a legendary player', says Spain boss De la Fuente
1c0qv932xf7y61j04brselmuro.subtitle: Lamine Yamal's exceptional goalscoring form continued as Spain beat Czechia in the Nations League, drawing lofty praise from his head coach.
paragraphs: Lamine Yamal is already on the path to becoming a legend of the game and "never ceases to amaze", Luis de la Fuente declared after Spain's win over Czechia on Saturday.
La Roja remain top of Nations League Group A3 with maximum points after three games, having held off a second-half fightback from Czechia to win 3-1 in Oviedo.

First-half goals from Barcelona duo Yamal and Rodri put Spain in a commanding position, though Czechia later had them on the ropes following Jiri Slama's goal, only for Ladislav Krejci's red card and a late strike from Mikel Merino to end their comeback hopes.
Yamal's opening goal was a trademark left-footed curler from the right corner of the area, after he exchanged passes with club-mate Dani Olmo.

He now has 12 goals in his last nine games for club and country combined (four for Spain in the Nations League, eight for Barcelona in all competitions), with a 3-1 LaLiga win over Sevilla being the only game in which he has failed to find the net in that period.
Asked if he was ever surprised by Yamal's production in his post-match press conference, De la Fuente said: "He never ceases to amaze us all.
"He is so talented, there is much more to see of the best version of Lamine.
"He is growing by leaps and bounds. He is a reference for the national team, a player with great weight, and we have to celebrate him."

Asked about Yamal's Ballon d'Or prospects, with just over three weeks left before the award ceremony in London, De la Fuente added: "If he were the only Spaniard among the nominees, I would tell him that he is the best in the world.
"He does everything well. If he is not the best because of competition with other Spaniards, he is one of the best. But he is on the way to being a legendary player."
Yamal was one of two players to be substituted at half-time, alongside Alex Baena, with De la Fuente looking to keep his attackers fresh ahead of Tuesday's trip to Croatia.
La Roja's performance levels dipped sharply after the interval, as they only registered five shots and 0.75 expected goals, compared to 13 attempts and 1.35 xG in the first period.
But De la Fuente insists it was necessary to manage the winger's load, saying: "We take care of Lamine exactly the same as the other players.
"We do not make a distinction. We take care of everyone equally.
"We thought that the game would go in a different direction, but we wanted to take away some minutes from his load, so that he could stay in the best condition."

1clrgb6ichllh1tvuhpbqvdajn.title: Havertz and Musiala withdraw from Germany squad in double injury blow
1clrgb6ichllh1tvuhpbqvdajn.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp suffered two withdrawals from his Germany squad, but had replacements to call upon from his second party of players.
paragraphs: Germany have been dealt a double injury blow as Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala have both withdrawn from the squad.
Musiala suffered a torn muscle fibre in his right thigh during the warm-up for their Nations League opener against the Netherlands.
Havertz started the match, which finished as a 1-1 draw, but was then withdrawn in the 30th minute due to a muscle strain – as announced by the German Football Association (DFB).
No timeline has been set for Havertz's return, but German media reports that Musiala will be out for three to four weeks for Bayern Munich.
Jurgen Klopp has named two squads for this extended international break, including 44 players, so Florian Wirtz and Jonathan Burkardt have now been called up one game earlier than originally planned.
Wirtz has come under criticism for his Liverpool performances so far this season, particularly after their 1-0 victory over Bournemouth.
He has made six appearances for Liverpool in all competitions this term, registering just one assist, despite creating 12 chances – the third-most of any Reds player.
Burkardt, meanwhile, has made a stellar start to the campaign for Eintracht Frankfurt, netting six goals in his five outings.
He is currently averaging a goal every 64.7 minutes and a 42.9% shot conversion rate.
Germany's second Nations League match sees them host Greece on Sunday.

1cm0oscojseck1v29y1up5akkc.title: Sweden 2-1 Romania: Isak and Gyokeres on target in Nations League win
1cm0oscojseck1v29y1up5akkc.subtitle: Sweden returned to League B with a victory in the Nations League, with their star strikers both hitting the back of the net in Stockholm.
paragraphs: Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyokeres were both on target as Sweden made a winning start to the Nations League with a 2-1 victory over Romania.
Having been promoted to League B during the last Nations League campaign, Sweden made a winning return to the competition.
They started fast, with Sebastian Nanasi seeing a curling effort pushed away by Ionut Radu with just 32 seconds on the clock.

And Isak found a way through in the 20th minute; he peeled off the back of Virgil Ghita to latch onto Yasin Ayari's throughball and his powerful effort nestled into the net, despite Radu getting a hand to the shot.

Just nine minutes later, though, Romania were back on level terms. A pacy counter-attack finished with Dennis Man flicking the ball over Victor Lindelof before volleying past a helpless Viktor Johansson.
Romania attempted to push for a second, but their momentum was halted two minutes before half-time when Gyokeres fired in the rebound of Lucas Bergvall's saved shot.

Elliot Stroud thought he had added a third for Sweden when his lovely looping shot flew into the top-right corner 53 minutes in, but his celebrations were cut short after the goal was ruled out following a VAR review for a handball by Isak in the build-up.
Both teams had further chances to add to their tallies, but neither could find another goal, with Sweden moving top of their group with the victory.
Sweden's superstars get the ball rolling
Isak and Gyokeres have endured very different starts to their respective seasons, but both of them will be thrilled to get on the scoresheet for their nation.

Isak has put last season's struggles behind him at Liverpool, already netting four goals in his seven games for them in all competitions, and he was a shining light for Sweden with a game-high three shots and seven touches in the opposition box.
Meanwhile, Gyokeres has stumbled so far in 2026-27, failing to hit the back of the net for Arsenal after making just five appearances and only as a starter, without scoring in them.
He may have netted the winner for Sweden, but he had a hard time imposing himself in the game, with only one shot in total, while he only managed 31 touches, just over half of what Isak did (60).

Elliot Stroud thought he had added a third for Sweden when his lovely looping shot flew into the top-right corner 53 minutes in, but his celebrations were cut short after the goal was ruled out following a VAR review for a handball by Isak in the build-up.

Both teams had further chances to add to their tallies, but neither could find another goal, with Sweden moving top of their group with the victory.

Sweden's superstars get the ball rolling

Isak and Gyokeres have endured very different starts to their respective seasons, but both of them will be thrilled to get on the scoresheet for their nation.

Isak has put last season's struggles behind him at Liverpool, already netting four goals in his seven games for them in all competitions, and he was a shining light for Sweden with a game-high three shots and seven touches in the opposition box.

Meanwhile, Gyokeres has stumbled so far in 2026-27, failing to hit the back of the net for Arsenal after making just five appearances and only as a starter, without scoring in them.

He may have netted the winner for Sweden, but he had a hard time imposing himself in the game, with only one shot in total, while he only managed 31 touches, just over half of what Isak did (60).

1covehf8wlgfd186xyhyxsoe4c.title: Germany 2-0 Serbia: Klopp earns first win after stunning Wirtz display
1covehf8wlgfd186xyhyxsoe4c.subtitle: After falling short in his first two games with Germany, Jurgen Klopp finally got into the win column with a dominant victory over Serbia.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp picked up his first win as Germany boss with a 2-0 victory over Serbia in the Nations League.

Florian Wirtz was the star of the show in a relentless display from the home side at the Allianz Arena, with the Liverpool midfielder scoring the second goal after Tom Bischof got a deserved opener late in the first half.

Germany started on the front foot as Aleksandar Pavlovic curled narrowly wide before Nick Woltemade sent a header off target, while Gnabry dragged an effort wide of the left post in the 18th minute, following a brilliant pass from Wirtz.

Djordje Petrovic was then on hand to deny both Gnabry and Wirtz with two brilliant saves, but he could do nothing when Bischof fired into the roof of the net after Wirtz's initial effort bounced back off the post, six minutes before half-time.

Germany continued to push either side of the break, with Petrovic tipping a fierce attempt from Bischof over the bar before Said El Mala's deflected strike landed just wide of the right post after the restart.

Woltemade inexplicably fired over from mere yards out from Philipp Treu's cross, but Germany doubled their lead just past the hour as Wirtz showed brilliant skill to take in a pass from Maximilian Mittelstadt and dribble past Srdjan Babic before scoring.

Serbia's first, and only, shot came in the 78th minute as Jonas Urbig easily dealt with a long-range attempt from Filip Kostic, as Germany's dominance on the ball was too much for the visitors to handle.
Wirtz inspires Germany to three points

The only criticism Klopp could possibly give his side will relate to their wastefulness in front of goal, as they scored just twice despite accumulating 3.82 expected goals (xG) from 32 shots, six of which were Opta-defined big chances.
Germany had as many shots on goal in the first half as they managed in their entire previous match against Greece (16).

But the former Liverpool boss will take great joy from the performance of current Reds player Wirtz; aside from the two goals, Klopp's biggest smile on the touchline came when Wirtz regained possession in the final third.

Despite his struggles at club level this term, Wirtz was at his best for Germany against Serbia. He created a match-high six chances, recorded the most touches in the opposition box (eight) and completed two of his three dribbles, while also playing a key role in Bischof's opener.

Wirtz scored his 12th goal for Germany at the age of 21 years and 37 days; only Edmund Conen in 1935 (20 years, 281 days) and Lukas Podolski in 2006 (20 years, 357 days) reached this milestone for the German national team at a younger age.

1d278ewvzy6121v58olswbrifd.title: Xavi sees 'superior' Netherlands in second half against Germany
1d278ewvzy6121v58olswbrifd.subtitle: Xavi was forced to settle for a draw on his Netherlands debut against Germany, but he felt his team should have taken all three points.
paragraphs: Xavi believed his Netherlands team deserved more than a point in their Nations League opener against Germany following a "superior" performance in the second half.
The former Barcelona boss made his Netherlands bow at Johan Cruijff Arena on Thursday, with his team playing out a 1-1 draw against Jurgen Klopp's Germany.
Felix Nmecha had given Germany a 32nd-minute lead when he finished past Bart Verbruggen, though the hosts felt that Brian Brobbey had been fouled in the build-up.
But the Netherlands dominated after the break, with Denzel Dumfries denied by Marc-Andre ter Stegen before Mexx Meerdink's goal was disallowed for a foul by Virgil van Dijk.
However, Xavi's side were able to get the goal their performance merited in second-half stoppage time when Cody Gakpo brilliantly volleyed Ruben van Bommel's cross home.

The Netherlands improved their expected goals (xG) total from 0.57 to 2.61 in the second half, while also having more shots (14 to five), more big chances (five to none) and touches in the opposition box (26 to 11) than their opponents.

In fact, the Oranje recorded an overall expected goals (xG) total of 3.18 to Germany's 1.45 xG. It was the first time they had registered above 3.0 in that metric against a nation ranked inside the top 30 of the FIFA rankings since June 2019.
"We were a bit nervous in the first half," Xavi said. "So at half-time, I said that we had to show more personality. I asked for more ambition.
"I saw that in the second half. I'm glad that the players realised after the break that we were superior.
"We deserved more than this. We created a lot of chances, put on good pressure and took a lot of initiative.
"I'm less happy with the number of lost duels, I'm not happy about that. But I have a good feeling about it.
"The debutants also did a great job. Mexx Meerdink was easy to play and fought continuously, and Ruben van Bommel filled in excellently with his ball conquest and assist."
But there was concern for Xavi following the stalemate, with Brobbey replaced in the 35th minute by Meerdink because of what appeared to be an injury to his hamstring.
The Sunderland striker arrived into the international break fresh from scoring a hat-trick against Manchester City, but it remains to be seen how severe the injury is.
Xavi confirmed that Brobbey would take no further part in the rest of the Netherlands' fixtures, and he revealed another striker would be called up to fill that gap in the final third.
"Brian is indeed injured, unfortunately, so we will call up another striker. We haven't decided who yet. I haven't had time for that yet," Xavi said of Brobbey's issue.
Brobbey's injury led to Germany's opening goal, with the Netherlands frustrated by their opponents, who appeared as though they were going to kick the ball out of play.
However, Nadiem Amiri and Joshua Kimmich instead kept the attack going, and Nmecha swept home after Nathaniel Brown's cross into the penalty area was flicked into his path.
"I think it's normal to stop when a player is injured on the ground, although there are no rules for it. They didn't do that, that's not sporting," Gakpo said of Germany's goal.
"We were pushing and we had opportunities. And that we still managed to score an equaliser, is nice."

1d9qvv4bsdhx01ptrel20b6jyr.title: O'Reilly withdraws from England squad with injury
1d9qvv4bsdhx01ptrel20b6jyr.subtitle: Nico O'Reilly will be unavailable for England's Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Czechia after leaving the squad due to injury.
paragraphs: England have confirmed Nico O'Reilly has withdrawn from their squad due to injury.
The Manchester City defender started in last Saturday's Nations League defeat to Spain at Wembley Stadium, but he was then absent for their win over Czechia on Tuesday.
O'Reilly assisted Harry Kane in a thrilling game against the world champions, but then made a mistake in the lead-up to Alex Baena's goal to make it 2-2.
The 21-year-old will now miss the Three Lions' trip to Croatia and home fixture against Czechia, with Thomas Tuchel opting against calling up a replacement for the left-back.
"Nico O'Reilly has returned to Manchester City and will play no part in the forthcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures," a statement read.
"No further replacements are planned as the Three Lions prepare to face Croatia in Rijeka on Saturday before returning to Wembley to take on Czechia on Tuesday."
England have won six of their last eight Nations League matches (L2), scoring 20 goals in the process.
That is more wins (W5 D6 L7) and goals (18) than they managed in their first 18 games in the competition.

The Three Lions have also won their last eight away matches in all competitions – a win against Croatia would see them equal their record of nine away wins in a row, set between December 1965 and October 1967 under Sir Alf Ramsey.
O'Reilly may now face a battle to be fit for Manchester City's next Premier League game, away to Liverpool on October 11.

1dj8oh7o6p4gt17bsshytl7bwe.title: Greece 0-0 Germany: Klopp's men frustrated in Nations League draw
1dj8oh7o6p4gt17bsshytl7bwe.subtitle: Greece once again frustrated Germany, as they held Jurgen Klopp's team to a 0-0 draw in Sunday's Nations League contest.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp's first international window in charge of Germany ended in underwhelming fashion as his team were held to a 0-0 draw by Greece.
Klopp has won just one of his first four games in charge of Germany, who sit third in Nations League Group A2, three points behind Greece and the Netherlands.
Indeed, Greece got the better of Germany in Klopp's second game in charge, winning 2-1, and there was to be no revenge for Klopp's team on Sunday.
Germany did think they had taken the lead midway through the first half at Stadio Toumbas, but Jonathan Burkardt saw his goal disallowed for handball.
The lively Derry Scherhant also went close before half-time, but some changes from Greece boss Ivan Jovanovic helped the hosts tighten matters up after the break.
Giorgos Masouras could well have won it for Greece, but he headed wide from a free header.
Philipp Treu, however, had the best chance to settle the contest, only to slice over late on.
Germany dominate, but lack clinical touch
If it was an all-round, dominant display Klopp was looking for, then it was certainly served up by his team.
Germany had 45 touches in the opponent's box, took on 21 shots and had 70.1% possession.
Yet they only translated that to one big chance, four shots on target and chances worth a combined 1.05 expected goals.
Greece, on the other hand, had just five attempts, but they were worth a combined 0.72 xG.

Klopp must, then, have his concerns about Germany's strength in both boxes, and five points from the 12 on offer across his first four games in charge of the national team is not the return he would have been hoping for.

1dofuka5qfm801nd72hkzwpc8t.title: Pickford welcomes England competition from Trafford
1dofuka5qfm801nd72hkzwpc8t.subtitle: James Trafford has started in both of England's Nations League games so far, but Jordan Pickford is ready to fight for the number one spot.
paragraphs: Jordan Pickford has welcomed the competition from James Trafford in the fight to be England's starting goalkeeper.
Pickford has been England's first-choice goalkeeper since the 2018 World Cup, but Trafford has started in each of their Nations League matches during this international break.

Trafford became the first England goalkeeper other than Pickford to start consecutive games since Nick Pope in September 2022, though the Everton shot-stopper could be back between the sticks when the Three Lions face Croatia on Saturday.
Pickford believes the competition will only help him grow as a goalkeeper, while insisting he has no immediate plans to retire.
"I feel for me personally it's always good to have good competition, I've always said in interviews I've always wanted that competition.
"We have a good crop of goalkeepers coming through and it's a credit to England to have that and may it continue for longer.
"I'll always push myself at the club to be the best version of me and keep getting those caps. You can't let your foot off the gas at any time you want to push yourself to be who you want to be.
"I'm 32 now, you see keepers playing still at 40, still playing at the highest level. It's about me focusing on myself; I set myself my own goals."

England have won their last eight away matches in all competitions – a win against Croatia would see them equal their record of nine away wins in a row between December 1965 and October 1967 under Sir Alf Ramsey.
Since beating England in the 2018 World Cup semi-final, Croatia are winless in all four games against the Three Lions (D1 L3).
Pickford played in the World Cup defeat in 2018, though he believes England cannot rely on their recent success over Croatia.
"I think it's always a good competitive match, we know we lost in the 2018 World Cup against them," added Pickford.

"But we are looking past recent history and we have always played well against them. You're always going to be against good competition at pot one in the Nations League; it's about being the best version of us."

1dpq5fzah0yjb1ulfpojg4v0ri.title: Netherlands 2-1 Serbia: Zirkzee's winner continues Xavi's unbeaten run
1dpq5fzah0yjb1ulfpojg4v0ri.subtitle: Joshua Zirkzee's 72nd-minute winner ensured the Netherlands continued their unbeaten run under Xavi, as they beat Serbia 2-1.
paragraphs: Joshua Zirkzee's 72nd-minute strike ensured the Netherlands continued their unbeaten Nations League run after overcoming a stubborn Serbia 2-1 in Group A2.
After Teun Koopmeiners fired in a free-kick, Serbia instantly levelled thanks to Mihajlo Cvetkovic's header at Philips Stadion.
But, with both sides missing a host of chances, it was Zirkzee's close-range strike which settled the contest.

The Netherlands almost made Vanja Milinkovic-Savic pay for his sloppiness inside the opening three minutes, but Mexx Meerdink was unable to keep his shot down before Noa Lang dragged an attempt wide of the post.
However, the Oranje took the lead in the 31st minute, with Koopmeiners fizzing a free-kick into the bottom-right corner.
But the Netherlands' lead lasted only four minutes as Serbia grabbed a shock equaliser thanks to Cvetkovic’s header.

It all came from Aleksa Terzic's left-wing delivery, with Cvetkovic guiding a finish into the far corner. That was the third goal the Netherlands have conceded in the last 15 minutes of the first half, with no team conceding more such goals so far in the 2026-27 Nations League.
The visitors should have taken the lead within 48 seconds of the second half, but Cvetkovic steered an effort wide of the upright after being played through on goal by Dusan Tadic.

After grabbing an equaliser against Greece in the Netherlands' previous Nations League encounter, Tijjani Reijnders should have scored after being slipped in by Joey Veerman, but the midfielder lashed a bouncing shot wide of the far post.
However, Reijnders was involved in the decisive goal, as Zirkzee swept home a 72nd-minute finish, ensuring Xavi's side sit top of Group A2.
Zirkzee the hero in Eindhoven
With the Netherlands struggling to break down a stubborn Serbia defence, it was looking like more dropped points for the Oranje.
However, Xavi decided to bring on Zirkzee for the second half, and his change paid off.
The Manchester United striker showed great instinct to be in the box at the right time to sweep home a six-yard finish.

That was Zirkzee's only attempt on target. Virgil van Dijk, on his 100th appearance for the Oranje, also made a vital contribution in the heart of defence, making nine clearances, while having four shots.
The Netherlands are undefeated in their last eight games in the Nations League, while having scored in four of their four games, with no team having done so more often in the competition.
Xavi's team registered 22 shots, with seven on target, and they created chances worth a combined 2.75 expected goals (xG).
Meanwhile, Serbia, who almost equalised in stoppage time through Nemanja Gudelj's long-range strike, mustered an xG of 1.66 from 14 shots.

1dxlw1dvi69hl16fjrlm2qr67b.title: Kane: On another day England could have beaten Spain
1dxlw1dvi69hl16fjrlm2qr67b.subtitle: England were 2-1 up against Spain when Harry Kane missed a penalty, with the world champions going on to turn things around and win 3-2.
paragraphs: Harry Kane conceded England could have beaten Spain "on another day" after starting their Nations League campaign with a 3-2 defeat to the world champions.
England came from behind to lead after a Marc Guehi error gifted Lamine Yamal a second-minute goal, with Anthony Gordon and Kane netting in the space of four first-half minutes.
However, Kane then struck the crossbar after his standing foot slipped when he took a penalty, and Spain flipped the script, with Alex Baena equalising shortly after.
Mikel Oyarzabal then secured all three points for Spain, coming back to haunt England, having also netted the winner in the Euro 2024 final.

England lost a match in which they led at half-time for the first time since June 2019 (versus the Netherlands in the Nations League). They had won 41 of their previous 42 games when ahead at the break since then (D1).

Kane has scored 17 goals in 19 appearances for England under Thomas Tuchel, but having scored 39 of his 40 penalties for club and country in 2023, 2024 and 2025, he has now missed three of his 16 spot-kicks in all competitions so far in 2026.
"I spoke before that we reached good levels at the World Cup but didn't quite put a full 90 minutes together," Kane told ITV Sport.
"Probably similar again. We had a couple of good moments though; that period was as good as we've played in a long, long time, and that's the standard we know we can reach.
"We're playing against the world champions, the European champions, and we went toe-to-toe. On another day, for sure, we'd have won that game.
"We have to take the positives from it. We have to dust ourselves down and go again in a few days."
England have conceded 3+ goals in consecutive matches for the first time since June 1995, having beaten France 6-4 in their third-place play-off at the World Cup.
Overall, they have conceded 13 goals in their last six matches in all competitions, almost double the amount they had shipped in their first 17 under Tuchel (seven).
But the Three Lions were disappointed, as this was also the first time they made two errors leading to a goal in a competitive match since June 2019 against the Netherlands in the Nations League.
"I think it was a bit of a missed chance," Gordon told ITV Sport.
"I thought it was a great game to watch and to play in; some of the attacking play was at the highest level. But I think in a game like that, mistakes cost you.

"You always feel like it's you're giving it away rather than them winning it. But, of course, you could argue both teams because they were as good as us and we were as good as them. I'm just gutted about the mistakes."
Gordon's goal came at the end of a pacy counter-attack, just days after he said England needed to rely on their own strengths instead of trying to match other teams' styles.

Asked if his goal was the epitome of how England should play, he added: "Kind of, if you want to phrase it that way, in terms of what I said in the week about being direct and playing to an English style, being quick, really putting teams on the back foot.
"It kind of summed up what I said, which was quite nice, but ultimately it didn't lead to a victory.
"Like I said a couple of days ago, I don't think there is a gap [to Spain]; I feel like we're right there. We can win that game so easily.

"I don't think there is a gap, and I think if we played them in the final, I would've felt confident. Being confident doesn't always translate into a win, but I think you've seen here tonight that we're a top team."

1ej1gkk4a5ujg10bv4hm5rln54.title: Wales 2-1 Norway: Williams hits free-kick winner after Heggem red card
1ej1gkk4a5ujg10bv4hm5rln54.subtitle: Wales claimed the first victory of their 2026-27 Nations League campaign, fighting back for a statement win over Norway in Cardiff.
paragraphs: Wales got their Nations League campaign up and running at the third attempt, with Neco Williams' free-kick proving decisive as they fought back to beat 10-man Norway 2-1.

Craig Bellamy's side were rooted to the bottom of Group A4 after defeats to Portugal and Denmark, and though Oscar Bobb gave them a mountain to climb in Cardiff on Thursday, Torbjorn Heggem's red card in the first minute of the second half gave them the impetus to fight back.

Norway received a boost ahead of kick-off as Arsenal playmaker Martin Odegaard was passed fit to start after falling victim to a rough challenge from Bernardo Silva against Portugal on Sunday, and it did not take long for him to get involved.
Eleven minutes in, Bobb played a quick give-and-go with Odegaard near the right corner of the box, then wriggled beyond Ben Davies and finished past Danny Ward.

Norway lost Julian Ryerson to injury soon afterwards, and Wales' Sorba Thomas got some joy against his replacement Marcus Pedersen, though only a lucky bounce off Ben Cabango – which took the ball into Ward's arms – denied Norway a second goal in the 36th minute.
And Wales made the most of that reprieve two minutes later, with the ever-dangerous Thomas sliding a great ball into the six-yard box to hand Dan James an easy finish.

A dream start to the second half then put Wales in complete control. Just 21 seconds after kick-off, James darted in front of the hesitant Heggem and was pushed to the ground, with the Norway centre-back sent off for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity.
And from the resulting free-kick, Williams whipped an inch-perfect effort beyond Orjan Nyland's reach and into the bottom corner, sparking wild celebrations among the home fans.
Only a good save from Nyland prevented Lewis Koumas from stretching Wales' lead, though the uncharacteristically quiet Erling Haaland then failed to direct a header on target at the other end.

Cabango was arguably fortunate to avoid conceding a penalty for handball and Jorgen Strand Larsen went close from distance as Norway pushed hard for an equaliser late on, but they could not avoid a second straight Nations League defeat.
Williams and James give Bellamy statement result
Wales went into Thursday's game off the back of three straight defeats – the last two of them to nil – and already looking bound for relegation back to League B.

They had failed to win their first six matches of 2026, across all competitions (D3 L3), but a memorable fightback against the surprise package from this summer's World Cup should do wonders for their confidence.

Williams' goal was Wales' first from a direct free-kick since Harry Wilson netted against North Macedonia in a 7-1 World Cup qualifying win last November. It was only Wales' second such goal in the Nations League, with Wilson previously scoring directly from a free-kick in a 1-0 win over the Republic of Ireland in October 2018.

Although Williams stole the headlines with his set-piece strike, James' role in Thursday's turnaround cannot be overstated, having scored Wales' equaliser, forced Heggem's red card and, in the process, forced the free-kick from which the hosts went ahead.
Ten of James' 11 goals for Wales have now been scored at the Cardiff City Stadium, including each of his last six.

And defensively, Wales restricted Haaland to two shots (one on target) and 0.35 expected goals. As a team, they finished with a lower xG tally than Stale Solbakken's visitors, 1.05 to 1.3, but Bellamy will not care after masterminding his first win over a side ranked above Wales in the FIFA World Rankings.

1enrx2qrova71bn7aa50eg9tw.title: India 0-4 Brazil: Estevao, Pedro and Lino shine in Kolkata friendly
1enrx2qrova71bn7aa50eg9tw.subtitle: Brazil thrashed India 4-0 in their final friendly of this international break, with Estevao, Pedro and Samuel Lino getting the goals.
paragraphs: Estevao and Pedro registered a goal and an assist apiece and Samuel Lino scored twice off the bench, as Brazil beat India 4-0 in an eagerly anticipated friendly in Kolkata.

Saturday's result meant Carlo Ancelotti's Selecao ended the international break with an unbeaten record and no other injury concerns to speak of, following Raphinha's midweek withdrawal from their squad.

India started positively with Apuia trying his luck from distance, but the midfielder could not test Brazil's debutant goalkeeper Pedro Morisco, while Vinicius Junior drew a solid near-post save from Gurpreet Singh Sandhu at the other end.

The Selecao slowly grew more dominant as the first half wore on, though, and they went in front after 28 minutes, with Sandhu unable to keep out Estevao's rasping 20-yard drive despite getting a touch on the ball down to his left.

The Chelsea man continued to threaten as his cross was headed against the right-hand post by Pedro, but that same duo combined for Brazil's second goal in the 42nd minute as Estevao's clever reverse pass put the Flamengo striker clean through, and he powered his finish past Sandhu.

Apuia reacted quicker than any yellow shirts when Sandhu blocked Vinicius' drive, and the Real Madrid superstar was one of several players to be withdrawn at half-time as both coaches rang the changes.
Vinicius' replacement, Lino, did not need long to make an impact, as he curled a lovely finish into the far corner just before the hour mark, having been found by Pedro's instinctive flick.

Though India looked a beaten team from that moment on, Ryan Williams had two chances to give the home fans something to cheer, forcing Mauro Junior into a desperate goal-line clearance, then firing narrowly wide from the right side of the area shortly afterwards.
There was another goal to come for the visitors, though, as Lino menacingly cut inside from the left flank before drilling past substitute shot-stopper Prabhsukhan Gill in stoppage time.
Young forwards show promise for Brazil

Brazil approached their first-ever meeting with India off the back of a 1-1 draw and a 4-2 win in back-to-back games against Australia, but the chaotic nature of their performances Down Under had led to criticism from some fans and pundits.

A thigh injury suffered by Raphinha further dampened the mood, and while Ancelotti acknowledged the Selecao were enduring a difficult period ahead of kick-off at the Salt Lake Stadium, he urged his players to "play with joy".

Though Brazil's tally of 1.2 expected goals (from 20 shots) was somewhat underwhelming against India, who are ranked 138th in the world and amassed 0.29 xG from nine attempts, there were several individual moments to savour.

Estevao's performance was a notable positive as Brazil enter the post-Neymar era, with the Chelsea winger now boasting six goals in just 14 appearances for his country, only seven of which have been starts.
Pedro marked his first Brazil start with a pair of goal involvements, while Lino's two goals were his first in senior international football, on his fourth cap.

Brazil will be back in Asia during the November international break, with friendlies against Japan and Singapore in the diary, and those young attackers will surely get more opportunities to impress next month.

1ex9mz1u93mlf1b37rwx3j1t42.title: Gordon urges England to focus on their strengths, not replicate Spain
1ex9mz1u93mlf1b37rwx3j1t42.subtitle: England's tactics in their World Cup semi-final loss were questioned, but Anthony Gordon believes they need to focus on their strengths.
paragraphs: Anthony Gordon agreed with Thomas Tuchel's comments about England's inability to control games and believes playing to their own strengths will help them win major tournaments.
England lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina 2-1, before going on to beat France in the third-place play-off and record their best finish at the tournament since winning it in 1966.

However, England were levelled with a lot of criticism for how they played in the semi-final, having gone to a back five after taking the lead in the match, through Gordon, to try and see out a victory.
The tactical tweak saw the Three Lions sit back and defend deeper, with Enzo Fernandez equalising before Lautaro Martinez finished the turnaround in stoppage time.
Tuchel claimed it was "not in England's DNA" to control matches like Spain – their Nations League opponents on Saturday – or Argentina and Brazil, and Gordon backed up that view.
"England, as a nation, we don't have that strength, like the Spanish, where we control games like they do," said Gordon in a press conference. "It's not in us.
"[The] scar [of losing to Argentina] doesn't have to be a negative one, because it might lead us to victory in the next tournaments.

"We can't keep looking at other countries and trying to be like them, because we're not them – we're English, and we have our own strengths which they don't have, so maybe we start playing the way we're good at."
Gordon secured a move to Barcelona from Newcastle United before the start of the World Cup and has made an impressive start to life in Spain.
He acknowledged that the way they approach play is very different to how England do, though it is not a bad thing.
"I'm not sure it's something that can be [taught]," he added.
"Playing in Spain, I can speak with an educated view on the way they keep the ball is different. It's much different than I've ever experienced playing in this country.

"I'm not sure we can ever get that, but we can definitely get better or maybe go the other way and really play to our strengths, which is play physical, play direct football, and on the counter-attack."
England are looking to begin their Nations League campaign with a win when they host Spain at Wembley on Saturday.

However, they have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2); those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).
England have, though, won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of the most recent five without conceding.

1f861q9batb1d12ijxftjbyv18.title: Odegaard: Silva 'completely lost his head' with late tackle
1f861q9batb1d12ijxftjbyv18.subtitle: Martin Odegaard was on the end of a late challenge from Portugal's Bernardo Silva, something the Norway captain said was unacceptable.
paragraphs: Martin Odegaard said Bernardo Silva's tackle on him during Norway's Nations League defeat to Portugal "does not belong on a football pitch".
The incident occurred during Sunday's 2-1 loss to Portugal, with Goncalo Ramos punishing an error from Norway goalkeeper Orjan Nyland to seal the win.
Joao Felix had given Portugal a first-half lead before Erling Haaland's scoring streak continued as he tucked home from close range six minutes after the restart.
In Norway's attempts to find an equaliser, Odegaard picked up possession in his own half before Silva came in late and swiped at the Arsenal midfielder after the ball was played.
Odegaard was clearly angered by the nature of the challenge as, shortly after, he shouted at Silva when he was on the ball before the pair came together later on.

Silva and Odegaard have faced off several times during battles between Manchester City and Arsenal, though the Norway captain said the nature of the tackle came from a player who had "completely lost his head".
"It does not belong on a football pitch," Odegaard told TV2 about the challenge from Silva.
"It's a shame that people behave like that. He completely lost his head. He just kicks me down long after I've played the ball. I don't understand what he's doing."
Odegaard appeared to be in pain at the end of the game as he refrained from taking a corner, with his side chasing an equaliser, and crouched down with his head in his hands.
The Arsenal star revealed that Silva did not apologise for the tackle, and instead chose to downplay the incident.
When he was leaving the Ullevaal Stadion, a reporter asked Silva about the challenge, to which he replied: "It's football, my friend."
Norway boss Stale Solbakken described the incident as "completely unnecessary", while defender Leo Ostigard believed Silva should have been sent off.
"The challenge from Bernardo Silva came very late," Ostigard said. "From the video replay, the tackle was extremely ugly. I think a red card would have been fully justified.
"It's a really nasty one. It's just absolutely awful to do. That's the kind of thing we don't want to see happen to our captain.
"When it comes that long after the ball has gone, it looks pretty deliberate."
Norway have two more fixtures during this international break, with a clash against Wales this Thursday followed up by a trip to Porto to face Portugal three days later.
Asked whether he would miss upcoming games, Odegaard said: "I hope not. I got a knock on my ankle there, so it probably won't be good [short term]."

1fn9kq3e2y81114yor61luqjf2.title: Former Man Utd midfielder Fred slams 'piece of crap' Ten Hag
1fn9kq3e2y81114yor61luqjf2.subtitle: Fred left Manchester United during Erik ten Hag's tenure, and the Brazilian midfielder was highly critical of the Dutch coach.
paragraphs: Fred has called former Manchester United boss Erik ten Hag "a piece of crap" for the way he managed the squad.
Ten Hag was appointed United boss in June 2022 and went on to win the FA Cup and EFL Cup before being sacked in October 2024.
The 56-year-old won 70 of his 128 matches in charge (D23 L35), while also losing the FA Cup final in 2022-23.
Since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, only Jose Mourinho (58.3%) and Michael Carrick (58.3%) have had a better win percentage than Ten Hag (54.7%) among permanent Manchester United managers.
Although he praised Ten Hag's tactical knowledge, Fred slammed the Dutch coach's man-management skills.
"Ten Hag was tactically very good, but with the group he was a piece of crap," Fred said on the Charla Podcast.
"He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with Rashford ... He wouldn't put me in to play, sometimes it got stressful.
"[With Ten Hag] Only his Dutch players played. A clique-ridden coach. But, tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with.
"He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano [was already] older. He took Cristiano out [of the starting lineup], and then there was a falling out."
Fred was brought to Manchester by Mourinho in 2018, and the pair worked together again at Fenerbahce last season, with the midfielder far more fond of the current Real Madrid boss.
"Mourinho's a great bloke, he is funny. I've just been with him at Fenerbahce; he brought me to United," said Fred.
"Before [Carlo] Ancelotti came along, his name was being mentioned for the national team [Brazil].
"So I'd show him the rumours and he'd say: 'F--- off, mate. I'm not going anywhere. I'm going to manage my club here.' A really decent bloke."

Fred has called former Manchester United boss Erik ten Hag "a piece of crap" for the way he managed the squad.

Ten Hag was appointed United boss in June 2022 and went on to win the FA Cup and EFL Cup before being sacked in October 2024.

The 56-year-old won 70 of his 128 matches in charge (D23 L35), while also losing the FA Cup final in 2022-23.

Since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, only Jose Mourinho (58.3%) and Michael Carrick (58.3%) have had a better win percentage than Ten Hag (54.7%) among permanent Manchester United managers.

Although he praised Ten Hag's tactical knowledge, Fred slammed the Dutch coach's man-management skills.

"Ten Hag was tactically very good, but with the group he was a piece of crap," Fred said on the Charla Podcast.

"He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with Rashford ... He wouldn't put me in to play, sometimes it got stressful.

1fovopk176myj14sm66idi1vin.title: Mendez predicts 'big things' for Columbus ahead of trip to Inter Miami
1fovopk176myj14sm66idi1vin.subtitle: The Columbus Crew still have hope of reaching the playoffs this season, and those ambitions will be tested once again by Inter Miami.
paragraphs: Brais Mendez believes things will only get better for the Columbus Crew this season as they prepare to welcome Inter Miami to the ScottsMiracle-Gro Field this weekend.
The Crew kept their playoff hopes alive with a 2-0 win over CF Montreal last time out, with second-half goals from Mohamed Farsi and Mendez sealing the win for Columbus.
Laurent Courtois' side are 13th in the Eastern Conference and six points adrift of FC Cincinnati in ninth, while their win against Montreal ended a two-game losing stretch.
Columbus also have the US Open Cup final to look forward to on October 21, with Western Conference high-flyers St. Louis City SC their opponents in the showpiece match.
Since signing a three-year deal with Columbus in July, Mendez has scored three times in nine MLS appearances, including a brilliant free-kick against Montreal.
Mendez revealed he was still adjusting to his new surroundings, but he believes Columbus are in for an exciting end to the season if they can maintain their winning momentum.
"Everything is a process, and everything needs its time, especially for me to adapt to my team-mates, the club, the culture, the hot weather of Columbus," Mendez said.
"The humidity is different to Spain's. I feel better now and more connected to my team-mates. I am very happy to help the team and be here. Big things will come. I am sure of it."
"I knew that the goalkeeper thought that I was going to cross the ball, I knew I could catch him by surprise.
"That's why I tried to place it as far as possible from him so he would not be able to reach it at the far post. I hit it well and I scored."
Columbus come up against a Miami team that are third in the East following a 2-2 draw with San Diego FC last weekend, with Anders Dreyer netting an 82nd-minute equaliser.
Lionel Messi had cancelled out Dreyer's opener, with Luis Suarez then turning the contest in Miami's favour in the 74th minute, only for the Herons to concede shortly afterwards.
Cristian Gonzalez will, however, be without several of his starting players, including Messi, who is preparing for his final match for Argentina against Benin on October 6.

German Berterame, Fricio Caicedo, Rodrigo De Paul, Lovend's Delinois, Matias Galarza, Daniel Pinter, Alex Shaw and Dayne St. Clair are also on international duty with their respective nations, something Gonzalez said Miami must simply deal with.
"Yes, obviously in this kind of situation. Being in such an important team, we have national team players, and we have to adapt," Gonzalez said.
"I always say the same thing, when you have a squad that is not so prolonged in terms of players, we have to find a way and try to put together the best team to go there and win the game."
Columbus Crew – Brais Mendez
Mendez scored his second direct free-kick goal, and the Crew's third of the year, after Columbus had scored one regular-season direct free-kick goal from 2023 to 2025.
He is the second Crew player in the last decade with multiple direct free-kick goals in a season, after Lucas Zelarayan in 2021 and 2022.
Inter Miami – Luis Suarez
Miami will have to make do without Messi, who has four goals in four career matches against Columbus, recording braces in both October 2024 and May 2025.
But they have a capable deputy in Suarez, who has 13 goals in 22 MLS appearances this season. He also has four goal involvements (three goals, one assist) in four league matches against the Crew.
MATCH PREDICTION: INTER MIAMI WIN

Miami are unbeaten in eight straight regular-season matches against Columbus (W6 D2), last losing to the Crew in August 2022. This is the Herons' longest unbeaten run against a single opponent in league play in club history.

Since returning from the World Cup break, Miami have won just one of the eight regular-season matches in which Messi has contributed to a goal (D5 L2). Prior to this, they had failed to win just 11 times in 46 league matches in which Messi had a goal involvement (W35 D8 L3).

Columbus, meanwhile, won for just the second time in nine regular-season matches last time out. The Crew have just one set of consecutive league wins since July 2025, defeating the Los Angeles Galaxy and Philadelphia Union in April.
Columbus Crew – 33.7%

1frt5j1auot131241p6kvlwwc5.title: 'It's not tennis' – Barella unconcerned by Italy rotation role
1frt5j1auot131241p6kvlwwc5.subtitle: Italy star Nicolo Barella believes he needs to step up when it comes to goalscoring, as he hailed Roberto Mancini's impact.
paragraphs: Italy midfielder Nicolo Barella has no issue with having to fight for his place in the starting XI.

It has been a mixed start to their Nations League campaign for Italy, with Roberto Mancini's side having lost 2-0 to Belgium before crushing Turkiye 4-1 in Bursa, and salvaging a 1-1 draw with France.
Barella missed out on the matchday squad for the Turkiye trip, and was only used as a substitute in Paris. He has featured for only 108 minutes across the three games so far.
During that time, Barella failed to register a goal or an assist.
However, he is expected to line up for the Azzurri in Bologna on Monday.
Speaking to reporters before the game, Barella said: "I am not old, but I do have a lot of games in my legs and have had to learn how to listen to my body.
"Playing 70 games a year, you don't have the same sharpness you did at age 23, but looking at the statistics, I am still one of those who covers the most ground.
"The only thing I'm lacking for the Nazionale is a few goals. That is where I'm lagging behind."
When asked about his response to not starting against France, Barella simply replied: "This is a team sport, it's not tennis."
Barella also spoke glowingly of Mancini, who he won the European Championship under in 2021.

"One of the best things about the coach is that he allows us players to feel a sense of peace. We had some very difficult and not positive experiences in recent years, especially when it comes to me, Gianluigi Donnarumma and Alessandro Bastoni," Barella said.
"The coach asked us to rediscover our enthusiasm, and I think we are doing that, because otherwise we wouldn't have got back on track in France and then nearly won it at the end."

1fx6014g8ajgl1xs79ntj1rz27.title: 'It's very hard to say no' to Napoli, says Gilmour
1fx6014g8ajgl1xs79ntj1rz27.subtitle: Billy Gilmour is playing his third season for Napoli, after getting an offer he could not refuse from them back in the summer of 2024.
paragraphs: Billy Gilmour admitted it was "very hard to say no" when Napoli approached him while at Brighton.
Gilmour spent two years with the Seagulls before making the move from the Amex Stadium to Napoli in August 2024, signing a five-year contract in Italy.
He has made 52 appearances for the Partenopei in all competitions and won the Scudetto in his first season at the club, under Antonio Conte.
The midfielder scored the first goal of his club career last term, netting in a 3-2 win over Pisa, and he has also hit the back of the net in 2026-27, in a 1-1 draw with Fiorentina.
"It's an exciting league,” Gilmour told Premier Sports TV.
"When you have these big clubs from Italy who approach and say they want to sign you, it's very hard to say no.
"I wanted to come here; I wanted to challenge for trophies and be at such a great club."
Gilmour signed for Napoli on the same day as Scotland team-mate Scott McTominay, who has taken Napoli by storm since his debut.
McTominay was named the Serie A Player of the Year in 2025 for his part in Napoli's Scudetto success, while he has been named in the league's Team of the Year in both of his seasons so far.
The 29-year-old has made 82 appearances, scoring 27 goals, though he is currently sidelined following heart surgery to correct a mild cardiac arrhythmia.
He is expected to return after the international break.
"Since he's been here, Scott's confidence has grown massively," Gilmour said.
"You can see how much he means to the fans and to us as players; we can rely on him whenever we need a goal and need help. The same goes for Scotland.
"We're missing Scott now, and hopefully things went well; we can't wait to have him back."

1fzdvkfezt9fe1nqwb3atnr56w.title: Mbappe: Working under Zidane 'like something from a movie'
1fzdvkfezt9fe1nqwb3atnr56w.subtitle: Current Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe will link up with former Blancos hero Zinedine Zidane for the first time this week, with France.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe has likened being coached by Zinedine Zidane to "something from a movie", as France prepare to play their first game under the legendary former midfielder.
Zidane succeeded Didier Deschamps in the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup, which saw France reach the semi-finals before losing 2-0 to eventual champions Spain.

Deschamps led Les Bleus for 14 years and 187 matches in total (also 103 as a player), overseeing their second World Cup triumph in 2018 in addition to runner-up finishes at the 2022 edition and at Euro 2016, with the latter tournament being on home soil.
And France's new era begins with a Nations League trip to Turkiye on Friday, with matches against Belgium – both home and away – and Italy to follow in the next two weeks.
Zidane made 108 appearances for France during his illustrious playing career, scoring 31 goals including a brace in their win over Brazil in the 1998 World Cup final.
He also scored a Panenka penalty in the 2006 final before receiving a red card for an infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi, as Italy went on to defeat Les Bleus on spot-kicks.
And Mbappe – who will keep hold of the captain's armband under the new regime – has a chance to pass Zidane in the all-time France appearance charts during the extended international break.
Mbappe's next cap will be his 107th, so he could potentially equal Zidane against Belgium next Monday and surpass him versus Italy on October 2, should he appear in all of those matches.

In an interview with AS, Mbappe recalled his first meeting with Zidane, which came when he was a youth player attracting interest from Europe's top clubs, while the former midfield icon was working in Real Madrid's academy.
"Years ago, he was the first to pick me up ‌and ⁠take me to Real Madrid, to the training complex. I was 13 or 14; it was ages ago," Mbappe said.
"And now he's my national team coach. It's like something from a movie, but he's top-level.
"It's real, we're in a new process in France, we have two years to prepare for the European Championships and we're working towards it now."

Zidane is the only manager to win three successive Champions League crowns, doing so with Real Madrid between 2015-16 and 2017-18, but he neglected to take another job in club football after leaving the Santiago Bernabeu for the second time in 2021.
He repeatedly outlined his interest in the France job during the latter years of Deschamps' tenure, and Mbappe is excited to see what changes he makes.
"It's a new phase with a new coach. It's going ⁠to be a new experience for everyone, since we've only ever had Deschamps," Mbappe said.
"It will be a change for us, but I think ⁠everything will turn out very well."

1gbxvraddlm741a2vdd005k0y5.title: Slegers: Big Arsenal squad is a 'luxury problem'
1gbxvraddlm741a2vdd005k0y5.subtitle: Renee Slegers is prepared to rotate her Arsenal squad ahead of their Women's Champions League opener against Koge.
paragraphs: Renee Slegers believes having a large squad is a "luxury problem" as Arsenal prepare for their Women's Champions League opener against Koge.
Arsenal won the Champions League in 2024-25 but fell at the semi-final hurdle last season, as Lyon came from behind to beat them on aggregate and reach the showpiece.
The Gunners, who also finished as runners-up to Manchester City in the Women's Super League last term, bolstered their squad over the summer as they aim to fight for silverware once again.

They brought in eight new signings, including Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodriguez, but so far, it has not had the desired effect, with Arsenal winning just one of their three WSL games (D2).
Slegers' side have a big week ahead of them, with a WSL clash with Chelsea to come after their Champions League outing.
But Slegers pointed out that Arsenal were prepared for their packed schedule.
"It's a luxury problem, of course," Slegers said when asked if a big squad was a nice problem to have.
"We have so many different options. The balance becomes, or the challenge becomes, how do you then choose certain things for certain games?
"We're still keeping the main ideas and consistency within the team. You don't chop and change everything.
"At the same time, if I look at where the players are at and where we are, from a game model understanding and players playing their roles, it's on a really high level throughout the squad.
"That also makes me really confident to say, 'I can make changes. These partnerships are working. This is working. This player knows her role on the pitch'.
"It's in a really good place, and that's where we wanted it to be. For the length of the season and all the games that we're going to play, we are able to do these things.

"The reason why we have the size of the squad with basically only senior national team players, so much quality doubled up in every position, is that we can use the whole squad. Especially when it's short turnarounds and we need freshness."
Arsenal are heavy favourites to beat Koge, with an 81.1% win probability according to the Opta supercomputer.
They have won both of their previous meetings with Koge in the Champions League, beating them twice in the 2021-22 group stage (3-0 home, 5-1 away).
However, Arsenal have lost their opening game in each of the last two Champions League seasons: 2-5 to Bayern Munich in 2024-25 and 1-2 to Lyon in 2025-26.
Slegers is also familiar with Koge herself, having faced them while in charge of Rosengard, and she is expecting a tough challenge.
"They're, of course, top of the league in Denmark," Slegers said. "They're a good team.

"I think they have a really good counter-attacking threat with the two players up top. They will try to close down spaces. We're expecting that, whether it's a back four or back five, we'll see when they come out.
"We're definitely respecting the threat that they can pose from fast attacks and counter-attacks. But, again, we're expecting to face a low block."

1gh6km6ztujfn1mybx1zd8jx6l.title: Pocognoli wants first Scotland win for the players' sake
1gh6km6ztujfn1mybx1zd8jx6l.subtitle: Sebastien Pocognoli is still waiting for his first win as Scotland boss, and he knows his players need more confidence.
paragraphs: Sebastien Pocognoli is eager to win his first game as Scotland boss so his players can grow in confidence.
Pocognoli's reign as Scotland boss began with a goalless draw with Slovenia, though his first home match ended in a 3-0 defeat against Switzerland after Jack Hendry was sent off early on.
Scotland have failed to score in each of their last four internationals for only the second time in their history, after May 1971; they have never gone five straight games without a goal.

Pocognoli (D1 L1) could become only the fourth Scotland manager to fail to win any of their first three games in charge of the national team after John Prentice, Berti Vogts and George Burley, with the trio all failing to win any of their first four matches.
While Pocognoli denied suggestions Scotland must beat North Macedonia on Saturday, he knows they need a win sooner rather than later.
"No, because the challenge is longer than this camp, you know, we have to do piece by piece," Pocognoli told BBC Scotland when asked about feeling pressure for the win.
"For sure, we want to have a first really positive [win] on the pitch.

"In terms of ranking, we want this, but I think it's important for the players to have a first win, that everything makes sense because the win makes the joy and the joy gives the freedom on the pitch to make decisions and to accelerate the process.
"If we have the three points in Slovenia, which I think we deserve, we talk maybe a little bit differently, but it's like this."
Scotland have lost only one of their previous seven away matches in all competitions (W4 D2), keeping a clean sheet in five of those matches.
After losing their first ever encounter with North Macedonia in September 2008 (0-1), Scotland are unbeaten in their three meetings since (W2 D1), winning 2-1 most recently in September 2013.

1gpk2w4i99ndh1glrfkpp13zyb.title: Cifuentes urges Portland to find clinical edge ahead of trip to San Jose
1gpk2w4i99ndh1glrfkpp13zyb.subtitle: The Portland Timbers will be looking to keep their playoff hopes alive when they make the trip to the San Jose Earthquakes this weekend.
paragraphs: Marti Cifuentes believes the only thing missing from his Portland Timbers team is the final product in attack after their disappointing defeat to Atlanta United last time out.
Portland were beaten 1-0 by the Five Stripes at Providence Park, with Aleksey Miranchuk's 28th-minute strike enough to compound the Timbers to a 12th defeat of the season.
That is despite Portland registering an expected goals (xG) total of 2.3 from their 21 shots at Lucas Hoyos' net to Atlanta's tally of 0.85 from their 10 attempts.

It was a result that left the Timbers in a precarious position in the Western Conference, with Cifuentes' side ninth in the division, but the Seattle Sounders, San Diego FC and Austin FC are all within striking distance.

Portland's struggles against teams below them in the standings has been a recurring theme in 2026, and ahead of a trip to PayPal Park to face the San Jose Earthquakes, Cifuentes wants his team to take their chances when they arrive.
"We created more shots, we regained the ball higher up the pitch and there was a lot of positives, but that does not explain the whole history," Cifuentes said.
"The whole history is that we need to be better in front of goal and we need to be more clinical. We need to be better in how we break down low blocks and so on.
"It's going to be a good challenge against San Jose because of the situations we are talking about. There are a lot of situations, but I do not want to spend my time there.
"I want to be focused, be positive and have a lot of energy to go to San Jose that are having a good season, and try to leave there with a good feeling."
San Jose, meanwhile, kept their playoff push going with a 2-2 draw against 10-man Los Angeles FC, with Reid Roberts scoring a 98th-minute equaliser for Bruce Arena's side.
Son Heung-min had given LAFC the lead before Aaron Long was sent off, but Denis Bouanga doubled the visitors' lead eight minutes into the second half at Levi's Stadium.
However, substitute Preston Judd halved the deficit, before Roberts' drive from distance nestled into the bottom-right corner to seal a share of the spoils.
The Earthquakes are fifth in the West and just two points off fourth-place FC Dallas, and Arena believes their draw with LAFC was a true test of his team's character against a difficult opposition.
"The fact that we went down two goals and came back and got a point out of the game is a tremendous test of character and competitiveness on our part," Arena said.
"I thought LAFC did an outstanding job in trying to close out the game. So give both teams credit. This was a really good MLS game today. A lot of quality out there.
"I think that was a very entertaining game for the people here, and to see players like Son [Heung-min] and [Denis] Bouanga and [Hugo] Lloris, he was fantastic.
"And to see quality like [Timo] Werner and have those kinds of players on the field, that was enjoyable and a great setting. The fan base was great. So a good day for MLS."
SJ Earthquakes – Reid Roberts
Roberts scored at 97:32 to secure a deserved point against LAFC last time out.

It was the latest result-changing goal by an Earthquakes player in an MLS match since Shea Salinas (97:34) scored a match-winning goal on July 15, 2020, in the MLS is Back Group Stage against the Vancouver Whitecaps.
Portland Timbers – Kristoffer Velde
Among players currently on the Timbers roster, Velde leads Portland in both goals (eight) and assists (nine).

With another assist, Velde would become the fifth player in club history have 10+ assists in a single MLS regular season, joining Diego Valeri (five), Sebastian Blanco (twice), Evander and Santiago Moreno.
MATCH PREDICTION: SJ EARTHQUAKES WIN

San Jose are unbeaten in their last four games with Portland (W3 D1) across all competitions, including a 3-1 win away from home in May. The Earthquakes have never swept the season series, while the four-match unbeaten run is their longest in the fixture since the Timbers joined MLS in 2011.

The Earthquakes' 12 victories this season are their most wins in a single season since the team's 13-win campaign in 2019. After having 11 wins in 2025, it marks the first time San Jose have recorded double-digit wins in back-to-back seasons since 2012 and 2013.

Portland, meanwhile, have failed to record a clean sheet on the road this regular season, one of four MLS teams without one. The Timbers have never gone a full MLS regular season without a road clean sheet after equalling their club record with five during the 2025 season.
Portland Timbers – 27.3%
