1gx0lwmkxy6021ggesfypovjdc.title: Pochettino names 'perfect role model' Adams as new USA captain
1gx0lwmkxy6021ggesfypovjdc.subtitle: Following Tim Ream's retirement from international football, Tyler Adams will once again wear the armband for the United States.
paragraphs: Mauricio Pochettino has named "perfect role model" Tyler Adams as the United States' new captain.
The decision comes after previous captain Tim Ream announced his retirement from international football, with Adams taking on the role for the second time.
The Bournemouth midfielder led the USA at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, where they were knocked out in the last 16 by the Netherlands.
Pochettino's side reached the same stage this summer when they hosted the tournament, and he believes Adams is the right person to lead the team through the next World Cup cycle.
"I think [we're] so happy to announce and for everyone to know that he's going to be our leader and our captain," Pochettino said about Adams.

"I think we've been [in] a very good relationship in the last two years. I think we were talking a lot, and I think he knows what I expect, and he's a perfect role model for everyone in the way that the philosophy, the future, representing that amazing country.
"I think he's the player and the person that can lead that period that we have ahead. And I [say] congratulations."
The USA have impressed during this international break, following up a 4-1 win over Peru with a 4-2 victory over Chile.
Next up for Pochettino's side is a clash with rivals Mexico, and the former Tottenham boss feels a tough atmosphere at State Farm Stadium will help his team grow.
"I think this type of adversity is a good example," added Pochettino.
"I celebrate to have this type of game, to play in a difficult atmosphere, and I think that for sure is going to help for the future."

1h0myvt5xzcp01iwot46hhqt3d.title: 'This is what we love' – Zidane revels in France's comeback win
1h0myvt5xzcp01iwot46hhqt3d.subtitle: Zinedine Zidane remains unbeaten in charge of France after his first international break, with his substitutions securing three more points.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane hailed France's "complete team performance" after they came from behind to beat Belgium in the Nations League.

France triumphed 4-1 at the Stade de France, but Zidane's unbeaten start with Les Bleus looked under real threat when they still trailed through Dodi Lukebakio's 35th-minute goal heading into the final 13 minutes.
However, Zidane's substitutions more than paid off, with Desire Doue drawing France level before Rayan Cherki put them ahead four minutes later.
And a three-minute brace from Michael Olise, who also set up Cherki's goal, then rounded off the scoring to give France a stunning win that puts them within touching distance of the quarter-finals.
France were completely dominant, with the scoreline eventually reflecting that, and Zidane revelled in the stunning comeback victory.
"This is soccer, this is what we love," Zidane said.
"We faced some difficulties in the first half, but that's part of the game; it's the kind of match you get from time to time.
"It's good to set things right – which is what we did – and we managed to play an extraordinary second half.
"We knew the substitutes could change the game because they are high-quality players.

"But, once again, it was a complete team performance; while the substitutes might have made the difference when they came on, everyone has been good over these past two weeks – everyone played their part, and that's what stands out to me."
Doue, Cherki and Olise were all spellbinding. Each of them crafted two chances, while Olise ended up having four shots, a total bettered only by Ousmane Dembele (five).
Olise has scored in his last three games in the Nations League (four goals), with no France player netting more than him in this international break.
"It's a collective effort, too," Olise said.
"He [Zidane] brings in ideas; we follow them – we've done that well over the last four matches, we're going to continue like this."

1hnz40ler5mb114h0wtlanlxld.title: Olise 'a pure talent' but Zidane lauds team effort from France
1hnz40ler5mb114h0wtlanlxld.subtitle: While reserving praise for France match-winner Michael Olise, Zinedine Zidane was pleased to see everyone contribute against Belgium.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane hailed the "pure talent" of Michael Olise after France's win over Belgium on Monday, but he was also glad to see other players contribute after making sweeping changes.
Zidane made nine alterations to the team that beat Turkiye 1-0 in his first game in charge last Friday, as Les Bleus made the short trip across the border to face Belgium in the Nations League.
Captain Kylian Mbappe was absent due to a minor left knee injury, but fellow star Olise came off the bench to provide the decisive moment in the 88th minute.

The Bayern Munich man travelled from inside his own half before slotting a neat finish into the bottom-left corner from the edge of the area, taking him to 13 goal involvements in his last 14 appearances for France (four goals, nine assists).
Zidane said of Olise afterwards, as quoted by L'Equipe: "He's a pure talent – I like this type of player. He wants to please people when he plays, but not only that.
"He feels football, he knows when to go and when to slow things down. I'm happy to be by his side, to see him play like this."
But Zidane was also impressed by many of those players that came into his lineup.

Paris Saint-Germain's Maghnes Akliouche created three chances and played a game-high 35 passes into the final third, while his club-made Desire Doue created four chances, attempted five shots and completed five dribbles.

It was just the fifth instance of a France player creating four or more chances, attempting five or more shots and completing at least five dribbles in a single game on record, after Nicolas Anelka (vs Faroe Islands in 2009), Franck Ribery (vs Belarus in 2012), and Mbappe twice (vs South Africa in 2022 and Azerbaijan in 2025).
Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet was another impressive performer at the back, completing 91.8% of his passes (67/73) and winning six of his nine duels.
"I'm very satisfied with what the team did, and not only with the ball. Like the match in Turkiye, but on a much better pitch, we were very good everywhere," Zidane added.
"We put things in place against a good Belgium team who also made us suffer, but we held on, we were brave, we weren't afraid to go into the opponents' half.
"That's what I like, that's what we want. We may have dropped a little bit in the second half, when we had some small difficulties, but that's logical.
"We made nine changes, but what I like about this team is that everyone feels involved."
France are back in action on Friday, with Italy visiting the Stade de France, before they round out the international break with another home game against Turkiye next week.

1i1sr8r1omutk154g1rmdpvz1g.title: Saka: Scars still remain from England's World Cup defeat to Argentina
1i1sr8r1omutk154g1rmdpvz1g.subtitle: England are preparing to begin their Nations League campaign, but Bukayo Saka said their World Cup exit was still fresh in the memory.
paragraphs: Bukayo Saka believes England's players are still scarred from their heartbreaking defeat to Argentina in the semi-finals of this summer's World Cup.
England were on the brink of reaching the World Cup final for the first time since winning the tournament in 1966, after Anthony Gordon's 55th-minute strike gave them the lead.
However, a Lionel Messi-orchestrated comeback saw Argentina score two goals in seven minutes late on to end the Three Lions' dreams of lifting the trophy.
Argentina were trailing until the 85th minute against England, the latest a team has been behind but gone on to win in normal time in a World Cup semi-final.
The Three Lions did, however, achieve their second-best finish at the World Cup after beating France in a thrilling third-place match, with Saka scoring a hat-trick in a 6-4 win.
But Saka, who was an unused substitute in England's defeat to Argentina, said there were still feelings of regret within the squad about their shortcomings at the World Cup.
"Obviously, there is still a scar on us when you believed and everyone was so united and so confident we could do it," Saka said.
"Not just us, but the whole country felt it. You try to move on as soon as possible, but you know, a scar is a scar, it decides to heal when it heals itself."
Argentina would go on to lose the final to Spain at MetLife Stadium, and Luis de la Fuente's side are up next for England in the first match of their Nations League campaign.

England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2). Those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).
Spain have also won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the final of Euro 2024.

Thomas Tuchel's side welcome Spain to Wembley Stadium in the first of four matches during the extended international break, with further matches against Croatia and Czechia (both home and away) to come.
It will be the first time England have stepped out onto the pitch since their third-place finish, and Saka insists their full focus is on making a good start in the Nations League.
"We are trying to draw a line under [the World Cup] now and focus on the new international season that we have coming up," Saka added.
"We have got four massive, difficult group games to try and qualify us for the Nations League [knockouts] that we are really focused on."

1ipyu2d1qzq1m1o208cjvigsew.title: Konate withdraws from France squad, Yoro called up
1ipyu2d1qzq1m1o208cjvigsew.subtitle: Ibrahima Konate has suffered a minor injury which has ruled him out of France's first four Nations League matches/
paragraphs: Ibrahima Konate has withdrawn from France's Nations League squad through injury, with Leny Yoro receiving his first call-up to the senior squad.
Konate felt pain in his right knee during Wednesday's training session and underwent an MRI.
He has been diagnosed with a minor sprain and released back to Real Madrid, for whom he has made seven appearances in all competitions since moving from Liverpool.
Following his withdrawal, Zidane has called on Manchester United's Yoro, who had initially been called up to the Under-21s squad.

1iyf7aju7687szj7i373ue45u.title: Joao Felix confident goals will come under new Portugal boss Jesus
1iyf7aju7687szj7i373ue45u.subtitle: Jorge Jesus began his Portugal tenure with a win over Wales in the Nations League, and Joao Felix is excited about what the future holds.
paragraphs: Joao Felix believes it is only a matter of time before Portugal find their shooting boots under new boss Jorge Jesus after they beat Wales 1-0 in the Nations League on Thursday.
Jesus was taking charge of Portugal for the first time following Roberto Martinez's departure, and his team made a blistering start to the match at Estadio Jose Alvalade.
Portugal eventually took the lead in the 22nd minute through Joao Felix, who picked out the bottom-left corner from outside the box after good work from full-back Nuno Mendes.
Cristiano Ronaldo spurned two chances at the end of a dominant first half that saw Portugal register 13 shots, their most in the opening 45 minutes of a game since November 2025 against Armenia (17).

Ronaldo should have doubled Portugal's lead early in the second half, but he could only turn Ruben Neves' delivery over the crossbar, with the five-time Ballon d'Or winner then seeing a goal ruled out for offside soon after.

But the Selecao were made to work for their win, with Wales coming on strong as the match progressed. Brennan Johnson lifted an effort onto the crossbar, with Ruben Dias on hand to clear Lewis Koumas' rebound off the line.

Portugal are now unbeaten in their last 10 home matches in all competitions (W9 D1), while in competitive games it’s 13 unbeaten since a 1-0 defeat to Spain in September 2022 (W12 D1), and Joao Felix is confident things will only get better under Jesus.
"We knew it wasn't going to be an easy game. Wales are a good team," Joao Felix told Sport TV. "The first game under a new coach is always difficult.
"We had very little time to work on the coach's game patterns, but I think that, overall, we played a great game and we deserve to be commended.
"I think we could see our dynamic, very attacking football, high pressing, without giving the opponent any space to breathe.
"We had 13 shots before half-time, which is a lot for the first half. I don't remember a single clear chance for them, when we had several.
"That's what people can expect. Attacking football, pressing, not letting opponents breathe and creating chances.
"We only scored one today, but in the next few games, if we continue like this, we will surely score more."

Joao Felix has now scored five goals across his last 10 starts for Portugal, while each of his last two goals have come from outside the box, as many as his first 11 for the national team, and he looks set to play a big role under Jesus.
The 26-year-old has worked with Jesus before at Al-Nassr, scoring 20 goals in 33 appearances on their way to the Saudi Pro League title in 2025-26.
Jesus made the decision to deploy Joao Felix in the second striker position, just behind Ronaldo and with Bruno Fernandes, Vitinha and Pedro Neto around him.
"I've always been myself; I always tried to do my best for the team, no matter what position I was playing," Joao Felix added.
"As I've always said, my position is right here, as a second striker. If this is the case, there is a much higher chance that things will go well.
"This is what happened last year. Today, the whole team delivered a good performance, and that's where I can help them the most."
It proved to be a frustrating match for Ronaldo, whose seven shots without scoring is his most in a game since a World Cup qualifier against Republic of Ireland in October 2025 (also seven).
Ronaldo was replaced by Goncalo Ramos in the 67th minute, and Jesus said the decision to substitute the Portugal captain was pre-planned.

"I took him out 25 minutes before the end of the game because I thought it was important to have a fresh player on the pitch who was able to defend with pressure and not let the central defenders of Wales build the game," Jesus said.
"I wanted to have a player at the first line with speed, and I knew that Goncalo Ramos could do that.
"I knew that Cris could stay a little longer, five to 10 minutes. But I would have taken him out anyway. I planned it."

1jdlty23ofll61aneb4fxs4e83.title: Schmetzer senses positive momentum after end to Seattle's winless run
1jdlty23ofll61aneb4fxs4e83.subtitle: The Seattle Sounders finally ended their 13-game winless run in MLS this week, and they have a home match against Minnesota United next up.
paragraphs: Brian Schmetzer already believed the Seattle Sounders were building some momentum even before they ended their four-month wait for a victory on Wednesday, as they look to go back-to-back against Minnesota United.
The Sounders went 13 games without victory after beating the San Jose Earthquakes on May 13, prior to the World Cup break.

They lost eight straight matches before turning the corner somewhat by drawing five in a row, prior to overcoming Real Salt Lake – who are also on a long winless streak of their own – by a 2-0 scoreline in midweek.
Now only outside the playoff spots on games won in the Western Conference, Seattle will look to inject some more impetus at home to Minnesota on Saturday.
But Schmetzer believes they were already on an upward trajectory of sorts, saying: "Well, I think we've already been starting to build – the five draws have been something.
"It's been a long time – May 13, for the guys that are publishing the facts. I think all the people in this room are good reporters. There's no fake news in here!
"I told those guys in there to enjoy the moment. And on a personal note, there were fans behind the bench saying, 'Congratulations Brian, enjoy this moment'.

"So I listened to those fans, and I told the same thing to the guys in there. I think we've been building some momentum, but this really gives them a lot of belief and that’s what we discussed before the game."
Minnesota are second from bottom in the West, albeit only three points behind the Sounders, after losing four straight games.

Their most recent defeat came by a 3-2 scoreline against the LA Galaxy last weekend, and if the Loons are to make a late push for the postseason, head coach Cameron Knowles knows it will take a collective effort.
"We're going to need everyone. We need everyone to push, whether it's in training during the week or whether it's coming into a game," he said.
"We need guys to step up and everyone to give exactly what they're capable of. Everyone in that locker room has shown they're capable of contributing."
PLAYERS TO WATCH
Seattle Sounders – Paul Arriola
Arriola assisted both Seattle goals against RSL on Wednesday, while he also had a joint-game-high three shots and the only Opta-defined 'big' chance of the match.
He also scored his first MLS goal for the Sounders earlier this month, to salvage a point against the Galaxy in a 1-1 draw on September 12.
Minnesota United – Kelvin Yeboah
Only Lionel Messi (20), Petar Musa (18), Brian White and Sam Surridge (16 each) have scored more goals in MLS this year than Yeboah's 14.
The Minnesota forward – who was on target against the Galaxy last weekend – also ranks third in the league for expected goals (14.6 xG), only behind Messi (17.2) and White (16.1).
MATCH PREDICTION: SEATTLE SOUNDERS WIN
When these two sides last met in MLS action, they played out a 0-0 draw at Allianz Field in March.
All of a sudden, Seattle's club-record winless streak has turned into a six-game unbeaten run, even if they did play out five draws in that time.
And they are the Opta supercomputer's favourites for this one, with Minnesota only managing one win in their last six MLS games (D1 L4).

Away from home, the Loons have lost their last two matches while conceding a total of nine goals (5-4 at Portland Timbers, 4-2 at St. Louis City SC), so without a big defensive improvement, they could be up against it.
Seattle Sounders – 45.8%
Minnesota United – 30.5%

1jgp0v4sjcfm117ra12teh8jg3.title: Barcelona defender Garcia leaves Spain squad after knee injury
1jgp0v4sjcfm117ra12teh8jg3.subtitle: Robin Le Normand has been called up to the Spain squad by Luis De la Fuente after Barcelona's Eric Garcia picked up a knee injury.
paragraphs: Robin Le Normand has replaced Eric Garcia in the Spain squad after the Barcelona defender picked up a knee injury.
Garcia did not feature in Spain's thrilling win over England in their Nations League opener, with Aymeric Laporte and Pau Cubarsi starting at centre-back for Luis De la Fuente's side.
The 25-year-old has featured in six of Barca's eight games this season, with the Blaugrana making the perfect start to the 2026-27 campaign.
Garcia leads Barca defenders in tackles won this season (10), while he has won the third-most duels (21), completed the third-most passes (393) and recorded the fourth-most clearances (16).
Spain released a statement which read: "Atletico Madrid player Robin Le Normand replaces Eric Garcia in the Spanish national team camp, which is playing in the UEFA Nations League group stage.

"The Barcelona centre-back felt some discomfort in his left knee and after the tests carried out, it has been decided to withdraw him from the squad due to the proximity of the upcoming international matches, thus avoiding any risk and preserving the player's health."
Following their win at Wembley Stadium, Spain host Croatia and Czechia before a return fixture against the former in the remainder of this international break.
Spain are unbeaten in their last 39 matches, the longest such run among all European nations in all competitions (W30 D9).

1jnuwjy0wm41s191l5w5d11b1n.title: Bellamy insists Wales 'performance was more important' than win over Norway
1jnuwjy0wm41s191l5w5d11b1n.subtitle: Wales came from behind to defeat 10-man Norway at Cardiff City Stadium, but Craig Bellamy took more pleasure in their display than the win.
paragraphs: Craig Bellamy insisted Wales' "performance was more important" than their win over Norway on Thursday.
Wales came from behind to defeat 10-man Norway 2-1 in the Nations League, ending a seven-match winless run across all competitions.
Daniel James cancelled out Oscar Bobb's opener before Torbjorn Heggem was shown a straight red card early in the second half, with Neco Williams scoring the winner from the resulting free-kick.

Heggem was sent off just 21 seconds following the restart, making it the quickest-ever second-half red card in a Nations League match, while this was Wales' first win after falling behind since November 2024 against Iceland (4-1).
While Bellamy was pleased with the three points, he took more pride in Wales' display at Cardiff City Stadium.
"Really pleasing. The performance was more important, to look like us," Bellamy told BBC Match of the Day Wales.
"We've worked hard to get to Nations League A and we know the teams are littered and loaded with good players.
"I know we've got a lot of players out, but we still have to be us. So that was nice and was pleasing.
"The last few days in training, we had an identity meeting. I have to give credit to the players, they've been brilliant.
"What do we want to do? Do we want to sit deep and play on counter-attacks or do we want to be aggressive and be on the front foot and keep the ball when we have it?
"That's really it. I think that's us. We do have to punch above our weight, but let's give it a right go. That's always been brought to me as a Welsh person growing up."
Norway struggled after going a man down, though Erling Haaland uncharacteristically missed a great chance at 2-1.
The visitors would have been optimistic after Martin Odegaard, who has assisted 14 goals in his last 15 matches for Norway, was declared fit, but Heggem's dismissal proved too much to come back from.
Stale Solbakken told TV 2 Play: "I think we were too careful in the first half. Far too much back-and-forth football."

1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.title: Carrick understands jeers from Man Utd fans after Mainoo substitution
1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.subtitle: Manchester United's travelling fans made their feelings known when Kobbie Mainoo was substituted with 10 minutes to play against Fulham.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick understands the "emotional" reactions to Manchester United's recent struggles, after his decision to withdraw Kobbie Mainoo against Fulham was booed by their travelling fans.
With just five points on the board after five games, United have made their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign, having also taken five at this stage of 2014-15.

Things could have been worse for the Red Devils at Craven Cottage on Sunday, too, as Matheus Cunha's deflected strike snatched a point in the 89th minute, after Lisandro Martinez's calamitous own goal had put them on the back foot.
With United 1-0 down and chasing the game, Carrick's choice to replace Mainoo with Mason Mount in the 80th minute was loudly jeered by the away end.
Mainoo had completed 64 of his 68 passes, 27 of which were in the final third, with only Bryan Mbeumo (100%) and Harry Maguire (95.8%) bettering his 94.1% pass accuracy among United's starters.
But Carrick feels that reaction came from a place of frustration and understands the disgruntled feeling among the fanbase.
"There are always going to be certain reactions when you're making changes," Carrick said. "I've spoken to Kobbie after the game and he's absolutely fine.
"I understand at times when we are chasing the game, everyone's a little bit emotional. The supporters are – as they should be – desperate for us to do the right thing.
"But I don't take any negatives or offence to it. I think we've just got to try and keep doing the right things to get back into the game.
"The supporters were unbelievable, I have to say, all the way through. They stuck with the boys and supported them.
"At least we've given them something small at the end to take from it, and I'm sure there's more to come."

With United 12th in the Premier League table going into the extended international break, the Opta supercomputer only assigns them a 17% chance of qualifying for the Champions League, but Carrick is sure there are plenty of twists and turns ahead.
"It's still a big season ahead," Carrick said. "It's a long season, and you're going to have these spells through a season. That's part of the journey. It's not a sprint; it's a long effort.
"I'm not playing it down. We wanted more points, so I'm not saying everything's great. I understand the frustration. We wanted to be better, and we wanted to do other things.
"But deflation is certainly not what we have within the club and within the group. The players didn't have that on the pitch, and that's what will carry us through the season, without a doubt."
United face Tottenham, who are still winless and prop up the table, in their next Premier League game on October 10.

1k36x0k0emsqb12pwrssuggwq0.title: England 2-3 Spain: Oyarzabal completes comeback to seal world champions victory
1k36x0k0emsqb12pwrssuggwq0.subtitle: England mounted a first-half comeback to lead at the break, but Spain refused to give up and completed their own turnaround to earn the win.
paragraphs: Mikel Oyarzabal scored the winner against England once again as Spain came from behind to win 3-2 in their Nations League opener.
Lamine Yamal gave the world champions an early lead before Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane flipped the script before the break.

But after Kane missed a penalty, Spain rallied to earn three points in their first match since the World Cup final, with Alex Baena equalising before Oyarzabal securing the victory, just as he did in the Euro 2024 final.

Spain made the perfect start at Wembley, with Marc Guehi dispossessed as he turned back towards his own goal. Yamal picked his pocket and ruthlessly punished the mistake, turning his shot in off the inside of the far post just two minutes in.
Ferran Torres then saw a goal disallowed shortly after; Fabian Ruiz bent a lovely cross into the box, but the striker's diving header was ruled out for offside.
Ferran then saw two golden opportunities go begging, with James Trafford making himself big to smother a one-on-one shot, before firing wide from a similar position.
An exquisite Yamal backheel slipped in Dani Olmo, who fired wide from a tight angle, before Kane bent one wide at the other end in England's first clear-cut opener.

But England needed just four minutes to flip the game on its head. Nico Williams' slip opened the door for a pacy counter-attack, and Gordon played a one-two with Jude Bellingham before slotting it past Unai Simon from the edge of the box 36 minutes in.
And with Spain on the ropes, Kane met Nico O'Reilly's chipped cross after getting in front of Aymeric Laporte, and Marc Cucurella could only help it in off his thigh.

Spain also conceded more goals in the first 45 minutes (two) than they did in the entirety of their World Cup-winning campaign (one).

1k97az1e32wuy15jn6xdw82rel.title: 'We will get through this' – Guardiola addresses Man City fans after Premier League verdict
1k97az1e32wuy15jn6xdw82rel.subtitle: Pep Guardiola has responded after Manchester City were found guilty of "systematically" breaking the Premier League's rules.
paragraphs: Pep Guardiola has addressed Manchester City's fans after the club were found guilty of serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18, saying: "We will get through this together."
In February 2023, the Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 breaches of the competition's rules across a nine-year period.

And in a statement released on Tuesday, the Premier League confirmed City had been found guilty of all charges that related to serious breaches of financial rules and the majority of charges which were "in relation to its failure to co-operate with the league's investigation".

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said City had "systematically broken Premier League Rules for nearly a decade" and described the decision as the "most significant" in the competition's history.

City have pledged to fight the ruling and have until October 2 to exercise their right to appeal, with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak saying last Friday he remained confident of proving the club's innocence.
Former City defender Micah Richards – who won a Premier League title and an FA Cup during his time at the Etihad Stadium – said the verdict left him feeling "absolutely devastated".
But former head coach Guardiola issued a more defiant response via his social media channels on Wednesday, outlining his continued support for the club's hierarchy.
"I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever," Guardiola wrote, alongside an image of himself and Al Mubarak.

"I am, always have been, and always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran [Soriano, chief executive of the City Football Group], the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters.
"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."
Guardiola won 20 major trophies during his decade-long stint with City, including six Premier League titles, three FA Cups, five EFL Cups and the Champions League in 2022-23.

1krsbncizt2sz1vrqelj0p9i2y.title: Norway 3-2 Denmark: Haaland brace decides Scandinavian scuffle in Nations League
1krsbncizt2sz1vrqelj0p9i2y.subtitle: Erling Haaland carried his World Cup and Premier League form into the 2026-27 Nations League, as Norway downed rivals Denmark 3-2.
paragraphs: Erling Haaland scored twice as Norway opened their Nations League campaign with an entertaining 3-2 win over Denmark, despite finishing the game with 10 men.

Having trailed 2-0 after just 18 minutes, Denmark fought back valiantly to level Thursday's matchup between Scandinavian rivals, but Haaland's second goal proved to be the winner, with the hosts surviving a late red card for David Moller Wolfe.

Two of Norway's other Premier League stars combined to give them the advantage in the 14th minute, as Oscar Bobb took in Martin Odegaard's cute pass, then shaped a curling finish around Denmark defender Oliver Provstgaard and into the far corner.

And Norway did not have to wait long for their second goal, as Antonio Nusa skipped infield and played a clever reverse pass in behind for Haaland, whose driven finish went straight through Filip Jorgensen.

Denmark found a route back into the contest in the 25th minute, with Mikkel Damsgaard's free-kick dipping over the Norway wall and beating Orjan Nyland, though only a superb reflex stop from Jorgensen prevented Patrick Berg from making it 3-1 late in the first half.
And the visitors drew level on the hour mark, with Rasmus Hojlund reacting quickest to nod home when Nyland blocked Morten Hjulmand's downward header from a corner.

But Haaland re-established Norway's lead when he lashed inside the near post following a well-worked corner routine that saw Odegaard receive a short pass from Nusa, reach the byline, and cut the ball back for the Manchester City talisman.
Moller Wolfe received his second yellow card three minutes into stoppage time, having blocked Gustav Isaksen's run down the right as Denmark chased another equaliser, but Norway held on.
New Nations League campaign, same old Haaland
Haaland's staggering form was one of the stories of this summer's World Cup, as he almost single-handedly powered Norway into the quarter-finals with seven goals in five games.

And he picked up where he left off at the start of their Nations League Group A4 campaign, scoring twice from a game-high five shots (four of which were on target), although his goals were hardly put on a plate, with all those efforts adding up to 0.35 expected goals (xG).
Haaland has now scored in 10 of his last 13 competitive games for Norway and Man City combined (16 goals in total), and in each of his last six (nine goals).

He last enjoyed a longer run between August and October 2025, going 12 straight matches with a goal. With two meetings against Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal to come during this international break, either side of a trip to Wales, Stale Solbakken will be desperate to see that streak continue.

1kunyghi1kc3w1ob361llq135v.title: Milan teenager Cisse has 'only shown 70% of my capabilities so far'
1kunyghi1kc3w1ob361llq135v.subtitle: Alphadjo Cisse has made an impressive start to the season with AC Milan, though he feels he can still offer more for the Rossoneri.
paragraphs: AC Milan teenager Alphadjo Cisse believes he has "only shown 70% of my capabilities so far" this season.
Cisse joined Milan in February, but spent the remainder of the 2025-26 campaign on loan at Catanzaro before breaking into the Rossoneri's first team this summer.
The 19-year-old impressed in pre-season under Ruben Amorim, scoring in their victory over Manchester United before also netting in Milan's Serie A opener over Torino.
Cisse became the youngest Italian player (19 years, 305 days) to score for Milan in Serie A since Patrick Cutrone (19 years, 236 days) did so against Cagliari on August 27, 2017.

And after also scoring in a 1-1 draw with Juventus, Cisse (19 years and 319 days old) became the youngest player to score in his first two away appearances for Milan in Serie A in the three-points-per-win era (since 1994-95).
He took that form into the international break, scoring the only goal in Italy Under-21s' European qualifier victory over Armenia Under-21s.
"This year has brought me a lot of joy," Cisse said in an interview with Rai Sport.
"I’ve only shown 70% of my capabilities so far, I know I can do much better.
"The goal [against Armenia] brings me a lot of happiness, and from now on I hope to be able to show lots of other characteristics."
Milan face Sassuolo in their first match after the international break, before taking on Salzburg in the Europa League.

1kwmnjrbyd9kx1gutn5xedfgxe.title: Chelsea 1-0 Arsenal: Thompson seals derby bragging rights
1kwmnjrbyd9kx1gutn5xedfgxe.subtitle: Chelsea held on to continue their unbeaten start, edging to a narrow victory over Arsenal thanks to Alyssa Thompson's strike.
paragraphs: Alyssa Thompson's first-half strike downed wasteful Arsenal as Chelsea secured a 1-0 win that moved them third in the Women's Super League.

Chelsea took advantage of a sloppy piece of defending from Arsenal six minutes before the break, and Renee Slegers' side could not find an equaliser as they tasted defeat for the first time this season.
Arsenal started fairly well, with Kyra Cooney-Cross causing problems, though she saw an early shot blocked by her own team-mate.
Kim Little – making her 184th WSL appearance for Arsenal – almost caught Chelsea out with a cross that deflected towards goal and had Hannah Hampton worried, but it struck the crossbar.

Mariona Caldentey also struck the woodwork; Alessia Russo started a fast break, picking out Little on the right, and her switch found the Spaniard, who drilled her low shot against the foot of the near post.

But Arsenal created their own problems in the 39th minute, with Steph Catley's loose clearance pounced upon. Kiera Walsh's powerful strike was pushed away by Anneke Borbe, but only as far as Thompson, who emphatically fired into the roof of the net from close range.
Melvine Malard then broke forward on the counter-attack four minutes later, racing down the right with nobody closing her down, but Borbe made herself big to smother the angled attempt.
It was a much-improved Arsenal who emerged after the break, with Lisa Baum and Caldentey both forcing Hampton into action.

Malard then ghosted between two Arsenal defenders only to flick a close-range effort wide, while Stina Blackstenius raced in behind only to chip over under pressure from Hampton, though the offside flag would have denied her anyway.
Arsenal's scoring woes go on as Chelsea stay unbeaten
It was a fairly cagey London derby between two sides who desperately needed a win so they did not lose sight of leaders Manchester City.

Chelsea are now unbeaten across their opening four games of a WSL campaign for the fourth successive season, while Arsenal only have five points to their name at this stage for the second time in the last three seasons (also 2024-25).

Arsenal's attacking troubles have drawn the eye this season as they have netted just two goals this campaign, and despite piling the pressure on Chelsea, especially in the closing stages, they never looked likely to get a goal.
They had 18 shots overall, but only two of those were on target, and their 1.04 expected goals (xG) tells the story of their lack of spark in the box as they dawdled over their chances.

This loss ends Arsenal's 20-game unbeaten league streak, but they will feel they could have had a late equaliser from the spot after a handball by Ellie Carpenter in the box, but nothing was given, with her arm tight to her body when the ball hit her.

Slegers had already beaten Sonia Bompastor twice this calendar year, but the Frenchwoman ensured she came out on top this time, even if she thinks Chelsea could have had more goals after getting seven of their 13 shots on target.

1lcd5udt7pv3314nikbdd0zwhj.title: Croatia 'not afraid' of Spain, says Kovacic
1lcd5udt7pv3314nikbdd0zwhj.subtitle: Croatia are looking to make it two wins from two in the 2026-27 Nations League, but next up for them is a trip to world champions Spain.
paragraphs: Mateo Kovacic insists Croatia are "not afraid of anyone" as they prepare to face world champions Spain in the Nations League.
Spain are the dominant figure in world football at the moment, having clinched their second World Cup over the summer with a 1-0 win over Argentina in the final.
They are currently on a 39-match unbeaten streak (across 90 minutes (W30 D9), the longest such run by a European nation in history.
Croatia won their opening Nations League match 2-1 against Czechia, and sit level on points with Spain, who enjoyed a 3-2 comeback win over England.
But as perhaps expected, Spain are heavy favourites in this clash, with the Opta supercomputer assigning them a 78.3% win probability to Croatia's 8.4%.
Kovacic, however, is not shying away from the challenge ahead of the team.
"Of course. Spain, right now, is the best team in the world," he said. "There's nothing better than playing against the best.

"It will be a difficult match against the best team in the world. But it will be difficult for them too. We have played against them several times, and sometimes we have done very well. Hopefully, we can repeat that.
"We're not afraid of anyone. We respect everyone. Spain is a very strong team. They're very united. They're a top team, but we'll focus on our own game."
Asked if getting a win on Tuesday would be impossible, Kovacic said: "No.
"We know about the 39 games without losing, but I don't want to dwell on that; I want to focus on our game and take the ball away from them."
Spain are unbeaten in their last three meetings with Croatia, winning two and drawing the other – though they eventually won that match on penalties in the Nations League.
Croatia's last win against Spain did come in this competition, winning 3-2 back in November 2018.
And Slaven Bilic is confident Spain are not unbeatable if Croatia can get their game plan right.
"Spain has some strengths that can be exploited, as England showed," Bilic said.
"We don't need a miracle; we need faith. We've played great matches against them. Matches are long.
"Against the Czechs, there were moments when we didn't know how to suffer. We can't repeat that. We know they'll have possession, but it can't always be theirs.
"We must have confidence in what we do, in ourselves."

1lfheoj9g7zqo1aqnm34c53qdf.title: Nico: Newcastle move the best decision I could have ever made
1lfheoj9g7zqo1aqnm34c53qdf.subtitle: Nico Gonzalez has made a strong start to life at Newcastle United, a move he said was the right call in order to progress his career.
paragraphs: Nico Gonzalez believes his move to Newcastle United this summer was the best decision he could have ever made after enjoying a strong start to life at St. James' Park.
Nico put pen to paper on a long-term contract in August for a reported £52m after spending just 18 months with fellow Premier League side Manchester City.
The 24-year-old made 59 appearances for City in all competitions, with 40 of those being starts, scoring four goals before being found surplus to requirements.
Newcastle signed the Spaniard after both Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes departed for big-money fees to Tottenham and Arsenal, respectively.
And Nico has wasted little time in getting used to his new surroundings, ranking sixth in Newcastle's squad for successful passes (155) despite only playing four matches.

He has played a crucial role in Newcastle's Premier League campaign under new boss Matthias Jaissle so far this season, and Nico revealed the atmosphere he experienced as an away player at St. James' was a part of his decision.
"Those moments [the unveiling] were in the middle of so many different emotions," Gonzalez said in an interview with Sky Sports.
"Leaving City, coming here and feeling that, was the best decision I could have ever made."
Jaissle's eight points are the most by a manager in his first five Premier League games in charge of Newcastle since Alan Pardew in January 2011 (nine).
A win against Coventry City next Monday would give him the most points in his first six in charge of the club in the competition (11) since Sam Allardyce in September 2007 (11).
During his time under Pep Guardiola, Nico ranked fourth in City's squad for tackles won (56), successful passes (2,908) and duels won (212).

However, he failed to nail down a starting spot, and with the additions of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi this summer, Nico acknowledged it was time to move on and pursue another challenge away from the Etihad Stadium.
"It was a huge opportunity for me," Gonzalez added.
"I was obviously at a top, top club in Manchester City, but I think Newcastle have been amazing the last few years and have even more potential, so I think we are a top team.
"The best thing is not about being in the best club; it's about enjoying football and being the best that you can, and helping the team.
"I was looking at my options and Newcastle was the best one."

The 24-year-old made 59 appearances for City in all competitions, with 40 of those being starts, scoring four goals before being found surplus to requirements. 

Newcastle signed the Spaniard after both Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes departed for big-money fees to Tottenham and Arsenal, respectively. 

And Nico has wasted little time in getting used to his new surroundings, ranking sixth in Newcastle's squad for successful passes (155) despite only playing four matches.

He has played a crucial role in Newcastle's Premier League campaign under new boss Matthias Jaissle so far this season, and Nico revealed the atmosphere he experienced as an away player at St. James' was a part of his decision. 

"Those moments [the unveiling] were in the middle of so many different emotions," Gonzalez said in an interview with Sky Sports.

"Leaving City, coming here and feeling that, was the best decision I could have ever made."

Jaissle's eight points are the most by a manager in his first five Premier League games in charge of Newcastle since Alan Pardew in January 2011 (nine).

A win against Coventry City next Monday would give him the most points in his first six in charge of the club in the competition (11) since Sam Allardyce in September 2007 (11).

During his time under Pep Guardiola, Nico ranked fourth in City's squad for tackles won (56), successful passes (2,908) and duels won (212). 

However, he failed to nail down a starting spot, and with the additions of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi this summer, Nico acknowledged it was time to move on and pursue another challenge away from the Etihad Stadium. 

"It was a huge opportunity for me," Gonzalez added. 

"I was obviously at a top, top club in Manchester City, but I think Newcastle have been amazing the last few years and have even more potential, so I think we are a top team. 

"The best thing is not about being in the best club; it's about enjoying football and being the best that you can, and helping the team.

"I was looking at my options and Newcastle was the best one."

1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.title: Amorim vows not to repeat Man Utd errors with Milan
1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.subtitle: AC Milan's unbeaten start in Serie A under Ruben Amorim rolled on, and he intends to continue allowing his team to play with freedom.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim insists he will not be pushed into making the same tactical mistakes he made during his stint with Manchester United, now he is in charge of AC Milan.
Amorim's unbeaten start in Serie A continued on Sunday with a comfortable 3-0 win against Lecce at San Siro, with the result moving Milan up to fifth in the standings.
Christian Pulisic's sensational touch and finish put Milan ahead early on, before Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira sealed the win for the Rossoneri during a dominant second half.
Milan's victory saw them remain unbeaten in their opening five Serie A matches of a season for the first time since 2022-23 (W3 D2).

Amorim (W3 D2) has become only the third foreign manager in Milan's history to not taste defeat in each of his first five Serie A games in charge, after Luis Carniglia (W3 D2) and Nils Liedholm (W4 D1), both in 1963-64.

Speaking after the game, Amorim revealed he allowed his side to play with "freedom", and when asked about the reasoning behind that decision, he highlighted his turbulent tenure at Old Trafford, where he was reluctant to adapt his style of play.
"It's an observation of the games and the characteristics," Amorim told DAZN, as quoted by Football Italia.

"Of course, I listen to the players, but a manager, especially in a big team, is always listening to the players, seeing and understanding them, but every player wants to push the game towards their characteristics, and if you want to have an identity, that is hard.
"It's always my decision. What I felt in the last games is the same that I felt at Manchester United, and I cannot make the same mistake.
"Sometimes we don't have the perfect characteristics to play in that way, and if we don't have them, we have to adapt. I think today worked.
"In another game, we can return to the build-up with three [at the back]. The important thing is to have different ways of playing.

"That's especially important in Italy, because the managers are really smart, they mark really well one against one, and when they lose the reference to what we want to do, it's harder for them to understand their mobility, just as they make it harder for me to understand their teams."

Milan have now won their first two home Serie A matches of a season while keeping a clean sheet in both for the first time since 2020-21, when they beat Bologna 2-0 and Spezia 3-0 under Stefano Pioli.

Their dominance was backed up by the underlying metrics, too. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.93 from their 10 attempts, while also restricting Lecce to a measly xG total of 0.17 from six shots.
It was a much-needed victory heading into the international break, with Milan coming into the clash with Lecce without a win in three matches in all competitions (D2 L1).
Roma, Inter and Lazio are the early pace setters in the division, all sitting two points clear of Milan, and Amorim feels his team are on the right track.
"If you look at the way we play, Roma and Inter had more time as a team, you can see the patterns are there," Amorim added.
"We didn't lose so many points, we dropped two to Lazio and Juventus away, so not everything is bad.

"Sometimes it looks like that, especially after recent results, but we have to see the balance. We won today against a good team that is doing well, but it is a different team, and sometimes we will have issues.
"It's a process, I think we should have more points, as against Juventus we weren't playing so well, but we were 30 seconds off getting three points.
"Even against Lazio, if you look at the balance of the game, I feel we deserved a little bit more."

1m6hibefmoqwp1de6sqjxg9vq1.title: 'It means everything' – Robertson marks 100th Scotland cap with victory
1m6hibefmoqwp1de6sqjxg9vq1.subtitle: Andy Robertson was beaming after winning his 100th Scotland cap, though he was disappointed not to mark the occasion with a goal.
paragraphs: Andy Robertson was proud to mark his 100th Scotland appearance with a victory, as Saturday's 2-0 win over North Macedonia got the Sebastien Pocognoli era up and running.

Following a goalless draw with Slovenia and a chastening 3-0 loss at home to Switzerland, Scotland finally got their first victory in the 2026-27 Nations League, with Kieron Bowie and John McGinn on target in Skopje.
Bowie's first international goal was a brilliant effort in the seventh minute, as he spun Mario Mladenovski then found the bottom-right corner from outside the area.

McGinn made it 2-0 from the penalty spot in the 69th minute, with Bojan Miovski deemed to have committed handball during a goalmouth scramble in which Scott McKenna – who was later sent off – headed against the post.
While it was an occasion to remember for Pocognoli, Robertson also celebrated a landmark moment, becoming only the second player to win 100 caps for Scotland, after Kenny Dalglish (102).

Dalglish's 30 international goals remain the joint-most by any Scotland player, alongside Denis Law, and Robertson – who only has four goals for his country – joked he had a chance of matching that figure after being heavily involved as an attacking outlet.
Having never previously had four shots in a game for Scotland, Robertson managed that figure in the opening 13 minutes, with Stole Dimitrievski making one wonderful save to keep the left-back out.
"It means everything to me, and it means everything to my family," Robertson told BBC Scotland afterwards.
"I've been away now 100 times; I've got to feel sorry for my wife! It's been an unbelievable journey. I remember my first game, and it's been a process since then.
"It's emotional for me. I love this country, there's only one person before me in the men's game to do that, so it's a pretty special achievement.
"I thought Kenny Dalglish was going to be worried about his goalscoring record in the first few minutes! I had about six shots!
"They did a nice presentation for me; I told them I wanted the win. The lads did so well to get the win, it'll be a special one for me and my family."
McGinn, meanwhile, said Scotland could not afford to rest on their laurels ahead of hosting Slovenia on Tuesday, as he praised Pocognoli's efforts to build a new identity.
"The most important thing tonight was a win and a clean sheet," McGinn said. "When results go against you, things are said about you both personally and as a team, it's part of football.
"We deserve the praise that comes tonight. It was not an easy game, but we handled it well.
"The manager has brought a lot of ideas, a lot of identity, and it's up to us to buy into it. It's up to us to keep believing in what he wants to do and bring our qualities to the pitch.
"Tuesday's going to be a difficult game, but we've got to back this up with another win."

1m9ymt7iknsn317sgev2gjguoq.title: Man Utd striker Sesko withdraws from Slovenia squad due to shin issue
1m9ymt7iknsn317sgev2gjguoq.subtitle: A shin injury troubled Benjamin Sesko at the end of last season, and a flare-up of the issue has ruled him out of Slovenia's upcoming games.
paragraphs: Manchester United have confirmed striker Benjamin Sesko must undergo tests after withdrawing from the Slovenia squad with a shin injury.
Sesko was a notable absentee as United drew 1-1 with Fulham on Sunday, with Matheus Cunha's deflected strike salvaging a point for the Red Devils following Lisandro Martinez's calamitous own goal.
Having joined from RB Leipzig in a £74m deal last August, Sesko scored 12 goals in 32 appearances across all competitions last term.
That tally was only matched by Bryan Mbeumo among his Red Devils team-mates, despite 13 of Sesko's outings coming from the bench.
The 23-year-old missed the final few games of 2025-26, however, as well as United's entire pre-season campaign, with a shin problem.
Sesko has played six times for Michael Carrick's side this season, scoring twice, though he has only started twice – against Sabah in the Champions League and Brighton in the EFL Cup.
In the aftermath of last week's cup defeat to Brighton, Carrick revealed that the same issue was bothering Sesko again, and he has now withdrawn from Slovenia's squad.
Sesko was initially named in Bostjan Cesar's party for Nations League fixtures against Scotland – who they will face home and away – plus North Macedonia and Switzerland.
In a medical update released on Monday, United said: "Benjamin will undergo tests this week before defining his individual recovery plan."
Sesko has almost three weeks of recovery time if he is to feature in United's next Premier League game, against bottom club Tottenham on October 10.
They also face Leeds United, Bournemouth and Chelsea in the league next month, having made their joint-worst start to a Premier League season through five matchdays (also five points in 2014-15).

1mec37kyn0o9715yn7pvc661gg.title: Sorensen: Vancouver cannot 'flip a coin' against Chicago
1mec37kyn0o9715yn7pvc661gg.subtitle: Jesper Sorensen felt his Vancouver Whitecaps team played with too much risk in their 3-3 draw with D.C. United last time out in MLS.
paragraphs: The Vancouver Whitecaps must get away from "flipping a coin" after the "Wild West" nature of their recent fixtures, so says head coach Jesper Sorensen.
Vancouver sit top of the Western Conference in MLS, but drew 3-3 with D.C. United in their last outing.
The Whitecaps came from behind to lead, but then were pegged back before going ahead again through Thomas Muller.
However, Sorensen's team conceded another equaliser in the 80th minute, meaning they have now won just two of their last five league games.
And Sorensen wants his team to get back to a more composed, solid approach when they take on the Chicago Fire on Tuesday.
"We'll have some players out, they'll have some players out," he said.
"Let's see how it's going to play out. Normally, we'd have the same approach as to how we'd like to play.
"Hopefully we can play a much better connected and much less wild game. We have to be more in control and not be as open, and not have it be quite as like the Wild West.
"It was how we were playing the game and how we have played as of late.
"We conceded 10 corners, which is not usual for us. It's very unusual. We flipped a coin last time, and we usually don't do that. We have to get away from that again."
Chicago Fire - Johan Gomez
Gomez scored the only goal in Chicago’s win over Charlotte FC on September 26.

It marked the first regular-season goal scored by a Fire player other than Robert Lewandowski or Maren Haile-Selassie since August 19, after the pair had netted Chicago's previous nine league goals between them (excluding own goals).
Vancouver Whitecaps - Brian White
White has scored seven goals in his last seven MLS appearances, including scoring in each of his last four games.
This is the fifth time White has scored in at least four straight league games for the Whitecaps, including a club record-tying five-match run in 2025 (also Camilo Sanvezzo in 2013).
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
The Whitecaps have won their last three regular-season away matches without conceding, the first time Vancouver have recorded three straight shutout wins on the road.
The only teams in MLS history to record four straight road shutout wins in a single season are LA Galaxy in 2010 and D.C. in 2007.
Chicago snapped a seven-match winless run in all competitions (D4 L3) with a 1-0 road victory over Charlotte FC last time out.
The Fire have gone three straight without a win at home (D1 L2) after failing to win only three of their previous 12 home matches (W9 D0 L3).
Chicago and Vancouver have alternated wins over the four meetings since 2020 with the Fire winning the last match, 3-1, on the road in March 2025.
The only time either team won consecutive meetings with the other was a pair of Whitecaps wins over the Fire in 2015 and 2016.
Vancouver Whitecaps - 37.7%

1mh1ibaer440p1qjfnhz9janks.title: Ronaldo's importance to Portugal should not be underestimated, insists Riemer
1mh1ibaer440p1qjfnhz9janks.subtitle: Brian Riemer's Denmark side host Portugal on Thursday in the Nations League, and he is wary of the threat posed by Cristiano Ronaldo.
paragraphs: Denmark boss Brian Riemer believes "it's a bit absurd" to suggest Portugal are better off without Cristiano Ronaldo.
Portugal lead their Nations League group ahead of their trip to Denmark on Thursday, having won against Wales and Norway to begin their title defence.
Ronaldo featured against Wales, seeing a goal chalked off, but was an unused substitute in Portugal's 2-1 victory over Norway last time out.
In his absence, starting strikers Goncalo Ramos and Joao Felix both scored for Jorge Jesus' side, with the head coach also insisting Ronaldo was left on the bench for tactical reasons.

Reports claimed Ronaldo's relationship with Jesus is now fractured, while some fans suggested Portugal are better off without their all-time leading scorer, but Riemer came to the 41-year-old's defence.
"I think it's a bit absurd to be discussing this in relation to Cristiano Ronaldo," Riemer told TV2 Sport.
"I believe that many people underestimate the importance he has in the Portuguese team. I even think that, the day he retires, Portugal will have a problem.
"There's something called hierarchy. There are many strong personalities in a team like Portugal. Who will make decisions and set the terms? It can be a big challenge.
"Definitely, you shouldn't underestimate Ronaldo's importance when he plays. Portugal's best team is with Ronaldo playing."
Ronaldo scored 29 goals in 33 games under the command of Jesus for Al-Nassr in the 2025-26 campaign, at an average of one goal every 99 minutes.
Jesus revealed Ronaldo could be in for some minutes against Denmark, while Portugal also host Norway before the end of the extended international break.

1mpcxk69szwjt1pm8nhi5n4com.title: Manchester City 4-2 Arsenal: Hemp scores twice as comeback win keeps champions perfect
1mpcxk69szwjt1pm8nhi5n4com.subtitle: Manchester City twice fell behind to struggling Arsenal, but the Women's Super League champions recovered to win a six-goal thriller.
paragraphs: Manchester City twice came from behind to clinch a thrilling 4-2 victory over Arsenal and maintain their 100% record in the Women's Super League this season.

Lauren Hemp struck twice for the hosts at the Etihad Stadium, while Kerstin Casparij scored a brilliant goal with her first touch off the bench and Khadija Shaw added a late clincher, with Andree Jeglertz's team earning their fifth win in as many games.
Following a cagey start, Arsenal enjoyed a spell of pressure without truly testing Ayaka Yamashita, as Lotte Wubben-Moy headed wide.

City's first real opportunity saw Shaw shoot straight at Anneke Borbe, and though the Jamaica striker had the ball in the net in the 36th minute, her header was chalked out for a foul after she clattered the Arsenal goalkeeper in mid-air.

And, after Yamashita pulled off a fine save to thwart Emily Fox, Arsenal hit the front in the 43rd minute. Wubben-Moy nodded Alessia Russo's cross back into the danger zone, and following a touch from Yamashita, the ball deflected in off Lisa Baum's knee.
City were not even behind for four minutes, though, as in first-half stoppage time, Hemp saw her left-footed drive take a wicked deflection off Fox and spin past Borbe.

An injury to Mariona Caldentey represented another blow for Arsenal right before the interval, but they restored their advantage five minutes into the second half. City had already got away with one giveaway in a dangerous area before Yui Hasegawa lost possession to Russo, who curled a pinpoint finish into the far corner.
But once again, City came storming back as Casparij came off the bench in the 62nd minute and, just 65 seconds later, bent a beautiful first-time effort beyond Borbe.
All the momentum was with the hosts at that point, and after a big intervention from Leah Williamson kept Shaw out, Hemp showed great composure to collect Hasegawa's far-post delivery and slot home.
And City made the points safe with six minutes of the 90 left, as Aoba Fujino slipped a neat pass into Shaw, who wrong-footed Williamson with her first touch, then stroked home.
Perfect five for City as pressure mounts on Slegers

City have started a WSL campaign with five straight wins for the third time, having previously done so in their 2016 title-winning season (won first six) and repeated the trick in 2017-18 (won first seven).

Jeglertz's team have also won 15 straight home matches in the WSL dating back to last season, with only Chelsea ever enjoying a longer winning run on their own turf in the competition – a 22-game run from March 2022 to February 2024.
City's clinical finishing was the difference, as they hugely outperformed their tally of 0.92 expected goals (xG), which came from nine shots (five on target).
Renee Slegers' visitors had 16 shots and hit the target nine times, generating 1.59 xG, but seven saves from Yamashita – many of which were routine – helped City keep them at bay.

While City go into the WSL's international break two points clear of Chelsea at the summit, Arsenal – last season's runners-up – are already 10 points off the pace in 10th, only making a worse start to a WSL campaign in 2014 (four).

Manchester City twice came from behind to clinch a thrilling 4-2 victory over Arsenal and maintain their 100% record in the Women's Super League this season.

Lauren Hemp struck twice for the hosts at the Etihad Stadium, while Kerstin Casparij scored a brilliant goal with her first touch off the bench and Khadija Shaw added a late clincher, with Andree Jeglertz's team earning their fifth win in as many games.

Following a cagey start, Arsenal enjoyed a spell of pressure without truly testing Ayaka Yamashita, as Lotte Wubben-Moy headed wide.

City's first real opportunity saw Shaw shoot straight at Anneke Borbe, and though the Jamaica striker had the ball in the net in the 36th minute, her header was chalked out for a foul after she clattered the Arsenal goalkeeper in mid-air.

And, after Yamashita pulled off a fine save to thwart Emily Fox, Arsenal hit the front in the 43rd minute. Wubben-Moy nodded Alessia Russo's cross back into the danger zone, and following a touch from Yamashita, the ball deflected in off Lisa Baum's knee.

City were not even behind for four minutes, though, as in first-half stoppage time, Hemp saw her left-footed drive take a wicked deflection off Fox and spin past Borbe.

1mugrndf4tj9311xpaha3as3qv.title: Kane says England 'sent a message' with thumping win over Croatia
1mugrndf4tj9311xpaha3as3qv.subtitle: Harry Kane said England had set the standard for future tournament performances with their historic 7-0 thrashing of Croatia.
paragraphs: Harry Kane said England had sent out a resounding message to the rest of Europe by routing Croatia 7-0 on Saturday, also acknowledging the Three Lions need to adopt the same mentality at future tournaments.
Kane scored twice as the Three Lions ran riot in Rijeka, making it back-to-back Nations League victories following their opening 3-2 defeat to Spain.
Thomas Tuchel's side were utterly dominant as they put up an expected goals (xG) figure of 6.43 – the largest ever recorded in any Nations League game, in any tier.
Bukayo Saka also helped himself to a brace, with Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers getting England's other goals.

It was England's biggest ever win against a team in the top 50 of the FIFA World Rankings and the heaviest defeat in Croatia's history, and Kane said the scale of their accomplishment should not be underestimated.
"Even when we were 1-0 up, we went for two, went for three, went for four, and that's got to be our mentality," Kane said, as quoted by ESPN.
"When you have a certain style of playing, you can't just pick and choose when you want to do it. It's just relentless. It's non-stop.
"You get four, you want five. You go and have a hungry mentality. That's needed to change, especially in the bigger games, in the bigger tournaments, and these games will only help us.
"We were playing against a really good side. We can't take this type of win for granted because it could have been a really tricky game for us.
"And it's always about sending messages, not just to yourself, but to the other teams around Europe. I think we've done that again.

"We're hungry. We're a young team. We have players in amazing form right now, and I think everyone's just excited to be out there on the pitch. Performances like this will only make us more motivated."
Kane now has 11 goals for England in 2026, becoming the first player to ever reach double figures in three separate calendar years for the Three Lions (also 12 in 2019 and 16 in 2021).
Both he and Gordon have scored in three straight games for England, becoming the first pair of players to do so for them since Kane and Marcus Rashford in 2019.
England, whose last seven-goal victory came against North Macedonia in a Euro 2024 qualifier three years ago, welcome Czechia to Wembley for their final game of this international break on Tuesday.
Should Kane feature in that match, he will match legendary former goalkeeper Peter Shilton at the top of England's all-time appearance charts, with 125 caps.

1muk7ea3o972z15gjzre3t9mhj.title: Kane and Bayern 'fairly close' to agreeing new contract
1muk7ea3o972z15gjzre3t9mhj.subtitle: Harry Kane is keen to extend his stay at Bayern Munich and is in talks over a reported two-year extension with the Bundesliga giants.
paragraphs: Harry Kane hinted his Bayern Munich contract renewal is "fairly close" and could be announced soon.
Kane joined Bayern from Tottenham in August 2023 and has gone from strength to strength with the Bundesliga giants, winning two straight titles and a DFB-Pokal trophy.
He has also written his name into the Bundesliga history books this term, having netted his 100th and 101st goals in the competition last time out in a 7-0 hammering of Union Berlin.
Kane reached the 100-goal landmark in his 98th appearance, making him the quickest player to hit that tally, smashing Dieter Muller's previous record of 129 games.
Overall, the England captain has netted 152 goals in 154 appearances, and in 2025-26 alone, he scored a whopping 64 times in all competitions (including the Club World Cup).
Kane's current contract is due to run out at the end of this season, but a new deal – reportedly through to June 2029 – is in the works.
"We're in good talks. We're fairly close," Kane told The Independent.
"There's still some things that we need to iron out. I'm happy there. I think it won't be too long before there's some sort of announcement."
Bayern are chasing a third straight Bundesliga title this term and are also among the favourites to clinch the Champions League.
They went into the international break second in the German top-flight, behind Borussia Dortmund, but Kane is excited to see what the team can achieve.
"I feel really comfortable in the team, with the coach, the environment," Kane added. "I want to just be at this level and push this level for as long as possible.
"Especially as you're getting a bit older, if you don't have a great season somewhere, or you don't play as well, the drop-off is maybe more than what it would have been when you're younger.
"So, it's just about extracting as much as I can, with the boss there, with the players I have in the team, I think they're getting the best out of me. I'm helping them as well."

1n597582ko2a31k68ulkm4b2dd.title: Gakpo determined to enjoy life at Liverpool after 'difficult' transfer saga
1n597582ko2a31k68ulkm4b2dd.subtitle: It looked like Cody Gakpo's time at Liverpool was over this summer, but he never made his high-profile move to Manchester City.
paragraphs: Cody Gakpo revealed it was a "difficult summer" after his potential move to Manchester City from Liverpool fell through.
Gakpo had a turbulent summer after the World Cup, with his future at Anfield remaining up in the air for the majority of the transfer window.
He was initially linked with a move to Tottenham before it emerged in the final days of the window that City were interested in bringing him to the Etihad Stadium.
However, the deal fell through in the final hours of deadline day, with Gakpo ultimately staying at Liverpool.
"I don't know if you want to go into detail about that, but there's no point in talking about it," Gakpo told The Telegraph.
"It was a difficult summer for me, my family and everything to do with football and life. So yeah, I just let it happen, and it ended the way it ended.
"It's a very long story. The summer was very tough, on all fronts. I just let it all sink in and saw how it would go, and it went this way.
"Now it is what it is. I just want to enjoy my life with my family and friends. And from playing football with my team-mates here and at the club."
Gakpo has made a strong start to the 2026-27 season for Liverpool, making six appearances under Andoni Iraola so far.
He has already racked up six goal involvements in all competitions – two goals and four assists – more than any other player for the club.
His 13 chances created, meanwhile, are second only to Dominik Szoboszlai.
"When you play for a big club like Liverpool, you have to perform," Gakpo, who also scored for the Netherlands in their 1-1 draw with Germany on Thursday, added.
"I don't want to talk about others or other players, but I know I could have done much better myself than last year.
"I don't know if the criticism was unfair. Maybe it was, but in a way, I understand it.
"At Liverpool, you have to win, perform and show that you are one of the best clubs in the world. We didn't do that last year, including myself. That's just the way it goes."

1n5p1b2ytadf71qmyd7fy0h20a.title: Joao Felix wants to assist Ronaldo's 1,000th goal
1n5p1b2ytadf71qmyd7fy0h20a.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo is close to reaching the 1,000-goal mark, and Joao Felix wants to be the player to assist the historic goal.
paragraphs: Joao Felix revealed he has thought about being the player to assist Cristiano Ronaldo's 1,000th goal, claiming "the goal will go down in soccer history".
Ronaldo scored in Al-Nassr's win over Abha earlier this month, taking his career total to 979 goals for club and country.
While the 41-year-old hinted his international career could be over by the end of the season, it also remains to be seen whether his club career goes beyond 2026-27.
Joao Felix plays alongside Ronaldo for both Al-Nassr and Portugal, and the former Chelsea forward would be honoured to assist his team-mates' milestone goal.
"I've thought about that," Joao Felix told Diario AS when asked about assisting Ronaldo's 1,000th goal.
"When he's one goal away, every time I get the ball I'll look for him to see if I can give him the pass.
"That goal will go down in soccer history, and being part of it would be a great moment."
Joao Felix impressed in his debut season with Al-Nassr, scoring 20 goals and providing 13 assists to help his team end a seven-year wait to win the Saudi Pro League title.
The 26-year-old was named the league's player of the season, and he was delighted to see Ronaldo finally get his hands on the trophy.
"It's something few people in soccer can say they've done," added Joao Felix. "I got to do it with the national team, and now at Al Nassr.
"It's an honour, honestly. We grew up watching Cristiano. He was our idol, someone we looked up to, and now I get to share these moments with him.
"Winning the league last year was especially meaningful. Being able to help Cristiano win the title he had been chasing since he arrived.
"We have to enjoy it as much as we can because we know it won't last forever. But while he's here, we'll be here too."

1o2557slkcbvs1hnp5z6fpwxsm.title: Neto completes Juventus return as Grabara replacement
1o2557slkcbvs1hnp5z6fpwxsm.subtitle: After Kamil Grabara was ruled out for the rest of the season through injury, Juventus have signed free agent Neto for the second time.
paragraphs: Juventus have announced the return of goalkeeper Neto on a free transfer following a season-ending injury to on-loan shot-stopper Kamil Grabara.
Neto has signed a contract until the end of the 2026-27 campaign and returns to Turin nine years after leaving for Valencia.
The 37-year-old's arrival comes after Grabara, who was on loan from Wolfsburg, sustained an anterior cruciate (ACL) injury just two days after making his debut for Juventus.
Grabara assisted Nico Gonzalez's opener during a 5-0 win over NEC in the Europa League, and he has since had successful surgery to repair the issue.
But having allowed Michele Di Gregorio and Mattia Perin to leave the club, Juventus have acted quickly to strengthen their goalkeeper options during the international break.
Neto played 22 times across all competitions during his previous stint from 2015 to 2017 with Juventus, keeping 12 clean sheets and winning five major honours.
Since his exit from Juventus nine years ago, he has gone on to represent Valencia, Barcelona, Bournemouth, Arsenal and most recently, Botafogo.
Juventus are seventh in Serie A after their first five games of the season, and they return to action after the international break against Cagliari on October 11.

1oo6jjpc45ake1uj9k7ei6gwnd.title: Colwill expects Chelsea to be better after international break
1oo6jjpc45ake1uj9k7ei6gwnd.subtitle: Chelsea's strong start to the season fizzled out before the international break, but Levi Colwill is confident they can improve after it.
paragraphs: Levi Colwill has backed Chelsea to come out on the other side of the international break "flying".
Chelsea made a strong start to life under Xabi Alonso, winning four of their first five matches across all competitions (L1).

However, having had to come from behind to draw 2-2 with high-flying Hull City, the Blues were then thrashed 3-0 by Brentford in their final match before the extended international break to leave them winless in three league games.
Chelsea have already lost more Premier League matches in 2026 (11) than they did in the entirety of 2025 (10).

Alonso became only the sixth Premier League boss to see his side concede at least two goals in each of his first five games, after Mick McCarthy, Sammy Lee, Terry Connor, Slavisa Jokanovic, and Scott Parker.

And Chelsea's defensive woes have been highlighted on multiple occasions, even before Alonso's appointment; since the start of last season, they have conceded 23 Premier League goals from non-penalty set-pieces, now the joint-most of any side, along with Bournemouth.
Colwill admitted the start of the season was not what Chelsea expected, but he wants to use the extended international break to get back on track.
"[There have been] some good bits, some other not so good bits," he said, as quoted by Chelsea's website.
"Luckily, we've got a while now to try and improve.
"Hopefully, we will come out the other side flying, pick up our play, and become a better team."
Chelsea return to action at home to Bournemouth on October 10.

1ooo5sawiqft91hpmfscpu5ncb.title: 'We are not a low-block team' – Norway to take the game to Portugal
1ooo5sawiqft91hpmfscpu5ncb.subtitle: Norway suffered a 2-1 defeat against Portugal in the Nations League last week, with the two sides facing off again on Sunday.
paragraphs: Stale Solbakken insisted his Norway side "are not a low-block team" as they plan to play on the front foot against Portugal.
Norway have won just one of their three Nations League games during this break (L2), most recently losing 2-1 to Wales after Torbjorn Heggem was sent off early in the second half.
Their other defeat came against Portugal in the reverse fixture, with Jorge Jesus' side picking up a 2-1 win in Norway.
In that match, Norway won the expected goals (xG) battle 2.52 to 1.04, creating six Opta-defined big chances and retaining 62% of possession.
Solbakken acknowledged it could be harder to dominate away from home against Portugal, but he insists his players will not sit back at the Estadio Do Dragao.
"We are not a low-block team. Always with our heads up, looking for the goal. I think the players also feel that we can take the game to Portugal's goal," said Solbakken.
"I have great respect for Portugal. The team is in the top two or top three in Europe at the moment.

"Portugal presses very well, with high intensity, and we have to think differently. In the first game, we managed to play through the central corridor, but now I think they will have a different plan. We have to be able to adapt to the circumstances.
"It was probably one of the best games we've ever played, in the first 60 minutes against Portugal. Hopefully, we can repeat that.
"Now it might be different, because Portugal are playing at home, but we'll give our best and see how far we can go."

Norway have lost nine of their 12 matches against Portugal (75% – W1 D2), their third-highest loss percentage against all opponents they faced more than five times (83% against the USSR, 77% against Yugoslavia).
They have conceded at least twice in each of their last four games; the last time they saw their opponents score at least two times in five consecutive games was in 1975-1976 (six).
