1or6s2qt4lt221k4i5blb8icwe.title: Olmo rejected Bayern twice, reveals Barcelona star's agent
1or6s2qt4lt221k4i5blb8icwe.subtitle: Dani Olmo has become an important player for both Barcelona and Spain over recent years, after twice rejecting Bayern Munich.
paragraphs: Dani Olmo twice rejected Bayern Munich before joining Barcelona, his agent has revealed.
Olmo joined Barca ahead of the 2024-25 campaign and has since scored 20 goals and provided 18 assists in 96 matches for the Blaugrana.
The Spain international has won two LaLiga titles, two Supercopas de Espana and one Copa del Rey since leaving RB Leipzig, while also winning the World Cup with La Roja this summer.
Since the start of the 2024-25 season, Olmo has directly contributed to the sixth-most goals among Barca players (38), while also creating the fourth-most chances (116).
Hansi Flick's side have made a perfect start to 2026-27, with Olmo providing three assists across their eight wins in all competitions.
Bayern tried to sign Olmo twice in the past, once before he joined Barca and the other while he was still at Dinamo Zagreb, though his agent believes it all worked out in the end.
"He rejected Bayern on my initiative when he was at Dinamo. I told him: you need to take another step, and that's what happened," Marc Bara told the Inkubator podcast.
"Later, he received another offer from Bayern as a Leipzig player, and Barcelona and other clubs were also interested.
"We chose Barcelona, which perhaps wasn't the best choice, but everything worked out for him afterwards.
"He won the European Championship, the Nations League, the World Cup, and is one of the ten best players in the national team.
"His story is like a movie, and I'm happy to have been part of it."

Barca will look to continue their perfect start when they host Getafe after the international break, while they will also face Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and Real Madrid in LaLiga this month.

1ozwcpqd6jbfw1jzlxdbbxe577.title: Chelsea 1-0 Austria Wien: Bompastor's side survive scare in Women's Champions League opener
1ozwcpqd6jbfw1jzlxdbbxe577.subtitle: Wieke Kaptein's early goal was enough for Chelsea to see off Austria Wien, but it was from a convincing display from Sonia Bompastor's side.
paragraphs: Chelsea began their Women's Champions League campaign with a nervy win as Wieke Kaptein's first-half stunner sealed a 1-0 victory over tournament debutants Austria Wien.
The Blues looked far from the team that reached the quarter-finals of the competition in 2025-26, but a moment of individual quality was enough to get them over the line.

Chelsea needed just 11 minutes to take the lead through Kaptein. Katharina Schiechtl's tackle on Melvine Malard saw the ball drop kindly to the midfielder, who took a touch before crashing her shot in off the crossbar from the edge of the box.
Sonia Bompastor was forced into making an early change as Keira Walsh left the field with an injury, but the Blues continued where they left off in their search for a second.
The lively Alyssa Thompson drilled a shot just wide of the left post following a driving run down the right, but Wien had their chances to level things up going into the break.
Virginia Kirchberger could only turn over after Modesta Uka's wicked delivery was spilled by Livia Peng before Louise Schoffel's effort whistled past the bottom-left corner.

Wien grew in confidence as the second half wore on as Uka's shot on the swivel was repelled by Peng, with the Chelsea goalkeeper then on hand to thwart Valentina Potzl after Veerle Buurman had played herself into trouble.

The visitors continued to get closer and closer to levelling things up, with Uka chopping inside before curling her attempt onto the post, but Wien were unable to find the equaliser their performance merited in the closing stages.
Chelsea ride their luck

Ahead of kick-off, Bompastor stressed the need for her Chelsea team to be more clinical, having stumbled to a 2-0 victory against Birmingham City in the Women's Super League last weekend, and once again her team looked vulnerable at both ends of the pitch.

In what was a historic match for Wien, becoming the fourth Austrian side to participate in the competition after Neulengbach, St. Polten and Sturm Graz, they announced their arrival on the European stage in some style, and were extremely unlucky not to leave with at least a point.

Uka was the particular standout for the visitors. She finished with team-high totals for shots (five), touches in the opposition box (seven), crosses (six) and attempted dribbles (three), while also coming within inches of scoring an equaliser in the second half.

The Blues were, however, able to hold on to begin their campaign with a win. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.43 from their 13 attempts compared to Wien's 0.87 from two more shots at Peng's net.
Bompastor will be hoping for improvements in the WSL this weekend, but things do not get any easier, with London rivals and two-time Champions League winners Arsenal their next opponents this Sunday.
Elsewhere, there was no such trouble for last year's runners-up Lyon, who thumped Servette 8-0, with Marie-Antoinette Katoto scoring a hat-trick at Stade de Geneve.

Defending champions Barcelona also got their campaign up and running with a win. They came from a goal down to beat Paris FC 5-2, with Caroline Graham Hansen and Ewa Pajor starring in the turnaround. Roma, meanwhile, played out a 0-0 draw with OH Leuven.

1pciepkv6nb591bfa90trf5n6q.title: Mancini and Bastoni say Italy will not play like underdogs against France
1pciepkv6nb591bfa90trf5n6q.subtitle: Italy go to France for their third Nations League fixture on Friday, with Roberto Mancini pledging the Azzurri will push for three points.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini insists Italy will play to win against France, with defender Alessandro Bastoni revealing that boosting the Azzurri's confidence and self-esteem has been a key focus of their returning head coach.
Italy have registered one win and one defeat so far in the Nations League, losing 2-0 at home to Belgium in Mancini's first game at the helm since 2023, before winning 4-1 in Turkiye.
Their next assignment is a daunting one, though, as they head to the Stade de France to take on Zinedine Zidane's France side.

Les Bleus have maximum points on the board in Group A1, and Italy have only won three of their last 15 head-to-head meetings with France dating back to 1982 (two draws, 10 defeats), albeit they did overcome them on penalties in the 2006 World Cup final.
While 12 places now separate Italy (15th) and France (third) in the FIFA World Rankings, Mancini is refusing to adopt an underdog mentality.
"It will certainly be a great game against a top team, full of extraordinary players, but we always want to make a good impression and will do our best," Mancini said, as quoted by Football Italia.
"When you are up against such strong teams, you never play not to win, so naturally we must always play looking for the victory. After that, anything can happen."

Defender Bastoni scored Italy's opening goal against Turkiye, exorcising some of his demons from March's World Cup qualification play-off defeat to Bosnia-Herzegovina, when he was sent off shortly before half-time.

Given the negativity of the last few years, with Italy becoming the first former World Cup winners to miss three straight editions of the tournament, Bastoni says building self-belief must be a priority for Mancini and his staff.
"We are capable of having our say in a one-off match against anyone, but we also want to be consistent and make sure that Italy have an identity on the pitch," Bastoni said.
"Our standard has to be the one we saw in the most recent match.

"Everyone hopes to get results as soon as possible, but we must also recognise we're at the start of this process. After the game against with Turkiye, we need patience, as more tough moments will come.
"The coach is working on our self-esteem. In Italy, we're very good at moaning, feeling sorry for ourselves and focusing on all the negatives.
"But in my view, we should also learn to say when we have done something good. too. The more we say it, the more we'll start to believe it, so we've got to work on that.
"I've seen strong characters in the squad, they aren't afraid to try something new, and that touch is probably what we needed."

1pdab9mi3roft1tudzxduqx8gf.title: Xavi promises 'intensity and passion' in new-look Netherlands approach
1pdab9mi3roft1tudzxduqx8gf.subtitle: Xavi will take charge of the Netherlands for the first time this international break, and he is preparing his team for a new approach.
paragraphs: Xavi has promised to bring "intensity, passion and a good rhythm" to the Netherlands' play as he prepares to take charge for the first time.
The Spaniard was named as the Oranje's head coach on a four-year deal after Ronald Koeman left in the wake of a disappointing World Cup campaign over the summer.
While the Netherlands enjoyed an unbeaten group stage, they fell at the first hurdle in the knockouts, losing on penalties to Morocco.
Xavi, a former World Cup winner with Spain, will face Germany in his first game in charge in Amsterdam on Thursday, as the Netherlands kick off their Nations League campaign.

Koeman was criticised at times for taking a defensive approach with his tactics, and while Xavi did not give away too many hints about his approach, he outlined what he expects from his players on Monday.
"Everything is new ​for me and for the staff, so it will first be to get to know each other, ​know all the players, insist or convince them about our way to play," Xavi told reporters.
"We don't have too much time. But no excuses; every coach is in the same situation.

"I want to explain the values that ​we want from the squad. I want to show them that I'm open to them; I want ​to help them. I want to enjoy the process with them. We want to create a family; we want ‌to ⁠create a big group.
"The players must come to the national team with happiness, but at the end, the main goal is to win.

"You cannot promise results, but ​we will work ⁠for results. I can promise that we will play with intensity, with passion, with a good rhythm, trying to be competitive and trying to ​take the initiative in the game. This is for sure.
"There's going ​to be ⁠a different way of playing. I don't want to compare, and I don't want to talk about the past. I respect Ronald a lot. But I'm focused on the present."
Virgil van Dijk will remain the Netherlands' captain, having revealed on Sunday that he plans to keep representing his national team until Euro 2028.
"It ​was a really good meeting," Xavi said of meeting Van Dijk in Liverpool to discuss his Netherlands future.
"He was very honest. He has the capacity to continue. He's a good leader. He's positive, ​he's motivated. He's ready to be the leader."

1pferb0aavbmk1p668syxtx3dj.title: Doue: Zidane told us we're on the right track
1pferb0aavbmk1p668syxtx3dj.subtitle: France were held to a 1-1 draw by Italy in the Nations League on Friday, though Zinedine Zidane took away plenty of positives.
paragraphs: Desire Doue agreed with Zinedine Zidane in believing France are "on the right track" despite dropping points in the Nations League against Italy.
In Zidane's first home match as France boss, Les Bleus were held to a 1-1 draw by Italy at the Stade de France.
Michael Olise opened the scoring with a stunning free-kick 10 minutes into the second half, but Alessandro Bastoni equalised after a costly mistake from Adrien Rabiot.
France failed to win a match after having opened the scoring for the first time since September 2024, when they lost 3-1 at home to Italy in the Nations League.
Dayot Upamecano also received a late red card after being shown a second yellow for dragging down Moise Kean.
He is the first player in the history of the France national team to receive two red cards in the same calendar year, after also being sent off against Brazil back in March.
Nevertheless, Doue took positives from the result, and so did Zidane.
"We're disappointed with the result; we would have liked to win in front of our fans," said the Paris Saint-Germain forward.
"We're not going to dwell on the negatives; we applied the coach's instructions in many aspects. We're on the right track, as he told us in the locker room.
"We're capable of creating a lot of danger; in the first half, they were very solid. We need to be more clinical; we came up against a great goalkeeper. But we stuck together."
Zidane added: "I'm very disappointed, we deserved better, but that's football. We should have killed the game off, but I'm proud of my players.
"The performance was very good, my players were exemplary. I'm frustrated for my players because they gave everything.
"We had possession in the first half but it was sterile, that's what we tried to correct at half-time. To hurt the opponent, you have to exploit the spaces.
"In terms of our play, we put things in place, they played their game, defensive, 'Italian style'. We weren't in too much danger."

1pnrn2gfgmlef1rvhmj39ofd3w.title: Gittens returning to Chelsea after suffering injury with England U21s
1pnrn2gfgmlef1rvhmj39ofd3w.subtitle: Jamie Gittens' time with England Under-21s has been cut short by injury, with Lee Carsley confirming his withdrawal from the squad.
paragraphs: Chelsea have been dealt a potential injury blow after Lee Carsley confirmed Jamie Gittens was returning to the club for treatment after sustaining an injury with England Under-21s.
Gittens was forced off with an apparent ankle injury during England's 4-2 win over Kazakhstan in European Championship qualifying.
The winger made way in the 39th minute and was later spotted on crutches, and he has already been ruled out of their final two qualifying games.
Head coach Lee Carsley explained that Gittens had returned to Chelsea, with England unwilling to take any risks with the youngster's fitness.
"Jamie got a kick on his ankle. We never take any risks," Carsley said, as quoted by The Sun.
"With the age of these players, we don't ever keep them in camp to see how they are. He will go back."
Gittens has made just two appearances for Chelsea since Xabi Alonso took over, with both of those coming in the EFL Cup, and only one coming from the start.
Indeed, he has been limited since joining the Blues from Borussia Dortmund at the start of last season, making just 29 appearances in total and netting only one goal.
The extent of Gittens' injury has not been disclosed yet, with Chelsea's next game coming against Bournemouth on October 10.

1q8lgyn5wojce11sb5vt3kfmq2.title: Lyon 0-0 Chelsea: Super Hampton save preserves Champions League point
1q8lgyn5wojce11sb5vt3kfmq2.subtitle: After a dramatic second half at Groupama Stadium, Lyon and Chelsea had to settle for a share of the points after a goalless stalemate.
paragraphs: A stunning late save from Hannah Hampton preserved a point for Chelsea as they played out a 0-0 draw with Lyon in the Women's Champions League.
Salma Paralluelo had a second-half goal ruled out for offside, while Chelsea had two penalties overturned by VAR, but it was Hampton's last-gasp heroics that salvaged a point.
Chelsea made a strong start and had the first shot on target as Melvine Malard brilliantly improvised by looping an overhead volley towards goal, but it was an easy catch for Mala Grohs.
Lyon did not take long to grow into the game, though, and Melchie Dumornay threaded it through to Paralluelo, who forced a smart save out of Hampton.
Dumornay drilled narrowly wide shortly after, with Marie-Antoinette Katoto then scuffing her attempt straight at Hampton.
Selma Bacha and Caroline Weir both failed to hit the target as Lyon finished the half on top, and the cagey nature of the game carried over after the break.

Chelsea were awarded a penalty after Tarciane caught Sjoeke Nusken late in the box, but after the referee initially pointed to the spot, a VAR review spotted Lucy Bronze offside in the build-up, and the penalty was overturned.

Lyon thought they had found a potential winner in the 72nd minute after Paralluelo raced onto another superb Dumornay pass and swept her finish past Hampton, but she set off too early, with the offside flag denying her.
Chelsea had another penalty overturned moments later after Lauren James went to ground, but there was not much in the challenge from Damaris Egurrola.
Grohs was fully behind James' first-time effort to deny Chelsea a winner, and just moments later, Hampton made a brilliant save at full stretch to keep out Ada Hegerberg's looping header.
Both sides struggle to find their golden touch

Chelsea have made a stuttering start to the season, struggling to find their free-flowing best in front of goal, but the same cannot be said of Lyon, who beat Servette 8-0 last time out in the Champions League.

The chances at Groupama Stadium on Wednesday were few and far between, though, with both sides ultimately finishing with nine shots apiece after the game opened up in the last five minutes plus stoppage time.

Lyon tested Hampton four times, while Paralluelo scored a lovely goal, if only she had slowed her run behind Bronze slightly better. The expected goals (xG) told the biggest story, with Lyon's 0.78 xG just bettering Chelsea's 0.73.

Ultimately, it was Hampton's late intervention that proved the most vital for Sonia Bompastor on her return to Lyon, as Hegerberg's header looked to be heading in until the goalkeeper got her fingertips to the ball.
Both Chelsea and England will have breathed a sigh of relief that her game did not come to a premature end after a heavy collision with Tabitha Chawinga.

While neither side managed to find a winner in France, Bayern Munich got their first Champions League win of the campaign, beating Benfica 3-0, scoring all of their goals from the 74th minute onwards.

Dumornay drilled narrowly wide shortly after, with Marie-Antoinette Katoto then scuffing her attempt straight at Hampton.

Selma Bacha and Caroline Weir both failed to hit the target as Lyon finished the half on top, and the cagey nature of the game carried over after the break.

Chelsea were awarded a penalty after Tarciane caught Sjoeke Nusken late in the box, but after the referee initially pointed to the spot, a VAR review spotted Lucy Bronze offside in the build-up, and the penalty was overturned.

Lyon thought they had found a potential winner in the 72nd minute after Paralluelo raced onto another superb Dumornay pass and swept her finish past Hampton, but she set off too early, with the offside flag denying her.

Chelsea had another penalty overturned moments later after Lauren James went to ground, but there was not much in the challenge from Damaris Egurrola.

Grohs was fully behind James' first-time effort to deny Chelsea a winner, and just moments later, Hampton made a brilliant save at full stretch to keep out Ada Hegerberg's looping header.

Both sides struggle to find their golden touch

Chelsea have made a stuttering start to the season, struggling to find their free-flowing best in front of goal, but the same cannot be said of Lyon, who beat Servette 8-0 last time out in the Champions League.

The chances at Groupama Stadium on Wednesday were few and far between, though, with both sides ultimately finishing with nine shots apiece after the game opened up in the last five minutes plus stoppage time.

Lyon tested Hampton four times, while Paralluelo scored a lovely goal, if only she had slowed her run behind Bronze slightly better. The expected goals (xG) told the biggest story, with Lyon's 0.78 xG just bettering Chelsea's 0.73.

Ultimately, it was Hampton's late intervention that proved the most vital for Sonia Bompastor on her return to Lyon, as Hegerberg's header looked to be heading in until the goalkeeper got her fingertips to the ball.

Both Chelsea and England will have breathed a sigh of relief that her game did not come to a premature end after a heavy collision with Tabitha Chawinga.

While neither side managed to find a winner in France, Bayern Munich got their first Champions League win of the campaign, beating Benfica 3-0, scoring all of their goals from the 74th minute onwards.

1qh777ogzeb9j1a3ltxl78p5qa.title: 'Role model' Yamal continues to delight Spain staff and team-mates
1qh777ogzeb9j1a3ltxl78p5qa.subtitle: Lamine Yamal has only just turned 19, but Luis de la Fuente already sees the Barcelona superstar as the ideal role model in Spain's squad.
paragraphs: Lamine Yamal is already a "role model" for Spain, despite his tender years, so says coach Luis de la Fuente.
Yamal has enjoyed another fantastic year for both club and country.
He registered 41 goal involvements in all competitions last season for Barcelona, as the Blaugrana successfully defended their LaLiga crown.
Yamal then went on to play a key role as Spain followed up their Euro 2024 triumph by winning the World Cup.
Spain have made a flying start to their Nations League campaign, winning all three of their games, and Yamal is their leading scorer, with four goals.
And De la Fuente says Yamal is already an inspiration for the rest of La Roja's squad, despite only being 19.
"Lamine always wants to play, like all the players. We evaluate and analyse whether it's advisable or not," De la Fuente told reporters ahead of Tuesday's clash with Croatia.
"Lamine is in fantastic form. He's a role model and a born competitor. He's in good shape to play the match. But so are other team-mates, who are all in perfect condition.
"Lamine wants to be the best. He's very competitive, and that's normal; he has the anxiety of a genius who always wants to be at the level he knows he can achieve."
De la Fuente's sentiment was echoed by Dani Olmo, who plays alongside Yamal at Barca.
Olmo said: "Lamine continues to improve with each match. He seems to be getting better and more mature every season.

"At the start of this season, he's helping us not only with his play but also by scoring goals, which is something he demands of himself. He's very important for us both at the club and with the national team."
Yamal has already scored eight goals and laid on six assists in eight appearances for Barca this season.

1qjt6hutsp8xs131lm5v95llkq.title: Palmer and Rice withdraw from England squad as Gibbs-White, Garner come in
1qjt6hutsp8xs131lm5v95llkq.subtitle: Thomas Tuchel will be without Declan Rice, Cole Palmer and Marcus Rashford for England's upcoming Nations League fixtures.
paragraphs: Cole Palmer and Declan Rice are part of a quintet of players who have withdrawn from England duty.
Palmer, who missed out on England's World Cup squad, was selected by Thomas Tuchel for the Three Lions' upcoming Nations League matches.
He has already registered four Premier League goal involvements this season (two goals, two assists).
However, the Chelsea playmaker has now opted out of the squad as he nurses an injury.
It is the same case for Rice, Marcus Rashford, Tino Livramento and Kobbie Mainoo.
Tuchel has called up Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner as replacements.
No player has scored more Premier League goals in 2026 than Nottingham Forest attacker Gibbs-White (13, level with Erling Haaland).

Garner, meanwhile, made his England debut during the March international window, and impressed against Uruguay and Japan, but the Everton midfielder ultimately missed out on a call-up for the World Cup.
The pair will now get a chance to impress in fixtures against world champions Spain, with a double-header against Czechia following, either side of a clash with Croatia.

1qm1h1gzv4y6g16xoopqleujvf.title: Mbappe leaves France camp after suffering tendon injury
1qm1h1gzv4y6g16xoopqleujvf.subtitle: Kylian Mbappe went off injured just before the hour against Turkiye, and he will play no further part in France's Nations League camp.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe has left France's camp following their 1-0 win over Turkiye in their Nations League opener through injury.
Zinedine Zidane made a winning start to life as France's head coach, with Mbappe scoring the only goal of the game nine minutes into the second half.
However, he pulled up immediately after scoring and was taken off the pitch within five minutes, having received treatment, seemingly with a knee problem.
Mbappe scored his 12th goal for France in 2026, equalling the highest total for a Les Bleus player in a single calendar year in the 21st century (also Mbappe with 12 in 2022).

He will not play any further part in this extended international break, however, with France confirming on social media that "he is suffering from a tendon injury and will return to [Real] Madrid for treatment".
Asked about Mbappe's situation shortly after the victory, Zidane told TF1: "It's not going well, unfortunately.
"I think he'll have to go back. We're not going to take any risks. He developed hypertension in his knee during the shot.
"It's not exactly encouraging for him to be able to continue."
Zidane is the first coach to win his first match in charge of France since Aime Jacquet against Italy in 1994 (D4 L1).
France sit second in Group A1, only behind their next opponents, Belgium, on goal difference.
But Zidane was thrilled to get off the mark with three points.
"It's very emotional. It's a successful debut," he added.
"It's not easy to come and play in Turkiye, with such a complicated atmosphere. We played the game we needed to.
"We played well; we pressed them high up the pitch. I saw a lot of interesting things even though we've only had three and a half training sessions.
"It's encouraging. I'm happy with what they did. It was good to see everyone."
As for Turkiye, they were in the game throughout and had their chances to get on the scoresheet, with Ismail Yuksek's unmarked diving header forcing a superb save out of Mike Maignan.
They had 12 shots, like France, and only had a marginally smaller expected goals tally (1.1 xG to Les Bleus' 1.2).
"I am proud; it's a shame we were unable to leave the field with a positive result," head coach Vincenzo Montella told Sky Sport Italia.
"It was an incredible performance, one of our best, especially considering who we were up against.
"We knew that you cannot afford even half a mistake against sides like this, but I thought we had our chances too, and it was a very even game.

"I saw a great team spirit, and that is something we need to carry with us into the next matches. It won't be easy to recover physically and mentally so quickly, so we need that spirit first and foremost.
"I feel sorry for my lads, because they really did give it their all."

1qojeh2n1l0bn1lthi9ii0jc3a.title: 'No gameplan and no ideas' – Makelele slams Mourinho's Madrid after derby defeat
1qojeh2n1l0bn1lthi9ii0jc3a.subtitle: Jose Mourinho criticised Ortiz Arias after Real Madrid's loss to Atletico Madrid, but Claude Makelele says the referee was not to blame.
paragraphs: Ex-Real Madrid midfielder Claude Makelele did not hold back on his former team's performance in their derby defeat to Atletico Madrid, saying they had "no gameplan and no ideas."
Madrid slipped to a 2-1 loss against their cross-city rivals on Sunday, their second in the first seven games of their LaLiga campaign.
With defending champions Barcelona making a perfect start, Los Blancos are already six points off the title pace, and Makelele feels there are glaring issues in their side.

During Sunday's game, Madrid only managed eight shots and 0.3 expected goals, compared to Atleti's 18 attempts and 2.35 xG, though that latter figure was boosted by the penalty from which Alejandro Grimaldo opened the scoring early in the second half.

Dean Huijsen was sent off and conceded that spot-kick for denying Giuliano Simeone a clear goalscoring opportunity, though Madrid had been flat in attack even with 11 men on the pitch, only posting 0.16 xG and one shot on target in the first half.
And Makelele, who represented Madrid 145 times between 2000 and 2003, before working under Mourinho at Chelsea, was bemused by their lacklustre display.
"There is no understanding between the players, nor with the coach. Mourinho must talk to them," he told ESPN.
"The team is weak, there is no gameplan and no clear ideas. There is nothing. Nothing, nothing, nothing... Absolutely nothing. We must demand more from them."

In stark contrast to Madrid's stuttering performance, Atleti scored their second goal – via Jonathan David – at the end of an 18-pass move – the most for any goal scored by either team in a Madrid derby in LaLiga since at least 2005-06.

Afterwards, Mourinho said "the story of the game" was an inept refereeing performance from Ortiz Arias, arguing both Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have seen red for Atleti, the former for a high challenge on Federico Valverde and the latter for treading on Jude Bellingham.
Mourinho brought printed images of both incidents to his post-match press conference, prompting Atleti to hit back on social media, posting: "Stop referee harassment now."
But Makelele was not interested in playing the blame game, saying: "The problem is not the referee; there is an obvious deficiency in the team."
After the extended international break, Madrid host Villarreal in LaLiga on October 10, before visiting Roma in the Champions League four days later.

1qpbmk3xuwfm61ouf8n55ikg6z.title: Marsch urges Canada to be 'cleaner' despite win over Chile
1qpbmk3xuwfm61ouf8n55ikg6z.subtitle: Canada made a winning return to action, edging past nine-man Chile 1-0 thanks to Jonathan David's early goal.
paragraphs: Despite Canada returning to action after the World Cup with a win, Jesse Marsch is keen to see a "cleaner" performance than the one he got against Chile.
Canada edged to a 1-0 victory over their nine-man opponents in the friendly at BMO Field despite dominating for large parts of the match.
Jonathan David scored the winner in the 12th minute. Jacob Schaffelburg's cross was met by Cyle Larin, who saw his shot saved, but it rebounded off him to David, who coolly tapped home.
Lucas Cepeda was then shown a straight red card 35 minutes in after a high boot on Richie Laryea.
Gabriel Suazo also made an early exit, receiving his second booking five minutes after the break – his first was for dissent before his late foul on Niko Sigur.

Canada pushed to try and make the most of their advantage in the second half, but even though they finished with 22 shots worth 2.6 expected goals (xG), with 16 of their attempts coming after the break, they could not get a second goal.
And it is that part of their game that Marsch wants to see an improvement on as they continue to build on their round-of-16 exit from the World Cup.
"Chile makes it hard," Marsch said. "I don't think [our] second half was very good.
"Chile remained aggressive even down two men. The way to make them pay was to be cleaner with the ball and cleaner with ideas and actions around the goal.
"We were too wild, not enough shots on frame, not enough final actions with good connections."
Canada also hit the woodwork twice, with Laryea and Jamie Knight-Lebel going close in the final six minutes of the 90.
Larin was a constant threat for them, having a game-high four shots, 12 touches in the opposition box, two 'big' chances, and winning two of his four aerial duels.
"Every game we play is a must-win," Larin said.
"You don't come here to play and just to draw or get a result."

1qw9rjyxcph9w1sg24xvvcerms.title: United States 4-1 Peru: Pochettino's youngsters shine in friendly win
1qw9rjyxcph9w1sg24xvvcerms.subtitle: The United States' stunning second-half performance secured a big friendly win over Peru in their first match since the World Cup.
paragraphs: Mauricio Pochettino's new-look United States team rallied in the second half to secure a 4-1 friendly win over Peru at Inter.co Stadium.
Gianluca Lapadula cancelled out Justin Ellis' early opener in the first half, but Malik Tillman, Julian Hall and Sebastian Berhalter all scored after the break to secure the victory.

It took less than four minutes for debutant Ellis to score on his home ground in Orlando on his debut, as he met Giovanni Reyna's left-sided free-kick with a glancing header that went in off the far post.
But Peru responded well to the setback and equalised within 11 minutes. Yoshimar Yotun looped a lovely cross into the far post, and Lapadula sent his header back across goal to restore parity.
Tillman had the chance to restore the USA's lead in the 20th minute after meeting Peyton Miller's delivery first-time, but Pedro Gallese was well-placed to thwart him.

Mathis Albert's introduction added a spark, and he won a penalty after cutting inside from the left, getting a shove right on the edge of the box in the 64th minute, though Peru believed the contact happened outside.
Tillman stepped up to guide his spot-kick into the bottom-left corner, with Gallese unable to get a touch despite diving the right way.
And Hall then got a debut goal of his own, getting between two defenders at the far post to tap in Berhalter's brilliantly dangerous low cross from the right in the 72nd minute.
Berhalter then rounded off the goalscoring in the 90th minute with a stunning long-range finish that nestled into the top corner, giving Gallese no chance.
United States make strong post-World Cup start
The buzz of the World Cup was strong in the USA, leading to quite a bit of disappointment when they were knocked out of the tournament in the round of 16 by Belgium.

But having lost three of their last four friendlies before the tournament, Pochettino shook up his pack, bringing on a lot of debutants, and he has now been given a good headache by his young players.

Ellis, who had a joint-team-high three attempts, wasted little time making an impact on a pitch he knows well, and in the second half, Hall took less than 10 minutes to score his first international goal after coming off the bench.
Pochettino made 10 changes, making sure to see as many in his squad as possible, and they impressed, having 16 shots, worth 2.39 expected goals (xG), with six of those on target.
And while they impressed offensively, they also looked strong at the back, only facing two shots on target, though Lapadula's header was a well-taken goal.

1qxo18bqectvr14l24hckiuzz8.title: Ronaldo rules out international retirement but apologises for Portugal exit
1qxo18bqectvr14l24hckiuzz8.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo released a lengthy statement about leaving Portugal's Nations League squad, but he is not thinking about retirement.
paragraphs: Cristiano Ronaldo has promised to have "one or more farewell matches" after confirming he will not retire from international duty with Portugal following a rift with Jorge Jesus.
Ronaldo announced he had left Portugal's Nations League squad ahead of their 4-2 win over Denmark last week and said he would "tell people the truth" about his decision.
The 41-year-old started in the Selecao's 1-0 win over Wales but was taken off in the 67th minute before being an unused substitute in Portugal's 2-1 victory against Norway.
In a lengthy statement posted on social media, Ronaldo said that Jesus had "broken his word" after saying that he would play him for the final 30 minutes against Stale Solbakken's side.
But has now apologised for his actions and said he would accept whatever punishment came his way, but Ronaldo refused to draw the curtain on his career with Portugal.
"I decided to leave the camp without waiting for any further breach of word," one part of Ronaldo's statement read.
"For me, the truth is still the most important thing in the relationship between people. However much it hurts, let them tell me the truth.
"Never, at any moment, have I interfered in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team manager in almost 25 years of my career.
"I accept, for better or worse, what they propose that I do. I respect the decision, and when they break their word to me, I feel that my place is not there.

"I also owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp. Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach's word, as those who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done it. The responsibility is exclusively mine.
"On this subject, I have heard a great deal of talk about farewell matches, that I must have a dignified farewell and that the Federation wants to give me that opportunity.

"I learned in life, often hungry and with nothing to eat, that no one gives anything to anyone. I can promise all my fans, naturally and especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that.

"Therefore, if I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals, I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team. This is, believe me, the purest of truths."
Ronaldo's 146 goals in 234 caps are the most by any male player in international football history, while he is one of only two players to feature in six editions of the World Cup.

However, since the start of 2025, Portugal have won 80% of their matches when Ronaldo has not appeared (P5 W4 D1), compared to just 59% when he has featured (P17 W10 D4 L3), also averaging almost twice as many goals per game without the five-time Ballon d'Or winner (3.4) than with him (1.9).

Cristiano Ronaldo has promised to have "one or more farewell matches" after confirming he will not retire from international duty with Portugal following a rift with Jorge Jesus. 

Ronaldo announced he had left Portugal's Nations League squad ahead of their 4-2 win over Denmark last week and said he would "tell people the truth" about his decision.

The 41-year-old started in the Selecao's 1-0 win over Wales but was taken off in the 67th minute before being an unused substitute in Portugal's 2-1 victory against Norway. 

In a lengthy statement posted on social media, Ronaldo said that Jesus had "broken his word" after saying that he would play him for the final 30 minutes against Stale Solbakken's side.

But has now apologised for his actions and said he would accept whatever punishment came his way, but Ronaldo refused to draw the curtain on his career with Portugal. 

"I decided to leave the camp without waiting for any further breach of word," one part of Ronaldo's statement read.

"For me, the truth is still the most important thing in the relationship between people. However much it hurts, let them tell me the truth.

"Never, at any moment, have I interfered in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team manager in almost 25 years of my career.

"I accept, for better or worse, what they propose that I do. I respect the decision, and when they break their word to me, I feel that my place is not there.

"I also owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp. Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach's word, as those who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done it. The responsibility is exclusively mine.

"I learned in life, often hungry and with nothing to eat, that no one gives anything to anyone. I can promise all my fans, naturally and especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that.

"Therefore, if I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals, I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team. This is, believe me, the purest of truths."

1qypb24zfarua12z1dgfcxnpiy.title: Cherki eyeing more responsibility with France in future
1qypb24zfarua12z1dgfcxnpiy.subtitle: Rayan Cherki enjoyed a positive cameo off the bench against Belgium, helping France to an emphatic comeback victory.
paragraphs: Rayan Cherki is keen to take on even more responsibility within the France national team, claiming he "learned to play in a new position" during this break.
Cherki has played a key role in Zinedine Zidane's unbeaten start to his life as Les Bleus' boss and scored his first international goal since June in their 4-1 win over Belgium in the Nations League.
The 23-year-old was one of three players to come off the bench to score, with his goal giving them the lead after Desire Doue had equalised. Michael Olise also netted twice.
In the four games during this break, only Ousmane Dembele (11) has created more chances than Cherki (seven), who has a joint-team-high two assists.
Cherki has been involved in Zidane's three-man midfield on the right, playing behind Olise to create an impressive link-up.
"People talk about my dribbling, but I'm now playing in a role that requires me to play complete, clean matches, and true football connoisseurs understand that," Cherki told TF1.
"During this training camp, I learned to play in a new position. It's a different style of play: I can't lose the ball.
"I like this position, and you'll see, as time goes on, that I'll take on even more responsibility."
France sit top of Group A1 with 10 points and are in a strong position to qualify for the quarter-finals during the November break.
It has been a strong start to life as France head coach for Zidane, who has been without the injured Kylian Mbappe for the last three games, and Cherki was full of praise for his new boss.
"Honestly, it's fantastic. We have an extraordinary relationship," Cherki said of Zidane.
"He treats all the players the same; he chats with everyone about anything and everything. He teaches us the fundamentals, especially the importance of having the ball."

1r2qk7n1dlhsd1915rgs064svi.title: Seattle Sounders 2-1 Sporting Kansas City: Roldan grabs last-gasp winner
1r2qk7n1dlhsd1915rgs064svi.subtitle: Cristian Roldan scored in the 90th minute to propel the Seattle Sounders to a 2-1 victory over Sporting Kansas City.
paragraphs: The Seattle Sounders made it three straight MLS wins as their surge up the Western Conference continued with a last-gasp 2-1 victory over Sporting Kansas City.
Cristian Roldan grabbed the decisive goal at Lumen Field for the Sounders, who sit seventh in the West and are unbeaten in eight games.

SKC goalkeeper Stefan Cleveland was busy early on when he denied Peter Kingston, tipping a long-range attempt over the crossbar, before the visitors went close through Calvin Harris, who forced Alex Roldan into a goal-line clearance.

A flurry of SKC chances followed, and they eventually broke the deadlock when Andre Luiz struck on the cusp of half-time, just after Seattle's Andrew Thomas had made a sprawling save to keep out Stephen Afrifa's attempt.
Yet Seattle drew level just six minutes after the restart, with substitute Sebastian Gomez capitalising on Jordan Morris' fantastic work in the build-up.
Caden Clark went close to nudging the Sounders ahead, but Thomas was called upon to thwart Taylor Calheira at the other end.
That save paved the way for Cristian Roldan to come up with the goods in the 90th minute, as he pounced on a defensive mix-up to clinch all three points.
Sounders flip the script
This is the first time since May that Seattle have won an MLS game that they were trailing at half-time.
And after a 13-match winless streak, it is now three victories on the spin for the Sounders, who are looking good for a playoff place.

Seattle are now unbeaten in five straight matches against SKC (W4 D1). The Sounders managed to avoid defeat only three times in their previous ten games against Kansas City (W3 L7), dating back to 2019.
Sporting, who sit bottom of the West, may consider themselves unfortunate, though, considering they had the better chances, creating opportunities worth a combined 2.05 expected goals to 1.7 xG.
Luiz was in the thick of the action again for SKC.

He has been involved in three goals in his last two appearances, after becoming the first player to record a goal and an assist in a regular-season away match for Sporting since Dejan Joveljic against LA Galaxy in March, when he netted and laid one up against the Houston Dynamo in SKC's previous outing.

1rcdfqtp0mepz13ff9xr39u36a.title: Modric 'ashamed' of Croatia's heaviest-ever loss to England
1rcdfqtp0mepz13ff9xr39u36a.subtitle: England's attackers ran riot in a 7-0 victory over Croatia, leaving experienced midfielder Luka Modric furious.
paragraphs: Luka Modric said Croatia's historic 7-0 defeat to England in the Nations League represented the first time he had felt "ashamed" in his illustrious international career.
Croatia slumped to the heaviest loss in their history on Saturday, in front of a crowd mostly made up of schoolchildren in Rijeka, due to UEFA-enforced restrictions on the home side.

Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka all scored before half-time, marking the first time England had seen four different players get on the scoresheet before the interval since March 2013 against San Marino (Frank Lampard, Jermain Defoe, Ashley Young, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain).
Kane and Saka then got another goal apiece as Thomas Tuchel's side refused to ease up after the break, while Morgan Rogers came off the bench to score England's seventh.

Croatia had never previously lost a home game by more than a three-goal margin, going down 4-1 to the same opponents in September 2008, while a 6-0 loss in Spain in 2018 was their previous worst-ever defeat.
And the scoreline was no fluke, either, with England putting up a huge expected goals (xG) figure of 6.43 to Croatia's 1.39.
That is the largest figure ever amassed by any team in a Nations League game by some distance, surpassing Belarus' 4.89 xG against San Marino in September 2018.
And Modric did not mince his words concerning Croatia's display after full-time, saying: "You can't play football like that. We looked like we had four or five less players.
"It is difficult to find an explanation for such a performance, without winning duels, making fouls, showing aggressiveness and togetherness.
"I've been here for 20 years, but for the first time, I feel ashamed after a game.
"You can lose, or you can play against an opponent who is better – and they are right now.
"But losing like this and squandering the reputation we've built over the years is unacceptable. I feel ashamed."

Things do not get any easier for Croatia, either, as they host Spain in their final game of this international break on Tuesday, knowing a defeat would almost certainly end their chances of qualifying for the last eight.
"We need to come together and stay united because another difficult game awaits us," Modric added.
"We have to show our true selves, that we have fight and pride, desire, willpower and unity. You can't lose that overnight."
Head coach Slaven Bilic, meanwhile, was at a loss to explain Croatia's complete loss of organisation.
"It is difficult to say anything after a night like this. We are sad, disappointed, and I feel sorry for the fans and the children who were at the game," Bilic said.
"We talked, it is hardest for us, and we did not expect this would happen. I don't know what to call it, whether it's a blackout, but it's hard to analyse a game when you lose 7-0.
"We knew they were a top team, but that we couldn't match them in any way... that attacks your confidence, your will, and everything falls apart and goes the wrong way."

1rrmwt2hbhkj91tfxap38uxmjj.title: David enjoying 'breath of fresh air' since joining Atletico
1rrmwt2hbhkj91tfxap38uxmjj.subtitle: Jonathan David is in fine form for club and country, and he credits his move to Atletico Madrid as a key reason for his change in fortune.
paragraphs: Jonathan David believes joining Atletico Madrid this summer has given him a "breath of fresh air".
The 26-year-old joined Diego Simeone's side on a season-long loan from Juventus on deadline day, with Atletico reportedly having the option to make the move permanent for €25m.
David struggled at Juve last term, scoring eight goals across 46 appearances and providing five assists, though he has enjoyed a much better start to life in LaLiga.
The Canada international has directly contributed to four goals in as many games for Atleti (three goals, one assist), scoring in each of his three LaLiga appearances.
Before the international break, in which he has already scored the winner in Canada's 1-0 victory over Peru, David netted the match-defining goal in a 2-1 win in the Madrid derby.

David is the only player to have scored in each of his first three matches with Atleti in LaLiga in the 21st century, and the only Atleti player to have scored on his LaLiga debut and on his debut against Real Madrid in the competition since 2000.
"Maybe it’s a breath of fresh air. Maybe it helps that it’s a bit of a change of environment," said David when asked about his recent form.
"I play with a lot of players that have that quality to find the last pass. They make it pretty simple for me, to be honest. All I have to do is finish."
Canada head coach Jesse Marsch also revealed he played a small role in David's transfer to Atleti.
"I know Simeone from playing against him, from watching him over the years," said Marsch.

"[I said to him] if you want an attacking player that can score goals, has a lot of quality, and also [to] work for the team and give everything he has to the team, I can't think of a better striker than Jonathan David."

1ry2cnu06y6yv1s6w7fz2va4cq.title: Belgium 3-0 Turkiye: De Bruyne steals the show with two stunners
1ry2cnu06y6yv1s6w7fz2va4cq.subtitle: Belgium returned to winning ways in the Nations League as Kevin De Bruyne scored twice in a 3-0 victory over Turkiye.
paragraphs: Kevin De Bruyne scored two stunning goals as Belgium defeated Turkiye 3-0 in the Nations League.

The Napoli midfielder scored either side of half-time at Stade Maurice Dufrasne, while Romelu Lukaku came off the bench to also get on the scoresheet and help Mark van Bommel secure his first home win as Belgium head coach.
De Bruyne needed just 10 minutes to break the deadlock, playing a give-and-go with Dodi Lukebakio before poking through the legs of Abdulkerim Bardakci and finding the bottom-right corner.

Both sides had their chances before half-time; Lukebakio saw a powerful strike pushed onto the woodwork by Ugurcan Cakir, while Merih Demiral inexplicably fired over from inside the six-yard box from Zeki Celik's low cross.

Lukebakio struck the frame of the goal again early in the second half before Senne Lammens got down quickly to keep out Yunus Akgun, and the goalkeeper's efforts were repaid by De Bruyne at the other end.
After Youri Tielemans regained possession just outside the box, he teed up De Bruyne, who wonderfully curled into the top-left corner from distance to give Belgium some much-needed breathing room.

Lukaku then wrapped up the victory in the 76th minute, converting from Charles De Ketelaere's low centre with ease, while Belgium also managed to hold onto their clean sheet despite late pressure from Turkiye.
Belgium's veterans thriving in new era

Van Bommel's introduction as head coach marked a new era for Belgium, and while the likes of Mika Godts and Lukebakio are proving their worth under the new boss, it was the familiar faces of De Bruyne and Lukaku who made the crucial difference.

Although Belgium's 1.24 expected goals (xG) tally was lower than Turkiye's 1.33, De Bruyne's two goals accounted for just 0.17 xG, highlighting the quality of the midfielder's strikes to give the hosts a 2-0 lead.
De Bruyne also created three chances, a tally only bettered by Godts (four) for Belgium, while he also won five of his 10 duels before being replaced in the 82nd minute.

For Turkiye, meanwhile, it was the same old story. They failed to take their opportunities in front of goal, which is what caused their group-stage exit at the World Cup, despite Arda Guler creating a match-high five chances.

1s0vejma7m6161a0bf5945j9fb.title: 'Don't make a big deal out of it' – Jesus shuts down reports of rift with Ronaldo
1s0vejma7m6161a0bf5945j9fb.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo cut a frustrated figure on Portugal's bench last time out, but Jorge Jesus attempted to assuage any fears of a rift.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus insisted there is no rift between himself and Cristiano Ronaldo after the 41-year-old was an unused substitute against Norway in the Nations League.
Ronaldo featured from the start in Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales, though he was taken off in the 67th minute and replaced by Goncalo Ramos.

Jesus had stated before the 2-1 win against Norway that he planned for Ronaldo to participate, but he did not bring him on during the victory, with Portugal's captain then training away from his team-mates on Monday and Tuesday.
Media reports suggested there had been a "crisis" meeting between Jesus, Ronaldo and the Portugal Football Federation (FPF) president Pedro Proenca to clear the air.
But at a press conference ahead of Portugal's clash with Denmark on Thursday, Jesus, who also managed Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, insisted there were no issues between the pair.
"I don't have one player; I have 23 players," Jesus said.
"Regarding Ronaldo, let me ask two questions; I won't answer any more. The main thing is Denmark.
"It's true that I made an agreement with him, just like I made a plan with Bruno Fernandes. I told Cris that he wouldn't play in the games in Norway and Denmark.
"I know his physical condition well; I was with him in Saudi Arabia. In games every three days, he rarely played. He never trained on the first and second days after the games.
"I agreed with him. That's what happened. I don't go to the bench thinking that, at the 60th minute, I'm going to take Carlos Daniel off. That's not how I am on the bench.
"The game dictates what I'm going to do. I agreed that he wouldn't play, but I might also need him in the final minutes... If the game required it.

"I worked with Cris for a year. It seems like there's already something going on between me and him. Don't make a big deal out of it; there's nothing going on. It was the same plan with Bruno Fernandes.
"Status is one thing; the rules are another."
Asked again about the friction between the pair, Jesus added: "Any player who warms up and then doesn't come on – no one is happy.
"Much less Cris, Pele, [Diego] Maradona. 'Warm up for thirty minutes, me?' Then, as the coach, I decided they weren't included."
Portugal are looking to continue their perfect start to the Nations League in Copenhagen, having taken six points so far to sit top of Group A4.
Denmark, meanwhile, are third, having followed up a 3-2 defeat to Norway with a 2-0 victory over Wales last time out.

"I worked with Cris for a year. It seems like there's already something going on between me and him. Don't make a big deal out of it; there's nothing going on. It was the same plan with Bruno Fernandes.

"Status is one thing; the rules are another."

Asked again about the friction between the pair, Jesus added: "Any player who warms up and then doesn't come on – no one is happy.

"Much less Cris, Pele, [Diego] Maradona. 'Warm up for thirty minutes, me?' Then, as the coach, I decided they weren't included."

Portugal are looking to continue their perfect start to the Nations League in Copenhagen, having taken six points so far to sit top of Group A4.

Denmark, meanwhile, are third, having followed up a 3-2 defeat to Norway with a 2-0 victory over Wales last time out.

1s4tz93967h5n1e5fvk2uf62ww.title: De la Fuente: Spain have recovered the spirit of 2010
1s4tz93967h5n1e5fvk2uf62ww.subtitle: Spain are showing no signs of slowing down as they prepare to play their first match on home soil since winning the World Cup.
paragraphs: Luis de la Fuente believes Spain have "recovered the spirit of 2010" with their recent exploits as his side prepare to host Croatia in the Nations League.
Spain are the reigning European and world champions, having lifted the World Cup for the second time in July by beating Argentina in the final.
On their way to clinching both titles, they have strung together a 39-game unbeaten streak (across 90 minutes), winning 30 of those matches (D9).
They extended their run with a stunning 3-2 comeback win over England, with Mikel Oyarzabal coming off the bench to haunt the Three Lions once more by scoring the winner.
Spain's next match will see them play on home soil for the first time since winning the World Cup, as they will host Croatia in Seville.
"For us, it is a pride to see our country committed to the national team," De la Fuente said in his press conference.
"Where we are going, we have recovered the spirit of 2010; people are proud to be Spanish.
"I am honoured to be the national coach of my country. I have a house in Seville, and it causes me a very special emotion."
Spain are unbeaten in their last three meetings with Croatia, winning two and drawing the other – though they eventually won that match on penalties in the Nations League.
Like La Roja, Croatia also opened with a win on Saturday, beating Czechia 2-1, which only leaves them behind Spain on goal difference in Group A3.
"Of course, I think Croatia can compete, and the first ones who have to believe it are them," De la Fuente said of their opponents.
"If not, they would not run. There is no rival or perfect day. The height of these situations is that even if you are superior to the opponent, you can lose.
"We know Croatia well; we have played a lot with them. They have world-class players and a very competent new coach.
"We have to give a better version of the one we gave in London. Footballers understand it that way. Every day we demand more from ourselves because the opponents are more complicated every day."

1sexch8cprg911c57jhr1vh2gd.title: Aston Villa sack Arroyo following winless WSL start
1sexch8cprg911c57jhr1vh2gd.subtitle: Having been thrashed 4-0 by Tottenham on Sunday, Aston Villa have relieved Natalia Arroyo of her duties.
paragraphs: Aston Villa have sacked manager Natalia Arroyo following their winless start to the Women's Super League season.
Villa sit 13th in the 14-team table after four games, having played out two draws and two defeats.

Things started promisingly as they held title favourites Chelsea to a 1-1 draw on the opening matchday, but a pair of heavy defeats to Manchester City (1-4) and Tottenham (0-4), either side of another 1-1 draw at Brighton, have left them marooned in the relegation play-off spot.
And on Tuesday, Villa confirmed Arroyo had been relieved of her duties, with women's technical advisor Brian Sorensen taking charge until a permanent successor is found.
The club said: "Everyone at Aston Villa would like to thank Natalia for her efforts and wish her all the best in her future endeavours."

Arroyo, who previously coached Real Sociedad for four years, took the reins in January 2025 and oversaw a strong end to that season, with Villa finishing sixth after being discussed as potential relegation candidates.
Villa then finished ninth in 2025-26 and failed to kick on at the start of the current campaign, despite making nine new signings in a busy transfer window.

1swnm130vactq13ofzh6lz9vl9.title: Sunderland hand Le Fee new five-year contract
1swnm130vactq13ofzh6lz9vl9.subtitle: Having helped Sunderland qualify for the Europa League and scored their first European goal in 53 years, Enzo Le Fee has penned a new deal.
paragraphs: Sunderland's creative midfielder Enzo Le Fee has signed a new five-year contract with the club.
Le Fee joined the Black Cats on loan from Roma in January 2025, with that deal containing a purchase obligation if they were to be promoted from the Championship.
The Frenchman immediately assumed a key role under Regis Le Bris, starting in a 2-1 play-off final victory over Sheffield United, which led to him becoming a permanent Sunderland player for £19m.
And he has continued to shine in the Premier League, making 41 appearances in the competition while scoring six goals and providing seven assists.

His 13 goal involvements and 61 chances created are both team-high totals since the start of 2025-26, and those figures helped propel Sunderland to a seventh-place finish and Europa League qualification last term.
Last week, Le Fee scored from the penalty spot to secure a 1-0 victory over AZ at the Stadium of Light, in Sunderland's opening match in that competition.

That made him the Black Cats' first goalscorer in Europe since October 1973, when Micky Horswill scored their second goal in a 2-1 victory at home to Sporting CP in the Cup Winners' Cup, only for the Lisbon giants to recover in the return fixture and progress 3-2 on aggregate.
"I'm really happy to have signed a new contract with Sunderland," Le Fee told the club's website, having agreed fresh terms to run until 2031.
"From the moment I arrived, I've felt the passion of the supporters and the ambition of everyone at the club – I've loved my time here.
"We've achieved something special together over the past couple of seasons, but I believe this is just the beginning.
"I feel very settled here and I'm excited to continue developing, competing at the highest level and helping the club move forward.
"I'm very proud to wear the Sunderland shirt and I can't wait to see what we can achieve together in the years ahead."

Having lost 5-3 to Manchester City in a thrilling encounter prior to the international break, Sunderland have four points from five Premier League games this season, with Brighton their next opponents on October 10.

1sx1zurasqtk41pnunepb1n4qu.title: Czechia 0-2 England: Gordon and Kane score again as Tuchel's side get off the mark
1sx1zurasqtk41pnunepb1n4qu.subtitle: England are off the mark in the 2026-27 Nations League, using their numerical advantage to earn a 2-0 victory over Czechia.
paragraphs: Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane both hit the back of the net for the second game running, this time helping England to a 2-0 win over 10-man Czechia in the Nations League.
England were aided by Pavel Sulc's first-half red card, and this time, when Gordon and Kane gave them the lead, they held onto it for their first victory in Group A3.

Czechia gave England an early scare after Elliot Anderson failed to intercept a long pass down the left wing and Sulc raced onto it, but James Trafford rushed out to smother the shot while one-on-one.

Lukas Cerv then volleyed wide of the target before England got their first clear opening when Morgan Rogers turned in the box and bent an effort onto the far post, with Anderson's follow-up blocked by Robin Hranac.
But the momentum changed in the 25th minute; Sulc caught Anderson above the ankle with his studs, and his yellow card was upgraded to a red following a VAR review.
Gordon saw a tight-angled shot parried just after the half-hour mark, while Kane forced Matej Kovar into a fine stop on the stroke of half-time.
But it took England just 67 seconds after the restart to break the deadlock, with Trent Alexander-Arnold whipping in a stunning cross, which Gordon nodded past the goalkeeper.

Lewis Hall sent the ball trickling narrowly wide as England upped the pressure, which told in the 68th minute as Kane latched onto the loose ball after Rogers tripped and swept a low finish into the bottom-right corner.
Czechia were not out of the game, though, with Adam Hlozek forcing Trafford into a fine stop nine minutes later from the edge of the box after a quick counter-attack.
Eberechi Eze and Jude Bellingham tested Kovar late on, but the Czechia goalkeeper kept the score down; though with a numerical disadvantage, they could not take advantage of that.
England find their groove in Prague
After losing their opener, there was slightly more pressure on England to get a win in this game, though Thomas Tuchel was insistent pre-match that it did not fall into the "must-win" category.
Either way, it was three points that England needed after the disheartening loss to the world champions.
Czechia, despite starting brightly, were up against it after the red card - the last side to beat England with 10 men were France in June 2017 (3-2 home win).

It was two in-form players that ultimately proved the difference. Gordon now has four goals and four assists across his last nine appearances, while he was assisted by Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first England appearance in almost two years.
As for Kane, he has now netted five goals in seven Nations League appearances since the start of the 2024-25 edition.

Despite having 22 shots worth 1.37 expected goals (xG) in a strong attacking display, Tuchel will be keen to focus on the clean sheet, given England had conceded 13 goals in their six games before this.

Trafford - the first England goalkeeper other than Jordan Pickford to start consecutive games since Nick Pope in September 2022 - made two big saves, though the Three Lions only conceded six shots worth 0.33 xG overall.

1t4mz1zeypxyb1g5ybxdunw0es.title: Cucurella reveals attempt to try and tempt Rodri to join Real Madrid
1t4mz1zeypxyb1g5ybxdunw0es.subtitle: Rodri was of interest to Real Madrid before joining Barcelona, with Marc Cucurella saying he tried to tempt him to the Spanish capital.
paragraphs: Marc Cucurella revealed he sent Rodri a "subtle message" to join him at Real Madrid this summer before the midfielder opted to join Clasico rivals Barcelona.
Cucurella was a part of a summer rebuild at Madrid, with the Spanish international joining Los Blancos for a reported €55m (£47.5m) transfer fee from Chelsea.
The likes of Yan Diomande, Ibrahima Konate, Denzel Dumfries and Bernardo Silva also moved to the Spanish capital, with Rodri another player linked with a move to Madrid.
However, Rodri decided against linking up with Jose Mourinho and instead joined Hansi Flick at Barcelona, signing for a reported €76.5m (£65m) from Manchester City.
Cucurella and Rodri's moves came after helping Spain to the second World Cup crown this summer, with the latter scooping the Golden Ball along the way for his performances.
Spain are preparing for their first match since beating Argentina in the final, with England their opponents in the first match of their Nations League campaign this Saturday.
But speaking ahead of their trip to Wembley Stadium, Cucurella said that he openly tried to sway Rodri's decision in an attempt to play alongside him at club level.
"I don't really like pressuring or influencing team-mates," Cucurella said. "These are personal things.
"It's true that I sent him a subtle message, before the news broke, saying I hoped we'd become team-mates.
"He replied, but didn't give anything away. I'm happy for him [at Barca], though I hope he doesn't have too much success."
Rodri has enjoyed a perfect start to life with Barcelona, helping the Blaugrana begin their LaLiga title defence with seven wins from seven matches so far.

Only Pau Cubarsi (456), Eric Garcia (393), Pedri (391) and Gerard Martin (378) have completed more successful passes in the league for Barcelona than Rodri (368), while he also ranks third in Flick's squad for tackles won (eight).

Barcelona have started a LaLiga season with seven wins in their first seven games for the fourth time, after doing so in 2013-14, 2017-18 and 2024-25, and they already find themselves six points ahead of Madrid in the table.
Madrid lost their second league game of the season last Sunday, going down 2-1 to city rivals Atletico Madrid after Dean Huijsen was sent off early in the second half.
Mourinho is already coming under pressure early in his second stint in the Madrid dugout, though Cucurella believes his team are more than capable of turning things around.
"We didn't finish the period before the break in the best way," Cucurella added. "It's all a process, but the important thing is to build a solid foundation.
"Let's see if we can find a good balance and build a strong, united group. If the season ends the way we all want it to, no one will remember the start."

1te3035tqghan1tv19sssrbvr3.title: Joao Felix planning European return but happy at Al-Nassr for now
1te3035tqghan1tv19sssrbvr3.subtitle: Joao Felix is halfway through a two-year deal with Saudi Arabian champions Al-Nassr, but he misses competing in the Champions League.
paragraphs: Joao Felix admits he often thinks about returning to Europe to compete in the Champions League, though the Portugal forward is happy at Al-Nassr for the moment.
Joao Felix joined Al-Nassr last year and helped them win the Saudi Pro League title in his first season, providing 33 goal involvements in as many games (20 goals, 13 assists).

Having been one of European football's hottest properties when he broke into Benfica's side in 2018-19, he made a blockbuster €126m move to Atletico Madrid at a young age but struggled in the Spanish capital.

After scoring 20 goals in 43 outings for Benfica in 2018-19, Joao Felix has never netted more than 10 times in a single season in Europe's top five leagues, enduring up-and-down spells with Atleti, Chelsea, Barcelona and AC Milan.
The 26-year-old only has one year remaining on his contract with Al-Nassr, who appointed Ange Postecoglou as their new head coach in July, as Jorge Jesus took the Portugal job.
He is hoping to help Cristiano Ronaldo pass the 1,000-goal mark in the coming months, with the 41-year-old netting to hit the net another 21 times.
But beyond that, Joao Felix is eyeing a return to the top level of European football.
Asked about his aims in an interview with AS, the attacker said: "To get better – I'm very happy at Al Nassr.
"This will be my second year. I'll be 27 at the end of the season. I do plan to return to Europe, though perhaps not right away.
"I don't know if that will be at the end of this season or the next, but I want to go back, play in the Champions League again and compete there again.
"It's always different. Playing in Europe, in the Champions League, against the best teams in the world... it gives you extra motivation. That's definitely on my mind.
"I'm very comfortable in Saudi Arabia. I'm happy and enjoying my football, but it's true that I'm also thinking about returning.
"I don’t know whether it'll be next year, in two years, three or four, but I'd like to play in European competitions again."
Al-Nassr are third in the Pro League table with 16 points from their first seven matches in 2026-27, two adrift of leaders Al-Hilal.

Joao Felix is currently on international duty with Portugal, who have won their opening two games under his former Al-Nassr boss Jesus and face Denmark next time out, in the Nations League on Thursday.
He found the net in their 2-1 win over Norway on Sunday, taking him to five goals in his last 10 starts for his country.

1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.title: Luis Enrique not taking Classique triumph for granted
1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.subtitle: Marquinhos struck the winner as Paris Saint-Germain overcame Marseille in Sunday's matchup between France's two most successful clubs.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique said Paris Saint-Germain can never take a win over Classique rivals Marseille for granted, after they battled to a 2-1 success at the Stade Velodrome.
Marquinhos' 74th-minute strike settled the contest as PSG claimed back-to-back Ligue 1 victories, having started their campaign with three winless games.
The Brazilian's goal came just two minutes after Angel Gomes got Marseille back on level terms, with that strike also coming hot on the heels of Ferran Torres' opener.
Marseille had captain Timothy Weah sent off shortly after going 2-1 down, with the United States international hauling Nuno Mendes down from behind while already on a yellow card.

PSG have now won 10 of their last 14 away Ligue 1 games against Marseille (D3 D1), though Nayef Aguerd missed a huge chance to snatch a point for OM deep into stoppage time, as he headed wide on the stretch.
And Luis Enrique says three points will never come easily for any visiting side at the Velodrome.
"It was the match we had planned for, with a lot of difficulties. Everyone said it would be easy, but playing at the Velodrome is not an easy thing," he told Ligue 1+.
"We tried to play, we created fewer chances in the first half because the opponent defended very well. In the second half, everything changed, we made a very good effort."

The result piles more pressure on Bruno Genesio, who is the first Marseille boss to lose four of his first five league games in charge of the club since the duo of Willy Kohut and Andre Gascard in 1938.

Marseille will spend the three-week international break 17th in the Ligue 1 table, with this the latest point into a season that they have sat in the relegation zone since 2011-12, when they were 20th with three points after six games and ultimately finished 10th.
But Luis Enrique expects them to come good eventually, saying: "Nothing was easy, we saw a very good OM team, with the way they defended. They have a great coach, I'm sure they will improve."

1tytdnqt0jdlu181prjod107ue.title: Richter: Sporting KC comeback proved Philadelphia are far from perfect
1tytdnqt0jdlu181prjod107ue.subtitle: The Philadelphia Union are the team in form in the MLS, and their 11-game unbeaten run is on the line against Orlando City SC this weekend.
paragraphs: Ryan Richter described the Philadelphia Union's thrilling comeback against Sporting Kansas City as "outrageous", but said it was a warning sign to not get complacent.
Philadelphia's unbeaten run in MLS extended to 11 matches at Sporting Park last weekend, despite finding themselves three goals down against Sporting KC.
Andre Luiz's brace and a goal from Wyatt Meyer blew the Union away in the opening 16 minutes, with their sensational stretch under interim boss Richter looking set to end.
However, Philadelphia turned the game on its head in the space of four second-half minutes, with Bruno Damiani, Cavan Sullivan and Milan Iloski hauling their team level.
The turnaround was complete thanks to an own goal from Zorhan Bassong, with the result helping Philadelphia move up to sixth in the Eastern Conference.

And while he was pleased with the mentality of his players to complete the turnaround against Sporting KC, Richter acknowledged that better sides in the division will punish them should Philadelphia hand them an advantage like that again.

"The mentality of this group is outrageous," Richter said. "It would have been easy for us to quit at half-time. We're on the road, long journey, down 3-0, guys going away with their national teams after the game.

"But the way the guys responded in the second half was fantastic. I am proud of them and congratulations to them for showing again the way they believe in each other right now and what is possible with this group.
"It's fun to be a part of, and it's fun to watch, but we have to keep going. We got a reminder that we're not perfect and when we're not at our best, any team can beat us."
Philadelphia's next MLS outing sees them welcome Orlando City SC to Subaru Park this weekend, with the Lions also in the hunt to secure their spot in the playoffs.
Just two points and one place separate the two sides in the standings after Orlando fell to a 4-2 defeat against the New England Revolution last time out.
Martin Perelman's side saw their three-match winning run in the league come to an end, with late goals from Peyton Miller and Carles Gil sealing the win for New England.

"Very frustrated, of course, with the result. It was a big challenge for us because we came here after the game on Wednesday and were facing, of course, a team that is doing well in the league," Perelman said of Orlando's defeat to the Revolution.
"The context of the game was difficult. We knew that. Taking that into account, I think we made a very big effort. We made some mistakes, especially in the first half.

"And then we were able to come back in the second half, compete, tie the game, and then, I think there we have some gaps to improve as a team. I think we grew a lot during this season in many things. We are competing. We are up there. Everybody knows how we started.

"I think the process of the team is there, but if something we need to improve is this. We need to close these kinds of games. So, that's the frustration, but I also need to recognise the effort of the players. I have to do it because it was there."
Philadelphia Union – Bruno Damiani
With the in-form Sullivan away on international duty with the United States, the emphasis will fall on Damiani to continue Philadelphia's excellent run of form under Richter.
Only Iloski (13) has scored more MLS goals for Philadelphia than Damiani's eight, though the Uruguayan does have five goals in his last three league appearances.
Orlando City SC – Martin Ojeda
Ojeda recorded his team-leading 12th MLS goal of the season and his 46th across all competitions this year against New England last time out.

The Argentine has recorded three goal contributions in his last four matches across all competitions (two goals, one assist) and he is now just one goal short of tying Facundo Torres' club record of 47 goals across all competitions.
MATCH PREDICTION: PHILADELPHIA UNION WIN
As predicted, Philadelphia are the clear favourites in the Opta supercomputers pre-match simulations. The Union are now 11 games unbeaten in the MLS, tying the club record.

However, wins at Subaru Park against Orlando have proved hard to come by in recent years. Indeed, Philadelphia have failed to win their last three home league matches against the Lions (D1 L2) since a 5-1 victory back in September 2022.

But they come up against an Orlando side that have managed just three away league wins all season, though prior to their defeat to New England in their last such match, had drawn against Minnesota United and beaten Atlanta United.
Philadelphia Union – 65%
Orlando City SC – 16.4%
