1u05b3hp5sign1kt8f0qhsjiid.title: Australia 1-1 Brazil: Rayan nets last-gasp equaliser for Ancelotti's new-look side
1u05b3hp5sign1kt8f0qhsjiid.subtitle: Australia came within touching distance of stunning Brazil, but Rayan popped up with a late equaliser to seal a share of the spoils.
paragraphs: Brazil denied Australia a famous victory in Queensland as Rayan's stoppage-time header earned the Selecao a 1-1 draw in Thursday's international friendly.
Carlo Ancelotti said the match was the beginning of a new generation for Brazil, but his team fell behind to Nestory Irankunda's stunning second-half free-kick.
However, Bournemouth forward Rayan made Brazil's late pressure count, with the two sides squaring off once again next Tuesday at Suncorp Stadium.
Connor Metcalfe helped Australia make a quick start, with his shot whistling over Hugo Souza's crossbar after Vinicius Junior was cheaply dispossessed by Jacob Italiano.

Irankunda then fired way wide before the Australian defence put their bodies on the line to keep out Vinicius and Raphinha, with the hosts going close to the opening goal just before the break, but a deep corner just evaded Alessandro Circati at the far post.

Brazil thought they had taken the lead on the stroke of half-time when a neat one-two between Endrick and Estevao saw the latter finish past Patrick Beach, but the goal was ruled out after a VAR review for a foul on Harry Souttar by Bruno Guimaraes in the build-up.
Ancelotti's side built on that momentum after the break, with the in-form Raphinha first seeing his shot smothered by Beach before he drilled narrowly wide of the right post.

Estevao then fired over after Vinicius' attempt deflected kindly to him, and Australia made the most of that reprieve in the 68th minute through Irankunda, who curled a sensational free-kick past Souza and into the top-left corner.

Brazil penned Australia back into their own penalty area in their search for a late equaliser, and their persistence was rewarded in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time, with Rayan's thunderous header from a Raphinha corner going in off the crossbar.
Irankunda and Herrington star for Australia's young guns

With both nations playing in their first matches since their respective exits from this summer's World Cup, many predicted Brazil's quality in the final third to be too much for Australia, but Popovic's side proved they are more than capable of mixing it with the established nations.

And Australia's combative performance at the back was spearheaded by Lucas Herrington. After becoming the youngest player to start a knockout match at the World Cup for the Socceroos this summer, he proved why he was worthy of his switch to the Premier League with Hull City.

Herrington won all three of the duels he contested, while only Circati (eight) and Souttar (six) made more clearances than his four. He also made two interceptions, but it was another exciting talent in Irankunda that shone at the other end.

Irankunda was handed a third consecutive start, his longest such run for Australia, and he delivered by becoming only the second player to score against Brazil for the Socceroos, after Shaun Murphy back in June 2001.

But after restricting Brazil to very little in their search for an equaliser, Australia will be frustrated after being undone by a set-piece. Ancelotti's side will, however, feel they were deserving of the result. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.15 from their 16 shots to their opponents' tally of 0.45 from their seven attempts.

1ugouwltxz6qhz6qvzbk0q4tv.title: Italy 0-2 Belgium: Godts and Lukebakio condemn Mancini to losing return
1ugouwltxz6qhz6qvzbk0q4tv.subtitle: Roberto Mancini was unable to mark his Italy return with a victory, as Belgium won their first match under new boss Mark van Bommel.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini lost on his return as Italy boss after a 2-0 defeat against Belgium in the Nations League.

Mika Godts struck in the 20th minute before substitute Dodi Lukebakio secured all three points in the second half as Mark van Bommel made a winning start to his reign as Belgium boss at Stadio Olimpico.

After Gianluigi Donnarumma and Senne Lammens made early saves at either end, with Charles De Ketelaere and Moise Kean denied respectively, Godts opened the scoring after sending Gianluca Mancini and Diego Coppola to the ground before slotting into the bottom-right corner.

Belgium dominated the first half after taking the lead, but could not add to their advantage as Donnarumma pulled off a brilliant double save to keep out De Ketelaere and Nicolas Raskin, while the Italy captain also saved a powerful header from Godts moments after Diego Moreira miscued a simple finish.

Maxim De Cuyper flashed a shot wide of the right post before the break, but Italy were the bigger threat in the second half as Kean forced Lammens into a clever save with his right leg just two minutes after the restart.

Francesco Pio Esposito then went close twice, first seeing his header go straight at Lammens before the Belgium shot-stopper pulled off a strong save to deny the Inter striker's first-time effort from Nicolo Cambiaghi's cut-back.

However, Italy were made to pay for their wastefulness in the 69th minute as Lukebakio drove forward from the halfway line, cut inside past Sandro Tonali and Daniel Maldini and curled into the bottom-left corner from distance.

The hosts had late chances to force a nervy ending, but Riccardo Calafiori saw his shot with the outside of his boot go wide of the right post, while Giorgio Scalvini inexplicably missed the target from inside the six-yard box.
Contrasting emotions for Mancini and Van Bommel

A better second-half display from Italy offered some hope for Mancini, with 1.22 of their 1.52 expected goals coming after the break, but the Azzurri were unable to turn things around against Van Bommel's Belgium.

Both Donnarumma and Lammens made six saves in what almost proved to be a tale of two halves in Rome, but Lukebakio's timely second for the Red Devils was enough to clinch a winning start to their Nations League campaign.

There was plenty for Van Bommel to be pleased with, as Kevin De Bruyne led the match in chances created (five), while Godts led the way in dribbles attempted (five) and, among Belgium players, possessions won (four) to go along with his goal.

The new Belgium boss will know Lammens' saves early in the second half played a huge role in the victory, especially after Belgium's missed opportunities before the break, though he will certainly be the happier of the two managers.
Up next for Belgium in the Nations League is a home match against France, while Mancini will be looking for the first win of his second stint when Italy travel to Turkiye next.

1umg60acgeijv1q9zpi8wpq0oj.title: Mead thrilled by 'seamless' transition at Man City
1umg60acgeijv1q9zpi8wpq0oj.subtitle: While Beth Mead was not on the scoresheet against Charlton Athletic, she played a big role in helping Manchester City get over the line.
paragraphs: Beth Mead says her transition to Manchester City has been "seamless" after she helped the team extend their perfect start to the Women's Super League.
City were made to work hard for all three points on Saturday but edged to a 1-0 win over Charlton Athletic to make it four wins from four so far.
Alex Greenwood scored the only goal of the game in the first half, bending in a free-kick for her first league goal since April 2024.
Mead more than played her part, though, as she finished with game-high totals for chances created (four), touches (98) and passes in the final third (47).
"It's a different way of playing [at City from Arsenal]; I've been playing in a different role here for most of the games," Mead told BBC Sport.
"It's a very good team who like to play football, and that's how I like to play. It's been a bit seamless fitting in, but very different players to play with; you have to get used to.
"I'm just trying to do the right things, recover well and go again. I'm trying to play as many minutes as I can. I'm never going to complain about that.

"It was difficult. It's hard off the back of a Champions League game. Charlton were really hard to beat; they defended really well. Our intensity could have been better on the ball, but we got the three points."
City have won each of their first four WSL matches in a season for the first time since 2019-20.
And the Citizens have now won 29 of their 30 games against newly promoted teams, winning eight in a row since a 2-1 loss at Liverpool in 2022-23.
Andree Jeglertz opted to make six changes to his starting line-up from their win over Liverpool last weekend, with Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp starting on the bench.
With Women's Champions League matches adding to their schedule, he noted how important it is to be able to shuffle his pack given the quality of his squad.
"It's a good performance; we should have created more scoring chances," he said.
"Sometimes the last pass wasn't there, but there was also players who haven't played together as much. We have rotated a couple of players.

"You can't say a player is a full-back because they need to be able to play in different areas. For me, it's about how can I get the best out of players like Alex Greenwood; sometimes she plays better in different areas."

1ur5y32ga6uu512tn6izb1ktkt.title: 'Stop referee harassment now' – Atleti hit back at Mourinho following derby comments
1ur5y32ga6uu512tn6izb1ktkt.subtitle: Jose Mourinho launched into a rant about refereeing standards following Real Madrid's defeat to Atletico Madrid, who have now hit back.
paragraphs: Atletico Madrid have hit back at Jose Mourinho following his rant about referee Ortiz Arias in the aftermath of their derby win over Real Madrid.
Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David were on target on Sunday as Los Colchoneros overcame their cross-city rivals 2-1 at the Estadio Metropolitano.
The victory lifted Diego Simeone's side to second in LaLiga, five points behind leaders Barcelona, going into the three-week international break, with Los Blancos a point further back in fourth.

But their win was not without controversy, as Madrid had centre-back Dean Huijsen sent off for denying Giuliano Simeone a clear goalscoring opportunity, and Mourinho felt Atleti were fortunate to keep all 11 men on the pitch.
Lee Kang-In avoided punishment for a high challenge that caught Federico Valverde on his ankle, leaving the Uruguay international requiring medical tests.
Cristian Romero, meanwhile, was only cautioned for what Madrid believed was a stamp on Jude Bellingham's knee, despite Arias being sent to the VAR monitor to check the incident.

1uuwiu0m1wfda1vd9kejfeivg6.title: Pulisic targets new Milan deal after positive signs under Amorim
1uuwiu0m1wfda1vd9kejfeivg6.subtitle: Christian Pulisic's AC Milan contract runs out at the end of this season, but he hopes to extend his deal after working with Ruben Amorim.
paragraphs: Christian Pulisic hopes to extend his AC Milan contract soon as he is "very positive" about their future under Ruben Amorim.
Amorim's Milan are fifth in Serie A after the opening five games, just two points behind leaders Roma, as the Rossoneri remain unbeaten in the competition (W3 D2).
Milan did lose their Europa League opener 2-0 against Benfica, but they bounced back ahead of the international break with a 3-0 league victory over Lecce.
Pulisic scored against Lecce; it was his first Serie A goal in 266 days, since December 2025 against Hellas Verona.
Between those strikes, the American had attempted 39 shots without finding the net in the league, before finally scoring with his 40th attempt.
The 28-year-old struggled for form under Massimiliano Allegri last season, scoring 10 goals and providing four assists in 34 games, 20 of which came as a starter.
However, after missing the start of the 2026-27 campaign with injury, Pulisic has found his feet quickly under Amorim.
Pulisic's current deal with the Rossoneri expires next summer, though reports suggest the club hold an option to extend by another year, and the forward is eager to continue in Milan.
"It has been a strange start to the season," Pulisic told Sky Sport Italia.
"I was coming back from an injury and I really wanted to play, but it took time. I worked with the team and coach to get back on the field.
"We are learning his system, how he wants to play. I am very positive about him. Our most recent match was one of the best, so we want to build on that.

"He wants us to find certain positions, especially when we have the ball, and to make specific movements. Obviously, we are also given some freedom in attack, but there are principles and positions to keep to.
"I am very happy at Milan. The club is giving me everything, it helps me a great deal. I am concentrating on playing, but we'll talk about it [new contract], I hope soon.
"I feel really happy at Milan and want to continue here."

1uv7la8e2fj8o1pwm899c6zg4z.title: Herrington: Australia's performances against Brazil show how far we've come
1uv7la8e2fj8o1pwm899c6zg4z.subtitle: Australia drew and lost to Brazil during their two friendly matches, but Lucas Herrington was full of praise for how they fought.
paragraphs: Australia defender Lucas Herrington is optimistic about the team's future, saying their performance in their 4-2 defeat to Brazil "shows how far we've come".
The Socceroos came within minutes of a shock win in the first of their two friendlies with Brazil but were ultimately held to a 1-1 draw last Friday after Rayan's stoppage-time leveller.
In Brisbane on Tuesday, Australia briefly led, with Alessandro Circati and Connor Metcalfe both scoring to flip the script after Vanderson's third-minute opener.
However, Raphinha equalised just before the break from the penalty spot, before goals from Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior – again from 12 yards – secured the win in the second half.
Australia became just the second team from the AFC confederation to score twice against Brazil in a game in the last 21 years, after Japan beat the Selecao 3-2 last October.
The hosts finished the game with just seven shots – scoring with both of their attempts on target – but posted 1.5 expected goals (xG) and had 51 final-third entries, more than Brazil's 44.
And Herrington was thrilled to see the fight Australia put up against Carlo Ancelotti's side across both matches, as he believes team and fan morale is at an all-time high.
"It's so special; you can see the support around the stadium," Herrington said.

"It's awesome, the first time playing for the Socceroos in Brisbane. It means everything. I would see them growing up in Brisbane, I know how big the football community is here. It's been so nice to come home and see the reception we've got.
"All I've ever wanted is to play for the Socceroos, so to do that so early and with such great people is amazing.

"You want to play these types of games, and I think it's a credit to Australia and the Socceroos and the fans that Brazil want to come here and play us. It was a great game; we really put them under pressure.
"It shows how far we've come. Since I've been a Socceroos fan, this is the biggest reception and the most excitement that's been around the team."

1v0edv0wojk4h1mvn4ekjy98c4.title: Tah: Germany prepared to 'walk through fire' for new boss Klopp
1v0edv0wojk4h1mvn4ekjy98c4.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp's Germany tenure began with a draw against the Netherlands, but Jonathan Tah has been impressed with his new boss.
paragraphs: Jonathan Tah praised Jurgen Klopp for his immediate impact since taking charge of Germany, saying that the players are ready to "walk through fire" for their new boss.
Klopp's first game in charge of Germany ended in a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands, with the former Liverpool boss denied a win by Cody Gakpo's stoppage-time equaliser.
The 59-year-old is now preparing to oversee his first game on home soil at WWK Arena, with Greece their opponents in the second game of their Nations League campaign.
Germany were perhaps fortunate to leave with a point against the Netherlands, with Xavi, also making his international bow, masterminding a dominant second-half display.
The Oranje finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.6 from their 14 shots after the break, while they were also able to restrict Germany to a tally of 0.2 from their five attempts.
But Tah is confident Klopp is the right man to take Germany forward, citing his success at club level with Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool behind his reasoning.
"It's the experience he brings from every club, that mix of fun and passion, that absolute will to win, and also the way he brings the team along. He can really fire us up," Tah said.
"I think after our initial meeting, everyone walked out thinking, 'Okay, we're ready to walk through fire together now'.
"He just has this ability to galvanise a team. We've seen that in the past too. That's something he does exceptionally well, and I think that's why he's been so successful."
Another player Tah was asked about was Liverpool's Florian Wirtz, who has again come under fire for a string of underwhelming performances so far this season.
Wirtz and Jonathan Burkardt have been called up one game earlier than expected to replace Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala, who sustained injuries against the Netherlands.
At club level, Wirtz has managed just one assist in six appearances in all competitions, though his 12 chances created are the third-highest total in Andoni Iraola's squad.
The former Bayer Leverkusen forward is yet to hit the form he showed during his time in the Bundesliga, but Tah has backed Wirtz to rediscover his spark.
"I find it pretty extreme the way he's been attacked," Tah said of Wirtz. "I know the kind of player he is and that he's going to shine even more.
"I know what he's capable of and, eventually, everyone will understand."

1v7grwu078eb91cajins4auyol.title: France 4-1 Belgium: Super-subs spark Nations League rout
1v7grwu078eb91cajins4auyol.subtitle: Belgium were holding out valiantly against France, but three substitutes flipped the script at the Stade de France.
paragraphs: Desire Doue, Rayan Cherki and Michael Olise scored in a remarkable finale to propel France to a come-from-behind 4-1 win over Belgium.
With just 13 minutes of normal time left in Monday's Nations League contest at the Stade de France, Zinedine Zidane's unbeaten start as France coach was in real jeopardy.
The visitors led through Dodi Lukebakio's 35th-minute strike, with the forward having burst clear on the counter-attack and finished brilliantly.
Without Kylian Mbappe, France lacked a clinical touch in the first half, with Ousmane Dembele, Maghnes Akliouche, Eduardo Camavinga and Esteban Lepaul seeing half-chances pass them by.
France's profligacy continued after the break, with Lepaul denied from point-blank range, yet Les Bleus' luck changed when Zidane turned to his bench.
Cherki and Olise were the first changes, and though they helped build the pressure, it was not until Doue entered the fray that they finally made the breakthrough.
Doue superbly created space on the edge of the box and, on the turn, drilled a sublime finish into the bottom-right corner.
The turnaround was complete four minutes later, as Olise drove to the byline and steered it back for Cherki, who duly finished.
Olise got in on the act in the 88th minute, nudging home from Doue's cutback.
And the same pair combined to complete a stunning rout in stoppage time, with Olise sliding in a crisp effort after latching onto Doue's sumptuous pass.
Super-subs to the rescue
France had all the ball, all the territory and all the intent for the vast majority of the second half, yet it really did seem as though they were short of ideas.
It seemed like Zidane would be left to bemoan Mbappe's absence, and that France's hopes of qualifying from Nations League Group A1 could be in the balance heading into the November fixtures.
Instead, their star power off the bench proved just too much for Belgium to handle.
Doue, Cherki and Olise were all spellbinding. Each of them crafted two chances, while Olise ended up having four shots, a total bettered only by Dembele (five).

Zidane made 10 changes to his starting XI, but he always knew he had real, world-class quality in reserve. This win did not come easy, but once France's talent clicked into gear, there was nothing Belgium could do.
France finished with 23 shots for a combined 2.0 expected goals, but that does not tell the whole story.
Belgium created opportunities worth a combined 0.59 xG, yet their second-half xG came in at just 0.04, as they were completely dominated.
It is now three wins from four for Zidane to start his tenure, while Mark van Bommel's Belgium sit on six points from a potential 12.

1vdbz2qe7f5h112epxk2r6i5lq.title: Mancini insists patience is needed for new Italy era
1vdbz2qe7f5h112epxk2r6i5lq.subtitle: Roberto Mancini lost on his second debut in charge of Italy, but he was confident of turning things around against Turkiye on Monday.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini believes patience will be needed at the start of his second stint with Italy after their defeat to Belgium in their Nations League opener.
Macini's return to the Azzurri dugout did not go to plan, with goals in either half from Mika Godts and Dodi Lukebakio sealing the win for Mark van Bommel's side.
The result saw Italy lose a home match while conceding two goals without scoring any for the second time in the last 40 years, after a 2-0 defeat against Croatia in August 2006.
Italy ended the match with 1.5 expected goals (xG), though only 0.3 of their tally came in the first half, while Belgium accumulated 2.5 of their 2.7 xG before the break.
Gianluigi Donnarumma made six saves to try and inspire a comeback for Italy, but Senne Lammens also made six stops at the other end to ensure Belgium emerged victorious.
Following the defeat, Mancini conceded that his team fell below expectations at the Stadio Olimpico, with a trip to Matli Stadyumu Ataturk Spor Kompleksi to face Turkiye up next.
Mancini's main request was to allow his Italy team time as they begin a new era, though he said the congested Nations League schedule was difficult for his players to navigate.
"I expect the team can put in a good performance against Turkiye, improving the pressing and the aggression," Mancini told reporters.
"In these days we haven't had time to prepare anything new, so I'm not expecting any great novelties.
"Above all, we need time to work to get to know each other and to build a team that can be competitive. We don't need anything else."
Mancini's comments were echoed by Sandro Tonali, who was a part of the team that failed to qualify for a third consecutive World Cup earlier this year.
It is a new-look Azzurri side, with the likes of Michael Kayode, Alessandro Romano, Issa Doumbia, Alessandro Vergara and Mohamed Ali Zom called up for the first time.
"The important thing now is to react, and we can do that within a few days. The group is very healthy, with a lot of young players," Tonali said.
"Having everything immediately is difficult, we don't have the star player. Time is there, we have to spend time together, work and enjoy ourselves together.
"We are healthy, strong men. With time our qualities will come out."
Following their clash with Turkiye, Italy face France next Friday before concluding the international break with a home game against Vincenzo Montella's side.
Because of the quick turnaround, Mancini revealed there would be several changes to the team that were beaten by Belgium.
"I think we have to stay calm and not get agitated in the way that is happening," Mancini added.
"We played against a strong side in Belgium, who did cause us difficulty, but then the team reacted well.
"Matches are made of episodes, the game could have changed, even if Belgium deserved to win in the end. In terms of personnel, we will definitely change.
"It is impossible to have one player available for four games this close together. We can also assess other players in matches this important."

1vj9a3vafo6cs1a6krcb93q86u.title: 'Alvarez is the past' – Barcelona move on from summer target
1vj9a3vafo6cs1a6krcb93q86u.subtitle: Barcelona were open about their pursuit of Julian Alvarez in the summer, but have closed the door on the Atletico Madrid striker for now.
paragraphs: Barcelona sporting director Deco insists their interest in Julian Alvarez "is the past" after failing to sign the Atletico Madrid striker this summer.

Barca reportedly saw an offer of over €100m rejected by Atleti, who later revealed they would refuse to negotiate with their rivals due to the Blaugrana's public pursuit of the Argentina international.
Real Madrid's €150m bid was also rejected by Atleti, while reports suggested Alvarez turned down interest from Premier League side Arsenal.
Alvarez has featured four times for Diego Simeone's side this term, with only one of those appearances coming as a starter, registering just one assist across all competitions.
The 26-year-old made his return from a brief injury in Atleti's Madrid derby before joining up with the Argentina national team.
Barca managed to sign Gabriel Jesus late on in the window after the exits of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, and Deco revealed any immediate interest in Alvarez is now over.
"Julian Alvarez is the past," Deco said at the Portugal Football Summit.
"Barcelona now have to look forward. It wasn't possible in the end. We made an offer. [Atleti] said they would not transfer him and we had to look for other solutions.
"I hope things go well for him and that he can help his club."
Barca have also been linked with a move for 15-year-old Manchester United prospect JJ Gabriel in recent weeks.
Widespread reports emerged stating Gabriel had asked to leave United, with Barca and Madrid among the teams said to be monitoring the situation.
Deco, however, has put an end to the speculation, saying: "There's nothing to say about this boy.
"It's normal that players are linked with us. It always happens. There's a huge market for that with a lot of interests involved, even when [players] are young.
"But we are not interested in any player in his situation. I'm not sure what's happening, and if he's still a Manchester United player. We are not involved in that.
"First of all, we need to understand how the situation is before we try to do something. To speak about young, teenage players, it is not our business."

Barca managed to sign Gabriel Jesus late on in the window after the exits of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, and Deco revealed any immediate interest in Alvarez is now over.

"Julian Alvarez is the past," Deco said at the Portugal Football Summit.

"Barcelona now have to look forward. It wasn't possible in the end. We made an offer. [Atleti] said they would not transfer him and we had to look for other solutions.

"I hope things go well for him and that he can help his club."

Barca have also been linked with a move for 15-year-old Manchester United prospect JJ Gabriel in recent weeks.

Widespread reports emerged stating Gabriel had asked to leave United, with Barca and Madrid among the teams said to be monitoring the situation.

Deco, however, has put an end to the speculation, saying: "There's nothing to say about this boy. 

"It's normal that players are linked with us. It always happens. There's a huge market for that with a lot of interests involved, even when [players] are young.

"But we are not interested in any player in his situation. I'm not sure what's happening, and if he's still a Manchester United player. We are not involved in that.

"First of all, we need to understand how the situation is before we try to do something. To speak about young, teenage players, it is not our business."

1vospb7qu65a1ac0d5isypkq0.title: Man City found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules
1vospb7qu65a1ac0d5isypkq0.subtitle: After being found guilty of multiple charges, Manchester City insisted they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League."
paragraphs: Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18 by an independent Commission, the league has said.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Premier League said City had been found guilty of all charges that related to serious breaches of the financial rules and the majority of charges which were "in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League's investigation".
Following widespread reports surrounding the verdicts last Friday, City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak insisted he was still confident of proving the club's innocence.
City have until October 2 to exercise their right to appeal, and the club suggested that they plan to do so as part of a robust statement published after the verdict.
It read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission that has been published.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League, and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.
"The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

The Commission found that during the nine-season period, among other breaches, City "arranged 'sham' contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on 'sham' agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs".
It added that "Manchester City was significantly in breach of both the Premier League’s and UEFA's spending limits".
Comments from Premier League Chief Executive Richard Masters were included in the league's statement. He said the issue of sanctions would be dealt with at a later stage.
"The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period," said Masters.
"It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

"It also vindicates the Premier League's decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

"It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

"This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches.
"Now we have the Commission's decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans."
The statement also made clear the Premier League's desire to move through the next stages of the process swiftly.

It added: "The club has the right to appeal the independent Commission's findings and has until Friday 2 October to exercise that right. The Premier League Board's intention is that the full process (including any appeals and publication of relevant decisions) is concluded as soon as possible."

1vti29e1jbzts1xjheqztrgw5c.title: Aguirre returns to Spain with LaLiga strugglers Valencia
1vti29e1jbzts1xjheqztrgw5c.subtitle: After spending two years away from LaLiga, Javier Aguirre is back in Spain, being tasked with trying to turn Valencia's fortunes around.
paragraphs: Javier Aguirre has been appointed as the new head coach of Valencia on a contract that will run until the end of the campaign.
Aguirre arrives at the Estadio de Mestalla following a two-year stint in charge of Mexico, who he led to the round of 16 at this summer's World Cup.
The 67-year-old's deal contains an option for him to remain at the helm for a second season in Valencia, who have made a dismal start to 2026-27.
Valencia are 19th in LaLiga with four points from their opening seven games, with Carlos Corberan sacked just two months after extending his deal until 2028.
Oscar Sanchez took interim charge and helped Valencia to their first win of the season against Alaves, before overseeing a 3-2 defeat to Real Sociedad last Sunday.
Aguirre arrives with plenty of experience. He has managed 468 matches in LaLiga, the fifth-highest total of any foreign coach in the history of the competition.

The Mexican will be the fourth foreign manager to coach seven different teams in LaLiga, after Roque Olsen (seven), Ferdinand Daucik (nine), and Marcel Domingo (11), having previously taken charge of Osasuna, Atletico Madrid, Real Zaragoza, Espanyol, Leganes and Mallorca.
Aguirre's arrival comes after he announced ahead of this summer's World Cup that he would be leaving Mexico, with Rafael Marquez coming in to take over.
He was unable to end Mexico's wait for a first quarter-final appearance since 1986, after they were beaten 3-2 by 10-man England on home soil.

The defeat was Mexico's first at the Azteca in a competitive match for 13 years, since losing to Honduras in a qualifier for the 2014 World Cup, while it was the first time they had conceded three goals at the venue since a 4-3 triumph over Brazil in August 1999.
But Aguirre will now turn his attention back to club football, having last been in charge of Mallorca, who he helped avoid relegation from LaLiga in 2021-22.
Aguirre also led Mallorca to the Copa del Rey final in 2024, but they were beaten on penalties by Athletic Club before he parted ways with the club that summer.
His first home game in charge will come against Athletic on October 17, but he will make his bow for Valencia six days earlier, away to Racing de Santander.

1w2ez5c95zm8s1n4q1e7fhnui5.title: 'Concern has never been a thing' for St. Louis boss Damet
1w2ez5c95zm8s1n4q1e7fhnui5.subtitle: St. Louis City will be aiming to extend their unbeaten run in MLS to 17 games when they face the New York Red Bulls on Wednesday.
paragraphs: St. Louis City boss Yoann Damet insisted "concern has never been a thing" for him this season as his side prepare to take on the New York Red Bulls.
After a slow start to the 2026 campaign, St. Louis are now fifth in the Western Conference, and they could go level on points with second-place FC Dallas if they beat the Red Bulls.
St. Louis defeated Toronto FC 3-1 last time out, conceding deep into second-half stoppage time, while they have also reached the final of the U.S. Open Cup in recent weeks.
Damet's side are on an 18-game unbeaten run across all competitions, but the Frenchman believes his players have been threatening a run like this one all season.
"I look at these guys and they have been the same since January," said Damet. "Concern has never been a thing.
"Focus and preparation has been a thing since the start of the year. I think every new day is a new day to get better and to prepare for our next game.
"I think those guys have been like that since day one, so this week has been no different.
"We know we have another big game in New York and everybody is excited and locked in preparing for that game."
NYRB, meanwhile, are eighth in the East after back-to-back 1-0 wins over the Columbus Crew and rivals New York City FC.
Julian Hall scored the lone goal in their win over NYCFC, the 18-year-old’s 10th goal of the season and fourth match-winner.
This match with St. Louis was scheduled to take place on Saturday, but was postponed due to adverse weather conditions.
New York Red Bulls – Cade Cowell
With top scorer Hall unavailable after being called up to the United States squad, Cowell will look to step up for NYRB.
The 22-year-old, who has scored twice in 2026, has six assists this term, with only Emil Forsberg registering more (seven).
St. Louis City – Simon Becher
Seven different St. Louis players have at least five goal contributions during the team's current 16-game unbeaten run, led by Becher's nine (seven goals, two assists).
Nine different St. Louis players have scored a match-winner in that time, with Tomas Totland (two) the only one with multiple (one own goal winner).
MATCH PREDICTION – ST. LOUIS CITY WIN
This will be St. Louis City's 148th match in all competitions and 130th in the regular season, but their first-ever match against the New York Red Bulls.
St. Louis extended their regular-season unbeaten run to 16 games (W11 D5) with a win over Toronto, equalling NYRB's 2016 run for the third-longest in a single regular season in MLS history.
The only longer single-season unbeaten runs in regular-season play in MLS history are 19 straight by Dallas in 2010 and 18 straight by the Crew in 2004.

NYRB have posted back-to-back wins for the third time this season with victories over Columbus and NYCFC. The Red Bulls have won three straight regular-season matches only once over the last three seasons, doing so in May 2025.
New York Red Bulls – 27.3%

1wn54tsih5751bpu2n7ej54il.title: Spain 3-1 Czechia: World champions still perfect as Krejci red card halts fightback
1wn54tsih5751bpu2n7ej54il.subtitle: Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Mikel Merino scored for Spain as they defeated 10-man Czechia 3-1 in the Nations League on Saturday.
paragraphs: Spain maintained their 100% record in the 2026-27 Nations League with a hard-earned 3-1 victory over Czechia, who had captain Ladislav Krejci sent off late on.

Following England's 7-0 humilation of Croatia elsewhere in Group A3, the world champions did not have things anywhere near as easy in Oviedo, after Luis de la Fuente made nine changes to his starting lineup.

After first-half goals from Lamine Yamal and Rodri, Jiri Slama's strike got the visitors – managed by Spaniard Santi Denia – back into the contest, only for Krejci's 85th-minute dismissal and a poacher's finish from Mikel Merino to kill their hopes of a fightback.

Yamal only needed six minutes to have an impact, as he exchanged passes with Dani Olmo, got the ball out of his feet near the right corner of the area, then curled a sumptuous effort past Antonin Kinsky.
Despite Spain dominating possession, they did not create another major chance until just beyond the half-hour mark, when Kinsky showed great reactions to deny Olmo.

But the Tottenham goalkeeper was beaten again in the 35th minute, with Rodri feeding his fellow Barcelona midfielder Olmo, continuing his run into the area, then finishing calmly when the ball deflected into his path.

Alex Baena also worked Kinsky late in the first half, but De la Fuente's withdrawal of Yamal at the interval removed some of Spain's attacking impetus, and Czechia got back into the game when Slama was slipped in by Adam Hlozek and finished unerringly across David Raya.

Czechia thought they had an unlikely equaliser in the 79th minute, as Raya spilled Krejci's looping header and Ryan Naderi prodded over the line, but Lukas Cerv was penalised for holding Robin Le Normand when the initial cross came into the area.

Krejci was booked for dissent following that incident, having screamed in the face of referee Vassilios Fotias, and that moment proved costly as the Wolves defender then dragged Roberto Fernandez back to stop a counter-attack and was shown a second yellow card.

Victor Munoz went agonisingly close to making it 3-1, but Spain's clinching goal did arrive in the 89th minute, with the Liverpool winger involved. He kept the attack alive following Stepan Chaloupek's terrible tackle on Fernandez, and when Kinsky parried his shot, Merino was waiting to fire into the empty net.
Czechs lose their cool as Barcelona stars dominate

Despite the one-sided look of the stat sheet, with Spain accumulating 1.99 expected goals (xG) to Czechia's 0.49, outshooting their visitors by 18 to five and having a 69% possession share, this game was far from straightforward for the World Cup holders.
Czechia looked to have La Roja on the ropes when Slama's goal halved the deficit, but Krejci's loss of composure ultimately cost them.
Ultimately, it was Spain's Barcelona stars that did the damage as they extended their record unbeaten run to 41 games and put themselves on the brink of the quarter-finals.

Yamal now has 12 goals in his last nine games for club and country (four for Spain in the Nations League, eight for Barcelona in all competitions), with a 3-1 LaLiga win over Sevilla being the only game in which he has failed to find the net in that period.

Spain's second goal was the result of a lovely combination between Rodri and Olmo, who were the only players remaining from their starting lineup the last time they faced Czechia, also in the Nations League in June 2022.

1wrp7lzqo8je81mup9pt0psejb.title: Netherlands 1-1 Germany: Gakpo denies former Liverpool boss Klopp in stoppage time
1wrp7lzqo8je81mup9pt0psejb.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp was just a minute away from a debut win in charge of Germany, only to be denied by his former Liverpool attacker Cody Gakpo.
paragraphs: A stoppage-time equaliser from Cody Gakpo denied his former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp a winning start with Germany, as the Netherlands salvaged a 1-1 draw in the Nations League.

It looked like Felix Nmecha's 32nd-minute strike would settle an entertaining and at times fractious affair between two old rivals under new coaches, with Barcelona great Xavi also making his Netherlands bow.
But in the second of three minutes of second-half stoppage time, Gakpo met a cross from debutant Ruben van Bommel brilliantly on the stretch, ensuring the points were shared in Group A2.

The first moment of drama came after 12 minutes, as Virgil van Dijk – another of Klopp's former Liverpool stalwarts – glanced Tijjani Reijnders' inswinging corner beyond Marc-Andre ter Stegen. But a VAR review led to the goal being chalked off, due to Brian Brobbey backing into the Germany goalkeeper.

Germany then saw Kai Havertz limp off following a high challenge from Quinten Timber, the twin brother of his Arsenal team-mate Jurrien, though substitute Younes Ebnoutalib almost made an immediate impact as Bart Verbruggen blocked his near-post drive.

And another injury to a Premier League forward played a role in the opening goal. As the Netherlands appealed for a foul on the stricken Brobbey, Germany looked set to kick the ball out, but Nadiem Amiri and Joshua Kimmich instead kept the attack going, and Nmecha swept home after Nathaniel Brown's centre flicked into his path.
A glaring miss from Karim Adeyemi prevented Germany from going 2-0 up late in the first half, but it was one-way traffic from then on with the Oranje laying siege to Ter Stegen's goal.

He thwarted Denzel Dumfries from close range with his right boot, then Mexx Meerdink – another Netherlands debutant – put the ball in the net but saw a foul given against Van Dijk. The young AZ forward also turned Dumfries' cross wide on the slide as Germany closed in on a big three points, but they would be denied with time almost up.

Gakpo showed tremendous athleticism to divert Van Bommel's cross past Ter Stegen while in mid-air, though the Dutch forward was arguably fortunate to avoid a very late red card after the restart, when he trod on Yannik Engelhardt.
Gakpo denies Klopp as the Netherlands impress
Few international coaching debuts in recent years have been as eagerly anticipated as this one.

Indeed, Klopp oversaw 674 games as a manager in the Bundesliga and the Premier League across spells with Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool, the most matches in Europe's top five leagues that any Germany coach had accumulated before taking charge.

But this game showed the size of the task awaiting him, as Germany were penned back throughout the second half by an impressive Netherlands side. The Oranje racked up 3.12 expected goals (xG) and 22 shots, compared to Germany's 1.5 xG from 10 attempts.
And in the end, it was Gakpo – who played 79 games under him for Liverpool, scoring 23 goals in that time – that made Klopp wait for his first victory in charge of his country.

There was at least a notable landmark for Klopp's captain Kimmich, who was at the centre of the controversy leading up to Nmecha's goal, on his 115th cap. He has now surpassed Toni Kroos (114) to sit seventh outright in Germany's all-time charts.

Both teams are back in action on Sunday, with Germany hosting Greece and the Netherlands visiting Serbia, but with Havertz and Brobbey both hobbling off, both came out of a bruising encounter with injury concerns.

A glaring miss from Karim Adeyemi prevented Germany from going 2-0 up late in the first half, but it was one-way traffic from then on with the Oranje laying siege to Ter Stegen's goal.

He thwarted Denzel Dumfries from close range with his right boot, then Mexx Meerdink – another Netherlands debutant – put the ball in the net but saw a foul given against Van Dijk. The young AZ forward also turned Dumfries' cross wide on the slide as Germany closed in on a big three points, but they would be denied with time almost up. 

Gakpo showed tremendous athleticism to divert Van Bommel's cross past Ter Stegen while in mid-air, though the Dutch forward was arguably fortunate to avoid a very late red card after the restart, when he trod on Yannik Engelhardt.

Gakpo denies Klopp as the Netherlands impress

Few international coaching debuts in recent years have been as eagerly anticipated as this one.

Indeed, Klopp oversaw 674 games as a manager in the Bundesliga and the Premier League across spells with Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool, the most matches in Europe's top five leagues that any Germany coach had accumulated before taking charge.

But this game showed the size of the task awaiting him, as Germany were penned back throughout the second half by an impressive Netherlands side. The Oranje racked up 3.12 expected goals (xG) and 22 shots, compared to Germany's 1.5 xG from 10 attempts.

And in the end, it was Gakpo – who played 79 games under him for Liverpool, scoring 23 goals in that time – that made Klopp wait for his first victory in charge of his country.

There was at least a notable landmark for Klopp's captain Kimmich, who was at the centre of the controversy leading up to Nmecha's goal, on his 115th cap. He has now surpassed Toni Kroos (114) to sit seventh outright in Germany's all-time charts.

Both teams are back in action on Sunday, with Germany hosting Greece and the Netherlands visiting Serbia, but with Havertz and Brobbey both hobbling off, both came out of a bruising encounter with injury concerns.

1wyyx7kypvzng1kqcxsqdpbbbk.title: Sweden 3-1 Poland: Gyokeres scores again for Potter's men
1wyyx7kypvzng1kqcxsqdpbbbk.subtitle: Sweden made it two wins from two as they continue their bid for promotion to League A, with Viktor Gyokeres on the scoresheet once more.
paragraphs: Viktor Gyokeres was on target for Sweden once again as Graham Potter's side stayed perfect in the Nations League with a 3-1 win over Poland.
Sebastian Szymanski had cancelled out Benjamin Nygren's early opener, but Yasin Ayari and Gyokeres both struck after the break to make it two wins from two in Group B4.
Piotr Zielinski and Patrik Walemark saw a shot saved at either end within the opening four minutes before Nygren nodded in Victor Lindelof's flick-on from a recycled corner eight minutes in.

Walemark was denied by a smart Marcin Bulka save at the near post shortly after, but Poland kept the pressure on and, after Matty Cash saw a driven shot pushed away by Viktor Johansson, they found an equaliser.

Nicola Zalewski shook off his defender on the left of the area and fizzed a dangerous cross into the six-yard box, with Szymanski sprinting forward to tap in from close range with two minutes of the first half remaining.
Ayari had already seen a curler touched behind in the second half before he got his 63rd-minute goal, this time bending his shot into the bottom-right corner after ghosting past Szymanski.
Gyokeres then made sure of the three points nine minutes later, volleying in unmarked at the far post after Walemark's perfectly weighted right-sided cross.
Gyokeres finds his groove with Sweden

It is no secret that Gyokeres has had a difficult start to the season, with the Arsenal striker restricted to a few appearances so far for the Gunners, though that might change following Kai Havertz's injury while away with Germany.
But with Sweden, who were without the injured Alexander Isak, he has already scored two goals in two games, making him their top scorer at the halfway stage of the international break.

Overall, he has now contributed to goals in his last five Nations League games (eight goals, two assists), but he was once again on the outskirts for large periods, having just two shots in total. His five touches in the opposition box were the second-highest total in the team, though.

Poland enjoyed a strong first half, with only one goal to show for it despite their 13 shots – which were more than Sweden managed throughout the entire 90 minutes (12) – but even after throwing on Robert Lewandowski in the closing stages, they could not mount a fightback.

1wzp4sylqp3g14dctwhmxr2c7.title: Martinez: Argentina must forget World Cup heartache and celebrate Messi
1wzp4sylqp3g14dctwhmxr2c7.subtitle: Lionel Messi will make his farewell appearance for Argentina during the international break, before he steps away from the Albiceleste.
paragraphs: Lisandro Martinez says Argentina's players are determined to put their World Cup final heartache behind them and savour Lionel Messi's international send-off next month.

The Albiceleste could have become the first back-to-back winners of FIFA's showpiece tournament since Brazil in 1958 and 1962, after Messi inspired them to a final appearance in North America this summer.
However, Enzo Fernandez's red card proved costly as Spain beat them 1-0 in extra time, with Ferran Torres scoring the all-important goal.

Argentina have now been World Cup runners-up four times (also in 1930, 1990 and 2014), the joint-most of any nation alongside West Germany/Germany, and they became the first team to not attempt a single shot in regulation time of a World Cup final.
But Manchester United defender Martinez says the time has come for Lionel Scaloni's side to put that defeat behind them, as they prepare to say goodbye to a legend.
Having announced his decision to retire from international football following the World Cup, Messi will make a farewell appearance at a friendly against Benin on October 5.

Bolivia and Burkina Faso will be Argentina's opponents before that match, which will see members of the 2022 World Cup-winning squad come together for a celebration of Messi's career at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.
"There's a lot of pain, preferably we don't remember it, but we must also highlight the tremendous effort we made throughout the tournament," Martinez told ESPN Argentina.
"Without a doubt, we had a great World Cup, but it hurts us all to have lost the final.
"Now we are here, back in our country, and we are going to enjoy ourselves."

Messi has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina, leading his country's all-time charts in both categories, with his last strike coming in their dramatic World Cup round-of-16 victory over Egypt this summer.
No player has directly contributed to more goals at the World Cup on record (since 1966) than Messi (33 – 21 goals and 12 assists), who has also featured in the most games at the finals (34).

Messi's 12 assists in the competition are also the most of any player, four more than the great Diego Maradona (eight), while only Kylian Mbappe (22 goals) has netted more often, though Messi was the first to surpass Miroslav Klose's previous record of 16 goals this year.

1x6wy3i0mkftp1abn66df9h20h.title: 'Liverpool will be happy' – Wirtz 'brimming with joy', says Klopp
1x6wy3i0mkftp1abn66df9h20h.subtitle: Florian Wirtz scored in Germany's 2-0 win over Serbia, and Jurgen Klopp believes those at his old club Liverpool will be delighted.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp reckons those involved at his former club, Liverpool, will be thrilled with Florian Wirtz's performances for Germany.
Wirtz scored in Germany's 2-0 win over Serbia in the Nations League on Thursday.
The playmaker also leads the way within Germany's squad for chances created (six) over this international break.
Wirtz has had a tough time of it at Liverpool since his mega-money switch from Bayer Leverkusen, and his performances this season have seen him come in for criticism.

However, the 23-year-old is the only player to rank in the top 10 in the Premier League this season for each of: High-intensity pressures in the opponent's half (181, joint-seventh), runs ahead of the ball (34, first) and defensive line-breaking passes (16, eighth).
And Klopp feels Wirtz hit his stride against Serbia.
"The way we want to play suits Flo Wirtz," Klopp said.
"I think everyone [at] Liverpool is very happy today. The boy is brimming with the joy of playing and has worked incredibly hard."
Germany were dominant, with Serbia managing just one shot, worth only 0.01 expected goals.
Klopp's team, meanwhile, accumulated chances worth 3.81 xG and had 32 shots.
Germany recorded 20 high turnovers, their most ever in a Nations League game and also more than in any match under Julian Nagelsmann.
They have allowed an average of just 8.7 opponent passes across their first three Nations League matches before a defensive action occurred. It is the lowest PPDA value of all teams in League A.
Asked what he enjoyed about the performance, Klopp said: "Everything! The opening stages, the middle part, the ending.
"The positioning in the box was incredible. To have that courage and know that we can allow ourselves to be cheeky and take risks if we win the ball back together.
"Everyone was there in our pressing moments. The last line defended really well by pushing up.

"Without the ball, it was outstanding, and with the ball, we played wonderful football. That has to be our baseline. Whether we can always manage that remains to be seen. This game will go into my archive. The next step in our development. We are learning. Learning under pressure."

1x7hu16c5gm981s0dwvjv1xjol.title: Spalletti relieved to see Juventus banish Sassuolo 'doubts' against Atalanta
1x7hu16c5gm981s0dwvjv1xjol.subtitle: Having seen their unbeaten Serie A start halted by Sassuolo on matchday four, Juventus bounced back with an impressive win over Atalanta.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti admitted Juventus' defeat to Sassuolo last week had created doubt in the Bianconeri's ranks, and he was delighted to see them banish that feeling by beating Atalanta.
Juve suffered their first defeat of the Serie A campaign on matchday four, conceding a stoppage-time winner to Vasilije Adzic in a 3-2 loss to Sassuolo.
However, they bounced back in style on Sunday with a 2-0 success against Atalanta and their former head coach Maurizio Sarri, with Francisco Conceicao and Bremer on target.

Juve have now won three of their first five games of a Serie A season while keeping a clean sheet in each victory for the first time since 2017-18, when they went on to win the Scudetto under Massimiliano Allegri.
And with a three-week international break now on the horizon, Spalletti was relieved to see his team cast aside the negativity of their previous Serie A outing.
He told Sky Sport Italia: "There was a moment when we were forced to defend, then we had to change something and, from there, we got back on track and played on an equal footing in the second half.
"We can certainly get better with the start of our actions and in the build-up. We could have hurt Atalanta more.
"But that's okay, also because the defeat against Sassuolo had created some doubts for us."

Spalletti also reserved particular praise for Randal Kolo Muani, whose performances he criticised last month, despite the Frenchman missing a big one-v-one chance with an expected goals (xG) value of 0.35 – the highest of any shot in the match.
"He had a really good game. I was disappointed when he popped up one-on-one with the goalkeeper because he deserved to score," Spalletti said of Kolo Muani.
"But he was still very happy at the end and we joked about it. We're all happy because now we can recover some of our strong players, who would have been useful to us recently."
While Juve are seventh in the table going into the break with 10 points on the board, Atalanta are four points worse off in 11th.
Sarri – a Scudetto winner in his only season in charge of Juventus in 2019-20 – has now lost nine Serie A matches against the Bianconeri, his joint-most against any club (also Roma).
Though La Dea have now lost three straight games, Sarri insists there is no crisis brewing in Bergamo.
"I don't think so, the first three games were a lower level of performance, but we have been improving," he said.
"This team needs to have more character, to light up that fire in its soul. This is a side with certain capabilities and we need to access them."

1x9zh2pp9s2l516nqef5vdzot0.title: Slegers concedes Arsenal are not in WSL title conversation
1x9zh2pp9s2l516nqef5vdzot0.subtitle: Arsenal are winless in their last four Women's Super League games, with a loss to Manchester City leaving them off the title pace.
paragraphs: Renee Slegers insists Arsenal are not in the conversation for the Women's Super League title race after a damaging 4-2 defeat to Manchester City.
Arsenal have made a stuttering start to the campaign, having been tipped as one of the favourites to challenge City for top spot before the season began.
Sunday's loss to City, who have a 100% record so far in the WSL in 2026-27, leaves Arsenal 10th in the table with just five points (W1 D2 L2), 10 behind the reigning champions.
The Gunners had twice led at the Etihad, through Lisa Baum and Alessia Russo, but Lauren Hemp, Kerstin Casparij and Khadija Shaw ensured the hosts snatched all three points.
One of Arsenal's biggest problems across all competitions has been their lack of goals, with only bottom club Charlton Athletic (two) netting fewer times than their four in the WSL.

Against City, Slegers' side had 16 shots, with their nine attempts on target matching the hosts' overall tally, and they won the expected goals (xG) battle 1.6 to 1.0, but they could not hold out for the win.
It comes after a disappointing outing in the Women's Champions League in midweek, too, when Arsenal threw away a 2-0 lead to draw with Paris FC last Wednesday.
And Slegers, who is under pressure after Arsenal's worst start to a WSL season since 2014, is determined to figure out what has gone wrong during the international break.
"It is a tough result," she told Sky Sports. "First half goes back and forth.

"Two teams that have momentum and create. Second half we start well, score a good goal. A lot changes when they make their three changes; they bring an energy, and one of the changes [Casprij] makes the goal.

"After that, it's more difficult. But it's quite an even game, two really good teams going against each other, but we didn't get the margins in the critical moments on our side. We can't concede four goals. We're not happy with that.
"After their changes, they became dominant.
"It's been a lot of games where we feel like we have it and then we don't. That's really pressing, demanding mentally.
"It's good the players go away, go to their national teams, get some new energy, change of environment, and they'll come back, and then we have the next game to prep for.
"There's a lot to review. How we've been doing things, from all aspects. Training programme, bigger things in the background. We're going to do everything we can to see where we can be better.
"At the moment we're not in the [title] conversation, no."
Arsenal will be looking to end their four-match windless streak in the WSL against Birmingham City when they return to domestic action on October 17.

1xcl7kve2hnpz1adp8wxyz1ro5.title: Philadelphia 'set the standard' in sixth straight win, says hat-trick hero Iloski
1xcl7kve2hnpz1adp8wxyz1ro5.subtitle: The MLS history books had some new names entering after Saturday's results, with Milan Iloski helping Philadelphia Union to another big win.
paragraphs: Hat-trick hero Milan Iloski was thrilled that the Philadelphia Union "set the standard" in their 4-2 victory over Orlando City SC in MLS on Saturday.

Philadelphia were missing some of their young United States stars, including Cavan Sullivan, but Iloski stepped up with a brilliant hat-trick in 51 minutes, with Indiana Vassilev also getting on the scoresheet.
The 27-year-old's first goal came from the penalty spot before Vassilev set up his other two on either side of getting on the scoresheet himself.
Orlando attempted a late fightback, with Ivan Angulo scoring their first goal in the 78th minute before Martin Ojeda netted their second in the 90th minute.
Philadelphia were dominant in their victory and moved up to sixth in the Eastern Conference after a sixth consecutive win that stretched their unbeaten streak to 12 games.
"A lot of hard work. We made sure we set that standard first," Iloski, who became only the third player in Philadelphia's history to score multiple hat-tricks in the same season, told Apple TV.
"Of course, scoring a hat-trick is great. But a lot of guys really stepped up and played really well.
"So, it is a full team effort, and we really showed our depth. It is a big performance for the team."

Philadelphia also entered the MLS record books thanks to their post-World Cup form, having racked up 32 points over their last 12 games, matching the Seattle Sounders for the most points in any 12-game span in league history.
The Sounders also came out on top, with a 3-1 victory over Minnesota United, moving them up to ninth in the Western Conference.
Jordan Morris, Hassani Dotson and Paul Arriola were all on target for Seattle, with the former's acrobatic 16th-minute finish making him the club's outright top scorer in the regular season (73).
It was also a historic win for Brian Schmetzer, who became the third-fastest head coach to reach 150 wins in MLS history (334 games, behind Bruce Arena and Bob Bradley).
And there was another landmark to celebrate, this time for Nashville SC's Hany Mukhtar, who scored his 100th MLS goal thanks to a first-half brace in their 2-0 win over Toronto FC.

He is just the 16th player in league history to reach a century, and the first German-born player to do so, while Nashville currently sit 14 points clear at the top of the East ahead of Inter Miami playing on Sunday.
Vancouver Whitecaps, meanwhile, remain top of the West despite a 3-3 draw with D.C. United, sitting three points clear of FC Dallas in second.
Dallas beat Los Angeles FC 1-0 to leapfrog their closest challengers, taking advantage of Houston Dynamo's 2-0 loss to Sporting Kansas City.

The Sounders also came out on top, with a 3-1 victory over Minnesota United, moving them up to ninth in the Western Conference.

Jordan Morris, Hassani Dotson and Paul Arriola were all on target for Seattle, with the former's acrobatic 16th-minute finish making him the club's outright top scorer in the regular season (73).

It was also a historic win for Brian Schmetzer, who became the third-fastest head coach to reach 150 wins in MLS history (334 games, behind Bruce Arena and Bob Bradley).

And there was another landmark to celebrate, this time for Nashville SC's Hany Mukhtar, who scored his 100th MLS goal thanks to a first-half brace in their 2-0 win over Toronto FC.

He is just the 16th player in league history to reach a century, and the first German-born player to do so, while Nashville currently sit 14 points clear at the top of the East ahead of Inter Miami playing on Sunday.

Vancouver Whitecaps, meanwhile, remain top of the West despite a 3-3 draw with D.C. United, sitting three points clear of FC Dallas in second.

Dallas beat Los Angeles FC 1-0 to leapfrog their closest challengers, taking advantage of Houston Dynamo's 2-0 loss to Sporting Kansas City.

2208B0258C566247C168DE0E73060A38.title: The FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 5’s Best XI includes Brobbey, Manzambi, Groß and Semenyo
2208B0258C566247C168DE0E73060A38.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 5’s Best XI includes Brobbey, Manzambi, Groß and SemenyoShareMatchday 5 of the Premier League season is done and dusted, with Manchester City establishing a three-point advantage at the top of the table courtesy of Arsenal’s defeat against Brighton.
It will be a sad time when Alisson finally leaves Liverpool, especially as he is still more than capable of producing excellent displays like the one against Bournemouth.

The Brazilian made two saves during the game, including an impressive effort to prevent Evanilson from opening the scoring in the first half – a shot worth 0.78 xGOT. That was his third Premier League clean sheet in a row.
The Barcelona loanee makes it into FotMob’s Team of the Week for the second time in three weeks thanks to another solid display.

Araújo wasn’t quite at his best in the final third, yet the right-back made five defensive contributions including two tackles, while also registering six recoveries throughout the game. He even won 86% of his aerial duels and played a massive part in Liverpool keeping that clean sheet for Alisson.
Everton kept their fifth clean sheet across seven matches in all competitions against Ipswich at the weekend and James Tarkowski played a big part in the 1-0 win.
The defender provided the assist for Everton’s only goal while also notching up 12 defensive contributions throughout the 90 minutes.

Seven of those were clearances, and Tarkowski was also a rock when it came to duels, winning 100% of his ground and 83% of his aerial duels in the contest. He was certainly more than deserving of his 8.5 rating.
Brentford’s 3-0 victory over Chelsea was arguably the result of Matchday 5 and Jannik Schuster was rock solid at the heart of the defence.

With 16, the Austrian centre-back registered the most defensive contributions in the game, and he even chipped in at the other end of the pitch, grabbing an assist and making three passes into the final third.
Aged just 20, Schuster could be the future of Brentford’s defence over the next few years.
Jay Dasilva’s thumping effort against Nottingham Forest gave Coventry their first Premier League win since 2001 and he fully deserves his spot in the Team of the Week.

The left-back was a menace on the left flank, succeeding with 100% of his dribble attempts while also making six passes into the final third. Frank Lampard will be expecting more of the same when domestic action returns next month.
Chema Andrés provided an assist on his Premier League debut last weekend, but he went one better against Arsenal, netting the third goal in Brighton’s victory against the champions.
It was a splendid performance by the midfielder who looked equally adept whether he was defending or trying to make things happen in the final third against the Gunners.
Five passes into the final third, nine defensive contributions, and winning five out of five aerial duels ensure he makes his FotMob Team of the Week debut.
Pascal Groß is ageing like a fine wine, isn’t he? The German midfielder covered the most ground against Arsenal (12.6 km), despite being the oldest player on the pitch.
He not only scored, but provided an assist during the contest, and also made eight passes into the final third.
Groß added five defensive contributions and was well deserving of making the Team of the Week for the second consecutive matchday.
🤯 Pascal Gross has won FotMob Man of the Match in ALL of Brighton’s last three games, averaging a rating of 8.8!He’s 35-years-old, by the way. pic.twitter.com/i2tV5QHRht
