          Liverpool vs Everton Prediction: WSL Preview
        
      
                          
                      Sep 27, 2026
          
                      Louise Bawden / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Can the Reds bounce back from a WSL defeat to the champions? We look ahead to Sunday's Merseyside derby at Anfield with our Liverpool vs Everton prediction and preview.

Anfield will welcome Gareth Taylor’s Liverpool with plenty of excitement and anticipation for Sunday's Merseyside derby with Everton on Sunday, particularly after they pushed champions Manchester City to the limit last weekend.
The Reds head into the derby with one win from their opening three Women's Super League games, but the results don’t tell the full story of their start to the new campaign.
There have already been encouraging signs of the more ambitious and attacking side Taylor is trying to build, with the biggest transformation coming in attack.

Liverpool have already scored seven times in the WSL this season, more than they managed across their opening 10 matches last term (six). Excluding the 2017 Spring Series, it is their best goal tally after three games of a WSL campaign.
Everton sit just above their neighbours after taking six points from their opening three matches, but the league table masks an extraordinary start in front of goal.
The Toffees have taken 41 shots and generated 2.9 xG, though they are yet to see one of their own players score this season.
Both of Everton’s victories have come courtesy of own goals, making them the first team in WSL history to win two matches 1-0 via an own goal in the same season.
Their victory over Charlton was particularly remarkable. Everton attempted 13 shots without registering a single effort on target, and yet they still walked away with the win.

Everton are only the second team in WSL history to score fewer than three goals across their opening three matches of a season and still collect as many as six points, after Sunderland in 2017-18. It is also the Toffees’ best points return at this stage of a campaign since 2022-23 (also W2 L1).
It creates a fascinating contrast at Anfield, with Liverpool's seven goals coming from 5.0 xG.

New signing Vivien Endemann has contributed to that. The Germany international became the first player in WSL history to both score and assist in two of her first three appearances in the competition. Only Khadija Shaw (5) can better her four goal involvements across the early weeks of 2026-27.
Endemann could join Caitlin Foord (6) and Alessia Russo (5) as the only players to register at least five goal involvements in their first four WSL appearances since 2020-21.

On top of improving Liverpool's attacking potency, Taylor’s influence can also be seen in the way Liverpool are trying to win the ball back higher up the pitch, with only Chelsea (56) and Arsenal (44) recording more high turnovers than Liverpool (39) in the WSL this season.
That approach was evident even in defeat to City, as Liverpool became the first team since Everton in November 2025 to record 15+ high turnovers against City in a WSL match.

For a side who struggled for goals last season, the early signs suggest Taylor has not simply added more attacking quality, but is building a team more capable of controlling games higher up the pitch.
Liverpool may have won the last Merseyside derby, but recent history at Anfield has belonged to Everton.
The Toffees have won each of their last five WSL games at Liverpool, their joint-longest winning run away to a single opponent in the competition (also Aston Villa).

Indeed, Liverpool have lost eight of their nine WSL matches at Anfield, with their only victory coming against Manchester United in March 2025. Five of those eight defeats have come at the hands of Everton.

The Reds can take confidence from the most recent meeting, though as they ran out 3-2 winners at Everton in March. They could now record consecutive WSL victories over their neighbours for the first time since winning three in a row across 2013 and 2014.

22CA79AD6DAFDF84DE8ABA6769AA4878.title: Greece could be the upstarts of this UEFA Nations League cycle
22CA79AD6DAFDF84DE8ABA6769AA4878.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesGreece could be the upstarts of this UEFA Nations League cycleShareWhisper it softly, but the Greek national team might just be finally waking up from its 12-year slumber.

After group-stage exits in their first two major tournaments – 1980 Euros and 1994 World Cup – third time proved the charm for Greece, who pulled off one of the greatest shocks in football history by defeating Portugal in the final of the 2004 Euros. They built on that by reaching the next two Euros and two of the next three World Cups, culminating in a Round of 16 penalty shootout defeat to Costa Rica in the 2014 World Cup. Since then, however, the Ethniki have been absent from every major tournament.

Euro 2004 papered over the cracks in their domestic game, caused by economic turmoil, systemic corruption, fan hooliganism, and structural mismanagement. Unlike many European leagues with balanced ownership models, Greek clubs are heavily privatized, and the power struggle over the Hellenic Football Federation (HFF) and refereeing appointments created an uneven playing field and eroded public trust. Scandals involving match-fixing, leaked audio tapes, and political interventions to rescue favoured clubs from relegation would turn domestic competitions into an arena of continuous controversy, alienating a generation of fans.

Greece’s financial crisis saw historic clubs like AEK Athens suffer relegation in order to clear massive debts, and it also saw the Greek league go from sixth in the UEFA coefficients in 2002/03 to an all-time low of 20th in 2020/21. Numerous lower-tier clubs left players unpaid for months, in addition to being without proper training facilities and basic infrastructure. And as the heroes of Portugal ‘04 retired, Greece struggled to find adequate replacements and finished bottom of their Euro 2016 qualifying group (including not one but two defeats to the Faroe Islands).

As it turned out, it was merely darkest before the dawn. With budgets slashed, Greek clubs pivoted from signing big-name veterans and focused on shoehorning teenage talents into the first team. Teams like PAOK overhauled their youth setup, hiring elite European coaching and sports science staff and constructing state-of-the-art training facilities. PAOK’s refurbished academy gave rise to future internationals like Christos Tzolis, Giannis Konstantelias, Konstantinos Koulierakis, and Stefanos Tzimas, all of whom are playing in Europe’s top five leagues. This youth investment has been mirrored throughout the nation, with the number of UEFA-licensed youth coaches nearly tripling from 665 in 2020 to 1,886 in 2023. Top-tier clubs have established an extensive network of 13 regional scouting centers across the country to provide room, board, and education for elite teenage players.

Christos Tzolis has started 4 games for Arsenal so far, and registered a goal involvement in every game! 🤯👏🏼4 assists and a goal, including 2 assists and a MOTM rating in the Community Shield today! 🏆He only cost £34 million… 🤯 pic.twitter.com/z87ZCgLtrx

After years of being defined by conservative, gritty tactics, Greece have shifted to a more modern, attack-minded style of play across all youth levels. They’re no longer focused on which players will be able to win the most U15 tournaments, but which players will be able to excel in a high-intensity, possession-based setup at the professional level several years down the line. They’re prioritizing individual creativity over immediate team results, with U6 players playing 2v2 in order to get as many touches as possible and fine-tune their dribbling, before moving up to 3v3, 5v5, 8v8, and only reaching 11v11 at U14 level. The HFF has ensured that these youngsters get early exposure by forcing third-tier clubs to field at least two U18 players in every single XI, as well as mandating at least one homegrown Under-21 player on the pitch at all times in the Greek Cup.

Slowly but surely, these seeds have started to bear fruit, with Olympiacos winning the 2023/24 UEFA Youth League (the same year that their first team won the Conference League). Greece earned promotion to League B in the UEFA Nations League but missed out on a spot in Euro 2024 following their penalty shootout defeat to Georgia, but they responded by earning promotion to League A. This season, however, there is a brand-new aroma to Greek football. After a summer that saw Konstantinos Tzolakis, Christos Mouzakitis, Tzolis, Konstantelias and Karetsas earn lucrative transfers, Greece’s squad is filled with players who are flourishing in Europe’s top five leagues.

This talent was on full display in Belgrade as Greece erased an early deficit and prevailed 2-1 against Serbia via late goals from Tzolis and substitute Anastasios Douvikas (the second-top scorer in Serie A last season). They did even better in their second Nations League match, winning 1-0 in Augsburg via a late goal from substitute Dimitris Kourbelis, the first time that Greece had beaten Germany in 11 attempts. Greece sit atop League A, and if they can continue their winning streak at home against the Netherlands and Germany, they will be all but guaranteed to qualify for the Nations League quarterfinals in March.
🇬🇷 That Greece front line is absolutely stacked with attacking talent. pic.twitter.com/lpgRCnuCwV

“It's exciting with all of these players going to these big, big leagues and big teams,” stated Hellas Footy host Stephen Kountourou. “It gives us hope that, if they play at a higher level, the national team can be elevated to a higher level, and they'll have that experience to then take us, finally, to a major tournament. A lot of people are saying ‘This is Greece's golden generation,’ but we can't start calling them a golden generation until they've actually reached a tournament. That's the aim: we're not expecting them to go and win the World Cup or Euros, but if they could start competing again in these major tournaments, I think that would be success for Greece. I don't see the success of this national team depending on what they win: if they can get there first, then we'll see what happens. It’s baby steps.”

It’s taken a while, but Greek football is thriving both in terms of domestic competitiveness and youth production. After winning 19 of 21 championships, Olympiacos have since won the title in four of the last nine seasons, with AEK Athens and PAOK laying claim to top honours. Whereas players like Vangelis Pavlidis used to have to leave home for Germany in order to receive a world-class football education, that’s no longer the case: elite talents like Charalampos Kostoulas and Christos Zafeiris are popping up wherever you look in Greece. And six years after ranking 20th, Super League Greece ranks 12th in the UEFA coefficient.

Greece have been here before: they kicked off their 2026 World Cup qualifying with a 5-1 demolition of Belarus before losing their next three and falling short of qualification. It’s one thing to start solid, but now, can they find some consistency and finally reemerge on the world’s biggest stage?

257387683964B2C1903D4A98BE49BBAA.title: Pochettino is bringing through the USA’s brightest crop of youngsters since Pulisic and co.
257387683964B2C1903D4A98BE49BBAA.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPochettino is bringing through the USA’s brightest crop of youngsters since Pulisic and co.ShareMauricio Pochettino has called up a youthful squad for the USA’s first fixtures since co-hosting the 2026 World Cup.

The hype around Cavan Sullivan has been intense for years. From the moment the American wonderkid joined Manchester City at the age of only 14, Sullivan has been built up as the USA’s greatest individual hope for the future. Now 16 years old, the future is now with Sullivan expected to make his national team debut in the current international break.

Picked by Mauricio Pochettino for the friendly matches against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada, Sullivan is part of a youthful contingent the US men’s national team head coach has turned to as part of his process to prepare his side for the 2030 World Cup. A new cycle signifies a fresh start for the USMNT.

Sullivan earned his call-up by catching the eye for the Philadelphia Union. The teenager is on a run of six goals in six games with only Lionel Messi more impactful as an individual difference-maker in Major League Soccer right now than Sullivan. The wonderkid is in wonderful form and could become the USMNT’s youngest debutant since Freddy Adu.

RBNY's Adri Mehmeti is another teenage talent called up by Pochettino for the first time. The 17-year-old is the sort of midfield pace-setter the USA have lacked for years, decades even. Physically, Mehmeti still has some growing to do, but the potential is clearly there for him to become a key figure for the national team.

Neil Pierre’s emergence for Philadelphia is timely for the USA considering their desperate need for defensive reinforcement. Tim Ream has been a reliable performer for the national team, but the former Fulham centre back is now 38. He will be into his 40s by the time of the 2030 World Cup.

Justin Ellis has broken through as a key figure for Orlando City this season with the Red Bulls’ Julian Hall yet another teenage talent who has made a profound impact in MLS recently. The number of young players using the league as a platform has been a big storyline of the 2026 season.

No fewer than 13 uncapped players have been called up by Pochettino for the September and October international window. Among them are a contingent of youngsters who appear ready for regular game time. Sullivan could be in this group. So too could Zavier Gozo who made the move to Crystal Palace from Real Salt Lake this summer.

There is also another contingent who might not be ready for prime time for a number of years. Prospects like Brooklyn Raines, Mathis Albert and Diego Kochen must use the experience of being involved in a USMNT camp to continue their development. Pochettino is firmly focused on the future.

Noahkai Banks might have been another young player called up. Pochettino courted the Augsburg defender only for Banks, who played for the USA at youth level, to file a one-time switch to represent Germany last week. Supporters reacted with disappointment, but Pochettino made clear that he wouldn’t dwell on Banks’ rejection.

“We want players who show commitment,” said Pochettino when asked about US Soccer’s recruitment of dual-nationals which will surely continue even after the failure to land Banks. “Commitment is not 50%, it’s 200%. It’s good, he was honest. We want players who want to commit and are desperate to play for the badge. That’s the most important thing.”

While the USMNT’s 2026 World Cup campaign ended abruptly with a heavy (and controversial) defeat to Belgium in the last 16, Pochettino established a tactical framework for the tournament that will give him a headstart now that he is at the start of a new cycle. A lot of the hard work has already been done.

Now, it’s about finding players who can execute his instructions at an even higher level. Pochettino is bringing through the most exciting crop of young American talent since Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Tyler Adams surfaced. He could elevate the USMNT’s level by integrating new players in a position or two.

The squad for the September and October international window is unashamedly experimental. Pulisic hasn’t been called up despite the fact he is the USA’s most reliable attacking difference-maker. Folarin Balogun has been given the time to settle back into life at Monaco after his failed deadline day transfer to Everton. McKennie is similarly out of this current squad.

Pochettino will call on these established stars again, but the next three weeks are about finding new players for the USMNT to build around. The road to the 2030 World Cup (via a possible Copa America, a Gold Cup and an Olympics) starts here. Sullivan and co. are ready to step up.

          Five Knee-Jerk Reactions to Premier League 2026-27 Matchday 5
        
      
                          
                      Sep 21, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We’re back with our weekly dose of knee-jerk reactions to the weekend’s Premier League action.
Every week here on Opta Analyst, we do something we don’t normally do and come to a load of conclusions based on just a single round of Premier League matches.
We usually rely on large data sets to make our judgements, but in this weekly column we react quickly and maybe a little too hastily.
It’s all a bit of fun, and many of our five reactions for this week will swiftly prove to be nothing more than exactly what we called them: knee-jerk.
But some might just hold up in the weeks to come. Read on to see which way you think these week’s conclusions will eventually go.

Coming into Matchday 5, it felt like there was no stopping Arsenal. They’d won all four Premier League games, as well as three more in other competitions, and few of their opponents had caused them any real problems at all.
Fabian Hürzeler’s side had produced some impressive results early in the season, but nobody expected them to blow Arsenal away quite like they did on Saturday.

They pressed the champions with a vicious and suffocating relentlessness that meant Arsenal just could not get any kind of grip on the game. Brighton forced a colossal 15 high turnovers (winning possession within 40 metres of the opposition's goal line), which is the second most by any team in the Premier League this season, behind only Brighton against an Aston Villa side who played most of that game with just 10 men (19).

They also recognised how difficult it is to carve out clear-cut chances against this Arsenal side, so shot on sight, often from distance. They scored twice from range to take Arsenal’s total to a league-high three goals conceded from outside the box this season.

Was this the blueprint for how to take the champions down, or a mere – and very natural – day off for the best team in the world right now? We’ll see if anyone else can do this to them after they’ve gathered their thoughts during the international break.
Some say you make your own luck, but there’s no denying that Spurs have been incredibly fortunate not to be relegated in the last two utterly dismal seasons.

In 2024-25, they were entirely reliant on the dreadful form of the promoted sides, who were so bad that there was never really a relegation battle of any sort. Then, last season, they escaped by the skin of their teeth after failing to address their myriad of problems in either transfer window.

Now, five games into 2026-27 and after a summer of upheaval, they are bottom of the table and staring at the very real possibility of another flirtation with the drop despite spending more than £300 million.

They have a lot of talent in their squad now, and certainly appear to have more potential, particularly in attack, than they did last term. Against Aston Villa on Saturday, they created more than enough, notably when the game was still level, to take control of the game, but failed to take their chances and were punished in brutal fashion. They won on xG but remain winless in actuality, with just two points from five games and a goal difference of -6.
It is now their worst ever start to a Premier League season and has left them with a lot of improving to do to avoid the possibility of another 17th-place finish – or worse.

We’ve learned over the last two years that nothing can be taken for granted with this club, and with no other team looking anything like as hopeless so far this season, there is every chance they get themselves into yet more trouble.
Brian Brobbey isn’t the most fashionable of footballers, and his physical approach to the game may mean he never gets the chance to play for a big-six club.

But even if he doesn’t play for a Champions League club that never lifts the ball off the floor and always has more than 60% possession, there is absolutely no denying what a handful he is. He deserves far more respect than many give him.

In Sunderland’s defeat to Manchester City this weekend, he scored three times from just five shots and became only the fourth player in Premier League history to score a hat-trick against the side starting the day top of the table, after Robbie Fowler vs Aston Villa in November 1998, Dirk Kuyt vs Manchester United in March 2011, and Romelu Lukaku vs United in May 2013.

He was extremely unfortunate to also end up on the losing side, too, becoming the sixth player ever to score a hat-trick and lose a Premier League game, and the first since Roque Santa Cruz for Blackburn vs Wigan in December 2007.

2ncvj5vcyw7n1ml6kanm08jnc.title: Klopp aiming to 'bring German football back to where we all want it to be'
2ncvj5vcyw7n1ml6kanm08jnc.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp is still rebuilding with Germany after just two games, and he will be keen to get his first win in charge against Serbia.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp says his focus remains on "bringing German football back to where we all want it to be" as he continues his search for a first win in charge.
Klopp's side have made a winless start to their Nations League campaign, drawing 1-1 with the Netherlands before they suffered a surprise 1-0 defeat to Greece.
No Germany head coach has ever failed to win each of their first three matches in charge.
Next up for Germany is a clash with Serbia, and Klopp will get the chance to see his second squad of players across the last two games of this international break.
"We will build a team that can cause problems for all teams," Klopp said.
"We're just getting started in this process. We are all interested in bringing German football back to where we all want it to be."
While Germany sit third in Group A2 with one point, Serbia prop up the table having lost their opening two matches against Greece and the Netherlands by 2-1 scorelines.
Serbia faced 51 shots across those two matches, and despite their recent struggles, Klopp is still confident they will provide a stern test for Germany.
"Serbia's approach won't be much different from what Greece did," Klopp said of their opponents.
"What makes Serbia particularly difficult to play against is their experience. They also have some excellent footballers. They know all the tricks of the trade, so we have to be prepared for that.
"They have a special mentality. It's not the best period in Serbian football at the moment, but the players themselves know what's at stake and have fought for one another.
"An opponent that sits deep is a major challenge for any team, at any stage of development."
While Klopp did not confirm who would act as captain in Joshua Kimmich's absence – with the 31-year-old only included in the first squad – he did disclose one starter.
Jonas Urbig will make his senior team debut on Thursday, and the goalkeeper is excited to get his first cap.
"I found out in training and was, of course, very happy," he said.
"It will be a very special moment for me."

2yffltvwa5kz1bc6i3oz1pawx.title: Sarr's move to Liverpool was 'never going to happen', says Parish
2yffltvwa5kz1bc6i3oz1pawx.subtitle: Ismaila Sarr was the subject of interest from Liverpool this summer, but the reported £50m bid fell way below Crystal Palace's valuation.
paragraphs: Crystal Palace chairman Steve Parish said Ismaila Sarr's proposed summer switch was "never going to happen" due to a huge gap in valuation of the Crystal Palace forward.
Sarr was linked with a late move to Liverpool in the transfer window, with the Reds aiming to strengthen the right side of their attack following Mohamed Salah's departure.
The Senegal international registered 22 goal involvements (21 goals, one assist) for Palace in all competitions last term, leading them to the Conference League title.
He has netted 33 goals and provided eight assists in 94 appearances across all competitions for Palace since joining them in 2024, earning him interest from Liverpool.
Sarr was reportedly the subject of a £50m bid from Andoni Iraola's side, a figure Parish said Palace did not consider remotely sufficient to sanction a departure to Anfield.
"It's unfortunate for Ismaila, but that wasn't really a situation that was of our doing," Parish told The Athletic.
"A club came in and, with the amount of money they bid, they couldn't seriously think in that market it was going to get done at that level.
"If you're selling players for £90m, and then you want to bid us half of that for the replacement, it's fine, you can do it. But it's never going to happen."
Liverpool's move for Sarr came after failing in their attempt to sign Brighton's Yankuba Minteh, while they also attempted to lure Yan Diomande and Ibrahim Mbaye to Anfield.
Sarr had also attracted interest from Turkiye earlier in the window, with Palace rejecting an offer reportedly worth around £26m from Galatasaray.

He had made a habit of scoring against Liverpool, too. Since the 2019-20 season, only Ollie Watkins and Erling Haaland (both eight) have netted more goals in all competitions against the Reds than Sarr (seven).
Palace remain in a strong negotiating position should Liverpool or another club renew their interest, given he has three years remaining on his current contract.
Sarr missed Palace's first four games of the 2026-27 campaign because of a groin injury, but has since returned for their win over Lech Poznan and draw with Leeds United.

338esj5f88ji1bkrzypb8hkcj.title: Greece 2-2 Netherlands: Reijnders rescues late draw in hard-fought comeback
338esj5f88ji1bkrzypb8hkcj.subtitle: Despite seeing two goals disallowed in the second half, the Netherlands snatched a point at the death against a dangerous Greece side.
paragraphs: Tijjani Reijnders scored an 89th-minute equaliser as the Netherlands came back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 with Greece.

After stunning Germany last time out, Greece looked set to make it three wins from three in the Nations League following first-half goals from Fotis Ioannidis and Giorgos Masouras, but Virgil van Dijk and Reijnders ensured the points would be shared at Stadio Toumbas.

Greece thought they were ahead inside the opening quarter of an hour when Christos Tzolis picked out the bottom-right corner, but the strike was ruled out as Vangelis Pavlidis obstructed Bart Verbruggen's view from an offside position.
Tzolis was soon forced off with an injury, but his replacement Masouras made an immediate impact in the 23rd minute as his flick-on allowed Ioannidis to run through on goal and curl past Verbruggen.

Ioannidis then returned the favour in first-half stoppage time, regaining possession after intercepting a blind back pass from Ruben van Bommel and squaring for Masouras to tap in from close range, though Greece's decision to sit on their lead after half-time proved costly.

Van Dijk halved the deficit for the visitors with a powerful header from Joey Veerman's floated corner in the 59th minute, while Denzel Dumfries saw a potential equaliser ruled out for offside soon afterwards.

The Real Madrid right-back would again be denied by the offside flag in the 73rd minute, moving beyond the final defender before turning home Van Dijk's knockdown, but there was no stopping Reijnders late on.

Gjivai Zechiel's acrobatic attempt from Noa Lang's cross was blocked by Konstantinos Mavropanos, but Reijnders was able to volley the rebound past Konstantinos Tzolakis from the edge of the six-yard box.
Greece made to pay for defensive mindset

Greece were brave on the ball in the first half and committed numbers forward on the counter, but Ivan Jovanovic's side offered almost no attacking threat in the second half; 0.93 of their 0.95 expected goals (xG) tally came in the opening 45 minutes.

Greece attempted two more shots than their opponents before half-time (seven to five), with the Netherlands attempting 13 more than Greece in the second half (14 to one); Greece's only shot after the break came in the 63rd minute and did not hit the target.
Credit must still go to the Netherlands, who did not give up their search for a point, despite seeing two goals narrowly disallowed against Dumfries after the break.
They have now scored late equalisers in two of their three Nations League games to remain unbeaten (W1 D2).

Greece can still take plenty of positives in knowing they are also unbeaten (W2 D1), sitting top of Group A2 and after causing plenty of trouble for both Germany and Netherlands so far in the competition.

          UEFA Women’s Champions League: Opta Supercomputer Matchday 1 Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the AI-powered Opta supercomputer, we provide our UEFA Women’s Champions League match predictions across Matchday 1 in 2026-27.

The Opta supercomputer will be with us every step of the way in the 2026-27 UEFA Women’s Champions League as the model works to provide you with data-backed predictions for all matches and season outcomes.

Matchday 1 kicks off on Tuesday 22 September with five games, including the reigning WSL champions Manchester City’s return to the UWCL after a one-year absence. Andrée Jeglertz's side will take on seven-time German Frauen-Bundesliga winners Bayern Munich away from home.
Four more matches follow on Wednesday, when the reigning European champions Barcelona host Paris FC, and eight-time UWCL winners OL Lyonnes travel to Swiss side Servette.
Below, Opta Analyst provides predictions for each game from MD1, powered by thousands of simulations from the Opta supercomputer.

The 2026-27 competition gets underway on Tuesday with two early 5.45pm kick-offs in Milan and Munich. The most eye-catching fixture of the two is between the reigning league champions in Germany and England, as Bayern Munich host Manchester City.

It is a daunting opening assignment for City. Bayern are ranked second in Opta's Power Rankings (95.9) and boast an enviable record on home soil in this competition. They went unbeaten across their five UWCL home matches last season (W4 D1) and have lost just one of their last 16 at home in Europe (W11 D4), a 2-0 defeat to Lyon in the quarter-finals of the 2024-25 campaign.

The supercomputer expects Bayern to make the most of that home advantage, with the German champions winning 52.4% of its 10,000 pre-match simulations. City, meanwhile, came out on top in 23.3%, underlining the size of the challenge awaiting them on their return to the competition.

The other early kick-off on Tuesday is between Inter and Häcken, with the home side making their UWCL debut in front of their own fans. While the Italians will be hoping to mark the occasion with a statement result, the Swedish club are slight favourites according to the supercomputer, winning 55.9% of simulations as they return to the competition for the first time since reaching the quarter-finals in 2023-24.
Arsenal, winners of the competition in 2024-25, begin their latest European campaign at home to HB Køge.

The Gunners have yet to fully hit their stride domestically, opening the WSL season with a 1-0 win at Brighton before being held by Crystal Palace and Manchester United at Emirates Stadium. Despite registering 47 shots across those two home matches, Arsenal scored just once, relying on a stoppage-time equaliser against United to extend their unbeaten run.

No English team have lost to Danish opposition in the UWCL since the north London club’s 5-1 defeat to Fortuna Hjørring in the 2002-03 semi-final (W7 D3 since), and the Opta supercomputer expects Arsenal to secure all three points in this one. Renée Slegers' side won 81.1% of its pre-match simulations – the highest percentage of any side playing on Tuesday night.

The supercomputer struggled to find a clear winner in its pre-game sims for Juventus vs Benfica, but the Portuguese club have the slight edge (39.9%). That's despite Juve beating Benfica 2-1 in last season’s league phase thanks to a brace from Cecilia Salvai.

Tuesday’s other clash is between Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain, with PSG looking to end a miserable eight-game winless streak in the UWCL (L6 D2) – their longest such run in the competition. The Opta supercomputer isn’t confident of them doing that though, as Madrid won 45.6% of its 10,000 pre-game sims.
Record UWCL champions, and last season’s losing finalists, OL Lyonnes make their 2026-27 bow on Wednesday night, travelling to Swiss club Servette in one of the early evening kick-offs.

It’s a daunting start for Servette, with Jonatan Giráldez's side unbeaten across their last 23 group/league stage games in the UEFA Women’s Champions League (W18 D5) since a 5-1 defeat to Arsenal in 2022-23.

Considering all of Lyon’s previous UWCL meetings with Swiss sides have ended in big wins (all vs Zürich: 8-0, 9-0, 3-0 and 4-0) it’s understandable that Lyon are given a 73.7% chance of victory on MD1 – the biggest chance of an away win across the two nights of action.
The Opta supercomputer also makes the away side favourites in the other early Wednesday fixture, with Roma travelling to Belgium to face OH Leuven.

The Italian side came out on top in 60.8% of the model's pre-match simulations, reflecting both their growing European pedigree and OH Leuven's struggles in last season's competition, where the Belgians won just one of their eight matches (D3 L4).

Attention then turns to Wednesday's later kick-offs, which feature two of the three highest-ranked teams in the women's Opta Power Rankings. Defending European champions Barcelona host Paris FC, while Chelsea welcome Austria Wien to The Cherry Red Records Stadium.

39cc0xssc61i10jsrfcqdfqjs.title: Ancelotti impressed by Brazil youngsters but Australia win marred by Raphinha injury
39cc0xssc61i10jsrfcqdfqjs.subtitle: Brazil earned their first victory since the World Cup on Tuesday, with several young players contributing to their 4-2 win over Australia.
paragraphs: Carlo Ancelotti said Brazil's young players were "seizing the moment" following Tuesday's 4-2 friendly win over Australia, though the game was marred by an injury to Raphinha.
The Selecao edged a six-goal thriller against the Socceroos at Suncorp Stadium, just four days on from a 1-1 draw between the sides in Townsville.

Vanderson's glorious third-minute volley put Brazil – who made seven changes to their starting line-up – in front, only for Alessandro Circati and Connor Metcalfe to strike for Australia in a five-minute spell and flip the match on its head.

Raphinha equalised from the penalty spot late in the first half before exiting the game at the interval, with what the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) described as "discomfort in his right thigh".
But the Selecao were superior after the restart as Bruno Guimaraes finished off a polished move and Vinicius Junior won and converted another penalty to secure the victory.

Ancelotti did not address Raphinha's withdrawal – which will be a major concern for Barcelona ahead of meetings with Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid later this month – in his post-match comments, instead focusing on the performances of his young players.

Twenty-year-old Cruzeiro goalkeeper Otavio won his first cap between the sticks, with Gabriel Bontempo also making his debut while Jair Cunha and Mauro Junior started for the first time at senior international level.
"It was a good game – we had difficulties, but we also showed good quality in our play," Ancelotti said. "We started well, then we lowered the pace of the game a little.
"But in the second half, I think the team reacted well, scoring a fantastic goal – the third – with a fantastic combination. We are happy.
"The best way is for the Selecao to perform well, to try to play a beautiful game and continue with this clear idea, with the progression of our youngsters.
"They are seizing this moment. I'm very clear with them: it's not a test. They're not here for me to see what they are like or what they can't do.
"They are very good and have to take advantage of this opportunity. We will monitor their progression.
"I repeat – I am very confident in these young players, and others will be involved in the next squad."
Sao Paulo midfielder Bontempo assisted Vanderson's opening goal and created the joint-most chances of any player, with two (level with Vinicius).
PSV full-back Mauro, meanwhile, led all Brazil players for duels contested (14), duels won (nine), tackles contested (five, two of which were successful) and aerial duels (seven).
Brazil face India in another friendly on Saturday, before taking on Japan and Singapore during the November international break.

Carlo Ancelotti said Brazil's young players were "seizing the moment" following Tuesday's 4-2 friendly win over Australia, though the game was marred by an injury to Raphinha.

The Selecao edged a six-goal thriller against the Socceroos at Suncorp Stadium, just four days on from a 1-1 draw between the sides in Townsville.

Vanderson's glorious third-minute volley put Brazil – who made seven changes to their starting line-up – in front, only for Alessandro Circati and Connor Metcalfe to strike for Australia in a five-minute spell and flip the match on its head.

Raphinha equalised from the penalty spot late in the first half before exiting the game at the interval, with what the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) described as "discomfort in his right thigh".

But the Selecao were superior after the restart as Bruno Guimaraes finished off a polished move and Vinicius Junior won and converted another penalty to secure the victory.

Ancelotti did not address Raphinha's withdrawal – which will be a major concern for Barcelona ahead of meetings with Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid later this month – in his post-match comments, instead focusing on the performances of his young players.

Twenty-year-old Cruzeiro goalkeeper Otavio won his first cap between the sticks, with Gabriel Bontempo also making his debut while Jair Cunha and Mauro Junior started for the first time at senior international level.

"It was a good game – we had difficulties, but we also showed good quality in our play," Ancelotti said. "We started well, then we lowered the pace of the game a little. 

"But in the second half, I think the team reacted well, scoring a fantastic goal – the third – with a fantastic combination. We are happy.

"The best way is for the Selecao to perform well, to try to play a beautiful game and continue with this clear idea, with the progression of our youngsters. 

"They are seizing this moment. I'm very clear with them: it's not a test. They're not here for me to see what they are like or what they can't do. 

"They are very good and have to take advantage of this opportunity. We will monitor their progression. 

"I repeat – I am very confident in these young players, and others will be involved in the next squad."

Sao Paulo midfielder Bontempo assisted Vanderson's opening goal and created the joint-most chances of any player, with two (level with Vinicius).

PSV full-back Mauro, meanwhile, led all Brazil players for duels contested (14), duels won (nine), tackles contested (five, two of which were successful) and aerial duels (seven).

Brazil face India in another friendly on Saturday, before taking on Japan and Singapore during the November international break.

3a3ixw4gjfhgz5rbo8v5473v.title: Argentina 4-0 Bolivia: Post-Messi era begins with emphatic victory
3a3ixw4gjfhgz5rbo8v5473v.subtitle: In their first game since Lionel Messi confirmed his international retirement, Argentina swatted aside Bolivia 4-0 in Cordoba.
paragraphs: Argentina hammered Bolivia 4-0 as they got the post-Lionel Messi era going in style at Estadio Mario Alberto Kempes.
Lautaro Martinez, Nico Paz, new captain Cristian Romero and Flaco Lopez were all on target for Lionel Scaloni's team on Wednesday.
The friendly in Cordoba marked Argentina's first match since the iconic Messi had announced his international retirement.
It was also Argentina's first game since their 1-0 defeat to Spain in the World Cup final.
Martinez's drilled finish got them going in the 19th minute, with Como star Paz then dinking home to make it 2-0.
Gianluca Prestianni hit the bar with a cross-shot before half-time, but Argentina got their third when Romero headed in from Paz's free-kick in the 54th minute.
Lopez then grabbed a maiden Argentina goal from the bench late on, just after he had seen a strike disallowed for offside.
There will be much tougher tests to come for Argentina in the wake of Messi's retirement and, technically, the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner is not done yet.
Argentina will give Messi a farewell when they take on Benin next week.
However, Scaloni's team were utterly dominant in this win. They conceded just three shots, none of which were on target, and had 18 attempts of their own.
Argentina's dominance is reflected by their expected goals tally of 2.24 compared to Bolivia's 0.11.
With Messi out of the picture, much of the attacking onus is going to fall on Martinez, Paz and Julian Alvarez.
Paz and Alcaraz had a team-leading three shots each, while Martinez led the way for touches in the opponent's box (seven).

Playmaker Paz also crafted three chances, which was the joint-most for Argentina, along with Franco Mastantuono, another youngster who will be looking to help fill the void left by one of the best to grace the game.

3jnohid0gubi1ibj9w14pv78y.title: Spain extend De la Fuente's contract through to Euro 2032
3jnohid0gubi1ibj9w14pv78y.subtitle: After he led Spain to European and world titles, Luis de la Fuente's future is secured for another six years.
paragraphs: Luis de la Fuente will stay on as Spain's head coach through to 2032, after the Spanish Football Federation extended his contract.

De la Fuente took over in December 2022 following Luis Enrique's resignation in the wake of Spain's disappointing showing at the World Cup in Qatar, and he has enjoyed huge success in his first four years.

The 65-year-old, who spent nine years with Spain's youth teams before taking over the senior team, led them to the 2022-23 Nations League title, as well as triumphs at Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup.
La Roja beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time in the World Cup final in July to secure their second title.
De la Fuente's current deal was due to run until the end of Euro 2028, but he will now remain in his post for an additional four years, which includes a World Cup title defence as co-hosts in 2030.
"We are seeking a project of stability and confidence," RFEF president Rafael Louzan said.
"This proposal is based on confidence in Luis de la Fuente and the sporting project he leads, for a multi-year cycle of competitions and major tournaments.
"We are talking about the most decorated coach in the history of the national team, and after fourteen years with us, Luis de la Fuente deserves a long future at the RFEF."
Spain are unbeaten in their last 38 matches in all competitions, the longest-ever run by any European or South American team in history.
At this summer's World Cup, they lifted the trophy having conceded just one goal in their eight games, the fewest goals conceded by any team in a World Cup-winning campaign.
In total, De la Fuente has taken charge of 49 matches across all competitions, winning 37 of those (D10 L2). His team have scored 126 goals during that time and conceded just 35.
He will now look to reach another Nations League final – having also done so in 2024-25 before losing to Portugal on penalties.
Spain begin their new campaign away to England on September 26, with a double header against Croatia to come on either side of hosting Czechia.

          England vs Czechia Prediction: UEFA Nations League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 6, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Tuesday's UEFA Nations League matchup with our England vs Czechia prediction and preview, as Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions look to make it three straight wins.
England hit a magnificent seven against Croatia on Saturday, making it back-to-back wins in their UEFA Nations League campaign in some style.
Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored twice each, while Jude Bellingham was also on target and laid on three assists. Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers also scored in an emphatic victory.
Thomas Tuchel's side have scored 11 goals in the three games across this extended international window, with one more match to come as Czechia visit Wembley on Tuesday.
England beat Czechia 2-0 in Prague last week, with Gordon and Kane scoring, and the Three Lions should be confident of another victory in this encounter.
It was a routine win for England, aided by Pavel Sulc's red card midway through the first half.
Tuchel has plenty of positives to take from the past couple of weeks, particularly in attack.

Across their last four games in all competitions, England have won 6-4 against France and 7-0 against Croatia. It's the first time they've scored 6+ goals in two different games in a calendar year since 2019, while they last did so in three different games in 1908.
Gordon has scored in each of his last four England appearances. The last player, other than Kane, to score in five in a row for the Three Lions was Wayne Rooney between October 2014 and March 2015.

The Barcelona winger has actually netted two headed goals in his last two England appearances. Those goals seem to have even come as a surprise to him, with the former Newcastle player joking, “I’m probably the worst header of the ball you will ever see” after nodding in his first against Czechia last week. Across 248 total club appearances, he has not scored a single header.
Other than Kane, Gordon is the only player to be directly involved in a goal in five consecutive England appearances across the last 10 years (four goals, two assists).

Against Croatia, Saka scored two right-footed goals in a match for the first time in his senior career for club and country (378 appearances). Bellingham, meanwhile, was directly involved in more than two goals in an England game for the first time. He is the first player to record three assists in a game for England since Trent Alexander-Arnold against San Marino in November 2021.

The captain is set to equal a record in this match. If he features, he will make his 125th England appearance, which will see him equal Peter Shilton as the all-time most-capped player in the Three Lions' history.
With his double last time out, Kane became the first player to score 10+ goals in three different calendar years for England: 11 in 2026, 16 in 2021 and 12 in 2019.
Kane has netted 89 goals across his 124 caps to date, and a flurry here could take him even closer to the century before 2026 is up.
They sit bottom of the group after losing their opening three games, going down 2-1 to Croatia and 3-1 to Spain, either side of that defeat to England.
Santi Denia has lost all three of his games in charge of Czechia, and could be the second manager to lose their first four matches with the nation after Václav Ježek in 1973, then as Czechoslovakia.
In fact, Czechia have lost five of their last six games in all competitions (D1), including each of the last four in a row. They last lost five consecutively between July 1972 and March 1973.

Czechia's recent poor form is not the only thing going against them heading into this match. They have lost six of their eight competitive meetings with England (W2), though they have always responded to back-to-back losses with a win, and have lost their last two.
England are also unbeaten in all eight of their games against Czechia at Wembley (W6 D2). In the most recent of those, the Three Lions finished their Euro 2020 group-stage campaign with a 1-0 win.

4187436E1239850926CE3036282E6B20.title: James Trafford’s inclusion hints at how Thomas Tuchel wants to evolve England’s style
4187436E1239850926CE3036282E6B20.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesJames Trafford’s inclusion hints at how Thomas Tuchel wants to evolve England’s styleShareJames Trafford has been given an opportunity to prove himself as England’s first-choice goalkeeper of the future.

Had it not been for James Trafford, Spain might have been out of sight before England could even threaten a comeback from 1-0 down in their UEFA Nations League opener on Saturday. The 23-year-old’s stop to deny Ferran Torres from doubling the world champions’ lead after only 16 minutes was particularly important.

That Trafford was handed the start by Thomas Tuchel in the first place surprised many. While it was expected that the England manager would experiment with a handful of different options due to injury and a willingness to broaden horizons after the World Cup, few had predicted a change of goalkeeper.

And yet Tuchel’s selection of Trafford to face Spain hinted at an evolution of England’s playing style. Jordan Pickford might be something of an icon for the Three Lions, earning 91 caps over nine years, but he has never been the most adept with his feet. This is where Trafford offers something different.

It hasn’t been easy for Trafford to get to this point in his career. He had to leave Manchester City to gain first team experience, which he received over two seasons at Burnley. When Trafford returned to City last year, it was on the promise that he would be first-choice at the Etihad Stadium. A shaky start to the season, however, pushed Manchester City into the market for Gianluigi Donnarumma.

A lesser goalkeeper, and a meeker character, might have shied away from taking on another challenge after such a disappointment, but Trafford has shone for Leeds United this season, joining the Elland Road club for a reported £40m this summer. Tuchel clearly likes what he sees in the 23-year-old, and there’s a lot to admire.

Trafford’s save percentage of 87% is the highest of any goalkeeper in the Premier League this season with only Emi Martínez averaging more saves per 90 minutes. The 23-year-old has been a big part of Leeds’ early-season success with Daniel Farke’s team flying high in fifth place. Some have speculated they could contend for European qualification.

A strong start to the season has seemingly pushed Trafford more firmly into Tuchel’s thoughts. While Trafford was part of England’s World Cup squad, there was never any realistic chance of Pickford losing his place. He’s been a key part of the national team for the majority of the past decade.

At the World Cup, though, Pickford wasn’t at his best. He might have done better in certain moments. Some fans still argue he should have saved Enzo Fernández’s goal for Argentina in the semi-final. Jude Bellingham seemed to make this point as he mouthed to Pickford “It’s [in] the middle of the goal” in the immediate aftermath.

Pickford also let in a shot at the near post against DR Congo. Even when the Everton goalkeeper kept the ball out of his net, he contributed to the defensive nervousness that characterised many of England’s performances at this summer’s World Cup. Pickford wasn’t immune from criticism.

For the first time in a number of years, the opportunity is there for someone else to grab the starting jersey and Trafford made the most of his chance against Spain, even if the match ended in defeat for England. Tuchel is expected to stick with Trafford for Tuesday’s follow-up match against Czechia.

🧤 Konstantinos Tzolakis is the only goalkeeper who has a higher rating than James Trafford in the Premier League this season! James Trafford is STARTING for England tonight, displacing the regular Jordan Pickford… who’s third in the ratings! 👀 pic.twitter.com/mT1ZD0CmGl

“We use the Nations League to see where we are with the other goalkeepers,” said Tuchel when asked to explain why he decided to start Trafford and bench Pickford with Jason Steele another option. “There was no reason from performances to open up this position for competition.

“I think it’s necessary with every other player that we are aware of ‘what if’. If a player that starts a season well, like Traff at Leeds, [he] has the chance to prove it and to play in our style. We just need to see it at some point. We use this competition to actually give him the chance to push on.”

Trafford wasn’t the only experimental selection for the match against Spain. Jarell Quansah started at right back while Myles Lewis-Skelly was deployed in central midfield. Both players demonstrated why they should be taken seriously as important figures for the future. Lewis-Skelly in particular who was missed when he was withdrawn after 70 minutes.

Further opportunities will be given to other young players between now and Euro 2028 and the 2030 World Cup beyond that. It is, however, difficult to envisage another goalkeeper emerging with a stronger case than Trafford’s to be England’s next number one, although Dean Henderson might have something to say about that.

Tuchel bore the brunt of the criticism for England’s World Cup failure. The German still hasn’t fully accepted culpability for what went wrong in the semi-final against Argentina, but his team selection in the loss to Spain at least demonstrated a willingness to try something different.

          Liverpool's Evolution: From Survival Mode to WSL Top-Four Contenders
        
      
                          
                      Sep 24, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Are Liverpool genuine top-four contenders in the WSL? We look at the transformation behind their impressive start, the performance that almost earned them a result against Man City, and how their players are helping to drive renewed hope.
Just four months ago, the idea of Liverpool challenging for a UEFA Women's Champions League place would have seemed improbable.
The Reds finished 11th in the Women's Super League in 2025-26, ending the season eight points clear of bottom-placed Leicester City but recording their second-lowest finish in the competition.
Their 2025-26 campaign began in disastrous fashion under the former Manchester City boss Gareth Taylor, as the Reds failed to win any of their opening 12 league matches (D4 L8).
A six-game losing streak at the start of the season set the tone, including an opening weekend loss to rivals Everton at Anfield (4-1) followed by a shock defeat at Leicester City on MD2.
Liverpool found themselves rooted to the foot of the table across the winter break with just three points collected, and facing serious questions about their future direction.
Their struggles continued into the start of 2026 as Liverpool's winless league run reached 15 matches, the longest in their WSL history.
Yet, even amid the poor results, there were signs they could compete.

During that difficult run, Liverpool lost to both Arsenal and Man City by just a single-goal margin, with both winning goals coming in the final four minutes. It was enough to suggest that the gap to the league's elite was not quite as wide as the table implied.
There were also off-field circumstances surrounding the club that cannot be ignored when looking back at Liverpool's 2025-26 WSL campaign.

The passing of former manager Matt Beard in September 2025 cast a shadow over the season. Beard was one of the most influential figures in the club's history, overseeing 106 WSL matches across two spells and guiding them to back-to-back league titles in 2013 and 2014. Against that backdrop, Liverpool's struggles became easier to contextualise.
Taylor’s first WSL victory with the Reds came at home against Tottenham in January, and while Liverpool won only three more league matches across the campaign, it proved enough to secure survival.
Now, less than a year later, the picture looks very different.

Liverpool began 2026-27 with a convincing 4-0 victory over Charlton Athletic, their first win in a season opener since 2023. The four-goal margin was also their biggest in a WSL match since a 4-0 victory over Leicester in May 2024.

They followed that with a 1-1 draw against Tottenham on MD2, a result that arguably failed to reflect the balance of play, before pushing Man City all the way on MD3. An unfortunate 89th-minute own goal by Grace Fisk ultimately denied Liverpool what would have been their first point against City since May 2023.

Results alone, however, only tell part of the story. The underlying numbers point to a Liverpool side that are playing with greater ambition than we saw for much of last season. They are pressing higher, spending more time in possession, and showing a greater willingness to take the game to their opponents rather than simply react to them.

Of course, there are still areas to improve, but the early season data suggests a meaningful shift in Liverpool’s approach. A side that spent much of last season battling at the bottom end of the table are showing signs of being better equipped to compete with the division’s leading teams.
So, can Liverpool turn that promising start into a genuine push for a top-four finish?
They may have left Manchester empty-handed on Friday night, but Liverpool's performance arguably told a more encouraging story than the result itself.

Too often in recent seasons have meetings with the WSL's elite been exercises in damage limitation. Liverpool's approach at the Joie Stadium was markedly different. They pressed aggressively, played through City's pressure and repeatedly forced the hosts into uncomfortable situations.

480kzgt5dqwq1euhyhwf837zn.title: Greenwood: Man City there to win in Champions League
480kzgt5dqwq1euhyhwf837zn.subtitle: Manchester City return to the Women's Champions League after a season-long absence, and Alex Greenwood is eyeing a deep run.
paragraphs: Alex Greenwood says Manchester City are "going to give it absolutely everything" to try and win the Women's Champions League this season.
City were absent from last season's campaign, but they are back in the competition following their Women's Super League title success in 2025-26.
Andree Jeglertz enjoyed a stellar first season with the team, and they have started their title defence in equally fine form, having won all three of their league games so far.
But their attention now turns to the Champions League, and they will begin their campaign away to Bayern Munich on Tuesday.

City are given the fourth-highest chance of winning the Champions League by the Opta supercomputer, though their 9.1% win probability is significantly lower than outright favourites Barcelona (41.2%).
Greenwood insists City have their eyes on the trophy, though.
"To qualify was massively important; it's an expectation that we have at this football club," Greenwood told UEFA's website.
"But every competition that we play in, we're there to win.

"We know it's going to be a challenge, but it's fantastic for the club. We're going to give it absolutely everything, like we do in every other competition, take it game by game and see how far we can go."
City are facing a German side for the first time in the Champions League.

Bayern, meanwhile, have won seven of their previous 11 matches against English teams in the competition (L4), including both legs of last season's quarter-final against Manchester United (3-2 A, 2-1 H).
On their last Champions League appearance in 2024-25, City lost their last two away games, both by a 3-0 scoreline to Barcelona and Chelsea, respectively.
"I've played in this competition enough times to know what it presents and what the challenges are," Greenwood added.
"We worked really hard to get back in this competition where I think we belong. I'm just excited to embrace the challenge.
"Champions League, Women's Super League, whatever competition we're in, we're in it with a real elite mindset to go and win, and that's been our mentality for the last 18 months."

          Tottenham vs London City Lionesses Prediction: WSL Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 3, 2026
          
                      Louise Beltrame-Bawden / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Sunday afternoon’s London derby with our Tottenham vs London City Lionesses prediction and preview, as Spurs look to cement second place in WSL table.

Since the start of April, only Chelsea (2.7) and Manchester City (2.6) have averaged more points per game in the Women's Super League than Tottenham Hotspur (2.4) and London City Lionesses (2.1). With two of the division's current top four sides going head-to-head, Sunday's clash promises to be one of the standout fixtures of the weekend.

Tottenham have emerged as one of the surprise packages of the new season, but their impressive start under Martin Ho is increasingly looking like something much more significant than simply a strong opening to the campaign.

Spurs have carried their momentum from last campaign into 2026-27, establishing themselves among the league's best in its early stages. Wins against West Ham (3-1), Crystal Palace (7-0) and Aston Villa (4-0) as well as a respectable draw at Liverpool (1-1) have them in second place.

Not only have Tottenham collected their second best points total (10) at this stage of a WSL season, but Ho has added real quality to his squad, and the transformation is evident in how his side are playing.

Each of the four longest passing sequences leading to goals in the WSL this season have belonged to Spurs. They are the only side to score following a sequence of 10 or more passes, and lead the competition for goals from build-up attacks (4), while only Manchester City (23) have produced more build-up attacks than Tottenham’s 22.
That control is translating into extraordinary attacking dominance.

Tottenham have attempted 77 shots while accumulating an expected goals (xG) of 9.3 , becoming the first team in WSL history to register 35 or more shots in consecutive games – 42 against Crystal Palace and another 35 against Aston Villa.
At the heart of that attacking transformation is a squad combining proven WSL quality with exciting young talent.

Victoria Pelova is the joint-leading scorer in the WSL this season after hitting braces in each of Tottenham’s last two matches. Another double against London City would make her just the fifth player to score multiple goals in three consecutive WSL appearances, and the first since Rachel Daly in May 2023.

Alongside her, 21-year-old Signe Gaupset has made her presence felt. Against Aston Villa on MD4, the Norwegian became the youngest player in WSL history to create eight chances from open play in a single match. She leads the competition this season for both chances created (18) and assists (three).

So this isn’t simply a Tottenham side getting results. Ho has built a team capable of controlling possession, constructing attacks patiently and overwhelming opponents, and the early evidence suggests Spurs are becoming an increasingly serious force in the WSL.
London City Lionesses have lived up to much of the early hype following another ambitious summer transfer window that brought a host of established stars to the club.
But if their ambition is to challenge the WSL’s leading sides and compete for Champions League qualification, these are the games in which they will want to make a statement.

They arrive at the BetWright Stadium with momentum after a 2-0 victory over Brighton on MD4, a  result delivered their first clean sheet in 14 league matches, although they have only once previously recorded successive WSL shutouts, against Liverpool and West Ham in October 2025.
There was also a significant moment at the other end of the pitch, with former Ballon d'or winner Alexia Putellas scoring her first goal for the Bromley-based side.
The Spaniard’s strike ended her longest top-flight goal drought since 2017, having gone seven league appearances without scoring.
And history suggests that when Putellas finds the net, her team usually wins: she has finished on the winning side in 129 of the last 130 league matches in which she has scored.
Putellas (19) also leads her London City teammates for attacking sequence involvements in the WSL this term, though Daniëlle van de Donk (18) and Grace Geyoro (17)  follow close behind.
With London City’s star names beginning to make their mark, Sunday represents another important test of just how quickly this ambitious team can establish itself among the WSL’s leading sides.

4ap1n1mxoqqa13sntb2jdzqjl.title: Zidane backs Dembele to lead France in Mbappe's absence
4ap1n1mxoqqa13sntb2jdzqjl.subtitle: Ousmane Dembele is set to captain France for their Nations League clash with Belgium, something Zinedine Zidane has full confidence in.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane is confident Ousmane Dembele can step up and be France's captain after Kylian Mbappe withdrew from the squad due to injury.
Dembele took the armband during France's 1-0 win over Turkiye in their Nations League opener, with Mbappe forced off after scoring the only goal in the 54th minute.
It has since been confirmed that the Real Madrid star suffered a hyperextension in his left knee, though the severity of the issue has not been disclosed at this time.

Mbappe will prove to be a big miss, not only for his leadership, but also for his quality on the pitch. He netted his 12th goal for France in 2026 last time out, equalling the highest total for a French player in a calendar year in the 21st century, set by himself in 2022.
Dembele also played his part at Turka Arac Muayene Kocaeli Stadyumu, finishing with team-high totals for chances created (four) and touches in the opposition box (seven).
"He is already doing it. He's vice-captain; he has that role, even when he's not captain," Zidane told reporters about what Dembele brings to the team as a captain.
"He is, he's a good guy, always there for others, and you have to take his experience. I expect something from everyone, not just the captains. It's a group that lives well.
"We've been together for a week; I can see that they're happy to be together. It's the French team; there are some great matches. Football goes so fast.
"I'm 54 years old; I'm here. I can't play any more, so I tell them to enjoy the moment, because it's flying. The French team is so beautiful that I want them to live these moments."
Zidane became the first coach to win his first match in charge of France since Aime Jacquet against Italy in 1994 (four draws and one loss in between).
The former Madrid boss said it was an emotional feeling to lead his country for the very first time, though he said there was still plenty to improve on for his team.
He revealed ahead of their trip to the Stade Roi Baudouin on Monday that he would be making several changes to his team given the tight turnaround.
France are second in Group A1 but level on points with Belgium after they beat Italy in their opening match.

It was put to Zidane whether the result or the performance was more important against Mark van Bommel's side, and he said: "Everything is important, but the most important thing is to get to know each other.

"We rested more, and we thought more about getting treatment than training because we don't have time. The idea is to prepare for the matches and afterwards, of course, to win the match. We are competitors, and what we want to do is win the match, above all.
"We have to improve; we will improve. But the idea is to get the ball back as quickly as possible and, above all, to have the ball, to run with the ball and not without the ball."

4d435n3bkqfu1iiva8cbi2pvv.title: Jesus to reveal reason for Ronaldo's Portugal exit after international break
4d435n3bkqfu1iiva8cbi2pvv.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo abruptly left Portugal's Nations League camp, but Jorge Jesus is not willing to discuss his row with the forward just yet.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus says he will explain the reasons behind Cristiano Ronaldo's departure from the Portugal squad after the final match of this international break.
Ronaldo abruptly left the Portugal camp ahead of their Nations League meeting with Denmark, after widespread reports suggested tensions had been building since their previous win over Norway.
The 41-year-old was an unused substitute as Portugal ran out 2-1 winners on Sunday, with Joao Felix and Goncalo Ramos both getting on the scoresheet.
After the victory, Jesus said it was a "tactical choice" to leave Ronaldo on the bench, with Norway dominating most of the proceedings despite losing.

The Portugal captain trained away from his team-mates on Monday and Tuesday, with media reports suggesting there was a "crisis" meeting being held between Ronaldo, Jesus and Portugal Football Federation (FPF) president Pedro Proenca to clear the air.
Jesus insisted he would not "hide or run away" from the topic, but he was not willing to discuss the matter in depth ahead of Thursday's match with Denmark.
"I will explain everything after the last game," said Jesus in his pre-match interview.
"I have spent many years in football and I know that I did nothing that should have caused things to go differently.
"After the Norway game [this coming Sunday], we will talk about this subject. I will not hide or run away from it.
"Nobody can take away what Cristiano represents. He’s an icon and that’s not in question."
Portugal's final match of this international break comes at home against Norway on October 4.

4llpo7fpmdgo1rppajl8yz96p.title: The Numbers Game: England bid to equal away-day record against old foes Croatia
4llpo7fpmdgo1rppajl8yz96p.subtitle: England head to Croatia for their third game in the Nations League on Saturday, with both teams having three points on the board.
paragraphs: England and Croatia have become very familiar foes in recent years.

Luka Modric and company were responsible for the first heartbreaking tournament defeat of the Gareth Southgate era in 2018, with Ivan Perisic and Mario Mandzukic scoring to cancel out Kieran Trippier's memorable free-kick.
Since then, the Three Lions have started two tournaments – Euro 2020 and the 2026 World Cup – with victories over Croatia, and Saturday's reunion in Rijeka may be pivotal for both teams.
Having both beaten Czechia and lost to Spain in their opening two games in Nations League Group A3, their head-to-head clashes could decide who progresses to the last eight next March.
But who will come out on top this weekend? Here, we preview the game using Opta insights.
What's expected?
The Opta supercomputer is siding with England ahead of this game, albeit not decisively.
Across 10,000 pre-match simulations run by the Opta model, the Three Lions triumphed in 48.6% of scenarios, with Croatia winning 27.4% and the remaining 24% of simulations finishing level.
And if you look past that 2018 semi-final defeat, an England win would continue a theme of dominance in recent head-to-head meetings with Croatia.
Since that game in Moscow, Croatia are winless in all four of their meetings with the Three Lions (D1 L3), including two Nations League fixtures in 2018 (0-0 home, 1-2 away).
In fact, England have won five of their last seven matches against Croatia in all competitions (D1 L1), dating back to a 3-2 defeat in 2007, which cost them qualification for Euro 2008.
The Three Lions have scored at least four goals in three of those wins, triumphing 4-1 in September 2008, 5-1 in September 2009 and 4-2 at the World Cup this June.
Croatia facing historic low
Following nine years under Zlatko Dalic, Slaven Bilic made a winning return to the Croatia job against Czechia last weekend, with Modric and Marco Pasalic scoring in a 2-1 away win.
But they were then blown away by Spain in Seville on Tuesday, losing 4-1 after briefly getting back on level terms in the first half, via Dion Beljo's first international goal.
Croatia could have no complaints about their margin of defeat, having only attempted five shots to Spain's 16 and put up 0.47 expected goals (xG) to their opponents' 1.81.
They have only produced a lower xG figure in three previous Nations League fixtures – versus France in March 2025 (0.18), Sweden in November 2020 (0.3) and England in October 2018 (0.42).
After that reality check, Croatia have now lost five of their 10 matches overall in 2026 (W5).
It is only the third time they have suffered that many defeats in a single calendar year (also 2018 and 2020), though they have never previously lost six in one year.

They will hope a return to home soil at Stadion HNK in Rijeka provides some comfort, having won eight of their last nine competitive home matches (D1) since a 1-0 loss to Turkiye in a Euro 2024 qualifier back in October 2023.
However, despite Croatia only losing four of their last 41 competitive games at home, three of those losses have been in the Nations League, against France and Portugal in 2020 and Austria in 2022.
Will Tuchel experiment with away-day record in sight?
Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane were on target on Tuesday as England, helped by a first-half red card for Czechia midfielder Pavel Sulc, emerged as 2-0 victors in Prague.

That win was England's sixth in their last eight Nations League matches (L2) across the top two tiers, having scored 20 goals in that span. That is more victories and goals than they managed in their first 18 games in the competition overall (W5 D6 L7, 18 goals).
It was also England's eighth straight away win in all competitions, giving them an opportunity to match an all-time team record this weekend.
Only once have they ever won nine away games in a row, doing so under World Cup-winning manager Alf Ramsey between December 1965 and October 1967.

It will be intriguing to see how Tuchel approaches his team choice for this game, after he handed Trent Alexander-Arnold his first England start since October 2024 – in a Nations League win over Finland under Lee Carsley – at right-back.
Alexander-Arnold teed up Gordon's opening goal with a trademark delivery to the far post, which was also his first assist in international football since that Finland game two years ago.

Tuchel had gone with the more conservative option of Jarell Quansah on the right side of defence against Spain, but with Alexander-Arnold ranking second among England players for chances created (three, behind Gordon with four) and passes into the final third (32, behind Elliot Anderson with 40), might the England boss favour his creativity from deep areas?

He also has options in midfield after handing Myles Lewis-Skelly back-to-back starts in the absence of his Arsenal club-mate Declan Rice, with Alex Scott winning his first senior cap in Prague and Morgan Gibbs-White making another lively cameo appearance.
PLAYERS TO WATCH
Czechia – Ivan Perisic
Perisic, who provided a goal and an assist against England the 2018 World Cup semi-finals, has started both of Croatia's games during this international break.
The 37-year-old has 15 goal involvements in his last 18 starts for Croatia, netting six times and registering nine assists.
Kane – who smacked a penalty off the crossbar after losing his footing in England's loss to Spain – has enjoyed playing on the road lately.
The England captain has found the net in each of his last five away internationals.

He could now become just the fourth player to score in six consecutive away games for the Three Lions, after James Windridge (six from March to June 1908), Tom Finney (seven from September 1946 to May 1948) and Stan Mortensen (six from May 1947 to October 1948).
