That win was England's sixth in their last eight Nations League matches (L2) across the top two tiers, having scored 20 goals in that span. That is more victories and goals than they managed in their first 18 games in the competition overall (W5 D6 L7, 18 goals).

It was also England's eighth straight away win in all competitions, giving them an opportunity to match an all-time team record this weekend.

Only once have they ever won nine away games in a row, doing so under World Cup-winning manager Alf Ramsey between December 1965 and October 1967.

It will be intriguing to see how Tuchel approaches his team choice for this game, after he handed Trent Alexander-Arnold his first England start since October 2024 – in a Nations League win over Finland under Lee Carsley – at right-back.

Alexander-Arnold teed up Gordon's opening goal with a trademark delivery to the far post, which was also his first assist in international football since that Finland game two years ago.

Tuchel had gone with the more conservative option of Jarell Quansah on the right side of defence against Spain, but with Alexander-Arnold ranking second among England players for chances created (three, behind Gordon with four) and passes into the final third (32, behind Elliot Anderson with 40), might the England boss favour his creativity from deep areas? 

He also has options in midfield after handing Myles Lewis-Skelly back-to-back starts in the absence of his Arsenal club-mate Declan Rice, with Alex Scott winning his first senior cap in Prague and Morgan Gibbs-White making another lively cameo appearance. 

PLAYERS TO WATCH 

Czechia – Ivan Perisic 

Perisic, who provided a goal and an assist against England the 2018 World Cup semi-finals, has started both of Croatia's games during this international break.

The 37-year-old has 15 goal involvements in his last 18 starts for Croatia, netting six times and registering nine assists.

England – Harry Kane

Kane – who smacked a penalty off the crossbar after losing his footing in England's loss to Spain – has enjoyed playing on the road lately.

The England captain has found the net in each of his last five away internationals. 

He could now become just the fourth player to score in six consecutive away games for the Three Lions, after James Windridge (six from March to June 1908), Tom Finney (seven from September 1946 to May 1948) and Stan Mortensen (six from May 1947 to October 1948).

4sv8g3qeperh1e4w49upqy18l.title: Women's Super League predictions: Can Man City pull clear as Chelsea and Arsenal face off?
4sv8g3qeperh1e4w49upqy18l.subtitle: Manchester City's 100% start will be put to the test against Charlton Athletic, while Chelsea face Arsenal in the blockbuster clash of MD4.
paragraphs: After three matchdays in the Women's Super League season, defending champions Manchester City remain the only team with a 100% record, following their frantic 4-2 victory over Liverpool last time out.

After drawing 2-2 with Bayern Munich in their Champions League opener on Tuesday, City visit Charlton Athletic – who are the only team yet to pick up a point – to kickstart the week's action on Saturday, before the focus turns to their potential title rivals.
Neither Chelsea nor Arsenal have suffered a defeat yet this term, but with both sides already off City's pace, their head-to-head clash at Stamford Bridge on Sunday looks vital.
There is also a Merseyside derby between Liverpool and Everton, while Manchester United will look to finally earn their first league victory under Eva Olid, at home to West Ham.
Who will come out on top in the WSL this weekend? We have a look at the Opta supercomputer's predictions for matchday four.
CHARLTON ATHLETIC V MANCHESTER CITY

With Manchester City making a perfect start and Charlton recording three straight defeats since their promotion, it should come as little surprise that our predictive model makes Andree Jeglertz's champions the clearest MD4 favourites, with a 75.6% win probability to Charlton's 10.6%.
Only once in the last eight campaigns have City enjoyed a longer winning start than this one, winning each of their first four matches in 2019-20.
But they will be supremely confident of matching that feat at The Valley, in what will be their first competitive meeting with Charlton in the WSL era.
Promoted sides have won just one of their last 28 meetings with the reigning champions in the competition (D3 L24), with Liverpool recording a 2-1 home victory over Chelsea in September 2022.

Last time out, Khadija Shaw became the first player to score in each of City's first three games of a WSL campaign, and she could become the fifth player to do so in the first four matches of a season for any club, after Kim Little in 2018-19 (four for Arsenal), Vivianne Miedema in 2020-21 (five for Arsenal), Martha Thomas in 2023-24 (four for Tottenham) and Aggie Beever-Jones in 2025-26 (four for Chelsea).
LONDON CITY LIONESSES V BRIGHTON
Charlton's last game was a thumping 4-1 defeat to the ambitious London City Lionesses, who have six points on the board after three games and sit fourth in the table ahead of facing winless Brighton.
Alexia Putellas and company are assigned a 52.9% win probability on Saturday, with Brighton only winning 23% of the supercomputer's pre-match simulations.

London City's three wins in their last four WSL matches (L1) are more than they managed across their previous 12 in the competition (W2 D3 L7), and their nine 'big' chances against Charlton last week were the most by any team in a WSL game since October 2020 (when Man Utd had 10 versus Brighton).

The Seagulls could fail to win their opening four matches of a WSL campaign for the third time after 2018-19 (first six) and 2019-20 (first five), and they have lost seven of their last nine league games in London.
MANCHESTER UNITED V WEST HAM
Olid got her first win in charge of Manchester United in the Women's League Cup on Wednesday, with a 10-1 thrashing of Sheffield United, and they will now look to translate that into a WSL victory.
They are given a 68% chance of beating West Ham – whose chances sit at 14.3% – having gone unbeaten in their last 12 league games against the Hammers (W8 D4).

United are winless in their first three WSL matches (D1 L2) for the first time and have lost two of their last three home games in the competition (D1), as many defeats as they suffered in their previous 20 (W12 D6).
West Ham struggle on their travels against the Red Devils, though, having lost each of their six such games in the WSL by an aggregate score of 1-19.
They have only won one of their three games this term (L2), but given United have attempted just 10 shots in the WSL in 2026-27, they might feel this is a good chance to get one over on them.
BIRMINGHAM CITY V CRYSTAL PALACE
Two of the new teams at this level face off, with Birmingham City seeking their first victory since promotion while Crystal Palace try to get back to winning ways.
Palace were the only team to do the league double over WSL2 champions Birmingham last season – the Eagles have actually won each of their last four league matches against the Blues.
However, it is Birmingham who are backed to come out on top on Sunday with a 44.7% win probability to Palace's 28.4%. Though at 26.9%, this is one of the most likely draws of the weekend.

Birmingham could start a WSL campaign without a win in four games (D1 L2 so far) for the third time, but Amy Merricks will be determined to halt her nine-match winless streak as a manager in the top flight (D3 L6).
Liverpool were 3-2 winners against Everton back in March and could win consecutive WSL games against the Toffees for the first time since 2013 and 2014 (three straight).

The Reds are marginal favourites to prevail in Sunday's derby, despite losing eight of their nine previous league games played at Anfield, including five against Everton. They are given a 44% chance of victory.

Only Man City (11), Chelsea and Arsenal (both 10) have won more WSL games in 2026 than Everton (seven), who could win three league matches in a row for the second time this calendar year (won four in a row in February).
Everton's chances of winning away to their Merseyside rivals are 29.1%, but this is the other most likely draw of the weekend, with 26.9% of the simulations finishing level.
TOTTENHAM V ASTON VILLA
After three matchdays, Tottenham are in the mix at the top, sitting second and just two points behind Man City, having made an unbeaten start to the season (W2 D1).

They are actually unbeaten in their last six league games and could go seven straight without defeat for the first time in the league's history; they have a 57.7% chance of extending that run with a win.

Aston Villa have won three of their last five WSL away games against Spurs (D1 L1), but they come into this match having drawn their last two league games on the road. There is a 22% chance of them adding a third draw to that run.
The Villans have not yet gone ahead in any of their three league games, something they must do if they are to turn their 20.3% win probability into a first victory of the season.
The spotlight clash of the matchday sees Chelsea and Arsenal look to keep the pressure on Man City and extend their respective unbeaten starts.
Arsenal (20) and Chelsea (11) are on the two longest unbeaten runs in the WSL currently.

And Chelsea are looking to go unbeaten in their opening four games for the fourth successive WSL season, while Arsenal could win as few as five points from their first four matches for the second time in the last three seasons (after 2024-25).

This will be the 10th meeting between Chelsea and Arsenal in all competitions since the 2023-24 season, with both teams picking up four wins apiece in that time (D1), though the Gunners won the most recent league meeting at Stamford Bridge 2-0, back in January.
Chelsea are the favourites to triumph, winning 51.9% of the supercomputer's simulations, compared to Arsenal's 23.6%.
And Renee Slegers will be determined to have her say, having already beaten Sonia Bompastor twice in all competitions this calendar year – no manager has ever won three in a row against her.

4ued3nzwi76n1hbx4tjx150jv.title: Scotland suffer 'big setback' in 'new chapter', says McGinn after defeat to Switzerland
4ued3nzwi76n1hbx4tjx150jv.subtitle: Ten-man Scotland fell to a 3-0 defeat at Hampden Park against Switzerland, leaving Sebastien Pocognoli winless after two games.
paragraphs: John McGinn believes Scotland suffered a "big setback" in their "new chapter" under Sebastien Pocognoli after losing 3-0 to Switzerland in the Nations League.

Scotland were dealt a huge blow just 11 minutes into Pocognoli's first home game in charge after Jack Hendry was shown a straight red card for a last-man challenge, and matters were made worse when Ricardo Rodriguez arrowed in the resulting free-kick.

Nico Elvedi and Zeki Amdouni netted for the visitors at Hampden Park after half-time, seeing Pocognoli (D1 L1) become the first Scotland manager to fail to win his first two games in charge since George Burley in May 2008 (D1 L1).

Scotland (two shots) failed to have a shot on target in a home game for the first time since September 2023 against England (seven shots), while they have failed to score in four consecutive games for the first time since 1971.
They are also without a clean sheet in eight home games, their worst run since going 10 in a row without a shutout between October 2001 and September 2003.

McGinn, who made his 91st appearance for Scotland, moving him alongside Jim Leighton in joint-third place for the most caps for his country, has urged his team-mates to learn from the humbling defeat.
"We could have done better at times, but we're starting a new chapter, learning to play a different way. That was a big setback for us," McGinn told BBC Scotland.
"We've got a lot to learn from, but a lot to take from it as well.
"I thought Oli McBurnie was outstanding. He's had a lot of criticism in a Scotland shirt, but [this game] was a thankless task and he gave everything for us.
"Going down to 10 men, it's a test of character; you need to dig in. It's a huge learning curve for us, and when we play them away, we need to win now."
Scotland will now face North Macedonia on Saturday, with the early pressure already piling on Pocognoli.

4ugjg5li8qod1oy7dyoc6i1kb.title: Juventus goalkeeper Grabara undergoes successful ACL surgery
4ugjg5li8qod1oy7dyoc6i1kb.subtitle: Kamil Grabara faces up to seven months on the sidelines after sustaining a serious injury on his debut for Juventus in the Europa League.
paragraphs: Juventus have confirmed Kamil Grabara has undergone successful surgery to reconstruct the anterior cruciate (ACL) ligament in his knee.
Grabara sustained the injury during a training session just two days after making his debut for Juventus during a 5-0 victory over NEC in the Europa League.
The 27-year-old, who is on a season-long loan with the Serie A giants from Wolfsburg, provided the assist for Nico Gonzalez's opener at Allianz Stadium.
However, it is believed the Poland international will now face up to seven months on the sidelines, following a summer of changes in the goalkeeping department at Juventus.
The Bianconeri allowed Michele Di Gregorio and Mattia Perin to leave the club, while also bringing in Guglielmo Vicario on loan from Premier League side Tottenham.
"Kamil Grabara underwent surgery this afternoon to reconstruct the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee," Juventus said in a statement.
"The procedure, performed at the Guardian Clinic in Konin by Dr Andrzej Pyda, in the presence of Juventus Club Doctor Dr Marco Freschi, was a complete success.
"The player will begin his rehabilitation programme in the coming days, with a view to returning to competitive action."
With the transfer window now shut, Juventus are reportedly close to agreeing a deal with Neto, who previously played in Turin between 2015 and 2017.
Neto is a free agent following the termination of his contract with Botafogo in June, and he is set to sign until the end of the season, according to reports.
The Brazilian played 22 times across all competitions during his previous stint with Juventus, keeping 12 clean sheets and winning five major honours.
Since his exit from Juventus nine years ago, he has gone on to represent Valencia, Barcelona, Bournemouth, Arsenal and most recently, Botafogo.
Juventus are seventh in Serie A after their first five games of the season, and they return to action after the international break against Cagliari on October 11.

4x2jogj427ih1sthlaz3k388x.title: Hall says Newcastle contract renewal was 'a no-brainer' amid Man Utd rumours
4x2jogj427ih1sthlaz3k388x.subtitle: Manchester United were tipped to move for Lewis Hall this summer, but the left-back eventually signed a new contract with Newcastle United.
paragraphs: Lewis Hall says it was "a no-brainer" to sign a new long-term contract with Newcastle United, despite attracting interest from Manchester United throughout the summer.
Earlier this month, Hall ended speculation over his immediate future by penning fresh terms with the Magpies, with his new deal reportedly running until 2031.
Having joined his boyhood club from Chelsea in 2023, Hall has made 109 appearances for Newcastle in all competitions, with 82 of those being starts.
He helped Newcastle end their 70-year domestic trophy drought by winning the EFL Cup in 2025, though a foot injury caused him to miss their victory over Liverpool in the final.
Hall has also started 2026-27 strongly under new boss Mathias Jaissle, providing two assists in all competitions and scoring his first goal of the campaign in Saturday's 2-1 home win over Hull City.
Asked by Chronicle Live if he ever felt like he had a difficult decision to make amid loud transfer speculation, Hall said: "No, honestly, it didn't.
"I guess whenever you're linked to another team, you know that you're doing something right. It's a credit to your own performances and how you are as a player, and how you are as a person.
"I took that as a positive, but at the same time, I love playing here and since the manager came in, I knew the ambitions and what we wanted to achieve.
"After not many conversations, not many training sessions, I knew that the manager was going to be really good for this club.
"I knew that as a team, bringing in new players and improving the squad was really important and as soon as we did that, it was a no-brainer to sign."

Hall was recently recalled to the England squad by Thomas Tuchel ahead of Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia (home and away) and Croatia, having missed out on the Three Lions' group for the World Cup.
And looking long-term, Hall believes being at St James' Park allows him to fulfil his ambitions, saying: "When you're with a team, you don't think too far into the future.
"Obviously, I'm really grateful for the contract that I've received and the trust that I've been given from the board and from the manager.
"I'm just taking it game by game, just trying to do the best I can for this club. We've got ambitions and as long as we achieve what we want to achieve, I'm sure I'll be here for a long time."
With eight points on the board from five Premier League games, Newcastle face Coventry City in their first game after the international break, on October 12.

50D8E5F6D50030B36E27C4C6F51ACF5D.title: Raphinha: The most in-form player in Europe has made a blistering start to 2026/27
50D8E5F6D50030B36E27C4C6F51ACF5D.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesRaphinha: The most in-form player in Europe has made a blistering start to 2026/27Share“It’s a joke!” Luis García didn’t mince his words following Sevilla’s 3-1 defeat to Barcelona at the weekend. And no, he wasn’t referring to a dodgy refereeing decision, or a defensive mishap that caused his side to crumble on home turf. Rather, he was referring to the 2026 Ballon d’Or.

Specifically, Raphinha’s omission from 30-man nomination list. Barcelona are well represented in the lead up to the individual award. Spanish trio Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Pau Cubarsí are the Blaugrana contingent in the running for the accolade, though in truth; only the former pair are genuine contenders for the 2026 award.

Even so, Raphinha at present is outperforming the trio, and, in truth, the other 27 players to make the cut for the prestigious gong. Indeed, the brilliant Brazilian has been directly involved in a goal in every competitive appearance for Hansi Flick’s men this season. He’s scored in all but one of eight outings, and even then; he provided a brace of assists as the defending LaLiga champions claimed a 4-2 win at Levante.

Saturday’s perfect hat-trick – the former Leeds United scored one with his right, another with his left, and the third with his head – took him to 12 league goals for the season. Even the great Lionel Messi failed to achieve the feat after the opening seven games of a league campaign at Barcelona.

What’s all the more important is that Raphinha’s form has come at a time when Barcelona ended the summer transfer window, arguably, a forward short. Marcus Rashford was replaced by Anthony Gordon. Karim Adeyemi’s arrival eased Ferran Torres’ move to Paris Saint-Germain. They ruthlessly pushed for Atlético Madrid hitman Julián Alvarez in their quest to replace Robert Lewandowski.

Naturally, Barcelona were never going to trigger Alvarez’s €500m release clause, and they needn’t have bothered with their pursuit of the Argentine. Turns out Barcelona had the perfect Lewandowski successor the whole time.

Joining for £69.3m, Gordon was never going to sign as a backup for the Brazil international on the left. Yamal is one of the first names on the team sheet down the right. Crowbarring Raphinha into the side could have backfired on Flick and Barcelona. In hindsight, it’s proven a masterstroke.

The 29-year-old has been granted the license to drift across the pitch not just in search of possession, but in order to drag markers out of position. Flick deploys inverted widemen in his favoured 4-3-3 setup. Left winger Gordon favours his right foot. Right winger Yamal prefers his left.

Raphinha’s willingness to drop a little deeper opens up space for the pair to exploit. He’s not a conventional number nine by any stretch, so there is no point acting like one. What is key, though, is that Raphinha is also capitalising upon the space he creates.

Speed has so often been a strong point of the forward’s game. When Raphinha switches on the afterburners, good luck keeping up with him. In wide areas, he had to cover greater distances to get into goalscoring areas. Now, his speed off the mark means he really comes alive inside the opposition box when he makes darting runs into the penalty area.

42 touches inside the opposition box ranks fifth in LaLiga this season. For context, Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé (85) tops this metric. The Frenchman spends more time in the area, because this plays to his strengths. For Raphinha, that lightning quick turn of pace so often bamboozles opposition defences.

It’s no coincidence that all 12 of his league goals this season have been scored inside the penalty area. Granted, three of them are penalties. Yet even so, Barcelona are proving even more potent when they break forward then last season, which is some going for a team that scored more goals (95) than any other team in the 2025/26 LaLiga campaign.

After all, their average of 4.43 league goals per game is almost double last season’s haul (2.5). Much of that is due to the speed of their attack having scored more counter-attacking goals (4) than any other team in Spain’s top tier. Raphinha has struck two of those. 14 shots following a counter attack is the third most in the division.

Crucially, too, is that not only is Raphinha able to get on the end of the ample chances that are created by this rampant Barcelona side, he’s proving incredibly efficient in front of goal. Of the 135 players to have managed at least five shots, only Pape Gueye (50%) boasts a better conversion rate than Raphinha (48%). The former has managed six shots. The latter has had 25. 11 of his 12 goals have been deemed big chances.

Back to García’s comments, however, and recency bias does play a part. That’s not suggesting Raphinha doesn’t deserve his flowers. He’s the most in-form player in Europe at present. Rather, over the course of the calendar year, the Barca star hasn’t quite hit the lofty heights, and that is through no fault of his own.

Injuries have wreaked havoc on both his playing time and his consistency. It’s denied Raphinha the chance to gain a head of steam for both club and country. As such, Flick’s use of the forward will prove beneficial for the player as he relies on shorter, sharper bursts rather than prolonged sprints that increase the likelihood of muscle injuries.

And if he can avoid a reoccurrence of those pesky problems going forward, then he’ll undoubtedly be in the running for the 2027 award. Barcelona are tearing opponents to shreds without showing a modicum of sympathy. If he can fire them to domestic and continental glory, then he’ll be in the running.

          How Would a Points Deduction Affect Manchester City’s 2026-27 Premier League Season?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 3, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After the Opta supercomputer ran 100,000 simulations of Manchester City’s 2026-27 Premier League season, we‘ve calculated the precise impact of every possible points deduction.
Ever since Manchester City were found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules, speculation has been rife as to what their punishment might be.
The club maintain their innocence, and on Friday confirmed they have lodged an official appeal against the Premier League’s ruling.

It’s a completely unprecedented situation in many ways, and there are so many unknowns that it's impossible to say with any certainty what’s going to happen next. But the widely held view seems to be that any appeals process will mean it’s a long time before any final decision is made on what sentence City will serve (if they fail in their appeal).

The range of punishments being mooted is vast, and we’re not here to say where on the scale it should fall, but given that Everton and Nottingham Forest were both handed points deductions for financial rule-breaking in recent years, there is a real possibility that City will also face one this season.

Whether they are also given further sanctions remains to be seen and is not for us to speculate on. But what we can do here at Opta Analyst is use the wisdom of the Opta supercomputer to tell us precisely what impact any points deduction would have on the Premier League in 2026-27.

City are top of the Premier League at the time of writing with the only remaining 100% record, having become only the 14th team in the history of the competition to begin a season with five wins from five. But a points deduction could completely derail their season.
That said, they would have had a lot of work to do to go on and win the title regardless, given that only four of the previous 14 teams to begin with five wins went on to win the title.

Clearly, a fast start doesn’t necessarily bring success, and the Opta supercomputer currently makes them second favourites, with a 39.9% chance of winning the title, behind Arsenal’s 44.2% (based on no points deduction, as is currently the case).

But how exactly would a points deduction affect their chances? The Opta supercomputer has run 100,000 simulations of the rest of the season, before then applying every possible points deduction and spitting out a final league position for City. We can then look at the percentage of simulations in which City finish in each position to assign a likelihood of each eventuality, depending on the size of the points deduction.

So, we are now able to say the extent to which their title chances would drop depending on the points deduction, as well as their chances of qualifying for the Champions League. But perhaps most interestingly, how big the deduction would need to be to make it likely that City are relegated.  Inspired by the fine work of Aurel Nazmiu on X, we used the Opta supercomputer to create this visualisation with numbers from our own model:

This is, of course, entirely speculative. It is still unclear what City’s punishment will be or if their appeal will be successful, given they maintain their innocence. We at Opta Analyst have no way of knowing how the punishment will be decided, whether there will even be a punishment, or if any sanctions will extend into future seasons.
But they could quite feasibly face a punishment that includes a points deduction, and with that comes the possibility of relegation from the Premier League this season.

According to the supercomputer’s findings, City’s chances of relegation are only certain – meaning they were relegated in every single one of the 100,000 simulations – when they were given a 74-point deduction. For every possible deduction of fewer than 74 points, there was at least one simulation in which City avoided the drop.

That means that the supercomputer saw (rare) circumstances in which City were docked 73 points but won enough games to still finish on a higher total than three other teams. That would likely require them to win almost all of their remaining games, which isn’t impossible, but it is very, very unlikely.

It took a deduction of 40 points to tip City over a 50% likelihood of relegation, with a steady increase from there up to 60 points, at which point their chances of relegation get very close to – but not quite – 100%.
For every deduction of 30 points of fewer, City were relegated in fewer than 20% of simulations. Anything up to 20 points, and their chances of relegation remain under 5%.

For Champions League qualification, it took a 38-point deduction to reduce City’s chances to under 1%, based on the Premier League’s top four making it into that competition. If a fifth spot is up for grabs – as it has been in the last two seasons – City would have slightly more wiggle room: a 40-point deduction would be needed to reduce their chances to less than 1%.

As for the title race, the supercomputer reckons City would retain a chance of more than 10% with anything under 10 points deducted, while it took 25 points being taken off their total for them to be reduced to complete outsiders, with less than a 1% chance of winning the league.
For now, there’s no knowing what City’s punishment will be, but the Opta supercomputer is able to give us a little more idea of the impact of any potential points deduction.

5260A198D817B369DE6CC7483FC62088.title: Joao Felix finally showing what the fuss is about in an expanded role for Portugal
5260A198D817B369DE6CC7483FC62088.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesJoao Felix finally showing what the fuss is about in an expanded role for PortugalShareThe career of the 26-year-old, which has taken many of Europe’s biggest clubs, has been one of modern football’s greatest curiosities.

Portugal’s new era looked a lot like the old one as Jorge Jesus picked his first lineup as manager. There was still a place, initially, for 41-year-old Cristiano Ronaldo whose fading contribution undermined Portugal’s entire 2026 World Cup campaign. João Félix was also selected to face Wales and Denmark.

The days of Félix being the face of Portuguese football’s next generation seemed long gone. Written off as a flop after a meandering route that took in many of Europe’s biggest clubs, Felix joined Al-Nasser in the Saudi Pro League last year. It was a move that appeared to indicate Felix had given up on making an impact at the elite level.

Against Wales and Denmark, though, Félix was Portugal’s best player. The 26-year-old found the back of the net in both games, demonstrating the sort of composure in front of goal that evaded Ronaldo. If there was one player who looked to have scored 146 international goals in his career, it wasn’t the 41-year-old.

Only Erling Haaland had more shots than Félix in Sunday’s meeting between Norway and Portugal while only Ronaldo had more in the win over Wales in Lisbon. At a time when it would have been easy for Félix to be pushed aside due to the location of his club, he is finally showing what he can do at international level.

Félix has long been a mystery box of a player. He became the second-most expensive teenager in football history after Kylian Mbappé when he joined Atlético Madrid for €126m in 2019, but was never a good fit for Diego Simeone’s playing style. While there were glimpses of Félix’s talent, he struggled for form.

From there, Félix made the ill-advised decision to join Chelsea when the Stamford Bridge club lacked any sort of direction. A loan to Barcelona similarly did little to help the Portuguese attacker’s development with a short stint at AC Milan possibly the most forgettable of his career.

Amid all these bouncing around, Felix failed to nail down a position. Some managers used him in a wide role despite the fact Félix has never been much of a one-on-one dribbler. Others deployed him as a second striker where his knack for finding space between the lines is useful.

To use Félix as a roaming number 10, though, the teams he played for required a rock-steady midfield platform to compensate. His selection frequently put too much strain on other parts of the side and so it was easier to use Félix as a depth option off the bench. That has been his role at several clubs.

In the Saudi Pro League, though, Al-Nasser have built around Félix who scored 20 league goals in 33 games in his debut season. Then the coach of his club side, Jesus embraced Félix in a way no manager had done since the attacker’s Benfica days and the results have been astonishing. It took a move to Saudi Arabia for Félix to show his potential again.

In Jesus, Félix has found a father figure. The veteran coach has put his arm around the shoulder of a widely misunderstood player who not so long ago was considered one of the most exciting in Europe. When Félix broke through at Benfica, he was compared to Johan Cruyff. That’s how much promise he had.

Since then, Félix has paid a heavy price for several bad career decisions, but he’s still only 26. There is still time for him to become the player many predicted he would be. Portugal are certainly benefiting from Félix operating in a free role that makes the most of his natural talent as a creator and a finisher.

“That’s where I can make things happen,” said Félix when asked about the second striker role Jesus has trusted him in for club and country. “He’s played me there since last year and everyone can see the results. I hope it will be the same in the national team – that things go well and people will see the real me.”

In Félix’s own words, he would entertain a return to Europe at some point in the future. “I’m happy and enjoying my soccer, but it’s true that I’m also thinking about returning,” said the 26-year-old. “I don’t know whether it’ll be next year, in two years, three or four, but I’d like to play in European competitions again.”

When Jesus was hired as Roberto Martínez’s replacement after the World Cup, many cynically – and perhaps fairly – looked at how the former Al-Nasser boss would favour Ronaldo. Instead, Ronaldo was benched for the win over Norway with Félix the main man in the number 10 role.

Perhaps more significant than Félix scoring in back-to-back games against Wales and Norway was the fact he played the full 90 minutes in successive matches as a Portugal international. A Saudi Pro League star is responding well to Jesus as Portugal’s new manager, but not the obvious one.

577ct7z5vig2z566vq5e9itf.title: England 3-0 Czechia: Kane doubles up on record-equalling appearance
577ct7z5vig2z566vq5e9itf.subtitle: Harry Kane marked his record-equalling appearance by being involved in all of England's goals in a 3-0 Nations League defeat of Czechia.
paragraphs: England swatted aside Czechia 3-0 as Harry Kane played a starring role on his landmark appearance.
Kane played his 125th game for the Three Lions on Tuesday, matching Peter Shilton as England's joint-most-capped player.
And Kane marked the occasion in style, playing a role in all of England's goals in a routine Nations League triumph at Wembley Stadium.
England made a dominant start, though they were not rewarded for their efforts until the 27th minute, when Kane swung in a cross, aiming for Eberechi Eze.
Eze stalled his run, but Vladimir Coufal was unaware and, under no pressure, the former West Ham defender slid in and diverted the ball into the back of Czechia's net.

England doubled their lead in sumptuous style 13 minutes later. Elliot Anderson swept a sublime pass over the top for Morgan Rogers, who cushioned a wonderful first-time pass into Kane's path, and the Three Lions captain made no mistake with his finish.

Kane struck the top of the crossbar with a swerving strike at the end of a slick move shortly after half-time, but he helped himself to his second when he headed home unchallenged from Lewis Hall's corner.

Thomas Tuchel took the chance to hand some of his fringe players a chance late on, including Rio Ngumoha, who became the second-youngest player to feature for England at Wembley (18 years, 38 days), behind Jude Bellingham (17 years, 136 days).
Czechia offered little threat, bar a stinging long-range drive from Roman Macek, as England eased onto nine points in Nations League Group A3, three behind leaders Spain.
Another special Wembley showing for Kane
Kane will have to wait until at least November for his record-breaking England cap, but he was always likely to have a say on the day he equalled Shilton.
The 33-year-old has now scored 2+ goals in six different matches for England at Wembley, now the outright most of any player, overtaking Alan Shearer (five).

He has also netted at least twice in 18 different games for the Three Lions, which is another record, while Kane is the oldest player in England's history to score a brace in consecutive appearances (33 years, 70 days tonight).
Kane's 13 goals in 2026 are now the second most any England player has scored in a single calendar year, behind the 16 he netted in 2021.
That goal tally is also the most among any European player in 2026, with Kane now ahead of France's Kylian Mbappe (12).
It was about as comfortable as you can get for England, who created chances worth 1.83 expected goals but allowed Czechia to have just five shots, which were worth a combined 0.17 xG.
England will need just a point from their last two games to join Spain in qualifying for the quarter-finals, while Czechia have lost five matches on the bounce.

          Premier League Fixture Difficulty vs Results: Which Teams Have Defied Expectations?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 2, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design, Ithiel Piñero / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look back at pre-season expectations for Premier League clubs' first five matches and assess how well they've done relative to the supposed difficulty of their fixture schedules.
Five matchdays is all it takes to dramatically alter perspectives and expectations in the Premier League.

Think back to pre-season, that fantastical time of renewal, hope and excitement. Intrusive thoughts about the campaign ahead barely register for most. Instead, brain power is dedicated to thinking about what could be achieved.
Reality can come at you quickly, however.
The 2026-27 Premier League season may only be in relative infancy, but pre-season already feels like a long time ago now, especially for certain clubs.

A good or bad start isn’t always indicative of what’s to come, though. There can be a whole host of reasons for either, and most won’t be permanent. For instance, fixture difficulty is something you cannot ignore – not every start to the season is equal.
On the eve of 2026-27, we used the Opta Power Rankings to determine which clubs had the easiest and toughest opening schedules.
Now, we can look back on those findings to see how they correlate with the real Premier League table after five matchdays.
Generally, there is a loose correlation between fixture difficulty and the points teams earned across the first five matchdays of the season.
For example, the 10 teams deemed to have the easier schedules averaged 8.2 points, whereas the 10 with the toughest have averaged 5.2. But it’s the extremes that are most interesting to look at.

Manchester City lead the fledgling table, of course, having won their first five games. Considering they came into the season with a fair amount of uncertainty surrounding them due to player churn and Pep Guardiola’s exit, their start to the campaign – on the field at least – couldn’t have gone much better.

But it must be pointed out that, according to the pre-season Opta Power Rankings, they had the second-easiest start with an average opponent rating of 91.4. Their opening slate wasn’t without challenges; beating Manchester United away from home despite having 10 men for over an hour was impressive, though most would’ve expected them to take close to maximum points from Bournemouth (H), Crystal Palace (A), Coventry (H) and Sunderland (H).

Liverpool were deemed to have the easiest schedule (91.2). Nine points from those five games probably left most fans slightly underwhelmed, though we must remember the Power Rankings can’t exactly account for elements like adapting to a managerial change with Andoni Iraola now in the hot seat.
In terms of most disappointing start to the season, Man Utd are certainly up there. The Opta Power Rankings suggested they had the third-easiest schedule, but they’ve amassed just five points.

A Matchday 1 defeat to promoted Hull City was alarming. They did at least follow that up with a 5-2 defeat of Ipswich Town at Old Trafford, but that remains their only victory. Sitting 12th after statistically the third-easiest start is understandably concerning.
Brighton are another of the outliers, but for completely different reasons to Man Utd.

With an opening slate of Aston Villa (H), Chelsea (A), Leeds (H), Coventry (A) and Arsenal (H), any nervousness from supporters would’ve been logical. The Opta Power Rankings assessed that as the fourth-hardest start.
But they took 10 points from those games, including an immensely impressive 3-0 dismantling of the champions in their last game before the international break that left them third in the table.

One caveat is that they have spent more time (87 minutes) this season playing against 10 men than any other club, though in fairness to them, they were at least 2-0 up when Villa and Coventry had a man sent off.
If Brighton have been the story of the season so far, then Hull have at least given them a run for their money.

5f3te9ge6hyk1dia3ufms1lxc.title: Pocognoli using experience of Belgium's 'golden generation' to handle Scotland pressure
5f3te9ge6hyk1dia3ufms1lxc.subtitle: Scotland start the Sebastien Pocognoli era on Saturday, and he wants pressure to become something that motivates, not hinders, his team.
paragraphs: Sebastien Pocognoli feels his experiences in the early days of Belgium's "golden generation" can help him manage expectations with Scotland, as he prepares for his first game in charge.

Scotland open their Nations League campaign in Slovenia on Saturday, with Switzerland and North Macedonia their other opponents in Group B1, having been relegated from the competition's top tier under Steve Clarke in 2024-25.

Clarke did lead Scotland to a second successive major tournament – and a record third under his watch – at the World Cup, but they suffered a meek group-stage exit following defeats against Morocco and Brazil.
Pocognoli is returning to international management, having coached Belgium's under-18 side before having stints in charge of Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco in the club game.
And he feels he has learned plenty about managing the pressure that comes with the international game, having been part of Belgium's much-feted "golden generation".

Pocognoli played alongside Vincent Kompany, Thomas Vermaelen, Jan Vertonghen and Mousa Dembele at the 2008 Olympic Games – a tournament where Belgium lost the bronze-medal match – before winning 13 senior caps between 2008 and 2014.

He never appeared at a major tournament for his country, with his final cap coming in 2014 World Cup qualifying, but he saw how the pressure to deliver silverware weighed on a squad that also featured Eden Hazard, Kevin De Bruyne and Romelu Lukaku.
"In my own case, I was part of the 'golden generation' at the start," he said. "I made the first step. We made the Olympic Games, and I was part of the [2014] qualification.

"But for me, there were high expectations on the Belgian players – an over-expectation. It was too much. It is a country of 12 million people, and you have to deal with France and Germany next to you, and England.
"There were fantastic players and that Belgium team reached third place in the [2018] World Cup. Fantastic. They were first in the FIFA rankings for five or six years. You can't do more than that.
"Maybe with some luck you can win a medal, but there was over-expectation and I think that generation reached its best, to be honest."
Though the expectations surrounding Scotland are not as sky-high as those that Belgium failed to meet, Pocognoli wants to make pressure a motivating factor for his team.
"Yes, the bar is very high," Pocognoli said. "I know this. But you have to deal with this heritage. The heritage is massively positive, so use it.
"If I put this as a pressure, we are not going to go the right way. I have to use it as a benefit to embrace."
Scotland – who are building towards a home European Championship campaign in 2028 – will welcome Switzerland to Hampden Park next Tuesday, for their first home game under Pocognoli.

5r3uw0xb0bzq1l0vn49kubyiq.title: Women's Super League predictions: Man Utd to beat Liverpool, Man City backed against Arsenal
5r3uw0xb0bzq1l0vn49kubyiq.subtitle: Manchester City take on Arsenal in the headline tussle of matchday five in the Women's Super League.
paragraphs: The Women's Super League table is starting to take shape after the first four matches of the 2026-27 campaign.
Reigning champions Manchester City are the only team with a 100% record still intact, after four straight wins to open the campaign.
Behind them, Chelsea and Tottenham are the only other teams yet to taste defeat, while London City Lionesses are also in touching distance of the top.
Arsenal have made a stuttering start, which was compounded by a 1-0 loss to Chelsea last time out, and things do not get any easier as they travel to City this weekend.
Things were more positive for Manchester United, who held out for their first league win under Eva Olid last time out, moving up the table and leaving four clubs without a victory.
So, who will come out on top in the WSL this weekend?
MANCHESTER UNITED V LIVERPOOL
The action begins on Saturday, with Manchester United and Liverpool both looking to build on morale-boosting wins, against West Ham and Everton, respectively.

Gareth Taylor (81) is aiming to tie former United boss Marc Skinner (82) for the second-most managerial wins in WSL history – only Emma Hayes (151) has recorded more – and our predictive model gives that a 17% chance of happening.
As it stands, United are heavy favourites to take all three points at 63.6%, given they have won four of their five WSL home matches against the Reds (L1).
United have conceded in each of their last 11 home league games, though, which might give Liverpool hope of earning consecutive WSL wins for the first time since March 2025 under Amber Whiteley.
Despite a 19.4% chance of a draw, there has never been a stalemate between these teams in the competition in nine previous meetings (six United wins, three Liverpool victories).
ASTON VILLA V CRYSTAL PALACE
It has been a tough start to the season for Aston Villa, who have gone winless in their four games (D2 L2), leading to Natalia Arroyo’s dismissal on Tuesday.
Brian Sorensen is in interim charge and will be in the dugout when Villa host Crystal Palace.
The hosts are the favourites to take the points, however, with a 45.2% win likelihood to Palace’s 27.9%.

Villa could go winless across their opening five matches of a WSL campaign for the third time (after 2023-24 and 2024-25), but they have won three of their last five league meetings with Palace (D1 L1).
Palace, meanwhile, have lost just one of their opening four league matches this term (W1 D2) – the fewest defeats of any promoted side at this stage of a single WSL campaign.
BRIGHTON V CHARLTON ATHLETIC
Two teams still searching for their first win go head-to-head at the Amex, with Brighton and Charlton Athletic desperate for their maiden victory of 2026-27.

Charlton are the only team still without a point – they could become the third team to lose their first five matches in the competition, after Yeovil Town (first seven in 2017) and Leicester City (first nine in 2021-22).
But Brighton are also winless in their last seven WSL games (D4 L3). Only once before have they endured a longer streak: nine between November 2022 and April 2023.
The Seagulls are tipped to come out on top, winning 58.6% of Opta's pre-match simulations, while Charlton only triumph in 19.8%.
EVERTON V BIRMINGHAM CITY
Birmingham City (23.7%) are another team still searching for a first victory, while Everton (51.8%) are looking to bounce back from their Merseyside derby defeat.
Everton are unbeaten in each of their last five WSL games against Birmingham (W3 D2), while they won the most recent meeting 2-0 in the League Cup last month.
Birmingham went unbeaten in their first seven away games against Everton in the WSL (W3 D4), but they did lose 3-1 in the most recent of those, in September 2021.

Worryingly for the Blues, they have lost the most points from winning positions in the top flight so far this term (four), which is something Amy Merricks will be keen to improve on sooner rather than later, if Birmingham open the scoring at Goodison Park.
TOTTENHAM V LONDON CITY LIONESSES
London City Lionesses went second after their win over Brighton last time out, but their stint behind Man City lasted less than 24 hours as they were leapfrogged by Tottenham.

Alexia Putellas made her mark in that victory, scoring her first goal for the club, ending her longest goal drought in top-flight football (seven games) since December 2017 (eight games for Barcelona); the Spaniard has ended on the winning side in 129 of the last 130 league games she has netted in.
Given that record, another goal from her would be welcome, given the Lionesses have lost each of their three away games against Spurs in all competitions by an aggregate score of 11-1.

Spurs are in strong form, too; only in 2021-22 (12) have they won more points after four games of a WSL campaign than their 10 in 2026-27, though a win in this match would see them set a club record for their best points return after five games (12 in 2021-22 and 2025-26).
It is the hosts who are backed to come out on top, with a 45.3% win probability. London City’s chances sit at 27.8%, but this is the other most likely draw of the matchday at 26.9%.
Chelsea have made an unbeaten – albeit not completely convincing – start in the WSL, extending that run with a dogged 1-0 victory over Arsenal.
The Blues' attention now turns to West Ham, and Sonia Bompastor’s side are the most likely winners this weekend according to the supercomputer, with a 74% chance of victory.
They are unbeaten in all 16 of their WSL meetings with the Hammers (W14 D2), while West Ham have lost all eight of their home games against Chelsea in the competition by an aggregate score of 26-2.

West Ham were 2-1 winners against London City in their most recent derby, though that is their only win this season (L3). They are given an 11.4% chance of getting a first WSL win against Chelsea, and a further 14.6% chance of claiming a point.
MANCHESTER CITY V ARSENAL
The action concludes with a huge clash on Sunday.
Arsenal know they cannot afford to drop more points if they want to keep Manchester City in their sights, even at this early stage.

Arsenal suffered more frustration in the Women’s Champions League, throwing away a 2-0 lead against Paris FC to draw 2-2, partly due to Leah Williamson's freak handball in the box after a defensive mix-up.

And things only seem to be getting tougher. City have won each of their last 14 home games in the WSL and could set the outright second-longest streak on home turf in the competition (Chelsea went 22 without defeat).
Arsenal do lead the head-to-head between the sides, winning 12 of the previous 25 meetings between the pair (11 City wins, two draws).

City have a 49.4% chance of winning their opening five games of a WSL campaign for the third time, while Arsenal are given a 25.1% win likelihood after going winless across their last three league games (D2 L1).

5shq40tllrkf1lri1z3qwciz8.title: Gyokeres not influenced by criticism after scoring for Sweden
5shq40tllrkf1lri1z3qwciz8.subtitle: Arsenal's Viktor Gyokeres scored his first goal of the season for Sweden against Romania, but he acknowledged his displays had to improve.
paragraphs: Viktor Gyokeres insisted he was not fazed by the criticism he has faced this season with Arsenal after ending his recent goal drought for Sweden in the Nations League.
Gyokeres was on target in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania at Strawberry Arena, with his strike proving to be the winning goal for Graham Potter's side.
Alexander Isak opened the scoring in the 20th minute, only for Dennis Man to level things up nine minutes later as both teams played out an entertaining first half an hour.
However, Gyokeres sealed the win two minutes before half-time, tucking home from close range after Lucas Bergvall's shot from distance was spilled by Ionut Radu.
It marked the Arsenal striker's first goal of the 2026-27 campaign for club and country, having failed to score in any of his five appearances in all competitions for the Gunners.

Gyokeres has only played 207 minutes of football for Arsenal this season, starting just two matches, despite netting 21 times across all competitions in his debut season for Mikel Arteta's side following his big-money move from Sporting CP.

Kai Havertz's injury while playing for Germany could open the door for more opportunities at club level for Gyokeres, who said recent criticism of his performances was something he was not interested in reading.
"If there is a lot of [criticism] and you read it, of course you can be influenced, but that is not something I do," Gyokeres said.
"If you do well, you get praise and if you don't score goals as a striker and play as they expect, there is criticism. That is how it is for all footballers. It goes up and down.
"It is normal. It's always nice to score a goal. It was a good finish from Lucas [Bergvall] and I was in a good position at the far post. I received it and got it in."
Gyokeres did, however, acknowledge his performances for Arsenal had to improve. He has only managed to muster one shot across all of his outings so far in 2026-27.
"I obviously need to do better, and yes, I want to do it, so that's no problem. It's good [the dialogue with Arteta]," Gyokeres added.
"I just try to do well when I get the chance and score goals. You always want to be on the field as a football player, that's just how it is.
"I haven't played a lot, but I've had a few games. It felt okay then, but it's clear that you want to play football, and you want to play as much as possible. If I focus, that will come."
But one player who is not short on confidence is Liverpool forward Isak, who made it five goals in eight matches for club and country so far this season.

Isak also finished with team-high totals for shots (three), touches in the opposition box (seven) and passes in the final third (26), while also playing the full 90 minutes against Romania, with Gyokeres replaced instead by Benjamin Nygren.
There was, however, a moment of concern for Isak, who went down and looked in some discomfort, but he revealed the issue was just some blood on his toe.
"You can see it," the Liverpool man told Sportbladet – who added that he "limped and grumbled badly for a good while" after the tackle – while pointing towards his toe.
"It was a real punch. Those of you who have played may know that it [the pain] takes a few minutes before it releases, but it was okay."

5xpun2m97xi71abl4ti4mrx2n.title: Wales have 'puncher's chance' against Portugal and 'alien' Ronaldo, says James
5xpun2m97xi71abl4ti4mrx2n.subtitle: Wales visit Portugal for their opening Nations League match on Thursday, with the Selecao still led by Cristiano Ronaldo.
paragraphs: Wales have a "puncher's chance" of upsetting Portugal in their Nations League opener on Thursday, even if the Selecao can still call upon an "alien" in Cristiano Ronaldo.
That is the view of midfielder Jordan James, as Craig Bellamy's side prepare for their League A campaign following promotion from the second tier in 2024-25.
Wales topped Group B4 in the last edition of the Nations League, ahead of Turkiye, Iceland and Montenegro, and their reward is a place in Group A4 this time around, with Portugal, Denmark and Norway.
While Wales went unbeaten in the 2024-25 Nations League (W3 D3), their last campaign in the top tier saw them go winless and earn the fewest points of any nation (D1 L5).
Portugal are, of course, the reigning Nations League holders, having beaten Spain on penalties in the 2024-25 final to win the competition for the second time.

And ahead of Thursday's matchup at Sporting CP's Estadio Jose Alvalade, they have won 11 of their 14 home matches in the competition overall (D1 L2), only losing to France (in November 2020) and Spain (September 2022).
But James – who has helped Wolves make a strong start in the Championship after arriving in a loan-to-buy deal from Rennes – says that fixture will hold no fear for Wales.
"Obviously, they're the best players in the world at the end of the day, you can't really sugarcoat it," James said, as quoted by BBC Sport.
"They've got Champions League winners, they've got these kinds of things. I think we're always underdogs. We're used to it, so hopefully we can use that to benefit ourselves.
"You can't count us out. We've got a puncher's chance at the end of the day and we're going there to cause an upset."
Thursday's game will be Portugal's first under Jorge Jesus, who succeeded Roberto Martinez following their round-of-16 exit from the World Cup.
Jesus previously managed Ronaldo at Al-Nassr last season, with the five-time Ballon d'Or winner scoring 29 goals in 33 appearances under him, hitting the net once every 99 minutes on average.

Ronaldo opted against following Lionel Messi's example and retiring from international football following the World Cup, with the 41-year-old set to continue representing his country for the time being.
Asked about Ronaldo's quality, James said: "We're all trying to achieve the same thing, to be the best player in the world. But you get those aliens that don't seem human.

"You look at Messi, Neymar, Ronaldo – they've just got that extra little quality where, in big moments, they turn up and can do it again and again and again. I think that's the main thing. The longevity of how they're able to do it is unbelievable."

Wales missed out on the World Cup after losing on penalties to Bosnia-Herzegovina in a play-off semi-final in March, and their current four-match winless run (D3 L1) is both their worst under Bellamy and their worst start to a calendar year since 2012 (five straight losses).
5xpun2m97xi71abl4ti4mrx2n.html:
Wales have a "puncher's chance" of upsetting Portugal in their Nations League opener on Thursday, even if the Selecao can still call upon an "alien" in Cristiano Ronaldo. 

That is the view of midfielder Jordan James, as Craig Bellamy's side prepare for their League A campaign following promotion from the second tier in 2024-25.

Wales topped Group B4 in the last edition of the Nations League, ahead of Turkiye, Iceland and Montenegro, and their reward is a place in Group A4 this time around, with Portugal, Denmark and Norway. 

While Wales went unbeaten in the 2024-25 Nations League (W3 D3), their last campaign in the top tier saw them go winless and earn the fewest points of any nation (D1 L5).

Portugal are, of course, the reigning Nations League holders, having beaten Spain on penalties in the 2024-25 final to win the competition for the second time.

And ahead of Thursday's matchup at Sporting CP's Estadio Jose Alvalade, they have won 11 of their 14 home matches in the competition overall (D1 L2), only losing to France (in November 2020) and Spain (September 2022).

But James – who has helped Wolves make a strong start in the Championship after arriving in a loan-to-buy deal from Rennes – says that fixture will hold no fear for Wales.

"Obviously, they're the best players in the world at the end of the day, you can't really sugarcoat it," James said, as quoted by BBC Sport. 

"They've got Champions League winners, they've got these kinds of things. I think we're always underdogs. We're used to it, so hopefully we can use that to benefit ourselves.

"You can't count us out. We've got a puncher's chance at the end of the day and we're going there to cause an upset."

Thursday's game will be Portugal's first under Jorge Jesus, who succeeded Roberto Martinez following their round-of-16 exit from the World Cup.

Jesus previously managed Ronaldo at Al-Nassr last season, with the five-time Ballon d'Or winner scoring 29 goals in 33 appearances under him, hitting the net once every 99 minutes on average. 

Ronaldo opted against following Lionel Messi's example and retiring from international football following the World Cup, with the 41-year-old set to continue representing his country for the time being.

Asked about Ronaldo's quality, James said: "We're all trying to achieve the same thing, to be the best player in the world. But you get those aliens that don't seem human.

"You look at Messi, Neymar, Ronaldo – they've just got that extra little quality where, in big moments, they turn up and can do it again and again and again. I think that's the main thing. The longevity of how they're able to do it is unbelievable."

Wales missed out on the World Cup after losing on penalties to Bosnia-Herzegovina in a play-off semi-final in March, and their current four-match winless run (D3 L1) is both their worst under Bellamy and their worst start to a calendar year since 2012 (five straight losses).

607geboi7jtx1xo74xelclhr8.subtitle: Donyell Malen will not get the chance to extend his brilliant start to the season with the Netherlands, with injury ruling him out.
paragraphs: Donyell Malen has withdrawn from the Netherlands' squad for their upcoming Nations League matches.
Malen has been in red-hot form for Roma in Serie A so far this season, and despite playing the full 90 minutes against Inter on Saturday, he will not represent his country due to injury.
It has not been specified what Malen's issue is, but he is one of two withdrawals, with Justin Kluivert also pulling out.

Since his Serie A debut on January 18, Malen has scored 20 goals in 23 appearances, at least twice as many as any other player in the competition in that period (Tasos Douvikas and Lautaro Martinez are next with 10).
Across Europe's big five leagues, he has scored more than any other player (Harry Kane and Raphinha have 18).
Malen has already netted six goals in Serie A this term, more than any other player, over-performing his 4.6 expected goals (xG).
He has also had more shots on target (10) than any other player and currently boasts a 57.5 minutes per goal rate in the Italian top-flight.
Xavi Hernandez, who is taking charge of the Netherlands for the first time during this extended international break, has called up Guus Til and Mexx Meerdink as replacements.
The Netherlands face Germany in their opening Nations League match on September 24, before facing Serbia away and at home on either side of their clash with Greece.

          WSL Matchday 5: The Opta Stats That Defined the Weekend
        
      
                          
                      Oct 5, 2026
          
                      Louise Bawden / Author, Maya Shah / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Arsenal’s difficult start continued, Man City and Chelsea stayed unbeaten and London City delivered the result of the weekend . Using Opta data, we uncover the standout performances, emerging trends and biggest numbers from Matchday 5 of the 2026-27 WSL season.
After five matchdays, there have already been 111 goals scored in the WSL – the second-most at this stage of the season behind just the 2020-21 campaign (115).

The opening weeks have seen league positions swap and change, but we head into the international break with Manchester City setting the pace. They have a perfect 15 points from 15, with Chelsea two points behind on 13 and highly anticipated newcomers London City Lionesses making their presence felt in third on 12 points.

The real story of these opening weeks, though, has arguably been Arsenal’s alarming start. The Gunners head into the international break down in 10th, with just five points from five games and back-to-back defeats leaving Renée Slegers under mounting pressure.
But, as ever, the results only tell part of the story. We’ve dug into the Opta data to uncover the standout performances, emerging trends and remarkable numbers that defined Matchday 5.
Arsenal’s alarming start to the season hit a new low on Sunday as they threw away a lead to lose 4-2 to Manchester City.

Having gone ahead, the Gunners were beaten in a WSL match for the first time since February 2024 against West Ham, ending a 37-game unbeaten run when scoring first and underlining the fragility that has defined their campaign.
There have not been many bright sparks during Arsenal’s difficult start, but summer signing Lisa Baum has provided a glimpse of what could be to come if they can turn things around.
The last younger player to do so was Ebony Salmon in November 2020, aged 19 years and 285 days.
In finding the net, Baum also helped Arsenal carve out a unique piece of WSL history.

For City, it was a very different story. They came from behind twice to beat Arsenal, securing their first WSL victory over the Gunners after conceding first since December 2020. In the five such meetings between those victories, City failed to win, drawing one and losing four.
It was also the fastest substitute goal in the competition since Pernille Harder against Everton in May 2023 (62 seconds).

Her leveller against the Gunners also meant the Dutchwoman also became the first defender in City’s WSL history to come off the bench and score a goal that either levelled the match or put City ahead.
City head into the international break with a perfect record and a growing sense of inevitability that whatever position they find themselves in, they can find a way to win.

Against Arsenal, Jeglertz's side generated just 1.01 xG to Arsenal's' 1.61, finishing the match with a -0.60 xG differential. It was the second-largest negative xG differential City have overcome in a WSL victory, and their first league win despite being second best on xG since a 2-1 victory over Brighton in March 2025 (-0.22).

With just one place separating the sides at kick-off, London City Lionesses seized the opportunity to overtake Tottenham in emphatic fashion. Spurs had begun the season in impressive form and sat second heading into the weekend, but a stunning 6-1 victory saw Eder Maestre's side move above them in the table.

They wasted little time taking control. Alexia Putellas’ third-minute opener was London City’s fastest WSL goal, while it was the earliest Tottenham have conceded in the league under Martin Ho, and their earliest since facing Arsenal in November 2024.

It means that Putellas has won 130 of the last 131 league matches in which she has scored, so once the ball hit the back of the net in the third minute, history suggested Spurs were already in trouble.

Diani was joined on the scoresheet twice by Putellas, with the pair making a little piece of WSL history in the process. It was the first time a French international and a Spanish international have both scored 2+ goals in the same WSL match.
For Tottenham, the scale of the defeat was particularly remarkable given their form coming into the game.

          Celebrating 1,500 WSL Matches: Looking Back on the League's Most Statistically Significant Games
        
      
                          
                      Oct 3, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the 1,500th WSL game set to be played this weekend, we look back at some of the matches that hold statistical significance across the competition’s history.
This weekend will see the 1,500th game in English Women’s Super League history played when Manchester City host Arsenal in one of the most anticipated fixtures of the 2026-27 season.

Ahead of Matchday 5 of the campaign, there have been 1,493 matches played across 17 seasons of WSL action – including the 2017 Spring Series. With six games scheduled before Sunday's showdown at the Etihad Stadium, Manchester City and Arsenal will have the distinction of contesting the league's landmark 1,500th fixture.
To mark the occasion, we look back at some of the most memorable matches in WSL history and the statistics that made them stand out.
The first ever WSL fixture took place on 13 April 2011 with Chelsea hosting Arsenal at Imperial Fields, Mitcham.

Arsenal edged a 1-0 victory thanks to Gilly Flaherty's 35th-minute strike, though chances were at a premium throughout. The two sides combined for just 13 shots and five efforts on target, making it one of the least open contests of the campaign.
The win was one of 10 Arsenal recorded during the inaugural 2011 WSL season, as they went on to finish three points clear of Birmingham City and win the league's first title.
Arsenal are also the team to have secured the biggest margin of victory ever seen in WSL history (+10), as they thrashed Bristol City 11-1 at Meadow Park in December 2019 under Joe Montemurro.
Perhaps unsurprisingly, this is also the highest-scoring WSL fixture of all time (12).

The warning signs were there for Bristol City. Rooted to the foot of the table without a single win to their name, they travelled to face the reigning champions knowing they were up against one of the most dominant sides in the league.
What followed was a mismatch of historic proportions.

Ten of Arsenal’s goals were either scored (6) or assisted (4) by Vivianne Miedema, who set WSL records for the most goals, assists and goal involvements by a player in a single WSL match. Those records still stand, although Chelsea’s Guro Reiten equalled the Dutch forward’s single-game assist record with four against Leicester City on 3 December 2022.

Two WSL matches have featured as many as nine different goalscorers, excluding own goals: Chelsea's 9-0 victory over Bristol City in September 2020 and Brighton & Hove Albion's thrilling 7-3 win against the Robins in March 2024.

Chelsea’s first home game of 2020-21 was a treat for their fans at Kingsmeadow. The Blues ran riot, scoring nine times from as many different players. Millie Bright, Sam Kerr, Niamh Charles, Maren Mjelde, Fran Kirby, Melanie Leupolz, Erin Cuthbert, Pernille Harder and Bethany England all found the net in a historic display.

Three and a half years later, Brighton's 7-3 victory at Ashton Gate produced another game with nine different goalscorers. Of the 10 goals scored, only Elisabeth Terland (two) found the net more than once.

Katie Robinson, Madison Haley, Pauline Bremer, Tatiana Pinto and Vicky Losada were Brighton's other scorers, while Amalie Thestrup, Brooke Aspin and Megan Connolly found the net for Bristol City in defeat, making it one of the most entertaining and free-scoring matches in WSL history.
One other WSL record was set in a match between Chelsea and Bristol City, too.

Chelsea's 6-0 win over Manchester City in February 2019 remains the only WSL match to feature two hat-trick scorers. Bethany England and Fran Kirby shared the six goals between them, taking turns to find the net throughout the contest. Kirby scored Chelsea's first, third and fifth goals, while England struck the others.
Kirby scored another hat-trick in their next game, a 4-0 win over Liverpool, meaning two of her three hat-tricks in the competition came in back-to-back appearances.
Only Vivianne Miedema (five) and Khadija Shaw (eight) have recorded more WSL hat-tricks than Kirby and England, who remain tied on three apiece.
