          Cristiano Ronaldo and Portugal: An Avoidably Fractious End to One of International Football’s Greatest Careers?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 2, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Emily Millen / Design, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After leaving Portugal's training camp, it would seem Cristiano Ronaldo's international career has come to a tense end. It didn't need to be like this.
Cristiano Ronaldo was – surprisingly to some – philosophical, realistic about his standing in the Portuguese national team.

Following years of debate about whether Portugal were better off with or without him in the starting XI, their former talisman appeared to accept that his role under strong-willed new coach Jorge Jesus – whom he’d previously worked with at Al Nassr – might be somewhat diminished, on the pitch at least.

“If the coach decides the best thing for the team is for me to start on the bench, I’ll accept that perfectly,” he told RTP after starting last week’s 1-0 UEFA Nations League win over Wales. “I’m here to help the national team in whatever way is needed. If I don't get to play, that’s no problem either; the most important thing is for the team to win and for the group to be united.
“I’ve always said that the group is above any individual player and I am fully available to fulfil whatever role is assigned to me.”
Fast-forward a week and Portugal are embroiled in a Ronaldo-shaped crisis, with the world-record holder for men’s international caps unlikely to feature for his country again.

Despite being “fully available to fulfil whatever role is assigned to me”, Ronaldo didn’t appear to appreciate being an unused substitute during Sunday’s 2-1 win away to Norway. At full-time, he marched straight down the tunnel instead of joining his teammates in acknowledging the travelling Portugal supporters.

Then, everything came to a head on Wednesday. Ronaldo confirmed he’d left the Portuguese training camp following “a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation” regarding Jorge Jesus’ pre-match press conference ahead of Thursday’s clash with Denmark.

Ronaldo had, predictably, been a key topic in the press conference. While Jesus acknowledged he “made a mistake” asking Ronaldo to warm up for 30 minutes, also insisting reports of his captain refusing to train were wide of the mark, he made it abundantly clear who was calling the shots.
“I can say to any player that you’re starting on the bench,” he said. “If I need you for 30 minutes, you’re going to play; if I don’t need you, you’re not going to play.
“The way I was reading the game [against Norway], [Ronaldo] didn’t come on. Because it’s not Cristiano, just like it will never be any player that will change my ideas as the coach. Never.
“Not him, not anyone in football. Not him, not anyone, not any president. Never. Zero.”

Could Jesus have taken a softer approach? Perhaps, but there’s also a strong argument Portugal have required a coach with such a personality for a long time, someone with the conviction and bravery to make tough – maybe even controversial – decisions.

Fernando Santos had seemingly paved the way for Ronaldo to be phased out when he dropped the centre-forward for Portugal’s last-16 clash with Switzerland at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. His replacement, Gonçalo Ramos, scored a hat-trick in a 6-1 win.
But after losing to Morocco in the quarter-finals, Santos left his post and was ultimately succeeded by Roberto Martínez, under whom Ronaldo remained one of the first names on the team sheet.

He started nine of Portugal’s 10 Euro 2024 qualifying games and all five of their matches at the finals. Ronaldo was also in the line-up for five of their six qualifiers for the 2026 World Cup, plus all five of their outings at the tournament in North America as Portugal finished second in their group and made it only as far as the last 16.

Ronaldo did, in fairness, have a good goalscoring record under Martínez, but long before he was hired there’d been debates about whether the former Real Madrid and Manchester United forward offered enough to the wider team to justify starting so often. In a modern age where out-of-possession intensity and pressing are almost sacrosanct, deploying a player who contributes little to that is a luxury few teams can afford against the best opposition. And those who can must build a team capable of shouldering the extra workload, like Argentina did for many years, successfully, with Lionel Messi.
Against Spain at the 2026 World Cup, Ronaldo had just 19 touches in 90 minutes, and none of those came after the 80th minute despite the game being 0-0 until stoppage time.

A few days earlier, however, Martínez had withdrawn Ronaldo – much to his apparent displeasure – in the 81st minute against Croatia with the score 1-1. Ramos had been introduced a little earlier, but with Ronaldo out of the way, he became the focal point of the attack and scored a dramatic late winner to send Portugal through.

Who’s to say the outcome against Spain would have been any different had Ramos (or anyone else for that matter) started instead of Ronaldo, though it was peculiar he didn’t get on at all, even if Martínez was reserving him for 30 minutes of extra-time that never materialised as Spain scored a late winner. It felt like the Portugal coach failed to heed a valuable lesson from the Croatia game.

6xyp8t0o0jmn1u6k76r836lkm.title: De Ketelaere reveals talks were held with PSG over summer transfer
6xyp8t0o0jmn1u6k76r836lkm.subtitle: Charles De Ketelaere was of reported interest to Paris Saint-Germain this summer, but he said a move from Atalanta failed to materialise.
paragraphs: Charles De Ketelaere revealed he came close to joining Paris Saint-Germain from Atalanta this summer, but the Ligue 1 champions instead chose to sign Ferran Torres.
De Ketelaere joined Atalanta from AC Milan permanently two years ago following a productive loan spell in 2023-24, when he scored 14 goals in 50 outings in all competitions.
Since his initial loan spell with Atalanta, only Nicolo Barella (251) and Federico Dimarco (283) have created more chances than De Ketelaere's 244 among Serie A players.

The Belgium international has amassed 63 goal contributions in that time (32 goals, 31 assists). Only Christian Pulisic (68), Marcus Thuram (75) and Lautaro Martinez (90) have managed more, with De Ketelaere's performances attracting interest.

PSG were credited with an interest in De Ketelaere this summer as they reshaped their attack, with Goncalo Ramos, Bradley Barcola, Ibrahim Mbaye, Randal Kolo Muani and Kang-in Lee all departing the Parisiens.
Atlanta named a price of €50m for De Ketelaere, but PSG were unwilling to match that valuation, instead choosing to sign Ferran from Barcelona for a reported €48.5m fee.
"Yes, I think it was around that amount," De Ketelaere confirmed. "But, we have to find a team that is willing to spend that amount.
"Several teams could do it in the Premier League, but it didn't happen. I spoke to PSG, but in the end they chose Ferran Torres.
"I'm happy at Atalanta, I know how important it is to play regularly as a starter following my time with Milan.
"I'd like to fight for titles one day. I have that ambition, but I'm only 25 and still have time."
De Ketelaere is yet to score for Atalanta in his six outings across all competitions in 2026-27, with Maurizio Sarri's side sitting 11th in Serie A heading into the international break.
He did, however, provide an assist during Belgium's 2-0 win over Italy in the Nations League on Friday, teeing up Dodi Lukebakio's 69th-minute winner at the Stadio Olimpico.

In what was Mark van Bommel's first game in charge of the Red Devils, only Kevin De Bruyne (five) created more chances than De Ketelaere (four), while the Atalanta midfielder also finished with team-high totals for successful dribbles (two), duels won (eight) and aerial duels won (two).
Belgium's Nations League campaign continues on Monday against France, with a clash against Turkiye to come before they face Zinedine Zidane's side again on October 5.

6z63q8jbc4gh1iufjqn29hn5j.title: Amorim: Milan still far from our potential
6z63q8jbc4gh1iufjqn29hn5j.subtitle: AC Milan are unbeaten in Serie A under Ruben Amorim, but the Portuguese coach knows there are still plenty of things to improve upon.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim believes AC Milan are "still far from our potential" despite making an unbeaten start to their Serie A campaign.
Milan have won three of their opening five league games in 2026-27 (D2), leaving them fifth in Serie A, two points behind leaders Roma.

Amorim (W3 D2) is only the third foreign manager in Milan's history to remain unbeaten in each of his first five Serie A games in charge, after Luis Carniglia (W3 D2) and Nils Liedholm (W4 D1), both in 1963-64.
Overall, he is the first Rossoneri manager to achieve this since Massimo Giacomini (W2 D3) in 1979-80.
However, Milan made a losing start to their Europa League campaign after a 2-0 defeat at home to Benfica.
Amorim acknowledged there are plenty of improvements needed when his squad return from the international break.
"We try to dominate the games consistently; we play well at times, but there's still a lot of work to do," Amorim told Sky Sport Italia.
"I don't like to hear people talk about this Milan as Amorim’s Milan. Milan is Milan.
"The club has a story and an identity that go beyond a coach’s name. I want to see a team with an identity that can win even when things don’t run perfectly.
"We are still far from our potential, but we need time and continuity. We have many games, we must win and improve at the same time, it's not easy.
"Many things are missing; I can say it without any problem. I think we have to improve as a team to create more chances."
Milan face Sassuolo in their first Serie A game after the extended international break before taking on Salzburg in the Europa League.

7f7vw8sd056e14cgu0lejgtqu.title: Mac Allister says 'no firm decision' over Liverpool future amid contract dispute
7f7vw8sd056e14cgu0lejgtqu.subtitle: Alexis Mac Allister recently said he had opportunities to leave Liverpool during the summer transfer window, with no new contract on offer.
paragraphs: Alexis Mac Allister says there is still "no firm decision" on his future with Liverpool, with the Reds yet to offer the midfielder a new contract.
Earlier this month, Mac Allister made headlines by saying Liverpool had informed him they were not in a position to offer him fresh terms, after he entered the final two years of his deal.

Mac Allister, who has won a Premier League title and the EFL Cup since arriving from Brighton in 2023, said he was "very sad" to have had no negotiations with the club, after his fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai penned new deals.
Mac Allister has retained a key role for Liverpool since Andoni Iraola took charge, making seven appearances in all competitions this season with five of those being starts.

The 27-year-old has now linked up with Argentina for a series of friendlies against Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Benin, the latter of which will serve as a farewell match for Lionel Messi after he announced his international retirement.
And in an interview with ESPN, Mac Allister said there had been no progress on resolving his contract stand-off.
"There's no firm decision yet. I still have two years left on my contract. As I said, I'm going to give it my all. A lot can happen in that time; there are plenty of options," Mac Allister said.
"Hopefully it'll be for more years, but if it's just two, I'll have to enjoy them with my family, because I have no doubt that I'm at one of the best clubs in the world."

The nature of Messi's involvement in the game against Benin – set for October 5 at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires – remains unclear, but it will bring the curtain down on one of the all-time great international careers.
Messi has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for La Albiceleste, with eight of those coming at the 2026 World Cup.

No player has directly contributed to more goals at the World Cup on record (since 1966) than Messi (33 – 21 goals and 12 assists), who has also featured in the most games at the finals (34). Messi's 12 assists at FIFA's flagship competition are also the most of any player, four more than the great Diego Maradona (eight, since 1966).
And though he fell narrowly short of delivering a second straight title in North America this year, Mac Allister feels Messi should be in contention for a record-extending ninth Ballon d'Or.
"Obviously, as Argentines we'd love for Messi to win it. He had an incredible World Cup and I don't see why he shouldn't be awarded it," he said.

"Also, it's understood that these days the numbers play a big part – something that didn't carry as much weight in the past – and you don't know exactly what people are voting for either. But everyone in the running is a great player; anyone who comes close will deserve it.
"We all know that Leo has always prioritised the team over individual achievements, so it wouldn't be a big deal for him."

7hm5xdmmefsy13b5vntbu54rb.title: Quill backs Dallas to 'be better' than in Austin draw
7hm5xdmmefsy13b5vntbu54rb.subtitle: Both FC Dallas and Los Angeles FC are looking to get back to winning ways after draws last time out, with hopes of climbing the table.
paragraphs: FC Dallas head coach Eric Quill is confident his team will "be better" than their last performance when they host Los Angeles FC in MLS on Saturday.
Dallas head into the match on the back of a five-match unbeaten streak, but after three straight wins, they were held to a 0-0 draw by Austin FC last time out.
It was just the seventh time this season they have been shut out – as they are the second-highest scorers in the Western Conference.
They currently sit fourth in the West, but are one of three teams on 44 points, and they know a win could help them close the gap to the leaders Vancouver Whitecaps.
Quill is looking for a big improvement from the performance against Austin, especially in the final third.
"It wasn't our typical game," Quill said of the draw with Austin. "I think everybody's used to four goals from us, so it wasn't there.
"But it wasn't for a lack of trying or a lack of opportunities that we created.
"We'll work in front of goal, get our confidence up and go into LAFC ready.
"[The players were] down because ties don't excite us, but there's plenty more football to come from us, and we're going to be better for this game."
LAFC, meanwhile, are sixth in the West, three points behind Dallas after failing to win their last two matches.
Following a shock 3-1 loss to Sporting Kansas City, they threw away a lead against the San Jose Earthquakes, conceding a 98th-minute equaliser.
Son Heung-min and Denis Bouanga both scored in that game but are among the list of absentees due to international duty. Head coach Marc Dos Santos is not making any excuses, though.
"We never approach the week crying about who's not here," he said.
"We have seven players out, but we embrace from day one of preparing as best as we can for the Dallas game with everybody that is here."
FC Dallas – Joaquin Valiente
Joaquin Valiente has recorded 11 assists for Dallas this season, the first player to have double-digit assists in a single season for the club since Michael Barrios had 15 in 2019.

Over the last 15 seasons, four Dallas players have had 10+ assists in a season and all hail from South American countries (Valiente – Uruguay, Barrios – Colombia, Maximiliano Urruti and Mauro Diaz – Argentina).
Los Angeles FC – Mathieu Choiniere
Son and Bouanga are both on international duty and will miss the match have combined to score half of LAFC's regular-season goals (20/40 excl. own goals) in 2026.

With David Martinez (six goals) also departing in September, that means Mathieu Choiniere is the club's next highest scorer with two goals, but he did not manage a single shot against San Jose and only had one touch in the opposition box.
MATCH PREDICTION: FC DALLAS WIN
Dallas have won four of their 15 regular-season meetings with Los Angeles FC (D3 L8), with all four of those wins coming at home.
They have lost just once (W4 D2) at home to LAFC, conceding multiple goals only once, while scoring two or more goals five times.

Dallas have also scored two or more goals in seven of their last 10 home games, and four of their last five. Since the start of the 2024 season, they have registered two or more goals in 29 home games, with only Inter Miami (37) having more in that time.

LAFC surrendered a late goal to San Jose for their fourth draw in their last six road games (L2). They have now drawn six road games this regular season and 13 total over the last two seasons combined after drawing 12 total road regular-season matches from 2022-24.
Los Angeles FC – 29.1%

7vg9y74erar31ej3v2zweeuo4.title: Germany 0-1 Greece: Kourbelis spoils Klopp's home debut
7vg9y74erar31ej3v2zweeuo4.subtitle: Germany remained without a win under Jurgen Klopp and in the Nations League as Dimitrios Kourbelis proved to be the hero for Greece.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp's wait for a first win in charge of Germany continued on Sunday as Dimitrios Kourbelis' second-half goal earned Greece a famous 1-0 victory in the Nations League.
Klopp was denied by Cody Gakpo's stoppage-time equaliser against the Netherlands in their Nations League opener, and his home debut at WWK Arena ended in a shock defeat.
Germany are third in Group A2 having taken just one point from their opening two games, with a home game against Serbia, who are also without a win, up next this Thursday.
It took until the 25th minute for Germany to carve out their first clear-cut opportunity, but Younes Ebnoutalib was unable to steer Kevin Schade's dangerous delivery on target.

Karim Adeyemi then fired over after being set free by Joshua Kimmich, with the Barcelona forward then forcing Konstantinos Tzolakis into making his first save of the match minutes later with a curling left-footed strike that was pushed behind.

The hosts' dominance continued after the break, with Bambase Conte dispossessing Christos Zafeiris and seeing his shot saved by Tzolakis, with the Greece goalkeeper then on hand to keep out Ebnoutalib and Kimmich's free-kick.

Greece came within inches of taking the lead against the run of play in the 67th minute through Fotis Ioannidis. Kimmich lost possession to Vangelis Pavlidis, who sent through Ioannidis, but his first-time attempt whistled past the left post.

But the visitors took the lead in the 74th minute when Christos Tzolis' deflected cross fell kindly to Kourbelis on the edge of the box. He skipped around Felix Nmecha before firing an effort at goal that took a knick off Kimmich on its way into the net.

Serge Gnabry attempted to get his team back into the match, but his shot was held by Tzolakis, with Germany's possession yielding little in the shape of chances as Greece held on to go top of Group A2 with six points from their first two games.
Plenty to ponder for Klopp

Ahead of sitting in the Germany dugout for the first time against the Netherlands, Klopp refused to make any promises of silverware and instant success during his time in charge, and this result proves there is still plenty of work for the former Liverpool boss to do.

Klopp made five changes to his team, and they were perhaps unfortunate not to find themselves in front after wasting a string of glorious chances, and their profligacy in front of goal was punished in the second half by Kourbelis.

Germany's dominance with the ball was backed up by the metrics, too. Thanasis Androutsos had the most accurate passes of any Greece's outfield players that started the match with just 21, with the hosts also ending the contest with 75.5% possession.

But the statistic that matters is the scoreline, and Greece will be delighted with their victory. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 0.77 from their eight shots, scoring with the only one they had on target, compared to Germany's tally of 1.34 from their 16 attempts.

867tayfi2f0r1ccqj3oifli5s.title: Jansen insists NYCFC 'will deal with' international absentees
867tayfi2f0r1ccqj3oifli5s.subtitle: Both New York City FC and Atlanta United will be without key players for their MLS clash at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Saturday.
paragraphs: Pascal Jansen expressed his disappointment in losing New York City FC players to the international break, but insists they "will deal with it" ahead of their trip to Atlanta United.
NYCFC are 10th in the Eastern Conference with just one MLS win since the Leagues Cup break after losing to rivals New York Red Bulls last time out.
Jansen will now be without goalkeeper Matt Freese against Atlanta, as well as defender Tayvon Gray and midfielder Aiden O'Neill, among a group of five players on international duty.
Jansen admitted some adjustments will be needed when they face Atlanta, but he is eager to pick up three points at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
"That's something that still amazes me in this league, that we have to play during a national team break," said the NYCFC boss.
"But it is what it is and we will deal with it. Unfortunately, we're coming off a tough game against Red Bull [a 1-0 loss]. I think we deserved more from that game.

"But now it's all full focus on Atlanta and we know we have a chance there, but we have to adjust a couple of things because there’s a few guys not available and this time not because of injury, because of international duty."
Atlanta, meanwhile, ended a four-game winless run in MLS with a 1-0 win over the Portland Timbers last time out.
The Five Stripes will also be missing key players against NYCFC, with Miguel Almiron and Aleksey Miranchuk both on international duty.

Since the start of last season, Miranchuk has recorded 95 chances created while Almiron has 87. They are the only pair of teammates to each create 80 or more chances since the start of the 2025 campaign, with both players setting up at least 40 shots for team-mates in each of the last two seasons.
Atlanta United – Matt Edwards
Due to players on international duty, Matt Edwards could start in defence for Atlanta.
After coming off the bench against Portland last time out, Edwards led his team-mates in interceptions (three) and aerial duels won (two), while winning five of his 10 duels overall.
New York City FC – Nicolas Fernandez Mercau

          Man City's Resilience, Lyon Dominate, Questions for Chelsea & Arsenal: UWCL Matchday 1 Lessons
        
      
                          
                      Sep 24, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Yash Thakur / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Matchday 1 of the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League delivered drama, dominant displays and plenty of talking points. We dive into the data to analyse the key stories from the action.
The 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League is underway and Matchday 1 delivered a little bit of everything.
There were narrow wins, thrashings and end-to-end contests as Europe's elite began their quest for continental glory.
Using Opta data, we break down the standout performers and biggest talking points from the opening matchday of this season's UWCL.
The reigning WSL champions began their UWCL campaign with one of the toughest assignments possible, travelling to Munich to face a Bayern side ranked second in the Opta Power Rankings.
The contest delivered everything expected of two European heavyweights: goals, a missed penalty and late drama, with the points ultimately shared in a 2-2 draw.
In doing so, City became the first English side to avoid defeat at Bayern Munich in the UWCL.

It was the first time in City’s history in the competition they had avoided defeat when trailing by two or more goals, while it was just the second time Bayern had failed to win a UWCL game in which they had led by 2+ goals, last doing so against Roma in November 2023.
José Barcala's team asserted themselves early, racing into a two-goal lead before the break. Their aggressive pressing forced City into mistakes, with Bayern recording 16 high turnovers.
Since 2019-20, only against Barcelona in December 2024 (25) and March 2021 (17) have City conceded more high turnovers in the competition.
City struggled to gain a foothold before half-time, managing only three attempts. But Beth Mead's goal shifted the momentum after the interval.

The visitors were then handed a golden opportunity to level from the penalty spot, only forEna Mahmutovic to brilliantly deny Khadija Shaw. It was the first penalty Shaw has missed since joining Manchester City.

Despite that setback, City continued to push and their persistence was rewarded in the 86th minute when Carlotta Wamser found the equaliser to complete the comeback with her first goal in light blue, and secure a valuable point on the road.
Andrée Jeglertz's influence from the bench again proved significant, as had been the case against Liverpool.

Second-half substitute Laura Blindkilde Brown provided the assist for Wamser's goal and helped City gain greater control in possession, offering composure against Bayern's intense press as the visitors finished the stronger of the two sides.
Arsenal and Chelsea both opened their European campaigns with 1-0 victories against HB Køge and Austria Wien respectively, but neither performance fully convinced.
With a heavyweight WSL meeting at Stamford Bridge looming this weekend, both sides left MD1 with three points, but just as many questions remain.
Arsenal needed a stoppage-time Mariona Caldentey penalty to overcome Danish champions Køge in a game they largely controlled but struggled to break open.
Renée Slegers' side monopolised possession, recording 69.7% of the ball and completing 620 passes at an 86% success rate, but their dominance rarely translated into clear-cut opportunities.

Despite attempting 19 shots, Arsenal generated only one big chance and managed just a single effort on target prior to Caldentey's winning penalty. It was another example of a recurring issue for the Gunners: controlling games without creating enough high-quality chances.

8aqj1c1phdxczwjolw9tv6cf.title: Bayern Munich 2-2 Manchester City: Wamser rescues draw in Women's Champions League opener
8aqj1c1phdxczwjolw9tv6cf.subtitle: Bayern Munich led 2-0 against Manchester City, but the Women's Super League champions fought back to salvage a point at Uhlsport Park.
paragraphs: Khadija Shaw missed a penalty but Carlotta Wamser's late goal saw Manchester City rescue a 2-2 draw in their Women's Champions League opener against Bayern Munich.
Bayern, last season's semi-finalists, charged into a 2-0 lead inside the first 28 minutes at Uhlsport Park.
Giulia Gwinn was played in by Linda Dallmann and made no mistake with a crisp, powerful finish.

Bayern were then in cruise control when they capitalised on a defensive mix-up from Man City, with Pernille Harder's cross causing havoc, and Kerstin Casparij was only able to turn it into her own net.
Yet, on the cusp of half-time, Beth Mead dragged City back into the contest as Casparij's cross found its way through to her, and she duly tucked home.
City looked all set to draw level around the hour mark, after Aoba Fujino was brought down by Ena Mahmutovic in Bayern's box.
Shaw, though, showed unusual profligacy as she saw her attempt saved by Mahmutovic, who atoned for her mistake.
Yet City did get their equaliser in the 86th minute, with Wamser whipping a fine effort in at the near post after she met Laura Blindkilde Brown's tee-up.
Man City show powers of recovery
City have made a fantastic start to their Women's Super League title defence, winning all three of their matches so far, but they endured a miserable opening half-an-hour of their European campaign.
This was their first meeting against Bayern, or indeed any German team, in this competition, although City should probably have expected their hosts to make a fast start.
After all, Bayern had won seven of their previous 11 Champions League matches against English teams, including both legs of last season's quarter-final against Manchester United (3-2 A, 2-1 H).
Harder is just one off scoring her 50th Women's Champions League goal. She is aiming to become only the third player to reach this milestone, after Ada Hegerberg (69) and Eugenie Le Sommer (50).
And though Harder did not score, she was a threat throughout, and she laid on two great chances late on for Edna Imade, who could have done better with her finishes.
As it was, Andree Jeglertz will at least be able to reflect on a spirited City comeback, and they rounded out with a fairly even stat sheet.

Bayern created chances worth 2.03 expected goals from 15 shots, while City had opportunities worth a combined 2.31 xG from just eight attempts. Room for improvement, but definitely a decent showing in attack.

8nw3v3yjb9ns1u5qpusbsjcz1.title: Real Madrid struggle inevitable after Kroos retirement, claims former assistant Ancelotti
8nw3v3yjb9ns1u5qpusbsjcz1.subtitle: Real Madrid have not won silverware across the past two seasons, and Davide Ancelotti feels Toni Kroos' retirement is the reason why.
paragraphs: Davide Ancelotti believes Real Madrid's struggles in recent seasons have stemmed from the retirement of midfielder Toni Kroos.
Kroos spent 10 seasons with Madrid after joining from Bayern Munich, winning four LaLiga titles and five Champions Leagues among 22 trophies during his time in the Spanish capital.
He made 465 appearances for Los Blancos, scoring 28 goals and providing 93 assists while forming a formidable midfield partnership with Luka Modric and Casemiro.
Madrid have failed to win any major silverware across the last two seasons under Carlo Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa, with Jose Mourinho now at the helm to try and change things.
Lille boss Davide Ancelotti, who formerly served as Madrid's assistant, insisted trying to replace someone like Kroos would be a mistake for Los Blancos.
"I don't want everything I say about Madrid to be interpreted as criticism, but when Modric or Kroos were there, every movement into space was followed by a ball arriving there," he told AS.
"I'm not saying that the footballers they have now don't have that ability. What I'm saying is that, to play vertically, you need someone who knows how to deliver the ball.
"Being vertical doesn't mean having eight runners. It also means having someone who can launch them. It's a style of play.
"You lose something that you will never get back. The best player in the world in his position. You can’t say, 'I need another Kroos,' because there isn’t another one.
"He was the owner of the match. He controlled the tempo. The game was played at the rhythm he wanted. He decided things, and he was fundamental because he managed the pace of the match.
"Inevitably, for the way Real Madrid played, losing Toni was extremely difficult. Suddenly, they lost so many things."

8r4cscg9vsoe11iz2zvr06c76.title: Tuchel: England have a plan for Spain
8r4cscg9vsoe11iz2zvr06c76.subtitle: England begin their Nations League campaign against world champions Spain, and Thomas Tuchel is determined to start with three points.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel revealed England "have a plan" to defeat Spain in their Nations League opener on Saturday.
The Three Lions host the world champions at Wembley Stadium in both of their first matches since the World Cup in the summer.

Spain lifted the trophy for the second time in their history after defeating Argentina 1-0 in the final, while England beat France 6-4 in the third-place play-off – their best finish at the tournament since 1966.
Luis de la Fuente's side are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest-ever such streak by a European nation.
Tuchel conceded England will have their work cut out against Spain and believes La Roja's possession-based style is a disadvantage for his side.
"I think it is an advantage in general. Not only against us, but against everyone," said Tuchel.
"This is how they play. I think they rely on that. This is how they train and they were brought up. This is clearly part of them.
"But at the moment, I think the more you analyse Spain and their last matches they played in, you have to admire the way in which they defend. They added this to their game.
"It is so difficult for every single team in the world to create chances against them. We have a plan, and we have ambition, and we want to prove the opposite.
"We want to be the exception to the rule, but at the moment they are a very complete team."

England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2); those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).
Spain have also won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the final of the 2024 European Championship.
England winger Anthony Gordon previously stated the Three Lions must play to their own strengths, but captain Harry Kane believes they can mirror Spain's style if needed.

"I get what he's saying," Kane said about Gordon's comments. "It's culture for Spain, playing a certain style from five, six or seven years old until they're professionals. In England, it's not so much like that.
"It doesn't mean we can't play under pressure or keep the ball. We still have a lot of amazing technical players – but we have a lot of strengths that they don't have; physicality, pace and power.
"They way we press and win duels, a lot of Premier League style football in a way.
"I think at our best we combine both. We're not just a team that play like Spain, but we have a lot of strengths that we can showcase."

8udkrq0y8no1fnmxnu6yujk8.title: Gordon: 'I've been dying to play with Trent for England'
8udkrq0y8no1fnmxnu6yujk8.subtitle: Trent Alexander-Arnold marked his England return with an assist against Czechia, and Anthony Gordon enjoyed playing alongside him.
paragraphs: Anthony Gordon said he had been "dying" to play with Trent Alexander-Arnold for England, after the duo combined to great effect in Tuesday's Nations League win over Czechia.
The Three Lions bounced back from their 3-2 defeat to Spain with a 2-0 victory in Prague, with Gordon and Harry Kane on target following Pavel Sulc's red card.
Gordon's goal – which was the first he has scored with his head for his country – took him to eight goal involvements in his last nine appearances for England (four goals, four assists).
Gordon was also on target against Spain on Saturday, and he is just the second Barcelona player to score in back-to-back games for England, after Gary Lineker in 1989.

He was picked out superbly by Alexander-Arnold's deep delivery to the far post, with the Real Madrid full-back winning his first cap in over a year, having been omitted from Thomas Tuchel's squads throughout last season and for the World Cup.
Alexander-Arnold's assist was his first for England since September 2024, against Finland in the last edition of the Nations League, under Lee Carsley.

"I make that run time and time again and only a certain number of players have that ability, technique and bravery to be willing to make the mistake trying that pass," Gordon said of Alexander-Arnold, talking to ITV Sport after the game.
"That's why he's so good and I've been dying to play with him for that reason.
"He's had his own journey with England. He would've liked to have played more than he has, but he's been a great character during this camp, I've really enjoyed being around him."
When those comments were put to Alexander-Arnold, he replied: "It's a great compliment, and he's great to play with.
"I spoke to Ant at half-time and said, 'if I'm getting into those spaces, make sure you get to the back post'. You don't expect to get it that fast, but we did and it worked.
"I try to get the ball and try and see what the best play is, to try and play forward and create something, and I was able to make that pass.
"When they go down to 10 men there's more pressure on us to win the game, but actually it makes it more difficult, they get very compact and defend.
"It was very hard to break them down, but we got that early on in the second half, which is what we needed."
Reflecting on his time out of the England setup, Alexander-Arnold – who has won on 20 of his 27 international starts – added: "It's always an honour to represent my country.
"It's been a long time, but I've always believed I can play for England. It was about proving it at club level. The manager gave me a chance, and hopefully he is happy with how I played."
The Three Lions visit Croatia for their third Nations League game on Saturday, before Czechia visit Wembley to round off this international break next Tuesday.

Reflecting on his time out of the England setup, Alexander-Arnold – who has won on 20 of his 27 international starts – added: "It's always an honour to represent my country. 

"It's been a long time, but I've always believed I can play for England. It was about proving it at club level. The manager gave me a chance, and hopefully he is happy with how I played."

The Three Lions visit Croatia for their third Nations League game on Saturday, before Czechia visit Wembley to round off this international break next Tuesday.

          What Did We Learn From Jürgen Klopp’s First Game Back in Management?
        
      
                          
                      Sep 25, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After over two years away from the dugout, Jürgen Klopp returned to the touchline on Thursday as Germany boss. How did it go, and were there signs that he can revive Die Nationalelf?
For a long time, Jürgen Klopp insisted he may never return to football management.

The 59-year-old left Liverpool in May 2024 after admitting he was “running out of energy” following nine years at Anfield. After a break from the game altogether, he returned with Red Bull as its head of global soccer, overseeing the running of their various teams around the world.
The managerial bug can be infectious, though, and following Germany’s disappointing 2026 World Cup and the departure of Julian Nagelsmann, Klopp was asked to come to the rescue.
On Thursday, he took charge of his first game since May 2024 as Germany travelled to face old rivals the Netherlands in their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League opener.

Expectations were high. Klopp leading the German national team always felt like it would happen eventually, and there is optimism the former Mainz and Borussia Dortmund boss can have the same revolutionary impact he had at all three clubs he’s managed.

As mentioned, Germany had a poor World Cup this summer. They started by thrashing Curaçao 7-1, though they needed a late winner to overcome Ivory Coast after that, before losing 2-1 to Ecuador in their final group game.
That was not ideal preparation for a tough last-32 clash with Paraguay, and so it proved. Germany struggled with their opponents’ physical approach and were ultimately eliminated on penalties.
Klopp signed a four-year deal to take over from Nagelsmann, overseeing the Euro 2028 and 2030 World Cup campaigns. His primary challenge is the Nations League, though, and it was a big test first up.

Not only was he taking on the Netherlands in Amsterdam, complete with their own new gaffer in Xavi Hernández – also managing his first game since May 2024 after leaving Barcelona – but he was set to face three of his former Liverpool players. Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Cody Gakpo all started for the Dutch, and one of them went on to deny his old boss a debut victory.

Klopp took the unusual step of naming a 44-man squad, with Augsburg goalkeeper Finn Dahmen the only player set to be present for all four Nations League games in this international window. One group of players will be available for the first two (vs Netherlands and Greece) and then others will join up for the last two (vs Serbia and Greece).

The move was met with general approval in Germany, allowing Klopp to look at many players, introduce new and exciting faces, and also protect players from too much football across the elongated international break.

That doesn’t entirely eradicate the risk of injury, though, and that was apparent when Jamal Musiala pulled up in the warm-up in Amsterdam. On top of that, Kai Havertz could only play the first half hour after being on the receiving end of a nasty challenge by Quinten Timber, the brother of Havertz’s Arsenal teammate Jurriën.

An early scare came from one of Klopp’s former charges, with Van Dijk converting a Tijjani Reijnders corner, only for the goal to be ruled out after a VAR check judged Brian Brobbey to have fouled Marc-André ter Stegen.
There was some familiarity in the first XI Klopp named as Germany manager. Joshua Kimmich was handed his 115th cap, taking him past Toni Kroos (114) and into seventh place outright.

There was also a new face in the side, with Freiburg right-back Philipp Treu earning his first cap, and he played a key role in the first goal of the Klopp era. Treu’s low cross into the Dutch box from the right was blocked by the sliding Jan Paul van Hecke, but the loose ball fell kindly for Felix Nmecha, who finished calmly. It was somewhat appropriate that a Dortmund player scored the first goal under Klopp, given the outstanding success he had with BVB between 2008 and 2015.

It wasn’t without some controversy. Brobbey was down hurt on the turf at the time and Germany played on while Dutch players were imploring them to kick it out. Ultimately, it was at the referee’s discretion and despite some disagreements between Denzel Dumfries and Kimmich, Klopp’s side were well within their rights to play on, and it was 1-0.

It was familiar shape from Klopp’s side. Havertz was the striker but dropped deep – indeed, Nadiem Amiri had a more advanced average position in the first 30 minutes – while the two full-backs got forward with regularity. The wide forwards, Karim Adeyemi and Kevin Schade, were the two most-advanced German players in that first half hour before Havertz was forced off.

Another new face, Younes Ebnoutalib, replaced Havertz, and if anything, Germany looked even better with the Eintracht Frankfurt man up top. It wasn’t entirely polished but there was energy, there was effort, and there was counter pressing so synonymous with Klopp.
After the game, Treu told RTL: “We wanted to press them from the front, put them under pressure, be difficult to play against and play with intensity.

          How Problematic is Manchester City’s Leaky Defence?
        
      
                          
                      Sep 23, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester City are top of the Premier League with a perfect record of five wins from five, but they haven’t been entirely convincing at the back. Is there any cause for concern?

Enzo Maresca’s comments after watching his Manchester City side’s rollercoaster victory over Sunderland on Sunday afternoon sparked an interesting philosophical debate. Rather than lean towards the are-you-not-entertained ethos of an Ange Postecoglou, Maresca intimated he would like to see rather more control from his team, and a little less excitement than they provided in this win.

The Italian may well prefer to watch a game with lots of goals, but he was likely stating this preference on this particular occasion because the chaos of City’s win, in which they needed to retake the lead three times in the first half alone – something that has only happened six times in Premier League history to any team – was not exactly the mark of champions. As the scoreline suggests, City allowed their opponents far too many opportunities to score.

Sunderland are a very good team but not one that routinely creates a lot of chances. On this occasion, away to title hopefuls, they had chances worth 3.57 expected goals, which is by far their highest since their return to the Premier League last year.

In fact, in 43 games since the start of last season, they’ve only managed more than 2.0 xG twice, with their previous best being 2.44 vs Newcastle in March. They’ve had under 1.0 xG in more than half (22) of their matches.

But they carved City open time and again. Brian Brobbey scored a hat-trick of what were essentially tap-ins, allowed into areas where he could not miss, time and time again. And at 4-3, Sunderland came within a Rúben Dias goal-line clearance of equalising again.

While match-going fans got their money’s worth and neutrals were thoroughly entertained, even though City won and kept up the only remaining 100% record in the Premier League, it's understandable that Maresca came away a little dismayed at his side’s defensive display.
“It’s much better to win games,” he said. “In this moment, it’s better to have three points more than less, no doubt. We scored five. We could have scored probably more goals.
“So that means that we created enough, but at the same time we need to avoid conceding goals like today. We had four clean sheets in a row and today we conceded three goals.”

It is a fact that City had kept four successive clean sheets before the Sunderland game, but it was slightly disingenuous of Maresca to try and reframe their form that way. That run included the midweek win over Championship side Norwich in the EFL Cup and a 1-0 win at home to newly-promoted Coventry, who caused City all manner of problems and could quite feasibly have scored three goals, let alone one.

Credit where it’s due: City were mightily impressive defensively in their 1-0 win at Manchester United, keeping their rivals at arm’s length despite playing most of the derby with 10 men. But across that four-game run of clean sheets, they conceded chances worth 2.82 xG. So, in other words, they could reasonably have been expected to concede three goals.
They do have Gianluigi Donnarumma in goal, so perhaps they just felt confident that they could rely on one of the best shot-stoppers and most commanding goalkeepers of his generation.

But the evidence from the Sunderland game suggests that is not a reliable method of defence. Sunderland’s 3.57 xG is the third highest ever by a team that went on to lose a Premier League game since xG data is available (2013-14). On another day, Sunderland would have won that match, just like United will feel aggrieved not to have won the derby, and Coventry were left rueing missed chances against City.
On the opening weekend of the season, too, City required 84th- and 91st-minute goals to come from behind and rescue a win at home to Bournemouth.

In other words, their ‘perfect’ record of five wins from five has been rather less convincing than it might appear from a quick glance at the league table. They are clearly feeling the loss of Rodri from the base of their midfield.

They have, though, still won each game, which is something no other team can say. They are able to rely on the goalscoring of perennial golden-boot winner and early leader in the top-scorers’ stakes, Erling Haaland (five goals).

Rayan Cherki (three goals, two assists) and Antoine Semenyo (two goals, three assists) have started the season very well, too, while Enzo Fernández (one goal) provides further attacking threat from the double pivot. Iliman Ndiaye looks to have settled well following his summer move from Everton, and Phil Foden (two assists) is another exceptional attacker when he’s not kicking Bruno Fernandes in the you-know-wheres.

But is their arguably unrivalled attack enough? Can they rely on being bailed out often enough to win the title? “Attack wins you games, defence wins you titles,” as goes the famous Sir Alex Ferguson quote. If that’s true, then City might have something to worry about.

Indeed, only Brighton (who have played two halves of football against 10 men) have scored more goals (16) in the Premier League this season than City (13), but six teams have conceded fewer than them (5). Those teams are Leeds, Everton, Brentford, Hull and, perhaps crucially, likely title rivals Arsenal and Liverpool.

“There’s no way Manchester City win the league,” Sky Sports pundit Paul Merson said after the Sunderland game. “Going forward, [they] were good but at the back they were all over the place. [That] catches up with you.”

          Winning Starts and WSL Titles: Are Manchester City on Course to Retain Their Crown in 2026-27?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 6, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Reigning WSL champions Manchester City are the only team with a 100% record after five matchdays of the 2026-27 season. Is there any stopping Andrée Jeglertz’s side?
Manchester City’s impressive 4-2 victory over Arsenal in Sunday’s Women's Super League clash at the Etihad Stadium continued their 100% start to the 2026-27 league campaign.

It’s now five wins from five for the reigning WSL champions, and Andrée Jeglertz’s side hold a two-point lead at the top of the table over Chelsea heading into the first women’s international break of the season.
But how often does a fast start lead to a team winning the WSL title? We look across history to see if it's mattered or not.
Man City have become the 10th team in WSL history to win their first five games of the season.

The more surprising statistic is that only three of the previous nine sides have followed up their fantastic start to the season with a WSL title at the end of that campaign; one apiece for Man City, Arsenal and Chelsea.

The most recent example was Chelsea in 2024-25. In what was Sonia Bompastor’s first season at the club, the Blues enjoyed a phenomenal start, winning each of their first nine games in the WSL before going on to lift the league title for the sixth successive season.
That nine-game winning streak at the start of the campaign equalled the best-ever start by a team in a WSL season, set by Arsenal in 2018-19 on the way to lifting the league title.
The third occasion of a team winning the top-flight title after winning their first five games of the season came in 2016 via Man City under Nick Cushing.
The Citizens went on to extend their winning start to six games in 2016 before securing the title in a 16-game season by five points over Chelsea.
City went one game better at the start of 2017-18, winning their first seven WSL matches that season, but then won just five of their final 11 games and finished second to Chelsea.

Arsenal are the only side to finish outside the top two places in the WSL table after winning all of their opening five games in a season – and they did it twice. They won their first five games in both 2020-21 and 2022-23 before eventually finishing in third.

Excluding the 2017 Spring Series, only one of the previous 15 WSL champions have gone on to lift the title after taking fewer than 10 points from their opening five matches, with Liverpool's remarkable 2014 triumph the sole exception.

That season, the Reds collected just six points from their first five games (W1 D3 L1) before mounting a remarkable turnaround to finish level on points with Chelsea and claim the title on goal difference.

Man City, meanwhile, are already in stronger territory than they were during their title-winning 2025-26 campaign. They lost one of their opening five matches last season (W4 L1), collecting 12 points before going on to secure a second WSL crown. Indeed, City are one of only six champions in the competition's history to have lost any of their first five league games, while no team has ever won the WSL after losing more than once in that span.

With 21 games still left to play in 2026-27, there will be more twists and turns in the WSL title race, but Man City have made the perfect start in their quest to win back-to-back crowns for the first time in their history.

9cna4pd5zgf3zcjqd3ndy6j5.title: Semenyo confident he can be Man City's Haaland backup
9cna4pd5zgf3zcjqd3ndy6j5.subtitle: Having scored twice against Sunderland, Antoine Semenyo backed himself to play as a makeshift number nine for Manchester City if needed.
paragraphs: Antoine Semenyo is confident he has the attributes to deputise for Erling Haaland as Manchester City's striker if required, following his brace against Sunderland.
Semenyo netted either side of half-time as City claimed a thrilling 5-3 victory over the Black Cats on Sunday, maintaining their 100% Premier League record going into the international break.
The Ghanaian also laid on an assist for Rayan Cherki, scoring and assisting in the same Premier League game for the fourth time in his career, and the second as a City player.

Since joining from Bournemouth in January, the Ghana international has scored 13 goals in 34 appearances for City in all competitions – only Haaland (19 goals in 32 games) has outscored him in that span.

In that same time, Semenyo has overperformed his expected goals (xG) total of 7.74 by a greater margin than any other City player (+5.26), while his conversion rate of 20.6% is slightly better than Haaland's 20.4%.

With City not signing another recognised striker in the summer transfer window, some have suggested Semenyo may have to deputise as a number nine at some point this season, and he is up for the challenge.
"I've heard about his backup striker thing. I don't know where it's come from! But, yes, if I need to, then I'll do it. I've no problem with doing that," he said, as quoted by ESPN.
"I think that [finishing] just comes naturally. Once I'm in front of the goal, I know it doesn't move. So as long as I hit it in the corner with a good connection, I know it will go in."
Another City attacker who has enjoyed an outstanding start to the season is Cherki, who showed quick feet inside the Sunderland area to score City's second goal on Sunday.
The Frenchman's six goal involvements in all competitions this season (four goals, two assists) are the second-most of any City player, behind Haaland (seven goals).
"I'm very happy because it was the goal to make it 2-1. I needed to help my team-mates," Cherki told City's website. "I want to give them good passes.
"I need to score a lot of goals for my team. I love the fans. And I think the fans saw a big game, so I'm very happy about that."

City now have three weeks off before travelling to Anfield to face Liverpool in their next Premier League game on October 11, having started a top-flight season with five straight wins for only the fifth time (also 1912-13, 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2023-24).
"Everyone feels good," Semenyo said of the mood around Enzo Maresca's squad.
"It's where we want to be, but we're not going to get too complacent or too relaxed. We know there are a lot more games to go.

"We just want to continue winning; we just have to keep going. It's seven or eight weeks we've been together now, so it's not been too long, but we're doing well. We're winning our games, and we'll keep improving."

In that same time, Semenyo has overperformed his expected goals (xG) total of 7.74 by a greater margin than any other City player (+5.26), while his conversion rate of 20.6% is slightly better than Haaland's 20.4%.

With City not signing another recognised striker in the summer transfer window, some have suggested Semenyo may have to deputise as a number nine at some point this season, and he is up for the challenge.

"I've heard about his backup striker thing. I don't know where it's come from! But, yes, if I need to, then I'll do it. I've no problem with doing that," he said, as quoted by ESPN.

"I think that [finishing] just comes naturally. Once I'm in front of the goal, I know it doesn't move. So as long as I hit it in the corner with a good connection, I know it will go in."

Another City attacker who has enjoyed an outstanding start to the season is Cherki, who showed quick feet inside the Sunderland area to score City's second goal on Sunday.

The Frenchman's six goal involvements in all competitions this season (four goals, two assists) are the second-most of any City player, behind Haaland (seven goals).

"I'm very happy because it was the goal to make it 2-1. I needed to help my team-mates," Cherki told City's website. "I want to give them good passes. 

"I need to score a lot of goals for my team. I love the fans. And I think the fans saw a big game, so I'm very happy about that."

City now have three weeks off before travelling to Anfield to face Liverpool in their next Premier League game on October 11, having started a top-flight season with five straight wins for only the fifth time (also 1912-13, 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2023-24).

"Everyone feels good," Semenyo said of the mood around Enzo Maresca's squad. 

"It's where we want to be, but we're not going to get too complacent or too relaxed. We know there are a lot more games to go.

"We just want to continue winning; we just have to keep going. It's seven or eight weeks we've been together now, so it's not been too long, but we're doing well. We're winning our games, and we'll keep improving."

9ktfcq7vynfq1itjoek2qh0aa.title: Denmark 2-0 Wales: Isaksen stars to get Riemer's side off the mark
9ktfcq7vynfq1itjoek2qh0aa.subtitle: Denmark got their first win of the 2026-27 Nations League, with two second-half goals helping them past Wales in Copenhagen.
paragraphs: Denmark earned their first win of the Nations League after cruising to a 2-0 victory over Wales at Parken.
A Ben Davies own goal broke the deadlock before Gustav Isaksen added some insurance, as Denmark moved onto three points in Group A4, leaving Wales bottom with none.
Isaksen and Patrick Dorgu gave Wales a couple of early warnings, flashing efforts just wide of the left post before the former thought he had broken the deadlock 24 minutes in.

A pacy counter-attack saw Rasmus Hojlund lift a delicate cross between the defenders and Isaksen superbly volleyed past a helpless Danny Ward, but it was chalked off following a VAR review for an offside in the build-up.
From a quick throw-in, Hojlund then teed up Mikkel Damsgaard on the edge of the D, but his fizzing drive struck the foot of the left post.

Connor Roberts saw an instinctive flick tipped over by Filip Jorgensen in Wales' best chance of the first half, while Neco Williams' deflected drive flew into the goalkeeper's gloves just after the break.
Damsgaard's whipped right-sided free-kick caused chaos in the 53rd minute, and in trying to block Hojlund from getting to the ball, Davies deflected it into the back of his own net.

It was another Damsgaard free-kick that led to the second goal, too. Joachim Andersen's header was cleared off the line, but Isaksen put his laces through the rebound to send a deflected volley over Ward in the 66th minute – this one survived the VAR check.

Two late goals were both ruled out, with Hojlund drifting offside before turning past Ward with four minutes of the 90 remaining, while Williams' finish did not count after the referee blew his whistle early for a foul by Ethan Ampadu in the build-up.
Isaksen piles more misery on Wales
Craig Bellamy was proud of what he saw from his side against Portugal on Friday, but Wales fell just short again in Copenhagen after Denmark turned on the style.
While Isaksen will be pleased to finish with his name on the scoresheet, he could easily have had a double – the offside against Hojlund denied him a spectacular first goal.
Since his senior Denmark debut in March 2024, Isaksen is the joint-top scorer for the nation (seven, level with Hojlund), with six of his goals coming at Parken.
Davies, meanwhile, left with an unwanted mark against his name - in his 102nd appearance for his country, he scored his first own goal.

The lack of goals at the other end may prove to be a worry for Wales, who have failed to score in the first half of any of their six games in 2026 in all competitions, attempting 30 shots without success.
They had 10 attempts in total on Sunday, worth 0.65 expected goals (xG), while Denmark had double the number of shots, racking up 1.31 xG from those.

9tje2qt2giqs1j8limk6xtqk3.title: Manchester United 1-0 Liverpool: Zigiotti Olme strike secures back-to-back WSL wins
9tje2qt2giqs1j8limk6xtqk3.subtitle: An early mistake by Khiara Keating was punished by Julia Zigiotti Olme as Manchester United defeated rivals Liverpool 1-0.
paragraphs: Julia Zigiotti Olme was the matchwinner for Manchester United in their 1-0 victory over Liverpool in the Women's Super League.

The Swedish midfielder scored the only goal at Progress with Unity Stadium in the sixth minute, with Liverpool unable to beat Phallon Tullis-Joyce at the other end after an inspired performance from the United goalkeeper.

United's opener came after a blunder at the back from Khiara Keating. The Liverpool shot-stopper passed the ball straight to Zigiotti Olme, who composed herself with a few touches before lifting over a backtracking Keating.

Liverpool responded well to that mistake with Cornelia Kapocs and Beata Olsson denied by a brilliant double save from Tullis-Joyce, while Jess Park saw a deflected effort hit the crossbar for United before the break.
Marie-Therese Hobinger saw a well-struck shot from distance saved by the Red Devils' goalkeeper, before Jenna Clark failed to direct Natalia Ramos' corner on target.
United squandered a golden opportunity to double their lead as Elisabeth Terland's curler was pushed away by Keating, but it mattered little as Eva Olid's side held on for all three points.
Olid's United hit their stride

After failing to win any of their first three WSL games (D1 L2), which included a 5-0 defeat to Chelsea, there was some early pressure mounting on Olid's United, but they have responded in impressive fashion.

A 10-1 win over Sheffield United in the League Cup was followed by a 2-1 victory over West Ham in the WSL, with United now winning back-to-back games in the league and four in a row across all competitions.

Their performance against Liverpool, however, was far from perfect. The visitors won the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.36 to 0.58 and recorded almost as many shots on target (eight) as United had attempts overall (nine).

Nevertheless, Tullis-Joyce's eight saves proved crucial as the Red Devils kept a clean sheet in a WSL home game for the first time since September 2025, ending an 11-game run of conceding in such games.

9vlzkzlzx76w132ohhn99dphy.title: 'Anything is possible' for Brighton as owner eyes major trophy
9vlzkzlzx76w132ohhn99dphy.subtitle: Brighton have hit the ground running in 2026-27 so far, and owner Tony Bloom has high hopes for what they can achieve this season.
paragraphs: Brighton owner Tony Bloom says "anything is possible" as the club target silverware following a stunning start to the 2026-27 season.
Brighton are currently third in the Premier League with 10 points, having lost just one of their matches so far (W3 D1).
They have also secured their place in the Conference League after winning their play-off, with their European campaign beginning next month.
And Brighton are also through to the fourth round of the EFL Cup after a superb 3-2 comeback win over Manchester United after going 2-0 down in the opening 10 minutes.

The Seagulls entered the international break with another statement result, thrashing reigning Premier League champions Arsenal 3-0, and Bloom has aspirations of emulating Leicester City's fairytale this season.

"The biggest teams in the league have a massive financial advantage, but in any one season, anything can happen, as you saw with Leicester City, so it's good to have dreams and goals for us as a club, and also for our fans," Bloom told Sky Sports.
"It's really difficult for teams outside those top six to win the Premier League.
“But anything is possible.
"We're after a major trophy, so obviously any major trophy would be a massive achievement for the football club.
"The Premier League is the bread and butter, and we're really optimistic that we can at least finish in the European places if not a bit higher than that."
Brighton are the highest goalscorers in the Premier League this season, with their 16 goals the most by a side in their first five games since Manchester City in 2022-23 (19).
No player has been involved in more top-flight goals this term than Pascal Gross (six – three goals, three assists), after he scored and assisted against Arsenal.

Fabian Hurzeler, who extended his contract through to 2029 back in May, has also been key to their current dominance, and Bloom was full of praise for his head coach, who led Brighton to an eighth-place finish last term.
"I have huge confidence in Fabian and our group of players," he said.
"As you say, we had 10 players out for most of August, so we've got some key players coming back, with some expected to return after the international break.

"It's very early to start predicting anything, but as Fabian always says, we've got to get the process right. We've got to prepare properly and always look to improve in every aspect of what we do. If we consistently do that, we have a very good chance of having a successful season.
"He's had to cope with lots of different situations in each of the two seasons, including a couple of bad runs when there would have been pressure on him.
"There's always pressure on elite head coaches at elite football clubs in elite football leagues, but he's come through both those situations extremely well.

"We, as a club, have helped him where we can, but he has had to do most of it himself. He's brought the players through with him and, now in his third year, he's gaining a huge amount of experience. I expect him to go from strength to strength."

          Czechia vs England Prediction: UEFA Nations League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Sep 28, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Tuesday's UEFA Nations League game at Fortuna Arena with our Czechia vs England prediction and preview. Thomas Tuchel’s side are looking to bounce back after a disappointing opening loss to Spain.
Both Czechia and England made a losing start to the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign, giving this fixture a must-win feeling early on in Group A3.

Luka Modrić rolled back the years to undo Czechia, helping Croatia to a 2-1 win on Saturday, while at the same time, England threw away a second-half lead to lose 3-2 at home to world champions Spain.

It was a disappointing return to action for the Three Lions, who made two errors leading to a goal in a competitive match for the first time since June 2019 against the Netherlands, which was also in the Nations League.

They were haunted once again by Mikel Oyarzabal, who popped up with the winner, just as he did in the Euro 2024 final. Harry Kane’s unsuccessful penalty attempt shortly after the break, when England were leading 2-1, proved particularly costly.
England have lost two of their last three matches in all competitions – also their heartbreaking World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina – as many as in their previous 23 combined.
They’ve not lost consecutive games since June/September 2022, also in the Nations League against Hungary and Italy.

But England’s recent defensive record will be the biggest worry for Thomas Tuchel. His team have conceded 13 goals in their last six games, almost double the amount they had in their first 17 under the German coach (7).
Indeed, they’ve conceded 3+ goals in their last two matches, last doing so in three in a row in February 1927.

At the other end of the pitch, England look just as strong as usual, and Kane has netted four goals in six Nations League appearances since the start of the 2024-25 edition. That's more than he scored across the first three editions of the competition he played in (3 in 18 games – 2018-19, 2020-21, 2022-23).

And he’s scored 17 goals in 19 appearances under Tuchel – since the German took charge in March 2025, only Erling Haaland (26), Kylian Mbappé (19) and Oyarzabal (18) have hit the back of the net more often than Kane in all competitions for European nations.
Jude Bellingham wasn’t on the scoresheet against Spain, but he did set up Anthony Gordon’s opener before winning the penalty after the break.
Bellingham has been involved in nine goals in his last nine international appearances (7 goals, 2 assists), more than any other England player since the start of the World Cup.

But Czechia have a goal threat of their own, and they will be hoping  Adam Karabec can make an impact against England. He averages a goal or an assist every 89 minutes for Czechia (3 goals, 1 assist in 355 minutes), netting in the loss against Croatia.
But Czechia are in desperate need of a win themselves after a difficult recent period that saw them exit the World Cup in the group stage with only one point to their name.
They’ve lost their last two games in all competitions, last losing more consecutively between June and September 2022 (4).
And that defeat to Croatia last time out ended a 19-game unbeaten home run (W14 D5) – they have not lost consecutive home matches since June 2016, a record they will be keen not to match.
This will be England’s first away game against Czechia since October 2019, a 2-1 defeat in a Euro 2020 qualifier.
Only three other teams have won consecutive home matches against England this century: Spain (3), France (2) and Sweden (2).
England have lost just one of their last nine meetings with Czechia in all competitions (W6 D2), though it was on that last visit in 2019.
