With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our WSL match predictions for Matchday 5 of the 2026-27 season.
The Women’s Super League table is starting to take shape after the first four matches of the season.
Reigning champions Manchester City are the only team with a 100% record still intact after four straight wins to open the campaign.
Behind them, Chelsea and Tottenham are the only other teams yet to taste defeat, while London City Lionesses are also within touching distance of the top.
Arsenal have made a stuttering start, which was compounded by a 1-0 loss to Chelsea last time out, and things do not get any easier as they travel to City this weekend.
Things were more positive for Manchester United, who held out for their first league win under Eva Olid last time out, moving up the table and leaving four clubs without a victory.
So, who will come out on top in the WSL this weekend? We have a look at the Opta supercomputer’s Matchday 5 predictions.
The weekend’s action begins on Saturday, with Manchester United and Liverpool both looking to build on morale-boosting wins against West Ham and Everton, respectively.

Gareth Taylor (81) is aiming to join former United boss Marc Skinner (82) with the second-most managerial wins in WSL history – only Emma Hayes (151) has recorded more – and our predictive model gives that a 17.3% chance of happening.
As it stands, United are heavy favourites to take all three points at 63.2%, given they have won four of their five WSL home matches against the Reds (L1).
United have conceded in each of their last 11 home league games, which will give Liverpool hope of earning consecutive WSL wins for the first time since March 2025 under Amber Whiteley.
Despite a 19.5% chance of a draw, there has never been a stalemate between these teams in the competition in nine previous meetings (six United wins, three Liverpool victories).
It has been a tough start to the season for Aston Villa, who have gone winless in their four games (D2 L2), leading to Natalia Arroyo’s dismissal on Tuesday.
Brian Sørensen is in interim charge and will be in the dugout when Villa host Crystal Palace on Sunday. The hosts are the favourites to win, with a 45.3% win likelihood to Palace’s 27.8%.

Villa could go winless across their opening five matches of a WSL campaign for the third time (after 2023-24 and 2024-25), but they have won three of their last five league meetings with Palace (D1 L1).
Palace, meanwhile, have lost just one of their opening four league matches this term (W1 D2) – the fewest defeats of any promoted side at this stage of a single WSL campaign.
But both of their away games have finished in draws, and at 26.9%, this match is one of the most likely stalemates of the weekend.
Two teams still searching for their first win go head-to-head at the Amex, with Brighton and Charlton Athletic desperate for their victory.

Charlton are the only team still without a point – they could become the third team to lose their first five matches in the competition after Yeovil Town (first seven in 2017) and Leicester City (first nine in 2021-22).
But Brighton are also winless in their last seven WSL games (D4 L3). Only once before have they endured a longer such streak: nine between November 2022 and April 2023.

          Lionel Messi’s Argentina Farewell Match Brings Curtain Down on a Golden Era that Almost Wasn’t
        
      
                          
                      Oct 6, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Lionel Messi will represent Argentina for the last time in a farewell match on Tuesday, closing out a glorious international career that ultimately rewarded his patience.

Not for the first time, Lionel Messi is returning to the Argentina national team. This occasion, however, will be accompanied by a sense of completion and celebration rather than obligation, as the Albiceleste bid farewell to probably the greatest footballer ever.

Messi will don the Argentina shirt one last time in Tuesday’s friendly against Benin (who else?!) after he was invited back for one last celebratory runout following his retirement from international football in the wake of defeat in the 2026 World Cup final.

He did retire once before, of course. In 2016, having suffered heartbreak in a major international final for the third year in a row, adding to the 2007 Copa América runner-up finish, Messi was seemingly done.

“This is tough and a difficult time,” he said after the Copa América Centenario final defeat to Chile. “The first thing that comes to my mind and that I have thought is that the end has come for me and our team. It has been four finals – [international success] just wasn’t for me unfortunately. I looked for it, and wanted it so badly, but it didn’t happen for me.

“I think [international retirement] is best for everyone, firstly for me and for a lot of people that wish this. The team has ended for me, a decision made. I tried many times [to win something with Argentina] and I leave without being able to obtain it.”

Fortunately, about six weeks later following a national campaign urging him to change his mind, Messi confirmed he wasn’t quitting. Another 10 years with the national team would follow, and what a time it ultimately proved to be.

But no, this isn’t another international retirement U-turn. Having finally enjoyed considerable international success, not to mention earning more caps (208 after Tuesday's game) and scoring more goals (125) for Argentina than anyone, Messi no longer has anything to prove to anyone.
Given what we’ve seen Argentina achieve since 2021, the barren spell that coincided with the first 16 years of Messi’s 21-year international career feels like something from an alternate reality.
Copa América final defeats in 2007, 2015 and 2016 were on top of the 1-0 extra-time loss to Germany in the 2014 World Cup decider.
And it wasn’t as if there was a huge amount of promise for Argentina immediately following Messi’s 2016 U-turn.

Debacle is the word that probably best sums up Argentina’s participation at the 2018 World Cup. They were poor in qualifying, reports of a player mutiny stirred relentlessly after a 3-0 loss to Croatia on Matchday 2, and then they were dumped out by France in the round of 16 (admittedly, they did run Les Bleus close in an instant classic in Kazan).

Messi took time away once again after Russia 2018. It was a difficult period for Argentina, who parted ways with Jorge Sampaoli as coach and appointed his assistant in his place. It was a widely unpopular decision that Diego Maradona infamously slammed in his characteristically earnest manner.
“He’s a great guy, but he can't even direct traffic,” Maradona told Clarín. “How can we give the Argentine national team to him? Are we all crazy?”

He was, of course, talking about Lionel Scaloni, who quite plausibly doesn’t know how to direct traffic, and it’s highly likely he never has. But you know what he’s done a pretty good job of directing? The Argentine national team.

Scaloni – and Pablo Aimar – seemingly did enough to convince Messi his absence needn’t be permanent, and what a curious quirk of fate this turned out to be, given Scaloni arguably only got the job because he was an easy and cheap option. Seven years on, he’s the one Argentina coach to win the World Cup and multiple Copa América titles – and it’s fair to say Messi was key to all those successes.
Scaloni is also the Argentina coach Messi has played for the most (79 caps), and that feels symbolic.

Where Scaloni has excelled is in creating a team who maximise Messi’s influence at the top end of the pitch without needing him to muck in off the ball like others, allowing him to focus on what he does best. The rest of the team pick up the slack by working that bit harder, but it’s dirty work that so many of them seem to relish doing, like it’s an honour to do the jobs deemed beneath (or wasted on) Messi.

That might not sound like a particularly kind appraisal of Messi’s teamwork attributes, but it’s hard to argue Scaloni’s recipe didn’t work. And those famous images of the Argentina team walking out to warm up at the 2026 World Cup, looking like Messi was leading his own personal militia, certainly supports the idea they were all in on it.

And why wouldn’t they be? After consecutive Copa América wins either side of glory at Qatar 2022 – their first World Cup triumph since 1986 – and a run to the final at this summer’s World Cup, Argentina have enjoyed the kind of success they’d not seen for generation, maybe longer.

F7DCC6E843721A39D4F3296F94E92022.title: The MLS Wrap: Son can’t stop LAFC slump while Revs overtake Messi’s Miami
F7DCC6E843721A39D4F3296F94E92022.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe MLS Wrap: Son can’t stop LAFC slump while Revs overtake Messi’s MiamiShareThe latest round of MLS matches came amid a moment of celebration for several first-time call-ups to Mauricio Pochettino’s United States team, including one for the league’s standout young star, Cavan Sullivan.

A few of those young players put in notable performances in the latest round of MLS matches, but it was Sullivan and his Philadelphia Union team who once again stole the limelight with a sensational comeback win in Kansas.
Was a wondergoal from Son Heung-min enough to give LAFC a much-needed win? And which team has come up on the rails to overtake Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami?
The latest MLS Wrap answers these questions and has the latest headlines, as well as unearthing some of the more under-the-radar stories in the North American league.
There have been points throughout the last three years when you simply can’t do a weekly roundup of MLS without mentioning Inter Miami and Messi.
The individual performances, coinciding with a team regularly winning games and challenging at the top of the table, meant they could not be ignored.
Even if you try to mix it up to give all the teams some coverage at some point, Messi and Miami demand inclusion most weeks.
Few other players have put in consecutive performances that necessitate such constant attention for their team, but one who is doing so currently is Cavan Sullivan at Philadelphia Union.

The Union’s run since Ryan Richter took over as interim coach is outstanding. They are yet to lose an MLS game during his tenure, and this weekend took that unbeaten run to 11 games in the league, featuring nine wins.

Their run of consecutive wins currently stands at five games thanks to a remarkable 4-3 win against Sporting Kansas City this weekend, coming back to take all three points despite having gone 3-0 down.
What's more, all four of their goals were scored in the space of ten second-half minutes.
A Sporting KC collapse or an unbelievable Philadelphia Union comeback?
Either way, Sullivan, who scored one of those goals to take him to six in his last six games, and the Union are in the headlines once again.

They haven’t stormed up the table like Philadelphia Union, and aren’t one of those teams having a season of two halves that can be separated neatly into pre and post-World Cup narratives, but New England Revolution have gone about the business of winning more games than they lose or draw in 2026, and have sneaked above Inter Miami in the table as a result.
They also boast a teenage American star of their own in 18-year-old Peyton Miller.
The winger scored twice in this weekend’s 4-2 win against Orlando City, building on the one he scored last week against Chicago Fire, and on the three assists in three games he managed in August.
Precise finishes on the break showed his composure even when running at speed with plenty of time to think. Not bad for a player who started out as a left-back.
On the back of such performances, he received a deserved first call-up to the USMNT for the upcoming international window.

The Revolution also have Carles Gil, who has consistently been one of the best players in MLS for eight seasons now, regardless of the kind of form in which the New England team as a whole have been in those years.

Gil contributed a brace of his own to go with Miller’s, and if they can continue with this combination of individual talent and teamwork and results, they may well remain above Inter Miami for the rest of the season and be a threat in the playoffs.

          Make or Break for Renée Slegers? Man City Test Awaits Under-Pressure Arsenal Boss
        
      
                          
                      Oct 2, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Emily Millen / Design, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Arsenal’s poor start has raised bigger questions than their results alone. We examine the data behind their lack of cutting edge ahead of a crucial trip to the Etihad on Sunday.

After finishing second in the Women's Super League last season, Arsenal would have been looking to build on their potential and bring home the title in 2027. However, with four matches played, the Gunners are already seven points behind leaders Manchester City in the league table.
Defeat to City this weekend would leave them 10 points off the top after only five matchdays. Arsenal have never trailed the league leaders by as much as 10 points after five games of a WSL season.
The same issues surfaced in Wednesday’s UEFA Women's Champions League 2-2 draw with Paris FC.

Arsenal had 69.5% possession and established a two-goal lead, but once again their control failed to translate into complete command of the game. Their performance in Paris highlighted a side still short on confidence and, at times, guilty of being their own worst enemy.

An inability to put the contest beyond doubt allowed Paris back into the match, with the French side generating 1.44 expected goals (xG) from open play compared to Arsenal's 1.16. While the penalty that sparked the comeback may have been unfortunate, the Gunners had already allowed Paris a foothold long before the equaliser arrived.

Given they've built their deepest squad in years with significant summer recruitment and have few injury concerns, not many would have thought Arsenal would have endured such a difficult start to the campaign.

They began with a hard-fought 1-0 win at Brighton, before a shock 0-0 home draw with newly-promoted Crystal Palace. Another game at the Emirates required a late equaliser against Manchester United, a late penalty against HB Køge saw them just about win their opening Champions League game, before suffering a 1-0 defeat at Chelsea last weekend.

The pre-season projection from the Opta supercomputer gave them a 25.6% chance of winning the WSL title across its 10,000 simulations; that figure has now fallen to 7.0%. A defeat at City on Sunday would leave their title hopes hanging by a thread.
Yet there is a familiar element to Arsenal’s struggles.

As was the case last season, the results are falling short of what the underlying numbers suggest. The Gunners' actual WSL points tally is already 2.4 points below their expected total this term, the second-largest underperformance in the league behind Brighton (5.9 points below).

Arsenal are averaging just 1.25 points per game, their lowest rate in any WSL season and are winless in three league matches. Only twice in their history have they endured a longer winless run in the competition, with four-game stretches in May 2014 and October 2023.

Their 97% field tilt against Crystal Palace was perhaps the clearest illustration. Arsenal dominated territory without translating that control into meaningful chances, recording the highest field tilt in a WSL match since the start of 2023-24.
For a team that went 20 WSL matches unbeaten before this run, the speed of the change is striking.

Arsenal are spending 54% of their playing time level — the highest proportion in the division, and a familiar sight for a team that accumulated eight draws last season out. Meanwhile, they have spent just 23% of games in a leading position, the eighth most in the WSL.

The question, then, is not simply whether Arsenal can recover their title challenge, but why a team with greater depth, significant recruitment and few injury concerns are once again struggling to turn control into results.
The most alarming aspect of Arsenal’s start is not simply that they are failing to score, but how little threat they are generating when they have the ball.
Sleger's side are dominating territory without consistently creating the openings that should follow.

The Gunners have scored just two goals from 78 shots across their four WSL matches. Only Charlton (1) have scored fewer goals, while Arsenal’s average of 39 shots per goal is currently the second-highest recorded by any team across a WSL season, behind only Yeovil Town in 2017-18 (46 per goal).
Indeed, Brighton are the only side underperforming their xG total by more than the Gunners – with a differential of -5.3 to the Gunners' -4.6.

a6b5quefmea11nqh9jbab1pao.title: Run of clean sheets should give Liverpool confidence, says Alisson
a6b5quefmea11nqh9jbab1pao.subtitle: Liverpool have gone three Premier League games without conceding ahead of the extended international break, with Alisson buoyed by that run.
paragraphs: Alisson says Liverpool's run of three straight clean sheets in the Premier League should give them confidence for the rest of the season, having ironed out their early defensive woes.
Liverpool started the Andoni Iraola era with back-to-back 2-2 draws against Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest, never leading either game at any point and looking shaky at the back.

It has been a different story since they beat Ipswich Town 2-0 with an Alexander Isak brace on September 4, though, having drawn 0-0 with Fulham before overcoming Iraola's former club Bournemouth 1-0 on Sunday.

Only Arsenal (4.04) and Forest (4.8) have given up a lower expected goals against (xGA) figure than Liverpool's 6.12 in the Premier League this season, with Leeds United and Everton (three apiece) the only sides to concede fewer goals than their four.
Alisson, meanwhile, has registered the fifth highest save percentage in the league (77.8%), also preventing 0.8 goals according to Opta's expected goals on target (xGoT) model.

The Brazil international made one superb save at the Vitality Stadium, getting down to his right to tip Evanilson's improvised attempt around the post, and he can feel the Reds' backline growing more assured with every shutout.
"I think every Premier League match away from home is tough to play. You have to fight a lot, and this wasn't any different for us," he told Liverpool's website.

"It wasn't the cleanest performance I think we've had, but those games, if you don’t play so well and then you still win it – and keep the clean sheet – I think this brings confidence for the rest of the season as well."
Another key factor in Liverpool's defensive improvement has been the form of new centre-back Jeremy Jacquet, who was named Player of the Match following Sunday's win.
Only Alexis Mac Allister (seven times) won possession more often for Liverpool than the 21-year-old (six, level with Ronald Araujo), while he also won three of his four duels.
But as Alisson noted, playing alongside a defender of Virgil van Dijk's calibre has made the youngster's adaptation smoother.
"I think Jeremy played really well. Virgil, the back four, Ronald, Milos [Kerkez], the midfielders as well, they helped us a lot defensively. Everybody fights a lot," Alisson continued.
"Jeremy has so much quality, of course, but I don't think it's the hardest job in the world to play alongside Virgil van Dijk! Virgil helped him a lot as well.
"I tried to help Ronald as well, someone who came to make us more solid defensively, and he's delivering as well. So, we are really happy to have them in our side."

Iraola is the first manager to remain unbeaten in his first five league games in charge of Liverpool (W2 D3) since Joe Fagan in September 1983, and he will look to keep his positive start going against Manchester City on October 11.

anil5wqtoq5a1jltql8l28jie.title: Fabian eager to follow up World Cup triumph with Nations League success
anil5wqtoq5a1jltql8l28jie.subtitle: Fabian Ruiz won the World Cup with Spain in the summer, and is now determined to progress in the Nations League.
paragraphs: Fabian Ruiz has welcomed the challenge of "winning again" as Spain prepare for their Nations League opener against England on Saturday.
Spain's clash with Thomas Tuchel's side at Wembley Stadium will be their first since defeating Argentina in the World Cup final back in July.
It marked La Roja's second triumph in the competition, while they now simultaneously hold the World Cup and the Euros, as they did from 2008 to 2012.
Spain are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest-ever streak by a European nation.
Despite their recent success, Fabian acknowledged how difficult it will be to continue winning trophies on the international stage.
"The manager has already told us that the past is forgotten; it's history, and that's wonderful, but now it's time to focus on the present," Fabian told AS.
"The hardest thing in football is winning again. Winning once is great, but doing it again is the difficult part.

"That's the challenge we have now: to want to win again, to keep winning. It's very difficult, but this team has what it takes to do it, and we're going for this title with a lot of enthusiasm; we also consider it very important.
"We hope to be in the final four [of the Nations League]."

Spain have reached the final in three of the last four Nations League tournaments, losing on penalties in the most recent in 2024-25; excluding penalties, La Roja have lost just one of their last 18 matches in the competition (W10 D7).
Luis de la Fuente's side have also won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the final of the 2024 European Championship.
Their last away game against the Three Lions also ended 2-1, at Wembley in the Nations League in September 2018.

atijk1c41fqw1v8o4fwmj69vr.title: Tuchel: Bellingham better if he plays with a bit of rage
atijk1c41fqw1v8o4fwmj69vr.subtitle: Jude Bellingham impressed once again for England in their defeat to Spain, and Thomas Tuchel wants the midfielder to play with emotion.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel claimed "it's better" for England if Jude Bellingham "plays with a bit of rage" as he did against Spain.
Despite losing 3-2 to Spain in their Nations League opener, Bellingham impressed in midfield against the likes of Rodri and Fabian Ruiz.
As well as assisting Anthony Gordon at Wembley Stadium and winning a penalty, which Harry Kane missed, Bellingham created a match-high five chances and competed in the most duels (15).
Bellingham has been involved in nine goals in his last nine international appearances (seven goals, two assists), more than any other England player since the start of the 2026 World Cup.
The midfielder was involved in a heated exchange of words with Real Madrid team-mate Marc Cucurella during their clash with Spain, and Tuchel believes such situations can help Bellingham.
"He likes that," Tuchel said ahead of England's Nations League encounter with Czechia on Tuesday. "He gets better if that happens.
"It's better if he plays with a bit of rage. It's what he does. I think sometimes he is looking for these moments to get his fire going."
And when asked about the encounter between Bellingham and Cucurella, Tuchel added: "I think he doesn't know any team-mates when he is in the national team.
"He wants to win. He doesn't know any team-mates. He is still friends with them but not for the 90 minutes."
England have lost just one of their last nine meetings with Czechia in all competitions (W6 D2), though it was on their last visit to the nation in October 2019 (2-1).
Only three other teams have won consecutive home matches against England this century: Spain (a run of three), France (two) and Sweden (two).

England have lost two of their last three matches in all competitions, as many as in their previous 23 combined. They have not lost consecutive games since June/September 2022, also in the Nations League against Hungary and Italy.

bb9mws7965rz1tzrewvuyeavl.title: New York Red Bulls 0-3 St. Louis City SC: Late show extends unbeaten streak
bb9mws7965rz1tzrewvuyeavl.subtitle: St. Louis City SC are now unbeaten in 19 straight games in all competitions after they claimed a 3-0 victory over the New York Red Bulls.
paragraphs: St. Louis City SC closed in on the Vancouver Whitecaps at the top of MLS' Western Conference with a 3-0 win over the New York Red Bulls.
In a match that was postponed from Saturday to Wednesday due to bad weather, St. Louis ultimately stormed to a victory that extends their unbeaten streak to 19 games.
Rafael Navarro finished from close range to open the scoring in the fifth minute at Sports Illustrated Stadium.
Roman Burki made a smart stop to deny Jorge Ruvalcaba, before Emil Forsberg squandered a gilt-edged chance to level the scores.
Eric Choupo-Moting saw an attempt cleared off the line, though Ethan Horvath then had to make a superb save to keep the Red Bulls in the contest.
Yet two substitutes sealed the points for St. Louis City. First, Simon Becher drilled in from the edge of the box, paving the way for Tomas Ostrak to finish off the job in stoppage time.
St. Louis City are within three points of the Whitecaps at the summit of the West, but they are one of the form teams in the competition.
That is now 17 straight MLS games without a defeat for St. Louis City, who have also scored in each of those matches.
Only two teams in MLS history have ever gone on a longer unbeaten run than this current streak managed by St. Louis City (W12 D5).
They are FC Dallas in 2010 (19 games) and the Columbus Crew in 2004 (18 matches).
Becher played a decisive role from the bench. He leads the way for goal involvements during this brilliant St. Louis run, with 10 (seven goals, three assists).

bfklrj0mtfyz1eaw5sr080xon.title: Yamal feels World Cup triumph should aid Ballon d'Or bid
bfklrj0mtfyz1eaw5sr080xon.subtitle: Lamine Yamal has continued to make his case for winning the Ballon d'Or, and he feels Spain's World Cup success should be a consideration.
paragraphs: Lamine Yamal believes lifting the World Cup with Spain should aid his hopes of winning the Ballon d'Or, with Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe viewed as his main rivals.

Yamal helped La Roja win their second world title in North America this year, although his individual impact at the tournament was limited after his 2025-26 season was ended prematurely by a hamstring injury.

He registered 24 goals and 17 assists in 45 outings across all competitions last season, helping Barcelona retain their LaLiga title, with his 41 combined goal involvements being the sixth-most of any player from Europe's top five leagues.
Yamal also attempted (429) and completed (225) the most dribbles of any player, while his 59 chances created following carries were also the most.
On Tuesday, Spain coach Luis de la Fuente declared one of his players should win the prize, just as Rodri did when they triumphed at Euro 2024.
And Yamal, who has not been shy about making his case as the October 26 ceremony inches closer, concurs with that view.

"It's the award for the best player of the year, a player who is different, who is a pleasure to watch play, the one who has that magic, who makes you smile, who makes you want to watch a game just for him," Yamal said in an interview with L'Equipe.
"I think my way of playing is my strongest argument and what makes me different.
"It's very important, in addition to being a good player, that you make your team win.
"The advantage I have is that I have been able to win the World Cup this year and, obviously, that is a plus for me.
"But if a person says, 'Lionel Messi deserves it' or 'Rodri deserves it', that's totally respectable."
Having come through the ranks at Barca, Yamal has faced plenty of comparisons to Messi, who he outshone in the World Cup final as Spain edged out Argentina in extra time.
But the 19-year-old wants to be remembered on his own terms, saying: "I play to make history, so that in 30 years' time, young people will say, 'he was really very good too'.

Yamal helped La Roja win their second world title in North America this year, although his individual impact at the tournament was limited after his 2025-26 season was ended prematurely by a hamstring injury.

Yamal also attempted (429) and completed (225) the most dribbles of any player, while his 59 chances created following carries were also the most.

And Yamal, who has not been shy about making his case as the October 26 ceremony inches closer, concurs with that view. 

"It's the award for the best player of the year, a player who is different, who is a pleasure to watch play, the one who has that magic, who makes you smile, who makes you want to watch a game just for him," Yamal said in an interview with L'Equipe.

"I think my way of playing is my strongest argument and what makes me different. 

"It's very important, in addition to being a good player, that you make your team win.

"The advantage I have is that I have been able to win the World Cup this year and, obviously, that is a plus for me.

bhh5cf70r3o61gj47k7td791s.title: Czechia clash too early to be a 'must-win' game for England, says Tuchel
bhh5cf70r3o61gj47k7td791s.subtitle: England and Czechia face off in their quest for a first Nations League win on Tuesday, but Thomas Tuchel said victory was not a must.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel believes it is too early to label England's Nations League clash against Czechia as a "must-win" game following their defeat to Spain.
England make the trip to Fortuna Arena on Tuesday, aiming to get their Nations League campaign back on track after they were beaten 3-2 by Luis de la Fuente's side.
The result saw the Three Lions lose a match they led at half-time for the first time since June 2019, which also came in the Nations League against the Netherlands.

It will be England's first away game against Czechia since October 2019 – a 2-1 defeat in a European Championship qualifier. Only Spain (a run of three), France and Sweden (both two) have won consecutive matches against the Three Lions this century.
England come into the game having conceded 13 goals in their last six games, almost double the amount they had in their first 17 matches under Tuchel (seven).

Following their meeting with Czechia, England travel to Croatia before facing Santi Denia's side again at Wembley Stadium on October 6, though Tuchel believes that failure to win the first clash was not the end of the world for his team.
"It's a bit early for must-win. I know what you mean, but it is a bit early in the group for a must-win," Tuchel told reporters.
"We always arrive and prepare the team with a target to win. It was the target against Spain, and it is the same [against Czechia].
"We respect the quality and the challenge it brings. You play in Prague against Czechia; it is difficult. There will be support for the home team.
"We always prepare for the win; we want the win. It is too early to speak for a must. It would be ideal. The problem is the opponent on the other side."
England have lost just one of their last nine meetings with Czechia in all competitions (W6 D2), though it was on their last visit to the nation in October 2019 (1-2).
But Czechia are another team who are looking to get their Nations League campaign up and running after they were beaten 2-1 by Croatia in their opening match.
Czechia have lost their last two games in all competitions, last losing more consecutively between June and September 2022 (four), but Tuchel is expecting a tough test.
"We only analysed one game from the Czech team, as they have a new coach," Tuchel added. We saw a flexible midfield of three. A lot of changes in position.
"Wingers, attacking full-backs and a team that was well-organised. Full of motivation to take their chance, that is what we saw.
"I feel I always need a result; you always need a result in football to get confidence, to get the support and belief.
"Especially after a defeat. If everyone in the camp truly believes, even then you still need it for yourself. The best reaction is if you can prove it in a result."
Tuchel also refused to rule out Nico O'Reilly and Ezri Konsa from playing against Czechia after the pair missed training because of minor injuries.
"I am not sure yet [will they play]. They missed training because of minor issues, but they are still issues," Tuchel said.
"They need to be assessed, and we will see [on Tuesday]."

blzjyjvf6m8e19peb688fslxv.title: Rayan targets Brazil improvement after snatching late draw against Australia
blzjyjvf6m8e19peb688fslxv.subtitle: Brazil avoided a scare against Australia in their first friendly of the international break, with Rayan's last-gasp goal salvaging a draw.
paragraphs: Rayan says Brazil know they must improve after his late goal snatched a draw with Australia in a friendly in Queensland.
Australia looked set to claim a famous victory over the Selecao, but instead Brazil earned a 1-1 draw.
Nestory Irankunda gave Australia the lead midway through the second half with a stunning free-kick, but Rayan's powerful header from Raphinha's corner ultimately pulled Brazil back into the match.
Brazil also had a goal ruled out by VAR on the stroke of half-time, as Bruno Guimaraes was deemed to have fouled Harry Souttar in the build-up to Estevao slotting home.
It was a new-look side for Carlo Ancelotti, who opted against picking his old guard following their World Cup exit.
Rayan believes it was a fair result in the end, though, and is determined to make sure Brazil end up on the winning side when they face off for the second time on Tuesday.
"We don't step onto the field to lose; we step onto the field to win," Rayan told Sportv.
"But it wasn't possible. Although we have another chance against them and we'll go for the win.
"We know that we have to improve our defensive side. We also knew how to play, but we know that we have to improve."

Brazil will feel they deserved not to walk away as the losing side, given they finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.2 from their 16 shots to their opponents' tally of 0.5 from their seven attempts.
While Brazil's superstars failed to hit the heights they have often shown in the past, Irankunda caught the eye of both coaches, with Ancelotti heaping high praise on him.
"We knew this, fantastic player," Ancelotti said.
"We watch a player with a lot of talent who is doing very well in Europe. We knew this kind of situation on set pieces, but his shot… fantastic."
And Australia head coach Tony Popovic was equally as complimentary of the 20-year-old, who he believes has benefited hugely from his move to Sporting CP from Watford.
"Nestory knows what we think of him. He's 20 years old. He started three games at a World Cup, played half a game in the other, and he's moved to a bigger club," Popovic said.
"There's a clear difference in Nestory already. He's matured so quickly in a short space of time in terms of what's expected at Sporting.
"What he's learning is that the transfer is one part. Now you go to a new club. They don't give you minutes, they don't guarantee you minutes, they give you nothing. You have to earn everything.
"So, he delivered, played very well, and he'll only get better. He's a young kid. I expect by the next World Cup, hopefully, he gets a lot of minutes at a bigger club; there'll be a big improvement.
"But yeah, just a wonderful person. Nothing's changed for us in how we feel about him and how we are together."

byuabj05c6b31trebts7mifbh.title: Xavi seeks more improvement after first win as Netherlands boss
byuabj05c6b31trebts7mifbh.subtitle: The Netherlands defeated Serbia 2-1 in the Nations League on Sunday to earn Xavi his first win as head coach.
paragraphs: Xavi believes the Netherlands "have to play better" despite their victory over Serbia in the Nations League on Sunday.
Mexx Meerdink scored twice as the Netherlands won 2-1 at Stadion Rajko Mitic, seeing Xavi pick up his first win since taking over from Ronald Koeman.

It was a dominant display from Xavi's side, who created 2.74 expected goals (xG) from 25 shots while restricting Serbia to 1.32 from 11 attempts, with the visitors also creating six Opta-defined big chances.
Meerdink impressed in just his second appearance for the Netherlands, while Joey Veerman controlled proceedings from midfield.

Veerman led the match in touches (135), passes (117 – level with Jan Paul van Hecke) and chances created (five), while also leading his team-mates in interceptions (three) and winning six of his nine duels.
Xavi drew plenty of positives from his maiden victory at the helm, but knows there is still plenty to improve upon.
"We have to be honest: we have to play better," said the Spaniard.
"But there were good things and I'm happy with the attitude and the effort.
"We dominated and created more chances than them. We maintained our positions, we were organised, and thanks to that we were able to make better use of the spaces."
There was a concern, however, for both Xavi and Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola after Cody Gakpo was forced off with an ankle injury in the first half.

As well as scoring a late equaliser in the Netherlands' 1-1 draw with Germany in Xavi's first match in charge, Gakpo also leads Liverpool players in direct goal involvements this season (six – two goals, four assists).
When asked if Gakpo's injury was serious, Xavi responded: "I don’t think so.
"It's his ankle, that's all I know. Tomorrow [Monday] we will know, but hopefully it's not too important."

cfj0jdvhsdcw17mwti4ku8wmu.title: Cucurella: Spain and Real Madrid situations not comparable
cfj0jdvhsdcw17mwti4ku8wmu.subtitle: Marc Cucurella is enjoying plenty of success with Spain, and he hopes to do the same at Real Madrid under Jose Mourinho.
paragraphs: Marc Cucurella does not believe it is fair to compare the situations of Spain and Real Madrid, with the latter in a different "process".
Spain are flying under Luis De la Fuente, adding the World Cup to their cabinet after already winning the European Championships in 2024.
La Roja are unbeaten in their last 40 games across all competitions (W31 D9), while their current nine-match winning run is their joint-best under De la Fuente.
Madrid, meanwhile, are fourth in LaLiga and six points behind leaders Barcelona after seven games, with Jose Mourinho returning to the helm this summer.
Cucurella insisted it is too early to judge Real Madrid's season, insisting they need time to improve under Mourinho.
"Everything is a process. We've been together here for a long time, and we have to accept that we're in a process at Real Madrid," said Cucurella.
"We started with a new coach. The beginning may not have been what we expected, but this is a process, and we'll have to assess everything at the end of the season."
Spain continue their Nations League campaign with a trip to Czechia on Saturday.
La Roja are currently top of Group A3 after a 3-2 win over England and 4-1 victory over Croatia last time out.
De la Fuente will be without both Ferran Torres and Nico Williams due to injury, while Alejandro Grimaldo and Eric Garcia pulled out of the squad earlier in the extended break.
Playing a total of four matches during this extended international break, De la Fuente feels injuries were inevitable.
"The drawback of this format is that it's difficult to recover," said De la Fuente.
"We always prioritise the players' health and want everyone to be in perfect condition. Because there's no time to recover."

ci4uhlo6b7nr1cldraznzj5kx.title: Van Bommel refuses to fault 'seven out of 10' Belgium after France defeat
ci4uhlo6b7nr1cldraznzj5kx.subtitle: Belgium were beaten 1-0 by France in their second Nations League game, but new head coach Mark van Bommel was determined to remain upbeat.
paragraphs: Mark van Bommel refused to criticise his Belgium players following their agonising Nations League defeat to France, rating their performance a "seven out of 10" and arguing they are on the right track.
Michael Olise's solo goal in the 88th minute settled Monday's contest in Brussels, as France went top of Group A1 in the Nations League with two wins from two games.
While Les Bleus boast a perfect record under new boss Zinedine Zidane, Belgium have registered one win and one loss under Van Bommel, having triumphed 2-0 in Italy on Friday.
France had 18 shots to Belgium's 12 and hit the target on seven occasions, compared to the hosts' two, while Zidane's team also won the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.22 to 0.69.
But Van Bommel was still broadly pleased with the Red Devils' efforts, ahead of a home game against Turkiye on Friday and a return trip to France next Monday.
"They all deserve at least a seven out of 10," Van Bommel noted. "I have nothing to fault them for. These are intelligent and quality players.
"We should not be critical; we are on the right track. Our way of pressing, our changes on the wings, and our way of creating chances were good.
"We can see the idea behind our actions. You could feel that everyone was enjoying themselves. The details are well mastered. We simply didn't manage to score."
France were without captain Kylian Mbappe due to a hyperextension in his left knee, while Olise, Ousmane Dembele and Rayan Cherki were all introduced from the bench.

Esteban Lepaul and Maghnes Akliouche started in attack, alongside Paris Saint-Germain's Desire Doue and recent Liverpool signing Bradley Barcola, but Van Bommel was still under no illusions regarding the strength of France's lineup.
"We cannot say that we played against a B team. It was a solid team," he added. "Of course, France are further ahead than us. I can't deny that.
"On Monday, we might be even more challenged at their place. This is only our first week together, we must not forget that.
"Our goal is the Euros in two years, but I am very happy with our performance."
While Belgium host Turkiye in their next Nations League fixture, France welcome Roberto Mancini's Italy to the Stade de France on Friday, with Mbappe still sidelined.

cuvnxabgh98v1wg07zvgbsrph.title: Austin must turn draws into wins during play-off push, says Sabovic
cuvnxabgh98v1wg07zvgbsrph.subtitle: Twelfth-place Austin FC host 11th-place San Diego FC as both teams push for a play-off spot in the MLS' Western Conference.
paragraphs: Austin FC midfielder Besard Sabovic believes they "need to start winning if we're going to make it to the play-offs".
Austin are 12th in the Western Conference, just two points off the postseason places and one point behind upcoming opponents San Diego FC.
After a goalless draw with FC Dallas last time out, Austin are unbeaten in seven games in MLS, though four of those games have ended as a draw.
With just eight games to go in the regular season, Sabovic is determined to win as many as possible in their search for a play-off spot.
"We're seven games [unbeaten], and we should do everything we can to continue this streak, but of course, it's getting closer and closer," said Sabovic.
"The season's ending soon, so we need to start winning if we're going to make it to the playoffs, which is everyone's goal."
For the first time this season, San Diego earned a result in a league match they trailed in the 75th minute or later when they played to a 2-2 draw with Inter Miami on Sunday.
Dating back to last season, San Diego had lost 13 straight regular-season matches when trailing in the 75th minute or later.
Despite the result against the reigning MLS Cup champions, San Diego remain winless in their last four MLS games (D1 L3) ahead of facing Austin.
Austin FC – Jon Gallagher
In the 0-0 draw with Dallas, Jon Gallagher registered two of Austin's three shots on target, tying for the most in any of his 200 career MLS regular-season matches.
As a team, the Verde have not attempted more than three shots on target in any of their last five MLS matches.
San Diego FC – Anders Dreyer
Anders Dreyer scored both of San Diego's goals against Miami, his 18th MLS regular-season game with multiple goal contributions.
The only other player with at least that many such games since the beginning of last season is Lionel Messi (23).
MATCH PREDICTION: AUSTIN FC WIN
Austin are on a seven-match unbeaten streak in MLS play (W3 D4); it is tied for the longest regular-season unbeaten run in their history, matching a seven-game streak in June-July 2022.
However, San Diego beat Austin 5-0 when the teams met in May, the largest margin of defeat in any match in Austin's club history.

San Diego have three different wins by five or more goals in their two MLS regular seasons, tied for the most by any MLS team over the last two seasons (with the Philadelphia Union and Vancouver Whitecaps).

cyhuti0bvht81ff1qrkw1dqf1.title: Zidane: France players are the protagonists, not me
cyhuti0bvht81ff1qrkw1dqf1.subtitle: France will get the Zinedine Zidane era underway in Turkiye on Friday, but the ex-midfield icon does not want to be the star attraction.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane insists he will not be the "protagonist" of France's new era, instead taking a back seat to his star-studded squad.
France face Turkiye in their Nations League opener at Kocaeli Stadium on Friday, with Zidane managing his country for the first time following 14 years under Didier Deschamps.
Deschamps led Les Bleus to their second World Cup triumph in 2018 – as well as runner-up finishes at the 2022 edition and at Euro 2016 – during his illustrious spell in charge.
He oversaw 187 matches in total, having also represented his nation 103 times as a player, with his 26 World Cup games being the most of any coach in the competition's history.
Zidane's appointment, though, has come with much fanfare, given his status as an icon of French football.
He scored a brace against Brazil in France's first World Cup final triumph in 1998, while he is also the most recent Frenchman to win the Ballon d'Or, claiming the prize that year.

And, across two spells as the head coach of Real Madrid, Zidane won three Champions League crowns in a row, two LaLiga titles, two Club World Cups, two UEFA Super Cups and two editions of the Supercopa de Espana.

Yet the former midfielder does not see himself as the star of the France setup, telling reporters: "After 14 years of Didier, this is new. But the protagonists are the players. I'm going to stay in my role.
"I feel a huge emotion to be able to be here as a coach, maybe even more than before my first game as a player."
One of Zidane's foremost tasks will be finding a way to keep several big-name attackers happy.

At this summer's World Cup, where France finished fourth, Kylian Mbappe set a new record for goal involvements at a single edition (14 – 10 goals, four assists) and became the competition's all-time leading scorer (22 goals).
Michael Olise recorded more assists than any other player has had at a single World Cup (seven, since 1966), while Ousmane Dembele scored six goals and assisted two.
Asked where he would field Dembele in particular, Zidane replied: "You'll see tomorrow. We have put things in place. The idea is to do interesting things.
"We're not going to talk about Zidane's touch. We only had three training sessions. We put two or three things in place. We will have to be good tomorrow."

Adrien Rabiot appeared alongside Zidane at France's pre-match press conference, and the AC Milan midfielder believes Deschamps' team were tactically outclassed by eventual champions Spain in their World Cup semi-final, which La Roja won 2-0.
"I'm thinking about the Nations League. We know that things in football move fast," Rabiot said. "The coach is here for four years. We have to take this competition and use it.
"It wasn't a lack of quality. We have no less quality than Spain, with all humility. They were better tactically; they may have prepared better for that match.
"Spain were able to put us in difficulty. If we play them again, we will have to find the key. We will have to work on this tactical point – we have collective and individual talent."

d6765eyx536j1ru5vr5jzx9b0.title: 'A player like him deserves this' – Scaloni pushed for Messi's Argentina farewell
d6765eyx536j1ru5vr5jzx9b0.subtitle: Despite announcing his international retirement after the World Cup, Lionel Messi will play for Argentina one more time on October 6.
paragraphs: Lionel Scaloni revealed he did everything in his power to ensure Lionel Messi would return to the Argentina national team one more time for a farewell match.
Messi announced his retirement from international football following Argentina's 1-0 defeat to Spain in the World Cup final, bringing an end to a glittering career with his country.
He retires as Argentina's all-time leading appearance-maker (207) and scorer (125), while also captaining his country to the World Cup in 2022 and two Copa America crowns.

The 39-year-old has played more games (34), registered more goal involvements (33) and laid on more assists (12) than any other player in World Cup history, while only Kylian Mbappe (22) has bettered his 21 goals at FIFA's flagship tournament.
The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner also leads the all-time World Cup charts for shots (140), shots on target (64), chances created (99) and dribbles (250).
However, Messi was called up to Scaloni's latest Argentina squad, and he will play one final time against Benin at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires on October 6.
"I ​believe that a player like him deserves this. Personally, I did my part ​because I wanted to be at his farewell," Scaloni told reporters.
"Since I don't know if I would be here later, we pushed hard so that he could ​be in this match.
"We knew everything he was going through and ​even so, he put in the desire and effort to want to come and ‌be able ⁠to say goodbye to the people who love him so much.
"If we have to pay tribute, we have to do it at this moment. With him, it will never stop, but later, the magic ​might not be ​the same."
Messi was pivotal to Argentina's first World Cup success since 1986 in 2022, scoring twice in their penalty shoot-out win against France following a 3-3 draw in normal time.
He followed that up with a sensational tournament this summer, scoring eight goals, including his first-ever World Cup hat-trick against Algeria.
"For me, getting to coach him was the ultimate experience. It was a dream. I told him so, and I'll say it for the rest of my life. There will never be anyone like him," Scaloni added.
"It's very rare for a player like that to come along – not just because of what he does on the pitch, but because of everything he conveys off it. Let's enjoy this.
"After the World Cup he just played, there isn't much more to add. If the award is for the best player, there's no doubt. It's already spoken for, the statistics prove it.
"As long as he's on a football pitch, it's hard to argue that he doesn't deserve it."
With Messi's international future already decided, the same cannot be said for Scaloni, whose contract will run out this December.
Asked if he had received an update on his ​future, ⁠Scaloni said he would meet with Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia in the coming days.
"It is a dream come true, but that doesn't mean I ⁠have to ​cling to the job forever," Scaloni said.
"There are certain conditions we need to discuss with the president, and we'll see if we ​can reach an agreement."

d9y1o8jngad71l61cx4ss24e4.title: Muller tips Olise or Mbappe for Ballon d'Or
d9y1o8jngad71l61cx4ss24e4.subtitle: Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal are the favourites for the Ballon d'Or, but Thomas Muller has picked another top contender.
paragraphs: Thomas Muller has backed either Michael Olise or Kylian Mbappe as the top two candidates to win the Ballon d'Or this year.
The winner of the award will be announced on October 26, but Muller has overlooked favourites including former Bayern Munich team-mate Harry Kane and World Cup winner Lamine Yamal.
Instead, he has tipped a different Bayern player to claim the award, looking to Olise, whose performances in 2025-26 helped the club win the Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal titles.
Olise ended the Bundesliga season with 34 goal involvements (15 goals, 19 assists), a new record for a winger since Opta data collection began in the German top-flight in 2004-05.
Only Kane (41) directly contributed to more Bundesliga goals than the Frenchman, who also scored five goals and provided seven assists in 13 Champions League games.
He also carried his form into the World Cup, becoming the first player on record (since 1966) to register seven assists in a single edition.
As for Mbappe, this summer he became the all-time top scorer at World Cups (22 goals) and has scored 50 goals in 52 games for Real Madrid since the start of last season.
Of players in Europe's top five leagues, only Kane (67) has netted more club goals than Mbappe in that time.

"For me, there are two candidates whose individual performances have impressed me the most, and those are Michael Olise and his brilliant World Cup partner Kylian Mbappe," Muller wrote in his newsletter, as quoted by Sky Sport Germany.
"The two combine spectacle with goal threat. In detail, they manage to be efficient with their finesse and power, and to make the whole thing look incredibly easy.
"For me, that's the stuff of a world-class footballer. It simply needs a touch of magic."
Muller also highlighted Olise's impressive start to the 2026-27 campaign.
Olise has registered 11 goal involvements across all competitions so far this term (eight goals, three assists), including a hat-trick in a 7-0 rout of Union Berlin before the international break.
"It's nothing new how he converts those chances from outside the penalty area, but it's still always a sight to behold," Muller added.

di4bcg7hnqt1lcnz7ql2gnxs.title: Bosnia-Herzegovina 1-1 Sweden: Gyokeres dampens Dzeko's farewell party
di4bcg7hnqt1lcnz7ql2gnxs.subtitle: Viktor Gyokeres scored once again for Sweden, who drew 1-1 with Bosnia-Herzegovina in what was Edin Dzeko's final international appearance.
paragraphs: Edin Dzeko's final appearance for Bosnia-Herzegovina ended in a 1-1 draw with Sweden in the Nations League.
Kerim Alajbegovic's 80th-minute equaliser ensured Dzeko would not bow out with a defeat after Viktor Gyokeres gave Sweden the lead just after the hour at Stadion Bilino Polje.

Sweden started on the front foot as Gyokeres' low drive towards the bottom-left corner was kept out by Salko Hamzic, and the Arsenal striker then saw a goal ruled out in the 17th minute by VAR after the ball touched his arm before he scored.
The home fans erupted when Dzeko found the back of the net before half-time, but his goal was also chalked off as the ball had gone out of play in the build-up.

Graham Potter's side then scored with their first shot of the second half after Alexander Bernhardsson regained possession and played Gyokeres through on goal, with the forward lashing into the roof of the net.

Bernhardsson, Gyokeres and Besfort Zeneli all missed chances to double Sweden's lead, and it proved costly as Alajbegovic's in-swinging cross evaded all the players in the box and nestled into the far corner.
Gyokeres oozing confidence in Sweden shirt

Gyokeres entered the international break low on confidence after a poor start to the season with Arsenal, but the 28-year-old is in exceptional form for Sweden, providing the goods again in Alexander Isak's absence.

Gyokeres has scored in all three games during this international break, seeing him become the first-ever player to score in six consecutive Nations League matches, with Potter's side still top of Group B4 after three games.

Bosnia, meanwhile, paid farewell to one of their greatest players. Dzeko exited the pitch to a guard of honour from his Bosnia team-mates, though he would have loved to leave with one last goal to his name.

Dzeko bows out as Bosnia's all-time leading appearance maker (152) and top scorer (73), though this game could signify a change in guard, with 19-year-old Juventus forward Alajbegovic scoring an important goal.

dn28cyhn5d6q12z85vtjecne2.title: Neymar pays tribute to Messi: Thank you for making me love football even more
dn28cyhn5d6q12z85vtjecne2.subtitle: Lionel Messi will play his final game for Argentina on Tuesday, and his great friend Neymar has paid tribute.
paragraphs: Neymar has hailed Lionel Messi ahead of the 39-year-old's final game for Argentina.
Messi confirmed his retirement from international football last month.
However, the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner will make a farewell appearance for Argentina against Benin on Tuesday.
And Neymar, who formed a formidable attack alongside Messi at Barcelona and also played with him at Paris Saint-Germain, has paid tribute to his close friend.
"Anyone who loves football has enjoyed you throughout all these years…" Neymar posted on Instagram.
"Today is your final game wearing the shirt of your national team, your country, and I hope you enjoy every second of it and that all the tributes today make you happy.
"It's not only Argentina that thanks you, the whole world thanks you for everything you’ve done for football.
"Thank you for making me love football even more. It was an honour to have played against you, and even more so to have made history alongside you.
"THANK YOU, Leo Messi."

dwhshekgvvba13w6xy4o6d9le.title: Messi will leave Argentina legacy that is 'unequalled', says Scaloni
dwhshekgvvba13w6xy4o6d9le.subtitle: Lionel Messi will pull on an Argentina shirt for the very last time against Benin, capping a stunning international career.
paragraphs: Lionel Scaloni says Lionel Messi is leaving behind "something incomparable" as he prepares to play his final match for Argentina.
Messi announced his international retirement in the aftermath of Argentina's World Cup final loss to Spain but will play one last game for the Albiceleste on home soil to say farewell to the fans.
The 39-year-old will face Benin on Tuesday, earning his 208th cap – the most of any player in the nation's history.
He also has more goals for Argentina than any other player (125) and more goal involvements at the World Cup than anyone else in history (33 – 21 goals, 12 assists).
Over the summer, he became the only man to start three World Cup finals, having led Argentina to glory in 2022, and also lifting two Copa Americas on either side of that triumph.
And as he prepares for his final-ever Argentina appearance, Scaloni once again heaped praise on his team's talisman.
"Messi leaves behind something unequalled," Scaloni said.
"We have to keep playing, but the feeling of having him on the pitch is unique. I've never seen anyone else convey what he does on a football field, and that is what we're going to miss.
"Only nostalgia remains now that he won't be there. He is an incredible example. The first to arrive, the last to leave, how he takes care of himself, how he faces each game.
"You can see he is a phenomenon just by how he plays, but he has things behind him that his team-mates see, and he is the best example there can be.
"He has left – or is leaving, because he has one more game – something incomparable."
Argentina have a so-far perfect record without Messi in the side, having beaten Bolivia 4-0 and Burkina Faso 7-0 across their two friendlies.

dwzioag14i691fct96u5wlzj9.title: Pochettino: Young stars like Sullivan do not come around often
dwzioag14i691fct96u5wlzj9.subtitle: Cavan Sullivan became the youngest goalscorer in the United States' history on Saturday, drawing big praise from Mauricio Pochettino.
paragraphs: Mauricio Pochettino admits it is difficult to find young players with the quality of Cavan Sullivan, and he knows the United States need to nurture the 17-year-old's talent.
The USA thrashed rivals Mexico 3-0 in Arizona on Saturday, earning their third victory in as many games during this extended international break.
Their young stars shone brightly once again, with 18-year-old Julian Hall scoring for the third time in his first three senior caps, while Sullivan made a piece of history in the second half.
Having intercepted an errant pass from Raul Rangel and lobbed the Mexico goalkeeper from distance, Sullivan – at the age of 17 years and five days – became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.
He surpassed Borussia Dortmund's Mathis Albert just four days after he claimed the record from Christian Pulisic, netting at the age of 17 years and 131 days against Chile.
The USA have one more game to play this month, against Canada in Minnesota on Tuesday, and Pochettino is determined to give his young players further chances to impress.
"It's amazing to have these talented players that appear now, and it's important for us – it is a big, big moment," Pochettino said.
"It's a big moment because we need to get it right with them. We need to protect them. We need to support them.
"Our responsibility now is that this group of talented players grow in the right direction. Today, they were so exciting.
"We need to continue with that idea, to keep that feeling – every time that they can be part of this national team, it's the most important thing."

Asked about Sullivan specifically, Pochettino said of the Philadelphia Union's breakout star: "He's a talented player with enormous quality, but with a very good balance, in possession and out of possession.
"He's a fighter. He's a warrior. It's difficult to find this type of player, no?"
Sullivan told TNT Sports of his history-making strike: "These are moments you dream of since you're three, four, five or six years old. I manifested this moment.
"I probably shouldn't have pressed the goalie; it felt like there was not really anybody pressing behind me. But that's why you go and that's why you put the work in, and I was rewarded for doing so.
"From there, it was sort of a blackout. I just remember chipping the ball, hoping it didn't hit the crossbar or go over. I was getting nervous when it was in the air!"
Sullivan has also had a tremendous campaign for the Union in MLS, breaking single-season records for the most assists (12) and total goal involvements (19, seven goals) by a teenager.

Their young stars shone brightly once again, with 18-year-old Julian Hall scoring for the third time in his first three senior caps, while Sullivan made a piece of history in the second half.

Having intercepted an errant pass from Raul Rangel and lobbed the Mexico goalkeeper from distance, Sullivan – at the age of 17 years and five days – became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

He surpassed Borussia Dortmund's Mathis Albert just four days after he claimed the record from Christian Pulisic, netting at the age of 17 years and 131 days against Chile.

The USA have one more game to play this month, against Canada in Minnesota on Tuesday, and Pochettino is determined to give his young players further chances to impress. 

"It's amazing to have these talented players that appear now, and it's important for us – it is a big, big moment," Pochettino said. 

"It's a big moment because we need to get it right with them. We need to protect them. We need to support them. 

"Our responsibility now is that this group of talented players grow in the right direction. Today, they were so exciting.

"We need to continue with that idea, to keep that feeling – every time that they can be part of this national team, it's the most important thing."

Asked about Sullivan specifically, Pochettino said of the Philadelphia Union's breakout star: "He's a talented player with enormous quality, but with a very good balance, in possession and out of possession.

"He's a fighter. He's a warrior. It's difficult to find this type of player, no?"

Sullivan told TNT Sports of his history-making strike: "These are moments you dream of since you're three, four, five or six years old. I manifested this moment.

"I probably shouldn't have pressed the goalie; it felt like there was not really anybody pressing behind me. But that's why you go and that's why you put the work in, and I was rewarded for doing so.

"From there, it was sort of a blackout. I just remember chipping the ball, hoping it didn't hit the crossbar or go over. I was getting nervous when it was in the air!"

Sullivan has also had a tremendous campaign for the Union in MLS, breaking single-season records for the most assists (12) and total goal involvements (19, seven goals) by a teenager.

evfncmhqwgeg1xgdmv21cayfj.title: Wirtz not set for an immediate introduction to Germany team, says Klopp
evfncmhqwgeg1xgdmv21cayfj.subtitle: Florian Wirtz was one of two call-ups to replace injured players in Germany's squad, but Jurgen Klopp plans to ease him into the fold.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp has no intention of throwing Florian Wirtz straight into his starting line-up for Germany against Greece in the Nations League.

Wirtz had initially been named in Klopp's second squad for the extended international break, but following injuries to Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala, he was brought into the fold a game earlier than planned.
He arrived at the team's training base on Friday and has only had time for one training session with Germany as they prepare for their next match.
It will be Klopp's first on home soil as Germany's head coach – following a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands in his opener – but Wirtz will not be starting the match.
"That would really be a huge ask," Klopp replied when asked if Wirtz was an immediate candidate to start.
"He found out [Friday] morning, arrived here in the evening, and then we say: now that you're here, go straight in and play.
"That would certainly be the worst thing we could do right now."
Wirtz has had a difficult start to this season, coming under criticism for his Liverpool performances so far this season, particularly after their 1-0 victory over Bournemouth.
He has made six appearances for Liverpool in all competitions this term, registering just one assist, despite creating 12 chances – the third-most of any Reds player.
But Klopp, while wary of talking about a Liverpool player as the club’s former manager, is confident Wirtz will only improve.
"No matter what I would say, whether positive or negative, it would be a huge story in this case," Klopp said of Wirtz's situation at Liverpool.
"Flo Wirtz's footballing abilities are beyond any doubt. We will work together on making sure he can show them on the pitch again every three days.

"We will absolutely try whatever we can contribute towards that. In general, I think he is on a very good path. But the world we live in is basically such that things never happen quickly enough for people."
Klopp's debut as Germany boss did not go exactly to plan, with the Netherlands equalising in the 92nd minute, through his former player Cody Gakpo, to deny him all three points.
But Klopp will be determined to make a winning start in Augsburg as he gets the chance to lead the team in front of the home fans for the first time.
Marc-Andre ter Stegen played a huge role in making sure Germany stayed in the game, making nine saves against the Netherlands, who had 22 attempts in total worth 3.2 expected goals (xG).
However, Klopp confirmed he will be making a change to his goalkeeper for the clash with Greece, as Alexander Nubel is set to come in.
"I heard that Marc was viewed critically – that surprised me after a game where the opposing coach said he saved our bacon," Klopp said.
"He made some outstanding saves, but twice he played a ball he didn't intend to – it happens. I'm not at all critical about it, but very happy with his performance.
"Alex will still get to play, not because of that. He deserves it too. I hope he enjoys it and keeps a clean sheet."

evjv177sn6az1n5tofp8cv5dq.title: Ronaldo-Jesus row cannot divide Portugal, says Fernandes
evjv177sn6az1n5tofp8cv5dq.subtitle: Bruno Fernandes says Cristiano Ronaldo remains Portugal's 'greatest symbol', even amid the fallout from his explosive exit from their camp.
paragraphs: Bruno Fernandes says Portugal's players, staff and fans cannot allow the row between Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus to divide them.

Earlier this week, Ronaldo abruptly left Portugal's camp amid reports that he was disgruntled with Jesus making him an unused substitute during a 2-1 Nations League win in Norway, saying he would tell his side of the story in due course.
Jesus has refused to go into detail about his disagreement with Ronaldo, only saying that he would never allow any player to dictate his decisions as a coach.
Without Ronaldo, Fernandes wore the captain's armband for the Selecao on Thursday, as they earned an entertaining 4-2 win over Denmark.
They have won each of their first three games in Nations League Group A4, with some supporters asking whether their attacking play is more fluid without the 41-year-old.

Since the start of 2025, Portugal have won 80% of their matches when Ronaldo has not appeared (P5 W4 D1), compared to 59% when he has featured (P17 W10 D4 L3), also averaging almost twice as many goals per game without Ronaldo (3.4) than with him (1.9).
But Fernandes, a former club-mate of Ronaldo's at Manchester United, says people should avoid taking sides amid the controversy.
His main concerns are that those who remain in the Portugal camp stay united, and that Ronaldo is remembered as Portugal's greatest-ever player if his international career is over.

"I had a conversation with Cristiano, and what I told him, which I'll repeat here, is this: 'The most important thing is that, regardless of what happens, Cristiano Ronaldo will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, of our football, and of the country,'" Fernandes told reporters on Saturday.
"He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people, and the most important thing is that we stop dividing things.
"[The players] are outside this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not make choices and respects all sides.
"But, at the same time, Cristiano is and will be the biggest icon of our national team. He deserves everyone's respect, regardless of who likes him more or less."

Ronaldo's 146 goals in 234 caps are the most by any male player in international football history, and he and great rival Lionel Messi became the first players to play at six different editions of the World Cup this year.

But while Messi led Argentina to a second straight final, scoring eight times and becoming the first player to start three showpiece matches at FIFA's flagship tournament, Ronaldo was restricted to three goals – a group-stage brace against Uzbekistan and a penalty against Croatia in the round of 32.
That spot-kick is the only goal Ronaldo has ever scored in a knockout-stage match at the World Cup, with his other 10 goals at the tournament coming in the group stage.
Porto's Estadio do Dragao will be the venue for Portugal's reverse fixture against Norway on Sunday, with Stale Solbakken's team only having three points on the board so far.

eyjsro6ino351x8tu8qcyqbs7.title: Alaba ready to 'build a new chapter' at Udinese
eyjsro6ino351x8tu8qcyqbs7.subtitle: David Alaba has been officially unveiled as an Udinese player following his signing in September, and he is raring to go.
paragraphs: David Alaba is fit and ready to start his time at Udinese, and he is looking forward to building a "new chapter of my career".
Alaba joined Udinese as a free agent in September, following his departure from Real Madrid at the end of last season.
The 34-year-old brings with him a wealth of European experience, having also spent 13 years with Bayern Munich before making the move to Madrid in 2021.

He won 25 trophies with the Bundesliga giants before going on to win two LaLiga crowns and two Champions League titles, in addition to a Copa del Rey, a Supercopa de Espana, a UEFA Super Cup, a Club World Cup and an Intercontinental Cup with Los Blancos.
However, Alaba's later years in Madrid were hampered by injuries, and he managed just 575 minutes across all competitions last term, but he insists there are no issues with his fitness.
"I feel good, and I feel ready to play," Alaba said, as reported by TuttoMercatoWeb.

"I've already been training with the team for about a week, and I trained hard in the previous months. I've spoken often with [Kosta] Runjaic about my role. I've played a lot as a centre-back, and I feel comfortable there.
"I've played in other positions too, but mainly I feel good as a centre-back. As for the clubs, I can say that yes, I spoke with other Italian clubs.
"I know what kind of player I am, and I'm here to play football. I'm here to write the next pages of my story as a footballer.
"I have a lot of experience, and I want to put it at the team's disposal. I'm less interested in the rumours."
Alaba has said he has high ambitions for what he can achieve with Udinese, who are currently 13th in Serie A after five matches.
But Alaba is looking forward to helping the team this season.
"I spoke mainly with the coach, Runjaic, and he convinced me of the project here," Alaba said.
"I took my time to make a decision, and over time I became convinced that this was perhaps the right path. I believe it's the right step for my career.
"I decided to come here not because of my past, but because I'm ambitious and I always want more. It's an important project, and I think it's the right step for my career.
"I don't need to prove anything to myself, but I came here to build a new chapter of my career and to help the team with my quality and experience."
Alaba could make his Udinese debut on Monday when they return to Serie A action against Torino.

eytwkdcmcjzb18fk8aiwfoso3.title: USWNT defender Fox signs new contract with Arsenal
eytwkdcmcjzb18fk8aiwfoso3.subtitle: Arsenal have handed a new contract to Emily Fox, who has been an ever-present for them in the opening three games of their WSL season.
paragraphs: United States defender Emily Fox has signed a new contract with Arsenal, reportedly to run until 2029.
Since arriving from the North Carolina Courage in January 2024, Fox has made 93 appearances for the Gunners in all competitions, scoring three goals from right-back.
She has helped Arsenal win three major trophies during that span, lifting the League Cup in 2023-24, the Champions League trophy in 2024-25 and the inaugural FIFA Champions Cup earlier this year.
Fox played the full 90 minutes as the Gunners overcame Barcelona 1-0 in the Champions League final 16 months ago, with Stina Blackstenius scoring the all-important goal in Lisbon.
Fox, who has 78 senior caps for the USWNT at the age of 28, appeared in 20 Women's Super League matches last term as Arsenal finished as runners-up to Manchester City, starting 18 of those games.

Only Alessia Russo (1,832) and Mariona Caldentey (1,747) played more WSL minutes than Fox (1,605) for Renee Slegers' team in 2025-26, and she has also been an ever-present at the start of 2026-27, with Arsenal taking five points from their opening three matches.

"I'm so happy to be extending my stay here. This has felt like home since the moment I joined, and I'm so grateful for the opportunity to continue to represent this club and compete for titles," Fox told the club's website.
"To be a part of Arsenal is to be a part of something bigger, and I feel like I'm in the best place to keep pushing for more."
Fox will hope to celebrate her new deal with a statement victory on Sunday as Arsenal go to Stamford Bridge to face Chelsea, having been rested for a 1-0 Champions League win over Koge on Tuesday.

f1dxe0lrw1iw1j1x7yn4bk245.title: Ronaldo motivated by 1,000 goals milestone and leading new Portugal generation
f1dxe0lrw1iw1j1x7yn4bk245.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo hinted at international retirement after Portugal's World Cup exit, but he decided against doing so with more to achieve.
paragraphs: Cristiano Ronaldo believes he can still help Portugal to further success ahead of their Nations League campaign as he closes in on reaching 1,000 career goals.
Ronaldo had already confirmed that this summer's World Cup would be his last, with Portugal losing to eventual champions Spain in the last 16 of the tournament.
The 41-year-old said he would not make any "rash decisions" over his immediate international future, and he was selected in Jorge Jesus' first Portugal squad.
He reunites with Jesus, who he won his first Saudi Pro League title with at Al-Nassr in 2025-26, and he has a fine record under the new Portugal boss.
Ronaldo scored 29 goals in 33 appearances under Jesus for Al-Nassr in the 2025-26 campaign, averaging a goal every 99 minutes.

Throughout his career, the only managers under whom Ronaldo has a better goals-per-game average in league play are Carlo Ancelotti (1.22) and Jose Mourinho (1.13) at Real Madrid, and Luis Castro and Rudi Garcia at Al-Nassr (both 1.1).

He is currently on 979 career goals, 833 of which have come for clubs and 146 for Portugal, but when asked if he had thought about retiring from international duty after the World Cup, Ronaldo responded: "Yes, I did.
"Of course, I'm always thinking about my decisions, my future, the present also. I'm a thinker, you have to think.
"I had a conversation with our president, with our coach. I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to achieve what they want.
"I think I can give the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football."
Portugal are the reigning Nations League holders, beating Spain on penalties in 2024-25, with Ronaldo also winning the title in 2018-19.
Ronaldo said that adding a third title was also an aim alongside his personal ambitions, adding: "Both aims are important.
"One thousand goals, yes, and the national team. Winning the Nations League, the competition starts tomorrow [Thursday], it's a new age."
Portugal welcome Wales to the Estadio Jose Alvalade in the first match of their Europa League campaign and the beginning of a new era under Jesus.
It will also be the first meeting between the two nations since the semi-finals of the 2016 European Championship, with the eventual champions Portugal winning 2-0.
Following their clash with Wales, Portugal will face Norway, away first and then at home, either side of a trip to Denmark.

Jesus has also included the likes of Fabio Silva, Renato Veiga, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves and Francisco Conceicao in his 25-man squad, and Ronaldo revealed the decision behind continuing for Portugal was to help guide the nation's up-and-coming talents.
"This is a new young generation. But for me, the basic point is to be on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games," Ronaldo said.
"For me, the most important thing, I know what I am. I know what I do to be here, to have the success that I have.
"I know why young kids love Cristiano, because they see me as an example, and I will continue to do that. Even when I am retired in 10 years!
"I'm happy with myself. It doesn't matter if I play tomorrow, if I rest for the next game. For me, the most important thing is that I feel good."
