ftbpro_01m43jphx6fj.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s 7 Most Spectacular Tantrums for Club and Country—Ranked
ftbpro_01m43jphx6fj.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath6:00 PM EDTHe’s had it up to here. /  Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty ImagesCristiano Ronaldo will not go gently into that good night. That much is clear.

The 41-year-old superstar’s walkout from the Portugal national team is just the latest example of his absolute refusal to be anything other than the main character in any given situation, with the tail-end of his career pockmarked by a series of increasingly petty (yet entertaining) grievances, sideshows and outbursts.

When Ronaldo does finally hit 1,000 career goals and siuuuuus off into the sunset—shirtless and abs-tensed—we will of course remember the trophies, the leaps, the moments of wonder... But we will also remember the tantrums, for they too are a big part of his gift to soccer.

Nothing to siuuu here. /  pedja milosavljevic/AFP/Getty ImagesRonaldo thought he’d won a tight World Cup qualifier against Serbia deep in stoppage time when he nipped in to finish past the keeper, only for defender Stefan Mitrović to clear the ball out from (clearly) behind the goal line.With no VAR to step in, the referee waved play on much to Ronaldo’s fury. The Portugal captain ended up throwing his armband to the ground after being booked for dissent—a move which raised eyebrows in his homeland.He later attempted to explain his actions on social media posting: “There are difficult times to deal with, especially when we feel that an entire nation is being harmed.”U O.K. hun?

The armband takes the brunt again. / Jasper Juinen/Getty ImagesThat was not the first time the armband had felt the full force of Ronaldo’s ire.Back in a 2010 friendly against neighbors Spain, the then-Real Madrid superstar twisted and wriggled his way through the defense and lifted the ball over keeper Iker Casillas for one of the all-time great international goals... Or, it would have been if Nani had not dived in to head the ball over the line from an offside position.The goal was correctly ruled out and Ronaldo did a weird little dance on the spot before making his armband get up close and personal with the Lisbon grass.Portugal ended up winning 4–0 and Nani sheepishly told reporters he didn’t mean to do it and he was very, very sorry, but neither fact was likely to have shortened Ronaldo’s sulk.

“What are you doing here?” / Angel Martinez/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesWhat we’re learning is that Ronaldo really does not like anyone to get in the way of his goals.Future Fulham manager Álvaro Arbeloa found this out during a routine win over Almería in the latter stages of the 2014–15 season when the defender poked home a cross into the box, nudging in front of Instagram’s most followed man, who had been poised at the back post to add to his own goal tally.As the rest of the Real Madrid players celebrated the novelty of an Arbeloa goal, Ronaldo hammered the ball back into the net angrily with a face like thunder.“I’m not upset about Cristiano’s gesture,” Arbeloa lied after the game.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Tackling the screen-time epidemic, one fan at a time. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesRonaldo’s Manchester United return in 2021 was not quite the glorious homecoming many had hoped it would be.The forward was still banging in goals during the the 2021–22 season, but couldn’t bring United any closer to a trophy, while tensions on and off the field bubbled. A frustrating 1–0 defeat away at Goodison Park proved too much for Ronaldo, who was caught on camera swiping a phone out of a young fan’s hands as he walked down the tunnel after the final whistle.He later received a two-match ban for the incident and was even cautioned by the police. Naughty naughty.

Benched. / Rico Brouwer/Soccrates/Getty ImagesPerhaps the point it all changed for Ronaldo.Up until the 2022 World Cup, you could legitimately make the case that Ronaldo was still one of the very best strikers around and deserved his place in the Portugal lineup on merit. Once the tournament in Qatar got going... Well, it was much harder.The then-37-year-old scored just once (from the penalty spot) in the group stages and was subbed by manager Fernando Santos in a 2–1 defeat to South Korea—an indignity he took with a typical lack of grace and stoicism.Ronaldo huffed, puffed and hung his head on the sidelines, prompting Santos to say of his captain’s conduct postmatch “I didn’t like it, not at all. I didn’t like it.”Santos then benched Ronaldo for the round of 16 clash with Switzerland, with replacement striker Gonçalo Ramos scoring a hat trick. Oops.

See ya never. / Liselotte Sabroe / Ritzau Scanpix/AFP/Getty ImagesThe latest in the Ronaldo catalogue of tantrums is a biggie.After being left on the bench (shock horror) by manager Jorge Jesus for a Nations League win over Norway, the 41-year-old went nuclear.After clear-the-air talks with the Portugal FA that clearly did not clear any air, Ronaldo exited the national team camp, posting on his socials: “In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure.”Portugal went on to beat Denmark 4–2 in their next match without Ronaldo on the roster and Jesus has since refused to back down.Reports suggest Ronaldo may have already played his final match for the national team—an ignominious end for one of soccer’s greats.

It all fell apart at United the second time around. / Oli SCARFF/AFP/Getty ImagesThe GOAT of Ronaldo’s grumps.With relations increasingly tense with new manager Erik ten Hag and goals ever more scarce, Ronaldo decided he’d had enough of it all at some point roughly midway through United’s 2-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League.The five-time Ballon d’Or winner reportedly left Old Trafford before the match was done, effectively calling time on his time at the club.A couple of weeks later an explosive interview with chief sycophant Piers Morgan dropped, during which Ronaldo lashed out at Ten Hag and the United hierarchy, while Wayne Rooney’s looks also caught strays for some reason.Morgan pushed back hard of course, telling Ronaldo at one point: "I know about your aftershave, I use it, it’s very successful, I have to say. People say ‘Ooh, you smell like Cristiano.’”

ftbpro_01m43n44r0v3.title: ‘Unbelievable’—Mauricio Pochettino Breaks His Own Rule With Cavan Sullivan
ftbpro_01m43n44r0v3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom11:30 AM EDTCavan Sullivan had a night to remember on Saturday. / Omar Vega/USSF/Getty ImagesIt was telling that Mauricio Pochettino had to be reminded to comment on Cavan Sullivan’s sensational 35-yard lob after an effusive outburst of praise for the teenager’s overall performance against Mexico. Having rattled through all his tenacious technical qualities, the goal that made him the youngest scorer in U.S. men’s national team history had slipped Pochettino’s mind.
That the USMNT manager was willing to spend any time discussing an individual player is a sign of how high Sullivan already sits in Pochettino’s estimations.

Back in the spacious press room at SoFi Stadium after the USMNT’s emphatic World Cup opener against Paraguay this summer, once the whirr of an air conditioning unit had been silenced at his request, Pochettino shut down every line of questioning into any individual performance. It was not a night to hail Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun or Tim Ream. The team (and the fans) earned the praise of a manager constantly wary of dishing out too many accolades.
Sullivan, it would appear, is an exception to that rule.

“Talented,” “tremendous,” “unbelievable” were some of the superlatives which Pochettino used to hail the 17-year-old’s showing in Saturday’s historic 3–0 victory over Mexico. Sullivan is being treated differently because he is doing things differently to every other U.S. star to cross paths with Pochettino.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC
To be the future you must rewrite history. pic.twitter.com/MID0hojIEy

“He’s a fighter. He’s a warrior,” Pochettino gushed when uncharacteristically opening up about the performance of Sullivan. “It’s difficult to find this type of player with tremendous quality with the ball, in possession, and then [he enjoys] when he needs to chase people and recover the ball. That is my impression after [two] weeks. And that is unbelievable to have a player like this.”
It’s that quality of “balance,” that shared intensity when he is attacking or defending, which has so endeared Sullivan to Pochettino.

The Philadelphia Union phenom earned the chance to humiliate Raúl Rangel with a long-range lob by pressing the Mexican goalkeeper. Pochettino and his coaching staff had actually been imploring Sullivan to keep on charging toward the wandering custodian shortly before his moment of brilliance. The forward instinctively delayed his dart to sucker Rangel into a stray pass which he would ruthlessly punish.

“He’s relentless in the way that he presses, his counter-pressing, all those things,” the USMNT’s new captain Tyler Adams beamed postmatch. Sullivan managed to rack up as many defensive contributions against Mexico as Adams, the team’s ballast at the base of midfield, despite playing 25 fewer minutes. A fact which won’t have passed Pochettino by.
USMNT Player Ratings vs. Mexico—Two Stars Are Born on Dream Night. dark. Next. USMNT ratings Mexico October 2026

Cavan Sullivan scored the USMNT’s second goal against Mexico on Saturday. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesPochettino was not only besotted by Sullivan’s behavior on the pitch. “I liked what he said after the game, ‘The most important [thing] was the result.’ [He’s] learning every day,” the U.S. boss beamed, “that is the good thing.”

Sullivan may have only turned 17 on Monday but he is a mature character with a feverish work ethic and clear idea about his career. This is a kid who does the dishes and goes to training rather than partying—he celebrated his recent birthday in the U.S. camp with a small cake.

That dedication has been apparent throughout his embryonic career. In preparation for a youth tournament in Spain, the then-13-year-old took a proactive approach to combating jet lag by progressively waking up half an hour earlier each day.
The occasion of his first senior international goal almost overwhelmed Pochettino’s new star pupil, but not quite. “If it wasn’t so hype,” Sullivan smiled, “I think I would’ve probably shed a tear.”

ftbpro_01m43rsv1h5d.title: Transfer Rumors: Haaland’s Two Choices; Real Madrid Eye £75 Million Premier League Star
ftbpro_01m43rsv1h5d.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC Staff7:05 PM EDTErling Haaland (left) and Alex Scott headline the gossip. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images (Scott), Bradley Collyer/PA Images/Getty Images (Scott)Sports Illustrated rounds up the latest transfer rumors and gossip from around the world.

Benjamin Šeško could be leaping to a new club. / Darren Staples/AFP/Getty ImagesIn the face of rampant interest from half of Europe, Erling Haaland has narrowed his Manchester City exit routes down to two options: Real Madrid or Barcelona. (Source: El Nacional)

Interest from Juventus and Barcelona in Benjamin Šeško has prompted Manchester United to set an asking price of €75 million ($84.4 million), which would represent a loss on what the Red Devils paid a little over a year ago. (Source: TuttoJuve)
Manchester United are prepared to battle Liverpool for the signature of Micky van de Ven, although Tottenham Hotspur are opposed to his sale entirely. (Source: Fichajes)
Any chance of a move as soon as January for Van de Ven is deemed to be minimal despite competing Premier League interest. (Source: Football Insider)
Xabi Alonso has given the green light for Chelsea to plough forward with a €120 million ($135 million) offer for Barcelona star Fermín López. (Source: El Nacional)

Liverpool have identified Brentford fullback Michael Kayode as a priority defensive addition next year. There will, however, be competition from the likes of Arsenal and Tottenham. (Source: CaughtOffside)

Kenan Yıldız is perennially linked with a Juventus exit. / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesAlex Scott—Bournemouth’s talented English midfielder on the radar of Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool—has now been billed as a target for Real Madrid. ftbpro_01m43srngc8a.title: Three Ways Vinicius Jr Can Turn Around His Real Madrid Form
ftbpro_01m43srngc8a.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath8:00 PM EDTVinícius Jr is threatening to become a problem player. /  Maciej Rogowski/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesIt’s been a tough few months for Vinícius Jr.
The Brazilian has openly admitted that Brazil’s disappointing round of 16 exit to Norway at the World Cup was hard to take and had a knock-on effect on his confidence.

By the first international break, Vinícius Jr had scored just once for Real Madrid in the 2026–27 season—a stat which has loomed especially large given the mega-money contract extension the forward recently signed after over a year of protracted negotiations and flirtations with Arsenal.
While Madrid manager José Mourinho has defended Vinícius from the Bernabéu boo boys, he has admitted the superstar, who came second in the 2024 Ballon d’Or vote, “isn’t at his best.”
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC
The Madrid derby defeat was a low point for both Los Blancos and Vinícius personally, with the forward putting in a limp display before being substituted after less than an hour.

A break from the Madrid fishbowl for Brazil duty has largely failed to provide the reset the 26-year-old needs, with his showing in the friendly win over India in Kolkata raising eyebrows. Vinícius completed only seven of 13 passes, attempted zero dribbles and missed one big chance against the team ranked 138th in the world by FIFA before coming off at halftime.

The star’s only goal in three matches this international break has come from the penalty spot—the fourth in a 4–2 win over Australia—and he looks far from the world-beating match-winner of recent memory.
Incredibly, a player who has scored 129 goals—including two in Champions League finals—is threatening to become a problem for Real Madrid.

The Vinícius Jr situation is already one of the dominant narratives of Madrid’s season, with the club trailing Barcelona by six points in La Liga and in danger of a third straight season without a major trophy.
Madrid have a crunch period coming up with the first Clásico of the season rearing into view on Oct. 25, and will need all their stars firing to compete on all fronts this season.

Dealing with an out-of-sorts superstar like Vinícius is one of the first big tests for Mourinho upon his return. Does the 63-year-old, once hailed for his man-management skills, still have what to takes to get the best out of his players?

Mbappé and Vinícius Jr have struggled to connect. / Federico Titone/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesOne of the big issues for Madrid ever since the arrival of Kylian Mbappé is the space he and Vinícius occupy on the pitch.
L’Equipe posted a damning graphic after the Madrid derby that showed the average positions of all Madrid players, with Mbappé and Vinícius essentially on top of one another.
The central problem is that Mbappé is a striker who drifts to the left rather than staying central, inevitably meaning the two players often overlap—and not in a good way.

Mourinho has made Mbappé key to his plans as the spearhead of the 4-2-3-1 system and it has paid dividends, with the Frenchman scoring seven in seven in La Liga so far in 2026–27. However, it has, in part, curbed the effectiveness of Vinícius.
No manager has pulled it off it yet, but some systemic tinkering might allow both to flourish without cramping each other’s styles. What that would actually look like though is hard to say.

Vinícius Jr hasn’t felt the love from Madrid fans recently. / Richard Haines/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesVinícius has always been a streaky player rather than a consistent goal threat and has thrived when made to feel like the main man.

Prior to Mbappé’s arrival, he shone as the star in the Champions League-winning team of 2023–24 when he was relied upon to produce those moments of magic and then felt the love of the Bernabéu when he did.

The contract saga has seemingly damaged the Brazilian’s standing among the notoriously demanding Madrid supporters, who have booed and whistled him regularly this season as penance for daring to a) drag out his renewal talks and b) be out of form.

ftbpro_01m43tk1z8sn.title: Man Utd Receive Huge Double Injury Boost Ahead of Premier League Return
ftbpro_01m43tk1z8sn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom12:45 PM EDTFinally there was some cause for celebration for Michael Carrick. / NurPhoto via Getty ImagesInjury updates in international breaks invariably take a negative slant for the game’s club sides, as Manchester United can attest already this fall. However, Michael Carrick was able to welcome Carlos Baleba and Matthijs de Ligt onto the pitch in a rare flicker of positive fitness news.

This elongated club hiatus has been so long that United found the time to stage a friendly with sister side Lausanne Sport. The visit of a fellow INEOS sporting investment offered Carrick the chance to try out some youngsters, give the few senior stars not involved in international duty some minutes and get a pair of treatment table regulars out on the grass.

Baleba is still waiting to make his Manchester United debut after signing for the club from Brighton in a deal worth up to £70 million ($92.5 million). The Cameroon international was deemed fit enough for the substitutes’ bench in United’s trip to Fulham on the eve of the break but did not get onto the pitch as his teammates toiled to a 1–1 draw.
Carrick has previously said that the 22-year-old is “pushing to get back as quickly as possible” and had the perfect opportunity to unshackle his new midfielder against Lausanne.

Carlos Baleba is still waiting for his competitive debut. / Poppy Townson/MUFC/Manchester United/Getty ImagesThe side current sat at the foot of the Swiss top flight also served as forgiving opposition for the lesser spotted De Ligt. Manchester United’s injury riddled center back is coming up to a year on the sidelines, with his last competitive appearance for the club all the way back in November 2025, when Ruben Amorim was still at the helm.

De Ligt underwent surgery on a nagging back problem in May which ruled out any involvement in this summer’s World Cup. The Dutch defender returned to first-team training in recent weeks and took his recovery up another level by featuring for United in this behind-closed-doors friendly.

It remains to be seen when De Ligt will be ready for a competitive return, although the Manchester Evening News suggest it could be as soon as next weekend’s Premier League clash with Tottenham Hotspur.

Marcus Rashford (left) and Kobbie Mainoo both pulled out of England duty. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesIt’s not all been plainsailing for Carrick this fall. Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo both had to pull out of England duty before a ball had even been kicked. An ongoing hip problem has been cited as the cause of Rashford’s enforced absence while his compatriot’s withdrawal was unexplained.

Benjamin Šeško also never made it to Slovenia’s international camp after a recurrence of a nagging shin injury at the end of September. “I am already working on getting back on the pitch as soon as possible to help both the national team and my club once again,” the workaholic promised.

Then there are the players who did go on to represent their country but may come to regret that decision. In a cruel twist of fate for Carrick, two of his potential left back alternatives were both forced to withdraw during the window.

Patrick Dorgu only lasted 30 minutes against Wales last weekend before pulling up with a hamstring complaint. Noussair Mazraoui collapsed in a heap against Lesotho after attempting and failing to complete an awkward tackle. The versatile pair have returned to Carrington to receive treatment from United’s medical department with one eye firmly fixed on a must-win visit from Spurs.

ftbpro_01m43tpn69ap.title: Why Cristiano Ronaldo Isn’t Playing for Portugal vs. Norway
ftbpro_01m43tpn69ap.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray1:45 PM EDTCristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal future hangs in the balance. / Grzegorz Wajda/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesIt’s been a blistering start for Portugal manager Jorge Jesus, who has masterminded three successive victories to kickstart his tenure.

The veteran coach clinched a narrow victory over Wales during his dugout debut, before proceeding to conquer both Norway and Denmark during awkward away days. As things stand, Portugal sits at the summit of its UEFA Nations League group with maximum points.
But Jesus’s reign hasn’t been without its complications.
Cristiano Ronaldo’s absence has taken center stage during the current international window and the 41-year-old will once again sit out Portugal’s upcoming clash with Norway on Sunday.
Here’s why the legendary striker won’t be involved.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Ronaldo’s tantrum has caused a stir. / Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty ImagesRonaldo has always been a combustible character, meaning it was little surprise to see him explode with rage after being snubbed by Jesus, who was formerly his manager at Al Nassr, during the reverse fixture with Norway last week.

Following a disastrous display against Wales which culminated in an early substitution, Ronaldo was dropped to the bench for the subsequent clash in Oslo. However, despite having been promised some minutes by Jesus, he was an unused substitute in the 2–1 win.
With the Seleção das Quinas needing to protect their narrow advantage, Jesus opted against throwing Ronaldo into the mix late in proceedings.
“I can promise whatever I want, I’m the coach,” Jesus said after the game. “No player will ever make a decision for me.”

Ronaldo’s reaction was, well, as expected. The five-time Ballon d’Or was incensed by his omission and Jesus’s remarks in the aftermath, and he then decided to leave the current Portugal camp with immediate effect—ruling him out of contention for the 4–2 win over Denmark and the home game with Norway.

Jesus refused to mince his words when discussing the Ronaldo situation.  / Horacio Villalobos/Corbis/Getty Images“After the press conference of the National Team coach, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I decided to leave the National Team camp,” Ronaldo wrote on social media earlier this week.
“In due time, I will tell all the Portuguese about the reasons that motivated my departure from the national team, which I always dedicated myself to.
“Now it’s time to wish good luck to Portugal and all my teammates, without exception.”

Ronaldo’s absence from the roster for the upcoming battle with an Erling Haaland-inspired Norway will once again dominate the headlines around the fixture, while also casting doubt over his future with the national team.

Billboards have been erected in support of Ronaldo. / PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA/AFP/Getty ImagesFollowing 23 years of service for Portugal and considering his status as a national icon, it was hardly shocking that many supporters leapt to Ronaldo’s defense—with some even erecting billboards to showcase their support.

Prominently placed in Lisbon and the wider area, the billboards read: “Thank you Cristiano Ronaldo for everything you’ve done for Portugal. You will always be our captain. Portugal is always with you.”
They also took aim at new boss Jesus, whom they accused of “mistreating” Ronaldo and possessing an “inflated ego.”
Unfortunately for the Portuguese Football Federation, the saga continues to rumble on.

ftbpro_01m43x4cbc4q.title: ‘We Really Should’—Zinedine Zidane Weighs in on Cristiano Ronaldo Debate
ftbpro_01m43x4cbc4q.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom2:15 PM EDTZinédine Zidane (right) and Cristiano Ronaldo won three Champions League titles together. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/ Getty ImagesCristiano Ronaldo’s former Real Madrid manager Zinédine Zidane has insisted that the world “really should celebrate” the Portuguese forward’s “great career” rather than scrutinize how it may be crumbling toward an ugly conclusion.

The fondness between Zidane and Ronaldo was forged by the years they shared together at Real Madrid. After serving as the club’s advisor, sporting director and then assistant manager, Zidane took on the top job in January 2016. Within the space of two-and-a-half years, Madrid had won three Champions League titles and La Liga while Ronaldo racked up more than a century of goals.

Given the gravitas earned from a playing career almost as lauded as Ronaldo’s, Zidane is one of the few managers in the game to have been able to rest his star man without losing his trust. Jorge Jesus tried to name a 41-year-old Ronaldo as a substitute for consecutive Portugal fixtures during the ongoing international break but only inspired his hasty exit.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed
Ronaldo’s conduct has been one of the dominant headlines this fall but Zidane was in no mood to criticize his former player.

“We really should celebrate his great career,” the France boss insisted when faced with this Ronaldo conundrum. “What he’s done is exceptional. I was lucky to have him on my team; he helped me win some incredible things. So hats off to Cristiano. I have a lot of respect for all players in general, but even more so for those I’ve spent time with—especially Cristiano, who helped us win so many titles.”
x3 Champions League, x1 La Liga, x2 Club World Cup, x1 UEFA Super Cup, x1 Supercopa de España
If this is the end, it wasn’t meant to end this way. pic.twitter.com/IoHayRTesH

While Zidane is entitled to give his informed view on the topic, the most pertinent set of people impacted by Ronaldo’s latest strop is the Portuguese public. One of the leading sports dailies led with the headline ‘CR11’ as Portugal put in a team performance to make up for the absence of its famous No. 7. The results of Jesus’s side have been defiantly positive in the face of Ronaldo’s absence, yet opinions are still split.

A poll commissioned by TVI and CNN Portugal found that there is an almost even split within the country when it comes to Ronaldo’s involvement in the next international break; 35% of those questioned were willing to see the 41-year-old extend his record-breaking career, while 37% thought his time had come. It was similarly close on the question of his international retirement, although only 10% considered Ronaldo worthy of a regular starting place.

The most interesting takeaway was the level of support afforded to Jesus. The last international manager to bench Ronaldo was Fernando Santos, the first coach to ever lead his nation to not one but two international trophies. The gamble initially worked—Ronaldo’s replacement for the 2022 World Cup round of 16, Gonçalo Ramos, scored a hat trick—but Santos was still dismissed when Portugal lost the subsequent quarterfinal.

Jesus is only three months into his new job and appears to have won the public around with his firm stance on Ronaldo. The 72-year-old admitted that he failed to fulfill his promise of bringing the veteran off the bench against Norway and would not back down when sitting opposite Ronaldo and the head of the Portuguese FA during emergency talks.
However, some billboards in Lisbon would suggest that Jesus’s approval rating is not quite bulletproof—he’s certainly lost at least one Portuguese citizen this fall.

ftbpro_01m43zhpyrav.title: ‘Leading’—Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool’s Race to Sign Alex Scott Takes Shape
ftbpro_01m43zhpyrav.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray4:00 PM EDTAlex Scott has won the admiration of Premier League giants. / Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesThe future remains uncertain for Bournemouth star Alex Scott amid significant transfer interest, but it’s currently Chelsea who are reportedly “leading the race” to sign the highly-coveted midfielder.

The 23-year-old’s rapid ascent at the Vitality Stadium has naturally grabbed the attention of Europe’s elite teams, as well as resulting in a promotion to England’s senior squad for the current international period.
Scott dazzled on his full debut during England’s 7–0 demolition of Croatia, offering yet another example of his unique blend of athleticism, tenacity and grace in the engine room.

Chelsea’s longstanding interest in the precocious midfielder yielded more than one bid for his signature in the most recent transfer window, but Bournemouth swiftly rejected all said offers—which were reportedly in excess of $79 million (£60 million).
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

As per the Telegraph, the Blues will revive their interest in Scott over the coming year and are currently leading the race to sign him amid links with their Premier League rivals Arsenal and Liverpool.

While Bournemouth have apparently ruled out a winter sale of their prized asset, Chelsea are willing to wait until next summer for Scott, who will have just one year remaining on his contract at that point.
But with Chelsea facing competition for his services, where will Scott end up next?

Arsenal invested in their midfield over the summer by signing Bruno Guimarães. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesOne of Scott’s named suitors, Arsenal, would prove a highly appealing option. After all, how often does the opportunity arise to join the Premier League champions? One consideration for Scott must be playing time, however, and there would be fierce competition for minutes at the Emirates Stadium. Arsenal already boasted some exceptional midfield options before last summer’s window. Declan Rice, of course, remains the headline act, but Myles Lewis-Skelly, Mikel Merino, Martin Ødegaard, Martín Zubimendi, Eberechi Eze and even the versatile Kai Havertz is an impressive supporting cast.Now the fight for minutes is even more intense in north London, with the arrival of Bruno Guimarães adding yet another dynamic to Mikel Arteta’s midfield.Arsenal certainly have more pressing areas of their squad which require bolstering, most notably the left wing and center forward positions. Scott would be an excellent addition, but undoubtedly a luxury one.

Liverpool need midfield reinforcements. / Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty ImagesUnlike Arsenal, Liverpool do find themselves desperate for greater quality and depth in midfield. Currently, Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch are the three prominent options in the double pivot. Trey Nyoni is a precocious academy graduate but just 19 years old, while Wataru Endō is little more than an emergency option in times of trouble. Having spent last summer adding quality to their forward line and defense, the Reds are expected to target a new midfielder in the coming windows. There is understandable clamor for a defensive midfield specialist given Liverpool’s persistent struggles at the back, but Scott remains difficult to ignore when assessing midfield targets. Andoni Iraola is the manager who helped propel him into the limelight at Bournemouth and Liverpool know the midfielder would thrive within the Spaniard’s high-octane pressing system. What has made Scott stand out at Bournemouth is his ability to straddle both defensive and attacking sides of the game, with few better all-rounders currently plying their trade in the Premier League. There’s no doubt he would improve Liverpool.

Xabi Alonso needs at least one new midfielder in January. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesChelsea also find themselves eager for midfield reinforcements after an unsatisfactory end to the summer transfer window. After losing Enzo Fernández at the 11th hour and failing to sign Lamine Camara as his replacement, they find themselves alarmingly light of options. Moisés Caicedo’s injury issues early in the campaign have exposed Chelsea’s lack of depth, with Valentín Barco, Jordan Henderson, Roméo Lavia, Reece James and Malo Gusto hardly an inspiring set of options in his absence—and the latter two also tasked with playing in the defense when necessary. It seems inevitable that Xabi Alonso will be gifted at least one midfielder this winter. The Telegraph insist that any move for Scott wouldn’t impact a separate deal for Camara, who appears a more likely addition in January than the Bournemouth star. With Chelsea willing to wait until next summer for Scott, Stamford Bridge appears the most probable destination. Scott would be joining a young and hungry team, coached by one of the most exciting managers on the planet. Game time would be guaranteed and he would be offered greater attacking freedom than at Arsenal or Liverpool given Caicedo’s defensive prowess.It seems inevitable that Chelsea will significantly up their previous offers for Scott in the near future.

ftbpro_01m45a7yat19.title: From Devil to Deity: How Lionel Messi Rewrote His Argentina Story
ftbpro_01m45a7yat19.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom9:00 AM EDTLionel Messi was not always Argentina’s hero. In fact, he spent longer as the nation’s villain. / Francois Nel/Getty ImagesIt’s both depressing and oddly fitting that New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium, that giant air conditioner plonked in the middle of a sprawling parking lot, should end the international career of the greatest player in the history of the sport—not once, but twice.

Lionel Messi’s final competitive appearance for Argentina, the last he would ever play before his father passed away, was a defeat to Spain in this summer’s World Cup final. A decade earlier, that same potato field in East Rutherford was the scene of Messi’s first international retirement.

“For me, the national team is over,” Argentina’s beleaguered No. 10 meekly revealed in the bowels of the MetLife, hunched over and clutching a wash bag after missing a penalty in a shootout defeat which handed Chile the 2016 Copa América. “I wanted this title more than any other but it wasn’t meant to be.”

Two finals, two defeats and two international retirements in the same soulless pit of concrete. However, the universal love-in which has greeted Messi’s decision to definitively step away from the blue and white stripes this time around is remarkably different to the vast array of emotions he inspired at his first retirement.

Lionel Messi had a tough time with the Argentine media. / Chris McGrath/Getty ImagesThe editor of the popular publication Diario El Sol, Federico Brusotti, once wrote: “There is something more Argentine than dulce de leche. It is our ability to turn our athletes into heroes or villains.”
While it can be hard to imagine given his current godly status, Messi has actually spent more time as Argentina’s villain than its hero.

By his own description, the nation’s all-time leading appearance maker and top scorer was “blamed, cursed at, lied about with no apparent remorse” for more than a decade while on international duty. There were reasons for this hate, just no justifiable ones.

Diego Maradona (left) and Lionel Messi were very different characters. / JAVIER SORIANO/AFP/Getty ImagesBorocotó, the revered editor of the seminal magazine El Gráfico, came up with what the physical embodiment of the Argentine game should look like in 1928:

“A pibe [urchin] with a dirty face, a mane of hair rebelling against the comb; with intelligent, roving, trickster and persuasive eyes and a sparkling gaze that seem to hint at a picaresque laugh that does not quite manage to form on his mouth, full of small teeth that might be worn down through eating yesterday’s bread.”

Almost half a century later, Diego Maradona would debut for Argentina, turning that description into flesh and giving rise to an obsession which would last for almost another 50 years. The 1986 World Cup winner was not far from the status of a deity, with some of his disciples even setting up a Church of Maradona.

This suffocating level of acclaim was the consequence of Maradona’s play and his personality. He was the pibe who rose from poverty to the pinnacle of soccer (and thereby life), quite literally freeing himself from a pile of human excrement in the slums of his childhood.

Messi is a different character entirely. Also short, slight and left footed, but there was no raw sewage in the lower middle class home of his youth. Not that any average Argentinian would know much about Messi’s upbringing or anything he did off the pitch given his chronic reluctance to utter a single word—in public or private.

One of Messi’s school teachers recalled a classmate speaking on behalf of little Leo, such was his fear of being heard. When he joined Barcelona’s youth team, Cesc Fàbregas “thought he was mute.” Juan Sebastián Verón remembered a petrified Messi pacing around their shared room before he had to give his first team talk as Argentina captain: “The kid didn’t know what to do.”

The contrasts with his predecessor were sharp. Messi got criticized for mistakenly walking past a child’s outstretched hand while lost in contemplation after a match. Maradona spent his postgame fiddling with a prosthetic dummy penis to evade doping tests. Messi stopped talking to journalists in protest, Maradona opened fire on them with an air rifle.

The issue for Messi, particularly during the early years of his Argentina career, was that these differences with the country’s greatest idol were impossible to avoid while Maradona was his actual manager for the national team.

Lionel Messi became the target. / Ryan Pierse/FIFA/Getty ImagesThe great player was no grand tactician, cycling haphazardly through more than 80 call-ups as Argentina unconvincingly qualified for the 2010 World Cup. Messi went seven months without an international goal at one point in the buildup to a tournament he failed to score at entirely. After a humiliating quarterfinal exit to Germany, the narrative which had been forming was clearly set: Blame Messi.

“He isn’t ready to shoulder the burden of the team; he isn’t cut out to take on the role of playmaker,” Martín Palermo, Messi’s former international teammate, scoffed after the tournament. “Messi doesn’t have Maradona’s mentality.”

At the 2011 Copa América on home soil, Messi went through another major tournament without a goal and was booed by the Santa Fé crowd. “He leaves Argentina truly hurt every time people speak ill of him,” Messi’s mother Celia Cuccitini fretted. “Why is it always him? He suffers a great deal; he leaves feeling terrible, and it takes him a long time to bounce back.”
Ironically, had Messi shown Argentina his suffering, it may have stopped.

Messi’s popularity rating sunk so low La Nación’s Claudio Mauri quipped that he had “less fans than a referee.” Hernán Claus recalled in Olé that Messi was accused of “not knowing the national anthem, that he feels Spanish, that he doesn’t love the shirt.”

ftbpro_01m45m1the42.title: Man Utd Manager Target Responds to Links of Premier League Return
ftbpro_01m45m1the42.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom7:00 AM EDTAntonio Conte is currently unattached. / Ivan Romano/Getty ImagesAntonio Conte would not currently appear to be pining for a return to management, particularly not the meat grinder that is modern Manchester United.

The former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss has been one of the names linked with a potential appointment at United, who have endured an underwhelming start to the new season. The pressure is not yet insufferable for Michael Carrick, but a failure to rediscover the sort of form which inspired his permanent appointment over the summer may cause the itchy trigger fingers in United’s boardroom to twitch.

The prospect of a manager as illustrious as Conte bouncing around free agency will only ramp up the speculation. However, the Premier League winner has played down his ambitions of a swift return to the dugout.

Conte had to virtually dial into an Italian festival celebrating his legendary former Juventus side over the weekend. “I would’ve liked to be there with you, but at this moment I am not in Italy,” he grinned. “I’m still enjoying my vacation, seeing as this year I have the opportunity to rest and relax.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

There would be no time for any R&R in the goldfish bowl of Old Trafford, although Conte’s intensity is part of his appeal. The manager whose “words assault you,” according to his former player Andrea Pirlo, has a rampant league record, winning five Serie A titles with three clubs (Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli) while also lifting the Premier League during his first season at Chelsea. Even his record at Tottenham Hotspur, who qualified for the Champions League under his watch and were fifth when he left the following year, looks impressive in light of the turmoil which has followed.
The appeal of Conte for most Manchester United fans is obvious, but one of the Old Trafford regulars with the loudest voice has poured cold water on this idea in the past.

Antonio Conte won the Premier League in his first stint in England. / Matthew Peters/Manchester United/Getty ImagesWhen Ole Gunnar Solskjær’s role at Manchester United came under scrutiny in 2021, there was a widespread clamor to appoint Conte. Gary Neville was one of the few public figures who railed against the idea. “He’s a great manager but I think certain managers fit certain clubs and I don’t think Conte fits United personally,” the former United right back argued. “As I say, great manager but doesn’t feel right for me that one.”

Neville’s argument was that United would be best advised avoiding a “hitman” type. The club had been burned by targeting a serial winner such as José Mourinho. For the few trophies that the Portuguese boss won, the scorched earth he left behind had a far longer lasting impact.

Conte has not exactly mellowed in the five years since Neville’s verdict. The outspoken Italian combusted at Tottenham, unleashing a withering takedown of the club’s fundamental character. He would win again at Napoli, steering the club to only their second ever Serie A title without Diego Maradona, but was constantly fighting with his players and upper management, invariably about transfers, or a lack thereof.

“At Napoli I failed in one thing: I didn’t bring unity to the environment and so it’s difficult to compete with others,” Conte admitted when he stepped down over the summer. “I failed because I didn’t unite everyone and I put my hands up. I realize that things cannot be changed.”
United is a fragile environment which needs plenty of unity. Carrick offers that calm head which will avoid combustion but he may also lack Conte’s proven killer edge.

ftbpro_01m45n1jrdgz.title: Croatia vs. Spain—Nations League: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m45n1jrdgz.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray8:00 PM EDTSpain is looking to pile further misery on Croatia. / Alex Caparros/FIFA/Getty Images (Croatia), Instagram/sefutbol (Spain)Spain is seeking to make it four victories from four in the UEFA Nations League as it closes the current international window by visiting Croatia on Tuesday.

The world champion has been typically excellent in Group 3 of League A, kicking things off with an entertaining 3–2 win over England. Things were much more emphatic in triumphs over Croatia and Czechia, however, which extended La Roja’s winning streak to 10 matches in all competitions.

Having thrashed Croatia 4–1 in the reverse fixture, Spain travels to Split with the expectation of securing back-to-back wins. Lamine Yamal was particularly impressive in the reverse fixture, scoring twice and providing an assist to continue his stellar form.

Slaven Bilić’s return to the Croatia hot seat has been pretty disastrous to date. Following a narrow win over Czechia and the defeat to Spain, the 58-year-old oversaw the nation’s worst-ever loss during an embarrassing 7–0 defeat to England on home soil. Massive improvements are needed to avoid yet more humiliation against La Roja.
This is a repeat of the 2022–23 Nations League final, which Spain won on penalties after 120 minutes of goalless action.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Lamine Yamal (right) has been in inspired form for Spain. / David Fernandez/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesRewind a year or two and this would have been a very different fixture. But Croatia’s rapid decline and dismal start under Bilić means Spain should run out handsome winners yet again.

La Roja have been in breathless attacking form, scoring three or more in each of their Nations League matches to date. While they are yet to keep a clean sheet, an inspired attacking unit led by Barcelona superstar Yamal has proven too much for opponents.

Meanwhile, Croatia’s defense has been utterly atrocious this international break, allowing 12 goals across three matches. One would expect the 2018 World Cup runner-up to take a more cautious approach on Tuesday to help steady the ship, but Spain’s fearsome forwards will be licking their lips regardless.
Croatia must make changes from Saturday’s humiliation. / FotMobHaving named arguably his strongest possible lineup against England, Bilić doesn’t have much room to maneuver for Spain’s visit.

Two changes could come in defense, however, with Joško Gvardiol shifting to left back and Josip Šutalo joining Luka Vuškovic at center half. Josip Stanišic could be replaced at right back by Ivan Smolčić.
After being overrun in midfield against England, Luka Modrić might be sacrificed for greater defensive security, with Mateo Kovačić dropping into a double pivot with Josip Mišić.
Igor Matanović could come into the attack to lead the line, replacing FC Dallas striker Petar Musa.
Croatia predicted lineup vs. Spain (4-2-3-1): Livaković; Smolčić, Vušković, Šutalo, Gvardiol; Mišić, Kovačić; Vlašić, P. Sučić, Baturina; Matanović.

Luis de la Fuente has the capacity to make changes without sacrificing quality. / FotMobLuis de la Fuente has been offered several selection headaches by recent withdrawals. Nico Williams, Ferran Torres and Álex Grimaldo have all left the camp, but that has offered opportunities to others.
For example, Espanyol striker Roberto Fernández led the line against Czechia in place of Ferran, although Mikel Oyarzabal is expected to return for the game with Croatia.
Álex Baena should continue at left wing following Williams’s departure, while Martín Zubimendi might come into the midfield to offer Rodri a well-earned rest.
There could be multiple changes in defense. Pau Cubarsí will return after being rested against Czechia, while Marc Cucurella and Marc Pubill should make comebacks in the fullback positions.
Unai Simón should return between the posts after David Raya earned a rare start last time out.
Spain predicted lineup vs. Croatia (4-2-3-1): Simón; Pubill, Cubarsí, Laporte, Cucurella; Zubimendi, Pedri; Yamal, Fermín, Baena; Oyarzabal.

ftbpro_01m45pa2z8k8.title: ‘Misunderstanding’—Portugal Chief Pleads for Cristiano Ronaldo Crisis Talks
ftbpro_01m45pa2z8k8.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott7:30 AM EDTCristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal future is unclear. / Octavio Passos/Getty ImagesPortugal manager Jorge Jesus has insisted Cristiano Ronaldo will be welcome in future international windows as the president of the nation’s Football Federation urged everyone involved to sit down and work through “a misunderstanding.”

Ronaldo left camp just two games into this extended window after a disagreement with Jesus, who left the veteran striker on the bench and then refused to apologize in a subsequent press conference. Reports suggested Ronaldo felt “betrayed” by the manager.
Behind the scenes, Portugal officials swiftly started looking at ways to rebuild Ronaldo’s relationship with the national team. A public charm offensive appears to be phase one.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Jorge Jesus hopes to make peace with Ronaldo. / Horacio Villalobos/Corbis/Getty ImagesManager Jesus has spent the past week insisting he did not even believe there was an issue between Ronaldo and himself.

After his side’s 2–1 over Norway, which was decided by a goal from the player who has replaced Ronaldo in the team, Gonçalo Ramos, Jesus was adamant this does not need to be the end of Ronaldo’s international career.
“I don’t know what will happen,” he said. “As far as I’m concerned, everything is open.
“It’s up to Cris to decide his own life. In the next call-up, if Cris is playing and wants to be in the national team, why not?
“It was a misunderstanding. In my opinion, it’s easy to resolve. When will I resolve it? I don’t know. The game is over, and only afterwards will we know how things will turn out.
Jesus added: “I haven’t spoken to him. It was a poorly resolved issue, there wasn’t really an issue. Something was created out of nothing, a problem that led to what it led to.

“I’m a coach, the national team manager. I don’t make the decisions. I’m part of a whole. If everyone wants to share what they think is best for the national team, I’m open to everything. [Ronaldo] is the one who decides what he wants for his life. As it was before the first call-up, it will be the same before the second. We shared before the first, and if he's interested, we'll share again in the second.
“I'm not the one who’s going to decide, nor can I. It’s not sad ... It was a year working with Cris. We have a very strong professional friendship.”

Ronaldo faces a huge decision about his next move. / Carlos Rodrigues/Getty ImagesAs Ronaldo weighed up his decision to leave the Portugal camp, officials from the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) got involved to try and avoid an issue with the greatest player in the nation’s history.

FPF president Pedro Proença initially tried to avoid discussing the subject during a recent interview with RTP—“This is a matter between the coach and the player”—but made sure to offer plenty of public support to Ronaldo.
“We are talking about one of the best players of all time,” Proença said. “We must pay homage to Cristiano Ronaldo. He is in the national team on his own merit, and that is unquestionable.
“He knows about this feeling. We are facing a misunderstanding, and this has to be resolved internally.”

Proença added: “Cristiano Ronaldo is part of our national team, he is our flag. And Jorge Jesus says he counts on Ronaldo. [Ronaldo] is an extraordinary player who could have ended his international career at the World Cup, but out of love for the national team, he didn’t.
“Now that these four games are over, we will have the time and peace of mind to all sit down and find a solution to this misunderstanding.
“Cristiano Ronaldo is part of our heritage and will always be here, if the manager wants him.”

ftbpro_01m45qw649q4.title: ‘Just Insane’—Norway Boss Provides Erling Haaland Update After Injury Scare
ftbpro_01m45qw649q4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom7:30 AM EDTErling Haaland asked to come off in Porto.  / Joao Gregorio/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesNorway manager Ståle Solbakken played down Erling Haaland’s enforced substitution as a case of fatigue thanks to a “grueling schedule” which, in his eyes, “is just insane.”

Haaland started all four of Norway’s Nations League fixtures this fall but asked to come off midway through the second half of Sunday’s clash with Portugal. The sight of Manchester City’s star striker wobbling off to the bench caused all manner of concern at the Etihad ahead of this weekend’s trip to Liverpool in the Premier League. Rather than any serious ailment, Haaland appears to be a victim of the modern game.

“There are many players who are really exhausted,” Solbakken explained. “[Sander] Berge and [Martin] Ødegaard are practically scraping rock bottom. Erling was digging deep for a long time. I think he took a real beating and served as an excellent target man. We were hoping for 60, and he managed 65. That’s a lot of positives.”

Heading into the clash with Portugal in Porto, Haaland had already been aware that he would not last the entirety of the contest. There had been discussion about saving the relentless scorer for the second half, but that was soon quashed.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

“He put in a good 60 minutes today,” Solbakken reasoned. “He played two full 90-minute matches against Denmark and Portugal. He was tired against Wales. That’s why we had a heart-to-heart yesterday. We went through the various possibilities.

“He could perhaps have played the last 45 minutes against Portugal. That was a topic of discussion. But he has a really bad feeling about that kind of thing. He’s had experiences where he was brought on in the League Cup, and it didn’t go particularly well. I’m very pleased that he managed to dig deep and deliver a good 60 minutes.”

Erling Haaland will invariably be in action for Manchester City this weekend. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesWith Norway’s international slate cleared and Manchester City not in action until that Anfield excursion on Sunday, Haaland has been afforded that most precious commodity in modern soccer: a break.

The striker made the short flight from Portugal to Málaga in the south of Spain after Sunday’s fixture for a blast of warm weather, Norwegian outlet Dagbladet have reported. Enzo Maresca is not expecting his top scorer back until later this week, where he will have to steel himself for another endless torrent of fixtures.

“It’s a grueling schedule,” Solbakken lamented. “For those playing in the Champions League who’ve had little time off, it’s more brutal than for the others. Especially for the players who didn't get a summer break because of the World Cup and going deep into the tournament. We did that.

“Having so little vacation and then heading straight into high-intensity leagues—and then you have this international break on top of that—it’s not about making excuses. It’s just insane. Especially for the smaller nations.”
Stats via Transfermarkt. Correct as of Oct. 5, 2026.

Haaland is a victim of his own success. Line up with the baby-faced forward in your team and the chances of scoring explode. It’s an option few managers can resist, which has taken Haaland to this breaking point.

“He plays pretty much every match for his club,” the striker’s international manager fumed. “He belongs to the group with the heaviest workload, precisely because he plays in every competition and is ‘The Main Man.’”

While he is yet to miss a minute for Manchester City in the Premier League or Champions League, Maresca has warned that Haaland will have to be rested at some point this season. Whether he chooses a trip to Anfield in City’s first game since their seismic guilty verdict to leave out his best player is another question entirely.

ftbpro_01m45wk3zmde.title: Kylian Mbappe Risks Jose Mourinho’s Wrath With Latest Injury Update
ftbpro_01m45wk3zmde.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:15 AM EDTJosé Mourinho (left) is unlikely to be impressed. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Mourinho), Instagram/k.mbappe (Mbappé)Kylian Mbappé took to social media to hint at a positive update on his knee injury with a video filmed while riding a bike, less than two weeks after Real Madrid manager José Mourinho insisted professional players must give up cycling.

“You are a football player 24 hours a day,” Mourinho told the Bet it Drives Show toward the end of September. “Everything reflects the job. What you eat, what you drink, how you sleep, even things in your private life.

“You cannot ski. You cannot ride a bike. You fall off your bike, and you don’t play three matches maybe, or maybe worse, maybe you break a leg ... There are a lot of things you have to give up to be a football player. If you feel it’s a hobby, you’re dead.
“There’s always a relationship between what you achieve and what you give up.”
That message clearly did not reach Mbappé, who took to Instagram on Sunday to post a video of himself cycling with one hand, using the other to film the video.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Mbappé hurt his knee on France duty. / Yagiz Gurtug/MB Media/Getty ImagesMbappé was active on social media at the weekend. Shortly before the cycling video, another post showed the Frenchman running on a treadmill.

Clearly, both activities are heavy on the knees and so it would appear as though the problem Mbappé picked up on France duty is already clearing up, although there is a big difference between light exercise and being cleared to return to training and competitive matches.

Madrid are back in action on Oct. 10, when Villarreal visit the Bernabéu. That comes just 15 days after Mbappé went down with the injury and so, even though he has been back on the treadmill, his involvement in that fixture is in doubt.
A trip to Roma in the Champions League comes four days later and that may well be a wiser target date for Mbappé, who will have one eye on Madrid’s upcoming fixtures.
October also brings home games against Sevilla and RB Leipzig, but it is El Clásico against Barcelona on Oct. 25 that will be circled on the calendar.

Madrid are likely to show caution with Mbappé’s return to action, particularly given the problems caused by a knee issue last season. The French forward was in and out of the treatment room between December and March, missing a total of seven matches in the process.

His absence is not expected to reach those levels this time around, with an appearance against El Clásico not in doubt. Instead, it will be a case of ensuring Mbappé reaches that crunch fixture at peak fitness.

ftbpro_01m45xxdv7wd.title: USMNT Legend Landon Donovan Fires Brutal Mexico Taunt After Huge Win
ftbpro_01m45xxdv7wd.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:50 AM EDTLandon Donovan enjoyed the USMNT’s win over Mexico. / Jamie Squire/Getty ImagesThe U.S. men’s national team all-time top scorer Landon Donovan had plenty of characters to spare when dropping a succinct post on social media which still managed to enrage a large slice of Mexico’s fanbase.
“#TresACero is the new #DosACero,” Donovan wrote to celebrate the USMNT’s 3–0 victory over El Tri on Saturday night.
In the space of just a handful of words, Donovan had successfully started a new trend while digging up the rotting bones of an enmity which dates back more than a quarter of a century.

Landon Donovan has history with Mexico. / Shaun Botterill/Getty ImagesDonovan’s reference to “Tres a Cero” is easy enough to decode: the U.S. won 3–0 in Arizona over the weekend. However, the national teams which the slippery striker played for developed a habit of beating Mexico 2–0; “Dos a Cero.”

The first of this sequence of results came in 2001, when Donovan watched from the bench as goals from Josh Wolff and Earnie Stewart afforded the USMNT a sweet victory against their southern neighbors. The Concacaf Clásico would return on the grand stage of the World Cup round of 16 the following year. The Stars and Stripes once again prevailed, with Donovan scoring the second goal of a 2–0 win.
The U.S. had a rich run of results against Mexico at the start of the 21st century, laying the foundations of a cherished scoreline that Mauricio Pochettino’s side managed to surpass on Saturday.
“The rivalry on the pitch is fierce—it’s a battle to the death,” Pochettino explained. “We want to beat Mexico, but afterwards, there is respect.” Clearly, Donovan didn’t quite get that memo.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Rafael Márquez did not have an enjoyable afternoon. / Chris Coduto/Getty ImagesRafael Márquez was one of Mexico’s arch antagonists against the U.S. during his glittering playing career. The former center back was sent off in that World Cup reverse in 2002 and came into this weekend’s derby aware of the stakes. Despite the significant size of the scoreline, Márquez was still able to see “positives.”

El Tri started the better of the two teams, pinning the U.S. back for the opening 25 minutes before Julian Hall broke the deadlock for the host. “I think Mexico started very well in the first half,” Pochettino freely admitted. “They forced us to play defensively. We never really found our rhythm.”

“It’s a process, and I’m confident we can maintain the level of play we showed against Colombia, at least up until the 28th minute [tonight], when the goal was scored,” Márquez argued. “I think there are positives to take away, but obviously, we need to be self-critical.”

When it came to pinpointing those issues, the new Mexico boss admitted his side did “lack a bit more clarity going forward” but wrote off most of the result to individual blunders from his goalkeeper. “The other issues were terrible mistakes where, ultimately, you practically gifted those three goals to the opposing team.”

ftbpro_01m45yp9m30y.title: ‘It’s a Consequence’—Jules Kounde Reacts to Lack of Minutes at Barcelona
ftbpro_01m45yp9m30y.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott9:00 AM EDTJules Koundé has tumbled down the pecking order this season. / Alex Caparros/Getty ImagesBarcelona defender Jules Koundé has admitted a “drop in his standards” last season has left him in a deserved battle for minutes this year.

Having largely been a permanent fixture in the Barcelona team since his arrival in the summer of 2022, Koundé’s place on the right side of defense has been taken away this season. He has started just once in La Liga and has gone unused on the bench in each of the team’s last three games.
“It’s the coach’s decision,” Koundé explained. “I feel very good physically, I have no injury.

“If I have less playing time, it’s due to last season, which was far below my standards. It’s a consequence and a challenge that I gladly accept. I’ll have to work, which is what I normally do. It’s up to me to rediscover my best form. I know that when I’m at my best, I’ll get playing time.”
Unsurprisingly, Koundé’s struggle for minutes has sent the transfer rumor mill into overdrive.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER
Koundé has spent a lot of time on Barcelona’s bench. / Javier Borrego/Europa Press/Getty ImagesHansi Flick’s Barcelona squad is overflowing with versatile defenders this season.

A deal was struck to bring João Cancelo back permanently following his loan from Al Hilal, but it is Eric García, typically a center back, that has dominated the minutes on the right side of Barcelona’s defense thus far.

19-year-old Xavi Espart has also been promoted from the academy in a boost to Flick’s squad. Espart is a right back by trade but has been the regular starter at left back, although Cancelo started the two La Liga games prior to the international break.

With right backs playing left back, center backs playing right back and left back Gerard Martín now a key figure centrally, Flick is inundated with options at the back and has built a squad full of players he trusts, meaning there has hardly been a place for Koundé after a disappointing 2025–26 campaign.

The season is long, but so is Flick’s list of preferred players. Koundé is in a battle to force his way back up the pecking order and, predictably, there has been significant speculation about his future at Camp Nou.

Koundé’s future is far from clear. / ANP/Getty ImagesBarcelona’s finances are by no means as perilous as they were a few years ago, but La Liga’s leaders are still operating with limited flexibility in the transfer market.

Often needing to sell to make room for new faces, it could quickly become hard for Barcelona to justify keeping a valuable asset like Koundé on the bench, and there would be no shortage of suitors of the Frenchman was officially put on the market.

That being said, Koundé’s next landing spot could easily be decided by his preferred position. He may have spent four years as a right back at Camp Nou, but he made his name as a center back and there have been countless reports suggesting he is keen to return to a central role. Moving to a new club would give Koundé the freedom to make such a switch.
As a France international, Koundé would have obvious appeal to Paris Saint-Germain, but the strongest interest is likely to come from the riches of the Premier League.

Koundé’s versatility sounds like a dream to Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, although the Gunners’ inability to offer regular minutes at center back could be a problem. Manchester City are another that would appreciate Koundé’s skillset but the uncertainty surrounding the team after being found guilty of financial misconduct could easily impact their transfer appeal.

Chelsea were chasing Koundé’s signature back in 2022 and thought they were close to getting a deal over the line before a late hijack from Barcelona. The Blues are likely to want a new defender over the next 12 months.

Manchester United would also likely be interested in Koundé. While the Red Devils are well-stocked at center back, questions about Leny Yoro’s future at Old Trafford could open the door for a replacement.

ftbpro_01m460vh4fnr.title: Argentina vs. Benin—International Friendly: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m460vh4fnr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray10:00 PM EDTArgentina welcomes an unfamiliar foe to Buenos Aires. / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Argentina), Benin National Soccer Team Website (Benin)Argentina bids an emotional farewell to its legendary talisman Lionel Messi on Tuesday, who will make his 208th and final international appearance in a friendly with Benin.

The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner announced his international retirement following a heartbreaking World Cup final defeat to Spain, which marked his last competitive appearance for La Albiceleste. But there’s still time for one final appearance at Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, where supporters will flock to pay tribute to the greatest player of all time.

Messi will hope to add to the 125 total goals he has scored for the national team in a first-ever fixture with Benin, and his teammates have been exceptionally clinical in his absence over the current international break. They have fired 11 goals past Bolivia and Burkina Faso in emphatic friendly wins, but will now focus on supplying their iconic captain one last time.

The Cheetahs will be eager to spoil the party, no matter how unlikely that appears to be. They have won two of their last three matches, with their draw with Burkina Faso—who Argentina just beat 7–0—sandwiched in between wins over Guinea and Mauritania.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Messi will take center stage during his final outing. /  Image Photo Agency/Getty Images“I’m forever grateful for being part of Messi’s wonderful story in the Argentina national team,” Lionel Scaloni enthused ahead of the Benin match, and he has played a crucial part in an extraordinary international career.
Messi walks away from the national team having won the World Cup and two Copa América titles under Scaloni’s guidance, helping him match Diego Maradona’s legacy for La Albiceleste.

There are bound to be tears from Messi, his teammates and supporters inside the Estadio Monumental as the curtain closes, but it should be a winning send-off for the 39-year-old against FIFA’s 93rd-ranked national team.
All eyes will be on Messi. / FotMobOf course, Messi will lead the line during his final bow, likely partnered by Julian Álvarez or Lautaro Martínez in the front two.
Nicolás Otamendi will also make his final appearance for Argentina, tapping out at 140 caps for the senior side. He has traveled to his homeland specifically for this fixture.
Nicolás Tagliafico and Giovani Lo Celso are both doubts to feature against Benin through slight knocks.
Scaloni is unlikely to make too many alterations from the team that scored seven last time out, especially given he was able to withdraw a host of players at halftime and throughout the second half.
Emiliano Martínez, Lisandro Martínez, Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo Fernández and Rodrigo De Paul are among the big names likely to feature.
Argentina predicted lineup vs. Benin (4-4-2): E. Martínez; Giay, Otamendi, Li. Martínez, Medina; De Paul, En. Fernández, Mac Allister, Paz; Messi, La. Martínez.

Benin could name the same XI that beat Mauritania. / FotMobBenin boss Gernot Rohr is without Dokou Dodo and Rachid Moumini for the friendly, but 21-year-old striker Sahid Ngobi has been called up and could earn some minutes.
Lorient forward Aiyegun Tosin will be tasked with unnerving the Argentina defense after recently scoring his fourth international goal.

At the other end of the field, goalkeeper Marcel Dandjinou will have the unenviable assignment of trying to thwart Messi and Co. He does enter the match in confident mood, though, after saving a penalty in the win over Mauritania.
Benin predicted lineup vs. Argentina (4-2-3-1): Dandjinou; Azongnitode, Roche, Tijani, T. Ouorou; D’Almeida, Imourane; Y. Ouorou, Olaïtan, Aloko; Tosin.

ftbpro_01m4626f3dvn.title: Lionel Messi Prepares for Argentina Farewell With Executive Producer Role at Disney
ftbpro_01m4626f3dvn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom11:45 AM EDTLionel Messi has to think about what he’s going to do after soccer. / Todd Kirkland/Getty ImagesDisney have surprisingly announced Lionel Messi as the executive producer for a new animation series based, in the loosest sense of the word, on the life of Argentina’s retiring superstar.

Messi’s career has a comic book quality to it. He is the national team’s undisputed hero, leaping off the posters on the childhood bedroom walls of so many of his current teammates to lead Argentina to four consecutive major tournament finals.
As the 39-year-old brings his story to a close with a farewell friendly against Benin on Tuesday night, Disney have commissioned a new show titled: Messi and the Giants.

The series, which is set to be released in summer 2027, centers around a 12-year-old boy with the distinctive brown mop of hair which Messi had in his youth. At that point in his life, the actual Messi was still living in Argentina and not much taller than four foot, with his parents desperately trying to convince Newell’s Old Boys to fund his growth hormone treatment.

The animated Lionel, by contrast, is trapped in an alternate virtual reality fighting giant monsters in convoluted scenarios which just so happen to require his soccer skills. Different strokes for different folks.
While lending your likeness to kids’ shows is one retirement plan, Messi would appear to have loftier ambitions for when he finally hangs up his boots.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER
Messi via IG: "Aupa Deportivo." pic.twitter.com/bJqsxWi3RD
Messi has already ruled out one of the most common avenues for retired professionals. “I don’t really see myself as a manager,” he has said on multiple occasions.

That is perhaps a wise decision. There is a short list of truly generational players who have made the transition to successful managers. Carlo Ancelotti, a talented individual in his day but not of Messi’s caliber, warned: “It is a completely different job—your career as a player won’t help as a manager.”

For a player as preternaturally gifted as Messi, an individual who walks around the pitch with a bird’s eye view of everything going around him, getting the information which he was able to instantly process across to a set of mortal players could be infuriating.

However, Messi isn’t planning on stepping away from the sport entirely. “I would like to have my own club,” he revealed earlier this year, “to start from the bottom and be able to give the opportunity to the boys, to the people, to grow and make an important club.”
The wheels for that plan are already in motion. Messi recently acquired Spanish second-tier side Eldense, having already bought fifth-tier outfit UE Cornellà in April.
Messi also has a stake in Deportivo LSM, an amateur Uruguayan club founded by his Inter Miami teammate and close friend Luis Suárez.

ftbpro_01m462vcq0v4.title: 'No Other Football Club’—Wrexham’s Unique Success Factor Explained by CEO
ftbpro_01m462vcq0v4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay2:30 PM EDTWrexham are in a unique position unlike any other club in the EFL Championship. / PA Images via Getty ImagesIt is difficult to discuss Wrexham Football Club without mentioning Hollywood owners Rob Mac and Ryan Reynolds in some form.

The Welsh club has been transformed under the ownership of the pair, who have taken the Red Dragons from the National League to the Championship via an unprecedented three successive promotions and the highest finish in the club's 162-year history.

Wrexham will never be able to escape the role money has played in their rise either, though it is too simplistic to say they have simply bought their success. Phil Parkinson has masterminded their remarkable rise across five seasons and ensured money has been invested wisely in a competitive playing squad whose members all share the same determination to win and work ethic to make it possible.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac bring huge appeal to Wrexham sponsors. / Nick Potts/PA Images via Getty ImagesIt all comes back to Mac and Reynolds, though. The pair remain firmly in control of Wrexham, with an estimated combined ownership stake of between 70% and 75%, while the Allyn family, the former owners of Welch Allyn, became minority investors in October 2024 with a stake of roughly 15%.

Apollo Sports Capital acquired another minority stake—believed to be just under 10%—in December 2025, while an additional 5% stake was sold to a U.S.-based investment group led by ASC Chief Executive Al Tylis and Chief Strategy Officer Sam Porter.
Mac and Reynolds maintain their stance as “custodians” of the club rather than co-owners, but there is no ignoring the fact that they would both benefit enormously should they ever decide to sell.

Wrexham AFC was valued at roughly $2.5 million when Mac and Reynolds completed their takeover in February 2021. The Hollywood pair paid a nominal $1.40 to acquire the club while committing to invest an additional $2.5 million into the playing squad and club infrastructure. Following Apollo Sports Capital's investment, Wrexham is now valued at approximately $475 million—an increase of around 18,900% from the club's reported valuation at the time of the takeover.

That doesn't mean they aren't spending money, though. Work is underway on a new $95 million Kop Stand that will increase the Racecourse Ground's capacity to 18,000, while the club spent a further $48 million on new players over the summer. A new training pavilion was built at Colliers Park for roughly $9 million, and another $2.5 million was spent on a new pitch.

It means Wrexham are still operating at a loss, though they appreciate they must speculate to accumulate and are preparing the club for their expected rise to the Premier League. That isn't a given, though, and there is always risk attached to such investment, with no guarantees of success.

Rob Mac and Ryan Reynolds poked fun at Southampton's involvement in the “Spygate” scandal in a recent viral advert. / Wrexham AFCA key part of their growth has been sponsorship, which grew by 31.5% in the last financial year, covering their League One promotion season. A staggering 57.7% of revenue comes from the rest of the world, the majority of which is North America, while total kit sales have jumped from just a few thousand per season to roughly 100,000 a year.

“We definitely punch above our weight class when it comes to sponsorships,” club CEO Michael Williamson told The Financial Times. “Because of the documentary, because of Rob and Ryan and because of our approach, [advertisers] get something really, really special that no other football club can provide.”

Just last month, Wrexham went viral when Mac and Reynolds starred in a new advert for Firefox that mocked the Southampton “Spygate” scandal, while the co-chairman also featured in a recent advert for Royal Bank of Canada, which has become the club's new back-of-shirt sponsor.

Those who partner with the club not only get unique coverage in the hugely successful Welcome to Wrexham docuseries, but also get to be part of a story about a revitalized community that has rediscovered its confidence and is now a thriving tourist destination.

Williamson added: “Their passion and their commitment are remarkable. But they aren’t just here for the football club, they’re here for the community. They understand the sustainability of the football club long term is ultimately dependent on the journey of the community coming along with us.

“Before Rob and Ryan there was uncertainty about brighter days ahead. And so people maybe didn’t go and get a loan [or take out] a mortgage because they didn’t know if they were going to have a job or not in the future. Now, people see hope.”

The next step in that journey could be the Premier League. The Red Dragons sit 14th in the Championship table after the first eight matches of the new season, having finished agonizingly short of the playoff positions last season. Had they defeated Middlesbrough on the final day, they would have finished sixth. Instead, they drew, Hull City finished sixth, won the playoffs and now sit eighth in the top flight.
“That really stung because I felt we were so close,” Williamson added.
With the continued support of Mac and Reynolds, Wrexham are getting closer to that ambition every day.
