ftbpro_01m497andqnv.title: ‘Love Football More’—Neymar Issues Emotional Lionel Messi Tribute Ahead of Argentina Farewell
ftbpro_01m497andqnv.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas4:14 PM EDTNeymar is one of Lionel Messi’s closest friends in soccer.     / Gustavo Pagano/Getty Images Countless tributes and messages have been directed Lionel Messi’s way in the hours leading up to his final game for Argentina. Long-time teammate, rival and close friend Neymar wrote a tribute of his own, stating Messi made him “love football even more.”

Neymar shared the pitch with Messi at the club level for Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain and was even present when Messi lifted his maiden Argentina trophy, given it came at the expense of Brazil in the 2021 Copa América. Before Messi’s farewell, Neymar took to social media to celebrate his friend’s illustrious international career.

“Anyone who loves football has enjoyed you throughout all these years,” Neymar posted to Instagram. “Today is your last game with the shirt of your national team, of your country, and I hope you enjoy every second, may all the tributes today make you happy.

“It’s not only Argentina that thanks you, the whole world thanks you for everything you’ve done for football. Thank you for making me love football even more. It was an honor to have played against you, and even more so to have made history alongside you. THANK YOU, Leo Messi,” Neymar finished, adding an emoji of a goat at the end of his message.

Neymar and Messi won everything there was to win during their four seasons together at Barcelona, forming a lasting friendship and two-thirds of the greatest attacking trio in soccer history. The final head of that three-headed monster also paid homage to Messi before his last dance with La Albiceleste.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Lionel Messi (left) and Luis Suárez have established a bond that extends beyond the pitch.  / Luis Robayo/AFP/Getty Images Alongside Messi and Neymar, Luis Suárez also won it all at Barcelona. The legendary Uruguayan striker then followed Messi to Inter Miami, and the duo are even co-owners of a soccer team in Suárez’s home country.
The pair of lethal South American goal scorers have been close friends for over a decade, and on Messi’s landmark day, Suárez made sure to pay his respects with a video tribute.

“Gordo! (chubby),” Suárez started, via DSports. “I just wanted to send you a big hug. I hope you enjoy your last match wearing your country’s national team shirt very much—which was so important for your career.

“You lived incredible things. You won things that every player wishes they could win representing your country. So you have a more than deserved recognition from all the people in appreciation of your career and what you represented for your country.
“Feel very proud of yourself. I send you a very big hug, and enjoy your day.”

Oct. 6, 2026 is a day that will live forever in Argentina’s folklore: the day the whole nation bid farewell to the man that marked an entire era for Argentina. The landmark occasion started with adidas posting a video in which Messi shared a few words to Argentina, thanking the nation’s supporters for “loving me so much.”
“The moment has arrived,” Messi said to start the video. “I leave in peace. I gave it my all. This jersey was my dream, my pride and my life.
“Thank you for loving me so much. I’m going to miss you.”

Argentina will face Benin on Tuesday night at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires. Messi will make his 208th and final appearance for La Albiceleste, dropping the curtain on the international career of the greatest player of all time.

fzhafkysws3g1ux8fnmoe3180.title: De la Fuente promises 'the best is yet to come' for Spain
fzhafkysws3g1ux8fnmoe3180.subtitle: Luis de la Fuente has penned a long-term contract extension to stay in charge of Spain, and he promised the best is still to come.
paragraphs: Spain boss Luis de la Fuente has vowed "the best is yet to come" from the reigning world and European champions.
De la Fuente has agreed a contract extension to stay in charge of Spain through to the end of Euro 2032.
Since De la Fuente replaced Luis Enrique in 2022, Spain have been dominant.
La Roja won Euro 2024 and then repeated the trick at this year's World Cup.
Spain are on a 38-game unbeaten run in competitive matches, which is a record for a European or South American team.
But De la Fuente insists Spain are not done yet.
"I only think about time and how fragile we are. Life has taught me to be very short-sighted," he said.

"My goal is to arrive in good shape for [Euro 2028]. But of course, I'm especially excited about reaching the 2030 World Cup, but also, now, the 2032 European Championship. We're going to try, with all our strength.
"The best is yet to come. The third star [World Cup crown] would be like something out of a movie."
Spain face England on Saturday before taking on Croatia and Czechia, in their opening Nations League games.

gri8oerjzzia14g3mxa0nic1r.title: Croatia must 'take special care' of Modric, says Bilic
gri8oerjzzia14g3mxa0nic1r.subtitle: Croatia host England in the Nations League on Saturday, and Slaven Bilic will hope Luka Modric can inspire victory against the Three Lions.
paragraphs: Slaven Bilic believes Croatia must "take special care" of Luka Modric as they prepare to face England in the Nations League.
Croatia started their Nations League campaign with a 2-1 win over Czechia before losing 4-1 to Spain last time out.
Modric opened the scoring in their win over Czechia, which was also the first goal of Bilic's second tenure with the national team.
The 41-year-old was used as a late substitute against Spain, with the world champions comfortably leading at the time of his introduction.
Bilic insisted they will monitor Modric's minutes, but is confident the AC Milan midfielder can make an impact for Croatia.
"Of course, as with many other players, we have to be mindful of his workload, which is why we take special care of him," said Bilic.
"He is simply unique. The old saying is that age is just a number, but with him, it really seems that way and he proves it.
"He simply keeps going because he is unique and because he means so much to the team.
"He is more than a player, more than a captain. He is an icon. His importance can be seen everywhere, at the table, at dinner, in meetings.
"But above all, he is here because he still gives so much on the pitch and makes a difference."
Croatia have won eight of their last nine competitive home matches (D1) since a 1-0 loss to Turkiye in an October 2023 European Championship qualifier.
However, despite losing only four of their last 41 home competitive internationals, three have been in the Nations League (v France and Portugal in 2020 and Austria in 2022).

Bilic's side will play mostly behind closed doors due to crowd disturbances involving Croatia fans during a Nations League match against France in March 2025. There is an exception for schoolchildren, plus 100 travelling England supporters.
Since beating England in the 2018 World Cup semi-final, Croatia are winless in all four games against the Three Lions (D1 L3).

h7xm4yhya9qp1bvfflwf0ykr5.title: Malen injury 'not too bad', assures Xavi after Netherlands withdrawal
h7xm4yhya9qp1bvfflwf0ykr5.subtitle: Donyell Malen's withdrawal from the Netherlands squad may have concerned Roma supporters, but Xavi is confident he only has a minor injury.
paragraphs: The injury that caused Donyell Malen to withdraw from the Netherlands' squad is "not too bad", head coach Xavi said in a positive update on the Roma forward.
Malen has been in sensational form since swapping Aston Villa for the Italian capital in January.

Since making his Serie A debut on January 18, Malen has scored 20 goals in 23 appearances in the competition, at least twice as many as any other player in that period (Tasos Douvikas and Lautaro Martinez are next with 10).
He has helped the Giallorossi make a flying start to the new campaign under Gian Piero Gasperini, as they sit top of the table on goal difference heading into the international break.

Like Scudetto holders Inter, they opened 2026-27 with four straight victories, though they did let a 2-0 lead slip in Saturday's head-to-head clash between the top two, a game that saw Malen play the full 90 minutes.
Roma's supporters face a nervous wait regarding Malen's condition after he pulled out of Xavi's first Oranje squad, with reports suggesting it is a knee issue.
But Xavi does not believe it is a serious injury, having discussed the withdrawals of Malen and Justin Kluivert at a press conference on Monday.
"It's a pity, because Donyell is in splendid form, but it happened at the last moment, the same as Kluivert," Xavi said. "That's football, you have to adapt.
"I believe Donyell is okay, that it is not too bad. I don't know how long it will take for him to recover."
Malen has already scored six goals in Serie A this term, more than any other player, while over-performing his 4.6 expected goals (xG).
He has also had more shots on target (10) than any other player in the division and currently boasts a 57.5 minutes-per-goal rate in the Italian top flight.
Malen will sit out the Netherlands' Nations League meetings with Germany, Serbia (twice) and Greece, with Xavi's Oranje debut on Thursday pitting him against new Nationalelf boss Jurgen Klopp.

Malen has already scored six goals in Serie A this term, more than any other player, while over-performing his 4.6 expected goals (xG).

He has also had more shots on target (10) than any other player in the division and currently boasts a 57.5 minutes-per-goal rate in the Italian top flight.

Malen will sit out the Netherlands' Nations League meetings with Germany, Serbia (twice) and Greece, with Xavi's Oranje debut on Thursday pitting him against new Nationalelf boss Jurgen Klopp.

hbjr7uly86ec1owb7dd7qv1uu.title: France 1-1 Italy: Rabiot error denies Zidane victory on home debut
hbjr7uly86ec1owb7dd7qv1uu.subtitle: Zinedine Zidane failed to win his first home match as France boss after Italy held Les Bleus to a draw at the Stade de France.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane was denied victory on his home debut as France boss after Italy fought back for a 1-1 draw at the Stade de France.

Michael Olise's stunning strike looked set to secure France a third consecutive 1-0 win in the Nations League, but Alessandro Bastoni pounced on an error from Adrien Rabiot to rescue a point for Italy, before Dayot Upamecano also saw red.

Although France dominated possession in the early stages, Italy squandered a huge chance to take the lead after Moise Kean shot straight at Mike Maignan from close range following a brilliant low cross from Michael Kayode.

The hosts hit the crossbar when Doue's deflected centre landed on Gianluigi Donnarumma's crossbar, but it was Italy who wasted another big chance before the break as Davide Frattesi's eventual shot from Kayode's long throw was deflected wide of the left post.
France then made Italy pay for their wastefulness 10 minutes into the second half. Rayan Cherki won a free-kick on the edge of the box, and he rolled the ball for Olise to smash in off the crossbar.

However, the Azzurri levelled against the run of play in the 68th minute as Rabiot played Lucas da Cunha into trouble, and Bastoni took full advantage as he won possession and expertly finished past Maignan.

France's hopes of finding a winner took a blow five minutes from time after Upamecano was shown a second yellow card for bringing down Kean, and the visitors managed to hold on for an important point on the road.
France miss Mbappe's magic

Zidane's side prevailed last time out against Belgium without star striker Kylian Mbappe, with Olise providing the goods on that occasion, but the Bayern Munich winger's contribution on this occasion was not enough for France.

Although Olise, Doue and Ousmane Dembele combined for 12 shots, with the latter responsible for six of those attempts, it was only an unstoppable effort from Olise which managed to get the better of Donnarumma, who made seven saves for Roberto Mancini's side.

Overall, Mancini will certainly be the happier of the two coaches. Italy won the expected goals (xG) battle 1.46 to 1.21 despite recording fewer shots (14 to 18) and far fewer touches in the opposition box (18 to 49).
France conceded eight shots before the break, their highest total at half-time of a home match since July 2016 in the European Championship semi-final against Germany (11).

While France remain top of Group A1 in the Nations League, Zidane will know his side must click in attack to give their defenders more to work with; France have scored once in each of their three games.

hi1iq0f80sjm1jy4maebp511y.title: Wales 0-1 Denmark: Hojlund penalty condemns Bellamy's side to third Nations League defeat
hi1iq0f80sjm1jy4maebp511y.subtitle: Rasmus Hojlund's 75th-minute penalty ensured Denmark overcame Wales in Group A4 of the Nations League.
paragraphs: Rasmus Hojlund's penalty was the difference as Denmark overcame a stubborn Wales 1-0 in the Nations League at Cardiff City Stadium.
After Danny Ward pulled off a couple of brilliant stops to deny the visitors, the Wrexham goalkeeper made an error in judgement by bringing down Gustav Isaksen inside the box.
That allowed Hojlund to convert his penalty, with Denmark now sitting in second place in Group A4, six points behind leaders Portugal.

Wales almost found the back of the net in the early exchanges, but Brennan Johnson fired wide from a tight angle before Denmark captain Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg was substituted after sustaining an early injury.
Morten Hjulmand headed wide of the upright, while Sorba Thomas failed to test Mads Hermansen with a free-kick at the other end.
The visitors should have taken the lead before half-time, but Isaksen was unable to convert his chances, first heading over from close range, and then blazing a wild attempt into the stands.

Ward had to be alert to keep out Hojlund’s close-range strike in the opening five minutes of the second half before making a stunning stop moments later, tipping Isaksen's header onto the left-hand post.
Johnson was presented with a good opportunity, but the Everton attacker could only fire over the woodwork, following an explosive run from Thomas down the left flank.

However, Ward went from hero to villain for Wales after bringing down Isaksen in the penalty area, with Hojlund stepping up to coolly convert the spot-kick into the bottom-left corner in the 75th minute.
Craig Bellamy's side struggled to muster a response afterwards, with Wales now sitting third in Group A4, with one win and three defeats.
Ward goes from hero to zero for Wales
Coming into this game, Wales knew they had to win if they were to have any chance of progressing to the quarter-finals of the competition.
They were indebted to Ward, who made a string of fine saves to keep Denmark at bay. The goalkeeper made three saves, with the one against Isaksen in the second half being the best of the bunch.

However, Ward showed a lack of concentration as he felled Isaksen in the 18-yard box, after conceding possession, presenting Denmark with the opportunity to seal all three points, which Hojlund duly took.
Hojlund has now scored eight goals in his last 10 competitive internationals for Denmark, who have won five consecutive meetings with Wales in all competitions, conceding just one goal.

The visitors deserved this victory, having recorded 13 shots with four attempts on target, reflected by an expected goals (xG) of 2.20. Conversely, Wales' six shots and 0.37 xG were both their lowest in a home fixture in the competition.

hl8g2s953m0u16yblg5azdqsv.title: Canada 'can beat just about anybody', says Marsch ahead of USA test
hl8g2s953m0u16yblg5azdqsv.subtitle: After Jacob Shaffelburg scored twice in Canada's 2-0 win over Peru, Jesse Marsch said the result proved his team can compete with anyone.
paragraphs: Jesse Marsch believes Canada's 2-0 victory over Peru proved they can beat "just about anybody" and views their upcoming clash with the United States as a yardstick to measure their progress.
A first-half brace from Los Angeles FC's Jacob Shaffelburg sealed a deserved victory for the hosts in Montreal, maintaining their 100% record in this international break.

Canada, who also defeated Chile 1-0 in their previous game, fired off 17 shots to Peru's four and won the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.94 to 0.23, creating four Opta-defined big chances, compared to their opponent's zero.
Marsch will now go up against his home country, as Canada prepare to face the USA in their final friendly of this international break, in Minnesota on Tuesday.
And he feels that game will be a valuable test, telling reporters after full-time: "I thought we dictated the pace and the way the game was played from the beginning.
"We feel like we could have come away with even more goals.

"We'll keep working on things, we'll keep trying to capitalise on moments and now, when we go to play the U.S. down there, we know we'll face an opponent that has a lot of quality, that is athletic, with a good coach and a good way of playing.

"It'll be a big challenge for us, but we feel confident against any opponent that we play, and if we dictate the terms of the match and control the game the way we like to control it, we feel we can beat just about anybody."
Marsch also highlighted Peru's recent results – including a 1-1 draw with Mexico earlier this week – as further evidence of the quality of Canada's latest performance.
Peru were also competitive against eventual World Cup winners Spain in a pre-tournament friendly in June, losing 3-1, though they went down 4-1 to the USA at the start of this international break.
"It's a credit to the team and a credit to what we're establishing here that we can manage that, because that's a team that gave Mexico a very good match," Marsch said.
"Even if you go back to when they played Spain over the summer, they gave Spain a really good match.
"We made them look worse than they are, because of how we performed."

hqajl9dq1rieztkd8vqjsxcu.title: Kaptein relieved to overcome 'difficult' Women's Champions League tie
hqajl9dq1rieztkd8vqjsxcu.subtitle: Chelsea survived a scare in their Women's Champions League opener, with Wieke Kaptein's goal enough to see off debutants Austria Wien.
paragraphs: Wieke Kaptein expressed her relief at beginning Chelsea's Women's Champions League campaign with a win after battling their way past Austria Wien on Wednesday.
Kaptein's stunning 11th-minute goal proved to be the difference as Chelsea claimed a 1-0 victory, but tournament debutants Wien had several chances to at least earn a point.
After Alyssa Thompson shot wide shortly after Kaptein's fine finish, Wien looked the more likely to alter the scoreline, bringing some good saves out of Livia Peng throughout.
Virginia Kirchberger turned over from close range before Louise Schoffel's effort whistled past the bottom-left corner as the visitors started to dominate at the end of the first half.
Peng had to be on her toes to deny Valentina Potzl and Modesta Uka, with the latter also curling a shot onto the left post in Wien's best chance of earning a deserved draw.
Sonia Bompastor's side were only able to muster an expected goals (xG) total of 1.4 from their 13 shots, while Wien registered a tally of 0.9 xG from two more attempts.
Kaptein acknowledged the difficulties her side faced against Wien, suggesting that her team should have capitalised on their early dominance by scoring more.
"It was a tough game. They put pressure on us and made it a little bit more difficult," Kaptein told Disney+.
"We could have scored more goals, and we needed to punish them more. Overall, we won, it's good, and now we need to focus on the next game.
"For sure [relief]. In the last 10 minutes, we were fighting. We stuck together as a team, but we could have kept the ball a bit better.

"They are a good team, and they are not in the Champions League for nothing. They were really dangerous in our half. But we need to look at ourselves as we could have punished them a little bit more."
Chelsea's victory followed an unconvincing 2-0 triumph against Birmingham City in the Women's Super League last weekend, which continued their unbeaten start in the league.
After beginning their campaign with a frustrating 1-1 draw with Aston Villa, the Blues thumped Manchester United 5-0 but have been far from their best in their last two matches.
They face their sternest test this Sunday against Arsenal, who are two points behind them in the WSL after taking five points from their opening three games.
However, Thompson believes their hard-fought victory against Wien is something Chelsea can build on ahead of their return to domestic action.
"The team came together in the end, and we fought as much as we could. It's a good test for us, for our first game to have a physical battle," Thompson said.
"We are going to play so many different teams and styles during the Champions League, so every test is great for us, and we came out with the three points, so it was a good win.
"The level dropped a little bit, and we were losing tackles, but we got back into the game and were ready for the physical fight.
"At that point, it turned into that, and we knew what game we had to play. We're strong, and we know we can play different styles, so in the end we just had to fight it out."

i19e037wx0lw15bn8hvvtpqdz.title: London City 'building something special' after going second in WSL
i19e037wx0lw15bn8hvvtpqdz.subtitle: Alexia Putellas scored her first Women's Super League goal for London City Lionesses, helping them to a third win of the season.
paragraphs: Alexia Putellas says London City Lionesses want to "build something special" after a 2-0 win over Brighton moved them up to second in the Women's Super League.
Putellas scored her first league goal since joining the Lionesses to help them to the victory that sees them move within three points of leaders Manchester City.

London City dominated throughout and got their reward for their bright start in the 29th minute, with Putellas picking out the bottom corner from the edge of the area after some sloppy Brighton defending.
The Seagulls almost equalised shortly after, with Emily Murphy's looping header hitting the crossbar, and Kiko Seike could only fire wide on the rebound.

Freya Godfrey also hit the woodwork for London City in the second half, but Lucia Corrales made sure of all three points in the 92nd minute by turning in Delphine Cascarino's cross following a counter-attack.
Putellas has been vocal about her hopes of big achievements with London City this season, and she is thrilled to be off the mark for her new club.
"I'm so happy, I'm so proud. The most important thing is we got three points here," she told Sky Sports.
"We are trying to be unpredictable. We can score through possession and counter-attacks; we can do both. I think we achieved that.
"It's a new challenge for everyone; we want to build something special here, and we have to keep pushing and showing up for each other. We want to give our best this season.
"It's the beginning; we just have begun. There's a lot of points yet. We have to improve the same details; we'll be there [around the top of the table] for sure."
London City only just edged the shot count (11 to 10) but had three shots on target compared to Brighton's one.
The visitors also accumulated a higher expected goals total, racking up 1.6 xG, while the Lionesses accumulated 1.3.

London City could drop back down the table by the end of the weekend, with five WSL matches being played on Sunday, but head coach Eder Maestre is confident they can continue to cause problems for the top teams.
"We have the underdog mentality; we're humble but have the target to reach those limits," she told Sky Sports.
"It's temporary, but we're dreaming big, so hopefully we can be in that position later in the competition."

i2t4lgiizda51ai6125dalujy.title: Mbappe suffered knee hyperextension with France
i2t4lgiizda51ai6125dalujy.subtitle: France will be without Kylian Mbappe for the rest of the international break, with Real Madrid confirming the diagnosis of the injury.
paragraphs: Real Madrid have confirmed that Kylian Mbappe has been diagnosed with hyperextension in his left knee.
Mbappe scored the winner for France in a narrow 1-0 victory over Turkiye, securing Zinedine Zidane a victory in his first match in charge.

However, he pulled up immediately after scoring and was taken off five minutes later, with France confirming that he had withdrawn from the squad to return to Madrid for treatment following the match.
France initially revealed their captain had suffered a tendon injury following the game, with Zidane saying "it's not going well" when asked about it.
While Madrid have not revealed how long he will be sidelined for, Spanish media are reporting he is only set for around two weeks on the sidelines.
Mbappe has already netted six goals in LaLiga this season, making him the first player to score that many goals in Madrid's opening five league matches since Karim Benzema in 2021-22 (also six).
It remains to be seen if he will be available for their first match after the international break against Villarreal on October 10.
Madrid then face Roma in the Champions League four days later before welcoming Sevilla to the Bernabeu the following weekend.

i5mnw08oz72q186guw1m53vs7.title: Zidane lauds Da Cunha displays in France midfield
i5mnw08oz72q186guw1m53vs7.subtitle: Lucas Da Cunha has impressed for France in the Nations League, and Zinedine Zidane spoke highly about the Como midfielder.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane praised the impact Lucas Da Cunha has had in France's midfield during this international break.
Da Cunha started against both Belgium and Italy in the Nations League, with Les Bleus winning the first match 1-0 before drawing 1-1 with the Azzurri on Friday.
Against Belgium, Da Cunha won possession more often than any other France player (six times), while also recording the second-most touches (97) and successful passes (83).
He then created the most chances of any player at the Stade de France on Friday (four), also completing 82 of his 85 passes (96.5%).
However, Da Cunha was involved in the mistake which led to Italy's equaliser, as Alessandro Bastoni pounced on a mix-up between the Como midfielder and Adrien Rabiot.
Nevertheless, Zidane defended the 25-year-old and focused on the positives from his two performances during this break.
"Football is about trying to make as few mistakes as possible. I'm not going to get into the question of whose fault it is. When there's a mistake, it's everyone's fault," said Zidane.
"What do I expect from a midfielder? What he has done, what he is doing and what he is doing.
"He deserves to be here with us, he deserves to have played, like all the others. I really like this player, he has a lot of personality.
"He's not afraid to play. He filters the passes. It's everything I love, he can make those 40-yard switches. He's quite an interesting player."
France are top of Group A1 in the Nations League after three games, and they face second-place Belgium in their final match of the extended break.

He then created the most chances of any player at the Stade de France on Friday (four), also completing 82 of his 85 passes (96.5%).

However, Da Cunha was involved in the mistake which led to Italy's equaliser, as Alessandro Bastoni pounced on a mix-up between the Como midfielder and Adrien Rabiot.

Nevertheless, Zidane defended the 25-year-old and focused on the positives from his two performances during this break.

"Football is about trying to make as few mistakes as possible. I'm not going to get into the question of whose fault it is. When there's a mistake, it's everyone's fault," said Zidane.

"What do I expect from a midfielder? What he has done, what he is doing and what he is doing.

"He deserves to be here with us, he deserves to have played, like all the others. I really like this player, he has a lot of personality.

"He's not afraid to play. He filters the passes. It's everything I love, he can make those 40-yard switches. He's quite an interesting player."

France are top of Group A1 in the Nations League after three games, and they face second-place Belgium in their final match of the extended break.

i89d3zf9rdegzelk5hbqmer1.title: Hallgrimsson impressed by energy on show in victory over Israel
i89d3zf9rdegzelk5hbqmer1.subtitle: The Republic of Ireland claimed their first Nations League win against Israel on Sunday, with three first-half goals doing the damage.
paragraphs: Heimir Hallgrimsson said he was impressed with the energy of his Republic of Ireland team during their 3-0 victory against Israel in the Nations League.
The Republic of Ireland swept aside Israel at Nagyerdei Stadion, with three goals in the space of 12 minutes from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealing the win.
Parrott opened the scoring in the 13th minute when his shot squirmed under Daniel Peretz after James Abankwah cut the ball back for the in-form striker to finish into the net.
It got even better for Hallgrimsson's side three minutes later when Idah tucked home, with Moylan's fine run ending with a shot that found the bottom corner in the 25th minute.

The Republic of Ireland scored three goals in the first 25 minutes of a match for the first time since October 2014 against Gibraltar (18th min), and only the second time in their history away from home, after August 1996 against Liechtenstein (four in 19th min).
They also enjoyed their joint-biggest win in the Nations League, and outright biggest away from home, alongside a 3-0 victory over Scotland in June 2022.

Hallgrimsson's side had three different goalscorers (excluding own goals) in a single game for the first time since October 2023 against Gibraltar (four), and the Republic of Ireland boss was thrilled with his team's display.
"I must say, I did not expect so much energy for 90 minutes," Halgrimsson said. "There were a lot of empty tanks at the end of the game.
"Given all the circumstances, with the emotions, the bad preparation and all of those things, to have this energy and power for such a long time really impressed me.
"The character was there. In tough times, you find your leaders, they will emerge. These guys showed how much they loved their country. The performance showed that."
The Republic of Ireland finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.57 from their nine attempts to Israel's 0.31 from their eight shots at Caoimhin Kelleher's net.

Israel have now conceded 3+ goals in 11 matches since the start of 2024 in all competitions, the joint-most of any UEFA nation in this time (level with Liechtenstein), with the Republic of Ireland's forwards impressing.

Up to and including the Republic of Ireland's first goal, each of the nation's last seven goals in competitive internationals (excluding own goals) had been scored by Parrott, the longest run by any player for the side.
Moylan, meanwhile, became the first player to score and assist a goal in the same match for the Republic of Ireland since Robbie Brady against Finland, also in the Nations League, in October 2024.

He now has six goal involvements (four goals, two assists) in four senior international appearances for his country, and he will be hoping to add to that tally in the Republic of Ireland's next game against Austria this Thursday.

ic1l0swye6up1788ghbuhiltm.title: Esposito brothers want to 'share the field more often' for Italy
ic1l0swye6up1788ghbuhiltm.subtitle: Francesco Pio Esposito and Sebastiano Esposito both featured for Italy in their Nations League win over Turkiye on Monday.
paragraphs: Francesco Pio Esposito hopes to "share the field more often" with brother Sebastiano for Italy after they both featured against Turkiye on Monday.
Italy ran out 4-1 winners in the Nations League, marking Roberto Mancini's first win since returning to the helm.
Francesco Pio Esposito scored and assisted in the victory, while his older brother Sebastiano Esposito recorded the most shots (three) of any Italy player.

They are the fourth pair of brothers to play in the same match for Italy, after Filippo and Simone Inzaghi (twice in 2000), Aldo and Luigi Cevenini (once in 1915), and Giuseppe and Felice Milano (three times between 1912 and 1913).

Francesco Pio Esposito, meanwhile, surpassed the five-goal mark with the Azzurri at 21 years and 92 days; only two players have achieved this at a younger age: Giuseppe Meazza (19 years and 261 days) and Gianni Rivera (21 years and 78 days).
"I thoroughly enjoyed playing with Seba. It was his first time, so I tried not to overwhelm him with emotions. We had fun, and I'm happy for his debut," Francesco Pio Esposito told Vivo Azzurro.
"Hopefully, we can share the field more often. There was a lot of desire and enthusiasm, which is what you always need when wearing this shirt."
Sebastiano Esposito added: "Mancini told us to enjoy it... Although it's not easy because of the emotions you feel.
"If you're playing for Azzurri with your brother, it's even more complicated. Mancini explained how we should position ourselves and move. It was beautiful."
Italy won an away match with a 3+ goal margin for the first time since November 2019 (3-0 v Bosnia-Herzegovina).
Indeed, the Azzurri have returned to winning with Mancini as head coach after 1,198 days since the last time (3-2 v Netherlands, June 2023).

idsknt1eils211okld1u2o6kh.title: Gyokeres 'extremely happy' at Arsenal despite exit rumours
idsknt1eils211okld1u2o6kh.subtitle: Viktor Gyokeres' future at Arsenal was in doubt during the summer window, but the striker is focused on proving his worth in north London.
paragraphs: Viktor Gyokeres insists he is "extremely happy" at Arsenal and wants to fight for his place under Mikel Arteta.
The 28-year-old joined Arsenal last summer and scored 21 goals across 55 appearances as the Gunners won the Premier League and reached the finals of the Champions League and the EFL Cup.
However, the Sweden international has struggled for minutes in 2026-27, starting on just two of his five appearances across all competitions and failing to register a direct goal contribution so far.
Kai Havertz has been Arteta's preferred option so far this term, and he scored three goals across seven games before suffering an injury while representing Germany.
Gyokeres was linked with a move away from Arsenal in the summer, with reports suggesting the Gunners were willing to include him in a swap deal for Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez.
Despite the rumours, Gyokeres is fully focused on earning more minutes and scoring more goals with Arsenal.
"Of course, there was a lot of speculation," said Gyokeres. "But I had a full pre-season, and it felt good.
"I was fully focused on Arsenal. For me, staying was a given. I'm extremely happy at the club.
"It's clear that I want to play football as much as possible. Hopefully that will come, too. You always want to be on the field as a football player.
"Of course, you expect more playing time, but we have an extremely good squad with a lot of good players and have been doing well here at the start.
"I obviously need to do better and I'm willing to do it, so it's no problem. It's good [the dialogue with the coach]. I just try to do well when I get the chance and score goals."
Gyokeres is on international duty with Sweden, for whom he has scored twice in as many Nations League matches.
He is set to feature against Bosnia-Herzegovina and Romania in the same competition before Arsenal face Leeds United on October 10.

igf1gaosvt0k1spb27po4j153.title: Bayern not expected to revive Wirtz interest as Rummenigge surprised by Liverpool struggles
igf1gaosvt0k1spb27po4j153.subtitle: Florian Wirtz has struggled at Liverpool, but Bayern Munich – who were potential suitors last year – are unlikely to move for him.
paragraphs: Bayern Munich supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge does not expect the club to revive their interest in Florian Wirtz in the near future, despite the Germany international's struggles at Liverpool.
Wirtz was coveted by Bayern after helping Bayer Leverkusen win an unbeaten Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal double in 2023-24, before he made a €137m (£116m) move to Anfield last year.
But the 23-year-old creator is yet to hit top form under either Arne Slot or Andoni Iraola, only registering seven goals and nine assists in 55 outings in all competitions.
He has made six appearances for Liverpool this season, registering just one assist despite creating 12 chances – the third-most of any Reds player.
Wirtz's struggles have prompted speculation that Bayern could look to bring him back to Germany, but Rummenigge pointed out the strong options already available to Vincent Kompany in his position.
"First of all, that's not my job," Rummenigge told AZ when asked about a possible move for Wirtz.
"You mustn't forget that Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry play in that position, and there are other options such as Ismael Saibari.
"There's no need to buy a fourth player for the amount of money Wirtz would probably cost. Whether something else could still be possible at some point? I don't know.
"The question is whether Wirtz is happy at Liverpool. I can't judge that.
"Uli [Hoeness] and I were in contact with his father and mother for a while. Then they made a different decision, and we respected that."
Asked if he was surprised to see Wirtz struggle in the Premier League, Rummenigge replied: "Honestly: yes.
"We were given the impression that he was going to Liverpool because the manager at the time, Arne Slot, had promised him the number 10 position, which he had also played at Leverkusen.
"That was an important factor in his decision to choose Liverpool. Financially, there were no dramatic differences. He made his decision, and we accepted it.
"That's why I say that every step a player takes is something he has to think through carefully beforehand."
Wirtz is currently on international duty with Germany, who have four points from their first two Nations League games under Jurgen Klopp, ahead of Thursday's clash with Serbia.

j3333qh4ryty1vb7sl2pc56j4.title: World Cup defeat to Argentina most painful moment of England career, says Kane
j3333qh4ryty1vb7sl2pc56j4.subtitle: England were beaten in the semi-finals of this summer's World Cup by Argentina, a defeat Harry Kane said still plays on his mind.
paragraphs: Harry Kane described England's semi-final defeat to Argentina at this summer's World Cup as the most painful moment of his career with the Three Lions.
England were on the cusp of reaching the World Cup final for the first time since 1966 when Anthony Gordon turned in Morgan Rogers's cross in the 55th minute.
However, two late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez completed the turnaround, with Lionel Messi bagging both assists at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

Argentina were trailing until the 85th minute against England, the latest a team has been behind but gone on to win in normal time in a World Cup semi-final, making the defeat all the more difficult for Kane.
Thomas Tuchel came under fire for his tactical approach to the match, electing to replace both Gordon and Declan Rice for more defensive options to try and see the win out.

England have now been eliminated in each of their last three matches at this stage of a World Cup (1990, 2018, 2026), while Kane has also been involved in the Three Lions' defeats in the European Championship finals against both Italy and Spain.
However, England's latest setback hurt him the most, with Kane saying: "I'm so passionate about England, especially because I have been on this journey now.
"I have been to the finals, to semi-finals and been so close. Each one hurts in a different way. This one hurt, for sure. More than any other one.
"I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar [in the quarter-final against France] just in the way that it happened.
"It just felt like it wasn't us as a team. It wasn't the team that we wanted to be and said we'd be.

"I sometimes think when you maybe go against your beliefs, and you lose, it feels 10 times worse than just losing in a way where, if we lose doing it our way, you accept it, take it on the chin and move on.
"It's tough and it will still be tough. You have to move on."
The result overshadowed a landmark occasion for Kane, who made his 121st appearance in all competitions for England, the outright most of any outfield player for the nation.
England were, however, able to end the tournament on a high, claiming third place after beating France 6-4 in an enthralling clash at Hard Rock Stadium three days later.
Tuchel's side are preparing for their first match since that victory this Saturday, with World Cup champions Spain their opponents in the Nations League at Wembley Stadium.

England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2). Those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).
And Kane said while the pain from such disappointments "stays with you", England must use it as fuel as they aim to reach the next level on the international stage.
"It's something that we haven't quite been able to do in the latter stages of tournaments against the bigger nations and the better nations," Kane added.
"And it may be a mixture of things. It may be personalities, it may be mentality, it may be just the direction and how we want to play in those games.

"I think it's conversations that we need to have as a group and team. Not just sit down but as we gradually go through these next games, through this next period of the Nations League, which we want to try and win.
"We want to try and take that next step because I think that'll be an important step for us as a team.

"I know there's a perception that the Nations League may not be as important, but when you haven't won for so long, I think just the feeling of winning a trophy with England could then catapult us to head into the Euros in a couple of years."

j49lyuo2wnib157sf60kt2alp.title: Ancelotti to maintain new Brazil approach after thrashing India
j49lyuo2wnib157sf60kt2alp.subtitle: Brazil ran out 4-0 winners in their first-ever meeting with India, and Carlo Ancelotti will continue to give his younger players a chance.
paragraphs: Carlo Ancelotti insisted he will continue to give young players a chance after Brazil's comfortable win over India on Friday.
Samuel Lino scored twice in a 4-0 victory, with Estevao and Pedro also scoring in Kolkata, in what was the first-ever meeting between the two countries.
The likes of Arthur Dias (19), Gabriel Bontempo (21) and Andrey Santos (22) all started for the Selecao, while 22-year-old goalkeeper Pedro Morisco also made his debut.
Brazil accumulated 1.2 expected goals (xG) to India's 0.29, with the hosts, expectedly, not offering much threat in the attacking third.
Nevertheless, Ancelotti was pleased to see how his younger players performed, and he plans to name a similar squad for next month's international break.
"We are doing very well in these aspects, we have to give them opportunities," said Ancelotti after the win.
"These are players who have more difficulties, players who don't get playing time at their clubs have more difficulty playing a competitive game, as might be the case with Estevao and Endrick.

"Getting to know these players better, I think Jair Cunha played very well. Bontempo better in the first game than in the second game. Breno [Bidon] came on showing his qualities. Artur Dias was very good, the goalkeepers too."
Brazil have gone unbeaten during this extended international break, drawing and winning against Australia before their victory over India.
Ancelotti's side will return to Asia next month to take on Japan and Singapore in friendly matches.

jasja5a88gdg12kq75hokms6r.title: Musah aiming to repay faith shown in him by Milan boss Amorim
jasja5a88gdg12kq75hokms6r.subtitle: Yunus Musah has played a big part in AC Milan's strong start to the 2026-27 campaign, forming a strong relationship with Ruben Amorim.
paragraphs: Yunus Musah is hoping to make the most of his second chance at AC Milan after being given a new lease of life under Ruben Amorim.
Musah has become an integral part of Amorim's plans this season after falling out of favour under Massimiliano Allegri and spending the 2025-26 season out on loan.
The 23-year-old joined Atalanta but failed to make an impact, starting six games across all competitions and scoring just two goals.
However, since Amorim's arrival at San Siro, Musah has racked up 419 minutes of action for Milan in his six outings, four of which have been from the start.

And though he is yet to register a goal involvement, his performances have certainly caught the eye. Within the Rossoneri's ranks, only Samuel Chukwueze (11) and Christian Pulisic (five) have completed more dribbles than Musah's four (level with Diego Moreira).
Musah's displays have seen him return to the United States national team after missing out on their World Cup squad, and he has put his resurgence down to Amorim's impact.
"I thought maybe [he was] just saying this like other managers just to keep you there at the club," Musah said.
"But as pre-season was going on, I saw that I was playing a lot, he was talking to me a lot, and it was true. And I started the season, played a lot of minutes, a lot of starts.

The result continued Milan's strong start under Amorim, with the club sitting fifth in Serie A and just two points behind early table-toppers Roma and Inter.

jfiqg8afxo45122d6ogsbdpet.title: Palmer misses too many opportunities to represent England, says Tuchel
jfiqg8afxo45122d6ogsbdpet.subtitle: Cole Palmer was one of five players to drop out of England's Nations League squad, something Thomas Tuchel thinks he will regret.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel believes Cole Palmer has wasted yet another opportunity to play for England after the Chelsea star withdrew from the Three Lions' Nations League squad.
Palmer was a surprise omission from Tuchel's World Cup squad this summer, with an injury-hit 2025-26 campaign impacting his form and resulting in him being left out.
However, Palmer has started the new season with the bit between his teeth, scoring two goals as well as providing two assists in five Premier League games for Chelsea.
But the 24-year-old, along with Declan Rice, Marcus Rashford, Tino Livramento and Kobbie Mainoo have all dropped out, with Palmer's reasoning due to a niggling injury.

Palmer has only played three times for England since Tuchel replaced Gareth Southgate, and the Three Lions boss said his latest withdrawal could hinder his chances of future call-ups with the European Championships on the horizon.

"For sure, it's a missed opportunity," said Tuchel in a press conference ahead of their Nations League opener against Spain at Wembley Stadium. "It's another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities.
"I don't blame him for it, it's just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team.

"For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp, there is the next level of impression that you cannot achieve, because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity."
Tuchel said he was not worried players may put their clubs above playing for their country.
"We are not managing the load. When I was in club football, I used the term 'international break' and, when you hear it from the other side, it is a totally different picture," he added.
"It is a competitive environment, but it is also an environment that the players love to be a part of.
"That is what togetherness and brotherhood look like, and that is what we have created since last September in qualifying. We will never compromise on that.
"We will never let it creep in that we have a feeling players do not want to come. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England."
England are preparing for their first match since finishing third at the World Cup, when they beat France 6-4 following their semi-final defeat to Argentina.
And they take on Luis de la Fuente's world champions, who are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest ever streak by a European nation.

England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2). Those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).

k26118i798ru19zg60owop19m.title: Norway 1-2 Portugal: Ramos punishes Nyland error to seal Nations League victory
k26118i798ru19zg60owop19m.subtitle: Jorge Jesus' strong start to his Portugal tenure continued with a win over Norway, though his team were helped by Orjan Nyland's mistake.
paragraphs: Orjan Nyland's second-half error proved costly as Goncalo Ramos helped Portugal to back-to-back victories in the Nations League after a 2-1 triumph against Norway.
Nyland gifted possession to Ramos, who lofted in the winning goal, with that error coming just three minutes after Erling Haaland had hauled Stale Solbakken's side level.
Joao Felix laid the foundations for the visitors' win in the first half, with Jorge Jesus' strong start to his Portugal tenure seeing his team go top of the Group A4 table.
Both sides started brightly at Ullevaal Stadion, with Joao Neves heading over before Haaland's first-time effort was brilliantly kept out by Diogo Costa at his near post.

However, it was Jorge Jesus' side who took the lead in the 17th minute through Joao Felix, who placed a fine finish from the edge of the penalty area past the dive of Nyland and into the bottom-left corner following Pedro Neto's cutback.

Norway cranked up the pressure at the end of the first half, with Haaland's towering header thwarted by Costa once again, with the Manchester City forward then nodding into the grateful arms of the Portugal goalkeeper in first-half stoppage time.

Haaland, however, was not to be denied his customary goal. Martin Odegaard's free-kick was spilled by Costa, with Patrick Berg nodding the rebound across the six-yard box for the Norway number nine to tuck home the leveller six minutes after the restart.

But no sooner had they got themselves level, Norway fell behind again. A calamitous error from Nyland saw his pass picked off by Ramos, who took a touch before lofting the ball over the retreating goalkeeper and into the net.
Rafael Leao nearly made an instant impact off the bench, but his shot deflected off Fredrik Aursnes and onto the crossbar, before VAR saved Nyland from further embarrassment.
A long ball forward from Costa caught Norway napping and Ramos was able to steal in front of Nyland before finishing, but the goal was ruled out for an offside against him.

The hosts controlled the final 15 minutes, with Andreas Schjelderup forcing Costa into action, but Portugal's defence held firm to make it two wins from two to begin their Nations League title defence.
No Ronaldo? No problem for Portugal

Jesus elected to make four changes to the side that battled their way past Wales on his Portugal bow, with Cristiano Ronaldo, whose seven shots without scoring against Craig Bellamy's side was his most in a game for his country since October 2025, one of those alterations.

But despite a change in personnel, it was one of the starters against Wales in Joao Felix who shone once more. He has now scored six goals across his last 11 starts for Portugal, with his former Al-Nassr boss Jesus getting the best out of him.

The defending Nations League champions were put through their paces by Norway, who were led by Haaland once again. The in-form striker has now scored in 11 of his last 14 competitive games for Norway and City combined (17 goals in total), and in each of his last six (10 goals).

However, a lapse in concentration from Nyland proved costly, with Norway pushing for an equaliser in the closing stages but unable to find a way past Costa, who made five important saves to preserve his team's victory.

Solbakken will feel his team had done enough to take at least a point from the contest. Norway finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.72 from their 22 shots, with 1.69 of that tally coming from Haaland, while Portugal mustered an xG of 1.03 from their 12 attempts.

k7w5zq6s68fm1xh6odhr5uuv9.title: Mbappe reveals his mother wanted him to join Liverpool in 2017
k7w5zq6s68fm1xh6odhr5uuv9.subtitle: Real Madrid and France superstar Kylian Mbappe could have joined Liverpool nine years ago, if his mother had her way.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe has revealed he was "close" to joining Liverpool in 2017, after his mother and agent, Fayza Lamari, "fell in love" with the club during negotiations with Jurgen Klopp.

Nine years ago, Mbappe was one of the hottest properties in world football after bursting onto the scene with Monaco, having registered 40 goal involvements in just 60 appearances for the club (27 goals, 13 assists).
Mbappe ultimately joined PSG in a loan deal that became permanent the following year, plundering 256 goals in 308 outings for the Parisiens and winning 15 trophies, including six Ligue 1 titles.
He then, of course, moved to Real Madrid in 2024, and though he has scored 94 goals in just 111 games for the Spanish giants, he is yet to win the Champions League, LaLiga, or the Copa del Rey.

While working as a German television pundit at this year's World Cup, at which Mbappe became the tournament's all-time leading scorer with 22 goals, Klopp reflected on Liverpool's pursuit of the then-teenage sensation.
Klopp disclosed he accompanied several Liverpool officials on a private plane from Blackpool to Nice, where they met with Mbappe and his mother to discuss a potential transfer.
And on Tuesday, in an interview with The Athletic, Mbappe revealed just how close he came to moving to Anfield.
"It was while I was playing in Monaco. I had to take a decision," Mbappe said. "And yes, I was close to Liverpool.
"My mum was a big fan of Jurgen Klopp and the favourite destination for my mum was Liverpool. She wanted me to go there.
"I didn't listen because I wanted to play in my city, in Paris. I didn't want to leave my country before I was someone.
"But yes, my mum was always saying, 'Liverpool, you're going to be there, playing at Anfield, it's going to be insane for you.' I was like, 'Okay!'

"She went there for the first step of negotiations. She went to the city, she went to the stadium, she met the people. She was like, 'It's a wonderful club, everybody's so kind, it's a family club, a big club.'
"She went to Anfield and fell in love with it. She watched a few games alone, to feel the atmosphere, because she wanted to imagine me in this stadium.

"All the time, we were talking. She'd say, 'For me, you have to go to Liverpool'. I said, 'Okay, okay, okay', because Jurgen Klopp was an amazing manager. I met him and had a wonderful relationship with him. I had big respect for him."

Reflecting on Klopp's attempts to explain Liverpool's project, Mbappe added: "I said, 'You don't need to convince me. You're Jurgen Klopp, it's Liverpool, a great club, so if I'm here, I have some interest. But I have other things, other projects, that are also good.'
"I said to him, 'Whatever decision I take is going to be a good decision, because we are talking about some of the biggest clubs in the world.'
"It's a funny story. But in the end, I took the decision to go to PSG because for me, born and raised in Paris, there was no better feeling than to show I could be a star in my hometown."
Mbappe will be in action for France during the international break, with Les Bleus' first game under Zinedine Zidane pitting them against Turkiye on Friday, in the Nations League.

kfpdqeeqq5b61s167hfxol4ih.title: Ronaldo benched for tactical reasons, says Jesus
kfpdqeeqq5b61s167hfxol4ih.subtitle: Portugal won 2-1 against Norway in the Nations League, with Cristiano Ronaldo an unused substitute for Jorge Jesus' side on Sunday.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus insisted it was a "tactical choice" to leave Cristiano Ronaldo on the bench during Portugal's Nations League victory over Norway.
Portugal won 2-1 on Sunday at Ullevaal Stadion after goals from Joao Felix and Goncalo Ramos, which came either side of a strike from Erling Haaland.
Joao Felix has now scored six goals in his last 11 games as a starter for Portugal as he continues to thrive under Jesus, whom he also worked under at Al-Nassr.
Jesus' side struggled for much of the contest, accumulating just 1.04 expected goals (xG) after being restricted to just 38% of possession, while Norway registered 2.52 xG from 22 shots.
Nevertheless, Portugal continued their perfect start to their Nations League title defence, even with Ronaldo unable to get minutes off the bench.
"It wasn't the right moment to bring Ronaldo into the game; it was a tactical choice," said Jesus on the matter.
"I needed a player with different characteristics, but that doesn't mean he's out of the options. Perhaps he'll play against Denmark."
Haaland posed the biggest threat to Portugal's win; the Manchester City striker led the match in shots (eight) and was responsible for 1.5 of Norway's xG tally.
Although Haaland managed to score, Jesus was satisfied with the way his side defended against Norway.
"It was an excellent victory because we played against one of the best teams in Europe right now. They are in the top five, like Portugal," added Jesus.
"They have a striker who can score at any moment. It’s incredible.

"Our back line, and especially the two centre-backs, with the help of Joao Palhinha and Ruben Neves when they moved into the defensive phase, were very strong in the central corridor. Even so, Haaland had seven shots inside the box and scored once.
"We were once again organised defensively and more creative offensively, also with the introduction of new players.
"Offensively, we still lack ideas, there isn't yet a collective effort. It's normal: I haven't had time for that."

ktrfhh9h465d1pb339g4qt7bh.title: Noonan wants to build on Cincinnati's 'deciding moment' against Houston
ktrfhh9h465d1pb339g4qt7bh.subtitle: FC Cincinnati are right in the mix for a playoff spot in the Eastern Conference, and they face a struggling CF Montreal side next.
paragraphs: Pat Noonan believes FC Cincinnati's last-gasp draw against the Houston Dynamo could be a "deciding moment" in their quest to reach the playoffs this season.
Cincinnati found themselves 2-0 down after 51 minutes at Shell Energy Stadium thanks to goals from Guilherme and Mateusz Bogusz, the latter scoring from the penalty spot.
Bryan Ramirez halved the deficit in the 73rd minute before Kevin Denkey scored a spot-kick in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage time to seal a share of the spoils.
It was a result that kept Cincinnati ninth in the Eastern Conference, but the likes of New York City FC, D.C. United and Toronto FC are all chasing Noonan's side.
Cincinnati make the trip to Stade Saputo this weekend to face struggling CF Montreal, and Noonan believes his team's latest stalemate could be a solid foundation to build on.
"I think it could be a deciding moment in this stretch run," Noonan said. "We have nine games left in the season, and every game is going to be so important to pick up points.
"And that's because of the position that we're in, where we're fighting for a playoff spot. This isn't about everything being pretty now, or style.
"We were able to get an important point, and so, for the psyche of the group and how to be on the road, like I said, against a strong opponent and push the game like that.
"How do we get more of that urgency, but not recklessness?"
Montreal, meanwhile, will just want the 2026 season to come to an end after they were beaten 2-0 by the Columbus Crew in their last league match.
Only Sporting Kansas City (17) have lost more MLS matches this season than Montreal (15), who find themselves rooted to the bottom of the East on 21 points from 26 games.
It's also been a disappointing start to Alexis Sanchez's Montreal career, as he has failed to register a single goal contribution in his seven matches for the club.
During their defeat to Columbus, Sanchez's frustrations were evident as his team struggled to create any opportunities whenever they got the chance to go forward.
Interim boss Philippe Eullaffroy understood the Chilean's concerns about the team, but he said Sanchez remained committed to the cause and was just showing his passion.
"Alexis would like the team to play faster forward and use more space behind the defenders. I agree, and I ask for it, but it is not happening," Eullaffroy conceded.
"After the game, he was upset and tense about the development of the second half, as were several of his team-mates."
Montreal – Prince Owusu
In a season of frustration for Montreal, Owusu has been the only shining light, scoring 13 goals in 24 league appearances so far this season.
Owusu also has a good record against Montreal. He has scored three goals in six MLS outings against them, only managing to find the back of the net more against D.C. (four).
Cincinnati – Kevin Denkey
With Denkey unavailable after being selected to represent Togo during the international break, Evander will be the man Cincinnati will turn to in the final third.
Only Inter Miami's Lionel Messi (33) has more goal involvements in the MLS this season than Evander's 25 (13 goals, 12 assists).
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW

Cincinnati earned a draw when trailing by two goals for the eighth time in the club's MLS era (since 2019) against Houston last time out. Three of those occurrences have happened this season and in all three of those occurrences in 2026, they had trailed by two goals in the second half.
But they will be hoping for a better result here. They have a good record against Montreal, winning their last four MLS meetings against them.
And Noonan's side will be desperate for a win. They are without a victory in their last five league matches (D3 L2) since a 2-1 triumph over NYCFC on August 19.

Montreal, meanwhile, will be out to end their poor run at Stade Saputo. Only Minnesota United (two) have fewer home wins in the MLS this season than Montreal (three), who last won in front of their home crowd on May 9 against Orlando City.

Pat Noonan believes FC Cincinnati's last-gasp draw against the Houston Dynamo could be a "deciding moment" in their quest to reach the playoffs this season.

Cincinnati found themselves 2-0 down after 51 minutes at Shell Energy Stadium thanks to goals from Guilherme and Mateusz Bogusz, the latter scoring from the penalty spot.

Bryan Ramirez halved the deficit in the 73rd minute before Kevin Denkey scored a spot-kick in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage time to seal a share of the spoils.

It was a result that kept Cincinnati ninth in the Eastern Conference, but the likes of New York City FC, D.C. United and Toronto FC are all chasing Noonan's side. 

Cincinnati make the trip to Stade Saputo this weekend to face struggling CF Montreal, and Noonan believes his team's latest stalemate could be a solid foundation to build on.

"I think it could be a deciding moment in this stretch run," Noonan said. "We have nine games left in the season, and every game is going to be so important to pick up points.

"And that's because of the position that we're in, where we're fighting for a playoff spot. This isn't about everything being pretty now, or style.

"We were able to get an important point, and so, for the psyche of the group and how to be on the road, like I said, against a strong opponent and push the game like that.

"How do we get more of that urgency, but not recklessness?"

Montreal, meanwhile, will just want the 2026 season to come to an end after they were beaten 2-0 by the Columbus Crew in their last league match.

Only Sporting Kansas City (17) have lost more MLS matches this season than Montreal (15), who find themselves rooted to the bottom of the East on 21 points from 26 games.

It's also been a disappointing start to Alexis Sanchez's Montreal career, as he has failed to register a single goal contribution in his seven matches for the club.

During their defeat to Columbus, Sanchez's frustrations were evident as his team struggled to create any opportunities whenever they got the chance to go forward.

Interim boss Philippe Eullaffroy understood the Chilean's concerns about the team, but he said Sanchez remained committed to the cause and was just showing his passion.

"Alexis would like the team to play faster forward and use more space behind the defenders. I agree, and I ask for it, but it is not happening," Eullaffroy conceded.

"After the game, he was upset and tense about the development of the second half, as were several of his team-mates."

Montreal – Prince Owusu

In a season of frustration for Montreal, Owusu has been the only shining light, scoring 13 goals in 24 league appearances so far this season.

Cincinnati – Kevin Denkey

With Denkey unavailable after being selected to represent Togo during the international break, Evander will be the man Cincinnati will turn to in the final third.

l19ef15wtq3j18exn3r706lgc.title: Portugal shelve Ronaldo controversy as Jesus demands full focus on Norway
l19ef15wtq3j18exn3r706lgc.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo's exit from the Portugal squad has hogged the headlines in recent days, but Jorge Jesus' team have another game to play.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus says Portugal's focus is purely on Sunday's clash with Norway, with the fallout from Cristiano Ronaldo's departure being shelved until after that game.
Ronaldo's glittering international career may be over after he stormed out of Portugal's camp earlier this week, amid reports of a rift with new head coach Jesus.
Jesus – who worked with Ronaldo at Al-Nassr – left the 41-year-old on the bench throughout a 2-1 Nations League win over Erling Haaland and company in Oslo last week.

Ronaldo then trained away from his team-mates before leaving the camp on the eve of the Selecao's entertaining 4-2 win over Denmark on Thursday, which saw Joao Cancelo, Goncalo Ramos, Vitinha and Joao Felix get on the scoresheet.

Ronaldo took to social media to say he will "tell the truth" about his exit from the camp in due course, while Jesus has refused to go into detail about the incident, only saying he would never allow any player to dictate his decisions as a coach.

Portugal will play their first home game since Ronaldo's departure on Sunday, knowing another victory over Norway at Porto's Estadio do Dragao would all but guarantee qualification for the last eight next March.
And that is the only thing on Jesus' mind, as he told reporters: "The focus has to be on the national team, and on Norway in this case, on what we have to do well.
"It's not about us ignoring Cris, he is a symbol of the national team and of Portugal. After the game, there will be plenty of time to talk about it."

Asked if Ronaldo could at least return in an ambassadorial role before the 2030 World Cup, which Portugal will co-host alongside Spain and Morocco, Jesus said: "You are already looking ahead to 2030. It's four years. Football is day by day, it's not even month by month.
"Tomorrow [Sunday], the game is the most important thing. It will be very intense, and that's what I want to talk about. I don't want to change the subject.
"I'm going to focus on what I talked about – the team and our opponent. Norway is a team, in my opinion, who are in the top five in Europe, with great players.
"Then, we will have time to analyse what happens here."
Jesus was then asked what sort of reception he expected from Portugal's home fans, given the perception of a rift between himself and the country's greatest-ever player.
"The affection that I seek is nothing more than what the national team should get," he said. "The affection should be for the team, for the players.
"I am part of a team, I am the commander of a team. Before, I was also a staunch, crazy fan of the national team, and I didn't look at the coach or the players, I looked at the flag.
"I don't want to be part of anything except the national team."

Since the start of 2025, Portugal have won 80% of their matches when Ronaldo has not appeared (P5 W4 D1), compared to just 59% when he has featured (P17 W10 D4 L3), also averaging almost twice as many goals per game without Ronaldo (3.4) than with him (1.9).

lch8oscyb3r011xedse39jmpj.title: Slegers accepts pressure amid poor Arsenal form
lch8oscyb3r011xedse39jmpj.subtitle: Arsenal's poor start to the season could get worse when they face Manchester City on Sunday, and Renee Slegers knows results must improve.
paragraphs: Renee Slegers acknowledged she has "to find the solutions" to Arsenal's poor form ahead of their huge Women's Super League clash with Manchester City this weekend.
Arsenal are winless in each of their last three league games (D2 L1) and could equal their worst runs without victory in the competition, set in May 2014 and October 2023.
The Gunners are only the third team in WSL history to score two or fewer goals and concede two or fewer goals across their opening four matches, along with Liverpool in 2014 and Chelsea in 2018-19.
Failure to win this game will see Arsenal record their second-worst start after five games in the division, behind only 2014 (four).
"I have to find the solutions, I have to be calm. I have to get direction," said Slegers.
"I have to lead now but at the same time, what I also feel is gratitude for how everyone is responding and how together we are, the session on the pitch was today. It was really, really good."
Slegers also explained the reason for missing her post-match interview after Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Paris FC in the Women's Champions League, during which the WSL side squandered a two-goal lead.
"After the game, there was emotion from my end but to control that point quickly I made the decision to be with the team instead," said the Gunners boss.
"So I spent time with the players straight after the game. I thought that was important and that was a decision I made in the moment in my leadership and I decided to be with the team."
City have won their home game against Arsenal in six of the last nine WSL seasons (D1 L2), with those matches averaging 3.9 goals (21 for City, 14 for the Gunners).
Arsenal versus City is one of only two WSL fixtures to see both teams win 10+ times, with the Gunners leading the head-to-head 12-11 (2 draws).

lhamzf4q2c8s18bytkx0sf7qz.title: Spain 4-1 Croatia: Yamal nets brace as unbeaten run reaches 40 games
lhamzf4q2c8s18bytkx0sf7qz.subtitle: In their first home match since winning the World Cup, Spain defeated Croatia at Estadio Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan in the Nations League.
paragraphs: Lamine Yamal scored twice and got an assist for Spain as the world champions defeated Croatia 4-1 in the Nations League.

Marc Pubill and Nico Williams were also on the scoresheet for La Roja at Estadio Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan, where Rodri showcased the World Cup before kick-off in Spain's first home game since winning the competition in the summer.

Just as he did against England in their Nations League opener, Yamal opened the scoring inside the first two minutes as he curled Alex Baena's cut-back into the bottom-left corner with a first-time finish.

Spain pushed for a second, with Pau Cubarsi shooting narrowly wide from distance, but Croatia scored against the run of play just before the half-hour mark as Dion Beljo headed in from Ivan Perisic's pinpoint cross.
However, the hosts were back ahead just three minutes later as Yamal played a corner short before eventually sending in a cross, which was headed in by an unmarked Pubill in the six-yard box.

Mikel Oyarzabal saw a goal ruled out for offside and Fermin Lopez struck the woodwork before half-time, but Spain eventually got their third in the 63rd minute as Yamal powered in at the near post following Pedri's level reverse pass.

Pedri saw a long-range strike pushed away by Dominik Livakovic shortly after Franjo Ivanovic curled wide at the other end, though Williams wrapped up a comfortable victory with a clinical finish in the 89th minute.
Yamal becoming inevitable for club and country

Through Yamal, Spain have scored in the first two minutes of play in consecutive matches for the first time in any competition since at least 2004, and it was just the start of another stellar performance from the teenager.

To go along with his two goals and assist, Yamal also created the joint-most chances for his side (two), attempted the most passes in the final third (24) and the most dribbles (nine), while also winning both of his tackles.
Despite conceding, Luis de la Fuente's side were in control throughout, accumulating 1.77 expected goals (xG) from 16 attempts while restricting Croatia to just 0.44 xG from five shots.
La Roja are now unbeaten in their last 40 matches across all competitions (W31 D9), the best such record by a European nation.

Indeed, Spain have won each of their last nine matches in all competitions, equalling their best winning streak with De la Fuente as head coach (W9 between June and July 2024), and it means they remain in control of Group A3 in the Nations League after winning six points from their opening two games.

lk70bbzpvx2910hrv2orwnf4b.title: Gakpo withdraws from Netherlands squad with ankle injury
lk70bbzpvx2910hrv2orwnf4b.subtitle: Liverpool have been dealt another injury blow during the international break, with Cody Gakpo the latest to return to Merseyside.
paragraphs: Cody Gakpo has returned to Liverpool and is unavailable for the Netherlands' last two Nations League games after suffering an ankle injury.
The forward sustained the issue in the Netherlands' 2-1 win over Serbia on Sunday and was substituted after just 17 minutes following a hard tackle.
Following the game, Xavi said he did not think the injury was serious, but after tests on Monday, Gakpo has withdrawn from the Netherlands squad.
Nobody has been called up to replace him for the remaining two games of the international break.
Liverpool confirmed Gakpo would undergo further assessment at their training centre but did not say how long he was expected to be sidelined.
It is a blow for the Dutchman, who has made a strong start to the season after being linked with a transfer away from Anfield to Tottenham and Manchester City this summer.
He has already racked up six goal involvements in all competitions – two goals and four assists – more than any other player for the club.
His 13 chances created, meanwhile, are second only to Dominik Szoboszlai.
Liverpool return to action against City on October 11.

m2km546gaa8e10unl6wphjtoa.title: Colombia must give Suarez more support, says head coach Lorenzo
m2km546gaa8e10unl6wphjtoa.subtitle: Colombia lost 1-0 to Paraguay in a friendly on Friday, with star striker Luis Suarez unable to make an impact at Sports Illustrated Stadium.
paragraphs: Colombia head coach Nestor Lorenzo believes his side "should have supported Luis Suarez a bit more" in their defeat to Paraguay on Friday.
Paraguay won 1-0 at Sports Illustrated Stadium thanks to Hugo Benitez's winner in the 56th minute.
Although Colombia recorded almost three times as many shots as Paraguay (14 to five), the latter accumulated more expected goals (0.95 to 0.89) and hit the target just as often (two).
Colombia struggled to get Suarez into the game; the striker was responsible for just one of their 14 shots and recorded the fewest touches of any starting player in the team (14).
Suarez had scored in each of his previous seven games for club and country, netting eight times in that run, and Lorenzo acknowledged Colombia must create more chances for their talisman.
"I think we should have supported Luis Suarez a bit more," said Lorenzo.
"We needed more width from the full-backs. And when we did get forward, perhaps we didn't deliver enough crosses, and we faced an opponent that defends very well deep in their own half.

"The problem is that we struggled to get our build-up play right, we let ourselves get pressed, we made a lot of mistakes in that area, and we played against a team that had just come from a very well-prepared World Cup, which made things difficult for us.
"There were times when we made very simple, very childish mistakes, I'd say, in the final play; either we didn't cross the ball, or we went back and lost possession.
"We're still building, and we'll draw conclusions as time goes on. I think there are some positive things to highlight, even though I acknowledge the team didn't play well."
Colombia face Peru in the final game of the international break on October 6.
