mh0lx0bjz5fa1j2rormxlpiry.title: Croatia 0-7 England: Tuchel's forwards dazzle in seismic Nations League win
mh0lx0bjz5fa1j2rormxlpiry.subtitle: England inflicted the heaviest defeat in Croatia's history, with Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka each scoring twice in a 7-0 demolition.
paragraphs: England turned in a devastating attacking performance to rout Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable Nations League encounter in Rijeka on Saturday.

Amid a bizarre atmosphere generated by a crowd made up almost entirely of schoolchildren, due to restrictions imposed on Croatia by UEFA, Thomas Tuchel's forwards effectively had the game won by half-time.

Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka were all on target before the break, with Kane and Saka getting another goal apiece in the second half and Morgan Rogers coming off the bench to get in on the act.

As they did in the second half of the teams' previous meeting, at the World Cup in June, England came flying out of the traps. On his first senior start, Alex Scott fed Bellingham on the edge of the area, and when the Real Madrid star slipped in Kane, he lifted his finish into the top-left corner for an eighth-minute opener.

Dominik Livakovic denied his Barcelona team-mate Gordon on two occasions either side of that goal, but a tremendous piece of skill from the winger led to England doubling their lead in the 21st minute.
Gordon plucked Saka's overhit cross out of the air with a glorious touch on the outside of his right boot, then centred for Bellingham to prod into a gaping net.

Both Saka and Gordon missed opportunities to add a quickfire third for England, but the visitors' relentless attacking play was rewarded again in the 39th minute, with Gordon darting in at the far post to nod Jarell Quansah's cross home.

Mateo Kovacic somehow failed to get Croatia back into the contest when he rounded Pickford and sliced wide of a completely unguarded goal, and it was 4-0 on the stroke of half-time as Gordon and Bellingham linked up on the left, with the latter providing a pinpoint delivery from which Saka could not miss.

And if Slaven Bilic hoped England might ease up after the interval, the Croatia boss was mistaken. Elliot Anderson played a superb give-and-go with Saka before steering a cross in from the right, with Kane sliding in to secure his brace in the 53rd minute.

Bellingham passed up a chance to make it 6-0 before the hour mark, but Josip Stanisic soon gifted England another goal. He planted a dismal pass straight into the chest of Saka inside the area, and after an exchange of passes with Kane, the winger finished into the top-left corner.

Saka should have had the match ball when he lifted a cross from Rogers over the crossbar, but the latter joined the fun three minutes from time, having rounded Livakovic following Bellingham's defence-splitting pass.
Magnificent seven as Three Lions feast on crumbling Croatia
There was plenty of frustration about the way Tuchel reined in England's attackers when it mattered at the World Cup, but he has let them strut their stuff at the start of this new cycle.

Before Saturday, Croatia's record defeat was a 6-0 loss in Spain eight years ago, and they had never lost at home by a margin greater than three goals. Here, they were arguably fortunate to only concede seven – England racked up 6.14 expected goals (xG) to their 1.37.

In front of just 100 travelling fans, all of England's front four were at their brilliant best. Kane's brace took him to 11 international goals this year, making him the first player to reach double figures in three different calendar years for the Three Lions (also 12 in 2019 and 16 in 2021).
Kane and Gordon are the first pair of players to score in three straight games for England since November 2019, when Kane achieved the same feat alongside Marcus Rashford.
Bellingham's goal was perhaps the pick of the bunch, with Gordon doing brilliantly to tee him up at the end of a 27-pass move – the most for any England goal in the Nations League.

Bellingham also became the first England player to record three assists in a single game since Trent Alexander-Arnold versus San Marino in November 2021, while Saka scored twice with his right foot in a senior match for the first time, in 378 outings for club and country.
England have one more game to play in this international break, against Czechia at Wembley on Tuesday, when three points could all but secure a spot in the quarter-finals next March.

Bellingham passed up a chance to make it 6-0 before the hour mark, but Josip Stanisic soon gifted England another goal. He planted a dismal pass straight into the chest of Saka inside the area, and after an exchange of passes with Kane, the winger finished into the top-left corner.

Saka should have had the match ball when he lifted a cross from Rogers over the crossbar, but the latter joined the fun three minutes from time, having rounded Livakovic following Bellingham's defence-splitting pass.

Magnificent seven as Three Lions feast on crumbling Croatia

There was plenty of frustration about the way Tuchel reined in England's attackers when it mattered at the World Cup, but he has let them strut their stuff at the start of this new cycle.

Before Saturday, Croatia's record defeat was a 6-0 loss in Spain eight years ago, and they had never lost at home by a margin greater than three goals. Here, they were arguably fortunate to only concede seven – England racked up 6.14 expected goals (xG) to their 1.37.

In front of just 100 travelling fans, all of England's front four were at their brilliant best. Kane's brace took him to 11 international goals this year, making him the first player to reach double figures in three different calendar years for the Three Lions (also 12 in 2019 and 16 in 2021).

Kane and Gordon are the first pair of players to score in three straight games for England since November 2019, when Kane achieved the same feat alongside Marcus Rashford.

Bellingham's goal was perhaps the pick of the bunch, with Gordon doing brilliantly to tee him up at the end of a 27-pass move – the most for any England goal in the Nations League.

Bellingham also became the first England player to record three assists in a single game since Trent Alexander-Arnold versus San Marino in November 2021, while Saka scored twice with his right foot in a senior match for the first time, in 378 outings for club and country.

England have one more game to play in this international break, against Czechia at Wembley on Tuesday, when three points could all but secure a spot in the quarter-finals next March.

mmi7g1n06ape19ev8uvfhbhip.title: Xavi confident Zirkzee can 'help Netherlands enormously'
mmi7g1n06ape19ev8uvfhbhip.subtitle: Joshua Zirkzee received a surprise call-up to replace the injured Brian Brobbey, and Xavi is excited to see how he can help the Netherlands.
paragraphs: Xavi believes Joshua Zirkzee suits the Netherlands' new style after calling him up to the squad as an injury replacement.
Brian Brobbey left the Netherlands camp after their 1-1 draw with Germany in their Nations League opener, with Zirkzee receiving his first call-up in just under two years.
Zirkzee has six Netherlands caps to his name, with his last call-up to the squad coming in November 2024.
The decision was questioned, with Zirkzee only making four substitute appearances for Manchester United this season without scoring.
Memphis Depay and Wout Weghorst are the other more commonly picked options in that position, but Xavi is confident Zirkzee will slot into his team.
"He can be very important for us. I think he's a good player. He can help us enormously," Xavi said.
"Our striker must understand our system and our ideas. He can help us more than the others at the moment. We focus on the players we select."
The Netherlands needed a 92nd-minute equaliser from Cody Gakpo to snatch a point against Germany, but Xavi will feel it is the least they deserved after a dominant second-half performance.
The Oranje finished that game with 3.2 expected goals (xG) from 22 shots, 10 of which were on target, as Germany were indebted to Marc ter Stegen's nine saves.
Xavi's side are now on a four-match winless streak in the Nations League, something the Spaniard will be looking to put right away to Serbia on Sunday.
"We have to win. It is an important match for the placement," Xavi said.
"[On Sunday], we will determine the line-up. I am happy with all the players who are available at the moment.
"Serbia play very differently. It will be a tough match against a physical team. They play a lot of long balls. We have to be prepared for that.
"The goal is to win and take the three points."
Serbia lost their Nations League opener 2-1 to Greece and sit bottom of Group A2, just behind the Netherlands.

mo77e3ujbt941eskdq7gnr5ao.title: The Numbers Game: Underperforming Arsenal take on perfect Man City
mo77e3ujbt941eskdq7gnr5ao.subtitle: With just five points and two goals to their name in the WSL this season, Arsenal are under increasing pressure ahead of facing Man City.
paragraphs: Arsenal were Manchester City's closest challengers for the Women's Super League title last season, with Andree Jeglertz's side finishing five points ahead of the Gunners.
But four games into the 2026-27 season, there is already a seven-point gap between the sides, with City boasting the division's only 100% record and Arsenal's title hopes already slipping away.
If Renee Slegers' side are to have any real chance of topping the pile at the end of the campaign, avoiding defeat at the Etihad Stadium on Sunday is surely a must.
Here, we use Opta insights to preview this weekend's headline clash and consult the Opta supercomputer to see who might come out on top.
What's expected?
The Opta supercomputer is forecasting another victory for the WSL leaders, with City triumphing in 49.7% of the model's pre-match simulations.
Arsenal's win probability is rated at 25%, with the remaining 25.3% of scenarios seeing the points shared.

These sides have proven to be well-matched historically, with City versus Arsenal being one of only two WSL fixtures to see both teams beat the other 10 or more times – the Gunners currently lead their head-to-head record 12-11 (two draws).

In addition, only Chelsea versus Arsenal (32 times), Arsenal against Liverpool (27) and Chelsea versus Liverpool (26) have been contested more times in WSL history than City against Arsenal (25 times before Sunday).
Their last head-to-head meeting, at Emirates Stadium in February, went the way of Arsenal as Olivia Smith scored the only goal in the 17th minute.

But City triumphed when they last hosted the Gunners, exactly one year before this fixture, on October 4, 2025. Iman Beney's 88th-minute strike earned a 3-2 victory for Jeglertz's team, with Khadija Shaw, Kerstin Casparij, Mariona Caldentey and Chloe Kelly also among the goals.
City have won their home game against Arsenal in six of the last nine WSL seasons (D1 L2), with those matches averaging 3.9 goals each time (21 for City, 14 for the Gunners).
City bid for perfect five
City have previously won their opening five games of a WSL campaign on two occasions, doing so in 2016 (first six) and 2017-18 (first seven).
In the former season, they went unbeaten and beat Chelsea to the title, and in the latter, they finished second following the Blues' own Invincible campaign.

Of the previous nine teams to start a WSL season with five straight wins, seven have gone on to finish in the top two, with three (City in 2016, Arsenal in 2018-19 and Chelsea in 2024-25) winning the title in those respective campaigns.
City have made a professional start to their title defence, sweeping aside Birmingham City (3-1), Aston Villa (4-1) and Liverpool (4-2) before battling to a 1-0 win at Charlton Athletic last weekend.

Jeglertz's team have averaged over 3 expected goals (xG) per game so far this term, putting up a tally of 12.2 (only bettered by Chelsea's 12.4) across the first four matchdays, although they have looked a little more vulnerable than the Swede would like at the other end, with three teams posting better xGA figures than their 3.96.

Their domestic form has been better than their results in Europe this term, having played out a 1-1 Champions League draw with Real Madrid on Thursday, after splitting four goals equally with Bayern Munich on matchday one.
Indeed, home has been where the heart is for City, who have won each of their last 14 home WSL matches.
Only Chelsea – who won an astonishing 22 straight matches on their own turf between March 2022 and February 2024 – have posted more consecutive home victories in the WSL.
This game will represent a landmark appearance for City captain Alex Greenwood, who will hope to celebrate her 200th WSL outing with a victory.

She will become the 10th player to pass the 200-game mark in the WSL, and if she starts, she will claim the record for the most starts made in a player's first 200 outings in the competition, overhauling Gemma Bonner (192).
Drab start piles pressure on Slegers
Instead of kicking on from their runner-up WSL finish last season, Arsenal have endured a drab start that has led to tough questions being asked of Slegers.

Arsenal are only the third team in WSL history to score two goals or fewer, while also conceding two goals or fewer, in their opening four matches of a season. Liverpool previously did so in 2014, while Chelsea replicated the feat in 2018-19 but recovered to finish third.
If Arsenal fail to win on Sunday, they are guaranteed to record their second-worst start to a WSL season through five matches, with their four-point haul in 2014 being their worst-ever.

And, having failed to win any of their last three WSL games (D2 L1), the Gunners could equal their worst winless streaks in the competition, having previously endured four-match droughts in May 2014 and October 2023.

Arsenal managed a mere 0.79 xG in last week's 1-0 loss at Chelsea, then were similarly lacklustre in attack on Wednesday, as they squandered a 2-0 lead to draw 2-2 with Paris FC in the Champions League.

The bizarre 87th-minute penalty Leah Williamson conceded by picking up a live ball, thinking she was taking a goal-kick, did not help matters, but the Gunners only put up 1.16 xG from open play compared to Paris' 1.44, so the result was hardly unjust.

And when looking at Arsenal's underlying attacking metrics, it becomes clear that their problem is twofold – they are not creative enough, or ruthless enough when they do generate scoring opportunities.

The Gunners underperformed their xG figures by 4.64 across the first four matchdays of the WSL season (two goals, 6.64 xG), though that underperformance was not the worst in the league – Brighton netted three times from 8.33 xG – and only Everton (0.07) averaged a lower xG figure per shot than the Gunners' 0.9 (level with Aston Villa).

Arsenal's 2.56% conversion rate so far in 2026-27 is truly dismal, given nine of the WSL's 14 teams have found the net with at least 10% of their shots (a group that includes City at 13.64%), and if the visitors are to get their season back on track, their big-name attackers simply must do more.

Alessia Russo, Caldentey, Stina Blackstenius and Kelly are all yet to find the net in the WSL this term, with Russo posting the worst xG underperformance of any player in the division (2.14 xG), although she did get on the scoresheet in Paris in midweek.
Manchester City – Lauren Hemp
With nine so far, Hemp is the only player to create more chances following a ball carry of at least five metres than Arsenal's Lisa Baum (five) in the WSL this season.

That pair of attackers have also tallied the joint-most shot-ending carries in the division through the first four matchdays (eight each, level with Lauren James), so we could be set for an intriguing duel in the wide areas.
Arsenal – Stina Blackstenius
Given Arsenal's attacking woes, they may need Blackstenius to step up against a team she has enjoyed facing in the past.
Blackstenius has scored (four goals in total) or assisted (two) on each of her last five WSL appearances against Man City.
It is the joint-longest such streak against the Citizens in the competition (alongside Lee Geum-Min), and Blackstenius is also the only player to score three winning goals against City in the WSL.

mr1iggwb17y81ahlcehafr1g3.title: Van Dijk only needed '10 seconds' to decide Netherlands future in Xavi meeting
mr1iggwb17y81ahlcehafr1g3.subtitle: After considering international retirement, Virgil van Dijk plans to continue until Euro 2028, despite the fact he will turn 37 that year.
paragraphs: Virgil van Dijk said it took him 10 seconds to decide to continue playing for the Netherlands when he held a meeting with new head coach Xavi.
Some had questioned whether the 2026 World Cup might be Van Dijk's last major international tournament, after the Netherlands impressively won their group before crashing out in the round of 32.
They were beaten on penalties by Morocco following a 1-1 draw, failing to reach the round of 16 when appearing at the World Cup for the very first time (failed to qualify on eight occasions).
Van Dijk has won 96 caps for his country and, after deciding to play on, he could bring up a century during the current international break.
The Netherlands open their Nations League campaign at home to Germany on Thursday, before back-to-back away games versus Serbia and Greece, and a home clash with Serbia on October 4.
And when former World Cup-winning midfielder Xavi visited Van Dijk in Liverpool to discuss his international future, the centre-back was given an easy decision.
"I needed a well-deserved holiday with my family and then an important meeting with the national coach," he said at a press conference, as quoted by De Telegraaf.
"After 10 seconds, I already knew I could continue. That was just a very good meeting. It's about trust and appreciation, and he said I could be important to the team.
"Physically, there is no doubt [I can continue], but I also want to keep having fun and feel the appreciation, and that is certainly there."
Van Dijk expects to play in a back four under Xavi, whose predecessor Ronald Koeman was repeatedly criticised by the Dutch media for reverting to a five-man backline during his two spells in charge.
"The way I experience it now, I don't think we're going to play with five at the back," Van Dijk said.
"Spain became world champions with four at the back. Most players are used to playing with four defenders."
Thursday's matchup in Amsterdam will pit Van Dijk against one of the most influential figures in his career, with former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp taking charge of Germany for the first time.
Van Dijk played 270 games under Klopp after being signed from Southampton by the German in January 2018, comfortably the most he has played under a single manager (Arne Slot is second, with 104).

And though Van Dijk wishes Klopp well in his new role, he is determined to inflict a debut defeat on his old boss, saying: "It's very nice to meet him again. He has been a very important person in my career, like Ronald Koeman.

"I was able to speak to him during the World Cup, after a training session in Dallas. It will be nice to see him again tomorrow, but hopefully we can make sure that he loses his first game as the coach of Germany."

msgz9o7jbdtj1tyq3mhlzvhcm.title: Mbappe has a 'good feeling' about Ballon d'Or
msgz9o7jbdtj1tyq3mhlzvhcm.subtitle: Kylian Mbappe has previously insisted he should win the Ballon d'Or this year, and the Frenchman has a "good feeling" about the award.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe has a "good feeling" about winning the Ballon d'Or this year.
Mbappe has been highly vocal recently over his ambitions to win the award for the first time.
The Frenchman is likely to be going up against Bayern Munich's Harry Kane and Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal, who has also insisted he should be considered as the favourite for the award.
While Yamal played a role in Spain winning the World Cup, Mbappe has scored 50 goals in 52 games for Real Madrid since the start of last season.
Of players in Europe's top five leagues, only Kane (67) has netted more club goals than Mbappe in that time.

Mbappe, who is also on 499 goal involvements in his club career, also finished as the top scorer at the World Cup, with 10 strikes to his name. He is now the record goalscorer in the history of the competition (22 goals).
And the 27-year-old feels this is his time to win the Ballon d'Or.
He told RFI: "I've had a good year. I've had a great year on an individual level, and I know that's the most important criterion for the Ballon d'Or.
"I was the top scorer in all the major competitions, and I think this could be a good year for me. I've got a good feeling about it.
"At the Ballon d’Or, they won’t be announcing a team in the envelope, but a player. So it's an individual trophy, and I think that's what has to take precedence over everything else.

"Of course, we must not overlook everything else, but the ability to perform well individually and to leave a lasting impression is what makes an impact on people when it comes to a trophy like that."
When it was put to him if he would be disappointed not to win the Ballon d'Or, Mbappe said: "Of course.
"A competitor is always disappointed when he doesn’t win. At that point, I think it'll be my competitive spirit that takes a knock. But we'll have to wait and see how it all pans out."

mz025kf3aw1y11c4kmb4cu2gn.title: Brighton 'don’t fear' player or manager exits, insists CEO Barber
mz025kf3aw1y11c4kmb4cu2gn.subtitle: Brighton are flying high in the Premier League this season, while they also have their eyes on European silverware in 2026-27.
paragraphs: Brighton chief executive Paul Barber insists the club "don't fear" losing players or coaches, as they have succession plans in place.
The Seagulls are flying high under Fabian Hurzeler this season, sitting third in the Premier League after five games.
They thrashed reigning champions Arsenal 3-0 before the international break, while they also reached the last 16 of the EFL Cup with a thrilling comeback win over Manchester United.
Brighton are the highest scorers in the Premier League this season, with their 16 goals the most by a side in their first five games since Manchester City in 2022-23 (19).
The likes of Maxim De Cuyper, Charalampos Kostoulas and Malick Yalcouye have impressed for the Seagulls, while Pascal Gross also won the Premier League Player of the Month award for September.
"If we do well, it's because our players and coaches are doing well. And if that happens, they're going to be on someone else's radar," Barber told Sky Sports News.
"We've been through that loop many times before, but that's our model. We don't fear it – we have succession plans in place on and off the field."

n050ylnj3vma1krl42q5ywaf4.title: Xavi: A shame for Netherlands to lose injured Van Hecke
n050ylnj3vma1krl42q5ywaf4.subtitle: The Netherlands have been dealt another injury blow, with Jan Paul van Hecke the latest to withdraw from the squad and return to his club.
paragraphs: Jan Paul van Hecke had to leave the Netherlands' Nations League squad through injury, with Xavi saying it is a "shame" the team will be without the defender.
It was confirmed on Wednesday that Van Hecke would return to Tottenham for further treatment for an issue he sustained against Serbia on Sunday.
Van Hecke had started both of the Netherlands' matches so far, partnering Virgil van Dijk in defence to help the team to a 1-1 draw with Germany and a 2-1 win over Serbia.
But he will play no further part in this international break, despite Xavi admitting that he had tried to fight through it.
"He took a knock against Serbia," Xavi said of Van Hecke. "He is a fighter, and he did try to keep going over the past few days.
"In training [on Wednesday], it became clear that the pain is too severe. That is a shame.
"But we still have 23 players left, and there are plenty of defenders among them."
It is the latest in a string of injuries for the Netherlands, who have already seen the likes of Donyell Malen, Brian Brobbey and Cody Gakpo among those to withdraw.
"It is the match schedule; you can't do anything about it. You have to adapt," Xavi added when asked about their injuries.
The Netherlands' win over Serbia last time out was Xavi's first, and they now turn their attention to Greece, who currently sit top of Group A2.
Last time out, Greece secured a shock 1-0 victory over Jurgen Klopp's Germany, but Xavi is not going into Thursday's clash with any fear.
"We cannot be afraid of Greece; we do have respect," he said of their opponents.
"They are doing well. They have a lot of talent, especially in the forward line. But it will be difficult."

n2peumd1da511dnwy8n8k7ax8.title: Tuchel: England cannot be in holiday mode
n2peumd1da511dnwy8n8k7ax8.subtitle: England face Croatia behind closed doors on Saturday, and Thomas Tuchel is wary of a pre-season vibe creeping in.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel has urged his England players not to "switch off and be in a holiday mood" ahead of their behind-closed-doors Nations League clash with Croatia.
England bounced back from their defeat to Spain with a 2-0 victory over Czechia last time out, leaving them second in Group A3.

The Three Lions have won six of their last eight Nations League matches (L2), scoring 20 goals in the process. That is more wins (W5 D6 L7) and goals (18) than they managed in their first 18 games in the competition.

England have also won five of their last seven matches against Croatia in all competitions (D1 L1), scoring at least four goals in three of those wins (4-1 in September 2008, 5-1 in September 2009, 4-2 in June 2026).
History is also on the line for Tuchel's side; a win in this game would see them equal their record of nine away wins in a row between December 1965 and October 1967 under Alf Ramsey.

However, Saturday's match is being played mostly behind closed doors due to crowd disturbances involving Croatia fans during a Nations League match against France in March 2025. There is an exception for schoolchildren, plus 100 travelling England supporters.
"To be behind closed doors, it's never nice. It's a strange atmosphere," said Tuchel.
"Everyone would love the atmosphere in the stadium – a proper football crowd which would be very, very different. This is a part we have to take into consideration.
"We cannot switch off and be in holiday mood. It might feel a bit like pre-season but it's not. It's a crucial match in the Nations League.
"We expect a difficult match against a big football nation and a proud country – a side full of quality. A mix of young and experienced players with a young coach.
"Everyone will be ready to give all for the new coach."

Much of the limelight during the international break has been taken away by Manchester City, who were found guilty of all the serious charges that were brought against them in 2023 by the Premier League.
While the potential sanctions have not been revealed, with City also appealing the decision made by an independent commission, relegation is not off the table.
With City stars Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson in the England squad, Tuchel insisted he would not be opposed to selecting players if they were playing in a lower division.
"There is always a possibility," said the England boss.
"I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, occasion, the tournament. I will never rule out that because they don't play in the top flight in their country.
"We need to look at it case by case."

n4htqqxe4hwi12rxzeicpwdr2.title: Jesus confirms Ronaldo will start on Portugal bow against Wales
n4htqqxe4hwi12rxzeicpwdr2.subtitle: Jorge Jesus is preparing for his first match in charge of Portugal against Wales, and he confirmed Cristiano Ronaldo would start.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus has confirmed that Cristiano Ronaldo will start his first game in charge of Portugal, against Wales in the opening match of their Nations League campaign.
Portugal welcome Wales to the Estadio Jose Alvalade on Thursday in what will be their first match since exiting the World Cup against eventual champions Spain in the last 16.
Roberto Martinez's three-year reign was brought to an end, with Jesus appointed as his successor on a four-year contract, taking him through to the World Cup in 2030.
The 72-year-old is a player Ronaldo knows well, with the pair linking up at Al-Nassr, where they became Saudi Pro League champions for the first time since Ronaldo arrived.
Ronaldo scored 29 goals in 33 appearances under Jesus for Al Nassr in the 2025-26 campaign, averaging a goal every 99 minutes.

Throughout his career, the only managers under whom Ronaldo has a better goals-per-game average in league play are Carlo Ancelotti (1.22) and Jose Mourinho (1.13) at Real Madrid, and Luis Castro and Rudi Garcia at Al-Nassr (both 1.1).
Following his unveiling, Jesus insisted Ronaldo "would never be a problem" for Portugal, and he revealed he intends to start the five-time Ballon d'Or winner against Wales.
"We have been in many situations of major competitions, such as the Champions League and the World Cup," Jesus said.
"I have never seen an audience with so many people. It's also good, football needs more and more agents to be shared with the national team and players.
"Today will be my first training on the field, because yesterday was a recovery session. And if nothing special happens, Cris will play tomorrow from the start."
This will be the first meeting between Portugal and Wales since the semi-finals of the 2016 European Championship, with the Selecao winning 2-0 en route to the trophy. .

Portugal are also the reigning Nations League holders, beating Spain on penalties in 2024-25. They have won 11 of 14 home matches in the competition (D1 L2), losing only to France (in November 2020) and Spain (in September 2022).

After their defeat to Spain at the World Cup, Portugal will be looking to avoid back-to-back losses for the first time since September and October 2014, when they were beaten by Albania and then France.

They will fancy their chances against a Wales side that remain winless in their last four matches (D3 L1), their worst run under manager Craig Bellamy. Not since 2012 have they had a longer winless start to a calendar year (L5).
Jesus was asked about the relative importance of the Nations League, or whether his full attention was on the 2028 European Championships and the 2030 World Cup.
"I'm in a team that has the best players in the world. All goals are to win," Jesus added.
"And therefore, the first competition is the Nations League, and we are the holders of the title and, of course, we have to defend it."

nqas3ngl6hbc1crlb6690av8x.title: 'The levels weren't what I expect' – Toone and Kelly omitted from England squad
nqas3ngl6hbc1crlb6690av8x.subtitle: England must navigate two qualification ties to reach next year's Women's World Cup, and Sarina Wiegman's squad features some surprises.
paragraphs: Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly have both been omitted from England's squad for next month's Women's World Cup qualification play-offs, with Sarina Wiegman saying both players have fallen short of their usual levels this season.
The Lionesses will take on Greece across two legs on October 9 and 13, with the winner of that tie progressing to a play-off final against either Slovakia or Ukraine.
England have not failed to qualify for the Women's World Cup since 2003, having reached at least the semi-finals at the last three editions, finishing as runners-up to Spain in 2023.
Toone and Kelly have been key members of Wiegman's England setup since she took charge in 2021, helping the Lionesses win back-to-back European Championships.
Both players scored in the 2022 showpiece, a 2-1 win over Germany at Wembley, while Kelly converted the decisive penalty in a shoot-out triumph over Spain in the 2025 final.

Aggie Beever-Jones and Lotte Wubben-Moy are among the other big names to be left out of Wiegman's squad, though captain Leah Williamson returns after missing the end of England's group-stage campaign with injury.
"The main reason is that I think the levels weren't what I expect from them on the pitch," Wiegman said of her decision to exclude Toone and Kelly.
"There is big competition going on and that is basically what it is. Of course, it has been a very hard decision for both of them.
"I really believe in them. We expect a bit more and we know they can bring more. That was the message – I'm convinced they can be better.
"I hope they respond really well. Where needed, we will support them too. I hope they can come back even better than they were before."

Toone has won 69 senior caps since making her debut in February 2021, though she has made an inconsistent start to the domestic season, with Manchester United only taking four points from their first four matches in the Women's Super League.
Kelly, who has only two caps fewer than Toone, has only started one of Arsenal's opening four games, tallying just 124 minutes of WSL action with the Gunners on five points.

Twenty-year-old Chelsea midfielder Lexi Potter has won her first senior call-up, having impressed during Sunday's 1-0 win over Arsenal, while Erica Meg Parkinson, Freya Godfrey and Grace Fisk are the other uncapped players to be included.

England squad: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea), Khiara Keating (Liverpool), Anna Moorhouse (Manchester City); Lucy Bronze (Chelsea), Jess Carter (Gotham FC), Niamh Charles (Manchester City), Grace Fisk (Liverpool), Alex Greenwood (Manchester City), Maya Le Tissier (Manchester United), Esme Morgan (Washington Spirit), Leah Williamson (Arsenal); Laura Blindkilde Brown (Manchester City), Lucia Kendall (Aston Villa), Erica Meg Parkinson (North Carolina Courage), Lexi Potter (Chelsea), Georgia Stanway (Arsenal), Keira Walsh (Chelsea); Freya Godfrey (London City Lionesses), Lauren Hemp (Manchester City), Lauren James (Chelsea), Beth Mead (Manchester City), Jess Park (Manchester United), Alessia Russo (Arsenal).

ns1rmjamy8tk1d0jmm3ez0n16.title: Mbappe: 'Disrespectful' to advise Olise to join Real Madrid this summer
ns1rmjamy8tk1d0jmm3ez0n16.subtitle: Michael Olise was linked with a stunning move to Real Madrid this summer, something Kylian Mbappe did not want to be involved with.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe said it would have been "disrespectful" to advise France team-mate Michael Olise to join him at Real Madrid this summer.
Olise was the subject of speculation after a stunning second season with Bayern Munich, which saw him help the club win the Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal.
He ended the Bundesliga season with 34 goal involvements (15 goals, 19 assists), a new record for a winger since Opta data collection began in the German top flight in 2004-05.
Only Harry Kane (41) directly contributed to more Bundesliga goals than Olise, who also scored five goals and provided seven assists in 13 Champions League games.
Florentino Perez pledged to spend big on a 'Galactico' player prior to winning Madrid's presidential election, only for the club to deny making a move for the in-demand Olise.
Olise carried on his form into the World Cup, becoming the first player on record (since 1966) to register seven assists in a single edition of FIFA's flagship competition.

Across Europe's top five leagues in all competitions this season, only Barcelona duo Raphinha (17) and Lamine Yamal (14) have managed more goal contributions than Olise's 11 (eight goals, three assists).
"I was aware of the speculation," Mbappe said. "But I know the situation well myself. Back when I was a PSG player, there were countless rumours.
"And I feel it would be disrespectful to advise a player to make a move. That would be unfair to Bayern, especially since Bayern is a great club where Michael can achieve a lot.
"One thing is clear, though: every club in the world would love to have Michael Olise. He is an outstanding player."
Olise's stunning performances in 2025-26 saw him crowned the Bundesliga Player of the Season.
Mbappe has faced criticism after failing to win a major trophy since joining Madrid in 2024, with Jose Mourinho returning this summer in a bid to change the team's fortunes.
The 27-year-old has managed eight goals and two assists in eight appearances in all competitions, and he believes Mourinho is the right man to lead Madrid back to glory.
"Jose Mourinho is extremely intelligent," Mbappe added. "That's why he's been able to achieve such great success in his career.
"He's very close to us players, and takes a real interest in us. He's a leader, he knows exactly how to get the best out of us."

Mbappe is preparing to play for France for the first time since their third-place defeat at the World Cup to England, with Turkiye their opponents in the first match of their Nations League campaign this Friday.

With two goals and an assist against England in their 6-4 defeat, Mbappe now holds the record for the most goal involvements on record (since 1966) at a single World Cup (14 – 10 goals, four assists), while no player has scored more World Cup goals than his 22.
He was asked whether he would follow in Cristiano Ronaldo's footsteps in turning out for his nation at 41-years-old, something Mbappe could not see himself doing.
"We have to be completely honest, considering the country I play for: France would never let me play until I'm 41," Mbappe said.
"Cristiano proves that if you're physically and mentally fit, you can play at a high level for a long time. In my case, though, I don't see it happening."

o0w0ojavvskfzvw31lgmcrhf.title: Robertson urges struggling Spurs to forget about last two seasons
o0w0ojavvskfzvw31lgmcrhf.subtitle: Tottenham are bottom of the Premier League after five games, having only escaped relegation by two points on the final day of last season.
paragraphs: Andy Robertson says Tottenham's players must forget about their struggles over the last couple of seasons if they are to climb the Premier League table.

Spurs will spend the international break bottom of the Premier League with just two points on the board, with this the first time they have propped up the table at least five games into a season since 2008-09.

Roberto De Zerbi's side did at least end their goalless start to the campaign against Aston Villa on Saturday, but after going down 3-2, they have lost 50 of their 141 Premier League games at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
In just seven years at the venue, they have suffered as many Premier League defeats as rivals Arsenal have suffered in 382 matches at the Emirates Stadium, which opened 20 years ago.
Spurs finished 17th in both 2024-25 and 2025-26, narrowly avoiding relegation in the latter of those seasons as they finished two points clear of West Ham on the final matchday.

They then spent over £300m on new players in the summer transfer window, but Robertson believes there is still a hangover from their disappointing recent seasons, which he and his fellow new arrivals can help to overcome.
"They're starting this journey. They've had a couple of really tough seasons in terms of finishes in the league," Robertson said in an appearance on The Overlaps' Stick to Football podcast.
"They've had to go into the market, they've spent a bit of money, but I do believe Tottenham are now starting a journey.

"Now, I don't know how far that journey can go, nobody does, but the determination in that group... you can see last season hurt them a lot. And maybe we're still guilty of carrying that weight of last season on our shoulders.

"That's the message of the manager, first and foremost. And also, that falls on me, and the other new players, if we need to forget. We need to now try and get Tottenham back to where we believe they belong. The fans are still carrying it as well and you don't blame them. They've been through such a tough time."
Robertson joined Tottenham on a free transfer after nine years with Liverpool, who he helped to win two Premier League titles, one FA Cup and two EFL Cups.
And when Robertson became aware his contract at Anfield would not be renewed, he immediately viewed Spurs as the most attractive destination available to him.
"I spoke directly to the manager. We had a couple of video calls over the summer. He's super ambitious, you can tell that as a manager," Robertson said of his initial conversations with De Zerbi.
"He wants to be able to win trophies. But he also knows that we need to start showing it sooner rather than later.
"It was always going to be Tottenham, even from January, as long as they stayed up. I ended up getting invested in Tottenham games.
"I was watching Tottenham thinking, 'come on', especially when De Zerbi came in. I was fully confident; I was really happy with how much Spurs wanted me."

Spurs' next Premier League game is against Manchester United at Old Trafford on October 10, with the Red Devils making their joint-worst start to a Premier League season after five matches (five points, level with 2014-15).

o7k6ie5pw9vm19jmzjjysrlqa.title: 'When he calls, you can't say no' – Ebnoutalib credits Klopp for choice to represent Germany
o7k6ie5pw9vm19jmzjjysrlqa.subtitle: Younes Ebnoutalib was eligible to represent either Germany or Morocco, and he says talks with Jurgen Klopp made his mind up.
paragraphs: Eintracht Frankfurt forward Younes Ebnoutalib has highlighted the role Jurgen Klopp played in his choice to represent Germany over Morocco, saying: "When he calls, you can't say no."

Klopp has named a larger, 44-man squad for his first international break in charge of Germany, who face the Netherlands in their Nations League opener on Thursday, before taking on Greece twice, either side of a home clash with Serbia.
Sixteen of them are uncapped as Klopp looks to familiarise himself with as many players as possible, with 23-year-old attacker Ebnoutalib among them.
Having joined Eintracht from Elversberg in a €10m deal in January, Ebnoutalib has made a superb start to this season, scoring four goals in as many Bundesliga games.

Only Patrik Schick, Phillip Tietz, Michael Olise and Yuito Suzuki can match that tally, with Ebnoutalib finding the net with all but one of his shots on target (five, from 11 total attempts) and overperforming his figure of 2.85 expected goals (xG).
Ebnoutalib represented Morocco at youth level, but talks with Jurgen Klopp left him in no doubt as to where his international future lay.
"I am very, very proud. There were also talks with Morocco, but they weren't as intense as with Jurgen," Ebnoutalib said.
"I'm just proud. You have to say, he is one of the best coaches in the world. And when he calls, you can't say no.
"The impression is very positive. He is, of course, someone who brings a great deal of experience and already has a certain presence because of what he has achieved over the years.
"So, naturally, you have a great deal of respect for him. But he was very nice and very likeable in the conversations.
"He is already very well known for the way he wants to play football, with high pressing, with a lot of energy and power. He has already fired us up.
"I think that's what he is known for, that he is very good at reaching people and getting them on board. He has certainly got us in the right mindset."

Klopp has overseen 1,080 matches across his managerial career, winning 588 of those (D256 L236). His 431 games in charge of Liverpool are the third-most by a manager in the club's history, behind Bill Shankly's 799 and Bob Paisley's 523.

Klopp's 334 Premier League games with the Reds, who won the title under him in 2019-20, are also the fifth-most with a single club in the history of the competition, after Arsene Wenger with Arsenal (828), Alex Ferguson with Manchester United (810), David Moyes with Everton (488) and Pep Guardiola with Manchester City (380).

Defender Philipp Treu is another player hoping to make his senior Germany debut in the coming days, with three of his Freiburg team-mates also called up following their run to the Europa League final last season.
"It's definitely something where you say, 'Hey, it's cool that I can now train under Jurgen Klopp'," Treu said of working with Klopp.
"And that's why I'm just looking forward to being on the pitch with him later, soaking it all in, and just giving it my all."

oa2hmo4uvcgy14ixcazdis5xb.title: Belgium and Italy in same situation, says Van Bommel ahead of debut
oa2hmo4uvcgy14ixcazdis5xb.subtitle: Mark van Bommel is preparing for his first game in charge of Belgium against Italy, and he believes the two teams are closely matched.
paragraphs: Mark van Bommel likened the situation surrounding Belgium to the one at Italy as he prepares for his debut in charge of the Red Devils in the Nations League.
Belgium make the trip to the Stadio Olimpico on Friday to begin their Nations League campaign, with this their first match since exiting the World Cup in the quarter-finals.
The 49-year-old is Belgium's third managerial change in as many years, and becomes the first Dutchman to take charge of the Red Devils since Dick Advocaat back in 2009.
Rudi Garcia was dismissed following the World Cup, with Belgium impressing in the group stage before losing late on to eventual tournament winners Spain in the last eight.

Excluding the third-place play-off match, Belgium have now been eliminated from each of their last four World Cup knockout stage ties against fellow UEFA nations, since beating Spain on penalties at the quarter-final stage of the 1986 tournament.
That brought an end to Garcia's reign. He took charge of 20 games, recording 12 wins (D6 L2), to finish with a 60% win rate, with Van Bommel the next man in the hot seat.
It is Van Bommel's fourth managerial role, and his first since spending two years in the Belgian Pro League with Royal Antwerp between 2022 and 2024.
He won 57 of his 107 matches in charge across all competitions (D21 L29), averaging 1.79 points per game along with a 51.4% win rate, while also winning three major titles.

But he comes up against another manager making his debut in Roberto Mancini, though it is his second stint with the Azzurri after he replaced Gennaro Gattuso following their failure to qualify for a third consecutive World Cup.
"It's not easy to prepare the team in four days. We had some meetings with the players to explain what we wanted to do," Van Bommel said.
"We want the ball, and if we lose it, to win it back as soon as possible. We want to dominate the game, but it’s not easy when starting a new era.
"We're in the Nations League against Italy, France and Turkiye, so there's no time to experiment, but Italy are in the same situation as us."
Van Bommel has named a strong 25-man squad for their clashes with Italy, France (home and away) and Turkiye, though some big names are also missing.
Thibaut Courtois is unavailable after requesting to be excused from the matches, while Jeremy Doku, Amadou Onana, Alexis Saelemaekers and Thomas Meunier also miss out.
He chose to name four uncapped players, which include goalkeepers Jari De Busser, Mike Penders and Maarten Vandevoordt, along with young full-back Kyriani Sabbe.
Kevin De Bruyne is also in despite struggling for fitness with Napoli, with reports saying Van Bommel flew to Italy to convince him to remain a part of the international set-up.
"Kevin, Lukaku, Tielemans, De Ketelaere, we have several players with a lot of experience, others who are in Serie A, so it's good that we can adapt to Italian football," he added.
"We've got players who can bring that experience to the team and help the younger members."

Van Bommel revealed he would adopt a 4-3-3 formation against Italy, but said his preparations had been hindered given the uncertainty around Mancini and whether he would change his tactics from his previous stint with Italy.
"It's difficult to prepare, because you don't know what he is going to do. Gattuso was the coach last season. I know Rino and his style of football," Van Bommel said.
"It won't be easy for Italy either. I watched many of Roberto's games. I'm not sure if he will do the same things, they might have a 4-3-3, we'll see."

owv3frz9a51szoys3zgrvbi3.title: Tuchel laments England's mistakes and missed chances
owv3frz9a51szoys3zgrvbi3.subtitle: England created a lot of their own problems against Spain, and could not turn their half-time lead into a victory over the world champions.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel was left to rue England's mistakes and missed chances as they were beaten 3-2 by Spain in the opening match of their Nations League campaign.
England had threatened to give Spain a scare after coming from behind – after a Marc Guehi mistake gifted Lamine Yamal a second-minute opener – through Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane before half-time.
However after the break, Kane then missed a penalty, rattling the crossbar after his standing leg slipped, and Spain mounted a comeback of their own.

Nico O'Reilly gifted the ball to Spain deep in England's half, with Alex Baena ultimately profiting before Mikel Oyarzabal netted the winner in the 74th minute, coming back to haunt England after scoring the winning goal at Euro 2024.
England have conceded 3+ goals in consecutive matches for the first time since June 1995 (3-3 v Sweden, 1-3 v Brazil on that occasion).
The Three Lions have also conceded 13 goals in their last six matches in all competitions, almost double the total they had shipped in their first 17 under Tuchel (seven).
This is the first time England have made two errors leading to a goal in a competitive match since June 2019 against the Netherlands, also in the Nations League.
"Terrible start, the worst start possible," Tuchel told ITV Sport.
"It makes it so, so difficult to be behind against this type of team. After 10-12 minutes, I think we were the better team. We dominated in the opponent's half.

"We created and scored two goals, our best 15 minutes after the whistle. We couldn't convert the penalty – I think then maybe Spain would have believed that their long run of unbeaten games ends here.

"Another big, big mistake for 2-2. The third goal was the only goal they really scored. Just is what it is. We have to keep going and learn from it. Take what is positive and take the points back to the Czech Republic."
Spain are now unbeaten in their last 39 games (in 90 minutes), extending the longest such streak by a European nation (W30 D9).
And it meant they piled more worry on England, who have won just six of their last 16 matches against nations ranked in FIFA's top 10.
"I was not in charge for all of these 16 matches, for sure not, and I think we did everything to beat Spain," said Tuchel.

"Details matter on this kind of level. Like I said, the amount of clear-cut mistakes was too high on our side, unfortunately, and in the last 20 metres they were more composed and more clinical to convert our ball-losses into clear-cut chances.
"We will keep on pushing this team.
"We proved it at the World Cup that we are capable to do it in tournaments. We cannot prove it in the result [against Spain], but I think the way we played was enough to beat them."

pegatjantgti1vobgwd9y86p2.title: 'We try and win every game' – Colorado determined to stick to identity to earn playoff spot
pegatjantgti1vobgwd9y86p2.subtitle: Colorado Rapids and the LA Galaxy both want to make sure they are in the postseason, but they still have work to do to make it happen.
paragraphs: Matt Wells wants the Colorado Rapids to stick to their identity as they continue their push to secure an MLS playoff spot against the LA Galaxy.
Colorado currently sit seventh in the Western Conference on 36 points, and they come into this game unbeaten in their last three matches (W1 D2).
However, they threw away a 3-1 lead against the Seattle Sounders last time out, conceding twice in the last 15 minutes, including a stoppage-time equaliser from Caden Clark.

And on the road, the Rapids have had their struggles, failing to win any of their last five away games in the competition, with their last such win coming against Minnesota United before the World Cup break in May.
But Wells is not changing his approach despite the end of the regular season approaching, as he remains confident Colorado have what it takes to clinch their playoff berth.
"No special messages [about the playoff push]," he said. "We try and win every game.

"So, for me, our process here is that we're always immersed in the game preparation. It's like if we want to look any further ahead than the Galaxy, then we'll go to the Galaxy and get a total of zero points.
"We have to be fully focused on our next opponent. We're trying to guess the dynamic of the team they'll put out, both personnel and tactically.
"We're in a good spot. It's about us going out in all of these games now. It's about us going out and playing to our identity, playing our style and executing the game plan that we've put into place.
"We know as a group, whenever we've done that, we've been successful."
The Galaxy are also pushing to make it to the postseason, and they sit three points behind the Rapids in eighth.
Greg Vanney's side have lost just one of their last four league games (W2 D1) and come into this match on the back of a 3-2 comeback win over Minnesota last weekend.
LA Galaxy – Marco Reus
Marco Reus scored the 13th regular-season goal of his MLS career on Saturday, but it was only his second league goal on the road for LA Galaxy.
Reus' three goals this month are tied for his most in a single calendar month for the Galaxy, also netting three earlier this season in April.
Colorado Rapids – Morgan Whittaker
On Saturday, Morgan Whittaker tallied a brace for Colorado in his first career start for the club, becoming the second Rapids player to do that this season (Kosi Thompson – April 12).
Prior to this season, the last Rapids player to have multiple goals in his first regular-season start for the club was Raul Diaz Arce in 2001.
MATCH PREDICTION: LA GALAXY WIN
LA Galaxy have earned 41 all-time regular-season wins against the Rapids (incl. shootout wins), tied for their most wins against a single MLS opponent (also the San Jose Earthquakes).
The only MLS team to have more wins against a single team in regular-season play is Columbus against the New England Revolution (42).

Trailing 2-1 in the 75th minute, the Galaxy scored twice to earn a 3-2 comeback win against Minnesota United last weekend. It was the second time over the last eight seasons that the Galaxy rallied to win after trailing in the 75th minute or later, also doing so in March 2024 at Sporting Kansas City.
But the Rapids earned a 3-3 draw Saturday against Seattle, their first time scoring three or more goals since a 6-2 win against the Houston Dynamo in April.
Colorado scored at least three goals in three of their first seven matches in 2026 across all competitions but have done so in just one of their last 23 games.
Colorado Rapids – 27.8%

phzjzor1ct0714pn2bxzrdw5a.title: 'I give up' – Klopp exasperated by debate over Kimmich's Germany role
phzjzor1ct0714pn2bxzrdw5a.subtitle: Continued questions over Joshua Kimmich's Germany future have left Jurgen Klopp frustrated, with the ex-Liverpool boss lashing out.
paragraphs: An exasperated Jurgen Klopp said he has given up on answering questions about Joshua Kimmich's Germany future, amid continued speculation regarding his place in the team.

Following a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a surprise 1-0 defeat to Greece, Klopp avoided becoming the first Germany boss to fail to win his first three games in charge on Thursday, as Tom Bischof and Florian Wirtz scored in a 2-0 win over Serbia.
That victory came without captain Kimmich, as Aleksandar Pavlovic played alongside the two goalscorers in the centre of Germany's midfield.
Ahead of Sunday's trip to Greece, Klopp allowed several players – including Bayern Munich stalwart Kimmich – to return to their clubs.
That only fuelled speculation in the German media that the 31-year-old, whose 116 caps are the seventh-most in Die Nationalelf's history, may not be part of Klopp's long-term plans.
But when that prospect was put to Klopp again at Saturday's pre-match press conference, his frustration was clear.
"You can tell that it's extremely difficult for me to say anything about that, because you want to make a story out of it. We played a good game. Our midfield was top class," Klopp said.
"But can you imagine how s***** it would be if Germany had three, and only three, top-class midfielders?
"Why make it about one player when it's about the fact that we need several good players? We need all sorts of players. We need leaders. We need runners. We need everything.
"It was a loaded question. I understand that it's a logical and normal question, but I think it’s coming too soon.
"I'm very satisfied with all the lads. I'm looking forward to the future, and I hope we have a large pool.
"I just don't stand a chance with that question, without you guys making something out of it. I give up. Seriously. Officially.
"With respect to that topic, I give up. Do what you want with it. I'm happy with the last game, and I'm happy that Joshua Kimmich is a leading player for Germany."
Germany are third in Group A2 ahead of their fourth game, with Greece leading the way on seven points.
The Netherlands are second with five, while Serbia are yet to earn a point.

q6b5vmfgkz9611l1o52dueykq.title: Conte wants next club to be one that 'somewhat lost sight of their history'
q6b5vmfgkz9611l1o52dueykq.subtitle: Antonio Conte has been out of work since May, but he already has an idea of what kind of club he would like to join next.
paragraphs: Antonio Conte says he would like his next job to be at a club that has "somewhat lost sight of their history" and does not mind the pressure that would come with it.
Conte has been out of management since the end of the 2025-26 campaign, when he left Napoli after leading them to a second-place finish behind Inter.
During his two-year stint in Naples, Conte won the Scudetto and a Supercoppa Italiana.
Since then, he has been linked with the Italy job – which eventually went to Roberto Mancini – as well as Manchester United and Juventus, amid pressure on both Michael Carrick and Luciano Spalletti.
Conte has said he would like to return to the Premier League, having previously managed Chelsea, whom he led to the Premier League title in 2016-17, and Tottenham.

"If you go to a club where the history speaks for itself – a history made up of trophies, league titles and victories – you can only honour that history in one way: by having the ambition to bring that club back – if it isn't there today – to fight for those goals," Conte said when asked about his future.

"I know full well that only one team can win every year, but I must carry in my heart – and instil in the hearts of the fans, my players and my directors – that spark, that hope that makes you say, 'F***, we can win'.
"Even that 1% – but it must be a 1% that can become 70, 80 or even 100%. It depends on how you convey it.
"The manager is important because he conveys that message, day in, day out.

"He has daily interactions with everyone: with his staff, the masseur, the kit man, the physiotherapist, the groundsman – all people who need to be involved and feel part of the drive to make history, and you only make history by winning.
"There are many clubs that have somewhat lost sight of their history. I'd like to go to one of these clubs to dust off that history and make it shine once more.
"Clubs where there's pressure, where, ultimately, you know full well that you're not going there just to take part, but to compete."

qch5619dbk9u1uymw7xa8r1ec.title: Spain winger Munoz learning from competition with Yamal
qch5619dbk9u1uymw7xa8r1ec.subtitle: Victor Munoz is serving as back-up to Lamine Yamal in the Spain squad, but the Liverpool winger is using the opportunity to grow his game.
paragraphs: Spain winger Victor Munoz called it "a privilege" to learn from Lamine Yamal as they compete for the same position in Luis De la Fuente's lineup.
Both players were a part of Spain's World Cup-winning squad in the summer, though Munoz did not feature due to injury as La Roja lifted the trophy for a second time in their history.
While Yamal also failed to have his desired impact at the tournament, he has helped Spain make a strong start to their Nations League campaign during this international break.
The teenager has scored three goals and provided one assist in wins over England and Croatia, with Munoz also featuring against the latter.
Yamal is currently one of the favourites to win the Ballon d'Or this month, and Munoz is making the most of training with the Barcelona superstar.
"I try to learn a lot from him; he’s a good friend of mine and we spend a lot of time together," said Munoz.
"It’s a privilege for me and he helps me a lot in my day-to-day life.
"[De la Fuente tells me to] just be myself. Try to help the team in attack and defence, try to be direct and try one-on-one. Those are what I think are my strengths."
Munoz completed a reported £35m (€40m) move to Liverpool in the summer, scoring once in six games so far, three of which were starts.
His only goal was an equaliser against Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, with Andoni Iraola's side still unbeaten across all competitions in 2026-27 (W4 D3).
"I do notice a difference between LaLiga and the Premier League," added the 23-year-old.
"LaLiga is more tactical, the Premier League is more physical. The intensity of the training sessions there is very high and it's helping me grow."

qhsho3pm0as61xs0e18vg4pe7.title: Van Dijk: Utter nonsense I influenced Netherlands World Cup tactics
qhsho3pm0as61xs0e18vg4pe7.subtitle: Virgil van Dijk is not impressed by claims he influenced a tactical change at the World Cup, hitting back during a press conference.
paragraphs: Virgil van Dijk slammed the suggestion that he had forced Ronald Koeman into changing his Netherlands tactics at the World Cup as "utter nonsense".
The Netherlands were knocked out of the World Cup in the round of 32 on penalties by Morocco – after a 1-1 draw – having gone unbeaten throughout their group stage.
Van Dijk served as Koeman's captain throughout the tournament, with the 63-year-old leaving his position following their early exit.
In a press conference ahead of the Netherlands' Nations League clash with Germany, Van Dijk clashed with reporters after it was insinuated that he was involved in tactical shifts.
Koeman had played a back four throughout the group stage, where they won two of their games and drew the other, before switching to a back five for their clash with Morocco.
"One of your colleagues also said, of course, that it was my idea to switch to playing with a back five. That is utter nonsense," Van Dijk told one reporter.
"The fact is we simply failed at the World Cup. Those are the hard facts.
"We didn't play a good World Cup. It's not about me. You perform together; you're a team. Your claim that I destroyed Dutch football after the World Cup – that sort of thing is completely baseless.
"The plan is devised by the staff. Nonsense is being spread so that I look even worse. That happens far too often.
"I was told that it was my fault we played with five, that Ronald Koeman and I have destroyed Dutch football.
"The plan worked for 89 minutes, even though it was a bad match. We almost broke through. The idea that I destroyed Dutch football makes absolutely no sense. I didn't decide that."
Van Dijk will continue to captain the Netherlands under new head coach Xavi and could win his 100th cap in this extended international break if he plays in all four of their Nations League matches.
The first of which comes at home against Germany on Thursday.

qilthhwpuk491mqo788h4wi1n.title: Argentina 7-0 Burkina Faso: Martinez gets three goal involvements as makeshift visitors thrashed
qilthhwpuk491mqo788h4wi1n.subtitle: Lionel Scaloni put out a strong Argentina lineup against Burkina Faso on Saturday, and he was rewarded with a dominant seven-goal win.
paragraphs: Lautaro Martinez scored one goal and assisted two as Argentina thrashed an understrength Burkina Faso side 7-0 in a friendly marred by travel disruption.

The visitors only arrived in Buenos Aires six hours before kick-off due to their original flight from Morocco being cancelled, and with several first-team players opting not to travel due to fatigue, head coach Amir Abdou fielded a youthful team.
Unsurprisingly, they were no match for the World Cup runners-up, who stormed into a five-goal lead before half-time.

The opening goal came just four minutes in, after Monmouni Diallo scythed down Agustin Giay near the byline on the right-hand side. Martinez's resulting penalty was saved by Razack Guira, but the Inter man was alive to the rebound to finish left-footed.

Argentina's second goal was a comedy of errors from Burkina Faso's point of view, as Julian Alvarez's cross was turned into his own net by Diallo, and Gianluca Prestianni made it 3-0 after just 12 minutes, having exchanged passes with Martinez.

The fourth and fifth goals arrived within 86 seconds of each other later in the first half. Nico Paz brought down Alexis Mac Allister's lofted pass and tucked home, then a cheap giveaway from Hasamadou Ouedraogo was punished in slick fashion by the Albiceleste, with Prestianni centring for an Alvarez tap-in.
Mercifully for Burkina Faso, the goals dried up somewhat in the second half, though Argentina still added two more.

The first of those came from Franco Mastantuono, who finished left-footed after being found by Martinez on the counter, and the Real Madrid winger was also involved in the build-up to the stoppage-time seventh. He found Valentin Barco on the left side of the area, and a lofted delivery from the Chelsea man was headed in by Giuliano Simeone.
Martinez maintains Argentina hot streak
With Lionel Messi set to make a farewell Argentina appearance against Benin on Tuesday, there was a danger of their preceding games being overlooked.

But Lionel Scaloni has certainly taken them seriously, and this victory – which came off the back of a 4-0 thrashing of Bolivia – saw several young players state their case for a central role in Argentina's new era.
Four of the hosts' six goalscorers were aged 23 or younger, though there was still room for two members of their 2022 World Cup-winning squad – Martinez and Alvarez – to contribute.
Martinez now has a hugely impressive 42 goals in 86 senior caps for Argentina, and half of those (21) have come since the start of 2024, having made his international debut way back in 2017.

Argentina's margin of victory was the joint sixth largest in their history and their joint-biggest since 1975, having also won 7-0 against Curacao (in 2023), Bolivia (in 2015) and Hong Kong (in 2014) in that time.

qopf73okp1491ws9iw17uiqju.title: Van Bommel relishing clash against 'special' Zidane and France
qopf73okp1491ws9iw17uiqju.subtitle: Mark van Bommel made a winning start to life in charge of Belgium, but a difficult test against Zinedine Zidane and France awaits.
paragraphs: Mark van Bommel is relishing the chance to do battle with Zinedine Zidane and France as he prepares to build on Belgium's strong start to their Nations League campaign.
Belgium began life under Van Bommel with a 2-0 win at the Stadio Olimpico against Italy, with Mika Godts and Dodi Lukebakio scoring in either half for the Red Devils.
The result saw Italy lose a home match while conceding two goals without scoring for only the second time in the last 40 years, following a defeat to Croatia in August 2006.
It was the perfect start for Van Bommel, who replaced Rudi Garcia following the World Cup, but his early tenure is set to face its sternest test at the Stade Roi Baudouin.
France, also under new management with Zidane, made a winning start to their Nations League campaign with a 1-0 victory over Turkiye, with Kylian Mbappe on target.
Mbappe has since been ruled out of the clash with Belgium after being diagnosed with hyperextension in his left knee, something Van Bommel was disappointed to hear.
"It is special to coach against someone ​like that," Van Bommel said. "He was an exceptional footballer and I played against him once, with ​Barcelona against Real Madrid.
"If a dribbling move is named after you, then you must have done pretty well. ‌As ⁠a coach too, of course. He is a good coach, that's clear.
"I think it's a shame that Mbappe isn't there, because you always want to have the best footballers playing against you.
"I don't know exactly what injury he has, but I would have liked him to be there."
Belgium were deserving of their win against Italy, finishing with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.76 from their 19 shots to the Azzurri's 1.7 from their 21 attempts.
And Van Bommel wants to see his Belgium team maintain the attacking approach they showed against Roberto Mancini's side.
"I started [my ​coaching tenure] last Monday by emphasising intensity and willingness to work," Van Bommel added.
"The idea has to remain the same. Of course, you ⁠have to take the quality of the opponent into account, but that does not change our ​style of play.
"If you are beaten in a situation, that's not a problem. As long as ​everyone knows what they have to do."
Following their clash with France, Belgium face Turkiye at home before concluding the international break against Zidane's side again at the Stade de France on October 5.

qoth7vtxk05i1dxyoa71q6hza.title: Kolo Muani not facing spell out after hand surgery
qoth7vtxk05i1dxyoa71q6hza.subtitle: Randal Kolo Muani has undergone surgery on a fractured finger on his right hand, but he will not miss any time for Juventus.
paragraphs: Juventus have confirmed Randal Kolo Muani will remain available for selection after undergoing surgery on a fractured finger.
Kolo Muani played 89 minutes on Saturday as the Bianconeri returned to winning ways in Serie A, beating Atalanta 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium.
He played on despite sustaining an injury to his right hand, and though the issue required surgery, reports in Italy said he would return to training with Juve within a couple of days.
A statement released on Juve's website said: "During the first half of Sunday's match against Atalanta, Randal Kolo Muani sustained an injury to the fifth finger of his right hand.
"Tests carried out after the match revealed a fracture of the proximal phalanx, making osteosynthesis surgery necessary.
"The operation, performed this afternoon by Dr Loris Pegoli, was completely successful and the player will remain available for selection."
Kolo Muani has appeared in all six of the Bianconeri's matches in all competitions this season, starting five of those and recording one goal and two assists in 468 minutes.

He was not selected in Zinedine Zidane's first France squad ahead of their Nations League fixtures against Turkiye, Belgium and Italy, so will continue training with his club ahead of Juve facing Cagliari on October 11.

qxfq9pg149jr1632xee1ruunj.title: Serbia 1-2 Netherlands: Meerdink double earns Xavi first victory
qxfq9pg149jr1632xee1ruunj.subtitle: Xavi got himself up and running with the Netherlands as goals in either half from Mexx Meerdink were enough to get past Serbia on Sunday.
paragraphs: Mexx Meerdink scored twice as the Netherlands earned their first victory under new boss Xavi after they beat Serbia 2-1 at Stadion Rajko Mitic in the Nations League.
The Netherlands needed a stoppage-time equaliser from Cody Gakpo on Xavi's debut against Germany, but they overcame a stern test on Sunday to seal all three points.

Dejan Joveljic brought the first save out of Bart Verbruggen in the 17th minute before Meerdink stung the palms of Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, with his shot coming after Gakpo was forced off due to an injury.

But the Netherlands made the breakthrough in the 30th minute when Crysencio Summerville was fouled inside the penalty area by Aleksa Terzic, with Meerdink stepping up and wrapping his effort into the bottom-right corner.
Denzel Dumfries should have doubled the visitors' lead after he was brilliantly slipped in by Meerdink, but Milinkovic-Savic was on hand to repel his attempt from a tight angle.

However, Serbia needed just 54 seconds after the break to draw level. Verbruggen made two excellent stops to deny Luka Jovic and Andrija Zivkovic, but Sasa Lukic's scuffed shot made its way back to Jovic, who finished first time from close range.

rdtewxxxoxyl1t0f3d1jxunw8.title: Bronze excited for Chelsea to 'prove ourselves' against Lyon
rdtewxxxoxyl1t0f3d1jxunw8.subtitle: Chelsea head to Lyon looking to make it two wins from two in the Women's Champions League, but Lucy Bronze is expecting a tough test.
paragraphs: Lucy Bronze is relishing the chance for Chelsea to "prove ourselves" against Lyon in the Women's Champions League.
Chelsea began their European campaign with a narrow 1-0 victory over Austria Wien last time out and are one of six teams with three points on the board so far.
Lyon were another that won their opener, but they sit top of the early standings after thrashing Servette 8-0 last time out.

In the Champions League, Lyon have won two of their four games against Chelsea (D1 L1); among sides they have faced more than twice, only against Juventus (43%) and Umea IK (25%) do they possess a lower win rate in the competition than against the Blues (50%).
And Bronze, a former Lyon player, is looking forward to the clash against her former side, seeing it as a good marker for where Chelsea are up to in the season.
"It's so exciting," Bronze said, as quoted on Chelsea's website. "My time at Lyon was amazing.
"All the girls, Ellie [Carpenter], Keish [Kadeisha Buchanan] and Melvine [Malard] had a great time at Lyon, and we all actually played there together as well.
"We're excited to go there, to be focused on the Champions League, and we know what pedigree Lyon have in the Champions League.
"To go toe to toe with another team who's one of the best in the world and test ourselves and prove ourselves is going to be exciting."
Chelsea have lost three of their last six away games in the Champions League (W2 D1), though all three defeats came in the knockout stages.
The Blues have lost just one of their 15 group/league-stage away matches in the competition (W11 D3).
Lyon are heavy favourites according to the Opta supercomputer, with a 65.2% win probability to Chelsea's 15.9%, but Bronze is not shying away from the test ahead of them.
"It's great. I love playing in the big games, the challenging games," she added.
"That's what the best players in the world want to do. They want to play for the best teams, to be able to compete for trophies, to compete in the league.
"That's exactly what we're doing this season. We're pushing ourselves in every single game to be able to compete and win every trophy we can."

ri1h1rkhmw761xfz05jlw3g17.title: Kane: This is my best chance of winning the Ballon d'Or
ri1h1rkhmw761xfz05jlw3g17.subtitle: Harry Kane is among the favourites to win the Ballon d'Or this year, and the Bayern Munich striker said he could not have done any more.
paragraphs: Harry Kane believes this is the best chance of his career to win the Ballon d'Or after a sensational season with Bayern Munich and England.
Kane is among the top contenders to lift the prestigious individual accolade next month, with Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe also in contention.
The England captain plundered 65 across all competitions for Bayern before scoring six more to help Thomas Tuchel's side finish third at this summer's World Cup.
No other player from Europe's top five leagues scored more than 50 goals in all competitions last term, with Mbappe his closest challenger with a half-century for Madrid.

Kane is hoping to become the fifth English player to win the Ballon d'Or and the first since Michael Owen in 2001. Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) had previously claimed the award.
And ahead of England's clash with Spain in their Nations League opener, Kane insisted he could have done nothing more in his attempt to try and lift the Ballon d'Or.
"Best chance right now, yeah, whether that's in the future as well. We'll have to wait and see, but I think yes, so far in my career, it is the best chance without a doubt," Kane said.
"I think I spoke quite openly last season from a personal point of view.
"It was my best year without a doubt, but also, from a team point of you was my best in terms of trophies and performances. It's something that would be amazing to win.
"I know there's been a lot of talk about it, and I'm sure it will be over the next month until it's announced and that's part and parcel of it.
"I'd be extremely proud to win it. I think I've done a lot of great things that I'm proud of last year for sure.
"But like I keep saying, ultimately, it's down to other people now and their opinion on it. The players and their opinion on last season, so we'll have to wait and see what happens.
"I know it won't be the last time I talk about it, but yeah, there's still another month or so to go. My focus is on trying to help this team get a good win against Spain."

Kane will be hoping to improve his Ballon d'Or chances against a Spain side that are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest ever streak by a European nation following their World Cup success.

The Three Lions have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2). Those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).

Jude Bellingham will also be keen to make an impact. The Real Madrid star has scored seven goals in 10 appearances for England in 2026. The last midfielder with more goals in a calendar year for the Three Lions was David Platt in 1993 (eight).

And his performances were recognised as he scooped the England Men's Player of the Year award for the second year running. Only Wayne Rooney (four) has won the award more times than Bellingham (two, level with Kane, Bukayo Saka, Frank Lampard and Steven Gerrard).
