rjx4wkmhfs981hz5g8z4tkgyk.title: Turkiye 1-4 Italy: First-half blitz gets Mancini's second stint up and running
rjx4wkmhfs981hz5g8z4tkgyk.subtitle: Italy claimed their first win in the Nations League as three goals inside the first 27 minutes proved to be enough to battle past Turkiye.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini claimed his first victory since returning to take charge of Italy as three-first half goals helped down Turkiye 4-1 in the Nations League on Monday.
Alessandro Bastoni, Davide Frattesi and Michael Kayode had Italy cruising by the 27th minute, though Baris Alper Yilmaz threatened a comeback early in the second half.
However, Francesco Pio Esposito's 50th-minute header proved to be decisive for Italy, who moved onto three points in Group A1 after their first two matches.

Bastoni handed Italy the ideal start in the ninth minute. A flat corner from the left was not dealt with by Zeki Celik, with the Inter defender winning his battle against Salih Ozcan and turning the ball into the roof of the net on the slide.

It got even better for the Azzurri soon after. A free-flowing move on the edge of the Turkiye area ended with Kayode's shot being saved by Altay Bayindir, but Frattesi was the quickest on the scene to tuck home the rebound in the 22nd minute.

And just five minutes later, Italy had their third. Another great piece of play between Giacomo Raspadori and Francesco Pio Esposito saw the latter shift the ball on to Kayode, who made no mistake from inside the box to mark his international debut with a goal.
Raspadori and Sebastiano Esposito then fired off target to cap a dominant opening 45 minutes for Mancini's side as the Turkiye players exited the pitch to a chorus of jeers.

However, Turkiye gave their fans something to cheer within 76 seconds of the restart when Yilmaz turned Oguz Aydin's teasing delivery past Gianluigi Donnarumma, who was out of position after coming out to try and claim a long ball over the top.

But no sooner had they got themselves back in the game, Bayindir gifted Italy their fourth goal. His loose pass was picked off and resulted in Sandro Tonali striking an effort against the right post, with Francesco Pio Esposito on hand to nod in the rebound.

The blistering start to the second half continued when Yilmaz's shot hit the woodwork on its way in, but the goal was ruled out for an offside against Arda Guler, with Aydin then failing to trouble Donnarumma from a tight angle.
Kerem Akturkoglu then blazed over a glorious chance before Eren Elmali failed to get a touch on Ismail Yuksek's cross, with Italy able to hold on to claim a deserved triumph.
Azzurri find their groove to rubbish Montella's pre-match prediction

Before kick-off, Turkiye boss Vincenzo Montella vowed that his team would emerge victorious against Italy, but his pre-match hopes of a morale-boosting win were all but over before half an hour had elapsed in Bursaspor.

Italy scored three goals inside the first 30 minutes of play for the first time since a World Cup qualifier against Lithuania in September 2021, with Moise Kean, an Edgaras Utkus own goal and Raspadori on target in that game.

This was also the first time the Azzurri had scored four goals in the Nations League since a 4-1 win against Israel in October 2024, and their dominance was backed up by the metrics in what was an entertaining encounter.

Mancini's side finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.39 from their 14 shots compared to Turkiye's 1.86 xG from one more attempt, though the hosts did win the xG battle in the second half (1.77 to 0.76).

There was also a special moment for Francesco Pio and Sebastiano Esposito, who became the fourth pair of brothers to contest the same match with Italy, after Filippo and Simone Inzaghi (twice in 2000), Aldo and Luigi Cevenini (once in 1915), and Giuseppe and Felice Milano (three times between 1912 and 1913).

rp2c9mrz8yca1j2dier76rljt.title: 'Not ideal' for Arsenal to drop points after late mix-up, says Russo
rp2c9mrz8yca1j2dier76rljt.subtitle: Leah Williamson was penalised for a handball in the box after a defensive mix-up as Arsenal gifted Paris FC a late equaliser from the spot.
paragraphs: Alessia Russo conceded it was "not ideal" for Arsenal to drop points in a 2-2 draw with Paris FC in the Women's Champions League, but hopes the goals keep flowing.
Arsenal had led 2-0 against Paris, but a freakish late mix-up ultimately gifted the hosts a late equaliser after they had pulled themselves back into the game.
Russo netted her first goal of the season just before the break, playing a neat one-two with Georgia Stanway before picking out the bottom corner.

Shortly after, Evelyne Viens hit the bar for Paris, who had created the better chances in the early exchanges, but Arsenal doubled their advantage five minutes into the second half with Stanway's first goal for the Gunners.
Paris continued to prove a threat on the counter-attack, though, and halved the deficit in the 71st minute, with Clara Mateo rounding Misa to slot in.

But with five minutes left, Leah Williamson secured the ball with her hand to take a goal-kick, but the referee deemed that Misa had already taken it when passing it to her, thus awarding a penalty for handball, which Maeline Mendy converted in the 87th minute.
"I mean, not ideal," Russo told Arsenal's media channels about the dropped points.
"I think we lost control of the second half a little way before [the penalty] anyway.
"So, it's about managing the game a little bit better. I also think the first half, and throughout the game, we had some really, really good spells, so now it's about using that to push forward."
Arsenal have now failed to win from 2+ goals up in the Champions League twice since the start of last season, having never thrown away that kind of lead between 2001-02 and 2024-25.
But despite the disappointing finish, one positive for the Gunners was Russo's first goal of the season after she drew a blank in her first five outings this season.
"I always want to try and score and create, and yeah, it was about finding the half the yard to get a shot off, so I'm happy to do that," she said.
"I think maybe [it's] an area we've been not confident in the last few games, but I see it every day in training, the quality that we have.

"I didn't think it was going to take us long. I think that it was nice to see that, but also just credit to all of us, the staff. We've been working really hard behind the scenes, really pushing, and we'll continue to do that."
While Arsenal failed to hold onto their lead, there were big wins elsewhere in the Champions League, with reigning champions putting six past Roma.
Caroline Graham Hansen netted a brace, as did Claudia Pina, with Ewa Pajor also on target, while a Shukurat Oladipo own goal completed their scoring in the 6-0 rout.
And Juventus ran out 3-0 winners over Hacken thanks to three second-half goals.

rra6xhird1g1lzfw8kg58xs0.title: 'Hats off to Cristiano!' – Zidane salutes Ronaldo's career amid Portugal rift
rra6xhird1g1lzfw8kg58xs0.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo caused a stir when he left Portugal's Nations League camp but Zinedine Zidane still has high praise for his former player.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane believes Cristiano Ronaldo's "great career" should be saluted amid reports of tensions between the 41-year-old and Portugal.
Ronaldo made headlines last week when he announced he had left Portugal's Nations League camp following their second game – a 2-1 win over Norway in which he was an unused substitute.
Reports prior to his exit suggested there was a disagreement between Ronaldo and Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus over his game time.
The Portugal captain said he would tell his side of the story in due course.
While Jesus has left the door open for Ronaldo to link up with the squad again in November, it remains unclear what is set to happen next month.
But Zidane, who managed Ronaldo at Real Madrid between 2016 and 2018, winning three Champions League titles and LaLiga among their honours, came to the defence of his former player.
"He made me win incredible things," Zidane said when asked about Ronaldo's current situation.
"I think we have to salute his great career; what he has done is exceptional.
"I was lucky enough to have him with me. Hats off to Cristiano!
"I still have a lot of respect in general for all the players, but even more so for those with whom I spent time, and especially Cristiano, who still made us win a lot of things."

Reports prior to his exit suggested there was a disagreement between Ronaldo and Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus over his game time.

The Portugal captain said he would tell his side of the story in due course.

While Jesus has left the door open for Ronaldo to link up with the squad again in November, it remains unclear what is set to happen next month.

But Zidane, who managed Ronaldo at Real Madrid between 2016 and 2018, winning three Champions League titles and LaLiga among their honours, came to the defence of his former player.

"He made me win incredible things," Zidane said when asked about Ronaldo's current situation.

"I think we have to salute his great career; what he has done is exceptional.

"I was lucky enough to have him with me. Hats off to Cristiano!

"I still have a lot of respect in general for all the players, but even more so for those with whom I spent time, and especially Cristiano, who still made us win a lot of things."

rrsw0lbtj8yh1b4ivbpwvxruq.title: Mancini: Winning start to Nations League the only medicine to cure Italy
rrsw0lbtj8yh1b4ivbpwvxruq.subtitle: Roberto Mancini begins his second stint in charge of Italy against Belgium in the Nations League, and he wants to get fans back onside.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini believes a winning start to Italy's Nations League campaign will be the perfect medicine after the Azzurri missed out on the World Cup this summer.
Italy welcome Belgium to the Stadio Olimpico on Friday, for what will be Mancini's first match back in charge after replacing Gennaro Gattuso.
Mancini previously led the Azzurri from 2018 to 2023, guiding them to the European Championship title five years ago by beating England on penalties.
During his first spell, Mancini led Italy on a 37-match unbeaten streak, a European record that has since been surpassed by Spain following their victory over Argentina in the World Cup final.

The 61-year-old won 38 of his 58 games during his first stint (D12 L8) before resigning in August 2023 after a failed qualification bid for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, before having a short-lived spell in charge of Saudi Arabia.
Italy have been placed in Group A1 alongside Belgium, France and Turkiye, and they will play all three nations during this extended international break.

The Azzurri have finished third in the Nations League twice, doing so in 2020-21 and 2022-23, and Mancini believes a good start will go some way to repairing the damaged relationship between the supporters and their team.
"To play well from the start, which won't be easy considering we've had just two days to prepare for this game," Mancini told reporters about his aims for the Nations League.
"This is what international football is like. We have to get things done quickly and get results. That is the only medicine for what ails us.
"We hope to reach the final four of the Nations League. It's a strong group and so it won't be easy, but we'll try. I can't wait to hear the national anthem playing.
"Many of these players are experienced, and naturally there is pressure, but it's positive pressure because playing football is their passion, and they need to enjoy it."

Mancini's last game in charge of Italy saw the Azzurri beat the Netherlands 3-2 to seal third place in the Nations League three years ago, but the end of his tenure was overshadowed by his failure to secure a spot at the Qatar World Cup.
After Luciano Spalletti's tenure, Gattuso also failed to lead Italy to the tournament, with Italy losing 4-1 on penalties to Bosnia-Herzegovina as they missed out on a third consecutive edition.
"Unfortunately, this is football, you can lose games sometimes in absurd fashion," Mancini added.
"But the good thing about the sport is that it gives you an opportunity to make up for it immediately. We must keep it in mind, but then focus on the future."
Gianluigi Donnarumma was in between the sticks for Italy during those near misses, and he too echoed the disappointment of Mancini.
Donnarumma has played for Italy since he was 17 years old, and following his nation's latest setback, he may not play at his first World Cup until he is 31.
"It's been very tough," Donnarumma told Sky Sport Italia. "I struggle to even explain it. This has been a very long and difficult summer, but we must start again.
"It's a new era, tomorrow we have a big game and the fans like us are disappointed, so it's up to us to fire them up and get them to fall back in love with the Azzurri jersey."

rtpfqwg2ox3h1se8jv58r9u3n.title: Netherlands boss Xavi relishing 'great challenge' against Klopp's Germany
rtpfqwg2ox3h1se8jv58r9u3n.subtitle: Xavi begins his tenure with the Netherlands against Germany in the Nations League, and he is looking forward to the challenge ahead.
paragraphs: Xavi described his first game in charge of the Netherlands as a "great challenge" as they prepare to welcome Germany and Jurgen Klopp to the Johan Cruijff Arena on Thursday.
It is a meeting of two coaches making their debuts for the respective nations, with Xavi having replaced Ronald Koeman after another early exit at this summer's World Cup.
The Netherlands were eliminated from the World Cup in the round of 32 on penalties by Morocco, the first time they had failed to reach the last 16 at the tournament.
Xavi had been out of management since leaving Barcelona in 2024, having won LaLiga in 2022-23 and the Supercopa de Espana in the same season.
He compiled 90 wins, 23 draws and 29 defeats in 142 games in charge of the Blaugrana across all competitions, giving him a win percentage of 62.7%.
Xavi is the first foreign coach of the Netherlands since Ernst Happel in 1977-1978, and he is looking forward to going head-to-head with former Liverpool boss Klopp.
"We have to play our best football tomorrow because Germany are a great team," Xavi told reporters.
"I can feel this rivalry. Everyone in our team is really looking forward to the game, and it is a great way for us to start this journey.
"He [Klopp] has been one of the best coaches in the world in recent years. It will be a great challenge for the whole team and for me personally.
"It is always the goal to win, but it is even more important to leave a good impression with the execution. I want the team to show passion, ambition, desire and our philosophy."
When he was unveiled, Xavi described himself as a "winner" and he was confident that his success as a player could be translated to the Netherlands' dugout.
Xavi also believes the quality within the Netherlands' ranks can deliver what he intends to achieve.
"They have the capacity to carry out what we ask of them. I have clearly seen that in the training sessions," Xavi added.
"They are hard workers and are open to listening. I am very happy with that. And I was impressed by the physical aspect, among other things."
The Netherlands also face back-to-back away games versus Serbia and Greece, and a home clash with Serbia on October 4 after they take on Germany.
Memphis Depay, Wout Weghorst, Marten de Roon, Guus Til and injured midfielder Mats Wieffer are missing from Xavi's first Netherlands squad.

Ruben van Bommel and Gjivai Zechiel have been handed senior call-ups, while Jurrien Timber is also expected to feature throughout their four matches having struggled with a groin injury at the start of the campaign.
"We are now focused on tomorrow, not on the rest of the matches. We are ready," Xavi said.
"We have to be a bit careful with Jurrien Timber, who was injured for a long time. But he is available, that goes for everyone."

rzk3tikbpi3j11qi14wfhf8nz.title: Berg Johnsen urges Sporting KC team-mates to be 'on the same wavelength'
rzk3tikbpi3j11qi14wfhf8nz.subtitle: Sporting Kansas City's hopes of reaching the MLS play-offs are slowly fading ahead of their trip to the Houston Dynamo on Saturday.
paragraphs: Sporting Kansas City captain Lasse Berg Johnson has urged his team-mates to "make sure we are on the same wavelength" as they prepare to take on the Houston Dynamo.
Sporting KC are currently bottom of the Western Conference, and their misery was compounded last weekend following a 4-3 defeat against the Philadelphia Union.
Despite leading 3-0 after 16 minutes, SKC conceded four goals in nine second-half minutes to fall further away from the play-off places.
Berg Johnsen believes his side must communicate better on the pitch if they are to turn their season around.

"We need to talk to each other and look at each other and agree on if we are going to press them for the next minutes or are we going to keep playing or are we going to go longer and go for the second balls," said the SKC captain.
"As a team, I don't think we have managed it well enough in those situations.

"We need to look at it and see how can we solve it better on the pitch, because in those moments, what usually happens is we players can be silent, so we need to talk to each other to make sure we are on the same wavelength.
"If we either go longer or if we try to play or if we press them or if we sit, we have not managed that good enough."
Houston, on the other hand, are second in the West and just five points behind leaders Vancouver Whitecaps.
However, after losing 1-0 to the San Jose Earthquakes, the Dynamo drew 2-2 with FC Cincinnati last time out; Houston have won just once in their last six MLS games (D3 L2).
Houston Dynamo – Guilherme
Guilherme scored his team-leading 14th goal of the season on Saturday, tied for the second-most goals in a single regular season by a Dynamo player, with Erick Torres in 2017.
The only player with more regular-season goals in a season for Houston was Mauro Manotas in 2018 (19).
Sporting Kansas City – Andre Luiz
Andre Luiz recorded his first MLS brace on Saturday and has scored three goals in his first four games with Sporting KC.
Sporting are averaging 2.25 goals per game in MLS matches in which Luiz has played, compared to 0.95 this season without Luiz playing.
MATCH PREDICTION: HOUSTON DYNAMO WIN

Houston extended their home unbeaten streak to nine games (W6 D3) with a draw with Cincinnati. The Dynamo have recorded five home unbeaten streaks of 10 or more games in their history, with the last one coming in 2019 (10 games).

The Dynamo earned a win on the road against SKC in August and are looking to sweep the season series for the first time. Houston have just two wins in their last 11 regular-season matches against Sporting KC and have not won at home since May 2021.
Sporting KC have scored three or more goals in three straight regular-season matches after scoring three goals just once in their first 22 league matches of 2026.
It is their first time scoring three or more goals in three straight league games since August 2022, and the club have never done so in four straight.
Houston Dynamo – 63.5%
Sporting Kansas City – 17.1%

s7b8t49nltsw1ptr5r75k92c2.title: Belgium 0-1 France: Olise keeps Zidane perfect with last-gasp winner
s7b8t49nltsw1ptr5r75k92c2.subtitle: France's wastefulness looked set to earn them a draw with Belgium, but Michael Olise came off the bench to ensure they left with a win.
paragraphs: Michael Olise came off the bench to snatch France a late 1-0 victory over Belgium in the Nations League to continue their 100% start.

It looked like Zinedine Zidane's side were set to be frustrated in the injured Kylian Mbappe's absence, but Olise took just 11 minutes after his introduction to score the winner at Stade Roi Baudouin.
France started brightly, and Desire Doue almost scored a stunning opener just 12 minutes in; he twisted away from his marker and slalomed into the box before firing his shot against the crossbar.
Doue almost turned provider shortly after as he whipped a delightful cross in from the right, and though Esteban Lepaul quickly adjusted his feet, his first-time effort was straight at Senne Lammens.
Maghnes Akliouche's free-kick was then spilled by Lammens, who jumped straight back up to smother Lepaul's follow-up. But Romeo Lavia was then needed on the line to deny Pierre Kalulu.
Doue continued to provide the sparkle for France and bent a whipped effort narrowly wide seven minutes after the break.
Two minutes later, Lucas da Cunha came close to a debut goal with his fizzed effort through the crowded box, but it struck the foot of the right post.
Belgium grew into the game the longer it went on, with substitute Dodi Lukebakio surging forward in the 73rd minute to poke a shot on goal, which Mike Maignan smothered.
Lukebakio stung Maignan's palms shortly after with a powerful low effort, and though the goalkeeper failed to hold it on the first attempt, no Belgian player was following in.

France's quality eventually told, however, as Olise latched onto fellow substitute Rayan Cherki's pass and strode forward from the halfway line before curling a lovely finish into the bottom right corner in the 88th minute.
France get over the line after a stuttering attacking display

France's wealth of attacking talent is clear for all to see, but Mbappe is the lynchpin, having also scored the winner against Turkiye last time out when Les Bleus had struggled to break their opponents down.
Zidane shuffled his pack, leaving an obvious replacement in Ousmane Dembele – who entered the fray in the second half – on the bench.
Three players made their debuts as starters in France's team (Andy Diouf, Jeremy Jacquet and Da Cunha), a first since August 2010, when there were six debutants in the line-up.
France certainly had plenty of chances to put the game to bed, racking up 18 shots with seven of those on target, with their attempts amounting to 1.15 expected goals (xG).

Doue was their best outlet, having five shots himself, with two of those testing Lammens and another hitting the woodwork. He had a game-high 16 touches in the opposition box, and also created four chances for his team-mates.
But it was Olise who turned the tide, pulling out a high-quality goal to spare France's blushes and ensure Zidane made it two wins from two.

Belgium will feel the game was theirs for the taking, having held off France for so long, but their first shot on target did not come until the 73rd minute, and when Matias Fernandez-Pardo had a golden opportunity to snatch a draw at the end, he went down too easily as he fired wide, with no penalty forthcoming.

sfulzbmntwbh1d0cmwqifixhy.title: Zidane ready to make changes ahead of crucial Belgium clash
sfulzbmntwbh1d0cmwqifixhy.subtitle: Zinedine Zidane will make "smart changes" as his France side prepare to meet Belgium in Group A1 of the Nations League.
paragraphs: France head coach Zinedine Zidane has stressed he will make changes to his side ahead of a crucial Nations League meeting with Belgium on Monday.
After three matchdays, Les Bleus occupy top spot in Group A1, sitting one point ahead of second-placed Belgium.
However, it has been a far from ideal campaign for the two-time World Cup winners, with Zidane having lost Kylian Mbappe and Dayot Upamecano to injury and suspension, respectively.
That has forced Zidane to utilise his squad depth, but the former Real Madrid coach is happy with the options he has at his disposal.
"There will be changes, that's for sure. It is our fourth match, and we can't just do anything," Zidane told reporters.
"We will make smart changes, and above all, we will do it to be competitive."
The 1998 world champion is determined to rotate his squad, with the hope that this brings togetherness as well as keeping everyone sharp for the games ahead.
"It is to show that we are all involved and that all the players are committed to this team, to demonstrate that there is a lot of competition within the French national team," Zidane said.
After overcoming Belgium 1–0 thanks to a late strike from Michael Olise in the reverse fixture, Zidane expects a stern test against Mark van Bommel's side at the Stade de France.
"They played very well in the first match against us and caused us tactical difficulties," said Zidane.
"They are capable of many things. Against Turkiye, they posed problems for the opposition, so they are strong both collectively and individually," added the France boss.
However, Zidane is relishing the challenge and "tension" of managing France, having replaced long-term coach Didier Deschamps after the 2026 World Cup.
Zidane said: "I have always felt it, and I like it. I like feeling that tension, I enjoy it.
"But what I love most of all is what I do – being with the players, with this group, that is what I enjoy.
"The demands are the same, but the difference is that the work with the national team differs from that at club level."

spg5pl0s04xv14ffyt4svtu51.title: Bellamy concedes Wales had to 'suffer a lot' against Portugal
spg5pl0s04xv14ffyt4svtu51.subtitle: Wales were narrowly beaten by Portugal to start their Nations League campaign, with Craig Bellamy's side put under pressure in Lisbon.
paragraphs: Craig Bellamy admitted Wales had to "suffer a lot" against Portugal but hailed his injury-hit side's resilience in their Nations League opener.
Wales began their Nations League campaign with a narrow 1-0 defeat to Portugal, with Joao Felix's deflected first-half strike proving the difference.
Cristiano Ronaldo also had a goal ruled out for offside after the break, while Wales finished the contest on top, hitting the woodwork late on through Brennan Johnson.

Despite that, Wales are without a win in their last five matches in all competitions (D3 L2), while they have lost five of their last 10 matches (W2 D3), one more than in their previous 25 outings (W11 D10 L4).
The 23 shots Wales faced against Portugal is their most in a single game since a Nations League match against Turkiye in November 2024 (25).
But Bellamy was impressed with how his team played despite being under pressure for long spells in the game.
"It was a difficult game for us. We had to suffer a lot," said Bellamy.
"I think that's the longest we've been in a game without the ball.
"We could have done more with the ball, but I'm beyond proud as well.
"We have a lot of players who weren't here. That's OK; we can handle it.

"A lot of players who don't play week in, week out. So, for them to use the energy they were able to, we've got to have a big heart to be able to do that. They've always shown that, and they showed that again."
The loss leaves Wales bottom of Group A4 after the first matchday, with Norway and Denmark also drawn alongside them.
Wales are missing the likes of Harry Wilson, Karl Darlow, Joe Rodon, Dylan Lawlor and Nathan Broadhead through injury, and face a quick turnaround before facing Denmark away on Sunday.
Bellamy is determined to see an improved performance when they step out in Copenhagen.
"There's more for us, so that's something we always look at as a positive," he added.
"How can we improve? How can we get better?"

t4d0bd3ewwd01gny6mbzs3t3q.title: Kane: England did what we had to do against Czechia
t4d0bd3ewwd01gny6mbzs3t3q.subtitle: England were under slight pressure to get a win against Czechia after their loss to Spain, and Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane secured it.
paragraphs: Harry Kane said England "did what we had to do" after beating 10-man Czechia 2-0 in the Nations League.
England suffered a disappointing defeat to Spain last time out, but they got their first win of this season's edition at Fortuna Arena.

Pavel Sulc was sent off after 25 minutes for a late tackle on Elliot Anderson, and the Three Lions made their numerical advantage count in the second half, with Anthony Gordon and Kane both on target for the second game running.
Kane has netted four goals in six Nations League appearances since the start of the 2024-25 edition.
The pressure was on England – despite Thomas Tuchel saying before the match that this was not a “must-win” fixture – and Kane was thrilled the team came out on top.
"Job done, it was a professional performance," he told BBC Radio 5 Live.
"It wasn't the most exciting game of football, but we did what we had to. Won the game, good clean sheet, and we take it into the next one.
"When a team who likes to defend get a man sent off, it becomes even tougher. You have to be patient. Against 10 you have to move it quickly, and as they tire, the spaces will open up."
Gordon was a key figure for England again with his opening goal; he now has four goals and four assists across his last nine international appearances.
He is also the second Barcelona player to score in consecutive appearances for England, after Gary Lineker in 1989.
"He's showing that he belongs at the highest level, for Barcelona and England," Kane said of Gordon, who had a team-high four shots and created four chances.

"His performances in the last couple of games have been some of his best that he has played in an England shirt, and I think he is just relishing putting the shirt on and being one of the main men in the team.
"He is an important player for us, and he showed that during the World Cup."
England had conceded 13 goals in their previous six appearances prior to this match, meaning a clean sheet would have been high on their priority list.

Next in Group A3, England travel to Croatia, who are also on three points after following up their win with a 4-1 defeat to Spain on Tuesday, but Tuchel was hesitant to give away any plans for the next match.
"I cannot tell you," he told BBC Radio 5 Live when asked about potential changes. "We have three days, which is a big difference to two games.
"We decided not to travel back to England but to stay in Prague one more night, get some good rest, and then travel to Croatia and have two training sessions there.
"We will push everyone to be available, even Nico O'Reilly and Ezri Konsa, hopefully and then we know more. The next match is important for us against a direct opponent, and we want to win."
On the game itself, Tuchel added: "We played a professional second half.
"We stepped up in urgency, bit of quicker play and better ball speed. We deserved to win the second half.

"With the red card, we became heavy, heavy favourites. A clean sheet is always important; it gives everyone a good feeling. Always things to improve, but overall a serious performance and a deserved win."

tafeaa7zwemq1wkj09tgzehu3.title: 'This time we will win' – Montella promisies Turkiye victory against Italy
tafeaa7zwemq1wkj09tgzehu3.subtitle: Turkiye began their Nations League campaign with a defeat to France, but Vincenzo Montella was confident of beating Italy on home soil.
paragraphs: Vincenzo Montella has vowed he will lead Turkiye to victory against Italy in the Nations League following their narrow 1-0 defeat to France on Friday.
Kylian Mbappe's 54th-minute strike was enough to earn Zinedine Zidane a victory in his first game in charge at Turka Arac Muayene Kocaeli Stadyumu.
Ugurcan Cakir was shown a late red card for a handball outside of the box, but Montella was thrilled with the way his team played against France's star-studded squad.
Turkiye finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.21 from their 12 shots, compared to France's tally of 1.17 from the same number of attempts.

And Montella's side come up against an Italy team who began their second stint under Roberto Mancini with a 2-0 defeat at home against Belgium, with Mika Godts and Dodi Lukebakio scoring in either half to hand Mark van Bommel a winning debut.
It is the first meeting between the two nations since a 0-0 draw in an international friendly in June 2024, but Italy have a good record in this fixture.
The Azzurri have never lost to Turkiye in their previous 14 matches against them (W10 D4).
However, Montella believes his team's performance against France is a solid foundation to build on, and he was confident of getting the better of Italy on Monday.
"You all played very well and showed your fighting spirit," Montella told his squad.
"We conceded a goal due to a momentary lapse in concentration, but we could have won this match.
"Now we will immediately gather our energy and focus on the Italy match. This time we will win, as long as we play with the same discipline and passion."
Turkiye find themselves third in Group A1 after the opening round of fixtures, with clashes against Belgium and Italy to come before the end of the international break.

tel52ebpc26g10vq0gdny0cw3.title: In-form Gyokeres full of confidence after another Nations League goal
tel52ebpc26g10vq0gdny0cw3.subtitle: Viktor Gyokeres believes he is back to his best after scoring for the seventh Nations League game in a row against Romania with Sweden.
paragraphs: Viktor Gyokeres revelled in his sensational scoring streak in the Nations League after his goal helped Sweden beat Romania 1-0 at Arena Nationala on Monday.
Gyokeres netted the only goal in the 13th minute, tucking in from close range after Sebastian Nanasi had turned a cross to the back post against the woodwork.
The in-form Arsenal striker has now scored in his last seven consecutive Nations League matches, while this was his fourth successive goal in this year's campaign.
Gyokeres' four goals are the joint-most in this year's competition, level with Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal, Leo Walta, Michael Olise and Troy Parrott.
His contributions to Graham Potter's side have been crucial after Alexander Isak withdrew from the squad with an injury, but Sweden have remained unbeaten in his absence.
Sweden are top of Group B4 after four matches, winning three of those, putting themselves in a commanding position to return to the top table of the Nations League.

Gyokeres' form comes at a crucial time ahead of the return of the Premier League, as Kai Havertz sustained an injury while playing for Germany, with the Swede the likely replacement for Mikel Arteta's side when they face Leeds United this Saturday.

The 28-year-old has failed to score in his first five appearances in all competitions for the Gunners in 2026-27, with just two of those being starts, but Gyokeres feels his strong run during the international break has put him back at the top of his game.
"It feels good. It feels like you get good chances, and then you score," Gyokeres told Viaplay, as quoted by Fotbolldirekt.
"But we could have done more in the first half and killed the game.
"We let them play and didn't get up in the press well enough in the second half, so we made it difficult for ourselves."
Sweden dominated their clash with Romania and should have added further gloss to the scoreline.
Potter's side finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.8 from their 12 shots, though only two were on target, compared to Romania's tally of 0.6 from 13 attempts.
Gyokeres was, however, pleased with the defensive display from his team, with Sweden keeping their first clean sheet in this year's Nations League.
"It's important for the team to have this type of match where things may not go exactly as we want," Gyokeres added.
"We managed to keep a clean sheet. It's been a while, so that's very positive. Then it's clear that we need to control the match a little more."
Sweden return to action next month when they face Bosnia-Herzegovina on November 14 before they take on Poland three days later.

thfihuws9x1xz59k2dq115ly.title: Isak leaves Sweden camp with 'minor injury'
thfihuws9x1xz59k2dq115ly.subtitle: After a brilliant start to the 2026-27 season for Alexander Isak, he now has an injury concern after leaving Sweden's camp after one game.
paragraphs: Alexander Isak has left Sweden's camp and is returning to Liverpool after suffering "a minor injury" while on international duty.
Isak played the whole 90 minutes against Romania on Friday and was on the scoresheet in their 2-1 win, extending his hot streak to start the season.
The striker has five goals in eight matches for club and country so far this term.
Isak had gone down and looked in some discomfort during the match against Romania but had initially said it was just a "heavy stamp" that led to his blood-stained sock.
Liverpool did not confirm the full extent of the injury in their statement, simply saying: "Isak is to return to Liverpool from international duty due to a minor injury.
"The striker will not be involved in Sweden's three remaining fixtures in the current international break and will now be assessed by club medical staff at the AXA Training Centre."
Isak endured an injury-hit first campaign at Anfield, suffering a leg fracture that ruled him out for months, having also missed five games between October and November last year with a groin issue.
However, Liverpool will hope he will be available for their first match after the international break, when they host Manchester City on October 11.

uiu7tetpefut1340eqpkbt6n5.title: Portugal 2-1 Norway: Ramos scores again as 10 men hold on
uiu7tetpefut1340eqpkbt6n5.subtitle: In Cristiano Ronaldo's absence, Goncalo Ramos once again took his chance to shine as he netted the winner for Portugal against Norway.
paragraphs: Goncalo Ramos grabbed Portugal's winner as Jorge Jesus' team survived Francisco Conceicao's late dismissal to see off Norway 2-1 in the Nations League.
Ramos has taken his chance to shine for Portugal in the wake of Cristiano Ronaldo's departure from their squad.
And the forward took his tally for this international break to three goals as Portugal maintained their 100% start to their Nations League Group A4 campaign.
They had to do it the hard way at Estadio Do Dragao, where 36th-minute Kristoffer Ajer's stunner put Norway ahead.
Ajer sublimely curled an exquisite finish into the top-right corner, but the defender's effort was matched in quality by Joao Cancelo just two minutes later.
Cancelo met Nuno Mendes' throw-in and, from the edge of the box, arrowed a first-time strike beyond Egil Selvik.
The full-back went close to a second early in the second half, before Erling Haaland dragged wide from his first, and only, opportunity.
Haaland was taken off shortly after in a surprise move, though he did not appear to be moving entirely freely, and Portugal almost took the lead when Ruben Neves sliced over from point-blank range.
Yet Portugal finally got their second goal in the 79th minute, with Joao Felix teeing up Ramos to finish deftly.

There was time for drama when a member of Norway's bench seemed to see red before Conceicao then received two bookings in swift succession for dissent, but Portugal held onto the points, despite their numerical disadvantage.
Ramos the main man as Portugal prove there is life after Ronaldo
Ronaldo's departure has overshadowed what has been a superb first four games in charge for Jesus, who has already guided defending champions Portugal into the Nations League knockout stages.

They have beaten Norway twice, and Jesus will be particularly pleased with how tightly under wraps his defence kept Haaland, who did have three shots but only had the one real chance, which he scuffed.
Ramos got the crucial goal, and both of the shots he had were on target, and if Ronaldo really is to retire, then Portugal do have their natural front man lined up.
It was a mixed day for Conceicao, who was Portugal's most creative player (four chances created), yet then showed a real lack of composure and professionalism to get himself sent off.
Ultimately, though, it is a case of job done for Portugal, who can rest easy heading into the November fixtures, knowing their place in the next round is secure.

vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.title: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC: Dreyer strikes late to deny Messi and co.
vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.subtitle: Inter Miami's recent struggles continued as they played out yet another draw in MLS, losing more ground on the Eastern Conference leaders.
paragraphs: Anders Dreyer netted a late equaliser to earn San Diego FC a 2-2 draw with Inter Miami, who were held to a fourth straight stalemate despite Lionel Messi's free-kick.

Dreyer opened the scoring early on, but Miami turned the game on its head, with Messi and Luis Suarez both hitting the back of the net, only for San Diego's striker to complete his brace with eight minutes remaining at Nu Stadium.

San Diego's 12th-minute opener came out of nowhere as Jeppe Tverskov slotted a perfectly weighted throughball in behind for Dreyer, who charged in behind Miami's defense from the halfway line before dinking a lovely shot over Dayne St. Clair.
Twelve minutes later, Miami were back on level terms. Messi's free-kick looked to be more of a cross as it floated towards the far post, but it missed everyone in the middle and snuck in.

German Berterame's curler was cleared in front of the line by the retreating Ian Murphy, but San Diego could not clear their lines as Yannick Bright picked out Messi, whose first-time shot was kept out by CJ dos Santos.
Marcus Ingvartsen had a goal disallowed shortly after at the other end for an offside in the build-up, while Dos Santos punched away an awkward strike from Suarez.
But the Uruguayan soon got his goal in the 74th minute, lifting over Dos Santos from a tight angle to find the far corner.
Miami's lead only lasted eight minutes, though, with Dreyer again timing his run to perfection to meet a Tverskov pass, and a rooted St. Clair could not get a hand to it.

Messi had the chance to win it in stoppage time, bending a low shot through the crowded box, but Dos Santos got down to keep it out despite seeing it late, meaning Miami sit 11 points behind Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC.
Messi makes more history despite Miami's frustrations
While Miami are unbeaten in their last five matches, they have drawn each of the last four, having held the lead in three of those.

But Messi has played his part in trying to get Miami back to winning ways, and netted his 101st goal for the Herons in total, while extending his lead in the Golden Boot race, as it was his 20th in MLS this season.
That means he is now just the second player in the league's history to score 20+ goals in three straight seasons, after Los Angeles FC's Denis Bouanga (2023-2025).
Messi finished the match with 10 shots – Miami had 19 overall – with five of those on target, while he also led the metrics for touches in the opposition box (14) and chances created (three).
But Dreyer ensured Messi would not end up on the winning side on Sunday, as he netted his 11th goal in MLS this term, more than any other San Diego player.
It was a vital point for San Diego, who halted a three-game losing streak and responded well to their 5-0 thumping at the hands of the Philadelphia Union.

Messi finished the match with 10 shots – Miami had 19 overall – with five of those on target, while he also led the metrics for touches in the opposition box (14) and chances created (three).

But Dreyer ensured Messi would not end up on the winning side on Sunday, as he netted his 11th goal in MLS this term, more than any other San Diego player.

It was a vital point for San Diego, who halted a three-game losing streak and responded well to their 5-0 thumping at the hands of the Philadelphia Union.

vdueugzzdr8v1u9dow76lhnu1.title: Maestre says 6-1 rout of Spurs could be a 'game-changer' for London City
vdueugzzdr8v1u9dow76lhnu1.subtitle: Alexia Putellas and Kadidiatou Diani inspired London City Lionesses to a 6-1 win over Tottenham on Sunday, taking them third in the WSL.
paragraphs: After London City Lionesses trounced Tottenham 6-1 in the Women's Super League, head coach Eder Maestre said the result could be a "game-changer" for his team.

Captain Alexia Putellas and France international Kadidiatou Diani scored two goals apiece as London City ran riot at Brisbane Road, with Danielle van de Donk and Delphine Cascarino also on target for the visitors.
Maestre's team were 3-0 up by half-time, with Putellas getting her goals in the third and 34th minutes, building on her first WSL strike in a 2-0 victory over Brighton last week.
Putellas now has 49 goal involvements in her last 50 starts at club and international level, scoring 28 times and providing 21 assists for London City, Barcelona and Spain.
London City have 12 points on the board after five WSL matches, and Maestre believes the dominant nature of their latest win will provide everyone at the club with a major boost.
"The three points are the same as you can have in every game, but this kind of win can be a game-changer, in terms of showing everyone that we are pushing hard," said Maestre.
"But, at the same time, we need to be humble as well. The teams that are used to being there and occupying these places [at the top] are still there.
"I'm so happy we're hitting our targets. When you have these kinds of players it is about trying to find chemistry and it takes time.
"It's a process, and we're in the process of building something strong."
Spurs had not lost any of their first four games of 2026-27, taking 10 points, but Martin Ho said they could have no excuses for the way their performance levels dropped.
"Really poor, not acceptable from us as a group. Defensively, we didn't win the first ball or the second ball. In duels, we were poor. We have to move on," Ho said.
"The team collectively needs to own that and we will, and that starts with me, I take responsibility for it.
"We were just not at it, but that can't be the level. Everyone will be disappointed – that was not the level we expect. We conceded six goals and you don't want to be doing that."
In Sunday's other early games, there were also one-sided victories for Brighton, who thumped pointless Charlton Athletic 5-1, and Chelsea.

Sonia Bompastor's Blues eased to a 3-0 win over London rivals West Ham, with Melvine Malard opening the scoring in the 38th minute, before late goals from Kiera Walsh and Maika Hamano made the points safe.
Everton also beat Birmingham City 2-1, while Aston Villa played out a 1-1 draw with Crystal Palace.

vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.title: Wirtz 'the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt' against Bournemouth, claims Carragher
vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.subtitle: Florian Wirtz struggled to make an impact against Bournemouth, and Jamie Carragher has questioned his starting place going forward.
paragraphs: Jamie Carragher believes Florian Wirtz must be dropped for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City after the international break, claiming his performance against Bournemouth was the "poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt".
Liverpool edged to a 1-0 victory over Bournemouth, giving Andoni Iraola a winning return to Vitality Stadium thanks to Alexander Isak's second-half goal.
Iraola is the first manager to remain unbeaten in his first five league games in charge of Liverpool (W2 D3) since Joe Fagan in September 1983.
However, Wirtz came under fire for his performance on the south coast as he struggled to make an impact.
He finished the match with a team-low 70.3% passing accuracy (completing 26 of 37 passes), had 53 touches, and just two off-target shots, though he did create a joint-game-high three chances.
Only Ronald Araujo (24) lost possession more often than the German (16).
And Carragher was far from impressed by Wirtz's showing, claiming that Iraola needs to think about leaving him out of the side if they want to improve their results.
"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," said Carragher on the bonus Jamie Carragher Podcast.

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy; he keeps possession. There's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.
"But the reason I worry is: I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.
"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley, and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game, it was what I've seen for the last 12 months: I don't see how he's going to hurt you.
"It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

"The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.

"And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No. 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player; I don't.
"I think going forward, Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team.
"Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home; for me, he can't be in the team."
Wirtz has been called up in Jurgen Klopp's Germany squad for the upcoming Nations League.
Klopp – the former Liverpool manager – has named two squads, with Wirtz getting a rest before being in contention for their final two games of the international break against Serbia and Greece.
"The one hope for Liverpool supporters now is Jurgen Klopp is the Germany manager," Carragher added.

"Wirtz goes away with the Germany team for three weeks, and he's obviously one of the best players in Germany; that's how they see him. Can Jurgen Klopp sprinkle a bit of stardust on him in that position?

"Jurgen is one of the greatest managers in the world; we know that. And what he gets out of players is probably more than most managers because of the nature of his personality, and fingers crossed something can happen for him.

"There's a scenario there that Jurgen Klopp and Germany have a great international window, he gets loads of goals, assists and comes back on a high. Manchester City's the next game; he impacts that, all is forgotten, all is forgiven. There's a potential turnaround there.
"I would love that to happen. I'd love him to be the match-winner against Manchester City."
Liverpool, who sit sixth in the Premier League table on nine points after an unbeaten start, return to action on October 11 against leaders Manchester City.

w4tlhtfp5huo11h5lb72ixdxq.title: Wiegman not focused on expiring England contract
w4tlhtfp5huo11h5lb72ixdxq.subtitle: Sarina Wiegman's contract as England boss expires after next year's Women's World Cup, but her focus is on qualifying for the tournament.
paragraphs: England boss Sarina Wiegman insisted her focus is on qualifying for next year's Women's World Cup and not on her expiring contract.
The Lionesses face Greece in a two-legged play-off semi-final, with the winner facing either Slovakia or Ukraine for a spot in next summer's competition.
Wiegman has led England to back-to-back European Championship titles so far during her tenure, while also reaching the World Cup final in 2023.

She is the first-ever men's or women's manager to reach five consecutive major international tournament finals, after also reaching the showpiece in both competitions during her time with the Netherlands.
Despite her contract with the Lionesses ending after the World Cup, Wiegman's full focus is on qualifying for the tournament.
"We had conversations before," said Wiegman when asked if talks had taken place about a possible extension.
"We have regular conversations together, and we talk about the future, but at this point I'm just really focusing on Greece, and we want to get through and qualify for the World Cup.
"I talk to Mark [Bullingham, FA CEO] every two weeks, and we speak about what's happening now, what's in the future, but there's no news now.
"I'm just focusing on Greece and hopefully the World Cup."
England were forced into the play-off rounds after finishing second in their qualifying group, which also featured Spain, Iceland and Ukraine.
The Lionesses finished level on 15 points with Spain, the reigning world champions, but missed out on top spot due to head-to-head after losing 4-0 to their rivals.

w6gh3flamwa117m0ohtrqzngo.title: The Numbers Game: Can Tuchel shore up England's defence against Czechia?
w6gh3flamwa117m0ohtrqzngo.subtitle: After opening their Nations League campaigns, Czechia and England are looking to pick up their first three points of 2026-27 on Tuesday.
paragraphs: Both Czechia and England stumbled at the first Nations League hurdle, losing their games to Croatia and Spain, respectively.
England played out a five-goal thriller with Spain but ended up on the wrong side of the result after throwing away a lead to eventually lose 3-2.
As for Czechia, they were undone by Luka Modric, who rolled back the years to help Croatia to a 2-1 victory.
That leaves both nations on zero points in Group A3, but neither will want to still be empty-handed with a third of their group games gone.
So, who will come out on top at Fortuna Arena? Here, using Opta data, we look at the key talking points ahead of Tuesday's clash.
Both teams will already feel this is a must-win fixture given the thick-and-fast nature of the Nations League campaign, and it is England who are expected to come out on top.
England have lost just one of their last nine meetings with Czechia in all competitions (W6 D2).
However, that loss came on their last visit to the nation back in October 2019 (2-1).
They are given a 68.8% chance of victory when they head to Prague, with a further 18.7% chance of a draw.
Only three teams have won consecutive home matches against England this century: Spain (a run of three), France and Sweden (both two).
Czechia will be looking to add their names to that list, but they are given just a 12.4% chance of coming away with all three points.
Will Tuchel fix defensive frailties?

England went through a rollercoaster of emotions at Wembley; a Marc Guehi error inside two minutes gave Lamine Yamal the opener, but Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane both scored to give the Three Lions a half-time lead.
Momentum then swung on a missed Kane penalty, with Alex Baena – profiting from Nico O'Reilly's slack pass – and Mikel Oyarzabal coming off the bench to secure all three points for Spain.
A lot has been made about England's identity over this international break and how they can bring the best out of their players, especially defensively.
And it is at the back that Thomas Tuchel will be keen to shore things up, and soon.
That match was the first time England have made two errors leading to a goal in a competitive game since June 2019 against the Netherlands, also in the Nations League.
England have conceded 13 goals in their last six games, almost double the amount they had in their first 17 under Tuchel (seven).
In fact, they have conceded at least three goals in their last two outings, having also beaten France 6-4 to secure third place at the World Cup, last doing so in three in a row in February 1927.
It is a stark contrast to early in Tuchel's reign when England went through qualifying for the summer's tournament without conceding a single goal.

Their recent run means that England have lost two of their last three matches in all competitions – also the heartbreaking 2-1 defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final – as many as in their previous 23 combined.
They have not lost consecutive games since between June and September 2022, also in the Nations League against Hungary and Italy.
One good thing for England is that at the other end, they remain strong, with Jude Bellingham picking up where he left off at the World Cup.
While he did not score against Spain, he did set up Gordon's opener before winning the penalty in the second half.
Bellingham has been involved in nine goals in his last nine international appearances (seven goals, two assists), more than any other England player since the start of the World Cup.
As for Gordon, he has scored in consecutive appearances for the Three Lions for the first time, having netted against Argentina and Spain.
In midfield, though they are without Declan Rice, Elliot Anderson is more than capable of holding down the fort.

He won possession more times than any other player in England's defeat to Spain (13). Since his international debut in September 2025, Anderson has won possession 125 times in 18 matches; no other England player has done so more than 50 times in this period.
Czechia look to strengthen home fortress again
Czechia's 2-1 defeat to Croatia last time out ended a 19-game unbeaten home run (W14 D5).
Modric scored the opening goal, and though Adam Karabec swiftly equalised, Czechia conceded again to substitute Marco Pasalic.
They have not lost consecutive home matches in June 2016, but given Czechia's recent form, Santi Denia may have some worries.
Czechia have lost their last two games in all competitions, last losing more consecutively between June and September 2022 (four).
They endured a difficult World Cup campaign, in which they were knocked out in the groups after finishing bottom with only a single point to their name (D1 L2).
Czechia struggled to find their rhythm against Croatia, managing only five shots worth 0.9 expected goals (xG), with only two of those hitting the target.

In addition to that, they only managed eight touches in the opposition box, while Czechia also got caught offside six times, a figure Denia will know they need to cut down if they want to cause England some real problems.
Czechia – Adam Karabec
Karabec averages a goal or assist every 89 minutes for Czechia (three goals, one assist in 355 minutes).
He netted their sole goal in the defeat last time out.
Karabec was one of just two Czechia players to have a shot on target in that match, while his only touch in the opposition box was what led to his goal.
Kane has netted four goals in six Nations League appearances since the start of the 2024-25 edition.
That is more than he scored across the first three editions of the competition he played in (three in 18 games – 2018-19, 2020-21, 2022-23).

Kane has scored 17 goals in 19 appearances for England under Tuchel. Since the German first took charge in March 2025, only Erling Haaland (26), Kylian Mbappe (19) and Oyarzabal (18) have scored more goals in all competitions for European nations.

wc2cwyh036qi111cc9o3y3hdj.title: Turkiye 0-1 France: Mbappe secures win on Zidane's debut
wc2cwyh036qi111cc9o3y3hdj.subtitle: Kylian Mbappe continued his scoring run for France, but it remains to be seen if he will be available next time out after going off injured.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane got off to a winning start as France coach, with Kylian Mbappe securing him a 1-0 win over Turkiye in their Nations League opener.

Mbappe found the breakthrough in the 54th minute but went off injured shortly after, and France could not add to his goal despite Turkiye goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir being shown an 87th-minute red card for a handball outside his box.

Turkiye almost stunned France just four minutes in as Baris Alper Yilmaz latched onto a long ball, only to be denied by Mike Maignan, who also sprang back up to deny Can Uzun before a belated offside flag went up.
Mbappe then scuffed an effort wide at the other end, while Rayan Cherki saw a low shot blocked by Merih Demiral as France struggled to break through Turkiye's defence.
Michael Olise forced a stretching save out of Cakir in France's best chance of the first half, and Adrien Rabiot then blazed over from the resulting corner.

Les Bleus made a sluggish start to the second half, though, and could have been behind in the 50th minute, but Maignan reacted brilliantly to push the unmarked Ismail Yuksek's diving header over the crossbar.

And just four minutes later, Mbappe broke the deadlock. Turkiye lost possession deep in their own half, and Olise immediately switched it to the France captain, who drilled past Cakir from the left of the box.
However, he hurt himself in the process, immediately pulling up, and he lasted just five more minutes before he was substituted off.
Mbappe's replacement, Desire Doue, saw a long-range curler pushed away while Jules Kounde hit the foot of the left post after sitting Uzun down in the box.

wh34n2kgjnf011d7yilj0rt8y.title: Klopp insists Germany's defeat to Greece is 'part of the process'
wh34n2kgjnf011d7yilj0rt8y.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp's first home match as Germany boss ended in a 1-0 defeat to Greece, though he believes there is no reason to panic.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp insisted Germany's defeat to Greece in the Nations League is "part of the process", as he took responsibility for the team selection.
Germany lost 1-0 at WWK Arena after substitute Dimitrios Kourbelis' deflected strike in the 74th minute was enough to see the visitors maintain their perfect start to Group A2.

Klopp's side won the expected goals (xG) battle 1.27 to 0.72, dominated possession (75.8%) and recorded twice as many shots as Greece (16 to eight), though could not find their way past Konstantinos Tzolakis, who made five saves.
Germany's new-look front four featured Younes Ebnoutalib, Bambase Conte and Kevin Scahde, though it was a familiar face in Karim Adeyemi who led the way in shots (three) and chances created (four).
After a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands in their campaign opener, Klopp is still waiting for his first win since succeeding Julian Nagelsmann, though the former Liverpool boss is far from concerned.
"It's part of the process. Absolutely," said Klopp after the defeat.
"The lineup, the composition, the substitutions: that's all one hundred percent my responsibility.
"It was clear that we wouldn't completely dismantle a deep-lying Greek opponent, especially in key moments where we perhaps lacked a bit of luck or their outstanding goalkeeper was there.
"I could have lived with not winning the game by a large margin, or even not winning at all, but you can't afford to lose it.
"We've only been together for a week, we're facing a deep-lying opponent, we're a newly assembled team, and then we need to have our systems in place.
"I'm sorry that the euphoria has somehow subsided... For me, that's not a problem; I just know that football needs training, football needs routines."
Germany face Serbia next on Thursday before their return fixture against Greece on October 4.

wr6gl8v1zsss1qwbwzekpnd0a.title: Zirkzee replaces injured Brobbey in Netherlands' Nations League squad
wr6gl8v1zsss1qwbwzekpnd0a.subtitle: Brian Brobbey's injury against Germany has seen him withdraw from the Netherlands squad, with Joshua Zirkzee called up to replace him.
paragraphs: The Netherlands have confirmed Joshua Zirkzee will link up with Xavi's squad for their upcoming Nations League fixtures following an injury to Brian Brobbey.
Brobbey was replaced in the 35th minute by Mexx Meerdink during Thursday's 1-1 draw with Germany, an incident which led to Felix Nmecha opening the scoring.
Cody Gakpo was able to salvage a point with a stoppage-time leveller at Johan Cruijff Arena, but Xavi has been forced into making an early change to his squad.
The in-form Sunderland striker looked in visible discomfort as he left the pitch, clutching his hamstring, though the Netherlands did not disclose the severity of the injury.
It offers the chance for Zirkzee to impress new Netherlands boss Xavi, with the Manchester United forward set to make his first appearance for his nation since November 2024.
Zirkzee has accumulated six caps for the Netherlands since making his debut against Turkiye in July two years ago.
The Netherlands sit third in Group A2 following the first round of fixtures, with Greece at the top of the table following their 2-1 victory against Serbia away from home.
Serbia are the Netherlands' next opponents this Sunday, before the Oranje travel to Greece and welcome Serbia to Philips Stadion on October 4.

x0mzan5qt69u1ll8ybllckjp9.title: Manchester United 2-1 West Ham: Terland and Medina hand Olid first WSL victory
x0mzan5qt69u1ll8ybllckjp9.subtitle: Eva Olid finally claimed her first Women's Super League victory as Manchester United survived a nervy ending to beat West Ham on Sunday.
paragraphs: Manchester United got their Women's Super League campaign up and running as goals from Elisabeth Terland and Andrea Medina clinched a 2-1 win over West Ham.
After failing to win their first three league fixtures, it proved to be the fourth time lucky for Eva Olid, with the Red Devils deserving of their first WSL triumph in 2026-27.
Terland needed just nine minutes at the Progress with Unity Stadium to give United the lead, with the Norwegian rising highest to head in Anna Sandberg's inviting corner.
Viviane Asseyi then squandered two chances to get West Ham level, with Ella Toone's strike from distance comfortably held by Constance Picaud-Inconnu at the other end.
Picaud-Inconnu then produced a stunning stop to tip Hanna Lundkvist's header over the crossbar, before Medina thundered against the woodwork early in the second half.

Terland then saw an attempt brilliantly saved down low by Picaud-Inconnu, but United's pressure eventually told in the 72nd minute when Medina picked out the top-right corner after seeing her initial effort blocked by Saki Kumagai.

But after United failed in their attempts to add further gloss to the scoreline, Asseyi was tripped inside the area by Sandberg, with the West Ham forward stepping up to send Phallon Tullis-Joyce the wrong way from 12 yards, though the Red Devils held on for the win.
Terland a head above the rest

United arrived into Sunday's clash with the threat of becoming only the second of the WSL's 'big four' teams to fail to win their first four games of the season, but they delivered a dominant display from start to finish, despite a late lapse in concentration.

They are now unbeaten in their last 13 league games against West Ham (W9 D4), with Terland's opener setting them on their way. Since her WSL debut in September 2022, only Khadija Shaw (31) has scored more headed goals in the competition than Terland (10).

United had attempted just 10 shots in the WSL this season ahead of facing the Hammers, and they bettered that in just one game here. They fired off 15 attempts, worth an expected goals (xG) value of 1.67, compared to West Ham's tally of 1.13 from their nine efforts.

Medina was the particular standout for the Red Devils, scoring her first goal for the club. She also finished with team-high totals for chances created (four), crosses (six), touches in the opposition box (11), and duels won (eight).

x6xbpdb7h4dk12hy7o2h904y9.title: Italy 'below expectations' against Belgium, laments Mancini
x6xbpdb7h4dk12hy7o2h904y9.subtitle: Roberto Mancini's first match back as Italy boss ended in a 2-0 defeat to Belgium, with the Azzurri jeered off at Stadio Olimpico.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini believes Italy's first-half performance against Belgium was "below expectations" and proved costly in their Nations League clash.
In their first match since Mancini's return to the helm, Italy lost 2-0 to Belgium at Stadio Olimpico after goals from Mika Godts and Dodi Lukebakio either side of half-time.
Italy have lost a home match while conceding at least two goals without scoring any for only the second time in the last 40 years, after a 2-0 defeat in a friendly against Croatia in August 2006.
The Azzurri ended the match with 1.5 expected goals (xG), though only 0.3 of their tally came in the first half, while Belgium accumulated 2.5 of their 2.7 xG before the break.
Gianluigi Donnarumma made six saves to try and inspire a comeback for Italy, but Senne Lammens also made six saves at the other end to keep Belgium in front.
While Mancini acknowledged Italy's improvements after the break, he admitted their first 45 minutes were not good enough.
"Belgium played better in the first half, we took the initiative in the second and could've equalised, but we conceded on a counter-attack with our error. This is football," Mancini told RAI Sport.
"The first half was below expectations, as Belgium played better, but not the second half.
"The team did really well until that second goal. We had four or five chances to equalise, we pinned them back, but Belgium are a strong side."
Italy, who have failed to qualify for each of the last three World Cups, were jeered off the pitch at full-time in Rome.
Riccardo Calafiori was "hurt" by the reaction of the fans and has urged his team-mates to focus on the positives from the defeat.

"They hurt, because at times I felt the passion of the crowd. We've got to do better, we all know that, starting from the next match," said Calafiori, who won possession eight times and created three chances.

"I saw a good team in fits and starts. We've just started working with a new coach, but other areas I didn't like, we left gaps and conceded two avoidable goals. We must try to look at the positive aspects.
"There is a lot of work to do, we've just started with a new coach, so we'll see."

xblzh5ci0yf31uqbnvsccynoz.title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal's Nations League camp amid reports of rift
xblzh5ci0yf31uqbnvsccynoz.subtitle: Media reports suggested there was some tension in Portugal's camp between Jorge Jesus and Cristiano Ronaldo, who has now left the squad.
paragraphs: Cristiano Ronaldo announced he has left Portugal's Nations League squad ahead of their match against Denmark on Thursday.
Ronaldo started for Portugal in their 1-0 win over Wales in their opening game before being taken off in the 67th minute, but was an unused substitute in the 2-1 victory against Norway.
Following that game, there have been reports of a rift between Ronaldo and head coach Jorge Jesus, who had stated before the game that he planned to use the 41-year-old at some stage.
In Wednesday's press conference, Jesus said he had already spoken to Ronaldo about his role this international break, saying he would also not play against Denmark.

The Portugal captain trained away from his team-mates on Monday and Tuesday, with media reports suggesting there was a "crisis" meeting being held between Ronaldo, Jesus and Portugal Football Federation (FPF) president Pedro Proenca to clear the air.

"After the press conference of the national team, and following a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have made the decision to leave the national team training camp," Ronaldo posted on Instagram.
"In due course, I will tell all the Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led me to leave the national team, to which I always dedicated myself.
"Now is the time to wish Portugal and all my team-mates good luck, without exception."
Ronaldo is the all-time leading scorer in men's international football (146 goals) and is pursuing the milestone of 1,000 career goals.
Portugal will be without Ronaldo for their clash with Denmark, as well as the return fixture against Norway on October 4.
The Selecao currently sit top of Group A4 with six points from six, with Jesus making a perfect start to his tenure.

xcevc6fjm5o7142oc5wiao3vx.title: Plenty of positives for Pocognoli as Scotland debut ends in goalless draw
xcevc6fjm5o7142oc5wiao3vx.subtitle: Sebastien Pocognoli's Scotland tenure began with a goalless draw against Slovenia, though he felt his side were worthy of all three points.
paragraphs: Sebastien Pocognoli said there were plenty of positives from his first match in charge of Scotland as they began their Nations League campaign with a 0-0 draw against Slovenia.
Pocognoli, sitting in the Scotland dugout for the first time since replacing Steve Clarke, watched on as his side overcame a tepid first-half display to claim a point away from home.
Andraz Sporar thought he had given Slovenia an eighth-minute lead when he crashed an effort in off the post, but the goal was ruled out for an offside against Danijel Sturm.
The Slovenia number nine then diverted an attempt just wide of the right post, with debutant Robbie Ure seeing his left-footed strike hit the post just before the break.
From there, the visitors dominated, and they should have gone in front when Oli McBurnie burst into the area, but he was unable to take the ball around Jan Oblak.
Aaron Hickey flicked a header from a corner just wide before substitute Kieron Bowie saw his shot from a tight angle smothered by Oblak as Scotland continued to probe.
McBurnie's header from point-blank range was repelled by the goalkeeper, but the best chance fell to Bowie late on. However, he scuffed his shot wide of the right post from close range.
Scotland had 17 shots against Slovenia, their most attempts in a match without scoring since June 2021 (19 shots against Czechia), but Pocognoli remained upbeat.
"I think we had two games in the same game, but you can analyse it in a positive way," Pocognoli said. "The first half was not what we expected in terms of structure.
"We were in between for the press. We were a bit surprised about the formation of Slovenia, but at half-time we fixed this, and you can see that the second half was much better.
"We produced what we wanted to show every minute, but in the first half we learned to stick together, to defend the box, to be resilient and to be patient to change the game.
"We were also challenged about set-pieces. After five minutes, we had many set-pieces to defend on, so that's the positive way to look at the first half.
"It was not always positive, but in the second half we had a game on the ball against a low block.

"So we had a lot of good movement through the side, through the lines, and we should have scored, to be honest, but the counter-press was good, the high [line] of the defence was good, just because the position of the players was better.
"Clean sheet, that's also positive, but we want to win, but I think we can take this positively."
Scotland are also now unbeaten in three consecutive away games in the Nations League for the first time (W2 D1), though they may feel they were deserving of all three points.
They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.9, with five of their 17 attempts on target, compared to Slovenia's tally of 0.5 from four shots.
However, Scotland failed to score in three competitive matches in a row for the first time since October 2004, something Billy Gilmour said must improve moving forward.

"Yeah, the two halves were totally different," Gilmour said. "I think in the first half we were still getting to grips with the situations off the ball and on the ball, but the second half was a good performance.

"Obviously, you need to score. We've had great chances. We never took them, but it's definitely something to build on. I mean, we're walking off gutted that we never scored, but in the second half it was really good.
"We came out in the second half, we were right at it, we stayed up there, we were putting pressure on them, creating chances, and the final part just never came.
"Of course, we're disappointed. We created enough chances to maybe take the game, but yeah, we came off having given it all."

"Yeah, the two halves were totally different," Gilmour said. "I think in the first half we were still getting to grips with the situations off the ball and on the ball, but the second half was a good performance.

"Obviously, you need to score. We've had great chances. We never took them, but it's definitely something to build on. I mean, we're walking off gutted that we never scored, but in the second half it was really good.

"We came out in the second half, we were right at it, we stayed up there, we were putting pressure on them, creating chances, and the final part just never came.

"Of course, we're disappointed. We created enough chances to maybe take the game, but yeah, we came off having given it all."

xj8xneulbxt13zk7nw3wcuxl.title: United States 4-2 Chile: Teenagers Hall and Albert break records in friendly win
xj8xneulbxt13zk7nw3wcuxl.subtitle: Records were broken by both Julian Hall and Mathis Albert as the United States made it back-to-back wins, beating Chile 4-2.
paragraphs: Teenagers Julian Hall and Mathis Albert were among the goalscorers as a new-look United States team beat Chile 4-2 in an entertaining friendly on Tuesday.

Mauricio Pochettino made 10 changes from the side that thrashed Peru 4-1 on Saturday, but the USA claimed another four-goal victory at Energizer Park, where Middlesbrough's Sebastian Berhalter played a starring role and was supported by some of the team's newcomers.

The St. Louis crowd were treated to an open start as Lawrence Vigouroux got down well to repel Miles Robinson's header, before Ben Brereton Diaz and Dario Osorio both struck the woodwork in the space of two minutes for Chile.

The USA went in front in the 37th minute as Hall cleverly dummied Sergino Dest's pass through to Berhalter, who applied a calm finish, though some weak goalkeeping from Chris Brady allowed Diego Ulloa to prod the equaliser over the line in first-half stoppage time.

Chile then went in front through a rasping strike from Maximiliano Gutierrez four minutes into the second half, but the USA were only behind for a couple of minutes as Hall's glancing header diverted Gio Reyna's inswinging cross home.
The USA led again when Chris Richards powered Berhalter's corner past Vigouroux with 72 minutes gone, and they got a clinching goal in added time.
Auston Trusty headed Antonee Robinson's free-kick back across goal, and on the stretch, Albert diverted the ball off the underside of the crossbar and in.
Both Hall and Albert made history for the USA on Tuesday, as their promising form continued ahead of a showdown with old rivals Mexico on Saturday.
Hall's goal – coming off the back of his debut strike against Peru – made the 18-year-old the youngest player to score on his first two outings for the USMNT.
And Albert's late effort made the Borussia Dortmund man the youngest scorer in the team's modern history, at the age of 17 years and 131 days (since at least 1988).
He surpassed Christian Pulisic, who had set the mark at the age of 17 years and 253 days old when he was also with Dortmund, against Bolivia in May 2016.

The USA only narrowly had more shots (18 to 17) and shots on target (nine to eight) than Chile, but their chances were of a far greater quality as they won the expected goals (xG) battle by 2.55 to 1.23.
