xk9d48m2npsc17n7ynf5ybhvf.title: 'Someone has got to make a play', says Mastroeni amid Real Salt Lake woes
xk9d48m2npsc17n7ynf5ybhvf.subtitle: Real Salt Lake still have not won in MLS since the World Cup, ahead of Sunday's clash with the high-flying New England Revolution.
paragraphs: Pablo Mastroeni feels Real Salt Lake's shortcomings have been in both boxes, saying "someone's got to make a play" if they are to end their 13-game winless streak.
RSL have not won since beating the Colorado Rapids on May 16, drawing four matches and losing nine in that stretch, with each of their last four being losses.
It is the longest single-season winless run in their MLS history, with their only longer sequence spanning being an 18-match skid between August 2005 and May 2006.
They travelled to Lumen Field to face the Seattle Sounders – who were themselves on a 13-game winless run – on Wednesday, only to lose 2-0 to goals from Danny Musovski and Albert Rusnak.

Now sitting three points adrift of the playoff picture, they host the New England Revolution on Saturday, when Mastroeni believes it will come down to the big moments, rather than his team's tactical approach.
Mastroeni told KSL Sports after the Seattle game: "Did we compete the right way? This is what I asked the guys in the locker room. Every one of them said yes.
"Did you work extremely hard for the guy next to you when he made a mistake? Absolutely. Tactically between the boxes, did we execute the gameplan? Yes.
"And that just leaves the boxes again. Someone's got to step up and make a play. I think that's the biggest difference. [Against Seattle], the two shots, their guys executed.
"You can't tactic your way into the goal. You can't structure your way into the goal. You've got to make plays to get in the goal. That's just the name of the game.

"If you're doing everything you can, and it's still not enough, we're either not good enough at the moment or we're unlucky. Either way, there's only one way forward, and that's put your head down and keep grinding."
The Revs, meanwhile, are second in the Eastern Conference but 11 points behind Supporters' Shield frontrunners Nashville SC.

They overcame Orlando City SC 4-2 in a thriller last time out, with Peyton Miller and Carles Gil both finding the net in second-half stoppage time, after New England had conceded an 88th-minute equaliser.
"We're never satisfied. We never give up. I think this is a special group, just how we're able to fight through adversity," said United States midfielder Brooklyn Raines.
"This group is really special, and it's just something that we continue to strive for – that we're never satisfied with anything."
Real Salt Lake – Morgan Guilavogui
Guilavogui will stay with RSL throughout the international break, having declined a call-up from Guinea, and his ball-carrying ability makes him a real threat.

His 130 progressive carries this season – in just 1,381 MLS minutes – are the third-most of any RSL player, after Noel Caliskan (175) and Juan Manuel Sanabria (131). Those players have played 2,197 and 1,746 minutes, respectively.
New England Revolution – Carles Gil
Gil's 12 goals in MLS this season are five more than any other player has scored for New England (Dor Turgeman and Peyton Miller have seven apiece).
His 29 shots on target are also more than any of his team-mates have had this season, and with 71 chances teed up for team-mates, he is the league's top creator in 2026.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
Real Salt Lake have got the better of New England of late, going unbeaten in the last four MLS matches between the two clubs.
A win for New England would be their first against Salt Lake in the league since May 2017, and during that period, RSL have outscored the Revs by nine goals to three.
The Opta supercomputer struggles to split the teams, however, which is perhaps understandable given RSL have home advantage but are in terrible form.
While RSL have 23 points from 13 outings on home soil this term (W7 D2 L4), the Revs have earned 17 from 13 road trips (W5 D2 L6).
New England Revolution – 36.7%

xmblg77wt2sf1dia65u132jv6.title: Jesus has 'zero' fear of Norway despite Fernandes injury issue
xmblg77wt2sf1dia65u132jv6.subtitle: Portugal have three points on the board in the Nations League and face high-flying Norway next, but Jorge Jesus is relishing the clash.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus says he is "not afraid of Norway" as Portugal prepare to build on their winning start to the Nations League.
Jesus' debut ended in a narrow 1-0 win over Wales on Thursday, with Joao Felix's deflected shot securing all three points.
However, Portugal now travel to Norway, who sit top of the group after a 3-2 win over Denmark, with Erling Haaland scoring a brace.

Norway have not lost at home since March 2024, and are high scorers in all competitions, having netted 37 goals in World Cup qualifying during a perfect campaign, and then scoring 13 goals in the tournament proper.
Jesus acknowledged the quality of the team they are facing but believes the quality in his own squad will shine through.
"[It's going to be a] difficult game because of the quality the team has; they demonstrated it at the World Cup," Jesus said of Norway.
"They have a forward duo that is perhaps the best in Europe right now, and besides that, they have other players we know from the Portuguese league.

"They have their strengths and their quality, but so do we. Despite having little time to work with me, we will have quality. I'm not afraid of Norway at all, zero. I look more at the team defensively than offensively."
Jesus will be without Bruno Fernandes for the trip to Oslo, though, with the Manchester United captain suffering from an injury.
He has played in all seven of United's matches this season, starting six of those, and featured from the start against Wales before being withdrawn in the 90th minute.
"Against Wales, we went in with practically everyone physically available and came out with a complicated problem with Bruno Fernandes; we'll see what happens," Jesus said.
"He's coming off an injury at United, and he told me he's been playing with that pain for the last three games, which is hindering him.
"It was one of the factors that prevented Bruno from playing at his best against Wales. I've already spoken to him, and I prefer not to risk it in this game, so he's fully fit for the Denmark match."
Cristiano Ronaldo is in the running to get a starting place, though, having had a goal disallowed against Wales last time out.
"Let's start with his performance against Wales. We had 15 shots inside the box, and of those 15, Ronaldo was involved in seven, and two of those were on target," Jesus said.
"That was a lot. His performance can be better, obviously; he came close to scoring, but I've already spoken to him.

"He played 65 minutes [against Wales]. I'll see how he is, whether I start him or come off the bench, because whether we like it or not, Cristiano isn't Joao Neves, who is 20 years old and can play two games in a row every three days.
"We have to look at it from that perspective, but he's one of the players about whom training will tell us something."

ycibu60ctvzf1bvfu5mmnmg5r.title: The Numbers Game: Spain take record unbeaten run to Wembley as Tuchel looks to rebuild trust
ycibu60ctvzf1bvfu5mmnmg5r.subtitle: England are still dealing with the scars of their World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina, ahead of their Nations League clash with Spain.
paragraphs: Just over two months on from their heartbreaking defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals, England are back in action at Wembley Stadium on Sunday.

And their opening game in the 2026-27 Nations League pits them against the team they would have faced in the World Cup final, had Thomas Tuchel's side not retreated into their own penalty area after Anthony Gordon's goal and conceded two late goals to Argentina.

Spain travel to London off the back of their second World Cup win, having held Lionel Messi and company to zero shots through 90 minutes of the final – the first time that has ever occurred – before claiming the trophy through Ferran Torres' extra-time goal.
The top two teams in Group A3 will progress to the quarter-finals next March, but with Croatia and Czechia also lurking, the Three Lions and La Roja will have to be switched on.
Who will get off to a positive start? Here, we preview the game using Opta insights.
What's expected?
Saturday's match looks almost too close to call on paper, and the Opta supercomputer is also struggling.
Across 10,000 pre-match simulations conducted by the predictive model, England were victorious in 33.6% of scenarios.
Spain have the slight edge, with a win probability of 40.2%, with the remaining 26.2% of simulations being drawn.
Spain have won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently triumphing 2-1 in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.
Their last away game against the Three Lions also ended in a 2-1 victory, at Wembley in the first edition of the Nations League, in September 2018.
Gareth Southgate's England did manage a memorable victory in the reverse fixture of that group, however, with a Raheem Sterling brace and a Marcus Rashford goal sealing a 3-2 triumph in Seville.
But England have only won two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine of those matches (D2).
One of those victories was a 1-0 triumph at home to Spain in November 2011, though, with the other being a 3-2 success in Germany in March 2016.
Tuchel aims to rebuild trust after semi-final collapse
It is now 60 years of hurt for England at major tournaments, with their next shot at silverware coming on home soil at Euro 2028.
And after this year's World Cup, perhaps more than any other edition in recent history, there was a real feeling of what could have been.
England were in a commanding position when Gordon applied the finishing touch to Morgan Rogers' cross 55 minutes into their tense semi-final clash with the Albiceleste in Atlanta.
They then immediately retreated into their shells, not helped by Tuchel introducing defenders Ezri Konsa, Dan Burn and Nico O'Reilly with his first three substitutions.

Between opening the scoring and conceding an 85th-minute equaliser to Enzo Fernandez, the Three Lions had just 11.9% possession, the lowest share ever recorded by a leading team in a World Cup match over a period of at least 10 minutes (since 1966) by a team who were leading. Their leading passer in that period was centre-back Marc Guehi, with six.
Defeat felt inevitable from the moment Argentina levelled, and now Tuchel – who faced stern criticism from supporters and the media – has bridges to build.

A win over the World champions would be a fine place to start, and it should be noted that Tuchel has the best win rate of any England manager to ever lead the team for at least 10 matches, at 77% (P22 W17 D2 L3), while the Three Lions have only averaged more goals per game under Walter Winterbottom (2.8) than Tuchel (2.3).

England have also won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of their most recent five without conceding. Only once in their history have they previously won six in a row to nil, doing so between March 2015 and March 2017.
But after the meek surrender that ended their World Cup dream, fans will want to see intensity and creativity.

The withdrawals of Declan Rice and Cole Palmer – who scored against Spain in the Euro 2024 final before being overlooked by Tuchel for the World Cup – do not help matters, though Morgan Gibbs-White could now have a chance to impress. His 13 goals in the Premier League this calendar year are the joint-most of any player, alongside Erling Haaland.
Spain out to extend record-breaking run
The mood in Spain's camp could hardly be more positive coming into this fixture, having followed up their World Cup triumph by handing head coach Luis de la Fuente a six-year contract extension.
They are also defending a 38-match unbeaten run in all competitions, winning 29 games and drawing nine in that time.
It is the longest-ever streak by a European or South American nation, dating back to a 1-0 defeat to Colombia in March 2024, which took place on English soil, at West Ham's London Stadium.

La Roja's last competitive defeat, which came all the way back in March 2023, also occurred in Britain, as they lost 2-0 to Scotland in a qualifier for Euro 2024. England will hope that is a positive omen.

But this is a truly special Roja side, led by Ballon d'Or contender Lamine Yamal but also boasting plenty of other talent across the board – including World Cup Golden Ball winner Rodri and Young Player of the Tournament Pau Cubarsi.
Aided by Yamal's brilliance, Spain also reached the final of the 2024-25 Nations League, eventually going down to Portugal on penalties following a 2-2 draw in the final.

Spain's last five Nations League matches have seen them both score multiple goals and concede multiple goals, which is the longest run by any nation – in any tier – since the tournament's inception in 2018.

La Roja have reached three of the last four Nations League finals, also losing to France in 2020-21 and beating Croatia on penalties in 2022-23. Excluding spot-kicks, they have lost just one of their last 18 matches in the competition (W10 D7).
And during the last edition of the Nations League, only Cristiano Ronaldo (eight goals) outscored Mikel Oyarzabal (four).

The Real Sociedad forward has 26 goals involvements across his last 25 international appearances (19 goals, seven assists), a run that started with him scoring the winner against England in the Euro 2024 final.
England – Jude Bellingham
While England's attack is spearheaded by one of Yamal's Ballon d'Or rivals in Harry Kane, Bellingham has been the Three Lions talisman this year, netting seven goals in 10 appearances for England.
David Platt was the last midfielder to find the net more often for them in a single calendar year, back in 1993 (eight).
Barcelona have scored 31 goals in their first seven games in LaLiga this season, with only Sevilla in 1940-41 (40) ever bettering their tally at this stage.

And Yamal has been a key part of their sensational attacking start, with only team-mate Raphinha (12) bettering his seven goals in the competition and only Kylian Mbappe (41) having more shots than his 38.

And during the last edition of the Nations League, only Cristiano Ronaldo (eight goals) outscored Mikel Oyarzabal (four). 

The Real Sociedad forward has 26 goals involvements across his last 25 international appearances (19 goals, seven assists), a run that started with him scoring the winner against England in the Euro 2024 final.

PLAYERS TO WATCH

England – Jude Bellingham

While England's attack is spearheaded by one of Yamal's Ballon d'Or rivals in Harry Kane, Bellingham has been the Three Lions talisman this year, netting seven goals in 10 appearances for England.

David Platt was the last midfielder to find the net more often for them in a single calendar year, back in 1993 (eight).

Spain – Lamine Yamal

Barcelona have scored 31 goals in their first seven games in LaLiga this season, with only Sevilla in 1940-41 (40) ever bettering their tally at this stage.

And Yamal has been a key part of their sensational attacking start, with only team-mate Raphinha (12) bettering his seven goals in the competition and only Kylian Mbappe (41) having more shots than his 38.

ygh90t5xvllp1ijr0nqxvxboo.title: Ancelotti encourages Brazil 'to play with joy' during difficult period
ygh90t5xvllp1ijr0nqxvxboo.subtitle: Brazil are undergoing a reset after their disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign, and Carlo Ancelotti believes they must enjoy the process.
paragraphs: Carlo Ancelotti has encouraged his Brazil players to "play with joy" during a "difficult period" for the national team.
Brazil were knocked out in the round of 16 at the World Cup this summer, prompting Ancelotti to overhaul the squad in preparation for the 2028 Copa America and 2030 World Cup.
While record-scorer Neymar retired after the tournament, the likes of Casemiro and Fabinho were left out by Ancelotti, who has given more minutes to younger players during this international break.
Brazil faced Australia twice in September, drawing 1-1 in Townsville before winning 4-2 in Brisbane, though Raphinha did suffer an injury in the victory.
Ancelotti's side take on India for the first time on Saturday, and he wants his players to play without pressure in Kolkata.
"The joy of playing football is important to Brazilians," said Ancelotti.
"Happiness is a very important quality that Brazilians have as part of their culture. So, I would like the players to play with joy, with happiness.
"Because sometimes, with the pressure of the game, you forget what football is, that it's a sport, that it's entertainment. And you have to play with joy.
"The truth is that these are tests. We're going to do another test [against India].

"I spoke with all the young players who are going to play or played in the first game and told them that for them it's not a test, it's an opportunity to show the quality they can have. So they need to take all of this calmly because it's not a test for them.
"It's true, the last few years for the Brazilian national team haven't been very good. Since 2002, Brazil hasn't managed to win the World Cup.
"All these defeats, this whole difficult period, serve as motivation for us to be a new generation of players who can compete with the best in the coming years."

yiidc45bzl8619509wbafcn63.title: Gasperini resolved to pick up where Roma left off in Serie A
yiidc45bzl8619509wbafcn63.subtitle: Roma sit top of the Serie A table ahead of the return to action this weekend, and Gian Piero Gasperini does not want their level to drop.
paragraphs: Gian Piero Gasperini is determined to see Roma "start where we left off" in Serie A when they return from the international break.
Roma made a stunning start to the 2026-27 campaign and sit top of the table, above reigning champions Inter due to their superior goal difference.
It is the first time since 2014-15 (when they recorded five wins) that Roma have remained unbeaten across their opening five league matches of the season.
Gasperini has so far been hesitant to say that Roma are in the Serie A title race, but they were rampant before the international break.
They are the second-highest scorers (14 goals, behind Inter's 15), and have the joint-second-best defensive record, conceding just three times (Cagliari have let in two).

"We had a pretty small number of players and couldn't play any friendlies, so we went for continuity with the work that we did in the first week and then took a few days off," Gasperini told Sky Sport Italia.
"[Monday] is the last day of holiday, and after that, we will get back into the league mentality, which we left during a great period of results and performances. We want to start where we left off.
"There have been lots of small factors, starting with the fact that I inherited a group that gave me their availability from the very first training session.
"The team had had a good end to the previous season, but the players immediately showed a willingness to explore different paths and different types of football.

"I also had the trust from the club. I've been appreciated by a club that initially brought me in as an opponent and rival. There was even a bit of scepticism. Gaining the appreciation of the Roma supporters has been a great success for me; I'm truly grateful."
Gasperini (299) is close to winning his 300th match as a manager in Serie A.
Only four managers have reached this milestone so far in the competition: Giovanni Trapattoni (352), Massimiliano Allegri (324), Luciano Spalletti (305) and Nereo Rocco (302).
He could reach that landmark against Como when his team returns to action on October 11, with Cesc Fabregas' side also in good form, having lost just one of their five league games so far (W3 D1).
"Anyone who watches football appreciates the evolution of their team, the quality of players they have and the quality of the games they play," Gasperini said about Como.
"Inter are still the strongest in terms of their squad and results, but Como can fight up there along with the rest of them.
"I've seen Fabregas say he uses Subbuteo to explain how to attack with depth. I have to use it to figure out how to stop him."
Gasperini is also preparing for the return of Roma's former boss Jose Mourinho, who will bring Real Madrid to Stadio Olimpico in the Champions League next week.
Mourinho led Roma to win the inaugural edition of the Conference League in May 2022, beating Feyenoord 1-0 in the final.
"Jose is, rightly, a special one, and he manages to find success on and off the pitch," Gasperini said of Mourinho.

"He won the Conference League and reached a Europa League final with Roma. He might have done a bit less in the league, but most of the fans still appreciate him. That means he has something special."

ykmt3bgt5dcn1rwmw6vsayuo3.title: Sorensen urges Whitecaps to keep performing at extremely high level
ykmt3bgt5dcn1rwmw6vsayuo3.subtitle: The Vancouver Whitecaps are looking to strengthen their grip on top spot in the Western Conference as they host playoff-chasing D.C. United.
paragraphs: Jesper Sorensen is thrilled with the level of Vancouver Whitecaps' performances this term and is determined to finish the MLS regular season strongly, starting with D.C. United.
Vancouver sit top of the Western Conference standings on 49 points, and they could clinch their playoff spot this weekend, though they would need to win and hope a few other results go their way.
They have alternated between a loss and a win in their last four league games, most recently brushing aside Real Salt Lake 3-0.
With not long left of the regular season, Sorensen revealed he is not changing his approach to games as he wants to maintain the Whitecaps' consistency ahead of a busy period.
"If we don't perform well enough, we can still win a game, but we'll not win consistently if we're not performing well on a consistent basis," Sorensen said. "For me, it's about how you play.
"I think over the course of the season, we have been performing extremely well, and that's what we have to keep up. You can lose a game even as the better team; that's how football works.
"But if you don't consistently perform and push the players towards good performances, it's difficult to improve."

D.C. are looking to try and make a late push for the playoffs; they sit 11th in the East but are only four points behind ninth-place FC Cincinnati despite winning just one of their last eight games (D4 L3).
They lost 2-1 to Charlotte FC last time out, and although the pressure is starting to mount on head coach Rene Weiler, he is focusing on the journey his players are going on.
"We are in the process of building something more sustainable, more consistent," he said. "We did the first step together.
"We cleaned up, and now we have to try to stabilise the team and then make a third step to winning more games.
"To overtake one or two teams [in the playoff race] is a big step, but I see a team much better than last season."
Vancouver Whitecaps – Yohei Takaoka
Yohei Takaoka has registered 11 clean sheets this season, recording 10+ shutouts in consecutive seasons.
The only other goalkeeper in club history to have 10 or more shutouts in any MLS season was David Ousted, who also did it in consecutive seasons (2014 and 2015).
D.C. United – Lucas Bartlett
Lucas Bartlett scored his third goal of the season for D.C. on Saturday, which ranks as the third-most among the team this season.
He is the first defender to score at least three goals in a single regular season for the club since Donovan Pines in 2023.
MATCH PREDICTION: VANCOUVER WHITECAPS WIN
Vancouver and D.C. are meeting for the 12th time and the first time since a 2-2 draw in Canada in September 2023.
That was the only match in the fixture's history in which both teams scored multiple goals, as the series has averaged 1.4 combined goals per match.

The Whitecaps earned a 3-0 win against RSL last time out, making it the club's ninth shutout win by multiple goals in the 2026 regular season. The MLS record for such games in a single campaign is 10, set by Chivas USA in 2007, Atlanta United in 2019 and Philadelphia Union in 2022.
As for D.C., they have played out a draw in five of their last seven road matches and six of their 11 games away from home this season.
The six away draws are United's most in a single regular season, since having seven in 2018, while it is two more than they had in 2025 (four).
Vancouver Whitecaps – 73.4%

yx2r1tpe17lw1omm77kg9e5yz.title: 'If there were five Monumentals, they would be full' – Scaloni braced for emotional Messi farewell
yx2r1tpe17lw1omm77kg9e5yz.subtitle: Lionel Messi will play his 208th and final game for Argentina on Tuesday, and Lionel Scaloni knows there will not be a dry eye in the house.
paragraphs: Lionel Scaloni feels Argentina's supporters could fill the Estadio Monumental five times over for Lionel Messi's farewell outing, which he is sure will be an emotional occasion.
The World Cup runners-up trounced Burkina Faso 7-0 on Saturday, following up their 4-0 win over Bolivia to remain perfect during this international break.
Argentina's next match will be their most eagerly anticipated of all, as Messi returns to the fold for one final time, for a farewell match against Benin on Tuesday.

Messi announced his decision to retire from international football in the aftermath of July's extra-time defeat to Spain in the World Cup final, and he will end his Argentina career with 208 senior caps – the most of any player in the team's history.
Messi also has more goals for Argentina than any other player (125) and more goal involvements at the World Cup than anyone else in history (33 – 21 goals, 12 assists).
The 39-year-old is the only player to start three World Cup finals, leading Argentina to glory in Qatar four years ago, and Scaloni expects a reception befitting an all-time great.
"I imagine Tuesday's match to be very emotional for everyone, including Leo. It will be an unforgettable day," Scaloni said.
"It will be his day and that of his team-mates, who also gave him his greatest footballing joy. I am grateful to be able to enjoy it, and I am going to be a mere spectator.

"I imagine that if there were five Monumentals, they would be full. I want people to understand what he transmits on the pitch, to his team-mates, to opponents, for people on the outside. That is what we are going to miss the most."

While Argentina are entering the post-Messi era, with a host of young players – including Nico Paz and Franco Mastantuono – impressing in recent games, they do at least look to have continuity in the dugout.

Scaloni is expected to renew his contract to at least run through the 2028 Copa America and potentially the 2030 World Cup, and midfielder Enzo Fernandez knows how important that would be for the Albiceleste.
"It would be very important for us that he continues, he put this together. We have to continue competing at the highest level," Fernandez said.
"Now we have to process the issue of Leo leaving and continue with the same line along which we came."
Asked how he retains his passion for a role he has held for eight years, Scaloni said: "I always try to live it.
"I understand what this position implies, but I believe that you can do both things and not lock yourself up only in a football office. Being able to enjoy yourself is important."

yyc48whrkuhm14mv9ti4qg6wu.title: Smith says focus remains on Charlotte after recording 50th victory
yyc48whrkuhm14mv9ti4qg6wu.subtitle: Dean Smith enjoyed his 50th win in charge of Charlotte FC last weekend, and he will be hoping to add another against the Chicago Fire.
paragraphs: Dean Smith intends to continue winning at Charlotte FC after claiming his 50th victory in charge of the Crown in all competitions, last time out against D.C. United.
Smith replaced Christian Lattanzio at Charlotte in December 2023 and has gone on to manage 112 matches for the club, with their results improving year-on-year under him.
Charlotte have finished fifth and then fourth in the Eastern Conference with Smith at the helm, while they find themselves fourth in the division so far this season.
However, they have failed to go beyond the first round of the playoffs while Smith has been at the club, something they will be hoping to rectify by the end of the 2026 campaign.
Ashley Westwood and Allan Saint-Maximin were on target in Smith's 50th win with Charlotte, with their goals sealing a 2-1 victory over D.C. at Bank of America Stadium.
Charlotte meet the Chicago Fire this weekend, and while Smith was thrilled with his personal achievement, he said that his main focus remains on the team's aspirations.
"[I'm] just pleased," Smith said. "I mean, it's 50 wins in 112 games. It's a good record, but we just want to keep winning them.
"It's not about my records, it's about the club. Every win, you probably don't enjoy them as much as you should because you're always thinking about the next game.
"So, hopefully we can get to the end of the season, and I'm enjoying the win for a special reason. I think we're getting there. The building blocks have been there.
"The ideology, everybody knows what is expected of them, so I think that's the easy part. The hardest part is always recruiting good people and good players."
Chicago are just four points behind Charlotte heading into this weekend's meeting, and they will be seeking a return to winning ways following a 3-0 defeat to Nashville SC.
Sam Surridge's 33rd-minute opener was followed up by second-half strikes from Cristian Espinoza and Hany Mukhtar to seal a comfortable triumph for the Eastern leaders.

The Fire were only able to register an expected goals (xG) total of 0.91 from their nine shots, only one of which was on target, with Gregg Berhalter conceding after the match that his team were simply beaten by stronger opposition.
"I don't look at it as if the result was unfortunate for us. We just lost to a better team. It's really simple," Berhalter said.
"I think the most important lesson from this evening is that Nashville are a benchmark for us. This is a team that we want to reach and with which we want to be able to compete.
"At the beginning, we were a little too conservative. We held on, then we lost a goal. We got back into the game, but then we lost another one.
"For us, the conclusion is that as a team, we have to improve."

The Fire's task against Charlotte will be made even more difficult, with Noah Allen, Chris Brady, Anzor Mekvabishvili, Puso Dithejane, Robert Lewandowski and Robin Lod all joining up with their respective national teams for the extended international break.
Charlotte FC – Allan Saint-Maximin
Since making his debut for Charlotte, only Cavan Sullivan (30), Kristoffer Velde (25) and Guilherme (23) have completed more dribbles in the MLS than Saint-Maximin's 22.
The former Newcastle United star also has five assists and one goal for Charlotte in that time, and he will be hoping to make his mark once again for Smith's side.
Chicago Fire – Maren Haile-Selassie
Haile-Selassie has scored eight goals this season for Chicago, the most among players currently on the Fire's roster.
Five of those goals have come in road matches this season, including four goals in his last four road matches.
MATCH PREDICTION: CHARLOTTE FC WIN

Chicago earned a 2-1 win over Charlotte in the first meeting between the two teams this season back in August. It was the third straight win in the series for the Fire, after they had lost five straight in the fixture entering last season.
The Fire were shut out for just the second time this regular season in their road loss to Nashville, tied for the fewest games being held scoreless this season with Inter Miami.
That ended a 21-game run with a goal in league play, as it was the first time Chicago had failed to score since March 7, against the Columbus Crew.
Charlotte, meanwhile, have recorded their two longest regular-season unbeaten runs in club history from July onward, with a 10-game streak in 2025 and a current eight-match run.
Over the past two seasons, the Crown have averaged 2.24 points per match from July to October, compared to 1.31 in March through June.

Charlotte FC – Allan Saint-Maximin

Since making his debut for Charlotte, only Cavan Sullivan (30), Kristoffer Velde (25) and Guilherme (23) have completed more dribbles in the MLS than Saint-Maximin's 22. 

The former Newcastle United star also has five assists and one goal for Charlotte in that time, and he will be hoping to make his mark once again for Smith's side. 

Chicago Fire – Maren Haile-Selassie

Haile-Selassie has scored eight goals this season for Chicago, the most among players currently on the Fire's roster.

Five of those goals have come in road matches this season, including four goals in his last four road matches.

MATCH PREDICTION: CHARLOTTE FC WIN

Chicago earned a 2-1 win over Charlotte in the first meeting between the two teams this season back in August. It was the third straight win in the series for the Fire, after they had lost five straight in the fixture entering last season.

The Fire were shut out for just the second time this regular season in their road loss to Nashville, tied for the fewest games being held scoreless this season with Inter Miami.

That ended a 21-game run with a goal in league play, as it was the first time Chicago had failed to score since March 7, against the Columbus Crew. 

Charlotte, meanwhile, have recorded their two longest regular-season unbeaten runs in club history from July onward, with a 10-game streak in 2025 and a current eight-match run.

Over the past two seasons, the Crown have averaged 2.24 points per match from July to October, compared to 1.31 in March through June. 

OPTA WIN PROBABILITY

Charlotte FC – 44.9%

Draw – 23.4%

Chicago Fire – 31.7%

yyjyzcfg4gz1v1lygu5o6dxf.title: Klopp not promising silverware ahead of Germany debut
yyjyzcfg4gz1v1lygu5o6dxf.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp is preparing to take charge of Germany for the first time on Thursday, though he was quick to temper expectations of his team.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp refused to make any promises of delivering silverware for Germany ahead of his debut against the Netherlands in the Nations League.
Klopp is preparing for his first game in charge at the Johan Cruijff Arena on Thursday after replacing Julian Nagelsmann following Germany's disappointing World Cup campaign.
Germany were knocked out in the round of 32 at the World Cup after losing on penalties to Paraguay, a defeat which led to Nagelsmann's departure after three years in charge.
The former Liverpool boss has signed a four-year deal, which will see him guide the team at the European Championship in 2028 and the World Cup two years later.
Nagelsmann had said following Germany's Euro 2024 quarter-final defeat that he was sad he ​would have to wait two years to lift the World Cup, something that did not come true.
Klopp was also asked about his remark at the ​start of his Liverpool tenure that he would probably have won a title if ​he was still in the job four years later.
"I ​don't want to promise anything," Klopp told a press conference. "What I can say ​is we will try and that's what it is about now. That's where we are at ‌the ⁠moment.
"We have had a little debate, rightly or wrongly, I think, about the impression that we have a lower quality than in other countries.
"This has become the main issue. We need to train better, train differently. But I firmly believe that it is always possible to improve training.
"This not only applies to football, but also to many other areas."
Germany have failed to go beyond the round of 32 in each of the last three editions of the World Cup, going out in the group stage in 2018 and 2022 before this summer's exit.
They last lifted silverware on the international stage in 2014, when they won the World Cup in Brazil.
Klopp made the decision to name two separate squads ahead of their Nations League fixtures against the Netherlands, Serbia and Greece, who they play home and away.
He named 16 uncapped players, with 44 players selected in total.
"I am in charge of the senior team and my task is ​to take the football there so that we are in ​with a ⁠chance to win every game we play," Klopp added.
"It won't work every day, but we are working at it. I hope we can see some things already tomorrow. We ⁠need to ​take steps and the boys are ready for ​that."
This will be the first meeting between the two nations since October 2024, with Jamie Leweling's 64th-minute strike enough to earn a 1-0 win for Germany.
Germany are unbeaten in their last three matches against the Netherlands (W2 D1) since a 4-2 defeat in a European Championship qualifier in September 2019.
"That doesn't mean anything to me, because I've never felt that rivalry," Klopp said of the rivalry between Germany and the Netherlands.
"It would be better to ask Rudi Voller, as someone who has actually experienced it firsthand.

"I know what this game means, and ideally, the atmosphere tomorrow night will be heated. It will be a difficult game for the players because the opposition is really good, with tremendous talent and some excellent footballers.
"It's crazy how many top players the Dutch national team has. If we want to have any chance at all, we have to approach it as a real 'derby'.
"For us, it's the beginning of something. We want to get off to a good start. Everything surrounding the game only plays a minor role."

yz317m1a7zkw1cjih001h8tcf.title: 'Don't betray me' – Mourinho highlights need for trust with Real Madrid players
yz317m1a7zkw1cjih001h8tcf.subtitle: Jose Mourinho has returned to Real Madrid, but he still has certain rules that help him get the best out of his players.
paragraphs: Jose Mourinho insists that trust between player and manager is key to getting the best out of a team as he looks to get Real Madrid back to the top of their game.
Mourinho returned to the Bernabeu after a 13-year absence and has made a strong start so far, losing just two of his eight matches in charge (W6).
Despite that, Madrid sit six points behind runaway leaders Barcelona, who have a 100% record so far, and went into the break on the back of a controversial 2-1 loss to derby rivals Atletico Madrid.
Mourinho is tasked with bringing some silverware back to Los Blancos, after they failed to get their hands on a single trophy last season and also struggled domestically in 2024-25.
"Don't betray me," Mourinho told the Bet It Drives Show when asked about trust and management.
"When I say don't betray me, of course, I'm speaking about football. Don't betray me, and I'll always be there for you.
"There are rules that are not negotiable. If you report at 9 a.m., it's 9 a.m. for everybody. If you arrive at 9.15, even if you're a superstar, you just can't. I don't accept it.
"But another thing is giving them freedom to express themselves."
Madrid started last season with Xabi Alonso at the helm, but he was sacked in January and replaced by Alvaro Arbeloa.
He then left his post at the end of 2025-26, with Madrid opting to turn to a more familiar figure to try and stop Barcelona's dominance.
During his first spell between 2010 and 2013, he won one LaLiga title, a Copa del Rey and the Supercopa de Espana.
"After two seasons where the biggest club in the world didn't have the best results and a little 'divorce' with the fans, the club contacted me," he said.
"They told me 'We know you. You know us. You know the club, you know the culture.
"We need you. We need you to rebuild. We need you to start again an amazing decade that the club had. We need a person with your profile'."

z50mt167hwpu1rb7p32bypwc9.title: Denmark 2-4 Portugal: No Ronaldo, no problem for Jesus in six-goal thriller
z50mt167hwpu1rb7p32bypwc9.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo's sensational departure from the Portugal camp did not affect Jorge Jesus' side against Denmark, as they earned a 4-2 win.
paragraphs: Portugal made light of Cristiano Ronaldo's absence as they earned a thrilling 4-2 away win over Denmark in the Nations League on Thursday.

The defending champions were playing their first game since Ronaldo abruptly left their camp on Wednesday, saying he would "tell the truth" about his reported row with head coach Jorge Jesus "in due time".
But Portugal did not miss the five-time Ballon d'Or winner in Copenhagen, with Joao Cancelo, Goncalo Ramos, Vitinha and Joao Felix scoring to keep them perfect after three games in Group A4.

After Rasmus Hojlund failed to get a touch on Adam Daghim's ball across the face of the Portugal goal, the visitors started to take control of the game, with Ramos turning Cancelo's scuffed cross-shot against the left post.

But the Selecao did have the lead just nine seconds after that near miss. Daghim's attempt to kickstart a Denmark counter-attack was cut out by Cancelo, who exchanged passes with Ramos before clipping a cute finish over Mads Hermansen.

Wearing the iconic number seven shirt following Ronaldo's departure, Rafael Leao forced Hermansen into action before Denmark struck back in stunning fashion, Mikkel Damsgaard curling a glorious effort into the far corner from the left of the box in the 23rd minute.

But the hosts were not level for long, as Ramos finished off another lovely Portugal move two minutes later. He backheeled skilfully to Fernandes before darting in behind, racing onto the Portugal captain's return pass and prodding into the near corner.

Hermansen denied Ramos and Fernandes either side of half-time, with the first of those saves coming after he cheaply conceded possession himself, but Hojlund got Denmark level eight minutes after the restart. He lobbed Diogo Costa following Damsgaard's defence-splitting pass, then taunted Portugal by copying Ronaldo's iconic "siuuu" celebration.

Portugal refused to go away, though, and after Ramos' acrobatic effort whistled over the crossbar, Vitinha ghosted onto Fernandes' cross and nodded past Hermansen at his near post with 67 minutes on the clock.
And there was still time for Ronaldo's Al-Nassr team-mate Joao Felix to add a fourth goal, sweeping a cutback from fellow substitute Diogo Dalot home three minutes from time.
Portugal attack thrives without Ronaldo
As is so often the case with Portugal, all the headlines in the build-up to Thursday's game were dominated by one man.

Ronaldo may be the all-time leading scorer in men's internationals, finding the net 146 times in 234 outings for Portugal, but Jesus responded firmly when asked about the forward's shock departure, saying: "It will never be any player that will change my ideas as coach. Never. Not him, not anyone in football."
And, at least on this evidence, perhaps Portugal are better off without Ronaldo in their lineup.

The combinations for their first two goals – both of which involved Ramos, the man leading the line in Ronaldo's absence – were slick, and they generated 19 shots and 2.74 expected goals (xG) throughout the game, compared to Denmark's 12 shots and 0.67 xG.

Hojlund celebrated mischievously after making it 2-2, but of all the goals, Vitinha's looked the most like something out of the Ronaldo playbook. Despite his stature as one of the shortest players on the pitch, the Paris Saint-Germain star scored his first senior international goal – on his 46th cap – with a perfect downward header.

zg8akpz6tfsq1pbm1tum4atjb.title: 'I would have liked to stay' – Kimmich reluctant to leave Germany camp
zg8akpz6tfsq1pbm1tum4atjb.subtitle: Joshua Kimmich is heading back to Bayern Munich after only being named in the first of Jurgen Klopp's two Germany squads.
paragraphs: Joshua Kimmich admitted he "would have liked to stay" with Germany for the entirety of the international break but understands why Jurgen Klopp called up two squads.
For Klopp's first matches in charge, he opted to call up 44 players across two squads to see as many players as possible in the extended break.
He remains winless after his first two matches in charge, though, having conceded a late equaliser to the Netherlands in a 1-1 draw before suffering a shock 1-0 loss to Greece on Sunday.
Six of the players from Klopp's first squad will stay on with the second: Finn Dahmen, Nico Schlotterbeck, Philipp Treu, Yannik Engelhardt, Bambase Conte and Serge Gnabry.
Florian Wirtz and Jonathan Burkardt were originally called up for the second squad but arrived earlier to replace the injured Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala.
Despite being the team captain, Kimmich is not one of those remaining in the squad for their last two games against Serbia and Greece.
"I would have liked to stay, but I also understand that the coach wants to get to know some other players," Kimmich said after the loss to Greece.
"That was the plan from the beginning: that we would rotate the squads.
"Accordingly, I'll be cheering the team on from home."
Klopp is the third German head coach to go winless in his first two international matches (D1 L1).
Previously, this had only happened to Sepp Herberger and Helmut Schon; the two later World Cup-winning coaches then won their third international match.
Germany's next match is at home to Serbia on Thursday before they round off this block of fixtures with a trip to Greece on October 4.

zhklqh0zv4m41kotvtsa2ypuv.title: The Numbers Game: Rampant England aim to finish strong
zhklqh0zv4m41kotvtsa2ypuv.subtitle: Harry Kane is set to make a landmark appearance as England aim to round off the extended international window in style against Czechia.
paragraphs: England round off the first international break of the season, aiming to make it three straight wins in the Nations League.
After starting their campaign with a 3-2 loss to world champions Spain at Wembley, England beat Czechia 2-0 and then thrashed Croatia 7-0.
Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored twice each, while Jude Bellingham was also on target and laid on three assists. Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers also scored in the emphatic victory.
Thomas Tuchel has seen his team plunder 11 goals in the three games across this extended international window so far, and there is one more match to come, as Czechia visit Wembley on Tuesday.
This fixture comes just a week on from a routine win in Prague, where the Three Lions were helped out by Pavel Sulc's red card midway through the first half.
Here, we preview England v Czechia, calling on Opta's key insights.
The Opta supercomputer is making England the clear favourites, with a 79.8% win probability.
Czechia come out on top in just 7.9% of the model's 10,000 data-led simulations, while there is a 12.3% chance of a draw.
And given the head-to-head record between these teams, it is hardly surprising to see England so well fancied.
Czechia have lost six of their eight competitive meetings with England (W2), though they have always responded to back-to-back losses with a win – they have lost their last two.
England are also unbeaten in all eight of their games against Czechia at Wembley (W6 D2), the most recent of which saw the Three Lions finish their Euro 2020 group-stage campaign with a 1-0 win.
The Three Lions have not lost back-to-back competitive home matches between November 1999 (v Scotland) and October 2000 (v Germany).
Tuchel's team showing their teeth

There was so much frustration among England's fanbase in the wake of Tuchel's pragmatic, perhaps pessimistic, approach during the World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina, as there was a real feeling that this Three Lions squad has the attacking talent to cut through most other teams.
That attacking quality has been on show over the past fortnight, and Tuchel will be eyeing up a strong finish to this extended stint with his squad.

Across their last four games in all competitions, England have won 6-4 against France and 7-0 against Croatia. It is the first time they have scored 6+ goals in two different games in a calendar year since 2019, while they last did so in three different games in 1908.

And while Kane remains England's talisman up top, there is a plethora of talent behind the Bayern Munich captain who are proving the Three Lions should always be out to stamp their authority on matches.
Gordon has scored in each of his last four appearances for England. The last player other than Kane to score in five in a row for the team was Wayne Rooney between October 2014 and March 2015.
The Barcelona winger has actually netted two headed goals in his last two England appearances – across 248 total club appearances, he has not scored a single header.
Other than Kane, Gordon is the only player to be directly involved in a goal in five consecutive England appearances across the last 10 years (four goals, two assists).
Against Croatia, Saka scored two right-footed goals in a match for the first time in his senior career for club and country.

Bellingham, meanwhile, was directly involved in more than two goals in an England game for the first time. He is the first player to record three assists in a game for the Three Lions since Trent Alexander-Arnold against San Marino in November 2021.
England have lost Alex Scott, who faces up to two months on the sidelines, and Ezri Konsa due to injury, with Rico Lewis called up, but their attack is fit and firing.
Czechia's dismal start
They sit bottom of the group after losing their opening three games, going down 3-1 to Spain and 2-1 to Croatia, either side of that defeat to England.
Santi Denia has lost all three of his games in charge of Czechia and could be the second manager to lose their first four matches with the nation after Vaclav Jezek in 1973, then as Czechoslovakia.
In fact, Czechia have lost five of their last six games in all competitions (D1), including each of the last four in a row. They last lost five consecutively between July 1972 and March 1973.

Across all of the teams competing in the 2026-27 Nations League, Czechia's 1.73 expected goals is the sixth-lowest. They have had just 16 shots, with only Gibraltar (14) and Liechtenstein (nine) having fewer attempts in the competition.
Only six teams, meanwhile, have conceded more goals than Czechia (seven) so far.
Czechia have already faced 56 shots – an average of 18.7 per game – with 22 of those hitting the target.
This is a team that are not clinical going forward and are open at the back. England, at home, should not be having any trouble.
England – Harry Kane
If Kane features in this match, he will make his 125th England appearance, which would see him equal Peter Shilton as the all-time most capped player in the Three Lions' history.
With his double last time out, Kane became the first player to score 10+ goals in three different calendar years for England: 11 in 2026, 16 in 2021 and 12 in 2019.

Kane has netted 89 goals across his 124 caps to date, and a flurry here could well set him on the way to really close in on a century before 2026 is up. At the very least, he should be targeting making this calendar year his best for a goal return on the international stage.
Czechia – Adam Hlozek
Given their drab form, Czechia hardly have many players who are shining in an attacking sense.
But Hlozek has been one of their better performers.
He leads the way in their squad in the past three games for goal involvements (two assists), shots (four) and chances created (four).
England's defence should not have too much to worry about, but Hlozek could pose them a few problems if given the chance.

And while Kane remains England's talisman up top, there is a plethora of talent behind the Bayern Munich captain who are proving the Three Lions should always be out to stamp their authority on matches. 

Gordon has scored in each of his last four appearances for England. The last player other than Kane to score in five in a row for the team was Wayne Rooney between October 2014 and March 2015.

The Barcelona winger has actually netted two headed goals in his last two England appearances – across 248 total club appearances, he has not scored a single header.

Other than Kane, Gordon is the only player to be directly involved in a goal in five consecutive England appearances across the last 10 years (four goals, two assists).

Against Croatia, Saka scored two right-footed goals in a match for the first time in his senior career for club and country.

Bellingham, meanwhile, was directly involved in more than two goals in an England game for the first time. He is the first player to record three assists in a game for the Three Lions since Trent Alexander-Arnold against San Marino in November 2021.

England have lost Alex Scott, who faces up to two months on the sidelines, and Ezri Konsa due to injury, with Rico Lewis called up, but their attack is fit and firing.

Czechia's dismal start

But what of Czechia?

They sit bottom of the group after losing their opening three games, going down 3-1 to Spain and 2-1 to Croatia, either side of that defeat to England.

Santi Denia has lost all three of his games in charge of Czechia and could be the second manager to lose their first four matches with the nation after Vaclav Jezek in 1973, then as Czechoslovakia.

In fact, Czechia have lost five of their last six games in all competitions (D1), including each of the last four in a row. They last lost five consecutively between July 1972 and March 1973.

Across all of the teams competing in the 2026-27 Nations League, Czechia's 1.73 expected goals is the sixth-lowest. They have had just 16 shots, with only Gibraltar (14) and Liechtenstein (nine) having fewer attempts in the competition.

Only six teams, meanwhile, have conceded more goals than Czechia (seven) so far.

Czechia have already faced 56 shots – an average of 18.7 per game – with 22 of those hitting the target.

This is a team that are not clinical going forward and are open at the back. England, at home, should not be having any trouble.

PLAYERS TO WATCH

England – Harry Kane

If Kane features in this match, he will make his 125th England appearance, which would see him equal Peter Shilton as the all-time most capped player in the Three Lions' history.

With his double last time out, Kane became the first player to score 10+ goals in three different calendar years for England: 11 in 2026, 16 in 2021 and 12 in 2019.

Kane has netted 89 goals across his 124 caps to date, and a flurry here could well set him on the way to really close in on a century before 2026 is up. At the very least, he should be targeting making this calendar year his best for a goal return on the international stage.

Czechia – Adam Hlozek

Given their drab form, Czechia hardly have many players who are shining in an attacking sense.

But Hlozek has been one of their better performers.

He leads the way in their squad in the past three games for goal involvements (two assists), shots (four) and chances created (four).

England's defence should not have too much to worry about, but Hlozek could pose them a few problems if given the chance.

zsa2ubvyobgz1wnufs92e6jek.title: 'The goals and the points will come' – Slegers optimistic despite Arsenal's slow start
zsa2ubvyobgz1wnufs92e6jek.subtitle: Arsenal were dealt their first defeat of the Women's Super League season against Chelsea, but Renee Slegers remained calm about her team.
paragraphs: Renee Slegers remains confident her Arsenal team can achieve great things this season despite slipping to their first Women's Super League defeat of the campaign.
Arsenal were beaten 1-0 by Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Sunday, with Alyssa Thompson pouncing on some sloppy defending to score the only goal just before the break.
The Gunners improved after the interval, having also seen Kim Little and Mariona Caldentey hit the woodwork in the first half, but they were unable to find an equaliser.
Arsenal's attacking troubles have been a topic of conversation as they have scored just two goals this campaign, with only Charlton Athletic (one) netting fewer in the WSL so far.
Slegers' side had 18 shots, but only two of those forced Hannah Hampton into making a save, with those efforts generating an expected goals (xG) total of just 1.04.
The result also saw Arsenal's 20-game unbeaten run in the WSL come to an end, leaving them seventh in the table and already seven points behind leaders Manchester City.

And while Slegers expressed her disappointment with the defeat, she backed her players to hit their stride sooner rather than later, with a Women's Champions League clash against Paris FC coming up this Wednesday.
"Very disappointed. We know it's a tough game Chelsea away. I think we did well in the first half in the physical battle and dominated until their goal," Slegers told Sky Sports.
"We found it hard in the second half and it cost us more energy. It's a cocktail of things. It's everything. Technical and psychological. We're looking at it.
"I believe in these players. The goals and the points will come. I believe in them."
For Chelsea, however, they ensured their own unbeaten run in the WSL continued. They are now 12 games without defeat in the league.

The Blues are also now unbeaten across their opening four games of a WSL campaign for the fourth successive season, while Arsenal only have five points to their name at this stage for the second time in the last three seasons (also 2024-25).
Keira Walsh has been key to Chelsea's strong start to the season, and she once again played a starring role in the middle of midfield against Arsenal.
She finished with team-high totals for chances created (three), accurate passes (62) and possession won (10), while only Lucy Bronze (107) had more touches for Chelsea than Walsh's 92.
The England international acknowledged the difficulties Chelsea came up against as Arsenal searched for an equaliser, but she was thrilled to help get her team over the line.
"It's hard, Arsenal were chasing a goal and changed formation a bit," Walsh said. "It was important that we kept a clean sheet and stayed in the game.
"Ellie [Carpenter] took us up the pitch a bit at the end and it really helped."
Walsh was also not reading too much into Chelsea's unbeaten league run, adding: "I don't really think we think about it.
"We've got both sides to our game and we showed that in spells. Everyone was fighting for each other. Every first and second ball was ours."
